records.full_text:
The Revolution in Hayti—President Jeffrard preparing to Escape—Suffering among the Negroes on the Island of Jamaica—An outbreak Feared—San Domingo Affairs.

NEW YORK, Sept. 1.—The Herald's Kingston, Jamaica, correspondent says, that the headway which the revolutionists are making in Hayti, has been deemed by President Jeffrard sufficiently alarming to induce him to make preparations for escape from his country. A mail steamer has therefore been chartered at Kingston to proceed to Port au Prince and there remain till the time arrives for him to seek safety in flight or till the danger of such an event has passed.

Owing to the severe drought of the present summer in the Island of Jamaica, the heavy taxes and other causes, the negro laborers there have been reduced to the most abject poverty and great suffering, and thousands of them are on the verge of starvation. They blame the governor and his officers as the cause of their afflictions, and so strong and bitter is their feeling against the local government that an outbreak on their part is feared in the western part of the Island, in consequence of which two gunboats have been dispatched to that locality.

The Herald's Santiago correspondent says, notwithstanding the havoc and destruction of the Spaniards during their invasion of San Domingo, the crops are now coming forward which promise ample subsistence for the inhabitants, and that the sacrifices which the war has compelled the people to endure have made them more united and determined to maintain their independence. The latter statement is hardly borne out by reports which we have already published of threatened hostilities between two native chiefs, Gen'ls Penisutal and Cotral. It is said that the Spaniards stole and destroyed large quantities of fine wools, principally the property of American merchants, which had been stored at different places, and now Gen. Gandana, the Spanish commander, having withdrawn his troops from the interior, has blockaded the principal forts of the Republic because the Dominican Government will not submit to his haughty and unreasonable demands in the peace treaty, thus preventing the exportation of large stocks of tobacco belonging to Americans as well as Europeans. To offset this blockade the Dominicans have determined to commission privateers to prey on Spanish commerce and an agent authorized to issue letters of marque has already left for the United States and Europe.

records.headline: The latest advices from San Domingo report that the last of the Spaniards
records.summary_en: The latest advices from San Domingo report that the last of the Spaniards have left the island, and the Dominicans are sole masters of their territory. One of their military chiefs has been appointed Protector General of the republic, and the citizens are busily reorganizing the various departments of government. A national convention for the formation of a permanent constitution and government is announced, patriot journals have been established at important points, and the people are everywhere rejoicing over the prospect of future independence and freedom undisturbed.

Se anuncia una convención nacional para la formación de una constitución y un gobierno permanentes, se han establecido periódicos patrióticos en puntos importantes y el pueblo se regocija en todas partes ante la perspectiva de una independencia y una libertad futuras sin perturbaciones.

records.headline: An editorial surveys recent European aggressions upon the republics of America
records.summary_en: An editorial surveys recent European aggressions upon the republics of America, and numbers Spain's attack on the Dominican Republic among them. Spain, on a pretext like the one that served in Mexico, attacked the republic with a view of subjugating it and bringing it under colonial rule, and threatened at the same time the republics of South America on the Pacific. She proceeded no further, the paper argues, because she met an unexpected stubborn resistance in the Dominicans, and because the progress of events in the United States warned her off.

No fue más lejos, sostiene el periódico, porque encontró una inesperada y tenaz resistencia en los dominicanos, y porque el curso de los acontecimientos en Estados Unidos la disuadió.

records.headline: News from St. Domingo
records.summary_en: News from St. Domingo to September 9 describes Dominicans celebrating the second anniversary of their liberation from Spain, after eighteen months of fighting forced Spain to evacuate the island. General Pimentel, elected provisional president in March, became unpopular for harsh and unlawful acts, and after citizens in the capital repudiated him he resigned, while General J. M. Cabral was commissioned as Protector of the republic to summon a National Convention.

El general Pimentel, elegido presidente provisional en marzo, se volvió impopular por actos duros e ilegales, y después de que los ciudadanos de la capital lo repudiaron, renunció, mientras el general J. M. Cabral fue nombrado Protector de la república para convocar una Convención Nacional.

records.headline: Advices received from St. Domingo to the 19th of September report
records.summary_en: Advices received from St. Domingo to the 19th of September report that President Cabral has prohibited all further issues of paper money, and efforts are making to restore the currency to a specie basis. A large quantity of copper money is expected from Porto Rico, and a terrific hurricane had visited the coast, doing great damage. A National Guard and a municipal police are to be organized, an agent of the republic has been appointed in New York city, and the republic has been divided into five provinces: Compostela de Azua, Santo Domingo de Guzman, Santa Cruz del Seibo, Concepcion de la Vega and Santiago de los Caballeros.
records.summary_es: Noticias recibidas de Santo Domingo hasta el 19 de septiembre informan que el presidente Cabral ha prohibido toda nueva emisión de papel moneda, y se hacen esfuerzos por restaurar la moneda sobre la base metálica. Se espera una gran cantidad de moneda de cobre desde Puerto Rico, y un terrible huracán había azotado la costa causando grandes daños. Se organizarán una Guardia Nacional y una policía municipal, se ha nombrado un agente de la república en la ciudad de Nueva York, y la república ha sido dividida en cinco provincias: Compostela de Azua, Santo Domingo de Guzmán, Santa Cruz del Seibo, Concepción de la Vega y Santiago de los Caballeros.

records.summary_en: The *Daily National Intelligencer* reported on November 13, 1865, that Don Pedro Valverde, a member of the "Yankee party," supports opening Dominican gold mines, mahogany forests, and pearl fisheries to immigrants under a liberal colonization law, and proposes establishing free and neutral ports jointly with President Geffrard of Hayti. In contrast, the newspaper noted that General Cabral has intimate relations with European consuls while the United States is unrepresented, and suggested that Cabral might pursue a close union with Hayti that could threaten the white race in the eastern part of the island. Additionally, the article stated that if Valverde is elected, the Dominican Republic would respond to Spanish demands for the repayment of conquest costs with a counter-demand.

records.headline: A report on the colored Americans of Santo Domingo, emigrants
records.summary_en: A report on the colored Americans of Santo Domingo, emigrants from the United States, tells how they formed a mutual assistance society for their own members and for any unfortunate stranger from the United States cast helpless on the Dominican shore, and how they took a ruined Bethel church and repaired and roofed it by their own exertions. When the Spanish forces took formal possession of Santo Domingo in 1861 they were deprived of the church, and the public exercise of the Protestant religion was not allowed them during the four years of Spanish rule. After the Spaniards evacuated the country and the republic was restored, General Cazneau, formerly United States commissioner at Santo Domingo, obtained the building again for them, and on the first Sunday of October it was reopened with a well-attended jubilee of thanksgiving for the restoration of equal rights to all races and of perfect freedom of conscience under the laws of the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: Un informe sobre los americanos de color de Santo Domingo, emigrantes de Estados Unidos, cuenta cómo formaron una sociedad de ayuda mutua para sus propios miembros y para cualquier extranjero desafortunado de Estados Unidos que llegara desamparado a la costa dominicana, y cómo tomaron una iglesia Bethel en ruinas y la repararon y techaron con sus propios esfuerzos. Cuando las fuerzas españolas tomaron posesión formal de Santo Domingo en 1861 fueron privados de la iglesia, y el ejercicio público de la religión protestante no les fue permitido durante los cuatro años de dominio español. Después de que los españoles evacuaron el país y la república fue restaurada, el general Cazneau, antiguo comisario de Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo, recuperó el edificio para ellos, y el primer domingo de octubre fue reabierta con un concurrido jubileo de acción de gracias por la restauración de la igualdad de derechos para todas las razas y de la perfecta libertad de conciencia bajo las leyes de la República Dominicana.

records.summary_en: An armed man abruptly entered a session of the Dominican Congress to announce the impending arrival of revolutionary forces and proclaim General Baez as president, causing the ministers to flee in terror. Following this confusion, General Pedro Guillermo was appointed dictator until Baez could arrive, and an election on December 14th unanimously named Buenaventura Baez President of the Dominican Republic. Meanwhile, Cabral accepted a military position under the new government, which Guillermo practically headed.
records.summary_es: Un individuo armado irrumpió súbitamente en una sesión del Congreso dominicano para anunciar la inminente llegada de huestes revolucionarias y proclamar presidente al general Báez, haciendo que los ministros huyeran despavoridos. En medio del desconcierto subsiguiente, el general Pedro Guillermo fue investido como mandatario provisorio hasta la llegada de Báez, y en los comicios del 14 de diciembre se proclamó unánimemente a Buenaventura Báez presidente de la República Dominicana. Entretanto, Cabral aceptó un cargo militar bajo el nuevo régimen, que de facto encabezaba Guillermo.

records.headline: A narrative of the crisis at the capital describes how the ministers
records.summary_en: A narrative of the crisis at the capital describes how the ministers, in the confusion, abandoned their seats and sought protection in the houses of the French, Italian and English consuls. Cabral appeared in public and declared that if the popular voice and welfare demanded the rule of Baez he would gladly give his consent; the popular feeling then turned in favor of Cabral, and he retained power for several weeks. The mysterious man who had frightened the Congress proved to be General Pedro Guillermo, who managed to have himself appointed dictator until Baez should arrive; and an election held on the 14th of December by the Constitutional Assembly unanimously appointed Buenaventura Baez President of the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: Una narración de la crisis en la capital describe cómo los ministros, en la confusión, abandonaron sus escaños y buscaron protección en las casas de los cónsules de Francia, Italia e Inglaterra. Cabral apareció en público y declaró que si la voz y el bienestar del pueblo demandaban el gobierno de Báez, él daría gustoso su consentimiento; el sentimiento popular se volvió entonces a favor de Cabral, y este retuvo el poder durante varias semanas. El hombre misterioso que había asustado al Congreso resultó ser el general Pedro Guillermo, quien logró hacerse nombrar dictador hasta que Báez llegara; y una elección celebrada el 14 de diciembre por la Asamblea Constitucional nombró por unanimidad a Buenaventura Báez presidente de la República Dominicana.

records.summary_en: An armed man carrying a cutlass interrupted a session of the Supreme Congress to announce the arrival of General Baez and demand peace from General Cabral. In the ensuing confusion, ministers sought refuge with foreign consuls, while Cabral stated he would consent to Baez's rule if demanded by the public. Finalmente, el general Pedro Guillermo asumió el mando dictatorial transitorio hasta que una asamblea constitucional, el 14 de diciembre, eligió por unanimidad a Buenaventura Báez presidente de la República Dominicana, aceptando Cabral un cargo militar subordinado a Guillermo.

records.summary_en: A mysterious armed man suddenly entered a congressional session and declared himself an emissary of General Baez, causing the ministers to flee in terror while General Cabral agreed to the popular will. The intruder was revealed to be General Pedro Guillermo, who had himself appointed dictator until an election on December 14 unanimously made Baez President of the Dominican Republic. Consequently, Cabral accepted a military position under the new government, of which Guillermo became the practical head.
records.summary_es: Un enigmático hombre armado irrumpió sorpresivamente en el recinto del Congreso proclamándose emisario del general Báez, lo que provocó la huida aterrorizada del gabinete ministerial mientras el general Cabral se plegaba a la voluntad popular. El intruso resultó ser el general Pedro Guillermo, quien se hizo ungir dictador provisional hasta que en las votaciones del 14 de diciembre se designó por unanimidad a Báez presidente de la República Dominicana. A consecuencia de ello, Cabral aceptó una comandancia militar en la nueva administración, cuyo timón efectivo retenía Guillermo.

records.headline: A letter from San Domingo reports a January 14 conversation
records.summary_en: A letter from San Domingo reports a January 14 conversation at the national palace between Secretary Seward and President Báez, at which the Dominican cabinet was present. Báez told the Secretary that the revolution had been made in the republic and accepted by the whole people, and that his government lacked nothing for its stability but the recognition of the United States. Seward answered that General Cabral — who, he said, had most loyally been the obstacle to recognition — had headed the republic when Spain's power was cast off, and that the United States, satisfied that the revolution was as successful as it was just and permanently established under Cabral, had instructed its consul to recognize the republic without hesitation; before those instructions could be executed, a change had taken place.
records.summary_es: Una carta de Santo Domingo reseña una conversación del 14 de enero en el palacio nacional entre el secretario Seward y el presidente Báez, con asistencia del gabinete dominicano. Báez dijo al secretario que la revolución se había consumado en la república y había sido aceptada por todo el pueblo, y que a su gobierno nada le faltaba para su estabilidad sino el reconocimiento de los Estados Unidos. Seward respondió que el general Cabral —quien, dijo, había sido muy lealmente el obstáculo para el reconocimiento— había encabezado la república cuando se derrocó el poder de España, y que los Estados Unidos, satisfechos de que la revolución era tan exitosa como justa y de que se había establecido permanentemente bajo la dirección de Cabral, habían instruido a su cónsul para que reconociera la república sin vacilación; antes de que esas instrucciones pudieran ejecutarse, había sobrevenido un cambio.

records.summary_en: In an exchange printed by the paper, a Dominican speaker pleads for recognition by the United States, calling the enjoyment of American favor essential to Dominica's stability and peace and hoping that the proclamation of general liberty in the United States had removed the obstacles to recognition. Secretary Seward replies by recounting how the United States established itself as a republic on the principle of the equality of men while African slavery still existed under state laws.
records.summary_es: En un intercambio publicado por el periódico, un orador dominicano suplica el reconocimiento de Estados Unidos, y califica el disfrute del favor estadounidense de esencial para la estabilidad y la paz de Dominica, con la esperanza de que la proclamación de la libertad general en Estados Unidos hubiera eliminado los obstáculos para el reconocimiento. El secretario Seward responde relatando cómo Estados Unidos se estableció como república sobre el principio de la igualdad de los hombres mientras la esclavitud africana aún existía bajo las leyes estatales.

records.headline: The Herald argues that the Dominican republic should be accepted
records.summary_en: The Herald argues that the Dominican republic should be accepted without further delay as an outpost of the United States, and says that since Mr. Seward's visit to the island the republic of St. Domingo, conducted by President Báez, has been recognized, as has that of Hayti. It accompanies the argument with a sketch of the republic: the eastern portion of the island of Hayti, comprising nearly three-fifths of it, its name derived from the Spanish name of the island, Santo Domingo; an area estimated at 17,500 square miles and a population of about 136,000, of whom one tenth claim to be whites and the rest are of African descent or of mixed African and European descent; a boundary with the Haytian republic running from the mouth of the river Massacre, on the north coast, to the Pedernales river on the south; and an interior of mountain ranges six to eight thousand feet high, covered with tropical forests, with large plains watered by numerous streams stretching toward the coast.

records.headline: From St. Domingo, the Crescent prints paragraphs from the Havana papers
records.summary_en: From St. Domingo, the Crescent prints paragraphs from the Havana papers on conditions in the republic. In Puerto Plata, commerce is reported pretty brisk; the whole island was prospering, perfect tranquility reigned throughout the country, Spaniards continued to be very well treated, and General Báez was generally well liked, from which it was hoped the government would very soon be consolidated under his presidency. Another paragraph gives an unconfirmed report that some of the interior provinces had sent communications to the President calling on him to declare war against the Haytians for the injuries they were committing on the frontier. records.headline: Until last September, Cabral held the supreme power, a Herald review of the Dominican struggle
records.summary_en: Until last September, Cabral held the supreme power, a Herald review of the Dominican struggle relates; a general election was then held for president. A large majority, it says, is known to have been given for Báez, particularly in Azua, Baní, Santo Domingo, Higüey, Moca and Macorís; but Cabral had Báez's votes thrown out on the ground that, being away from the country, Báez could not be considered a candidate, and Cabral, fraudulently elected, continues to hold tyrannical power. Several hundred of the friends of Báez have been arbitrarily banished from the island and are now destitute in Panama, Puerto Rico, Colón and Chagres, along the Spanish Main and in the United States, and a brother of General Báez has lain chained in a dungeon at Santo Domingo since last June, for fear of some attempt to reinstate him.
records.summary_es: Hasta septiembre pasado, Cabral mantuvo el poder supremo, relata una reseña del Herald sobre la lucha dominicana; se celebraron entonces elecciones generales para presidente. records.headline: A French account of the bay of Samana, printed in translation
records.summary_en: A French account of the bay of Samana, printed in translation, describes a bay whose fine situation has always caught the eye of navigators: several rivers flow into it, one of them, the Yuna, navigable for over fifty miles; it is surrounded by forests abounding in the finest building timbers, and the country around it contains mines of iron, copper and lead, and, still more valuable, mines of coal. Had France kept St. Domingo, the writer says, Samana would long ago have become one of the busiest centres of European trade with America. He recounts the French attempts on the bay: a settlement founded in 1673, renewed attempts in 1699 and under the Count d'Estaing, and the plan's revival in 1822 and under Louis Philippe, when it failed because of the formal opposition of the British Cabinet, who argued that France, having lost her colony of St. Domingo, had no real claim to occupy Samana. The writer turns at last to the recent attempt of the United States, to be judged, on the question of right, in the same light.
records.summary_es: Un relato francés sobre la bahía de Samaná, publicado en traducción, describe una bahía cuya excelente situación siempre ha llamado la atención de los navegantes: varios ríos desembocan en ella, uno de ellos, el Yuna, navegable por más de cincuenta millas; está rodeada de bosques que abundan en las mejores maderas de construcción, y el país que la rodea contiene minas de hierro, cobre y plomo y, aún más valiosas, minas de carbón. Si Francia hubiera conservado a Santo Domingo, dice el autor, Samaná se habría convertido hace mucho en uno de los centros más activos del comercio europeo con América. Refiere los intentos franceses sobre la bahía: una fundación en 1673, nuevos intentos en 1699 y bajo el conde d'Estaing, y la reactivación del plan en 1822 y bajo Luis Felipe, cuando fracasó por la oposición formal del gabinete británico, que alegó que Francia, habiendo perdido su colonia de Santo Domingo, no tenía derecho real a ocupar Samaná. El autor se vuelve por último hacia el reciente intento de los Estados Unidos, que debe juzgarse, en cuanto a la cuestión de derecho, bajo la misma luz.

records.headline: The Haytian government was about to establish friendly relations
records.summary_en: The Haytian government was about to establish friendly relations with the Dominican republic, the Herald reports from news of a late date: a circular of the Secretary for the Interior, addressed to the commandants of the frontier territories, recommended them to adopt the necessary measures to prevent all persons with arms or warlike stores from crossing the borders or in any way endangering the peace between the two republics; the government would enforce the regulations in the strictest terms as soon as the Dominican government adopted similar measures, and persons travelling from one republic to the other would be duly provided with passports. The paper also prints a translation of the message of General Salnave to the people and army of Hayti: called to the presidency by a decision of the National Assembly of June 14, 1867, he vows that the law will be the strength of the government, that the public liberties established by the constitution will be respected, and that the public welfare will be the supreme law of his administration.
records.summary_es: El gobierno haitiano estaba a punto de establecer relaciones amistosas con la República Dominicana, informa el Herald a partir de noticias recientes: una circular del secretario del Interior, dirigida a los comandantes de los territorios fronterizos, les recomendaba adoptar las medidas necesarias para impedir que personas con armas o pertrechos de guerra cruzaran las fronteras o pusieran en peligro de cualquier modo la paz entre las dos repúblicas; el gobierno haría cumplir los reglamentos con el mayor rigor tan pronto como el gobierno dominicano adoptara medidas similares, y las personas que viajaran de una república a la otra serían debidamente provistas de pasaportes. El periódico publica además una traducción del mensaje del general Salnave al pueblo y al ejército de Haití: llamado a la presidencia por decisión de la Asamblea Nacional del 14 de junio de 1867, promete que la ley será la fuerza del gobierno, que las libertades públicas establecidas por la constitución serán respetadas y que el bienestar público será la ley suprema de su administración.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that the bay and a portion of the peninsula of Samaná, located on the northeast coast of the island of Hayti, possess great natural facilities for repairing vessels and occupy an important strategic position relative to inter-oceanic routes. The article stated that possession of Samaná would be of incalculable value to the United States for commercial purposes and as a naval station, comparing its potential importance to that of Gibraltar. Additionally, the excerpt described the area as having a fertile soil, a salubrious tropical climate, and being reachable from New York in four days by steamer.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que la bahía y una parte de la península de Samaná, situadas en la costa nororiental de la isla de Santo Domingo, ofrecen excelentes condiciones naturales para el carenado y reparación de buques y ocupan una posición estratégica primordial respecto a las rutas interoceánicas. El artículo aseveró que la posesión de Samaná revestiría un valor inestimable para los Estados Unidos con fines mercantiles y como base naval, comparando su trascendencia potencial con la de Gibraltar. Además, el extracto describió la zona dotada de un suelo feraz y un saludable clima tropical, accesible desde Nueva York en cuatro singladuras por vapor.

records.headline: The naval station made over to the United States by the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The naval station made over to the United States by the Dominican Republic is described by the Evening Post, in a description the Press reprints under the heading 'Our Newest Possessions.' It is situated on the south side of the peninsula of Samana, in the island of Hayti. The bay of Samana is almost completely land-locked, forty-three miles long by eight in width, with an entrance but three miles wide; it is capacious enough to contain any fleet that might be collected, and its shape affords a harbor where vessels can anchor with perfect safety. The Yuna, the largest river of Hayti, empties into its western end, and the small town of Santa Barbara stands on its northern shore.
records.summary_es: La estación naval cedida a los Estados Unidos por la República Dominicana es descrita por el Evening Post, en una descripción que la Press reproduce bajo el título «Our Newest Possessions». Está situada en el lado sur de la península de Samaná, en la isla de Haití. La bahía de Samaná está casi completamente cerrada por tierra, con cuarenta y tres millas de largo por ocho de ancho y una entrada de solo tres millas; es lo bastante capaz para contener cualquier flota que pudiera reunirse, y su forma ofrece un puerto donde los buques pueden anclar con perfecta seguridad. El Yuna, el río más grande de Haití, desemboca en su extremo occidental, y el pequeño pueblo de Santa Bárbara se encuentra en su costa norte.

records.summary_en: According to the *New-York Tribune* on October 4, 1867, the peoples of Hayti and the Dominican Republic recognized that union was necessary to maintain their independence and prosperity, following past experience and Spanish intervention. A treaty—awaiting only the ratification of the Dominican Congress—had its preliminaries signed six days after the arrival of six delegates sent by President Balnave, amidst great enthusiasm from the government and people. The treaty's articles provided for the suppression of frontier brigandage and the extradition of political refugees, a commitment by both parties to preserve the inviolability of their respective territories (ruling out any United States purchase of the Bay of Samaná), and the settlement of claims arising from injuries sustained during the 1844 separation.
records.summary_es: Según el *New-York Tribune* del 4 de octubre de 1867, los pueblos de Haití y de la República Dominicana reconocieron la imperiosa necesidad de la unión para preservar su independencia y prosperidad tras las lecciones del pasado y la intervención española. Se firmaron las bases de un tratado —pendiente solo de la ratificación del Congreso dominicano— a los seis días del arribo de seis delegados comisionados por el presidente Salnave, en medio del fervor popular y oficial. Los artículos del convenio pactaban la represión del bandolerismo fronterizo y la extradición de asilados políticos, el solemne compromiso de ambas partes de salvaguardar la inviolabilidad de sus territorios respectivos (descartando cualquier adquisición estadounidense de la bahía de Samaná) y la indemnización de reclamaciones por perjuicios sufridos durante la separación de 1844.

records.headline: A Dominican concession printed by the Tribune settles its disputes
records.summary_en: A Dominican concession printed by the Tribune settles its disputes in the courts of the Dominican Republic: disputes between the grantee and the government, or between the grantee and any other party, are to be settled by those courts. Another camel road is to be opened from Santiago de los Caballeros to the port of Monte Cristo, to expedite the transfer of copper ore from the mines of the interior to the coast; the constructors may open branch roads in any direction, extend the road to Santo Domingo City, and navigate the river Yaque by steamers, and they hold the right of converting the camel road into a railroad at a future period. Messrs. Joseph W. Fabens and James R. Young, of New York City, are the principals in the undertaking. The paper also prints a correspondence between Mr. Martin F. Hood, of London, and the Secretary of the Interior on the conditions under which foreigners will be allowed to work the mines in Santo Domingo: the old law that required foreigners going to St. Domingo to work in the mines to become naturalized citizens has been abrogated, and they are now as free to work in the mines as the natives, without changing their nationality.
records.summary_es: Una concesión dominicana publicada por el Tribune resuelve sus disputas en los tribunales de la República Dominicana: las disputas entre el concesionario y el gobierno, o entre el concesionario y cualquier otra parte, serán resueltas por esos tribunales. Se abrirá otro camino de camellos desde Santiago de los Caballeros hasta el puerto de Monte Cristi, para facilitar el traslado del mineral de cobre desde las minas del interior hasta la costa; los constructores podrán abrir caminos ramales en cualquier dirección, extender el camino hasta la ciudad de Santo Domingo y navegar el río Yaque en vapores, y tienen asegurado el derecho de convertir el camino de camellos en ferrocarril en el futuro. Los señores Joseph W. Fabens y James R. Young, de la ciudad de Nueva York, son los principales de la empresa. El periódico publica además una correspondencia entre el Sr. Martin F. Hood, de Londres, y el secretario del Interior sobre las condiciones en que se permitirá a los extranjeros trabajar las minas en Santo Domingo: la antigua ley que exigía que los extranjeros que fueran a Santo Domingo a trabajar en las minas se naturalizaran ciudadanos ha sido derogada, y ahora son tan libres como los naturales para trabajar en las minas, sin cambiar su nacionalidad.

records.headline: Among its articles is one providing for the suppression of brigandage
records.summary_en: A newly signed treaty between Haiti and St. Domingo includes articles providing for the suppression of frontier brigandage, the extradition of political refugees, the preservation of territorial integrity, and the settlement of claims dating from the 1844 separation. Because the treaty pledges that no portion of either territory will be alienated, the newspaper notes there is no longer any hope of the United States acquiring the bay of Samana by purchase. The agreement, initiated by Salnave's government and welcomed by the Dominican people, aims to heal 23 years of strife and is already benefiting the region through peace and resource development.

records.full_text: Another article of the treaty pledges the contracting parties to preserve inviolate the integrity of their respective territories. No portion of either Hayti or St. Domingo is on any account to be alienated. This being so, there is now no hope of the United States becoming the owner by purchase of the bay of Sanana. Cabral was, we are aware, willing to part with it, but the Dominicans would not allow him to do so; and so long as the treaty between the two republics remains in force it is clearly impossible that our government can acquire a foot of land in any part of the island, for it provides that both republics shall unite to repel any attempt on the part of any foreign Power to take possession of a single foot of territory in any part of the island. And the Dominicans and Haytiens, however bitterly they may hate each other, will readily unite to prevent a foreign Power from obtaining a lodgement on the soil of St. Domingo.

General Cabral, at all events, has ordered the Minister lately sent to Port au Prince to exchange the ratifications of the treaty to suspend all relations with Salnave's government, and leave the Haytien territory without delay. HAVANA, Nov. 17—We have the announcement that St. Domingo City has been destroyed, probably by an earthquake. I have telegraphed for details, which I shall forward at once.

The news of the insurrection in Hayti is confirmed. On the 12th of October the scene in the legislative chambers was very violent, and the language used was of the most threatening character. It all arose from a motion made to relieve Montes, who is in a Cape Haytien dungeon. The members all spoke in his defence. It is said Prince Salnave became so audacious as to secretly incite a rabble of women and boys to attack the House of Assembly. This they did with loud vivas for Salnave and cries of “Down with the Assembly,” hurling at the same time bricks, bottles, sticks, &c. The dwellings of many were vigorously stoned. The American consul was fired at, but escaped unhurt. A unanimous protest of the diplomatic corps has been presented against any further repetition of such scenes, and demanding of the government to see to it that the like does not again occur. At last accounts the city of Port au Prince was quieting. The treaty with the United States is as yet in suspense.

records.summary_en: A Havana press dispatch reported that a tremendous hurricane struck St. Domingo on October 30, lasting four hours, destroying nearly all harbor shipping and Commerce street in St. Domingo city, and causing two hundred deaths, though no American vessels were reported lost. Additionally, a dispatch from Havana stated that the treaty with St. Domingo had been annulled, the Haytian Minister had returned, revolutionary movements were rife with Dominican forces on the Haytian frontier, and an intended issue of $600,000 in bonds was unpopular.

ST. DOMINGO.

SPECIAL TELEGRAM TO THE HERALD.

Terrific Hurricane—Destruction of Property on Land and Afloat.

HAVANA, Nov. 18, 1867.

A terrible hurricane blew over the island on the 30th of October. It desolated the capital and destroyed two hundred lives. The hurricane lasted four hours and destroyed nearly all the shipping in harbor. No American vessels are reported. Comercio street, St. Domingo city, is in ruins. There was no news from the interior.

LATE FROM HAYTI.

The Dominican Government had recalled its Minister to Hayti, in consequence of an insurrectionary outbreak in the district of Cibao, in Santo Domingo, wnich the Dominican authorities believed had been instigated by the Haytians. The Haytian Government, in delivering his passports to the Minister, Gen. Valvende, had addressed a note to him, assuring him of the sincere desire of the Haytians for peace, and that whatever aid had been given the Dominican insurgents had been given by the Haytian rebels. Gen. Cabral, however, had notified the Haytian Government that relations between the two countries were suspended, and President Salnave had issued a proclamation reciting the facts of the dispute, and declaring that if the Dominicans made war, the Haytians were ready.

records.headline: The Spy, discussing the sister republic of St. Domingo, holds
records.summary_en: The Spy, discussing the sister republic of St. Domingo, holds that the spirit of the Dominican population is decidedly opposed to American aggression, on account of the past treatment of the colored race in this country, and that on that account alone the efforts of the State Department to purchase the bay of Samana have proved abortive: the financial difficulties of the Dominican government would long ago have induced it to dispose of a portion of its territory but for a public opinion that would at once become a deadly enemy of the administration, and even the cause of rebellion against it. In this dilemma, it relates, the Dominican cabinet entered into negotiation with the Paris banking house of Erlanger & Co.: the firm was to open a subscription in France for a loan of two millions and a half of dollars in gold, one tenth of the amount to be guaranteed by the house if the subscription had little success in Europe, its advances to be guaranteed in securities on the custom-house duties of the republic. The government of Cabral indignantly refused to accept the proposition, though the country's financial difficulties may yet compel the administration to come to terms.
records.summary_es: El Spy, al tratar de la república hermana de Santo Domingo, sostiene que el espíritu de la población dominicana se opone decididamente a la agresión americana, a causa del trato pasado dado a la raza de color en este país, y que solo por esa razón han resultado infructuosos los esfuerzos del Departamento de Estado por comprar la bahía de Samaná: las dificultades financieras del gobierno dominicano lo habrían inducido hace mucho a desprenderse de una porción de su territorio si no fuera por una opinión pública que se convertiría de inmediato en enemiga mortal de la administración, e incluso en causa de rebelión contra ella. En este dilema, refiere, el gabinete dominicano entró en negociación con la casa bancaria parisina Erlanger & Co.: la casa abriría una suscripción en Francia para un empréstito de dos millones y medio de dólares en oro, cuya décima parte garantizaría la propia casa si la suscripción tuviera poco éxito en Europa, y sus anticipos serían garantizados con valores sobre los derechos de aduana de la república. El gobierno de Cabral se negó indignado a aceptar la proposición, aunque las dificultades financieras del país podrían aún obligar a la administración a llegar a un acuerdo.

records.headline: Conflicting reports of Cabral's defeat and Báez's proclamation
records.summary_en: Conflicting reports of Cabral's defeat and Báez's proclamation are printed in the Herald's St. Domingo telegrams of December 23–24. A press telegram from Santo Domingo of December 20 announces that Cabral's government has been defeated, owing to the defective organization of his troops; that a pronunciamiento of the people against him has been issued and Báez proclaimed President; and that a commission is going to Washington to complete arrangements for the transfer of the bay of Samana to the United States. Later advices from Santiago de Cuba report that well-informed persons there doubt the news of the defeat of General Cabral's forces, as well as the announcement of a pronunciamiento in favor of ex-President Báez. From Santo Domingo City the paper also reports that Señor Pujol, still at Santiago, was expected there and is to offer the lease of Samana for ninety-nine years; that in the Legislative Chamber the ten-million-franc loan recently negotiated in Paris was approved; and that Consul Savage, on a telegram from the American consul at Santiago de Cuba, has telegraphed Secretary Seward advising him to defer further proceedings in relation to the St. Thomas purchase.
records.summary_es: Informes contradictorios sobre la derrota de Cabral y la proclamación de Báez se publican en los telegramas del Herald sobre Santo Domingo, de fechas 23 y 24 de diciembre. Un telegrama de prensa de Santo Domingo, del 20 de diciembre, anuncia que el gobierno de Cabral ha sido derrotado, a causa de la defectuosa organización de sus tropas; que se ha emitido un pronunciamiento del pueblo en su contra y Báez ha sido proclamado presidente; y que una comisión va a Washington a ultimar los arreglos para la transferencia de la bahía de Samaná a los Estados Unidos. Avisos posteriores de Santiago de Cuba reportan que personas bien informadas allí dudan de la noticia de la derrota de las fuerzas del general Cabral, así como del anuncio de un pronunciamiento en favor del expresidente Báez. Desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo el periódico informa además que el señor Pujol, todavía en Santiago, era esperado allí y va a ofrecer el arrendamiento de Samaná por noventa y nueve años; que en la Cámara Legislativa fue aprobado el empréstito de diez millones de francos negociado recientemente en París; y que el cónsul Savage, a raíz de un telegrama del cónsul americano en Santiago de Cuba, ha telegrafiado al secretario Seward aconsejándole diferir las gestiones relativas a la compra de Santo Tomás.

While the provinces of St. Domingo, Cibao, Azua, and Samana remained tranquil, General Hungria's Baecist revolution continued to make progress in the northern part of the republic. From St. Domingo.

HAVANA, Dec. 6.—Evening.—Señor Pujol is not at all reserved as to the commission which he bears. It is to close negotiations in relation to Samana. He will leave here to-morrow by the steamer Morro Castle for New York.

General Cabral's position is thought to be desperate, through the influence of the clergy, and the fact that the Dominican troops have not been paid. Baez will probably be President within a few weeks.

records.headline: The resignation of part of Cabral’s Cabinet had been accepted, and
records.summary_en: News from San Domingo reports that Señor Pujol will leave for New York by the steamer Moro Castle to close negotiations in relation to Samaná, and that part of President Cabral's cabinet has resigned, with Valverde, Curiel and Perdomo appointed to fill the vacancies. Congress has sanctioned a new civil code and a reorganization of the judiciary, the French loan has been disapproved, and extraordinary powers have been conferred on Cabral, while in the north the Baezist revolution under General Hungría is still making progress and the provinces named are tranquil.
records.summary_es: Las noticias de Santo Domingo informan que el señor Pujol partirá hacia Nueva York en el vapor Moro Castle para cerrar las negociaciones relativas a Samaná, y que parte del gabinete del presidente Cabral ha dimitido, con Valverde, Curiel y Perdomo nombrados para cubrir las vacantes. El Congreso ha aprobado un nuevo código civil y una reorganización del poder judicial, el empréstito francés ha sido desaprobado y se han conferido poderes extraordinarios a Cabral, mientras en el norte la revolución baecista bajo el general Hungría sigue avanzando y las provincias mencionadas están tranquilas.

records.headline: A Dominican mission has arrived at Washington from New York
records.summary_en: A Dominican mission has arrived at Washington from New York, the Herald's correspondent reports: Colonel Juan Macías, of the Dominican army, is among them, and General Pujol informed the correspondent that he is vested with plenary powers to negotiate. The object of the visit is to lay before Secretary Seward, by instructions from President Cabral, a proposition to sell the peninsula and bay of Samana to the United States. The terms of the purchase are two million dollars cash down and three hundred thousand dollars per annum for fifty years, the government of St. Domingo reserving to itself one fifth of the proceeds from the various mines on the peninsula — a stipulation General Pujol has the option of waiving if the sale can be better facilitated by it. At the expiration of the fifty years the peninsula becomes the fee-simple property of the United States, the total cost being seventeen millions.
records.summary_es: Una misión dominicana ha llegado a Washington procedente de Nueva York, reporta el corresponsal del Herald: el coronel Juan Macías, del ejército dominicano, figura entre sus miembros, y el general Pujol informó al corresponsal que está investido de plenos poderes para negociar. El objeto de la visita es presentar al secretario Seward, por instrucciones del presidente Cabral, una proposición para vender la península y la bahía de Samaná a los Estados Unidos. Los términos de la compra son dos millones de dólares en efectivo de contado y trescientos mil dólares anuales durante cincuenta años, reservándose el gobierno de Santo Domingo una quinta parte de los productos de las distintas minas de la península, estipulación que el general Pujol tiene la opción de renunciar si con ello se facilita mejor la venta. Al expirar los cincuenta años, la península pasará a ser propiedad plena y absoluta de los Estados Unidos, con un costo total de diecisiete millones.

It was expected that Cabral would soon announce his abdication; Báez was at Curaçao, and his arrival at Puerto Plata was daily expected.

Se esperaba que Cabral anunciara pronto su abdicación; Báez se encontraba en Curazao y su llegada a Puerto Plata se esperaba a diario.

records.headline: Domingo and Hayti was immicent, in fact, had already broken out
records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that war between St. Domingo and Hayti was imminent and had effectively broken out following the Haytian capture of the Dominican schooner *Copotille*, which was accused of supplying the Cacos rebels. The Haytian government declared a state of war after seizing papers signed by General Cabral that encouraged the rebels, while Cabral's agent failed to secure a loan for firearms from ex-President Geffrard in Kingston. Additionally, it was believed that Salnave was retaliating by assisting the Baez party in St. Domingo with money and arms.

El gobierno de Puerto Príncipe decretó el estado de guerra tras incautar pliegos suscritos por el general Cabral alentando a los alzados, al tiempo que el enviado de Cabral fracasaba en Kingston al gestionar ante el expresidente Geffrard un crédito para comprar fusiles. Se estimaba asimismo que Salnave tomaba represalias aprovisionando con fondos y pertrechos a la facción de Báez en Santo Domingo.

SANTO DOMINGO.

SPECIAL TELEGRAM TO THE HERALD.

Baezist Policy—Samana to be a Free Port—An Alliance with Hayti.

HAVANA, April 27, 1868.

The steamer Pajaro del Oceano, Captain Ochoa, has arrived here with advices from St. Domingo to the 20th inst.

Although General Baez had taken the usual oath as President of the republic, Congress was endeavoring so to amend the Constitution during its present session as to confirm the leading points of General Baez' policy. These were the following:— To make Samaná a free port of entry and a general foreign mail station. To arrange the mail and trade service at Samaná so that it should form a neutral station and become the centre of the Caribbean telegraphic cable service.

A brother of General Baez and General Caminero had gone to Hayti to negotiate for a permanent alliance between both republics. According to the proposed terms of the new alliance all disputed territory shall contribute *provisionally* a line of division. But such neutral provinces shall be bound to complete the geological and mineralogical survey of their respective limits. The general survey of the respective republics thus completed shall specify the situation and value of the gold and silver mines and of the debts secured by guaranties of such mines.

The general banker, Jesurun, and Colonel Fabens have been charged with the negotiation of a loan to be secured by the revenues from customs of the Dominican republic.

records.headline: A letter from Santo Domingo City, dated April 18, reports the March session of Congress
records.summary_en: A letter from Santo Domingo City, dated April 18, reports the March session of Congress, at which Generals Hungría and Luciano appeared and resigned the ample faculties entrusted to them by the interior towns, after the Secretary of the Interior had read to the body their message declaring the calamities brought upon the republic by the administration of Cabral. Congress at once reinvested the generals with the same faculties, to continue until the arrival and induction into office of President Báez — a sequence the writer says entirely refutes the misrepresentations sent from the capital to certain journals of the island of Cuba, stating that President Báez would not return. The letter adds that the government of the United States is about to get the Bay of Samaná on its own terms, and will not, therefore, take over the island of St. Thomas as it intended.
records.summary_es: Una carta desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo, fechada el 18 de abril, informa de la sesión de marzo del Congreso, en la que los generales Hungría y Luciano comparecieron y renunciaron a las amplias facultades que les habían sido confiadas por los pueblos del interior, después de que el secretario del Interior hubiera leído ante la cámara el mensaje de los generales en el que declaraban las calamidades traídas a la república por la administración de Cabral. El Congreso volvió a investirlos de inmediato con las mismas facultades, para que continuaran hasta la llegada y toma de posesión del presidente Báez, secuencia que, según el corresponsal, refuta por completo las falsas versiones enviadas desde la capital a ciertos periódicos de la isla de Cuba, según las cuales el presidente Báez no regresaría. La carta añade que el gobierno de los Estados Unidos está a punto de obtener la bahía de Samaná en sus propios términos y que, por tanto, no tomará la isla de Santo Tomás como se había previsto.

records.headline: The Free Trader recounts the history of the guano claims at Alto Velo.
records.summary_en: The Free Trader recounts the history of the guano claims at Alto Velo. Americans who had been taking guano from the island were ejected by the Dominican government, which asserted its jurisdiction, and the parties then sought a contract with that government for permission to ship guano and claimed damages. Secretary of State Jeremiah S. Black refused to notice the claim for damages until the United States agent at St. Domingo should have ascertained and reported the grounds upon which the Dominican government had asserted its jurisdiction; before the answer was received, Black had ceased to be Secretary of State and had been succeeded by Mr. Seward, and the rebellion and the war, various revolutions in the Dominican Republic, and war between that government and Hayti postponed any consideration of the claims. When the question was raised again, the department answered that two parties of Americans had claimed the island as discoverers, that St. Domingo had asserted a title and ejected the claimants, and that it declined to give any encouragement to Americans to resort there for guano without first obtaining the consent of St. Domingo.
records.summary_es: El Free Trader relata la historia de las reclamaciones por el guano de Alto Velo. Los estadounidenses que extraían guano de la isla fueron expulsados por el gobierno dominicano, que afirmó su jurisdicción, y los interesados buscaron entonces un contrato con ese gobierno para obtener permiso de embarcar guano, reclamando además daños y perjuicios. El secretario de Estado Jeremiah S. Black se negó a atender la reclamación de daños hasta que el agente de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo averiguara e informara sobre los fundamentos en que el gobierno dominicano había basado su jurisdicción; antes de que llegara la respuesta, Black había cesado como secretario de Estado y había sido sucedido por el señor Seward, y la rebelión y la guerra, varias revoluciones en la República Dominicana y la guerra entre ese gobierno y Haití pospusieron toda consideración de las reclamaciones. Cuando la cuestión se planteó de nuevo, el departamento respondió que dos grupos de estadounidenses habían reclamado la isla como descubridores, que Santo Domingo había afirmado un título y expulsado a los reclamantes, y que se negaba a dar estímulo alguno a los estadounidenses para acudir allí por guano sin obtener primero el consentimiento de Santo Domingo.

records.headline: An editorial in the Republican reviews the Alto Velo guano claim
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Republican reviews the Alto Velo guano claim: parties from Baltimore say they discovered guano upon the island of Alto Velo, lying about twenty miles south of the southernmost promontory of the island of San Domingo or Hayti, claimed it as not at the time the property or under the sovereignty of any government, and began to open and remove the valuable deposits, until in October an armed vessel of the Dominican Republic removed them. Their attorney, Judge Jeremiah S. Black, has ever since been urging their claims at Washington, either to obtain compensation or to induce the government to take forcible possession of the island, in defiance of the weak and distracted republic which assumes sovereignty over it. The Republican attributes Black's break with President Johnson — his withdrawal from the President's defense in the impeachment trial, and his present war on Mr. Seward — to the refusal of both to interfere in his behalf in this claim; it notes that the Court of Claims has likewise decided that the case is without any merit, and warns that four of the impeachment managers have committed themselves to a recommendation of what it calls this preposterous claim.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en el Republican examina la reclamación del guano de Alto Velo: interesados de Baltimore dicen que descubrieron guano en la isla de Alto Velo, situada a unas veinte millas al sur del promontorio más meridional de la isla de Santo Domingo o Haití, la reclamaron como si en aquel momento no fuera propiedad ni estuviera bajo la soberanía de gobierno alguno, y comenzaron a abrir y extraer los valiosos depósitos, hasta que en octubre un buque armado de la República Dominicana los retiró. Su abogado, el juez Jeremiah S. Black, ha urgido desde entonces las reclamaciones en Washington, ya sea para obtener una indemnización o para inducir al gobierno a tomar posesión forzosa de la isla, en desafío de la débil y atribulada república que asume la soberanía sobre ella. El Republican atribuye la ruptura de Black con el presidente Johnson — su retiro de la defensa del presidente en el juicio político y su guerra actual contra el señor Seward — a la negativa de ambos a intervenir en su favor en esta reclamación; observa que la Corte de Reclamaciones ha decidido igualmente que el caso carece por completo de mérito, y advierte que cuatro de los fiscales del juicio político se han comprometido a recomendar lo que califica de reclamación disparatada.

ST. DOMINGO.

Carlos and Valentin Baez have lately been in Hayti on a confidential mission, offering, it is said, a treaty of great and self-evident advantages to both republics. It proposes to establish a liberal and uniform tariff, place all the frontier ports under a common system of regulations, and open a free and unreserved transit of merchandise from one to the other.

This would open a large and valuable trade across the frontier to both parties, and do away with the ruinous smuggling that has heretofore enriched a few border chiefs at the expense of both treasuries.

ST. DOMINGO.

The Reactionary Forces at Work Against Baez—His Brother Held by the Haytien Cacos—Interesting Review of the Situation—Dominican Speculators on Their Way to the United States.

ST. DOMINGO, May 20, 1868.

Several Dominican generals recently made the island of St. Thomas a rendezvous. Among them were Cabral, Luperon, Embert, Adon, Pina, Ricardo, Fernandez and Pimentel. They concerted a plan of operations against Baez. The result was that ex-President Cabral sailed for Jacmel May 15 on board the English steamer. He is to take command of the revolutionists along the southern frontier—in San Juan, Neyba, Las Matas, Cercado, Barahona, &c. The chieftains Timoteo and Andres Ogando, Sico Moreno, Damian Castillo and Mariano Rodriguez sent a young man named Abelard Dubreuil through Haytien territory to meet General Cabral. Baez and his partisans, as well as Cazneau, represent that this movement in the south is in favor of President Salnave. This is like what such would report to carry out their own schemes.

General Luperon went to Turks Island so as to operate against the north of this republic—the provinces of Cibao—whither the people call him as their leader. He will there meet Generals Polanco, Alvarez and many others who await his arrival to pronounce against General Baez.

General Pimentel is to go from Curaçao in company with General Castillo, Linares, Valverde and others to operate against Seybo and St. Domingo provinces, in which neighborhood they are to meet the brave General Manzueta, whom Baez has been unable to put down, either with threats or promises or by the imprisonment of his family. He kept in the vicinity of Llamasá, a district in St. Domingo province, and never ceased fighting the Baezists.

General Baez does not know how to get his government into working order, as the employes resign almost immediately after appointment. They all regard Baez's government as illegal and transitory, and no one is willing to compromise himself therewith. This is the reason why Señor F. M. Delmonte has not accepted the portfolio that Baez has tendered him, although he has been urged and besought to accept it.

By letters from St. Thomas we have learned that the Cacos hold Carlos Baez a prisoner. He was on his way to Salnave's government for the purpose of selling that portion of Dominican territory bounded on the south by the Rio Yaqui. This sale was the condition by which Baez agreed with Salnave's Minister, Delorme, for the aid which the latter would give in overthrowing Cabral. The western portion of the island, the Haytien side, has no savannas nor pasture lands to raise cattle. From the Rio Pedernales, whence the dividing line goes, according to the Aranjuez treaty of 1777, to the Rio Yaqui there are magnificent bays, which the Haytiens have always coveted without ever having taken the measures to secure so valuable a portion of our island. To fulfil this part of his engagements Baez has had to mutilate our constitution by dropping the article which points out the limits of the republic as well as the clause which creates the office of Vice President. Baez wants absolute power, and as the constitution of 1865 is very liberal and controlled the President's action while it abolished the death penalty in political cases, he has substituted the constitution of 1854, which makes him master and lord over the Dominicans and imposes capital punishment for political offences. This same substitution he attempted in 1865, when he came to power, but before he could carry it out he was overthrown and had to take refuge in the French Consulate.

Baez has also presented to Congress a bill of his expenses during the revolution that has just brought him to power, but out of decorum they have not made public the amount. The following is the only allusion to it made in the reply of Congress to the President's message:—"As to the detailed accounts of the revolutionary outlays which have been presented by the worthy General Buenaventura Baez, they are entirely approved, as well as the agreement entered into with Señores J. A. Jesurun & Zoons of the neighboring island of Curaçao, which amounts to $37,145 80, which is approved in all its tenor and conditions."

So many documents and mortgages will be secured by Baez in the names of Jesurun, Fabens and Cazneau that, even if the peninsula of Samana were sold for ten times its value, the proceeds could not liquidate all the claims that he will have on the treasury of the republic. In connection with this trio of speculators it is very positively asserted here that Jesurun and Fabens are authorized by Baez to raise a loan of $200,000 in the United States, on account of Samana. This money is needed to improve Baez's situation, at least until such time as the bay and peninsula of Samana can be disposed of for good. I do not think these rumors can be well founded, as Jesurun and Fabens left here on April 20 and Baez was inaugurated only on May 2. The Boletin Oficial of that date attacked such a project, and brought severe charges against ex-President Cabral for having sought to alienate Samana. What is certain, however, is, that whatever engagements those gentlemen make in the United States are null and of no validity, as they are not authorized by government legally constituted. Baez has been proclaimed by a faction who overthrew Cabral without electing Baez in a constitutional manner through popular suffrage, as the constitution then in force required. The latter has seated himself in the Presidential chair in spite of the will of the majority, and has imprisoned, exiled and persecuted the most distinguished citizens of the republic.

ST. DOMINGO.

Precarious State of the New Government—The Reaction Organized—Expected Invasion from Venezuela—Health of the Island, &c.

ST. THOMAS, July 14, 1868.

The news from St. Domingo confirms the impression that the government of General Baez is by no means secure. While it is ostensibly master of the country, there is an under-current of deep dissatisfaction, which must soon burst forth into open rebellion.

The leaders of the movement in the south are anxiously waiting to see the north and east take up arms. A simultaneous movement in all sections was the plan agreed upon at St. Thomas, so that the strongest force could be directed against Azua and thence on to St. Domingo City.

General Cabral was expected to land on the southern coast with a well-equipped expedition from Venezuela. Should he succeed in effecting a landing, there is little doubt that the whole south would rally to his support. The health of the island, however, is good.

THE NEWS.

EUROPEAN.

The steamship City of Baltimore, from Liverpool via Queenstown, arrived at this port yesterday.

The public mind in England was very much occupied with the approaching general election.

Accounts from the manufacturing districts of England and Scotland were unfavorable.

The London money market was easy and the stock market steady.

DOMESTIC.

The steamship Morro Castle, from Havana, brings later advices from Hayti and St. Domingo.

Salnave was still holding Port-au-Prince, which was being besieged by the revolutionary forces.

Salnave is directing the defence in person. He has received the American Minister with every mark of kindness. Baez was offering the bay and peninsula of Samana as security for a loan of $1,000,000 from the United States.

records.headline: A letter from St. Domingo City, dated July 4, reports the campaign
records.summary_en: A letter from St. Domingo City, dated July 4, reports the campaign against Báez in the north and in the south, under headlines that also speak of threats against the lives of those who negotiate the sale or lease of Samaná. General Polanco has taken the field against President Báez, while besides him Generals Ogando, Andújar, Moreno and others are operating in the south under the immediate command of ex-President Cabral himself; the government troops that are encamped at Azua make no attack upon them, but keep strictly on the defensive, and meanwhile the insurgents are doing all they can to make a connection with the northern rebels, so as to commence a combined movement forwards. General Luperón, who is commander-in-chief of the revolutionists, left St. Thomas June 30 for Jacmel, accompanied by General Pedro Valverde and Colonel Antonio Madrigal, intending to take command in the north; Generals Pimentel and others also sailed from St. Thomas on the 30th for Turk's Island. In Seibo and San Cristóbal some attempts at insurrection have taken place, and Báez has sent commissioners to see if he can succeed in putting a stop to the trouble.
records.summary_es: Una carta desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo, fechada el 4 de julio, informa de la campaña contra Báez en el norte y en el sur, bajo titulares que hablan también de amenazas contra la vida de quienes negocien la venta o el arrendamiento de Samaná. El general Polanco ha entrado en campaña contra el presidente Báez, mientras que, junto a él, los generales Ogando, Andújar, Moreno y otros operan en el sur bajo el mando inmediato del propio expresidente Cabral; las tropas del gobierno acampadas en Azua no los atacan y se mantienen estrictamente a la defensiva, y mientras tanto los insurgentes hacen todo lo posible por enlazar con los rebeldes del norte para iniciar un movimiento combinado de avance. El general Luperón, comandante en jefe de los revolucionarios, salió de Santo Tomás el 30 de junio hacia Jacmel, acompañado del general Pedro Valverde y el coronel Antonio Madrigal, con la intención de tomar el mando en el norte; los generales Pimentel y otros zarparon también de Santo Tomás el día 30 hacia la isla Turca. En Seibo y San Cristóbal ha habido algunos intentos de insurrección, y Báez ha enviado comisionados para ver si logra poner fin a los disturbios.

Government troops at Azua stay on the defensive while towns desert, prisoners are taken at Higuey, and the capital lives in alarm as money runs out and Baez cannot find men willing to fight.

records.headline: The Tribune's special correspondent writes from Puerto Plata
records.summary_en: The Tribune's special correspondent writes from Puerto Plata, July 5, that the threatened invasion of St. Domingo by ex-President Cabral and the exiled generals of his party, Luperón, Polanco and others, has taken place: Cabral, after passing through Hayti under shelter of the arms of the Cacos, has crossed the frontiers and is at Banica with a considerable force of men, while General Ramírez Báez and Colonel Le Mar, each at the lead of a large body of troops, have been sent against him, and in Santiago, which has been threatened by Polanco, the authorities are rapidly organizing a military force to resist him. The correspondent reports the manifesto the malcontent generals have published, addressed to the people of St. Domingo, setting forth that the revolutionists are not animated by a spirit of vengeance, but that it is absolutely necessary to the peace and prosperity of the country that Báez should be removed from the presidency — that should he abdicate power, dissensions may speedily be healed, but if he resists their demands a general civil war is imminent. In the city of St. Domingo great disquiet prevails in consequence of the imminency of another desperate struggle; the prisons, it is said, are full, and one of the prisoners has been tried by a council of war and sentenced to death, but an appeal has been made to the Supreme Court, where it is expected the sentence will be reversed.
records.summary_es: El corresponsal especial del Tribune escribe desde Puerto Plata, el 5 de julio, que la amenazada invasión de Santo Domingo por el expresidente Cabral y los generales exiliados de su partido, Luperón, Polanco y otros, ya se ha producido: Cabral, tras pasar por Haití al amparo de las armas de los cacos, ha cruzado la frontera y se encuentra en Banica con una considerable fuerza de hombres, mientras que el general Ramírez Báez y el coronel Le Mar, cada uno al frente de un numeroso cuerpo de tropas, han sido enviados contra él, y en Santiago, amenazada por Polanco, las autoridades organizan rápidamente una fuerza militar para resistirlo. El corresponsal reproduce el manifiesto publicado por los generales descontentos, dirigido al pueblo de Santo Domingo, en el que exponen que los revolucionarios no están animados por un espíritu de venganza, pero que es absolutamente necesario para la paz y la prosperidad del país que Báez sea apartado de la presidencia: que si abdica del poder, las disensiones podrán curarse pronto, pero que si se resiste a sus demandas, una guerra civil general es inminente. En la ciudad de Santo Domingo reina gran inquietud ante la inminencia de otra lucha desesperada; se dice que las cárceles están llenas, y uno de los prisioneros ha sido juzgado por un consejo de guerra y sentenciado a muerte, pero se ha presentado una apelación ante la Corte Suprema, donde se espera que la sentencia sea revocada.

EXPECTED ATTACK ON PORT-AU-PRINCE.

ADVVICES FROM HAYTI.

Salnave Still Defending the Capital—The American Minister—The Cacos Approaching.

Advices from Port-au-Prince to the 10th ult. report that the revolutionary forces under Salnave's opponents were closing around the city.

The President was on the best of terms with the American Minister, Mr. Hollister, who was using his influence and his best efforts to have peace restored to the country. It was rumored at Port-au-Prince that the general in command at Cape Hayti had deserted to the Cacos.

General Baez, President of the Dominican Republic, had offered the bay and peninsula of Samana to the United States as security for a loan of $1,000,000, which he was anxious to obtain from our government.

records.headline: An account reprinted in the Avis, beginning in the middle of the report
records.summary_en: An account reprinted in the Avis, beginning in the middle of the report, describes the forces gathered together for the purpose of overthrowing the government: in the centre stands a general in command of a column, and he is one of the most implacable enemies of Báez; on the frontiers of the south General Ogando, Moreno and others have risen; on the frontiers of the north General Polanco had also taken up arms against the government. There is no doubt that Báez will fall very soon, the account says, for public opinion is very unfavorable to him, and he is detested on account of his tendency to sell the country to the Spaniards or Americans. The revolution is imminent, and it is very probable that General Luperón, who is the chief of the movements in operation in the Dominican Republic, will come to power; Luperón is now in Christiansted on his way to St. Domingo, and is attended by some of his friends.
records.summary_es: Un relato reproducido en el Avis, que comienza a mitad del informe, describe las fuerzas reunidas con el propósito de derrocar al gobierno: en el centro se halla un general al mando de una columna, uno de los enemigos más implacables de Báez; en las fronteras del sur se han sublevado los generales Ogando, Moreno y otros; y en las fronteras del norte el general Polanco también ha tomado las armas contra el gobierno. No hay duda de que Báez caerá muy pronto, dice el relato, pues la opinión pública le es muy desfavorable y es detestado por su tendencia a vender el país a los españoles o a los estadounidenses. La revolución es inminente, y es muy probable que el general Luperón, jefe de los movimientos en curso en la República Dominicana, llegue al poder; Luperón se encuentra ahora en Christiansted, de camino a Santo Domingo, acompañado de algunos de sus amigos.

records.headline: A column of advices reports that a battle took place on the 24th of July
records.summary_en: A column of advices reports that a battle took place on the 24th of July, between the revolutionists and the forces of Salnave, which ended in a victory for the former; that the revolutionists have concentrated 4,000 troops, well provided with provisions and ammunition, around the city of Port-au-Prince, and are pressing on with renewed vigor; that General Lynch, a revolutionary commander, has issued a manifesto protesting against the cession of any Haytien territory to the United States; that the Dominican troops have crossed the frontier and commenced the invasion of Hayti; and that a general and his son had been murdered, with robberies and depredations reported in various parts of the country. Advices from St. Domingo represent the revolutionary movement against Báez as steadily progressing, under the leadership of General Luperón; a decisive victory has been gained by one of his generals, and the speedy fall of Báez, and the expulsion of his government, is anticipated.
records.summary_es: Una columna de noticias informa que el 24 de julio tuvo lugar una batalla entre los revolucionarios y las fuerzas de Salnave, que terminó con la victoria de los primeros; que los revolucionarios han concentrado 4.000 tropas, bien provistas de víveres y municiones, alrededor de la ciudad de Puerto Príncipe, y avanzan con renovado vigor; que el general Lynch, comandante revolucionario, ha publicado un manifiesto en el que protesta contra la cesión de cualquier territorio haitiano a los Estados Unidos; que las tropas dominicanas han cruzado la frontera y comenzado la invasión de Haití; y que un general y su hijo habían sido asesinados, con robos y depredaciones reportados en varias partes del país. Las noticias de Santo Domingo presentan el movimiento revolucionario contra Báez en progreso constante, bajo la jefatura del general Luperón; uno de sus generales ha ganado una victoria decisiva, y se anticipa la pronta caída de Báez y la expulsión de su gobierno.

records.headline: A dispatch from St. Domingo
records.summary_en: A dispatch from St. Domingo City, dated July 11, 1868, reports that rebel General Timoteo Ogando routed the government forces at Ceiba, killing General Brigman, and that an alarmed President Baez placed two cannons before his house and ordered forty prominent citizens, including men he had held in prison, to leave the country. It also reports aid and money reaching Baez from Curacao, Dominican exiles sailing from there under General Aybar, government troops living off the cattle of private owners, and whole companies deserting on the march.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo, fechado el 11 de julio de 1868, informa que el general rebelde Timoteo Ogando derrotó a las fuerzas del gobierno en Ceiba, dando muerte al general Brigman, y que un alarmado presidente Báez colocó dos cañones ante su casa y ordenó a cuarenta ciudadanos prominentes, incluidos hombres que había tenido presos, que abandonaran el país. También informa de ayuda y dinero que llegaban a Báez desde Curazao, de exiliados dominicanos que zarparon de allí bajo el mando del general Aybar, de tropas gubernamentales que vivían del ganado de propietarios privados y de compañías enteras que desertaban en la marcha.
records.passage: from Curacao to the Rebels? Crimes and Atrocities? Summary of Events. St. Domingo City, July 11, 1868. Yesterday there was great alarm in this city. The news which government has received in relation to its first reverses are deplorable. As I told you in my last letter, General Ramirez Baez had gone from Azua with a body of troops to take San Juan; but he put more reliance on the bravery of a German officer named General [Brightman?], as none of the Baez family—the President included—has ever been in an engagement. When the rebel commander, General Timoteo Ogando, learned this movement he advanced to meet General [Brightman?], and attacked him at Ceiba and completely routed his troops, leaving General [Brightman?] among the dead on the field. Immediately after having received news of this defeat the President ordered two cannons to be placed before the door of his house, as if the danger threatened him very closely. He also sent passports to forty prominent citizens, with orders to leave the country. He also banished Señores J. M. Perez, M. M. Santamaria, A. Brua, S. de Castro, R. Santin, T. Aguero, B. Medina, D. Henriquez, F. Duluc, F. Chain, and W. de Costa Gomez, whom he had held in prison. The Baezists state that government is preparing to send the families of the exiled [illegible] if this barbarous measure be carried out the city will be largely thinned of its population, as there are now scarcely eight thousand inhabitants here,

Baez is also awaiting a delayed European loan and pinning hopes on the sale of a tract of land to the United States for $2,000,000 through his agent, Colonel Fabeus, with the bargain reportedly already closed with Mr. Seward. Meanwhile, General Luperon has been proclaimed Commander-in-Chief of the impending rebellion to overthrow Baez.

Báez esperaba asimismo un demorado empréstito europeo y cifraba sus esperanzas en la enajenación de una franja de tierra a los Estados Unidos por 2.000.000 de dólares por mediación de su agente, el coronel Fabens, negocio presuntamente ya concertado con el secretario Seward. records.full_text:
ST. DOMINGO.

The Triumph of the Revolution Foreseen—Baez Looking to the United States for Help—Sale of Samana, &c.

ST. THOMAS, Nov. 14, 1868.

The latest accounts from St. Domingo show that the government of Baez is tottering to its fall. The people are thoroughly dissatisfied with his administration, and the leaders of the opposition are pushing their advantages in every direction.

Another hope for Mr. Baez is the sale of Samana to the United States for $2,000,000. Colonel Fabens, who is now in Washington, is said to be the agent of Baez for that purpose and, in fact, it is asserted that the bargain is already closed between Fabens and Mr. Seward.

Whether this be true or not, it is certain that Baez looks to the United States as his only salvation, and that he is willing to make any sacrifice of territory to retain power.

records.headline: A private letter from Santo Domingo denounces the Baez administration, saying its efforts to obtain gold through the Samana
records.summary_en: A private letter from Santo Domingo denounces the Baez administration, saying its efforts to obtain gold through the Samana negotiation, a Spanish protectorate and foreign loans have failed, while ruinous contributions are exacted from the people. It describes cattle seized in the province of La Vega and sold in Santiago, with the money then presented in La Vega as part of a foreign loan, and it lists arrests, forced contributions, the exile of 22 political prisoners on the schooner Dos Hermanos, and executions in Azua.
records.summary_es: Una carta privada desde Santo Domingo denuncia a la administración de Báez y dice que sus esfuerzos por obtener oro mediante la negociación de Samaná, un protectorado español y préstamos extranjeros han fracasado, mientras se exigen contribuciones ruinosas al pueblo. Describe ganado incautado en la provincia de La Vega y vendido en Santiago, cuyo dinero fue presentado después en La Vega como parte de un préstamo extranjero, y enumera arrestos, contribuciones forzadas, el exilio de 22 presos políticos en la goleta Dos Hermanos y ejecuciones en Azua.
