records.summary_en: In a conversation with senators on Friday, the President urged the ratification of the treaty to acquire San Domingo, warning that otherwise the territory might be offered to a European government, thereby undermining the Monroe Doctrine. He presented evidence that the majority of the people voted for annexation and that insurrectionary leaders, whose rebellion lacked strength after being cut off from Hayti, were not inherently opposed to it. Furthermore, the President expressed his belief that acquiring San Domingo would immediately benefit U.S. commerce and the Darien canal, while potentially leading to broader territorial control of the Gulf islands.
records.summary_es: En conferencia con senadores el viernes, el presidente encareció la pronta ratificación del tratado para incorporar a Santo Domingo, advirtiendo de que, en caso contrario, dicho territorio podría ser brindado a una potencia europea en quebranto de la doctrina Monroe. Exhibió pruebas de que la generalidad de la ciudadanía sufragó a favor de la anexión y de que los caudillos insurrectos, cuyas fuerzas languidecían al quedar desasistidos desde Haití, no repudiaban la medida en esencia. Manifestó asimismo su convicción de que la anexión de Santo Domingo acarrearía inmediatos provechos al tráfico marítimo estadounidense y al proyectado canal del Darién, franquando de paso el control de las islas del Golfo.

records.full_text:
THE PRESIDENT'S ANXIETY.

Persistence is a prime quality, and General Grant has always been credited with a considerable share of it. He is illustrating it just now in the manner he sticks to and urges the ratification of the San Domingo treaty—very shrewdly, too. All the reasons he presents to senators and representatives—and not a day passes but we learn of conversations held with them—are based on the public and political advantages which belong to the acquisition. In the conversation had with senators on Friday last, at the capitol, the president urged the ratification of the treaty upon the ground, among others, that if we failed, the people of San Domingo could, and probably would, offer themselves and territory to some European government, being determined to obtain security and prosperity. The president asked how, in that case, could we make the Monroe doctrine operative. He presented evidence and reports from San Domingo which went toward establishing the fact that the great body of the people had voted for annexation. That the insurrectionary leaders were not opposed per se to such annexation was shown by official copies of documents in the Dominican records, proving that Cabral and others had made similar advances to those carried out by Baez. It is not the doing, but the management that they fight. The insurrection had but little strength, being cut off by Admiral Poor's remonstrance to the Saget government from such supplies as they had expected from Hayti.

records.headline: A Santo Domingo letter of March 13, brought by the steamer Tybee
records.summary_en: A Santo Domingo letter of March 13, brought by the steamer Tybee, reports that the Secretary of State will receive the official notification of the Dominican people's decisive wish to incorporate their country with the United States: the national vote opened on February 10, by February 20 it was positively known at the capital that an immense majority of the entire adult population had declared for annexation, and by February 27, the anniversary of independence, the official returns had certified the result, which was announced at the President's levee by the Minister of Foreign Relations to the consular corps and dignitaries; the minister also addressed the crowd in the palace reception saloon, in a speech whose translation the Herald says was forwarded to it.
records.summary_es: Una carta de Santo Domingo del 13 de marzo, traída por el vapor Tybee, informa que el secretario de Estado recibirá la notificación oficial del deseo decisivo del pueblo dominicano de incorporar su país a los Estados Unidos: la votación nacional se abrió el 10 de febrero; para el 20 ya se sabía positivamente en la capital que una inmensa mayoría de toda la población adulta se había declarado por la anexión, y para el 27, aniversario de la independencia, las actas oficiales habían certificado el resultado, anunciado en la recepción del presidente por el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores al cuerpo consular y a los dignatarios; el ministro también se dirigió a la multitud en el salón de recepciones del palacio, en un discurso cuya traducción, dice el Herald, le fue enviada.

records.headline: Closing items of the Herald feature include the case of Mr. Hatch
records.summary_en: Closing items of the Herald feature include the case of Mr. Hatch, an American citizen imprisoned for some time, who will be taken to St. Domingo City and delivered to United States Consul Perry; the Hartmont loan has failed because the time for complying with its conditions expired, the sum already advanced — not legible in the printing — being secured by lands, mines and Alta Vela guano; the Telegrafo still remains at Tortola, the Báez government claiming the vessel on the ground that she committed acts of piracy in Dominican waters; and the district governor's address hails the votes in nearly all the provinces authorizing negotiations to place the country under the protection of the United States, while business is reported very good and provisions scarce.
records.summary_es: Las notas finales del reportaje del Herald incluyen el caso del señor Hatch, ciudadano estadounidense preso desde hace algún tiempo, que será llevado a la ciudad de Santo Domingo y entregado al cónsul estadounidense Perry; el préstamo Hartmont fracasó porque expiró el plazo para cumplir sus condiciones, y la suma ya adelantada —no legible en la impresión— está garantizada por tierras, minas y guano de Alta Vela; el Telégrafo permanece aún en Tórtola, pues el gobierno de Báez reclama el buque por actos de piratería en aguas dominicanas; y el discurso del gobernador del distrito celebra los votos de casi todas las provincias que autorizan negociar para colocar el país bajo la protección de los Estados Unidos, mientras el comercio se reporta muy bueno y escasas las provisiones.

records.summary_en: The *Chicago Tribune* reported on March 26, 1870, that the public lands of San Domingo are nearly all private property with titles rooted in violence, and characterized President Baez as a brutal adventurer seeking to sell his country to escape justice. The newspaper argued that it is not the mission of the United States to buy foreign nations to improve their condition, warning that doing so would set a boundless precedent while burdening Americans with more debt and taxes.
records.summary_es: El *Chicago Tribune* afirmó el 26 de marzo de 1870 que las tierras baldías de Santo Domingo constituían casi en su totalidad propiedades particulares con títulos cimentados en la violencia, tachando al presidente Báez de déspota aventurero que buscaba malvender la patria para esquivar la acción de la justicia. La publicación alegó que no correspondía a los Estados Unidos comprar estados foráneos con miras a redimirlos, previniendo que tal medida sentaría un funesto precedente cargando a los contribuyentes con mayores empréstitos e impuestos.

records.full_text:
"President" Baez is a cowardly and brutal adventurer, who, having run his career of assassination and despotism, seeks escape from the avenging arm of justice by selling his country and his countrymen for money to a foreign government. It is no answer to say that the Dominicans will be better off as part of the American Republic than they now are. It is no part of the "mission" of the United States to buy foreign peoples to improve their condition. We are surrounded with others scarcely less wretched than the Dominicans. Once admit that it is our duty to buy all unhappy nations whose people may be bettered by the change, and where shall we stop? Mexico, and Central America, Spain, Ireland, Paraguay, Rome, Turkey, Japan, and China, appeal to us even more strongly than San Domingo.

But the effect of the treaty upon San Domingo is not of the least importance compared with the effect upon ourselves. Are we ever to get out of debt? Are we ever to have a reduction of taxes? We have covered up $7,500,000 in the eternal snows of Alaska. A proposition to bury an equal sum under the volcanic rocks of St. Thomas is still pending,—and so borne down by debt that we are paying a tax of 108 per cent.

records.headline: A Cincinnati Commercial correspondent calls the San Domingo business a job and a swindle, saying a treaty for annexation
records.summary_en: A Cincinnati Commercial correspondent calls the San Domingo business a job and a swindle, saying a treaty for annexation was signed on November 29 without the Dominican people knowing anything about it. He says the United States gave the Baez party $150,000 without authority from Congress, along with warships and artillery, signed one treaty leasing Samana for fifty years at $150,000 a year and another for annexation, and under the annexation treaty would pay over a million dollars and assume the republic's indebtedness.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal del Cincinnati Commercial califica el asunto de Santo Domingo de maniobra y estafa, y dice que un tratado de anexión se firmó el 29 de noviembre sin que el pueblo dominicano supiera nada al respecto. Afirma que los Estados Unidos entregaron al partido de Báez 150.000 dólares sin autorización del Congreso, junto con buques de guerra y artillería, firmaron un tratado que arrienda Samaná por cincuenta años a 150.000 dólares al año y otro de anexión, y que bajo el tratado de anexión pagarían más de un millón de dólares y asumirían la deuda de la república.

Franco argued the annexation vote was fraudulent, citing an insurrection in Puerto Plata, the imprisonment of over 200 political dissidents in Santo Domingo, and active resistance led by General Cabral across the southern and northern provinces.

records.full_text:
A DOMINICAN OFFICER'S REPLY TO GEN. TATE.

Col. G. X. Franco, a Dominican officer, writes to THE TRIBUNE in reply to to Gen. Tate, who, as the embassador of Salnave, he regards as the natural enemy of Gen. Cabral. Regarding the annexation vote he says: "That the vote in favor of annexation is legal is false. This is proved by the insurrection of the people at Puerto Plata, their manifesto against annexation, and the blood that flowed upon the occasion." Col. Franco further says the statement made by Gen. Tate that "Cabral has only a few hundred men" is false. "Cabral has thousands of the best men of the Republic in his ranks, and holds the whole of the Province of the South, which contains from 35,000 to 40,000 inhabitants. In that part of the Republic there are 14 different communities. In the North, Gens. Pimentel, Cabrera, Valerio, and others are operating, and now hold eight settlements. They have, likewise, a large number of soldiers. In the East there are many political refugees, who are, every now and then, fighting the Government troops. In the Homenage Fortress at San Domingo are imprisoned more than 235 persons. Does Gen. Tate think that a country can be legally annexed under such circumstances?"

records.headline: A San Domingo annexation bill failed again to gain consideration
records.summary_en: A San Domingo annexation bill failed again to gain consideration in Washington, and its sponsor was to make another attempt the next day under a suspension of the rules: the bill provides for the annexation of St. Domingo as the Territory of Dominica, with the consent of the Dominicans, and for the payment of $1,850,770, and no more, to liquidate the debt of the new Territory.
records.summary_es: Un proyecto de anexión de Santo Domingo volvió a no lograr consideración en Washington, y su autor haría otro intento al día siguiente bajo suspensión de las reglas: el proyecto dispone la anexión de Santo Domingo como Territorio de Dominica, con el consentimiento de los dominicanos, y el pago de $1,850,770, y no más, para liquidar la deuda del nuevo Territorio.

Currier, the Dominican Consul General at New York: the acts contain 15,110 signatures for annexation to 111 against, the largest vote cast in the republic for twenty-six years; the only material opposition, it says, is on the Haytian frontier, where lawless bands are accused of guerrilla tactics and of being instigated by the British and Spanish consuls at Port au Prince to defeat annexation.

Baez was forced to choose between Europe and the United States. European friends, and even European mediation for his relief from Hayti, were certainly within his reach, but not compatible with the proposed relations at Washington. In this dilemma President Grant assumed the responsibility of retaining the Dominican State within the American system. records.summary_en: The translated Dominican presidential message in this window argues that existing interests point to the United States as the natural protector of the Dominican republic, that the desire of leading political figures in the provinces brought the two cabinets into closer union and led to two contracts with a Washington commission, and that selling Samaná alone could not secure the country's future: whatever sum it brought would assure only a short existence and might awaken claims that, if satisfied, would frustrate economic salvation or, if thwarted, breed rebellion — a point the large property-holders and lovers of peace understood.
records.summary_es: El mensaje presidencial dominicano traducido en esta ventana sostiene que los intereses existentes señalan a los Estados Unidos como protector natural de la república dominicana, que el deseo de figuras políticas importantes de las provincias acercó a los dos gabinetes y condujo a dos contratos con una comisión de Washington, y que vender Samaná por sí sola no podría asegurar el futuro del país: cualquier suma obtenida garantizaría solo una existencia breve y podría despertar pretensiones que, de satisfacerse, frustrarían la salvación económica o, de frustrarse, engendrarían rebeliones — punto que entendieron los grandes propietarios y los amantes de la paz.

records.headline: Mr. Perry's long
records.summary_en: Mr. Perry's long communication to Secretary Fish was read to the Senate's special committee, in which Perry said he had acted only for the interests of the United States and of President Grant's policy. He reported being told that Cazneau was running the whole Dominican government and represented large land interests, and he described the negotiations with President Baez, including a proposal, which he protested, to draw up two separate papers, one to control the election in St. Domingo and another for the United States government.
records.summary_es: La larga comunicación del Sr. Perry al secretario Fish fue leída ante el comité especial del Senado, y en ella Perry dijo que había actuado solo por los intereses de los Estados Unidos y de la política del presidente Grant. Informó que le habían dicho que Cazneau dirigía todo el gobierno dominicano y representaba grandes intereses de tierras, y describió las negociaciones con el presidente Báez, incluida una propuesta, contra la que protestó, de redactar dos documentos separados, uno para controlar la elección en Santo Domingo y otro para el gobierno de los Estados Unidos.

records.headline: This editorial fragment, opening in mid-argument, urges annexation
records.summary_en: This editorial fragment, opening in mid-argument, urges annexation as a war measure against Spain: with St. Domingo annexed, Spanish Cuba will be flanked by American guns, and the acquisition of Samaná, a strategic point commanding the Antilles, will show Spain that the United States is prepared for war; once St. Domingo is under the American flag, the paper argues, even Spanish arrogance will hardly venture a quarrel, the surest way to prevent war being to show that you are prepared for it.
records.summary_es: Este fragmento editorial, que se abre a mitad de un argumento, insta a la anexión como medida de guerra contra España: con Santo Domingo anexado, la Cuba española quedará flanqueada por cañones estadounidenses, y la adquisición de Samaná, punto estratégico que domina las Antillas, mostrará a España que los Estados Unidos están preparados para la guerra; una vez Santo Domingo bajo la bandera estadounidense, sostiene el diario, ni la arrogancia española se atreverá apenas a una querella, pues el modo más seguro de evitar la guerra es mostrar que se está preparado para ella.

records.headline: This window opens with Senate testimony on Dominican sentiment
records.summary_en: This window opens with Senate testimony on Dominican sentiment: an unnamed witness says he mingled with the people at Samaná, Puerto Plata and twenty or thirty miles back from St. Domingo City to learn their sentiment; that Cabral and all his party are in favor of annexation but want to have a hand in it, a judgment he bases on conversations with Cabral's strongest friends in the city; and that any party opposing annexation in possession of the island would be too weak to make organized opposition, two-thirds or three-fourths of the inhabitants being in favor; the window then opens the testimony of Babcock, a United States engineer officer stationed at Washington since the close of the war, who went to St. Domingo first in July as a special agent with written instructions from the State Department.
records.summary_es: Esta ventana se abre con testimonio senatorial sobre el sentir dominicano: un testigo sin nombre dice que se mezcló con el pueblo en Samaná, Puerto Plata y veinte o treinta millas hacia el interior desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo para conocer su sentir; que Cabral y todo su partido están a favor de la anexión, pero quieren tener parte en ella, juicio que basa en conversaciones con los amigos más firmes de Cabral en la ciudad; y que cualquier partido opuesto a la anexión, en posesión de la isla, sería demasiado débil para oponer resistencia organizada, pues dos tercios o tres cuartos de los habitantes están a favor; la ventana abre luego el testimonio de Babcock, oficial del cuerpo de ingenieros del Ejército de los Estados Unidos, estacionado en Washington desde el fin de la guerra, que fue a Santo Domingo por primera vez en julio como agente especial, con instrucciones escritas del Departamento de Estado.

records.headline: One-third of the Dominican domestic debt consists of arrears
records.summary_en: One-third of the Dominican domestic debt consists of arrears due to the soldiers and civil employees of the government, this Chicago Tribune window, opening in mid-argument, warns — arrears owed to men reconciled to the lease of Samaná and afterward to annexation by the promise of payment from the United States; it says that after paying the foreign debt of $300,000 and deducting the Samaná advance, probably $1,000,000 would remain toward the national indebtedness, and that something less than $600,000 would pay off the arrears and the depreciated paper currency — once forced on soldiers and civilians as pay, fallen below half a cent to the dollar, and packed away by country people in boxes to await the day of settlement.
records.summary_es: Un tercio de la deuda interna dominicana consiste en atrasos debidos a los soldados y empleados civiles del gobierno, advierte esta ventana del Chicago Tribune, que se abre a mitad de un argumento — atrasos debidos a hombres reconciliados con el arrendamiento de Samaná y después con la anexión por la promesa de pago de los Estados Unidos; dice que, después de pagar la deuda externa de $300,000 y deducir el anticipo de Samaná, probablemente quedaría $1,000,000 para la deuda nacional, y que algo menos de $600,000 pagaría los atrasos y el papel moneda depreciado — impuesto antes a soldados y civiles como paga, caído a menos de medio centavo por dólar y guardado por cajas por la gente del campo a la espera del día de la liquidación.

records.headline: Baez, Fablos, and Cazeneau proposed to make Babcock a grant of
records.summary_en: The *Chicago Tribune* reported on the negotiations involving Babcock, Sackett, Fablos, Cazeneau, and Baez, noting that the final treaty closely resembled the one drafted in the U.S. State Department. According to the excerpt, Babcock and Sackett rejected Cazeneau's proposal for a secret treaty, and Babcock declined a land grant at Samana offered to him by Baez, Fablos, and Cazeneau. The report also details Babcock's correspondence with Cazeneau—shared with President Grant—and actions regarding the American flag and coaling station at Samana following the treaty's signing.
records.summary_es: El *Chicago Tribune* dio cuenta de las negociaciones mantenidas entre Babcock, Sackett, Fabens [Fablos], Cazneau [Cazeneau] y Báez, señalando que el texto final del tratado concordaba sustancialmente con el redactado en el Departamento de Estado de los Estados Unidos. Conforme al extracto, Babcock y Sackett desestimaron la propuesta de Cazneau de concertar un tratado secreto, en tanto que Babcock declinó una concesión de tierras en Samaná que le brindaron Báez, Fabens y Cazneau. La relación detalla además la correspondencia sostenida entre Babcock y Cazneau —elevada al presidente Grant— y las resoluciones sobre el izamiento del pabellón estadounidense y la instalación del apostadero de carbón en Samaná tras la firma del convenio.

SAN DOMINGO.

The Senate refused, at 1 o'clock, to go into executive session for the purpose of taking up the San Domingo treaty, and decided to go on with the Tax bill.

records.headline: The Herald editorializes on the Senate inquiry into Mr. Hatch's claim
records.summary_en: The Herald editorializes on the Senate inquiry into Mr. Hatch's claim against the Báez government, an inquiry that has brought up the whole Dominican question and the overtures for annexation: whatever Hatch's guilt or innocence of opposing annexation among the Dominicans, the prominent fact, it argues, is that an American citizen was imprisoned, tried and sentenced to death without cause yet shown, while prominent officials knew of it by written and verbal notice and apparently winked at the outrage; had he been a British subject, Báez would never have imprisoned him, and the editorial closes by noting Hatch's arrival on the steamer De Soto from Havana, suffering nervous prostration from his incarceration.
records.summary_es: El Herald editorializa sobre la investigación senatorial de la reclamación del señor Hatch contra el gobierno de Báez, investigación que ha sacado a relucir toda la cuestión dominicana y las gestiones de anexión: sea Hatch culpable o inocente de oponerse a la anexión entre los dominicanos, el hecho prominente, sostiene, es que un ciudadano estadounidense fue preso, juzgado y condenado a muerte sin causa mostrada hasta ahora, mientras funcionarios prominentes lo sabían por avisos escritos y verbales y aparentemente hicieron la vista gorda; si hubiera sido súbdito británico, Báez nunca lo habría apresado, y el editorial cierra notando la llegada de Hatch en el vapor De Soto, desde La Habana, aquejado de postración nerviosa por su encarcelamiento.

records.headline: President Grant's letter of June 27, printed here, answers an inquiry
records.summary_en: President Grant's letter of June 27, printed here, answers an inquiry about General Babcock's mission: Babcock did not exceed Grant's written or verbal instructions in connection with the Confidential Basis; he was sent to San Domingo to ascertain the wishes of the Dominican people and government as to annexation and, if he found them favorable, the terms on which they desired it; the Confidential Basis he brought back was not binding on either government unless each chose to continue the negotiations, and was null and void unless accepted and carried into effect; Grant also directed the Navy Secretary to have the commander of the United States steamer Seminole seize the Telegrafo on the high seas and send her to Baltimore for adjudication, she having interfered with American merchant shipping, and he closes that Babcock's conduct meets his entire approval.
records.summary_es: La carta del presidente Grant del 27 de junio, aquí impresa, responde a una consulta sobre la misión del general Babcock: Babcock no excedió las instrucciones escritas ni verbales de Grant en relación con la Base Confidencial; fue enviado a Santo Domingo a averiguar los deseos del pueblo y del gobierno dominicanos en cuanto a la anexión y, si los hallaba favorables, los términos en que la deseaban; la Base Confidencial que trajo consigo no obligaba a ninguno de los dos gobiernos salvo que cada uno decidiera continuar las negociaciones, y era nula si no se aceptaba y se llevaba a efecto; Grant también ordenó al secretario de Marina que el comandante del vapor estadounidense Seminole apresara al Telégrafo en alta mar y lo enviara a Baltimore para adjudicación, por haber interferido con la navegación mercante estadounidense, y cierra afirmando que la conducta de Babcock merece su aprobación entera.

records.headline: The Free Press quotes a committee-report sentence on the Hatch case
records.summary_en: The Free Press quotes a committee-report sentence on the Hatch case — that it cannot say he can establish no just claim against the 'Republic of Dominica' — and remarks that, as Dominica is a little island belonging to Great Britain and a very different thing from San Domingo or the Dominican Republic, Mr. Hatch will probably doubt whether he can establish a claim, just or otherwise, against it.

records.headline: Among the Free Press's items is a toast drunk at a recent dinner
records.summary_en: Among the Free Press's items is a toast drunk at a recent dinner at Port au Prince in honor of the British chargé d'affaires in Hayti, and warmly received there: 'Senator Sumner, the man whose eloquence has thus far prevented the annexation of San Domingo — may his pleadings in favor of the autonomy of St. Domingo prove to the Congress of the United States that the Haytians and the Dominicans desire ardently to preserve their independence, and not to annex themselves to any great power.'
records.summary_es: Entre las notas del Free Press figura un brindis pronunciado en una cena reciente en Puerto Príncipe en honor del encargado de negocios británico en Haití, y acogido allí con calor: «El senador Sumner, el hombre cuya elocuencia ha impedido hasta ahora la anexión de San Domingo — que sus alegatos en favor de la autonomía de Santo Domingo prueben al Congreso de los Estados Unidos que los haitianos y los dominicanos desean ardientemente preservar su independencia, y no anexarse a ninguna gran potencia».

records.headline: A war in Dominica might embroil the world, the Herald argues
records.summary_en: A war in Dominica might embroil the world, the Herald argues in this editorial fragment: opening in mid-argument, it denies as untrue an offensive and defensive alliance between China and Hayti — in which case Russia, the friend and ally of St. Domingo because of Dominican friendliness to the United States, would make a demonstration on China's northern boundary — professes no opinion on Hindustan, and argues that with the great numbers of Chinese and Japanese immigrants in the West Indies the question of war in Dominica deserves grave consideration, the window closing in mid-sentence.
records.summary_es: Una guerra en Dominica podría envolver al mundo, sostiene el Herald en este fragmento editorial: abriéndose a mitad de un argumento, niega por falsa una alianza ofensiva y defensiva entre China y Haití —caso en el cual Rusia, amiga y aliada de Santo Domingo por la amistad dominicana hacia los Estados Unidos, haría una demostración en la frontera norte de China—, no profesa opinión sobre el Indostán y sostiene que, con el gran número de inmigrantes chinos y japoneses en las Indias Occidentales, la cuestión de la guerra en Dominica merece grave consideración; la ventana se cierra a media frase.

records.headline: Ample power to renew negotiations with the American Government for a
records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported on August 4, 1870, that the Dominican government retained ample power to renew annexation negotiations with the United States and propose modifications to address opponents' objections. It noted that the U.S. protectorate had been extended for one year from July 1, 1870, providing the Dominicans with a guaranteed shield against internal revolution, tensions with Hayti, and European intervention. Additionally, the newspaper stated that President Baez and his ministers expressed regret over attacks against President Grant and General Babcock regarding the affair, while dismissing charges made against themselves by unfamiliar critics.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó el 4 de agosto de 1870 que el gobierno dominicano conservaba plenas facultades para reanudar las negociaciones de anexión con los Estados Unidos y proponer modificaciones encaminadas a salvar los reparos de la oposición. Destacó que el protectorado estadounidense había sido prorrogado por un año a partir del 1 de julio de 1870, brindando a los dominicanos un escudo garantizado frente a revoluciones intestinas, desavenencias con Haití e intervenciones europeas. Además, el periódico consignó que el presidente Báez y sus ministros lamentaron los ataques dirigidos contra el presidente Grant y el general Babcock a propósito de este asunto, desestimando los cargos que detractores desconocidos formularon en su contra.

records.full_text: Col. Fabens (who was the bearer to this Government of the news of the rejection of the treaty) returns in the Tybee to the United States, and in his capacity of Dominican Minister to Washington he is clothed with ample power to renew negotiations with the American Government for a treaty of annexation, and to propose such modifications of the old treaty as circumstances may demand, in order to meet within reasonable limits the objections of the opponents of the measure. It is some consolation to the Dominicans, under the disappointment which naturally they feel at the turn things have unexpectedly taken, that the United States protectorate of this country has been extended for one year from the 1st July, 1870; for this is a guarantee to them of immunity thus far, both from intestine revolutionary troubles and foreign invasion. Their relations with Hayti are not at present of the most friendly kind, but they feel that while this protectorate lasts they are safe from troubles in that quarter, and also that no European Power will presume to repeat the experiment which Spain tried a few years ago.

records.summary_en: Advices received from St. Domingo report that war between the governments of St. Domingo and Hayti is imminent. records.headline: The Herald's remedy for St. Domingo's troubles is annexation
records.summary_en: The Herald's remedy for St. Domingo's troubles is annexation: Cabral is doing his utmost to embarrass President Báez, with President Saget of Hayti expected to aid Cabral because Báez favors the Salnave party against Saget, and the only way to end these bloody dissensions, the paper argues, is the annexation of either one or both of the island's republics to the United States; the lost opportunity to acquire St. Domingo on fair terms is regretted, and with it under the American flag, the paper claims, the disturbances convulsing Haytians and Dominicans would finally end and a rich, fruitful tract be added to the Union.
records.summary_es: El remedio del Herald para los trastornos de Santo Domingo es la anexión: Cabral hace todo lo posible por embarazar al presidente Báez, con la expectativa de que el presidente Saget, de Haití, ayude a Cabral porque Báez favorece al partido de Salnave contra Saget, y el único modo de poner fin a estas sangrientas disensiones, sostiene el diario, es la anexión de una o de ambas repúblicas de la isla a los Estados Unidos; lamenta la oportunidad perdida de adquirir Santo Domingo en términos justos y afirma que, bajo la bandera estadounidense, cesarían por fin los trastornos que convulsionan a haitianos y dominicanos y se añadiría a la Unión una tierra rica y fructífera.

records.headline: A letter from Don Apolinar de Castro quotes the latest advices from the capital, Santo Domingo, dated the 14th
records.summary_en: A letter from Don Apolinar de Castro quotes the latest advices from the capital, Santo Domingo, dated the 14th, confirming the arrival of Cabral on the northern frontier, where he was received with enthusiasm. The advices report the firm position of Generals Adon and the Ogandos, who will soon march on Azua, a deepening division in Baez's party since Hungria's withdrawal from the ministry, and an irreparable lack of means to carry on the government.
records.summary_es: Una carta de don Apolinar de Castro cita las últimas noticias de la capital, Santo Domingo, fechadas el día 14, que confirman la llegada de Cabral a la frontera del norte, donde fue recibido con entusiasmo. Las noticias informan de la firme posición de los generales Adón y los Ogando, que pronto marcharán sobre Azua, de una división cada vez mayor en el partido de Báez desde la retirada de Hungría del ministerio, y de una falta irreparable de medios para sostener el gobierno.

records.headline: Secretly aided by President Báez, plots against the Saget administration
records.summary_en: Secretly aided by President Báez, plots against the Saget administration open the Herald's survey of Haitian and Dominican troubles — grave frauds and counterfeited national bank notes in Hayti, with counterfeiters sentenced to death, and Spanish intrigue stirring up the enemies of annexation in St. Domingo — from which it asks why Congress acted so blindly on Dominican annexation: President Grant's West Indian policy, it argues, is wise and deserves fair consideration, the American people and merchants favor it, and when it is next taken up the legislature should respect the people's desires.
records.summary_es: Ayudados en secreto por el presidente Báez, los complots contra la administración Saget abren la revista que hace el Herald de los trastornos haitianos y dominicanos —graves fraudes y billetes del banco nacional falsificados en Haití, con falsificadores condenados a muerte, y la intriga española azuzando en Santo Domingo a los enemigos de la anexión—, de donde pregunta por qué el Congreso actuó tan ciegamente en la anexión dominicana: la política antillana del presidente Grant, sostiene, es sabia y merece consideración imparcial; el pueblo y los comerciantes estadounidenses la favorecen, y cuando vuelva a tratarse, la legislatura debería respetar los deseos del pueblo.

records.summary_en: Reports cited by the paper say the Cibao province was in arms against Baez, that Cabral's reported defeat may instead have been a victory, and that Baez had issued a decree on state warrants that angered merchants speculating in them. It adds that conservative and wealthy Dominicans hoped the United States would not abandon the annexation scheme while the people awaited President Grant's message.

Añade que los dominicanos conservadores y adinerados esperaban que Estados Unidos no abandonara el plan de anexión mientras el pueblo esperaba el mensaje del presidente Grant.

records.headline: In the Senate on December 9, Mr. Sumner of Massachusetts submitted
records.summary_en: In the Senate on December 9, Mr. Sumner of Massachusetts submitted a resolution asking the President to send the Senate all papers and correspondence relating to the proposed annexation of the Dominican portion of the island of St. Domingo or the purchase of any part of it. The resolution also calls for an account of the Dominican government's debt and liabilities, especially to Haiti, the constitutional provisions on selling the national domain, communications from Haiti, the instructions given to the American naval squadron, and information on President Baez's position and on how far he has been maintained in power by United States vessels of war; on Mr. Conkling's suggestion it was laid over temporarily and ordered printed.
records.summary_es: En el Senado, el 9 de diciembre, el señor Sumner de Massachusetts presentó una resolución pidiendo al Presidente que enviara al Senado todos los documentos y la correspondencia relativos a la anexión propuesta de la parte dominicana de la isla de Santo Domingo o a la compra de cualquier parte de ella. La resolución pide también una relación de la deuda y las obligaciones del gobierno dominicano, especialmente con Haití, las disposiciones constitucionales sobre la venta del dominio nacional, las comunicaciones de Haití, las instrucciones dadas a la escuadra naval estadounidense e información sobre la posición del presidente Báez y sobre hasta qué punto ha sido mantenido en el poder por buques de guerra de los Estados Unidos; a sugerencia del señor Conkling quedó sobre la mesa temporalmente y se ordenó su impresión.
records.passage: Washington, Dec. 9—Mr. Sumner (Mass.) submitted the following: Resolved, That the President of the United States be requested to communicate to the Senate, if in his opinion not incompatible with the public interests, copies of all papers and correspondence relating to the proposed annexation of the Dominican portion of the island of St. Domingo, or the purchase of any part thereof, including the original and all subsequent instruction to any agent or consul of the United States, with the correspondence of such agent or consul; also, any protocol or convention signed by such agent or consul. Also, an account of the debt and liabilities of the Dominican Government, especially its obligations to the neighboring republic of Hayti. records.headline: A Washington correspondent traces the history of the scheme to annex San Domingo, which the President is pressing
records.summary_en: A Washington correspondent traces the history of the scheme to annex San Domingo, which the President is pressing again, with General Butler expected to introduce the annexation resolutions in the House. He recounts how General Cazeneau had long promoted annexation, how General Babcock's treaty failed in the Senate, and how Secretary Fish had warned Babcock against Cazeneau because of the vast land concessions Cazeneau was known to have secured in the Bay of Samana and elsewhere.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal en Washington traza la historia del plan de anexionar Santo Domingo, que el presidente está impulsando de nuevo, y se espera que el general Butler presente las resoluciones de anexión en la Cámara. Cuenta cómo el general Cazeneau había promovido la anexión durante mucho tiempo, cómo el tratado del general Babcock fracasó en el Senado, y cómo el secretario Fish había advertido a Babcock contra Cazeneau por las vastas concesiones de tierras que se sabía que Cazeneau había conseguido en la bahía de Samaná y en otros lugares.

records.summary_en: The *Chicago Tribune* reported that the population of Dominica was originally opposed to annexation, and that a subsequent plebiscite revived by General Grant was a "perfect farce" in which Baez's soldiers seized and imprisoned anyone who voted against it. The newspaper noted that the Dominican Republic was engaged in a civil war with insurgents led by former President General Cabral controlling the countryside, and that annexation would saddle the United States with roughly fourteen million dollars in debt, including a 30,000,000-franc gold debt owed to Hayti.

records.full_text: The Republic of Dominica, although territorially embracing two-thirds of the island, has a population variously estimated at from 200,000 to 250,000, nearly all hybrids, Spanish and negro. General Grant sets the population at less than 100,000, but all other authorities place it at the higher figures. Hayti has a population of about 600,000, nearly all pure blacks, or with French blood intermingled. Hayti has paid France an indemnity of 60,000,000 francs, a moiety of which sum the Haytiens claim as due them by the San Dominicans; and by treaty between Hayti and San Domingo, it is provided that neither party shall alienate any portion of the territory. This fact is perfectly well known to the government here. I have before me a letter dated the 5th of February, 1868, addressed to "Hon. W. H. Seward, Secretary of State," by Louis Achille de Pitti-Fernandi, Consul of Hayti at New York, in which, by order of his government, he protests against any sale or transfer of any portion of the island; giving, among other reasons, the statement that he protests "in consequence of the existence of a treaty between the Government of Hayti and San Domingo, by which it is provided that no part of the island can be alienated by either of the two governments." In this letter the Haytien Consul also urges that at all events a vote of the inhabitants should be had—a plebiscite—and that at that time it was evident the population of Dominica was opposed to the annexation.

records.headline: Secretary Fish has done a good thing, the Chicago Tribune says
records.summary_en: Secretary Fish has done a good thing, the Chicago Tribune says: the President, referring in a rather incoherent manner to the Dominican Republic as Santo Domingo — that being the name of the whole island, including Hayti — was addressed through Secretary Fish by the Haytian Minister, remonstrating against the seizure of his end of the island; Fish returned the letter, endorsing it as impertinent in a minister to criticise the official language of the chief magistrate of the nation to which he is accredited — 'Fish is a dolphin,' the item concludes.
records.summary_es: El secretario Fish ha hecho una buena cosa, dice el Chicago Tribune: hace algún tiempo, el presidente, refiriéndose de modo algo incoherente a la República Dominicana como Santo Domingo —siendo ese el nombre de toda la isla, incluida Haití—, recibió por conducto del secretario Fish una protesta del ministro haitiano contra la ocupación de su extremo de la isla; Fish devolvió la carta, anotándola como impertinente en un ministro que critica el lenguaje oficial del magistrado supremo de la nación ante la cual está acreditado —«Fish es un delfín», concluye la nota.

records.headline: The paper reports Senator Sumner's Senate argument against annexation, saying he contended an unratified treaty
records.summary_en: The paper reports Senator Sumner's Senate argument against annexation, saying he contended an unratified treaty could give the United States no jurisdiction in Dominican waters and that exercising it was a usurpation and an act of war without Congress. It contrasts President Grant's annual message calling Senate rejection of the Dominican treaty folly with the Haitian president's anxieties over annexation.

Contrasta el mensaje anual del presidente Grant, que calificó de insensatez el rechazo del Senado al tratado dominicano, con las ansiedades del presidente haitiano por la anexión.

records.headline: In the Senate debate printed here, an amendment enlarging the investigation
records.summary_en: In the Senate debate printed here, an amendment enlarging the investigation to points other than St. Domingo was rejected, and a personal controversy followed over an alleged imputation on the President's honesty in connection with a pecuniary interest in lands in Dominica and over responsibility for a published report of a conversation between Sumner and a gentleman in Chicago, the report's truthfulness being denied; after an exchange in which one senator conceded that parts of the day's debate were not creditable, the Schurz amendment was adopted, and an amendment requiring the commissioners to be appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate was moved, the window closing during its advocacy.

records.headline: This Chicago Tribune editorial window, opening in mid-argument
records.summary_en: This Chicago Tribune editorial window, opening in mid-argument, argues against annexation: if the Republic of Dominica cannot last six weeks without civil war, if no authority is recognized there but the bayonet and life and liberty depend on the will of the faction leader of the moment, what invites the United States to incorporate so distant and squabbling a republic, when it has enough of reconstruction on its hands; it asks why Americans should incorporate a foreign people it describes in contemptuous terms as degraded, ignorant and speaking a different language, and it says the attempt to force the annexation of this Dominican Republic is being made as an administration measure at a present cost of several millions and a perpetual annual cost of twice as many, with the President, his official family, the Vice President and influential senators and representatives behind it — the window closing in mid-list.
records.summary_es: Esta ventana editorial del Chicago Tribune, que se abre a mitad de un argumento, se pronuncia contra la anexión: si la República de Dominica no puede durar seis semanas sin guerra civil, si allí no se reconoce autoridad alguna sino la bayoneta y la vida y la libertad dependen de la voluntad del caudillo de la facción dominante, ¿qué invita a los Estados Unidos a incorporar una república tan distante y pendenciera, cuando tiene bastante reconstrucción entre manos?; pregunta además por qué habría de incorporarse a un pueblo extranjero al que describe en términos despectivos como degradado, ignorante y de lengua distinta; y afirma que el intento de forzar la anexión de esta República Dominicana se impone como medida de la administración, a un costo presente de varios millones y un costo anual perpetuo del doble, con el presidente, su familia oficial, el vicepresidente y senadores y representantes influyentes detrás — y la ventana se cierra a media enumeración.

records.headline: The Spy prints the Senate's Santo Domingo commission resolution
records.summary_en: The Spy prints the Senate's Santo Domingo commission resolution, in its closing sections: the commissioners are to learn what grants, concessions and franchises have been given, and to whom, the terms on which the Dominican government desires annexation as a territory, and such other information as bears on the republic's future incorporation into the United States; they are to report to the President, who shall lay their report before Congress, and they are to serve without compensation beyond their expenses and a secretary's pay fixed by the Secretary of State with the President's approval. The Senate then adjourned at 6:45 in the morning until twelve, and on reassembling went into executive session after receiving the credentials of Mr. Jewett of Missouri, presented by Mr. Schurz, to fill temporarily the vacancy left by Mr. Drake's resignation.
records.summary_es: El Spy publica la resolución del Senado sobre la comisión de Santo Domingo, en sus secciones finales: los comisionados deberán averiguar qué donaciones, concesiones y franquicias se han otorgado, y a quiénes, los términos en que el gobierno dominicano desea la anexión como territorio, y cuanta otra información se refiera a la futura incorporación de la república a los Estados Unidos; deberán informar al Presidente, quien presentará su informe ante el Congreso, y servirán sin remuneración más allá de sus gastos y el sueldo de un secretario fijado por el secretario de Estado con la aprobación del Presidente. El Senado levantó entonces la sesión a las 6:45 de la mañana hasta las doce, y al reanudarla pasó a sesión ejecutiva tras recibir las credenciales del Sr. Jewett de Misuri, presentadas por el Sr. Schurz, para ocupar temporalmente la vacante dejada por la renuncia del Sr. Drake.

records.headline: The paper reports Senator Conkling defending the president against Sumner, arguing that mention of the whole island
records.summary_en: The paper reports Senator Conkling defending the president against Sumner, arguing that mention of the whole island in the annexation message did not menace Haitian independence. Conkling also disputed reports that Sumner had been threatened with personal violence by the president.
records.summary_es: El periódico informa que el senador Conkling defendió al presidente contra Sumner, argumentando que la mención de toda la isla en el mensaje de anexión no amenazaba la independencia haitiana. Conkling también disputó los informes de que Sumner había sido amenazado con violencia personal por el presidente.

records.headline: The Senate debate on the Santo Domingo commission resolution
records.summary_en: The Senate debate on the Santo Domingo commission resolution is reported by the Tribune: Mr. Schurz's amendment, to postpone all investigation until three months after the withdrawal of the United States naval force from San Domingo waters, was supported by Mr. Sumner on the ground that an expression of the popular will of the Dominican Republic, for or against annexation, should be uninfluenced by a pressure of bayonets — he cited with approval the English law forbidding a military force within a certain limit of an election poll, and argued that the amendment involved a great principle of constitutional liberty. Mr. Thurman of Ohio retorted that the principle had not been appreciated by the Senator from Massachusetts when he voted for the Fifteenth Amendment enforcement and naturalization bills authorizing the presence of the military at the polls in New-York and other states; and in a personal controversy that followed, Mr. Sumner admitted to Mr. Edmunds that when at the last session he became satisfied he could not support the treaty he ought to have communicated the fact to the President, and regretted not having done so — the extent, he said, of his offending, which did not justify the denunciation heaped upon him.
records.summary_es: El debate del Senado sobre la resolución de la comisión de Santo Domingo es reseñado por el Tribune: la enmienda del Sr. Schurz, de posponer toda investigación hasta tres meses después de la retirada de la fuerza naval de los Estados Unidos de las aguas de Santo Domingo, fue apoyada por el Sr. Sumner con el argumento de que una expresión de la voluntad popular de la República Dominicana, a favor o en contra de la anexión, debía estar libre de la presión de las bayonetas; citó con aprobación la ley inglesa que prohíbe una fuerza militar dentro de cierto límite de un colegio electoral, y sostuvo que la enmienda entrañaba un gran principio de libertad constitucional. El Sr. Thurman de Ohio replicó que el principio no había sido apreciado por el senador de Massachusetts cuando votó a favor de las leyes de ejecución de la Decimoquinta Enmienda y de naturalización que autorizaban la presencia de militares en los colegios electorales de Nueva York y otros estados; y en una controversia personal que siguió, el Sr. Sumner admitió ante el Sr. Edmunds que cuando en la sesión pasada se convenció de que no podía apoyar el tratado debió haber comunicado el hecho al Presidente, y lamentó no haberlo hecho: esa era, dijo, la medida de su falta, que no justificaba la denuncia acumulada sobre él.

records.headline: The catalogue of inquiries in the Santo Domingo commission resolution
records.summary_en: The catalogue of inquiries in the Santo Domingo commission resolution is printed by the Intelligencer, in a window opening midway through it: the physical, mental and moral condition of the Dominican people and their material wealth and industrial capacity; the country's resources in minerals, agriculture, the products of its waters and forests, the character and cultivable extent of its soil; its climate and health, its harbors and rivers, its meteorological character and remarkable phenomena; the government's debt and obligations, funded and admitted or unadjusted and in dispute; its treaties and engagements with other powers; the extent of its boundaries and territory, and what proportion is covered by foreign claimants or by grants of concessions, and generally what concessions or franchises have been granted, with the names of the grantees; the terms on which the Dominican government may desire annexation as a territory of the United States; and such other information as bears on the Dominican republic's future incorporation. By the resolution's second section the commissioners are to report to the President as soon as conveniently may be, and he shall lay their report before Congress.
records.summary_es: El catálogo de indagaciones de la resolución sobre la comisión de Santo Domingo es publicado por el Intelligencer, en una ventana que se abre a mitad del texto: la condición física, mental y moral del pueblo dominicano y su riqueza material y capacidad industrial; los recursos del país en minerales, agricultura, los productos de sus aguas y bosques, el carácter y la extensión cultivable de su suelo; su clima y salubridad, sus puertos y ríos, su carácter meteorológico y fenómenos notables; la deuda y las obligaciones del gobierno, consolidadas y reconocidas o no ajustadas y en disputa; sus tratados y compromisos con otras potencias; la extensión de sus límites y territorio, y qué proporción está cubierta por reclamantes extranjeros o por donaciones de concesiones, y en general qué concesiones o franquicias se han otorgado, con los nombres de los concesionarios; los términos en que el gobierno dominicano pueda desear la anexión como territorio de los Estados Unidos; y cuanta otra información se refiera a la futura incorporación de la república dominicana. Por la segunda sección de la resolución, los comisionados deberán informar al Presidente tan pronto como sea conveniente, y él presentará su informe ante el Congreso.

records.headline: The Spy traces the annexation scheme to the Cazneaus, heard of again
records.summary_en: The Spy traces the annexation scheme to the Cazneaus, heard of again in San Domingo after the collapse of the Confederacy and making propositions to Mr. Seward for its fulfilment, in an editorial window opening mid-sentence: the matter fell through then, and was revived on General Grant's accession, when a convention was drawn up under General Babcock, one of the President's young military secretaries, with Admiral Porter, in the Spy's phrase, as wet nurse, and Cazneau as interpreter. Mr. Fish, the editorial says, had particularly warned Babcock against Cazneau as a dangerous man mixed up in private schemes and speculations, who wanted only to make a cat's-paw of the United States to realize on the vast concessions of lands in the bay of Samaná and elsewhere that he had secured; but Babcock, ignorant of Spanish, gladly accepted the services of Cazneau, who was master of the situation and said what he liked — the window closing mid-sentence as it turns to Babcock's liking for the bay of Samaná.
records.summary_es: El Spy atribuye el plan de anexión a los Cazneau, de quienes se vuelve a oír en Santo Domingo tras el colapso de la Confederación, haciendo proposiciones al Sr. Seward para su realización, en una ventana editorial que se abre a mitad de una frase: el asunto fracasó entonces, y revivió con el ascenso del general Grant, cuando se redactó una convención bajo el general Babcock, uno de los jóvenes secretarios militares del Presidente, con el almirante Porter, en la expresión del Spy, como nodriza, y Cazneau como intérprete. El Sr. Fish, dice el editorial, había advertido particularmente a Babcock contra Cazneau por ser un hombre peligroso, mezclado en planes y especulaciones privadas, que solo quería hacer de los Estados Unidos un instrumento para realizar las vastas concesiones de tierras en la bahía de Samaná y otras partes que había asegurado; pero Babcock, que ignoraba el español, aceptó gustoso los servicios de Cazneau, quien era dueño de la situación y decía lo que quería: la ventana se cierra a mitad de una frase cuando pasa a la afición de Babcock por la bahía de Samaná.

records.headline: Discussing Mr. Sumner's charges, this Tribune editorial window
records.summary_en: Discussing Mr. Sumner's charges, this Tribune editorial window — which opens by answering an imputation against him, that he intended no injury or oppression of any race nor to deprive men of chances to vindicate their capacity for self-government — reports his allegations: that the President's proceedings in reference to San Domingo are a menace to the Republic of Hayti, which embraces four-fifths of the population of the island; that threats of violence have been openly made against Hayti by the United States naval forces in those waters; and that the President in his annual message referred no less than nine times to the Dominican Republic as the whole island, entirely ignoring the existence of Hayti. Senator Morton calls the last an inadvertence, and the Tribune thinks it very likely was; but, it argues, the annexation of San Domingo would be only a step to the annexation of Hayti, whose thrifty portion the President's commercial advantages cannot be attained without; that the Haytians are strongly opposed to the annexation of Dominica, and still more strongly to the annexation of themselves, is not disputed — the window closing as the editorial turns to Mr. Gerrit Smith's argument.
records.summary_es: Al discutir los cargos del Sr. Sumner, esta ventana editorial del Tribune —que se abre respondiendo a una imputación contra él, de que no pretendía daño ni opresión de raza alguna ni privar a los hombres de oportunidades de reivindicar su capacidad de autogobierno— informa de sus alegaciones: que los procedimientos del Presidente en referencia a Santo Domingo son una amenaza para la República de Haití, que abarca las cuatro quintas partes de la población de la isla; que las fuerzas navales de los Estados Unidos en esas aguas han proferido abiertamente amenazas de violencia contra Haití; y que el Presidente en su mensaje anual se refirió no menos de nueve veces a la República Dominicana como si fuera toda la isla, ignorando por completo la existencia de Haití. El senador Morton califica esto último de inadvertencia, y el Tribune cree que muy probablemente lo fue; pero, argumenta, la anexión de Santo Domingo sería solo un paso hacia la anexión de Haití, sin cuya parte próspera no pueden alcanzarse las ventajas comerciales del Presidente; que los haitianos se oponen firmemente a la anexión de Dominica, y aún más firmemente a la anexión de ellos mismos, no se discute: la ventana se cierra cuando el editorial pasa al argumento del Sr. Gerrit Smith.

records.headline: Inquiries about Báez and Cabral are answered in a speech against the annexation
records.summary_en: Inquiries about Báez and Cabral are answered in a speech against the annexation printed by the Freeman, from one described as bound to be well informed, in a window opening mid-course: Cabral, the speaker is assured, once favored the sale of the bay of Samaná to the United States but has never favored annexation, and his policy is to bring the two governments of Dominica and Hayti together again, as they were down to the revolution and war that ended in the uncertain independence of the Dominican part of the island. The evidence, the speaker says, is not that the two chieftains agree but that they differ — one seeking unity for the two governments, the other seeking to sell his country for a price; and whatever the people's sentiment, Báez has been maintained in power by the naval force of the United States: 'Deny it, if you can.' He then supposes Louis Napoleon, in an evil hour, setting up Jefferson Davis as head of the United States government and treating with him to yield Texas to become part of Mexico, itself to become more or less part of France — the window closing inside the supposition.
records.summary_es: Las preguntas sobre Báez y Cabral se responden en un discurso contra la anexión publicado por el Freeman, de alguien descrito como necesariamente bien informado, en una ventana que se abre a mitad del discurso: Cabral, se le asegura al orador, favoreció una vez la venta de la bahía de Samaná a los Estados Unidos pero nunca ha favorecido la anexión, y su política es volver a unir los dos gobiernos de Dominica y Haití, como estuvieron hasta la revolución y la guerra que terminaron en la incierta independencia de la parte dominicana de la isla. La evidencia, dice el orador, no es que los dos caudillos estén de acuerdo sino que difieren: uno busca la unidad de los dos gobiernos, el otro busca vender su país por un precio; y cualquiera que sea el sentimiento del pueblo, Báez se ha mantenido en el poder por la fuerza naval de los Estados Unidos: «Niéguenlo, si pueden». Supone luego a Luis Napoleón, en una hora funesta, instalando a Jefferson Davis como jefe del gobierno de los Estados Unidos y tratando con él para ceder Texas para que pasara a formar parte de México, destinado a su vez a formar parte más o menos de Francia: la ventana se cierra dentro de la suposición.

records.headline: The Telegraph reprints an editorial on Mr. Sumner's charges
records.summary_en: The Telegraph reprints an editorial on Mr. Sumner's charges, in a window opening amid an argument over trade with Dominica and a denial that he intended the injury or oppression of any race of men or to deprive them of chances to vindicate their capacity for self-government: the President's proceedings in reference to San Domingo, the editorial says, are alleged by him to be a menace to the Republic of Hayti, which embraces four-fifths of the population of the island; threats of violence have been openly made against Hayti by the United States naval forces in those waters; and the President in his annual message referred no less than nine times to the Dominican Republic as the whole island, entirely ignoring the existence of Hayti. Senator Morton calls the last an inadvertence, and the editorial thinks it very likely was; but it strongly suggests that the annexation of San Domingo would be only a step to the annexation of Hayti, the President's commercial advantages being unattainable with the island's thrifty portion unannexed; that the Haytians are strongly opposed to the annexation of Dominica, and still more strongly to the annexation of themselves, has been made manifest in many ways and is not disputed — the window closing as the editorial turns to Mr. Gerrit Smith's argument.

records.headline: Under the head 'San Domingo,' the Gazette states its own position
records.summary_en: Under the head 'San Domingo,' the Gazette states its own position: it has taken little interest in the question, and regards it as one on which honest men and good patriots may fairly differ. The primary question is one of fact — do the people of the Dominican Republic really desire annexation to the United States? If they do, the Gazette inclines to receive them into the Union; if they do not, it strongly objects to annexing them by force, wanting no acquisitions of territory whose people prefer to keep apart. It has heartily supported Senator Morton's proposition, because its adoption seemed calculated to shed light on the vital question.
records.summary_es: Bajo el encabezado «San Domingo», el Gazette expone su propia posición: se ha interesado poco en la cuestión, y la considera una de esas sobre las que hombres honestos y buenos patriotas pueden diferir justamente. La cuestión primaria es de hecho: ¿desea realmente el pueblo de la República Dominicana la anexión a los Estados Unidos? Si la desea, el Gazette se inclina a recibirlo en la Unión; si no la desea, se opone firmemente a anexarlo por la fuerza, pues no quiere adquisiciones de territorio cuyo pueblo prefiera mantenerse aparte. Ha apoyado de corazón la proposición del senador Morton, porque su adopción parecía calculada para arrojar luz sobre la cuestión vital.

records.headline: A conference of the Democratic members of Congress at the capital
records.summary_en: A conference of the Democratic members of Congress at the capital on the San Domingo question, reported under the head 'The Democrat, and San Domingo,' decided unanimously to oppose the annexation project: they admitted that the acquisition of territory had been the manifest destiny and doctrine of the Democratic party, but held the objections to San Domingo too great to be overcome — that Dominica represented only half of the island, that its population was, in the conference's characterization, a half-civilized and ignorant race, and that the scheme was shrouded in corruption.
records.summary_es: Una conferencia de los miembros demócratas del Congreso en la capital sobre la cuestión de Santo Domingo, reseñada bajo el encabezado «The Democrat, and San Domingo», decidió por unanimidad oponerse al proyecto de anexión: admitieron que la adquisición de territorio había sido el destino manifiesto y la doctrina del partido Demócrata, pero sostuvieron que las objeciones a Santo Domingo eran demasiado grandes para ser superadas: que Dominica representaba solo la mitad de la isla, que su población era, en la caracterización de la conferencia, una raza semicivilizada e ignorante, y que el plan estaba envuelto en corrupción.

records.headline: In a despatch from Port-au-Prince the Herald prints General Cabral's manifesto
records.summary_en: In a despatch from Port-au-Prince the Herald prints General Cabral's manifesto announcing the defeat of Báez: 'Baez is faithless to us. In exchange for gold he wants to sacrifice our independence, and our independence we must maintain as the only thing we have, and as the most precious jewel we can bequeath to future generations.' The manifesto's concluding paragraph, as the Herald quotes it, looks past the revolution to 'the election of men of known honesty to fill the offices of public administration,' and ends: 'Citizens, union and we will save the Dominican Republic.' The Herald calls the manifesto's language pointed, strong, and meaning business.
records.summary_es: En un despacho desde Puerto Príncipe, el Herald publica el manifiesto del general Cabral que anuncia la derrota de Báez: «Báez nos es infiel. A cambio de oro quiere sacrificar nuestra independencia, y nuestra independencia debemos mantenerla como lo único que tenemos, y como la joya más preciosa que podemos legar a las generaciones futuras». El párrafo final del manifiesto, tal como lo cita el Herald, mira más allá de la revolución hacia «la elección de hombres de honradez conocida para desempeñar los cargos de la administración pública», y termina: «Ciudadanos, unión y salvaremos la República Dominicana». El Herald califica el lenguaje del manifiesto de incisivo, fuerte y que va en serio.

records.headline: A Washington item explains that the Seward-Stevens West India fund is now exhausted: Seward spent most of $100,000 of it
records.summary_en: A Washington item explains that the Seward-Stevens West India fund is now exhausted: Seward spent most of $100,000 of it on his West Indies trip, and General Babcock took the remaining $150,000 to lease the Bay of Samana. It reports that Mr. Dawes, chairman of the House Committee on Appropriations, refused two senators' request for a bill to pay the rent now due to Envoy Fabens, saying he could only make appropriations authorized by law, and that Senator Sumner calls the whole proceeding without the shadow of law.
records.summary_es: Una nota de Washington explica que el fondo Seward-Stevens para las Indias Occidentales ya se agotó: Seward gastó la mayor parte de $100,000 de ese fondo en su viaje a las Indias Occidentales, y el general Babcock tomó los $150,000 restantes para arrendar la bahía de Samana. Informa que el señor Dawes, presidente del Comité de Asignaciones de la Cámara, rechazó la petición de dos senadores de un proyecto de ley para pagar la renta ya vencida al enviado Fabens, diciendo que solo podía hacer asignaciones autorizadas por la ley, y que el senador Sumner califica todo el procedimiento como carente de toda sombra de legalidad.

records.headline: The Sun reports that the money expended by the President in the Dominican job
records.summary_en: The Sun reports that the money expended by the President in the Dominican job is drawn from an appropriation of $250,000 made in 1868: of this, $100,000 is said to have been spent by Mr. Seward in various investigations and negotiations respecting San Domingo, and the other $150,000 was used to pay the first year's rent of the bay of Samaná; for the second year's rent, the Sun says, there is no appropriation, nor, so far as now appears, any likelihood of getting one.

records.headline: The Tribune prints the closing numbered objections of an argument
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints the closing numbered objections of an argument against the annexation, in a window opening on the tail of the ninth — a settled principle of public law, that when one sovereign succeeds to another by purchase it takes all its just obligations as well as all its rights. The tenth objection is that Báez, the present President of the Dominican Republic, has no authority to dispose of his country: its constitution is its fundamental law, and its seventh article provides, 'The territory of the Republic is inalienable. No person or authority can transfer the whole or any portion of it to any other Power'; no amendment voiding the provision has been adopted, nor any legal or valid consent of the people obtained, and Báez's consent is 'the dernier resort of a ruined tyrant' who sells his country for a moneyed consideration, cash down, in advance. The eleventh is that this is no time to enlarge the national territory at so fearful a cost, with hundreds of millions of acres of the finest agricultural and mineral lands still untitled and unproductive and a burden of taxation heavier than can readily be borne — the window closing as it urges reducing existing obligations first.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica las objeciones numeradas finales de un argumento contra la anexión, en una ventana que se abre al final de la novena: un principio asentado de derecho público, que cuando un soberano sucede a otro por compra, asume todas sus obligaciones justas así como todos sus derechos. La décima objeción es que Báez, el actual presidente de la República Dominicana, no tiene autoridad para disponer de su país: su constitución es su ley fundamental, y su artículo séptimo dispone: «El territorio de la República es inalienable. Ninguna persona ni autoridad puede transferir todo o parte alguna de él a ninguna otra Potencia»; no se ha adoptado enmienda alguna que anule la disposición, ni se ha obtenido consentimiento legal o válido del pueblo, y el consentimiento de Báez es «el último recurso de un tirano arruinado» que vende su país por una contraprestación dineraria, en efectivo y por adelantado. La undécima es que este no es momento de ampliar el territorio nacional a un costo tan temible, con cientos de millones de acres de las más finas tierras agrícolas y minerales aún sin titular y sin producir y una carga de impuestos más pesada de lo que puede soportarse con facilidad: la ventana se cierra cuando insta a reducir primero las obligaciones existentes.
