records.headline: An editorial in The New York Herald examines the strategic arguments
records.summary_en: An editorial in The New York Herald examines the strategic arguments and financial scandals surrounding Dominican annexation. The article asserts that the Dominicans live in constant fear of Hayti, alleging that Haytians have repeatedly invaded the Dominican Republic—which it refers to as Dominica—and are currently instigating Cabral's insurrection. The paper argues that American annexation would pacify the island and establish order, but warns that preposterous land concessions and railway schemes encumber the country. In particular, it highlights that a syndicate of speculators secured all valuable waterfront lots around Samaná Bay, while another group obtained one-fifth of all Dominican public lands in exchange for a scientific survey, cautioning that these scandalous jobs may prove too egregious for Congress to accept.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en The New York Herald analiza los argumentos estratégicos y los escándalos financieros que rodean la anexión dominicana. El artículo sostiene que los dominicanos viven en constante temor a Haití, alegando que los haitianos han invadido reiteradamente la República Dominicana —a la que llama Dominica— y están instigando actualmente la insurrección de Cabral. El periódico argumenta que la anexión estadounidense pacificaría la isla y establecería el orden, pero advierte que concesiones de tierras y proyectos ferroviarios desmedidos gravan al país. En particular, resalta que un sindicato de especuladores se apoderó de todos los solares valiosos en la ribera de la bahía de Samaná, mientras que otro grupo obtuvo la quinta parte de todas las tierras públicas dominicanas a cambio de un estudio científico, advirtiendo que estos escandalosos negociados podrían resultar demasiado excesivos para que el Congreso los apruebe.

records.summary_en: A Washington news item dated February 24 reports, through a New York Herald special, that a Dominican leader has issued a proclamation calling upon all true Dominicans to rally to expel Baez. The proclamation speaks of the country being sold as a piece of merchandise.
records.summary_es: Una noticia de Washington fechada el 24 de febrero informa, a través de un despacho especial del New York Herald, que un líder dominicano ha emitido una proclama llamando a todos los verdaderos dominicanos a unirse para expulsar a Báez. La proclama habla del país vendido como una pieza de mercancía.

records.headline: A correspondent for The Charleston Daily News describes an official
records.summary_en: A correspondent for The Charleston Daily News describes an official reception held aboard ship at Samaná Bay for local Dominican civil and military authorities. The dispatch profiles military commandant Enrique Abreu as an educated native officer supportive of American annexation, while noting the presence of Governor José Silvano Acosta, the local Italian priest, the port collector, and the municipal magistrate. At the collation, Commandant Abreu offered a toast praising the United States as the champion of New World liberty and looking forward to the fulfillment of the Monroe Doctrine throughout Spanish America. Writing as the frigate Tennessee departed for Santo Domingo on January 30, the correspondent adds under the heading "The Scientific Explorations" that survey parties under geologist Professor W. P. Blake returned with favorable reports after exploring the head of the bay and the Yuna River.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal de The Charleston Daily News describe una recepción oficial ofrecida a bordo en la bahía de Samaná para las autoridades civiles y militares dominicanas de la localidad. El despacho perfila al comandante militar Enrique Abreu como un oficial nativo educado y partidario de la anexión estadounidense, a la vez que señala la presencia del gobernador José Silvano Acosta, el párroco italiano de la localidad, el recaudador del puerto y el magistrado municipal. Durante el refrigerio, el comandante Abreu ofreció un brindis elogiando a los Estados Unidos como defensores de la libertad en el Nuevo Mundo y anhelando el cumplimiento de la Doctrina Monroe en toda la América española. Al escribir cuando la fragata Tennessee partía hacia Santo Domingo el 30 de enero, el corresponsal añade bajo el título «Las exploraciones científicas» que las comisiones de reconocimiento bajo la dirección del geólogo profesor W. P. Blake regresaron con informes favorables tras explorar la cabecera de la bahía y el río Yuna.

records.headline: A correspondent for The Charleston Daily News reports on an address
records.summary_en: A correspondent for The Charleston Daily News reports on an address delivered by Frederick Douglass on the public plaza in Samaná before approximately 130 local residents. The dispatch notes that the orator spoke on American national greatness and the emancipation of enslaved people, observing that the local audience appeared entirely unacquainted with prominent abolitionist figures such as Abraham Lincoln or Senator Charles Sumner. Under the heading "Arrival at San Domingo," the writer reports that an overland courier party bearing dispatches to President Báez reached the capital on January 31, while the frigate Tennessee anchored three miles offshore on February 2 following a thirty-five-hour passage from Samaná Bay. The correspondent describes Santo Domingo City as an ancient and dilapidated town of seven to eight thousand inhabitants, identifying it as the oldest European settlement in the Americas.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal de The Charleston Daily News informa sobre un discurso pronunciado por Frederick Douglass en la plaza pública de Samaná ante aproximadamente 130 residentes locales. El despacho señala que el orador habló sobre la grandeza nacional estadounidense y la emancipación de los esclavos, observando que el público local parecía desconocer por completo a destacadas figuras abolicionistas como Abraham Lincoln o el senador Charles Sumner. Bajo el título «Llegada a Santo Domingo», el autor informa que una comitiva de correos por tierra con despachos para el presidente Báez llegó a la capital el 31 de enero, mientras que la fragata Tennessee fondeó a tres millas de la costa el 2 de febrero tras una travesía de treinta y cinco horas desde la bahía de Samaná. El corresponsal describe la ciudad de Santo Domingo como una población antigua y deteriorada de siete a ocho mil habitantes, identificándola como el asentamiento europeo más antiguo de las Américas.

records.headline: A correspondent for The Charleston Daily News describes the formal
records.summary_en: A correspondent for The Charleston Daily News describes the formal reception of the American annexation Commissioners by President Báez in Santo Domingo City. Following introductory remarks translated into French by Commissioner Andrew D. White, Báez welcomed the visitors, promised full cooperation, and urged the delegation to examine thoroughly both the proponents and opponents of annexation. Under the heading "Richness and Fertility," the dispatch reports that an overland party traveling across the island observed luxuriant vegetation and valuable timber, including mahogany, satinwood, and abundant lignum-vitae. The correspondent adds that a local merchant displayed samples of river gold washed from the Jaina River and rich copper ore from nearby mountains, reporting that native miners using simple tools extract several ounces of gold daily and sell it for fourteen dollars in silver per ounce.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal de The Charleston Daily News describe la recepción formal de los comisionados de anexión estadounidenses por parte del presidente Báez en la ciudad de Santo Domingo. Tras unas palabras de presentación traducidas al francés por el comisionado Andrew D. White, Báez dio la bienvenida a los visitantes, prometió plena colaboración e instó a la delegación a interrogar minuciosamente tanto a los partidarios como a los adversarios de la anexión. Bajo el título «Riqueza y fertilidad», el despacho relata que una comisión por tierra que cruzó la isla observó una vegetación exuberante y maderas de gran valor, entre ellas caoba, madera de satén y abundante guayacán. El corresponsal añade que un comerciante local exhibió muestras de oro de río extraído del río Jaina y rico mineral de cobre procedente de montañas cercanas, informando que los mineros nativos que emplean herramientas sencillas extraen varias onzas de oro al día y las venden a catorce dólares en plata por onza.

records.headline: An editorial in the Tribune observes that the San Domingo Commission
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Tribune observes that the San Domingo Commission is devoting six or eight weeks to inquiries across a territory with fewer than 200,000 inhabitants, where fatal fevers, if as prevalent as claimed, will soon show in the illness of the commissioners and their aides. Directing European and American attention to the mission, the paper declares that while it will not anticipate the final report, the commissioners will certainly not favor annexation if they find a majority of the Dominicans adverse to it, regardless of the island's riches. The editorial adds that even if the commissioners were to recommend an act of aggression, rapacity, or bad faith, the American people would veto it.
records.summary_es: Un editorial del Tribune observa que la Comisión de Santo Domingo dedica seis u ocho semanas a indagaciones en un territorio de menos de 200,000 habitantes, donde las fiebres mortales, si son tan comunes como se afirma, pronto se manifestarán en la enfermedad de los comisionados y sus asistentes. Al dirigir la atención europea y estadounidense a la misión, el periódico declara que, si bien no anticipará el informe final, los comisionados ciertamente no favorecerán la anexión si hallan a una mayoría de los dominicanos opuesta a ella, sin importar las riquezas de la isla. El editorial añade que, aun si los comisionados llegaran a recomendar un acto de agresión, rapacidad o mala fe, el pueblo estadounidense lo vetaría.

records.summary_en: The Sun argues that Mr. Baez does not seem to understand that the annexation treaty has been rejected by the Senate and the alternative treaty for leasing Samana Bay has lapsed, so the United States is not bound to pay him a second year's rent. It calls Samana a poor and unhealthy harbor where coal costs eighty-five dollars a ton, against twelve dollars at St. Thomas, and contrasts the $150,000 rent Baez asks with the $5,000 a year the United States pays for a coaling wharf at St. Thomas.

records.headline: A dispatch reports that dispatches from the San Domingo commission
records.summary_en: A dispatch reports that dispatches from the San Domingo commission bring a preliminary account of its proceedings, confirming correspondents' assertions that Haiti's threatening stance forms the chief obstacle to annexation. The dispatch states that Haiti affords moral and perhaps physical backing to the insurgent leader Cabral in his incursions along the Dominican border, fearing that United States annexation of San Domingo would lead to the absorption of the entire island. Haiti is said to prefer fighting first, forcing an armed American occupation from the outset, though prospects otherwise remain favorable to annexation and an affirmative commissioners' report. The commission is expected to return by April 1, with Congress remaining in session to consider its findings.
records.summary_es: Un despacho informa que los despachos de la comisión de Santo Domingo traen una relación preliminar de sus actuaciones, confirmando las aseveraciones de los corresponsales de que la postura amenazante de Haití constituye el principal obstáculo para la anexión. El despacho afirma que Haití brinda apoyo moral y acaso físico al líder insurgente Cabral en sus incursiones a través de la frontera dominicana, por temor a que la anexión de Santo Domingo a los Estados Unidos conduzca a la absorción de toda la isla. Se indica que Haití preferiría luchar primero, forzando una ocupación armada estadounidense desde el comienzo, aunque por lo demás las perspectivas continúan siendo favorables a la anexión y a un informe favorable de los comisionados. Se espera que la comisión regrese para el 1 de abril y que el Congreso permanezca en sesiones para examinar sus conclusiones.

records.headline: San Domingo's mineral deposits and timber resources are detailed
records.summary_en: San Domingo's mineral deposits and timber resources are detailed in an article asserting that the country's forests are worth even more than its rich mines. Citing Walton and local accounts, the paper lists gold operations at Cotuy, Guaba, Rubio, and Baoruco, copper and emerald mines at Maymon and La Esmeralda, and silver, iron, and quicksilver deposits across regions including Jarabacoa, La Vega, Puerto Plata, and the Haina River. Iron ore near Cotuy is noted as capable of transport down the Yuna River to Samaná Bay. In addition to precious stones and various ores, the report identifies extensive varieties of timber covering the country's slopes, including mahogany, cedar, ebony, Brazil wood, fustic, lignum vitae, and ironwood.
records.summary_es: Un artículo detalla los yacimientos minerales y los recursos madereros de Santo Domingo, afirmando que los bosques del país valen incluso más que sus ricas minas. Citando a Walton y testimonios locales, el periódico enumera faenas auríferas en Cotuy, Guaba, Rubio y Baoruco, minas de cobre y esmeraldas en Maimón y La Esmeralda, y yacimientos de plata, hierro y azogue en regiones como Jarabacoa, La Vega, Puerto Plata y el río Haina. Se señala que el mineral de hierro cercano a Cotuy puede transportarse por el río Yuna hacia la bahía de Samaná. Además de piedras preciosas y diversos minerales, el informe identifica extensas variedades madereras en las laderas del país, entre ellas caoba, cedro, ébano, palo de Brasil, fustete, guayacán y palo de hierro.

records.headline: In a review of current periodicals, the Chicago Tribune remarks
records.summary_en: In a review of current periodicals, the Chicago Tribune remarks that the appointment of the San Domingo commissioners has opened a new subject for American magazines. The reviewer highlights an article in the March Galaxy entitled "The Annexation of San Domingo," written by "Americus," which traces the history of the annexation movement from its inception to the departure of the frigate Tennessee and provides data on the island's industrial condition. The article is illustrated by a map compiled from an official map published in 1858 by order of the president of the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: En una reseña de publicaciones periódicas, el Chicago Tribune señala que el nombramiento de los comisionados de Santo Domingo ha abierto un nuevo tema para las revistas estadounidenses. El crítico destaca un artículo en la edición de marzo de The Galaxy titulado «The Annexation of San Domingo», firmado por «Americus», que repasa la historia del movimiento de anexión desde su inicio hasta la partida de la fragata Tennessee y ofrece datos sobre la condición industrial de la isla. El artículo está ilustrado con un mapa compilado a partir de un mapa oficial publicado en 1858 por orden del presidente de la República Dominicana.

records.headline: A Washington dispatch to the Richmond Dispatch reports that Mr. McMichael of Philadelphia
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch to the Richmond Dispatch reports that Mr. McMichael of Philadelphia, special bearer of dispatches, has arrived with a preliminary report from the San Domingo commissioners. While detailed contents are withheld from publication, the dispatch states the commissioners confirm that Haiti's threatening attitude forms the greatest obstacle to annexation. Haiti is reported to be giving moral and possibly physical support to the revolutionary leader Cabral along the Dominican border, fearing that annexation would result in the United States absorbing the entire island. Haiti is said to prefer fighting first to force an armed American occupation, but prospects otherwise remain favorable to annexation and an affirmative report.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Washington para el Richmond Dispatch informa que el señor McMichael, de Filadelfia, portador especial de correspondencia, ha llegado con un informe preliminar de los comisionados de Santo Domingo. Aunque los pormenores se reservan de la publicación, el despacho señala que los comisionados confirman que la actitud amenazante de Haití representa el mayor obstáculo para la anexión. Se informa que Haití brinda respaldo moral y posiblemente físico al líder revolucionario Cabral a lo largo de la frontera dominicana, temiendo que la anexión conduzca a que los Estados Unidos absorban toda la isla. Se afirma que Haití preferiría luchar primero para forzar una ocupación armada estadounidense, pero por lo demás el panorama sigue siendo favorable a la anexión y a un informe favorable.

records.headline: The editorial reports that the steamer Tennessee, after much talk of her loss, has reached the Bay of Samana safely
records.summary_en: The editorial reports that the steamer Tennessee, after much talk of her loss, has reached the Bay of Samana safely, and that some of her passengers, including members of the San Domingo Commission, crossed the island to the city of Santo Domingo on the south coast. Quoting a Republican writer's account of the country and its people, the editorial argues against President Grant's annexation of St. Domingo and warns that he and his friends will likely find the Dominicans a burden before many months are over.
records.summary_es: El editorial informa que el vapor Tennessee, tras mucho hablarse de su pérdida, ha llegado sano y salvo a la bahía de Samaná, y que algunos de sus pasajeros, incluidos miembros de la Comisión de Santo Domingo, cruzaron la isla hasta la ciudad de Santo Domingo, en la costa sur. Citando el relato de un escritor republicano sobre el país y su gente, el editorial argumenta contra la anexión de Santo Domingo por el presidente Grant y advierte que él y sus amigos probablemente encontrarán a los dominicanos una carga antes de que pasen muchos meses.

Were ancient Hispaniola even a blessing to us, modern Dominicans would be a curse, as Gen. Grant and his friends will probably find before they are many months older. As to its inhabitants, we have the high Republican authority of Mr. Fulton for this: "The majority of the people of the country are of pure African descent. Of this there cannot be the slightest doubt, and we could trace but little evidence of what is called a mixture of races among the country people, though the population of Santo Domingo is mixed and motley. Among the elderly men and women especially there is a grace of carriage and a dignity of manner that is peculiarly attractive, and reminds one of the high-toned Spanish character. They are cleanly but very slightly appareled. The men wear a white mantle when out at night or to protect them from the rain, and assume quite a picturesque aspect. They all carry swords at their side, and I saw some boys not over fifteen years of age with the inevitable sword. records.headline: Herald correspondence from Samana reports that the United States Commission, with its geologists, botanists
records.summary_en: Herald correspondence from Samana reports that the United States Commission, with its geologists, botanists, naturalists and press correspondents, has been at work since arriving, sending parties out to explore the country bordering the bay up to the mouth of the Yuna river and into the interior. The commissioners go ashore daily to talk with the villagers and examine their small cleared plantations, while the correspondent cautions that newcomers, dazzled by the warm climate and lush growth, are viewing everything in rose color, though the soil is rich, vegetation grows rapidly, and palms, oranges and coconuts abound.
records.summary_es: Una correspondencia del Herald desde Samaná informa que la Comisión de los Estados Unidos, con sus geólogos, botánicos, naturalistas y corresponsales de prensa, ha estado trabajando desde su llegada, enviando grupos a explorar el territorio que bordea la bahía hasta la desembocadura del río Yuna y hacia el interior. Los comisionados desembarcan a diario para hablar con los aldeanos y examinar sus pequeñas plantaciones despejadas, mientras el corresponsal advierte que los recién llegados, deslumbrados por el clima cálido y la vegetación exuberante, lo ven todo de color de rosa, aunque el suelo es rico, la vegetación crece con rapidez y abundan las palmas, las naranjas y los cocos.

records.headline: A correspondent in Samana finds the climate most agreeable and the bay breezes balmy, but the land mostly dense wood
records.summary_en: A correspondent in Samana finds the climate most agreeable and the bay breezes balmy, but the land mostly dense wood with only a few poorly cultivated acres, though the rich soil could grow sugar cane, coffee, cocoa and oranges abundantly if labor could be found. He describes an interview in which President Baez pressed the country's boundless resources and the people's wish for annexation, and he questions the enormous land grant to Fabens, said to cover a tenth of the whole republic, which Baez defended but was also said to regret.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal en Samana encuentra el clima muy agradable y las brisas de la bahía templadas y refrescantes, pero el territorio es en su mayor parte bosque denso con solo unos pocos acres mal cultivados, aunque el suelo rico podría producir caña de azúcar, café, cacao y naranjas en abundancia si se encontrara mano de obra. Describe una entrevista en la que el presidente Baez insistió en los recursos ilimitados del país y en el deseo de anexión del pueblo, y cuestiona la enorme concesión de tierras a Fabens, que según se dice abarca una décima parte de toda la república, la cual Baez defendió pero también, según se dijo, lamentó haber hecho.

records.headline: A dispatch from Santo Domingo dated January 23, 1871, describes sailing into Samana Bay and anchoring about two
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Santo Domingo dated January 23, 1871, describes sailing into Samana Bay and anchoring about two miles from Santa Barbara, the only town on the peninsula. It describes the town's roughly one hundred small bamboo and palm houses, its roughly three hundred inhabitants, many of them descendants of a colony of Black Americans sent there more than forty-five years earlier, and its small trade in tobacco, hides and woods.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Santo Domingo fechado el 23 de enero de 1871 describe la entrada navegando a la Bahía de Samaná y el fondeo a unas dos millas de Santa Bárbara, el único pueblo de la península. Describe las cerca de cien casas pequeñas de bambú y palma del pueblo, sus cerca de trescientos habitantes, muchos de ellos descendientes de una colonia de negros americanos enviada allí más de cuarenta y cinco años antes, y su pequeño comercio de tabaco, cueros y maderas.
records.passage: At 11 o'clock in the morning we were only seven miles from the entrance of the harbor, and as we slowly sailed between Cape Samana and Cape Raphael, entering the magnificent gulf, we thought we [could?] understand the feelings of Columbus when he beheld the same beautiful green hills, and kissed the earth with transport. At 1:45 o'clock (exactly seven days after leaving New York) we anchored in Samana Bay, about two miles from the town of Santa Barbara, commonly called on American maps Samana. By-the-way, we had found a very great diversity in the topographical charts of this island, and the only correct guide is probably the map prepared at the instance of President Baez [illegible]. The town lies upon Samana Bay, a little harbor about three miles in depth on the southeastern portion of the peninsula which bears its name, and the [Gulf?] has the same dimension. SANTA BARBARA. The only town upon the peninsula is Santa Barbara, opposite which we are anchored. It nestles at the foot of the hills on the beach, and would be called a village in America, and a very wretched one, too. records.headline: A correspondence describes local trade and American residents
records.summary_en: A correspondence describes local trade and American residents in the Dominican Republic, noting that native cigars sell cheaply at $1.00 per hundred or $12 per thousand. Under the heading of small commerce for a country rich in natural wealth, the writer reports that a single steamer, the Tybee, plies between Santo Domingo City, Samaná, Puerto Plata, and New York, bringing flour, smoked fish, and liquor while exporting modest quantities of tobacco, hides, dyewoods, mahogany, and wild honey. A further notice observes that five or six American families have settled in the town, including two brothers named Burr from Bangor, Maine, who operate a fruit plantation and keep a billiard room in their hillside home.
records.summary_es: Una correspondencia describe el comercio local y los residentes estadounidenses en la República Dominicana, señalando que los cigarros del país se venden a bajo precio, a $1.00 el ciento o $12 el millar. Bajo el epígrafe de escaso comercio para un país colmado de riquezas naturales, el autor informa que un único vapor, el Tybee, cubre la ruta entre la ciudad de Santo Domingo, Samaná, Puerto Plata y Nueva York, transportando harina, pescado ahumado y licores mientras exporta cantidades modestas de tabaco, cueros, maderas tintóreas, caoba y miel silvestre. Una nota posterior añade que cinco o seis familias estadounidenses se han establecido en el pueblo, incluidos dos hermanos llamados Burr, oriundos de Bangor, Maine, quienes explotan una plantación de frutas y mantienen una sala de billar en su vivienda en la colina.

records.headline: A telegraphic dispatch reports the arrival of dispatches from the San Domingo commissioners
records.summary_en: A telegraphic dispatch reports the arrival of dispatches from the San Domingo commissioners containing a preliminary account of their work. While full details are withheld from publication, the dispatch states that the commissioners confirm correspondents' suggestions that the threatening posture of Haiti presents the chief barrier to the annexation of Santo Domingo. Haiti is said to be lending moral and perhaps physical backing to Cabral's incursions along the border, fearing that annexation would lead the United States to absorb the remainder of the island. It is further reported that Haiti might fight first to force an immediate armed American occupation, though annexation prospects are otherwise considered favorable.
records.summary_es: Un despacho telegráfico informa sobre la llegada de correspondencia de los comisionados de Santo Domingo con una relación preliminar de sus labores. Aunque los pormenores completos se reservan de la publicación, el despacho señala que los comisionados confirman las sugerencias de los corresponsales de que la postura amenazante de Haití constituye la principal traba para la anexión de Santo Domingo. Se afirma que Haití presta apoyo moral y acaso físico a las incursiones de Cabral por la frontera, por temor a que la anexión lleve a los Estados Unidos a absorber el resto de la isla. Se añade que Haití podría combatir primero para forzar una inmediata ocupación armada estadounidense, si bien por lo demás las perspectivas de anexión se consideran favorables.

records.headline: Writing from San Domingo on February 15, 1871, the correspondent describes the capital on the western bank of the river
records.summary_en: Writing from San Domingo on February 15, 1871, the correspondent describes the capital on the western bank of the river Ozama, a walled city 375 years old that is now utterly indefensible against modern artillery by land or sea. He walks through its ruins, above all the great Franciscan religious house covering several acres, where a tall orange tree laden with fruit grows in the very centre of the roofless church, bees swarm in the crevices of its walls, and animals are stabled by its altars.
records.summary_es: Escribiendo desde Santo Domingo el 15 de febrero de 1871, el corresponsal describe la capital en la orilla occidental del río Ozama, una ciudad amurallada de 375 años que hoy es totalmente indefendible contra la artillería moderna por tierra o por mar. Recorre sus ruinas, sobre todo la gran casa religiosa de los franciscanos, que cubre varios acres, donde un alto naranjo cargado de fruta crece en el centro mismo de la iglesia sin techo, las abejas bullen en las grietas de sus muros, y hay animales estabulados junto a sus altares.
records.passage: Is very massive, lead to the country, the chief of which is the Puerto del Conde, just outside this gate is a cemetery. Past this runs the old Spanish highway along the southern coast to Azua, once a fine road, but now akin to everything else in this blasted and ruined land, if any one doubts the "great first cause," —the all-prevailing law that controls the universe, let him come and look at Dominica. If the cry of Cacique and Carib rises to heaven for plundered kingdoms, and slaughtered households; —if the land is red with the blood of her children;—so, too, it is full of the bones of her oppressors, and in less than four centuries their monuments have crumbled and their mightiest works have perished. This city is full of ruins, and no small part of its limited area is occupied by them. The most impressive are those of the great religious house of the Franciscans, located on the highest ground within the walls, and covering several acres, with the wreck of buildings and desolated gardens. Ascending a steep street over antiquated pavements which grandee and Caballero have trodden before you, you pass under a massive portal, and stand in a growth of shrubbery and trees, so thick that the eyes can hardly penetrate it. An orange tree 80 feet high, laden with fruit stands in the very center. records.headline: A correspondent writing from Santo Domingo describes the city as orderly and its people as honest in their dealings
records.summary_en: A correspondent writing from Santo Domingo describes the city as orderly and its people as honest in their dealings, estimating the population at no more than about 8,000 and saying he has seen no intoxicated Dominican or brawl since arriving. He then turns to the United States commission, which in two weeks had conferred with the government, received deputations, questioned officials and examined records, while members set out to investigate Azua, Puerto Plata, Santiago de los Caballeros and other districts.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal que escribe desde Santo Domingo describe la ciudad como ordenada y a su gente como honesta en sus tratos, estima la población en no más de unos 8.000 habitantes y dice que no ha visto a ningún dominicano ebrio ni ninguna riña desde su llegada. Luego pasa a la comisión de los Estados Unidos, que en dos semanas había conferenciado con el gobierno, recibido delegaciones, interrogado a funcionarios y examinado registros, mientras sus miembros salían a investigar Azua, Puerto Plata, Santiago de los Caballeros y otros distritos.

records.headline: The paper prints the text of the Congressional joint resolution
records.summary_en: The paper prints the text of the Congressional joint resolution defining the duties of the commissioners appointed to examine conditions in the Dominican Republic. The resolution directs the commissioners to investigate Dominican public debt and obligations, foreign treaties, territorial boundaries, concessions granted to foreign claimants, and the terms on which the Dominican government might seek annexation as a United States territory. Section 2 instructs the commissioners to report as soon as practicable to the President for transmission to Congress, while Section 3 provides that they shall serve without compensation beyond expenses, with their secretary paid by the Secretary of State. A concluding proviso specifies that nothing in the resolution shall be construed as committing Congress to annexing the territory of the "republic of Dominica."
records.summary_es: El periódico publica el texto de la resolución conjunta del Congreso que define las funciones de los comisionados designados para examinar la situación en la República Dominicana. La resolución ordena a los comisionados indagar la deuda pública y las obligaciones dominicanas, los tratados extranjeros, los límites territoriales, las concesiones otorgadas a reclamantes extranjeros y los términos en que el gobierno dominicano pudiera pretender la anexión como territorio de los Estados Unidos. El artículo 2 dispone que los comisionados presenten su informe cuanto antes al presidente para que este lo someta al Congreso, mientras que el artículo 3 establece que servirán sin remuneración aparte de sus gastos, fijándose el sueldo del secretario por el secretario de Estado. Una disposición final aclara que nada en la resolución se interpretará en el sentido de comprometer al Congreso con la política de anexionar el territorio de la llamada «república de Dominica».

records.headline: An article headed "Converting the Heathen" reports that prominent
records.summary_en: An article headed "Converting the Heathen" reports that prominent figures accompanying the San Domingo commission took it upon themselves to persuade local residents to support annexation. Upon landing, Frederick Douglass addressed an assembled crowd on the benefits of annexation, followed by General Franz Sigel and later former Senator Benjamin Wade, who urged the inhabitants to embrace the American republic. Because Douglass and Wade spoke English and Sigel spoke German, the audience understood none of them, and when Douglass asked those in favor of annexation to raise their hands, only three individuals responded. The Republican remarks that the episode casts doubt upon the administration's assurances that the Dominican population universally desired annexation.
records.summary_es: Un artículo titulado «Convirtiendo a los paganos» informa que destacadas figuras que acompañaban a la comisión de Santo Domingo asumieron por cuenta propia la tarea de persuadir a los habitantes locales para que respaldaran la anexión. Nada más desembarcar, Frederick Douglass se dirigió a una multitud congregada sobre los beneficios de la anexión, seguido por el general Franz Sigel y más tarde por el exsenador Benjamin Wade, quien instó a los pobladores a acogerse a la república estadounidense. Dado que Douglass y Wade hablaron en inglés y Sigel en alemán, los asistentes no entendieron a ninguno de ellos, y cuando Douglass pidió a los partidarios de la anexión que levantaran la mano, apenas tres personas respondieron. El Republican comenta que el suceso arroja dudas sobre las seguridades del gobierno de que la población dominicana deseaba unánimemente la anexión.

records.headline: An editorial in the Fremont Weekly Journal questions the prudence of Dominican annexation
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Fremont Weekly Journal questions the prudence of Dominican annexation in light of border conflicts and reports from the commission. Noting President Báez's assertion that annexation is sought to obtain protection against the chronic hostilities between Haiti and San Domingo, the paper warns that adopting this burden could embroil the United States in a costly conflict with Haiti, which dreads American expansion across the island. The editorial further points out that Samaná Bay has been overrated as a naval station, citing the commission's geologist, Professor Blake, who found its coal deposits useless for ocean steamers and its waters lacking sufficient depth for large vessels. Correspondents are nevertheless said to agree that no evidence has been found of corrupt administration interests in the annexation scheme.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en el Fremont Weekly Journal cuestiona la prudencia de la anexión dominicana a la luz de los conflictos fronterizos y los informes de la comisión. Al señalar la afirmación del presidente Báez de que la anexión se procura para obtener protección frente a las crónicas hostilidades entre Haití y Santo Domingo, el periódico advierte que asumir esa carga podría involucrar a los Estados Unidos en un costoso conflicto con Haití, que teme la expansión estadounidense en la isla. El editorial señala además que la bahía de Samaná ha sido sobrestimada como estación naval, citando al geólogo de la comisión, el profesor Blake, quien constató que sus yacimientos de carbón carecen de utilidad para vapores transoceánicos y que sus aguas carecen de profundidad suficiente para buques grandes. No obstante, se indica que los corresponsales coinciden en que no se han hallado pruebas de intereses corruptos del gobierno en el plan de anexión.

records.headline: The Springfield Weekly Republican quotes a speech delivered
records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican quotes a speech delivered by a member of the San Domingo commission who describes being enchanted by the island's scenery, mild climate, luscious fruits, and music despite local accounts of civil wars and oppression. The speaker confesses that while he cannot yet say what he will advise his countrymen regarding annexation of the Dominican Republic, he feels strongly inclined to annex himself and his family to the island. Commenting on the address, the paper remarks that the commissioners and their attendants are enjoying a delightful holiday during the most favorable season in the West Indies, traveling across and around the island under alluring circumstances while preparing a detailed report for the American government and public.
records.summary_es: El Springfield Weekly Republican reproduce un discurso pronunciado por un miembro de la comisión de Santo Domingo, quien describe hallarse cautivado por los paisajes, el clima benigno, las frutas exquisitas y la música de la isla, pese a los relatos locales sobre guerras civiles y opresión. El orador confiesa que, si bien aún no puede adelantar qué aconsejará a sus compatriotas respecto a la anexión de la República Dominicana, se siente fuertemente inclinado a anexionarse a sí mismo y a su familia a tan hermosa isla. Al comentar el discurso, el periódico observa que los comisionados y su comitiva disfrutan de unas placenteras vacaciones durante la estación más propicia de las Antillas, recorriendo la isla por tierra y mar bajo circunstancias sumamente atrayentes mientras preparan un informe detallado para el gobierno y el público estadounidenses.

records.headline: The Spirit of Democracy prefaces a telegraphic report from Havana
records.summary_en: The Spirit of Democracy prefaces a telegraphic report from Havana by claiming it was prepared under orders from President Grant's commission to sway public opinion in favor of what the paper calls the Santo Domingo swindle. The dispatch, dated February 10 at San Domingo and transmitted via Havana on February 17, states that the United States commissioners were received enthusiastically everywhere they traveled. It further reports that agents from Venezuela, Costa Rica, and Nicaragua had arrived on the island and were awaiting instructions to organize colonists prepared to migrate to Santo Domingo as soon as annexation is assured.
records.summary_es: The Spirit of Democracy encabeza un informe telegráfico de La Habana afirmando que fue preparado por orden de la comisión del presidente Grant para manipular la opinión pública a favor de lo que el diario califica como la estafa de Santo Domingo. El despacho, fechado el 10 de febrero en Santo Domingo y transmitido por La Habana el 17 de febrero, asegura que los comisionados de los Estados Unidos fueron recibidos con entusiasmo por doquier. Añade que habían llegado a la isla agentes de Venezuela, Costa Rica y Nicaragua, quienes esperaban órdenes para organizar a colonos dispuestos a trasladarse a Santo Domingo en cuanto la anexión fuese una certeza.

records.headline: A letter from San Domingo, reprinted from the Philadelphia Age
records.summary_en: A letter from San Domingo, reprinted from the Philadelphia Age under the heading "The Dominicans Bitterly Opposed to Annexation," asserts that hostility toward annexation among the population is more intense than ever. The correspondent claims that President Báez has established a reign of terror, using American warships and his own troops to intimidate the populace and suppress free expression through fear of imprisonment or exile. The letter warns that if annexation is consummated, a bloody revolution will inevitably follow, requiring American forces to exterminate the Dominican population. It further contends that fewer than one-tenth of the inhabitants support the measure, with nearly all supporters concentrated in the capital city.
records.summary_es: Una carta desde Santo Domingo, reproducida del Philadelphia Age bajo el título «Los dominicanos amargamente opuestos a la anexión», asevera que la hostilidad hacia la anexión entre la población es más intensa que nunca. El corresponsal afirma que el presidente Báez ha instaurado un régimen de terror, valiéndose de buques de guerra estadounidenses y de sus propias tropas para intimidar a la población y acallar la libre expresión mediante el temor al encarcelamiento o al destierro. La carta advierte que, de consumarse la anexión, sobrevendrá inevitablemente una sangrienta revolución que obligará a las fuerzas estadounidenses a exterminar a la población dominicana. Sostiene además que menos de una décima parte de los habitantes respalda la medida, concentrándose casi la totalidad de los partidarios únicamente en la capital.

records.headline: In the closing of a published letter on San Domingo, the writer argues the case for annexation on the ground that a united
records.summary_en: In the closing of a published letter on San Domingo, the writer argues the case for annexation on the ground that a united United States, with its commerce growing, would have in Samana an ever-ready harbor and safe retreat. He adds that a government stands on fear or on affection, and that it would be unwise to display only enough force to irritate but not enough to overawe.
records.summary_es: En el cierre de una carta publicada sobre Santo Domingo, el autor defiende la anexión con el argumento de que unos Estados Unidos unidos, con su comercio en crecimiento, tendrían en Samana un puerto siempre listo y un refugio seguro. Añade que un gobierno se sostiene sobre el temor o sobre el afecto, y que sería imprudente mostrar solo la fuerza suficiente para irritar pero no la bastante para imponer respeto.

records.headline: An editorial paragraph in The Sun reports allegations that foreign steamship
records.summary_en: An editorial paragraph in The Sun reports allegations that foreign steamship owners have traveled to San Domingo to obtain Dominican vessel registrations from President Báez. According to these accounts, the owners intend to bring their ships under the United States flag once the republic is annexed, with managers of one steamship line reportedly securing registry for more than 10,000 tons of shipping. The paper comments ironically that it hopes the owners paid little for the privilege, adding that if this scheme were the worst job connected to the San Domingo enterprise, the annexation project would be far more innocent than it actually is.
records.summary_es: Un párrafo editorial en The Sun recoge denuncias de que propietarios de vapores extranjeros han viajado a Santo Domingo para obtener registros marítimos dominicanos del presidente Báez. Según estas versiones, los navieros pretenden acoger sus embarcaciones a la bandera de los Estados Unidos una vez que la república sea anexionada, habiendo conseguido los administradores de una línea completa de vapores dicho trámite para más de 10,000 toneladas de arqueo. El diario comenta con ironía que espera que los empresarios hayan pagado poco por el beneficio, añadiendo que si esta maniobra fuese el peor de los negociados ligados a la empresa de Santo Domingo, el proyecto de anexión resultaría mucho más inocente de lo que en verdad es.

records.headline: Dispatches to the Herald report diplomatic friction along the Haitian border
records.summary_en: Dispatches to the Herald report diplomatic friction along the Haitian border alongside news of the American commission. American officials warned the Haitian authorities and General Alexis against assisting the insurgent Luperón, with Minister Bassett naming Haitian consuls in Jamaica and Curaçao as aiding Dominican rebels, while the influential governor of Santiago is reported to have abandoned the Báez party. Under the heading "Movements of the Dominican Commission," a letter from Puerto Plata dated March 6 reports that the commissioners departed for Monte Cristi accompanied by Báez officials. The correspondent states that annexation is expected to succeed despite strong local opposition to Báez, noting that threats have been made to burn Puerto Plata if annexed, with two houses already set on fire.
records.summary_es: Despachos enviados al Herald informan sobre fricciones diplomáticas en la frontera haitiana junto con noticias de la comisión estadounidense. Funcionarios estadounidenses advirtieron a las autoridades haitianas y al general Alexis contra prestar auxilio al insurgente Luperón, señalando el ministro Bassett a los cónsules haitianos en Jamaica y Curazao como partícipes en la ayuda a los rebeldes dominicanos, al tiempo que se informa que el influyente gobernador de Santiago ha abandonado el bando de Báez. Bajo el encabezado «Movimientos de la comisión dominicana», una carta desde Puerto Plata con fecha del 6 de marzo informa que los comisionados partieron rumbo a Monte Cristi acompañados por funcionarios de Báez. El corresponsal señala que se prevé el éxito de la anexión a pesar de la fuerte oposición local a Báez, destacando que se ha amenazado con incendiar Puerto Plata si es anexionada, habiéndose prendido fuego ya a dos viviendas.

records.headline: The decaying colonial architecture of its towns is described
records.summary_en: The decaying colonial architecture of its towns is described in a correspondence from the Dominican Republic. It recounts President Báez's conference with Commissioner Benjamin Wade regarding border hostilities. Báez told Wade that General Cabral commands no following of discontented Dominicans, but merely accompanies a Haitian force led by a Haitian general and composed of Haitian troops with a few foreigners and relatives. According to Báez, the Haitian government mounted this demonstration specifically to influence public opinion in the United States and prevent the Dominican Republic from uniting with a powerful protector. The correspondent also describes the port of Santa Bárbara de Samaná as a picturesque but impoverished settlement of eighty or ninety dwellings constructed from American scantling and flattened bamboo.
records.summary_es: Una correspondencia desde la República Dominicana describe la ruinosa arquitectura colonial de sus poblaciones. Relata la conferencia del presidente Báez con el comisionado Benjamin Wade sobre las hostilidades fronterizas. Báez declaró a Wade que el general Cabral no encabeza a dominicanos descontentos, sino que apenas acompaña a una fuerza haitiana dirigida por un general haitiano e integrada por tropas de ese país, unos pocos extranjeros y allegados suyos. De acuerdo con Báez, el gobierno haitiano organizó esta demostración deliberadamente para influir en el público de los Estados Unidos y evitar que la República Dominicana se una a una potencia fuerte. El corresponsal retrata asimismo el puerto de Santa Bárbara de Samaná como un poblado pintoresco pero humilde de ochenta o noventa viviendas hechas de maderos estadounidenses y bambú aplanado.

records.headline: A report of the United States Commission finds the people of Samana enthusiastic and unanimous for annexation
records.summary_en: A report of the United States Commission finds the people of Samana enthusiastic and unanimous for annexation, though their opinion should not be taken for that of a majority of the islanders, since all the trade, protection and support of the settlement come from the United States. In a sample conversation, a resident says annexation means getting into the States and having law, that it gives protection for themselves and their property and prevents the wars that have destroyed their crops a dozen times, and that many will not stay if the annexation scheme is defeated.
records.summary_es: Un informe de la Comisión de los Estados Unidos encuentra que el pueblo de Samana está entusiasta y unánime a favor de la anexión, aunque su opinión no debe tomarse por la de la mayoría de los isleños, ya que todo el comercio, la protección y el apoyo del asentamiento provienen de los Estados Unidos. En una conversación de ejemplo, un residente dice que la anexión significa entrar en los Estados y tener ley, que da protección para ellos y su propiedad y evita las guerras que han destruido sus cosechas una docena de veces, y que muchos no se quedarán si el plan de anexión es derrotado.

records.headline: An article in the Alexandria Gazette explains the territorial
records.summary_en: An article in the Alexandria Gazette explains the territorial and political division of Hispaniola, stating that the island spans roughly 27,000 square miles, with the western two-fifths forming the Republic of Haiti and the eastern three-fifths occupied by the Dominican Republic. Emphasizing that Haiti and San Domingo are distinct nations sharing the island side by side, the paper stresses that President Grant proposes to annex the Dominican Republic rather than the entire island, making annexation an absorption of a separate nationality rather than simply a tract of land. The article estimates the Dominican population at 150,000 to 200,000 inhabitants, of whom no more than one-tenth are white.
records.summary_es: Un artículo en la Alexandria Gazette explica la división territorial y política de La Española, precisando que la isla abarca cerca de 27,000 millas cuadradas, de las cuales las dos quintas partes occidentales forman la República de Haití y las tres quintas partes orientales corresponden a la República Dominicana. Al subrayar que Haití y Santo Domingo son naciones distintas que conviven en una misma isla, el periódico recalca que el presidente Grant propone anexionar la República Dominicana y no la totalidad de la isla, de modo que el proyecto implica la absorción de una nacionalidad independiente y no solo de un territorio. El artículo calcula la población dominicana entre 150,000 y 200,000 habitantes, de los cuales no más de una décima parte es de raza blanca.

records.headline: Dispatches to the Wheeling Daily Register report from Puerto Plata
records.summary_en: Dispatches to the Wheeling Daily Register report from Puerto Plata that the San Domingo commission departed for Monte Cristi accompanied by President Báez and Dominican officials. The correspondent notes a prevailing belief that annexation will proceed despite fierce local opposition to Báez, reporting that opponents have threatened to burn the town if annexed, two houses have already been set on fire, and armed patrols guard the streets at night. Partisans of Cabral predict a widespread uprising, and Báez's political situation is described as precarious though his supporters remain resolute. A related dispatch from Havana adds that the American consul at Cap-Haïtien warned the local Haitian commander against permitting General Luperón to cross the frontier to join the rebellion against Báez.
records.summary_es: Despachos al Wheeling Daily Register informan desde Puerto Plata que la comisión de Santo Domingo partió hacia Monte Cristi acompañada por el presidente Báez y funcionarios dominicanos. El corresponsal señala la creencia generalizada de que la anexión seguirá adelante pese a la enconada oposición local a Báez, e informa que los opositores han amenazado con incendiar la ciudad si es anexionada, se ha prendido fuego a dos casas y patrullas armadas vigilan las calles de noche. Los partidarios de Cabral pronostican un levantamiento generalizado y la situación de Báez se describe como precaria, aunque sus partidarios se mantienen firmes. Un despacho relacionado desde La Habana añade que el cónsul estadounidense en Cabo Haitiano advirtió al comandante haitiano de la plaza que no permitiera al general Luperón cruzar la frontera para sumarse a la rebelión contra Báez.

records.headline: An editorial headed "Santo Domingo" in the Daily Kennebec Journal addresses
records.summary_en: An editorial headed "Santo Domingo" in the Daily Kennebec Journal addresses public skepticism regarding the proposed annexation of the republic. The paper acknowledges common objections that the United States already possesses abundant territory, that the island is distant, that its inhabitants are reputedly lawless and ignorant, and that the measure threatens to embroil the country in foreign debts, revolutions, and political intrigue. To evaluate these concerns, the editorial notes, the President dispatched a commission of three impartial and upright citizens to investigate the country's government, population, soil, resources, and liabilities. The Journal urges the public to suspend judgment until the commissioners complete their inquiry and deliver their forthcoming report.
records.summary_es: Un editorial titulado «Santo Domingo» en el Daily Kennebec Journal aborda el escepticismo de la opinión pública respecto a la propuesta de anexionar la república. El periódico reconoce las objeciones habituales de que los Estados Unidos ya disponen de suficiente territorio, que la isla se halla apartada, que se dice que sus habitantes son rebeldes e ignorantes, y que la medida amenaza con involucrar al país en deudas ajenas, revoluciones e intrigas políticas. Para evaluar estas inquietudes, apunta el editorial, el presidente comisionó a tres ciudadanos de probada imparcialidad e integridad para investigar el gobierno, la población, el suelo, los recursos y las deudas del país. El Journal exhorta a la ciudadanía a no precipitar un juicio hasta que los comisionados concluyan su examen y rindan su próximo informe.

records.headline: An account in the Daily Kennebec Journal reports observations
records.summary_en: An account in the Daily Kennebec Journal reports observations from the San Domingo commission, noting that the commissioners found the island remarkably rich, with soil more fertile than neighboring islands and vast inland tracts of valuable mahogany and timber. The report explains that the commissioners consider it their duty to gather facts rather than argue for or against annexation, allowing the public to draw its own conclusions. In response to a serenade by Dominican citizens, Commissioner Dr. Samuel Gridley Howe delivered an address describing how the island's enchanting scenery, balmy climate, luscious fruits, and music captivated his senses, offering a bright contrast to local grievances regarding civil wars and political oppression.
records.summary_es: Una reseña en el Daily Kennebec Journal recoge impresiones de la comisión de Santo Domingo, indicando que los comisionados hallaron la isla sumamente rica, con un suelo más fértil que el de las islas vecinas y extensos bosques interiores de caoba y maderas de gran valor. La nota explica que los comisionados consideran que su deber es recabar hechos y no abogar en favor o en contra de la anexión, dejando que el público extraiga sus propias conclusiones. En respuesta a una serenata ofrecida por ciudadanos dominicanos, el comisionado Dr. Samuel Gridley Howe pronunció un discurso en el que relató cómo los fascinantes paisajes, el clima benigno, las exquisitas frutas y la música cautivaron sus sentidos, en grato contraste con las quejas locales por las guerras civiles y la opresión política.

records.headline: An exploring party of the commission travelled from Samana up the Yuna River and overland to St. Domingo
records.summary_en: An exploring party of the commission travelled from Samana up the Yuna River and overland to St. Domingo, finding at Punta Gorda only lignite coal, worthless for fuel, and a river navigable by small boats for forty-two miles through an extremely fertile plain. The party passed through San Francisco de Macoris, a town of about 8,000 people making cigars and raising stock, and through La Vega, Cotuy and the mountain ranges beyond, and reports that the people along the route favoured annexation with great unanimity.
records.summary_es: Un grupo explorador de la comisión viajó desde Samaná remontando el río Yuna y por tierra hasta Santo Domingo, y encontró en Punta Gorda solo carbón de lignito, sin valor como combustible, y un río navegable por embarcaciones pequeñas durante cuarenta y dos millas a través de una llanura sumamente fértil. El grupo pasó por San Francisco de Macorís, un pueblo de unos 8.000 habitantes que fabrica cigarros y cría ganado, y por La Vega, Cotuí y las cordilleras más allá, e informa que la gente a lo largo de la ruta favorecía la anexión con gran unanimidad.

Many rumors were prevalent as to the chances of the messenger ever reaching Cabral's lines, doubts being expressed that Baez would permit him to actually go through. Yesterday, however, the 6th inst., information was received on board the Tennessee that a messenger had made his appearance at the Haytien lines, bearing a despatch from Cabral, and a courier had immediately been sent from this place for instruction as to whether the letter should be received. The Commissioners were informed by the Haytien authorities that, as they desired to preserve the strictest neutrality between the contending forces in the Dominican portion of the island, they would only allow the messenger to come through their territory at the request of the Commission, and then to be received on the vessel. Dr. Howe immediately made preparations for accepting the messenger and endeavoring to see Cabral if possible, but Mr. Wade considered that the proper course was to treat him as an outlaw and a cutthroat, and not to have any dealings with him. records.headline: The Herald's correspondent in Port-au-Prince reports that both
records.summary_en: The Herald's correspondent in Port-au-Prince reports that both the Haitian government and the Haitian public harbor deep apprehension toward the American commission and the proposed annexation of the Dominican Republic. The writer states that Haitians fear the United States, like an anaconda swallowing one section of the island, will subsequently absorb their own republic and extinguish their national autonomy. In an interview granted to the correspondent following their conference with the American commissioners, Haitian President Nissage Saget, Secretary of State Lorquel, and General La Motte voiced steadfast opposition to Dominican annexation and protested the threatening posture assumed by the United States toward Haiti during the negotiations.
records.summary_es: El corresponsal del Herald en Puerto Príncipe informa que tanto el gobierno como el pueblo haitiano albergan un profundo recelo hacia la comisión estadounidense y la proyectada anexión de la República Dominicana. El cronista afirma que los haitianos temen que los Estados Unidos, cual anaconda que engulle una parte de la isla, terminen por absorber su propia república y extinguir su autonomía nacional. En una audiencia concedida al corresponsal tras reunirse con los comisionados estadounidenses, el presidente haitiano Nissage Saget, su secretario de Estado Lorquel y el general La Motte manifestaron una firme oposición a la anexión dominicana y protestaron por la postura amenazante que los Estados Unidos han adoptado hacia Haití mientras el asunto permanece pendiente.

records.headline: A report in the New York Herald quotes an address delivered
records.summary_en: A report in the New York Herald quotes an address delivered by an American commissioner—identifying colleagues Andrew D. White as visiting Santiago and Puerto Plata and Dr. Samuel Gridley Howe as en route from Santo Domingo City—in response to a welcoming speech from prominent local citizens. The commissioner asserts that expressions favoring immediate annexation to the United States reflect the overwhelming sentiment encountered across both seaport towns and agricultural interior districts. He explains that President Grant instructed the commission to ascertain whether the Dominican population freely desires annexation, stating that the American government would never annex an unwilling or deeply divided populace. The commissioner claims that during his inquiries across the island he has encountered scarcely a single citizen opposed to annexation.
records.summary_es: Una crónica en el New York Herald reproduce el discurso pronunciado por un comisionado estadounidense —quien menciona que sus colegas Andrew D. White recorre Santiago y Puerto Plata y el Dr. Samuel Gridley Howe viaja desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo— en contestación al saludo de destacados vecinos. El comisionado afirma que las manifestaciones en pro de una pronta anexión a los Estados Unidos coinciden con el sentir generalizado hallado tanto en las ciudades portuarias como en los distritos agrícolas del interior. Explica que el presidente Grant encomendó a la comisión cerciorarse de si la población dominicana desea libremente la anexión, advirtiendo que el gobierno estadounidense jamás accedería a anexionar a un pueblo renuente o profundamente dividido. El comisionado sostiene que en sus indagaciones por la isla apenas ha encontrado a un solo ciudadano que se oponga a la anexión.

records.headline: A correspondent of the New-York Tribune reports that President Báez's government
records.summary_en: A correspondent of the New-York Tribune reports that President Báez's government is bankrupt, on its last legs, and sustained only by the hope of annexation, leaving citizens exhausted by military conscription and desiring only peace and security. Under the printed heading "A Valley in the Clouds," a dispatch dated February 21 from Azua recounts an expedition of three persons thirty or forty miles northeast into the mountains to the elevated valley and town of Maniella. The writer describes ascending 2,500 feet from the cactus-covered plain of Ocoa Bay into a temperate climate where northern plants flourish.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal del New-York Tribune informa que el gobierno del presidente Báez está en bancarrota, al borde del colapso y sostenido únicamente por la esperanza de la anexión, dejando a los ciudadanos agotados por el reclutamiento militar y deseosos únicamente de paz y seguridad. Bajo el título impreso «A Valley in the Clouds», un despacho fechado el 21 de febrero desde Azua relata una expedición de tres personas que recorrió entre 30 y 40 millas al noreste hacia las montañas hasta el templado valle y pueblo de Maniella. El redactor describe un ascenso de 2,500 pies desde la llanura cubierta de cactus de la bahía de Ocoa hacia un clima templado donde prosperan plantas norteñas.

records.summary_en: The Tribune's correspondent reports from Port-au-Prince that the U.S. Commissioners' visit to Haitian President Saget was purely formal, arguing that any Haitian claims regarding Dominican annexation negotiations should be presented through regular diplomatic channels. The writer states that the Tennessee, carrying Commissioners Wade and Howe while Commissioner White traveled overland from Santo Domingo to Puerto Plata, departed Azua on February 25. The correspondent asserts that President Báez waved goodbye sorrowfully from the beach, characterizing him as reluctant to lose the protection of the warship's 9- and 11-inch guns.
records.summary_es: El corresponsal del Tribune informa desde Puerto Príncipe que la visita de los comisionados estadounidenses al presidente haitiano Saget fue puramente formal, sosteniendo que cualquier reclamo haitiano sobre las negociaciones de anexión dominicana debe presentarse por los canales diplomáticos regulares. El autor señala que el Tennessee, que transportaba a los comisionados Wade y Howe mientras el comisionado White viajaba por tierra desde Santo Domingo hasta Puerto Plata, partió de Azua el 25 de febrero. El corresponsal afirma que el presidente Báez se despidió con tristeza desde la playa, caracterizándolo como reacio a perder la protección de los cañones de 9 y 11 pulgadas del buque de guerra.

records.headline: A correspondent of the New-York Tribune outlines the anticipated
records.summary_en: A correspondent of the New-York Tribune outlines the anticipated findings of the forthcoming report of the San Domingo Commission to the United States government. The report will state that the popular voice in the Dominican Republic is almost unanimous in favor of immediate annexation, comparing the sentiment to the American resolve against returning to British rule. The correspondent notes that Dr. Howe's assessment of climate and public health will be favorable, and that the population is almost entirely Roman Catholic. Regarding natural resources, the writer reports that investigators found only small quantities of poor-quality coal and a thin vein of lignite near Samaná.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal del New-York Tribune resume las conclusiones previstas en el próximo informe de la Comisión de Santo Domingo al gobierno de los Estados Unidos. El informe señalará que la voz popular en la República Dominicana es casi unánime a favor de la anexión inmediata, comparando este sentimiento con la determinación estadounidense de no regresar al dominio británico. El corresponsal añade que la evaluación del Dr. Howe sobre el clima y la salud pública será favorable, y que la población es casi enteramente católica. Respecto a los recursos naturales, el redactor indica que los investigadores solo hallaron pequeñas cantidades de carbón de mala calidad y una delgada veta de lignito cerca de Samaná.

records.summary_en: According to the *Worcester daily spy* on March 17, 1871, U.S. commissioners Messrs. Wade and Howe met with the president of the Haitian republic and his cabinet. Mr. Wade stated that the commissioners were charged with making inquiries regarding the Dominican republic with a view toward more intimate relations, though the meeting itself had no reference to annexation. President Saget reciprocated the expressions of friendship and offered to aid their researches.

El presidente Saget correspondió a las demostraciones de afecto y brindó facilidades para sus investigaciones.

records.full_text: PORT AU PRINCE, March 7.—The commission reached here the second of March, from Azua. All are in excellent health. They will wait here for Commissioner White, who is expected here by the 10th, bringing with him two scientific expeditions, under Professors Blake and Ward, that crossed before him. The Tennessee will then start immediately for home, touching at Santiago de Cuba and Key West for coal. The questions of debt and disputed boundary are the most important since the last dispatches. The Haytiens are bitterly opposed to annexation. The commissioners, however, were received civilly. Cabral's strength consists almost wholly of Haytien support. The information that the Tennessee had been reported missing first reached the party here. The statement of Gen. Banks that she was unseaworthy was received with great indignation, and denounced as heartlessly cruel. She is one of the strongest and best ships in the navy, with a select company of efficient officers, who expect now, unless delayed by the Nantasket, to reach home by the 25th of March, or, at the farthest, the 1st of April. A delay of one week from this cause is possible, and if the ship is not heard from for two weeks it should not cause anxiety. Mail from the commission leaves for New York to-day by the steamer Port au Prince.

records.headline: A letter from Azua dated February 25, 1871, describes excursions by the visiting overland party to mineral springs
records.summary_en: A letter from Azua dated February 25, 1871, describes excursions by the visiting overland party to mineral springs about eighteen miles away, including a hot sulphur spring, and to a petroleum district a few miles from Azua. At the oil wells they found a derrick and dilapidated machinery, two bored wells and visible oil, and were told former American Consul Arthur Folsom had invested about $10,000 there and secured a hundred barrels of good lubricating oil.
records.summary_es: Una carta de Azua fechada el 25 de febrero de 1871 describe excursiones del grupo visitante a unos manantiales minerales situados a unas dieciocho millas, incluido un manantial caliente de azufre, y a un distrito petrolero a pocas millas de Azua. En los pozos de petróleo encontraron una torre y maquinaria deteriorada, dos pozos perforados y petróleo visible, y les dijeron que el ex cónsul americano Arthur Folsom había invertido allí unos 10.000 dólares y obtenido cien barriles de buen aceite lubricante.

A PETROLEUM EXCURSION. On Sunday morning last we secured horses, provisions and a guide and started for a visit to a petroleum district distant a few miles from Azua. For a short distance we followed a main road, which was in pretty good condition; but soon leaving this we struck into a narrow wood path winding around through the dense chaparral, swaying our bodies and bending our heads to avoid the low branches, most of which were provided with sharp thorns. The morning was well advanced when we started and the sun was quite hot, but we have become somewhat accustomed to the heat and do not mind it as we did at first. Soon we came to a beautiful spring, carefully protected from animals by an enclosure of woven branches. The water was not very cold, but was good, and its appearance had a refreshing effect upon us. Near this spring we found several large mango trees, where we left our pack mule and servant, with directions to prepare our repast by the time we should return from the oil wells. A short distance further on we came to the petroleum, and found that considerable labor had been expended here in order to make use of the oil. A derrick was still standing and machinery was lying about in a dilapidated condition. Two wells had been bored, and a considerable supply of oil obtained, large quantities of which were visible. records.headline: A special correspondent of the Herald reports that the arrival of the Commission's flagship
records.summary_en: A special correspondent of the Herald reports that the arrival of the Commission's flagship Tennessee at Azua created a great sensation, with President Báez aboard as a passenger and escorting visitors into town with a considerable cavalcade. Commissioner Wade was the sole commissioner aboard the vessel, as Dr. Howe and Professor White had undertaken separate overland journeys across the island toward Puerto Plata. The correspondent criticizes Howe and White for vacillation and unnecessary delays, contrasting them with Wade, who promptly took testimony from Azua's leading citizens and advocated returning immediately to the United States.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal especial del Herald informa que la llegada a Azua del buque insignia de la Comisión, el Tennessee, causó gran sensación, llevando como pasajero al presidente Báez, quien escoltó a los visitantes hacia el pueblo con una comitiva considerable. El comisionado Wade era el único comisionado a bordo del navío, ya que el Dr. Howe y el profesor White habían emprendido travesías terrestres por separado a través de la isla hacia Puerto Plata. El cronista critica a Howe y a White por sus vacilaciones y demoras innecesarias, en contraste con Wade, quien prontamente tomó testimonio a los principales ciudadanos de Azua y defendió el regreso inmediato a los Estados Unidos.

records.headline: Dispatches to the Chicago Tribune report that the San Domingo Commission arrived
records.summary_en: Dispatches to the Chicago Tribune report that the San Domingo Commission arrived in good health at Port-au-Prince from Azua on March 3. The party awaits Commissioner White, who traveled overland from Santo Domingo to Puerto Plata and is expected aboard the steamer Nantasket by March 10 alongside two scientific expeditions under Professors Blake and Ward. The correspondent notes that questions of debt and the disputed boundary remain prominent, with Haitians strongly opposed to annexation though receiving the commissioners civilly. Statements by General Banks asserting that the Tennessee was unseaworthy were received with indignation, with the ship expected to reach home by late March or April 1.
records.summary_es: Despachos enviados al Chicago Tribune informan que la Comisión de Santo Domingo llegó con buena salud a Puerto Príncipe desde Azua el 3 de marzo. La comitiva espera al comisionado White, quien viajó por tierra desde Santo Domingo hasta Puerto Plata y a quien se espera a bordo del vapor Nantasket para el 10 de marzo junto con dos expediciones científicas bajo la dirección de los profesores Blake y Ward. El corresponsal observa que los asuntos relativos a la deuda y a la frontera disputada continúan siendo prominentes, con los haitianos resueltamente opuestos a la anexión aunque recibieron cortésmente a los comisionados. Las afirmaciones del general Banks en las que declaraba que el Tennessee no estaba en condiciones de navegar fueron recibidas con indignación, estimándose que el buque llegará a casa para finales de marzo o el 1 de abril.

records.headline: The separate movements of the San Domingo Commissioners are detailed
records.summary_en: The separate movements of the San Domingo Commissioners are detailed by a New-York Tribune correspondent, who reports that Dr. Howe undertook a four-day excursion to El Seibo before traveling overland to Azua, while Commissioner White crossed the island to Puerto Plata. These diverging routes left Mr. Wade alone aboard the flagship Tennessee, while the Nantasket went to Puerto Plata to retrieve White and rejoin the party at Port-au-Prince around March 7. The writer notes that after completing their inquiries at Azua and conducting a brief visit to Haiti, the expedition will sail for home via Santiago de Cuba, introducing a subsequent narrative of their departure from Santo Domingo City following a shipboard funeral.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal del New-York Tribune detalla los desplazamientos por separado de los comisionados de Santo Domingo, informando que el Dr. Howe realizó una excursión de cuatro días a El Seibo antes de viajar por tierra a Azua, mientras que el comisionado White cruzó la isla hacia Puerto Plata. Estas trayectorias divergentes dejaron al señor Wade como único comisionado a bordo del buque insignia Tennessee, mientras que el Nantasket se dirigió a Puerto Plata para recoger a White y reunirse con la comitiva en Puerto Príncipe alrededor del 7 de marzo. El cronista agrega que tras concluir las indagaciones en Azua y cumplir una breve visita a Haití, la expedición navegará de regreso a casa pasando por Santiago de Cuba, dando paso a la narración de su salida desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo tras un funeral a bordo.

records.headline: An editorial in the Worcester Daily Spy observes that newly
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Worcester Daily Spy observes that newly arrived letters from correspondents with the San Domingo commission confirm the fertility of Dominica and the public desire for annexation, while focusing on inquiries into the Dominican debt that President Báez sought to conceal. Citing a dispatch published in the New-York Tribune, the paper states that Commissioner Wade pressed for a complete statement of admitted liabilities and disputed claims, securing important documents and indicating that the debt is probably about 53,000,000. The quoted Tribune writer endorses Senator Sumner's characterization of Báez as a 'political jockey' who deceives his people and attempted to manipulate the commissioners.
records.summary_es: Un editorial del Worcester Daily Spy observa que cartas recién llegadas de corresponsales junto a la comisión de Santo Domingo confirman la fertilidad de Dominica y el deseo público de anexión, al tiempo que se enfocan en las indagaciones sobre la deuda dominicana que el presidente Báez procuró ocultar. Citando un despacho publicado en el New-York Tribune, el periódico señala que el comisionado Wade exigió una declaración completa sobre los pasivos admitidos y las reclamaciones disputadas, obteniendo documentos importantes e indicando que la deuda asciende probablemente a cerca de 53,000,000. El autor del Tribune citado respalda la caracterización hecha por el senador Sumner de Báez como un «jockey político» que engaña a su pueblo e intentó manipular a los comisionados.

records.summary_en: Citing the Santo Domingo correspondent of the New York Herald, the Worcester Daily Spy reports that the conflict along the frontier against Dominica is essentially a Haitian war, with General Cabral held as a helpless prisoner of the Haitians. Informants who held secret interviews with Commissioner Dr. Howe assert that this report is true and claim that Cabral is seeking refuge on board the warship Tennessee. The dispatch further notes that parties have informed the commissioners that Cabral favors annexation, while Haitians are raising funds to present a medal to Senator Sumner.

Informantes que sostuvieron entrevistas secretas con el comisionado Dr. Howe aseguran que este informe es verídico y afirman que Cabral busca refugio a bordo del buque de guerra Tennessee. El despacho agrega que diversas personas han informado a los comisionados que Cabral favorece la anexión, mientras que los haitianos recaudan fondos para entregar una medalla al senador Sumner.

records.headline: A commentary in the Chicago Tribune questions how coercive measures
records.summary_en: A commentary in the Chicago Tribune questions how coercive measures by American officials, including consular officers, can be reconciled with assurances given to Congress that only truth and honest representations were sought regarding Santo Domingo. The writer asks whether prominent leaders such as Cabral, Luperón, Pimentel, and other Dominicans like them should not be permitted to speak, demanding why precautions have been taken to suppress their sentiments if an honest inquiry was intended. The piece concludes that the determination to annex the country should not rely on schemes unworthy of a power professing goodwill, truth, and justice.
records.summary_es: Un comentario en el Chicago Tribune cuestiona cómo las medidas coercitivas adoptadas por funcionarios estadounidenses, incluidos funcionarios consulares, pueden conciliarse con las seguridades dadas al Congreso de que solo se buscaban la verdad y representaciones honestas respecto a Santo Domingo. El autor pregunta si a líderes destacados como Cabral, Luperón, Pimentel y otros dominicanos afines no se les debería permitir hablar, exigiendo saber por qué se han tomado precauciones para acallar sus sentimientos si en verdad se pretendía una indagación honesta. El texto concluye que la determinación de anexar el país no debería depender de maquinaciones indignas de una potencia que profesa buena voluntad, verdad y justicia.
