records.headline: The New National Era publishes an extract from the commission
records.summary_en: The New National Era publishes an extract from the commission report analyzing Dominican political conditions and popular feeling regarding annexation. The commissioners observe that the influence of petty military chieftains and constant intrigues by exiles on neighboring islands have generated lawlessness and fabricated rumors of insurrection, driving many citizens to seek annexation to a strong power for protection. Under the heading 'Local Liberties,' the report notes that constant struggles have greatly impaired municipal liberties, though local councils could become centers of good governance under a stable system. Under 'Desire for Annexation,' the commissioners state that across all parts of the country, even the most remote districts, the people were found to be well informed about annexation and eager for its accomplishment.
records.summary_es: El New National Era publica un extracto del informe de la comisión que analiza las condiciones políticas dominicanas y el sentimiento popular respecto a la anexión. Los comisionados observan que la influencia de pequeños caudillos militares y las constantes intrigas de exiliados en islas vecinas han generado desorden y rumores ficticios de insurrección, llevando a muchos ciudadanos a buscar la anexión a una potencia fuerte en busca de protección. Bajo el título «Local Liberties», el informe señala que las continuas luchas han menoscabado gravemente las libertades municipales, aunque los ayuntamientos locales podrían convertirse en centros de buena gobernanza bajo un sistema estable. Bajo «Desire for Annexation», los comisionados manifiestan que en todas partes del país, incluso en los distritos más remotos, la población se encontraba bien informada sobre la anexión y deseosa de su consumación.

records.headline: The New National Era publishes a portion of the commission report
records.summary_en: The New National Era publishes a portion of the commission report detailing the mineral resources and soil characteristics of San Domingo. Expedition geologists report that iron ore is abundant and easily accessible for pig-iron production, copper ores show fair richness, an extensive gold region awaits exploration, and high-purity rock-salt deposits near Neyba can be quarried in large transparent blocks. They report that supposed coal deposits at Samaná and Puerto Plata proved upon examination to be low-grade lignite of little value compared to English or Pennsylvania coal. The report then begins a classification of Dominican soils into five agricultural categories, starting with uniformly rich mountain slopes and fertile valleys.
records.summary_es: El New National Era publica una parte del informe de la comisión que detalla los recursos minerales y las características del suelo de Santo Domingo. Los geólogos de la expedición informan que el mineral de hierro es abundante y de fácil acceso para la producción de arrabio, las menas de cobre presentan una riqueza razonable, una extensa región aurífera aguarda exploración y los depósitos de sal gema de gran pureza cerca de Neyba pueden extraerse en grandes bloques transparentes. Señalan que los supuestos yacimientos de carbón en Samaná y Puerto Plata resultaron ser, tras su examen, lignito de baja calidad y escaso valor comparado con el carbón inglés o de Pensilvania. El informe inicia luego una clasificación de los suelos dominicanos en cinco categorías agrícolas, comenzando con laderas montañosas uniformemente ricas y valles fértiles.

records.headline: The New National Era prints findings from the commission report
records.summary_en: The New National Era prints findings from the commission report regarding agriculture, crops, and cattle raising in San Domingo. The commissioners state that northern vegetables grow in perfection, pineapples thrive luxuriantly, and wheat has been successfully raised at an elevation of 4,000 feet in the valley of Constanza. The report emphasizes that tobacco is cultivated everywhere as the nation's principal export, while corn easily yields three crops a year. It describes city markets as richly supplied with tropical fruits and vegetables at all seasons, and observes that abundant natural grasses across the vast eastern savannas give San Domingo pre-eminence over neighboring islands in cattle raising.
records.summary_es: El New National Era publica las conclusiones del informe de la comisión relativas a la agricultura, las cosechas y la ganadería en Santo Domingo. Los comisionados indican que las hortalizas del norte se cultivan a la perfección, las piñas prosperan con exuberancia y el trigo se ha cosechado con éxito a una altitud de 4,000 pies en el valle de Constanza. El informe destaca que el tabaco se cultiva en todas partes como el principal renglón de exportación del país, mientras que el maíz rinde fácilmente tres cosechas al año. Describe los mercados urbanos como abundantemente provistos de frutas y verduras tropicales en todas las estaciones, y señala que los abundantes pastos naturales de las extensas sabanas orientales confieren a Santo Domingo preeminencia sobre las islas vecinas en la cría de ganado.

records.headline: The Tiffin Tribune publishes the concluding section and signatures of the report
records.summary_en: The Tiffin Tribune publishes the concluding section and signatures of the report submitted to President Grant by commissioners B. F. Wade, Andrew D. White, and S. G. Howe. The commissioners report that their request to explore the interior of Haiti met with an effective refusal, restricting their inquiries to what could be gathered without giving offense. Reviewing both divisions of the island, they express firm persuasion that the annexation of Santo Domingo to the United States would benefit both the Haitian and Dominican peoples. They argue that annexation would offer an example of an orderly and prosperous state and establish a guaranteed boundary between the French-speaking and Spanish-speaking nations, putting an end to destructive border wars.
records.summary_es: El Tiffin Tribune publica la sección final y las firmas del informe presentado al presidente Grant por los comisionados B. F. Wade, Andrew D. White y S. G. Howe. Los comisionados informan que su solicitud para explorar el interior de Haití se topó con una negativa efectiva, lo que limitó sus averiguaciones a lo que pudo recopilarse sin causar ofensas. Al examinar ambas divisiones de la isla, expresan la firme convicción de que la anexión de Santo Domingo a los Estados Unidos beneficiaría tanto al pueblo haitiano como al dominicano. Sostienen que la anexión ofrecería el ejemplo de un Estado ordenado y próspero y establecería una frontera garantizada entre las naciones de habla francesa y española, poniendo fin a destructivas guerras fronterizas.

records.headline: An editorial reprinted from the New York Tribune in the New National Era analyzes
records.summary_en: An editorial reprinted from the New York Tribune in the New National Era analyzes the border disputes and political rivalries between Haiti and Santo Domingo. The piece states that Cabral is backed by Haitian men and munitions along the contested border to overthrow President Báez, appealing to Dominican patriotism against Báez's annexation overtures. It defends President Grant's orders directing naval officers to give moral support to Báez, framing it as a warning preventing Haiti and Cabral from subverting the Dominican government by force while annexation remains under consideration. The paper rejects Senator Sumner's criticisms of this policy, questioning whether Haitian President Saget possesses any greater legitimacy than Báez.
records.summary_es: Un editorial reproducido del New York Tribune en el New National Era analiza las disputas fronterizas y las rivalidades políticas entre Haití y Santo Domingo. El texto afirma que Cabral cuenta con el respaldo de tropas y pertrechos haitianos a lo largo de la frontera en disputa para derrocar al presidente Báez, apelando al patriotismo dominicano contra las propuestas anexionistas de este. Defiende las órdenes del presidente Grant que instruyen a los oficiales navales a brindar apoyo moral a Báez, calificándolas de advertencia para evitar que Haití y Cabral derroquen por la fuerza al gobierno dominicano mientras la anexión se encuentre bajo consideración. El periódico rechaza las críticas del senador Sumner a esta política y cuestiona si el presidente haitiano Saget posee mayor legitimidad que Báez.

records.headline: The Herald and Tribune publishes the concluding section of the report of the San Domingo commissioners.
records.summary_en: The Herald and Tribune publishes the concluding section of the report of the San Domingo commissioners. The commissioners recount that when seeking to ascertain Haitian views and claims upon Santo Domingo, their requests to travel into the interior were met with an effective refusal from the Haitian government. Looking to the interests of both divisions of the island, they conclude that the annexation of Santo Domingo to the United States would be scarcely less beneficial to Haiti than to the Dominican Republic. They argue that annexation would set an example of an orderly and prosperous state while establishing a guaranteed boundary between the French-speaking and Spanish-speaking nations to end destructive border conflicts.
records.summary_es: El Herald and Tribune publica la sección final del informe de los comisionados de Santo Domingo. Los comisionados relatan que, al intentar conocer las opiniones y reclamaciones haitianas sobre Santo Domingo, sus solicitudes para viajar al interior recibieron una negativa efectiva por parte del gobierno de Haití. Considerando los intereses de ambas divisiones de la isla, concluyen que la anexión de Santo Domingo a los Estados Unidos sería casi tan provechosa para Haití como para la República Dominicana. Sostienen que la anexión sentaría el ejemplo de un Estado ordenado y próspero, a la vez que fijaría una frontera garantizada entre las naciones de habla francesa y española para poner fin a los destructivos conflictos fronterizos.

records.headline: The Holmes County Republican summarizes the commissioners' findings
records.summary_en: The Holmes County Republican summarizes the commissioners' findings on Dominican resources and examines the arguments for and against annexation. The paper outlines the report's favorable view of the island's iron ores, healthy mountain climate, and diverse agricultural lands spanning mountain valleys, the Llanos savannas, and the fertile plains of La Vega. The article notes that while the people, climate, and terms of purchase are all favorable, the United States already possesses far more territory than its population requires. The paper contends that the decisive argument for annexation is the acquisition of Samaná Bay to prevent the island from falling under European monarchical influence, observing that German commercial interests have already absorbed trade in San Domingo.
records.summary_es: El Holmes County Republican resume las conclusiones de los comisionados sobre los recursos dominicanos y examina los argumentos a favor y en contra de la anexión. El artículo señala que, si bien la población, el clima y los términos de compra resultan favorables, los Estados Unidos ya poseen mucho más territorio del que requiere su población. El periódico sostiene que el argumento decisivo para la anexión es la adquisición de la bahía de Samaná para evitar que la isla caiga bajo la influencia monárquica europea, observando que los intereses comerciales alemanes ya han absorbido el comercio en Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The Kenosha Telegraph publishes extracts from the San Domingo commission report highlighting the advantages of acquisition and the condition of Dominican public finances. Under 'The Advantages of Annexation,' the commissioners state that acquiring the territory would provide a powerful military and naval base and foster an important commercial city at Samaná Bay, where an American citizen has already acquired waterfront property. They emphasize that easy water and rail communications with the interior make Samaná's future of national importance. The paper also reproduces the commissioners' statement of the government's debt and claims, listing unpaid salaries, treasury notes, and loans, followed by a summary of revenue from licenses and registry taxes.

Destacan que las fáciles comunicaciones fluviales y ferroviarias con el interior confieren a Samaná una importancia nacional para el futuro. El periódico también reproduce el balance de los comisionados sobre la deuda y reclamaciones del gobierno, enumerando sueldos impagos, billetes de tesorería y préstamos, seguido de un resumen de ingresos por licencias e impuestos de registro.

records.full_text:
UNANIMOUS FOR ANNEXATION.
The Dominicans repeat their wish to be annexed on the terms of the treaty of 1869, asking, in addition payment for rent for Samana bay during the two years the negotiations were pending. They are also willing to appropriate one-fifth of the public funds for schools, providing the United States will appropriate $300,000 for the establishment of an agricultural and scientific college. In relation to Dominican independence, the Commissioners say that there is but one chance for that republic ever to retain its independence; to become, after a period of probation, one of a union of states, the freedom and substantial dependence of each being guaranteed by the strength of all. It is under the resolution of Congress, to recommend that such a course be adopted or abstained from. They simply state as their belief, founded upon the observations they could make, and all the facts they could learn, that this is the only way in which Dominican independence can be secured, that if it should be judged best not to adopt that course, even the present shadow of independence will be taken away. The Dominican territory is one of the purest and richest on the earth. Unless some such means as are above mentioned are resorted to, it will lie exhausted and helpless until some nation shall seize and hold it in colonial subjection.

records.full_text:
THE GRANTS TO AMERICANS.
The Commissioners were not unmindful of various rumors which had been circulated on divers occasions, that concessions or grants of land were made to officials of the Government of the United States when the treaty of annexation was negotiated in 1869. No pains were spared to ascertain the exact truth of this statement. In addition to the examination of all grants from the government of the republic, the Commission further carried their researches to all municipal grants by the town of Samana, where rumor had located the supposed grants. The officers of the municipality and the records were carefully examined. Inquiries were also made of the authorities of the city of San Domingo. After this investigation the Commissioners can declare, without hesitation, that there is no particle of evidence for these charges.

records.headline: The Buchanan County Bulletin publishes the conclusion of the San Domingo commission
records.summary_en: The Buchanan County Bulletin publishes the conclusion of the San Domingo commission report alongside findings from their investigation into municipal administration. The commissioners explain that Haitian reluctance to permit exploration into the interior obliged them to rely on indirect information regarding that republic. In their conclusion, they affirm their conviction that annexing Santo Domingo to the United States would benefit Haitians as well as Dominicans by offering an example of orderly government and establishing a permanent, guaranteed frontier between the two nations to halt border warfare. The report also notes that a careful inquiry into municipal officers and records in the city of Santo Domingo revealed no evidence supporting charges against local authorities.
records.summary_es: El Buchanan County Bulletin publica la conclusión del informe de la comisión de Santo Domingo junto con los resultados de su investigación sobre la administración municipal. Los comisionados explican que la renuencia haitiana a permitir exploraciones en el interior los obligó a recurrir a información indirecta sobre esa república. En su conclusión, afirman su convicción de que la anexión de Santo Domingo a los Estados Unidos beneficiaría tanto a los haitianos como a los dominicanos, al ofrecer el ejemplo de un gobierno ordenado y fijar una frontera permanente y garantizada entre ambas naciones para frenar las guerras fronterizas. El informe señala asimismo que una minuciosa pesquisa sobre los funcionarios y registros municipales de la ciudad de Santo Domingo no arrojó prueba alguna que sustentara las acusaciones contra las autoridades locales.

records.summary_en: The Buchanan County Bulletin prints sections of the San Domingo commission report evaluating the strategic value of Samaná Bay and the state of the Dominican public debt. The commissioners describe Samaná, Ocoa, and Manzanillo as deep-water harbors, highlighting Samaná as a future military and naval stronghold capable of sustaining a major commercial city linked to the interior by rail and water. Under 'The Debt of the Government,' the paper reproduces the commissioners' itemized balance sheet of public obligations, listing unpaid salaries, treasury notes, Cabral's obligations, and various loans, followed by a summary of revenue from licenses, stamped paper, and postal services.

Bajo «The Debt of the Government», el periódico reproduce el balance desglosado de las obligaciones públicas elaborado por los comisionados, enumerando sueldos impagos, billetes de tesorería, obligaciones de Cabral y diversos préstamos, seguido de un resumen de ingresos por licencias, papel sellado y servicios postales.

records.headline: The Vermont Phœnix reports arguments delivered by Senator Justin Morrill
records.summary_en: The Vermont Phœnix reports arguments delivered by Senator Justin Morrill against the annexation of Santo Domingo. Morrill warns that displaying American naval and financial power excites the jealousy and fear of neighboring republics, whereas the United States should serve as their counselor and guide rather than a beast of prey. He questions whether the American population is sufficiently homogeneous to assimilate new territory, pointing out that recently acquired regions like Alaska, Arizona, Utah, and New Mexico remain largely un-American. Observing that former slaveholders in the South will do little to elevate emancipated laborers, he urges against multiplying national risks, concluding that Samaná Bay would prove a costly burden rather than a necessary commercial harbor.
records.summary_es: El Vermont Phœnix informa sobre los argumentos presentados por el senador Justin Morrill contra la anexión de Santo Domingo. Morrill advierte que el despliegue del poder naval y financiero estadounidense despierta los celos y el temor de las repúblicas vecinas, cuando los Estados Unidos deberían servirles de consejero y guía en lugar de actuar como una bestia de presa. Cuestiona si la población estadounidense es lo bastante homogénea como para asimilar nuevos territorios, señalando que regiones recientemente adquiridas como Alaska, Arizona, Utah y Nuevo México siguen siendo en gran medida no asimiladas. Al observar que los antiguos amos en el Sur harán pocos sacrificios para elevar a los trabajadores emancipados, insta a no multiplicar los riesgos nacionales, concluyendo que la bahía de Samaná resultaría una carga costosa en vez de un puerto comercial necesario.

records.headline: The Springfield Weekly Republican reports Mr. Morrill's remarks
records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican reports Mr. Morrill's remarks, urging the United States to suspend annexations and cultivate friendship with neighboring nations. If any territory is acquired, Morrill contends it should be Canada, a contiguous land of kindred stock and tongue, rather than San Domingo. He argues that annexing San Domingo would heavily increase American taxes, asserting it is absurd to expect that a country with no public lands and 120,000 to 160,000 poor inhabitants unwilling to labor could contribute anything toward the national debt. Criticizing President Grant's December message, he maintains that treasury funds would only flow outward, and begins addressing the commercial argument regarding Samaná Bay.
records.summary_es: El Springfield Weekly Republican informa sobre las declaraciones del señor Morrill, en las que insta a los Estados Unidos a suspender las anexiones y cultivar la amistad con las naciones vecinas. Si se adquiere algún territorio, Morrill sostiene que debería ser Canadá, una tierra contigua de linaje e idioma afines, en lugar de Santo Domingo. Sostiene que anexar a Santo Domingo aumentaría considerablemente los impuestos estadounidenses, afirmando que es absurdo esperar que un país sin tierras públicas y con entre 120,000 y 160,000 habitantes pobres y poco dispuestos a trabajar pueda aportar algo al pago de la deuda pública. Al criticar el mensaje de diciembre del presidente Grant, sostiene que los fondos del tesoro solo saldrían sin retorno, y comienza a abordar el argumento comercial relativo a la bahía de Samaná.

records.headline: The Burlington Weekly Free Press reports Senator Morrill's speech
records.summary_en: The Burlington Weekly Free Press reports Senator Morrill's speech warning that the proposed annexation of Santo Domingo would burden the United States with a costly elephant. Morrill questions whether the American people are sufficiently homogeneous to assimilate the territory, noting that populations in earlier acquisitions lack attachment to American institutions. He argues that the voyage of the Tennessee, which remained out of communication with the world for thirty-three days, demonstrates the total absence of commercial traffic along the Samaná route and its useless remoteness. Furthermore, he declares that the bay is proverbially unhealthy and too shallow for large vessels to approach within three miles of the shore, offering no protection to American shipping.
records.summary_es: El Burlington Weekly Free Press informa sobre el discurso del senador Morrill en el que advierte que la propuesta anexión de Santo Domingo impondría a los Estados Unidos la carga de un elefante costoso. Morrill cuestiona si el pueblo estadounidense es suficientemente homogéneo para asimilar el territorio, señalando que las poblaciones de adquisiciones anteriores carecen de apego a las instituciones estadounidenses. Sostiene que el viaje del Tennessee, que permaneció incomunicado del mundo durante treinta y tres días, demuestra la total ausencia de tráfico comercial en la ruta de Samaná y su inútil lejanía. Además, afirma que la bahía es proverbialmente malsana y demasiado poco profunda para que buques de gran calado se acerquen a menos de tres millas de la costa, sin ofrecer protección alguna a la marina mercante estadounidense.

records.passage: CONDITION OF THE COUNTRY. The Commissioners found the government organized and in complete operation in all its departments, exercising every function of legitimate Government, with Gen. Buenaventura Baez as Chief Magistrate, in full and peaceable possession of all parts of the republic except on the Haytien border, which is disturbed by insurrectionary leaders, aided by the Haytiens and political intriguers. These are incited to be extraordinarily active at this time by the fear of annexation to the United States. From all that the Commissioners could ascertain, President Baez has the respect of a great majority of the Dominican people for his administrative abilities, and the strong attachment of many leading men, who regard him as the only statesman among them who can hold them together against domestic factions and foreign foes. In [illegible], after five years of anarchy, consequent on the expulsion of the Haytien power, Gen. Baez was regularly elected President of the republic. It appears that he was chosen as the man who, by his education, fortune and public services, would be most likely to secure general confidence and heal the wounds inflicted by the civil and foreign wars. In one of the delegations of leading citizens who tendered to him the Chief Magistracy, was Gen. Cabral. There is credible testimony to the fact that, under him, despite the difficulties that have beset him, the republic has enjoyed as much liberty as any of his predecessors dared to allow, and more tranquility than they knew how

records.headline: The South-eastern Independent prints extracts from the report of the United States Commissioners
records.summary_en: The South-eastern Independent prints extracts from the report of the United States Commissioners to Santo Domingo concerning border warfare and Dominican internal stability. The Commissioners conclude that Dominican insurgents would long ago have been suppressed had they not received foreign assistance and backing from Haiti, a neighboring state with nearly three times the Dominican Republic's population and revenue. They state that Haitian authorities have maintained an unrelenting aggressive policy under a president brought to power by a bloody insurrection. Additionally, the Commissioners observe that provincial rivalries and regional chieftains aggravate Dominican difficulties, but express their belief that these challenges would disappear if the republic were protected through connection with a stronger power.
records.summary_es: El South-eastern Independent publica extractos del informe de los comisionados de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo sobre la guerra fronteriza y la estabilidad interna dominicana. Los comisionados concluyen que los insurgentes dominicanos habrían sido sofocados hace mucho tiempo de no haber contado con auxilio extranjero y con el respaldo de Haití, un Estado vecino que casi triplica la población y los ingresos de la República Dominicana. Señalan que las autoridades haitianas han mantenido una política agresiva implacable bajo el mando de un presidente elevado al poder mediante una insurrección sangrienta. Asimismo, los comisionados observan que las rivalidades provinciales y los caudillos regionales agravan las dificultades dominicanas, pero expresan su convicción de que estos problemas desaparecerían si la república fuera protegida mediante su vinculación con una potencia más fuerte.

records.summary_en: The newspaper reported that a Senator argued the annexation of Santo Domingo would provoke the jealousy and fear of other American republics, which view the United States without special affection due to past difficulties with Paraguay, Cuba, Peru, and Brazil. Furthermore, the Senator stated that the people of Santo Domingo are not homogeneous with America, making the territory a costly burden, and asserted that the Monroe Doctrine does not justify the United States seizing adjoining lands.
records.summary_es: El diario dio cuenta de la intervención de un senador quien sostuvo que la anexión de Santo Domingo concitaría los recelos y el temor de las demás repúblicas americanas, las cuales miraban a los Estados Unidos sin particular simpatía a raíz de pasados diferendos con Paraguay, Cuba, Perú y Brasil. Agregó además que la población de Santo Domingo no guardaba afinidad ni homogeneidad con el pueblo estadounidense, constituyendo el territorio una carga onerosa, y afirmó que la doctrina Monroe jamás justificaba la apropiación de territorios circunvecinos por parte de los Estados Unidos.

records.full_text:
A BULLY AMONG REPUBLICS.
Our reputation among sister republics in America the Senator did not consider wholly unblemished, and it was not likely to grow brighter from Santo Domingo complications. Our experience with Mexico when Texas became a part of this Union; the Greytown affair in 1852; the career of Walker, the fillibuster; our difficulty with Paraguy for ten years or more; our attitude toward Cuba; the trouble with Peru in 1860; a recent unpleasantness with Brazil in regard to the passage of the gunboat Wasp, up the Paraguy to relieve Minister Washburn, were recited to show that there was no special love for this government among those nations. The annexation of Santo Domingo, whether of spontaneous origin or nursed by the military, naval and financial power of the United States, cannot fail to excite the jealousy and fear of all the American republics.

records.headline: An editorial in the Bellows Falls Times argues that the Dominican people
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Bellows Falls Times argues that the Dominican people do not favor American annexation, recalling that they previously drove Spanish forces from their territory through revolution. The paper asserts that the plebiscite favoring annexation was a delusive juggle engineered through the inducements of President Báez and the intimidating presence of United States naval guns. It notes that General Cabral and his followers actively contest the transaction in arms, holding an estimated 10,000 of the republic's 22,212 square miles in conjunction with Haiti. Under the heading "Santo Domingo and Her Debts Go Together," the editorial warns that the United States would be legally and honorably bound to assume all Dominican liabilities, rendering any disclaimer by Báez worthless.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en el Bellows Falls Times sostiene que el pueblo dominicano no favorece la anexión a los Estados Unidos, recordando que anteriormente expulsó a las fuerzas españolas de su territorio mediante una revolución. El periódico afirma que el plebiscito a favor de la anexión fue una maniobra engañosa orquestada mediante las dádivas del presidente Báez y la presencia intimidatoria de los cañones de la Armada estadounidense. Señala que el general Cabral y sus partidarios combaten activamente la transacción con las armas en la mano, controlando unas 10,000 de las 22,212 millas cuadradas de la república conjuntamente con Haití. Bajo el encabezado «Santo Domingo y sus deudas van juntos», el editorial advierte que los Estados Unidos quedarían obligados jurídica y moralmente a asumir todas las deudas dominicanas, careciendo de valor cualquier compromiso en contrario suscrito con Báez.

records.headline: The Bellows Falls Times publishes the concluding portion of Senator Justin Morrill's speech
records.summary_en: The Bellows Falls Times publishes the concluding portion of Senator Justin Morrill's speech against the annexation of Santo Domingo. Morrill observes that the American Constitution provides no direct authority for territorial annexations and denies the existence of any enlightened public sentiment favoring the measure. He contends that President Grant's personal popularity constitutes the entire backbone of the annexation project, asserting that without executive endorsement it would lack even a corporal's guard of supporters. In closing, Morrill appeals to national honor, declaring that he will not jeopardize the country's enduring character or exchange its moral grandeur for mere material greatness.
records.summary_es: El Bellows Falls Times publica la parte final del discurso del senador Justin Morrill contra la anexión de Santo Domingo. Morrill observa que la Constitución estadounidense no otorga autoridad directa para anexiones territoriales y niega la existencia de una opinión pública ilustrada que respalde la medida. Sostiene que la popularidad personal del presidente Grant constituye la única fuerza motriz del proyecto de anexión, afirmando que sin el respaldo del ejecutivo la iniciativa no contaría ni con un piquete de partidarios. Para concluir, Morrill apela al honor nacional, declarando que no pondrá en riesgo el carácter perdurable del país ni cambiará su grandeza moral por mera grandeza material.

records.summary_en: Commissioners reported the Dominican government in complete operation under Báez except on the Haitian border, disturbed by insurrectionary leaders aided by Haitians and made active by fear of U.S. annexation. They said Báez had the respect of a great majority of Dominicans and had given the republic as much liberty and more tranquility than predecessors, recounting his 1848 election after the expulsion of Haitian power.

records.headline: The Spirit of Democracy publishes findings from the report of the United States Commissioners
records.summary_en: The Spirit of Democracy publishes findings from the report of the United States Commissioners to Santo Domingo detailing the island's population, minerals, and agriculture. The report states that white ancestry largely predominates among native Dominicans and affirms that the country possesses vast resources capable of extensive development through labor. Geologists accompanying the expedition identify deposits of iron, copper, gold, lignite, rock salt, and petroleum, noting that abundant iron ore could support cheap pig iron production, while reported coal at Samaná and Puerto Plata proved to be inferior lignite. The Commissioners report that extensive salt formations near Neiba yield pure blocks for commerce, and they identify rich mountain slopes and valleys as the first of five agricultural land classes.
records.summary_es: The Spirit of Democracy publica las conclusiones del informe de los comisionados de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo sobre la población, los minerales y la agricultura de la isla. El informe señala que la ascendencia blanca predomina ampliamente entre los dominicanos nativos y afirma que el país posee vastos recursos susceptibles de un gran desarrollo mediante el trabajo. Los geólogos de la expedición identifican yacimientos de hierro, cobre, oro, lignito, sal gema y petróleo, destacando que el abundante mineral de hierro permitiría una producción económica de arrabio, mientras que el supuesto carbón en Samaná y Puerto Plata resultó ser lignito de escaso valor. Los comisionados informan que extensos depósitos de sal cerca de Neiba producen bloques puros para el comercio, y clasifican las ricas laderas y valles montañosos como la primera de cinco clases de tierras agrícolas.

records.headline: The commissioners' report states that acquiring Samana Bay would give the United States a powerful military and naval
records.summary_en: The commissioners' report states that acquiring Samana Bay would give the United States a powerful military and naval station and the site of an important commercial city, with easy inland communication by water and rail. The report also sets out the results of its inquiry into the Dominican government's debt and obligations, including unpaid salaries, bonds, loans and pending claims, and presents a statement of the republic's revenue for 1870.

El informe también expone los resultados de su investigación sobre la deuda y las obligaciones del gobierno dominicano, incluidos sueldos impagos, bonos, préstamos y reclamaciones pendientes, y presenta un estado de los ingresos de la república en 1870.

records.headline: The Spirit of Democracy prints an extract regarding the mission
records.summary_en: The Spirit of Democracy prints an extract regarding the mission to Haiti and conclusions on Santo Domingo of the United States Commissioners. their mission to Haiti and conclusions on Santo Domingo. The Commissioners state that they sought to ascertain Haitian claims regarding Santo Domingo and the views of the Haitian people concerning political changes on the island, but their requests to travel into the interior were met with what amounted to a refusal. Reviewing the interests of both divisions of the island, the Commissioners express their conviction that annexation to the United States would be hardly less beneficial to Haitians than to Dominicans. They argue that annexation would establish a peaceful, orderly state in the region and provide an equitable boundary line between the French-speaking and Spanish-speaking populations.
records.summary_es: The Spirit of Democracy publica un extracto del informe de los comisionados de los Estados Unidos, relativo a su misión en Haití y sus conclusiones sobre Santo Domingo. Los comisionados exponen que procuraron conocer las reclamaciones haitianas sobre Santo Domingo y la opinión del pueblo haitiano respecto a los cambios políticos en la isla, pero sus solicitudes para viajar al interior recibieron una respuesta equivalente a una negativa. Al examinar los intereses de ambas divisiones de la isla, los comisionados manifiestan su convicción de que la anexión a los Estados Unidos resultaría casi tan beneficiosa para los haitianos como para los dominicanos. Sostienen que la anexión implantaría un Estado pacífico y ordenado en la región y establecería una línea fronteriza equitativa entre las poblaciones francófona e hispanohablante.

records.headline: An editorial attacks the report of the Commissioners appointed by Grant to investigate whether it was politic to annex
records.summary_en: An editorial attacks the report of the Commissioners appointed by Grant to investigate whether it was politic to annex San Domingo to the United States, calling it a document prepared to please Baez and full of falsehoods, and noting that Grant, after laying it before Congress, backed down and refused to press its consideration. The paper also publishes two letters from General Cabral inviting the Commissioners to visit his headquarters and the country held by his forces and ask the people whether they favored annexation, an invitation the editorial says the Commissioners were very careful not to accept.
records.summary_es: Un editorial ataca el informe de los comisionados nombrados por Grant para investigar si era conveniente anexar Santo Domingo a los Estados Unidos, calificándolo de documento preparado para complacer a Báez y lleno de falsedades, y señalando que Grant, después de presentarlo al Congreso, dio marcha atrás y se negó a impulsar su consideración. El periódico publica también dos cartas del general Cabral invitando a los comisionados a visitar su cuartel general y el territorio ocupado por sus fuerzas y a preguntar al pueblo si favorecía la anexión, una invitación que el editorial dice que los comisionados tuvieron mucho cuidado de no aceptar.

records.headline: The Spirit of Democracy prints a letter addressed to the United States Commissioners
records.summary_en: The Spirit of Democracy prints a letter addressed to the United States Commissioners by insurgent leader General Cabral from his camp fifteen miles west of Azua. Cabral reminds the Commissioners of their mission to study the Dominican people's sentiments on annexation, declaring that Dominicans have protested against the treaty not only in writing, but daily with arms in hand for more than a year. He informs them that General W. Álvarez and Francisco Travieso have been dispatched to escort them should they choose to inspect the revolutionary districts in person. The paper adds a political notice reporting that the Ohio Legislature endorsed President Grant's principle that no territorial acquisition should be enforced against the will of the American people.
records.summary_es: The Spirit of Democracy publica una carta dirigida a los comisionados de los Estados Unidos por el líder insurgente general Cabral desde su campamento a quince millas al oeste de Azua. Cabral recuerda a los comisionados su misión de estudiar los sentimientos del pueblo dominicano sobre la anexión, manifestando que los dominicanos han protestado contra el tratado no solo por escrito, sino a diario con las armas en la mano durante más de un año. Les comunica que el general W. Álvarez y Francisco Travieso han sido comisionados para escoltarlos en caso de que decidan inspeccionar personalmente las localidades en revolución. El periódico añade una nota política informando que la Legislatura de Ohio respaldó el principio del presidente Grant de que ninguna adquisición territorial debe imponerse contra la voluntad del pueblo estadounidense.

records.headline: The Green-Mountain Freeman publishes remarks urging that arguments
records.summary_en: The Green-Mountain Freeman publishes remarks urging that arguments against annexing Santo Domingo be heard alongside the dissemination of the Commissioners' forthcoming report. While expressing differences with the administration's annexation policy, the speaker credits President Grant with pure intentions and declines to attack his personal reputation. The speaker anticipates that the Commissioners will praise the Dominican climate simply because a five-week stay caused them no illness, and will commend the soil for yielding tropical fruits like bananas and pineapples unknown in Northern states. He predicts the report will speak slightingly of reported gold, copper, and iron mines once examined at close hand, and despondently regarding coal at Samaná, where only inferior lignite was found.
records.summary_es: El Green-Mountain Freeman publica declaraciones en las que se insta a que los argumentos contra la anexión de Santo Domingo se escuchen a la par de la divulgación del próximo informe de los comisionados. Aunque expresa discrepancias con la política anexionista del gobierno, el orador reconoce al presidente Grant intenciones puras y rehúsa atacar su reputación personal. Anticipa que los comisionados elogiarán el clima dominicano sencillamente porque una estancia de cinco semanas no les causó enfermedades, y alabarán el suelo por producir frutas tropicales como plátanos y piñas desconocidas en los estados del Norte. Pronostica que el informe hablará con desdén de las supuestas minas de oro, cobre y hierro al examinarlas de cerca, y con desaliento respecto al carbón de Samaná, donde solo se halló lignito de inferior calidad.

records.headline: The Green-Mountain Freeman publishes arguments refuting the claim
records.summary_en: The Green-Mountain Freeman publishes arguments refuting the claim that Samaná Bay is required to protect American commerce, under the printed headline "Bay of Samana a Costly Elephant." The article contends that Samaná cannot serve as a coaling station unless coal is transported there from elsewhere, noting that Santo Domingo lies far eastward of standard shipping lanes. Steamers bound for Aspinwall travel west of Haiti and far away from Samaná, while vessels trading with Mexico and the Gulf States navigate between Florida and Cuba to utilize the Gulf Stream. The paper maintains that foreign ownership of West Indian islands has never injured American shipping, arguing that commerce destined for Louisiana or Texas would never make an eastward detour to visit Samaná.
records.summary_es: El Green-Mountain Freeman publica argumentos, bajo el titular impreso «La bahía de Samaná, un elefante costoso», que refutan la afirmación de que la bahía de Samaná sea necesaria para proteger el comercio estadounidense. El artículo sostiene que Samaná no puede servir como estación carbonera a menos que se transporte carbón hasta allí desde otros lugares, señalando que Santo Domingo queda muy al este de las rutas marítimas habituales. Los vapores con destino a Aspinwall navegan al oeste de Haití y muy apartados de Samaná, mientras que los buques que comercian con México y los estados del Golfo transitan entre Florida y Cuba para aprovechar la corriente del Golfo. El periódico sostiene que la posesión extranjera de islas antillanas nunca ha perjudicado a la marina mercante estadounidense, afirmando que el comercio hacia Luisiana o Texas jamás se desviaría hacia el este para tocar Samaná.

records.headline: Samaná Bay offers no protection to American shipping and is unnecessary for national defense
records.summary_en: Samaná Bay offers no protection to American shipping and is unnecessary for national defense, according to arguments reported by The Vermont Watchman and State Journal. The speaker contends that vessels would have to sail 240 miles out of their course and 240 miles back—a useless voyage of 480 miles—merely to reach a remote harbor, suggesting that the demand for Samaná is only an excuse to acquire the whole of Santo Domingo. He asserts that the United States possesses ample territory and that the population of the country he calls Dominica is impoverished, unaccustomed to labor, and racially incompatible with American society in language, customs, and religion. He warns that under any treaty or joint resolution, San Domingo would ultimately have to be admitted as a full state with its own senators and representatives.
records.summary_es: El Vermont Watchman and State Journal informa sobre los argumentos relativos a la bahía de Samaná, que señalan que la bahía no ofrece protección a la marina mercante estadounidense y resulta innecesaria para la defensa nacional. El orador sostiene que los buques tendrían que desviarse 240 millas de su rumbo y otras 240 millas de regreso —una travesía inútil de 480 millas— simplemente para llegar a un puerto remoto, sugiriendo que la petición de Samaná no es más que una excusa para apoderarse de todo Santo Domingo. Afirma que los Estados Unidos ya poseen tierras suficientes y que la población del país que llama Dominica es pobre, poco habituada al trabajo e incompatible con la sociedad estadounidense en idioma, costumbres y religión. Advierte que, mediante tratado o resolución conjunta, Santo Domingo tendría que ser admitido en última instancia como un estado con sus propios senadores y representantes.

records.headline: The Nebraska Advertiser publishes extracts from the United States Commissioners' report
records.summary_en: The Nebraska Advertiser publishes extracts from the United States Commissioners' report evaluating Samaná Bay and Dominican finances. The Commissioners present Samaná Bay as an advantageous military and naval station with prospects for the growth of an important city of national importance under United States authority. Under the heading "Financial Statement," the report presents an inquiry into government debts and obligations, alongside a resume of revenues for 1870 designed to show the republic's overall financial condition. Listed receipts and categories include customs revenues, lighthouse dues, anchorage, pilotage, wharfage, and import and export dues. The statement also catalogues fiscal liabilities, including unpaid official salaries, bonds, treasury notes, general loans, and obligations owed to Cabral.
records.summary_es: El Nebraska Advertiser publica extractos del informe de los comisionados de los Estados Unidos que evalúan la bahía de Samaná y las finanzas dominicanas. Los comisionados presentan la bahía de Samaná como una ventajosa estación militar y naval con perspectivas para el crecimiento de una ciudad de importancia nacional bajo la autoridad de los Estados Unidos. Bajo el encabezado «Financial Statement», el informe presenta una indagación sobre las deudas y obligaciones gubernamentales, junto con un resumen de ingresos para 1870 concebido para mostrar la condición financiera general de la república. Los ingresos y renglones enumerados incluyen rentas aduaneras, derechos de faro, anclaje, practicaje, muellaje y derechos de importación y exportación. El estado también cataloga pasivos fiscales, entre ellos sueldos oficiales impagos, bonos, notas del tesoro, préstamos generales y obligaciones con Cabral.

records.headline: Commissioners found the Dominican government organized and in complete operation under General Báez, in peaceable possession of all
records.summary_en: Commissioners found the Dominican government organized and in complete operation under General Báez, in peaceable possession of all the republic except the Haitian border disturbed by insurrectionary leaders aided by Haitians and active from fear of U.S. annexation. They said Báez had the respect of a great majority of Dominicans, recounting his 1848 election after the expulsion of Haitian power and the tranquility under him.
records.summary_es: Los comisionados encontraron el gobierno dominicano organizado y en completa operación bajo el general Báez, en posesión pacífica de toda la república excepto la frontera haitiana perturbada por líderes insurrectos ayudados por haitianos y activos por temor a la anexión estadounidense. Dijeron que Báez contaba con el respeto de una gran mayoría de los dominicanos, relatando su elección de 1848 tras la expulsión del poder haitiano y la tranquilidad bajo su gobierno.

records.headline: This portion of the commissioners' report describes San Domingo's abundance: cotton raised near Azua, cinchona on the higher
records.summary_en: This portion of the commissioners' report describes San Domingo's abundance: cotton raised near Azua, cinchona on the higher mountains, tobacco suited to the whole country, three crops of Indian corn a year, more than forty kinds of tropical fruit, and immense herds of cattle on the savannas. It also describes the island's forest products, neglected but well-stocked fisheries, and its health, concluding that the popular idea that Dominican territory is particularly unhealthy and liable to yellow fever is entirely erroneous.

También describe los productos forestales de la isla, sus pesquerías descuidadas pero bien provistas, y su salubridad, concluyendo que la idea popular de que el territorio dominicano es particularmente insalubre y propenso a la fiebre amarilla es enteramente errónea.

records.summary_en: The commissioners report that earthquakes have done no serious damage in the island since 1846 and that the slight shocks each year are scarcely noticed, though hurricanes sometimes cause considerable damage. Of the island's three great bays, Samana, Azua and Manzanilla, only Samana has military importance, and the commissioners state that acquiring it would give a powerful military and naval station and the site of a great commercial city; the report then sets out the government's debt and finances.

records.headline: Under the headline "The President's Message," the Holmes County Republican quotes
records.summary_en: Under the headline "The President's Message," the Holmes County Republican quotes commentary from the Philadelphia Ledger evaluating President Grant's message on Santo Domingo. The Ledger, described as an independent paper with Democratic leanings, commends the President's plain and straightforward narrative recounting how he first learned of the Dominican people's desire for annexation to the United States. It characterizes Grant's intentions as clear and honorable, praising his patient forbearance in enduring harsh criticism of his official judgment and personal attacks upon his integrity. The excerpt concludes that Grant remained patient because he was confident the facts, once laid before the public, would fully vindicate his conduct.
records.summary_es: Bajo el titular «El mensaje del presidente», el Holmes County Republican cita un comentario del Philadelphia Ledger que evalúa el mensaje del presidente Grant sobre Santo Domingo. El Ledger, descrito como un diario independiente de inclinación demócrata, elogia la narración llana y directa del mandatario al relatar cómo conoció por primera vez el deseo del pueblo dominicano de anexionarse a los Estados Unidos. Califica las intenciones de Grant de claras y honorables, alabando la paciente moderación con la que soportó duras críticas a su juicio oficial y ataques personales contra su integridad. El extracto concluye señalando que Grant mantuvo la calma porque confiaba en que los hechos, una vez expuestos ante el público, vindicarían plenamente su conducta.

records.headline: The Tama County Republican publishes, from the official report of the United States Commissioners
records.summary_en: The Tama County Republican publishes, from the official report of the United States Commissioners to Santo Domingo, the sections headed "Hayti" and "Conclusion". In the section on Haiti, the Commissioners report that they sought to ascertain Haitian claims regarding Santo Domingo and the sentiments of the Haitian people regarding neighboring political changes, but their overtures to the Haitian president were discouraged and their request to explore the interior was met with a virtual refusal. In their conclusion, the Commissioners express their firm conviction that the annexation of Santo Domingo would be hardly less beneficial to the Haitian people than to Dominicans. They argue that this benefit would stem from establishing a well-ordered, prosperous state in the region and creating an equitable boundary between the French-speaking and Spanish-speaking nations.
records.summary_es: El Tama County Republican publica las secciones tituladas «Hayti» y «Conclusion» del informe oficial de los comisionados de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo. En la sección sobre Haití, los comisionados informan que intentaron conocer las reclamaciones haitianas sobre Santo Domingo y los sentimientos del pueblo haitiano respecto a los cambios políticos en el país vecino, pero sus gestiones ante el presidente haitiano fueron desatendidas y su solicitud para explorar el interior fue recibida con una virtual negativa. En su conclusión, los comisionados manifiestan su firme convicción de que la anexión de Santo Domingo resultaría casi tan beneficiosa para el pueblo haitiano como para los dominicanos. Sostienen que este beneficio provendría del establecimiento de un Estado bien ordenado y próspero en la región y de la creación de una frontera equitativa entre las naciones francófona e hispanohablante.

records.headline: Under the headline "What Jamaica Thinks of Annexation," the New National Era reprints
records.summary_en: Under the headline "What Jamaica Thinks of Annexation," the New National Era reprints an editorial from the Kingston Morning Journal of March 14, 1871, regarding the United States Commission to Santo Domingo. The Jamaican journal observes that while the annexation of the Dominican Republic to the United States would once have appeared disastrous for West Indian populations, that era has passed. It explains that the emancipation of four million enslaved people in the United States represents a revolution exceeding even American independence, transforming former chattels into free citizens eligible for public office and high honors. The editorial highlights that no American political mission had ever before been composed of such diverse personnel, remarking upon the presence of individuals of African descent.
records.summary_es: Bajo el titular «What Jamaica Thinks of Annexation», el New National Era reproduce un editorial del Kingston Morning Journal del 14 de marzo de 1871 sobre la Comisión de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo. El diario jamaiquino observa que, si bien la anexión de la República Dominicana a los Estados Unidos habría parecido en otro tiempo desastrosa para las poblaciones antillanas, esa época ya ha quedado atrás. Explica que la emancipación de cuatro millones de personas esclavizadas en los Estados Unidos constituye una revolución superior incluso a la independencia estadounidense, al transformar a antiguos siervos en ciudadanos libres elegibles para cargos públicos y altos honores. El editorial resalta que ninguna misión política estadounidense anterior había estado integrada por miembros tan diversos, destacando la presencia de personas de ascendencia africana.

records.headline: The New National Era continues reprinting the Kingston Morning Journal's editorial
records.summary_en: The New National Era continues reprinting the Kingston Morning Journal's editorial concerning the mission of Senator Benjamin F. Wade to Santo Domingo. The Jamaican paper views the commission's work as a historic movement that offers a solution to the problem of Dominican self-government. It predicts that Dominicans will learn governance from their American fellow citizens and quickly become a progressive people, anticipating that within another generation the Dominican Republic could be admitted into the Union as the State of Dominica. The editorial suggests that such a state would shine brightly in the American constellation and serve as a model for other Caribbean territories, expressing confidence that Senator Wade's mission has laid the foundation for that future.
records.summary_es: El New National Era continúa la reproducción del editorial del Kingston Morning Journal sobre la misión del senador Benjamin F. Wade en Santo Domingo. El periódico jamaiquino considera la labor de la comisión como un movimiento histórico que ofrece una solución al problema del autogobierno dominicano. Pronostica que los dominicanos aprenderán a gobernarse de sus conciudadanos estadounidenses y se convertirán rápidamente en un pueblo progresista, anticipando que en el término de otra generación la República Dominicana podría ingresar a la Unión como el Estado de Dominica. El editorial sugiere que dicho estado brillaría intensamente en la constelación estadounidense y serviría de modelo para otros territorios del Caribe, expresando confianza en que la misión del senador Wade ha sentado las bases de ese porvenir.

records.headline: The West-Jersey Pioneer publishes the conclusion of the Santo Domingo Commission's report
records.summary_en: The West-Jersey Pioneer publishes the conclusion of the Santo Domingo Commission's report and President Grant's accompanying message transmitting it to Congress on April 5, 1871. In their concluding remarks, Commissioners B. F. Wade, Andrew D. White, and S. G. Howe assert that annexation would end exhausting border warfare between Haiti and Santo Domingo, allowing both nations to direct their resources toward public education and economic development. In his message, President Grant states that his official duty is finished and hands the issue over to Congress and the American people. While reiterating that his own belief in the mutual benefits of annexation is confirmed by the report, Grant recommends taking no legislative action during the current session beyond printing and disseminating the document for public consideration.
records.summary_es: El West-Jersey Pioneer publica la conclusión del informe de la Comisión de Santo Domingo y el mensaje adjunto del presidente Grant con el que lo transmitió al Congreso el 5 de abril de 1871. En sus observaciones finales, los comisionados B. F. Wade, Andrew D. White y S. G. Howe afirman que la anexión pondría fin a la desgastante guerra fronteriza entre Haití y Santo Domingo, permitiendo a ambas naciones encauzar sus recursos hacia la educación pública y el desarrollo económico. En su mensaje, el presidente Grant manifiesta que su deber oficial ha concluido y deja el asunto en manos del Congreso y del pueblo estadounidense. Aunque reitera que el informe confirma su convicción sobre los beneficios mutuos de la anexión, Grant recomienda no adoptar ninguna medida legislativa durante la presente legislatura, aparte de imprimir y difundir el documento para la consideración pública.

records.headline: Under the heading "Political State and Form of Government,"
records.summary_en: Under the heading "Political State and Form of Government," the Ashtabula Weekly Telegraph publishes an excerpt from the United States Commission's report outlining Dominican political institutions. Following notes on their examination of official records and supplementary inquiries conducted during a week-long stay in Port-au-Prince, the Commissioners describe the Dominican government as theoretically a constitutional republic with executive, legislative, and judicial branches. The executive consists of a president and vice president chosen by an electoral college for six-year terms and barred from immediate re-election, assisted by an appointed Council of State consisting of four ministerial portfolios. The legislative branch, known as the Senado Consulto, comprises nine members chosen by primary assemblies—two representing Santo Domingo City, two for Santiago, and one for each remaining province and district.
records.summary_es: Bajo el encabezado «Political State and Form of Government», el Ashtabula Weekly Telegraph publica un extracto del informe de la Comisión de los Estados Unidos que describe las instituciones políticas dominicanas. Tras señalar el examen de documentos oficiales y las averiguaciones complementarias realizadas durante una estancia de una semana en Puerto Príncipe, los comisionados describen el gobierno dominicano como una república constitucional en teoría, dividida en los poderes ejecutivo, legislativo y judicial. El ejecutivo se compone de un presidente y un vicepresidente elegidos por un colegio electoral por mandatos de seis años y sin posibilidad de reelección inmediata, asistidos por un Consejo de Estado integrado por cuatro carteras ministeriales. El poder legislativo, denominado Senado Consulto, consta de nueve miembros elegidos por asambleas primarias: dos en representación de la ciudad de Santo Domingo, dos por Santiago y uno por cada provincia y distrito restante.

records.headline: From Port-au-Prince and Santo Domingo, The New York Herald publishes
records.summary_en: From Port-au-Prince and Santo Domingo, The New York Herald publishes telegraphic dispatches reporting political and military developments. An April 9 dispatch from Port-au-Prince via Havana states that the steamer Hornet is again offered for sale and will probably be purchased by the Dominicans, while public excitement concerning annexation is subsiding and a loan to redeem paper currency and establish specie payments is under discussion. An April 12 dispatch from Santo Domingo announces that government forces loyal to President Báez have once again defeated General Cabral. The dispatch adds that several indecisive engagements have also taken place recently in the northern provinces between troops commanded by General Luperón and forces belonging to Báez.

El informe añade que en las provincias del norte se han registrado recientemente varios enfrentamientos indecisos entre tropas comandadas por el general Luperón y fuerzas pertenecientes a Báez.

records.headline: An editorial paragraph in the New York Herald comments on a letter
records.summary_en: An editorial paragraph in the New York Herald comments on a letter sent by Dominican insurgent General Cabral to Vice President Schuyler Colfax. The paper reports that Cabral indignantly denies favoring annexation and swears never to lay down his arms until the country he calls Dominica is free. The Herald dismisses Cabral's declarations as excessive, asserting that he would likely favor annexation as eagerly as President Báez if he were receiving the purchase money or held substantial property in Samaná. The editorial concludes that the Dominican annexation question has been dropped in the United States, warning Cabral not to stir up dead issues that could disrupt Republican party harmony in upcoming political campaigns.
records.summary_es: Un suelto editorial en el New York Herald comenta una carta remitida por el general insurgente dominicano Cabral al vicepresidente Schuyler Colfax. El periódico señala que Cabral niega indignado favorecer la anexión y jura no deponer jamás las armas hasta que el país que llama Dominica sea libre. El Herald califica de excesivas las declaraciones de Cabral, afirmando que probablemente apoyaría la anexión con tanto entusiasmo como el presidente Báez si fuera el beneficiario del dinero de la compra o poseyera cuantiosas tierras en Samaná. El editorial concluye que el asunto de la anexión dominicana ha sido descartado en los Estados Unidos, advirtiendo a Cabral que no reviva temas extintos que puedan alterar la armonía del Partido Republicano en las próximas campañas políticas.

records.summary_en: The Memphis Daily Appeal publishes foreign telegraphic reports under the sarcastic heading "Delights of Grant's Paradise." An April 12 dispatch from San Domingo reports that troops supporting President Báez have again defeated General Cabral, while several indecisive engagements have recently taken place in the northern provinces between forces led by General Luperón and those loyal to Báez. An April 8 dispatch from Port-au-Prince via Havana, placed under the subhead "Peace and Quiet Partially Restored," reports that the steamer Hornet is offered for sale once more and will probably be bought by Dominicans. The item adds that public excitement concerning annexation is declining in San Domingo, and that a proposal to redeem paper currency and establish specie payments is being discussed.

Un despacho del 8 de abril desde Puerto Príncipe vía La Habana, situado bajo el subtítulo «Peace and Quiet Partially Restored», indica que el vapor Hornet se ofrece nuevamente en venta y probablemente será adquirido por los dominicanos. La nota añade que la agitación pública sobre la anexión disminuye en Santo Domingo y que se encuentra en discusión una propuesta para redimir el papel moneda y fijar pagos en metálico.

records.headline: The Daily State Journal reports on a lecture delivered by a traveler
records.summary_en: The Daily State Journal reports on a lecture delivered by a traveler who accompanied the United States Commission to Santo Domingo. The speaker extols the island's fertile soil and healthy climate, dismissing allegations that the temperature prevents labor by citing men contentedly sawing hardwood in the sun. At Samaná, he met an American colored colony whose original members he had seen depart from Baltimore forty-seven years earlier; six original settlers survived, while the community had grown to over six hundred descendants who maintained their Methodist church. Describing local sobriety and order, the lecturer notes that during three weeks in Santo Domingo City he saw only one drunken man, an American, and witnessed only one street dispute, concluding with a defense of the administration's policy.
records.summary_es: El Daily State Journal informa sobre una conferencia ofrecida por un viajero que acompañó a la Comisión de los Estados Unidos a Santo Domingo. El disertante elogia el fértil suelo y el clima saludable de la isla, descartando las afirmaciones de que la temperatura impide el trabajo al citar a hombres que aserraban maderas duras bajo el sol con total satisfacción. En Samaná se encontró con una colonia de negros estadounidenses cuyos primeros integrantes había visto zarpar desde Baltimore cuarenta y siete años atrás; seis de los pobladores originales aún vivían, mientras que la comunidad había crecido hasta superar los seiscientos descendientes, conservando su iglesia metodista. Al describir la sobriedad y el orden locales, el conferenciante señala que durante tres semanas en la ciudad de Santo Domingo solo vio a un ebrio, un estadounidense, y presenció una sola riña callejera, concluyendo con una defensa de la política del gobierno.

records.headline: The Prescott Journal prints extracts from the United States Commission's report
records.summary_en: The Prescott Journal prints extracts from the United States Commission's report describing the minerals, soils, and agriculture of Santo Domingo. The report states that iron ore is abundant and accessible for producing pig iron, whereas reported coal at Samaná and Puerto Plata proved to be inferior lignite. The Commissioners classify the island's soils into five agricultural categories, including mountain valleys, the Llanos, the fertile plain of La Vega, dry districts like Azua, and coastal red clay lands. Declaring Santo Domingo one of the most fertile regions on earth, the report catalogues abundant tropical crops, including sugar cane, coffee, tobacco, and valuable forest woods, while noting that local fisheries have fallen into neglect.
records.summary_es: El Prescott Journal publica extractos del informe de la Comisión de los Estados Unidos que describen los minerales, los suelos y la agricultura de Santo Domingo. El informe señala que el mineral de hierro es abundante y accesible para producir arrabio, mientras que el supuesto carbón en Samaná y Puerto Plata resultó ser lignito inferior. Los comisionados clasifican los suelos de la isla en cinco categorías agrícolas, que comprenden los valles montañosos, los Llanos, la fértil llanura de La Vega, regiones secas como Azua y tierras costeras de arcilla roja. Tras declarar a Santo Domingo como una de las regiones más fértiles del planeta, el informe cataloga abundantes cultivos tropicales, entre ellos caña de azúcar, café, tabaco y valiosas maderas forestales, observando al mismo tiempo que las pesquerías locales han caído en el abandono.

records.headline: The Evening Telegraph reports on communications between Dominican opponents of annexation
records.summary_en: The Evening Telegraph reports on communications between Dominican opponents of annexation and Commissioners Andrew D. White and Samuel Gridley Howe. The Dominicans informed the Commissioners that outside of President Báez's immediate adherents, no one in the republic desired annexation, insisting that Dominicans valued their independence as highly as Americans and that Báez misrepresented public sentiment. They declared the annexation plebiscite illegal, pointing to the ongoing revolution, prisons crowded with patriots, and refugees in hiding or exile, with White and Howe acknowledging having met notable fugitives in Port-au-Prince, including Ángel María Caminero. The article also cites El Pabellón Dominicano of March 31, which condemned the Báez government and denounced the annexation treaty as a corrupt job compromising the honor and interests of both nations.
records.summary_es: El Evening Telegraph informa sobre las comunicaciones entre opositores dominicanos a la anexión y los comisionados Andrew D. White y Samuel Gridley Howe. Los dominicanos comunicaron a los comisionados que, al margen de los partidarios inmediatos del presidente Báez, nadie en la república deseaba la anexión, insistiendo en que los dominicanos valoraban su independencia tanto como los estadounidenses y que Báez tergiversaba el sentir popular. Declararon ilegal el plebiscito anexionista, señalando como pruebas la revolución en curso, las cárceles llenas de patriotas y los fugitivos escondidos o en el exilio, admitiendo White y Howe haber conocido a notables refugiados en Puerto Príncipe, entre ellos Ángel María Caminero. El artículo cita asimismo a El Pabellón Dominicano del 31 de marzo, que condenaba al gobierno de Báez y denunciaba el tratado de anexión como una componenda corrupta que comprometía el honor y los intereses de ambas naciones.

records.summary_en: In Senate debate over the Samana Bay lease, Senator Harlan confirmed that under the lease the United States was in possession of Samana Bay and the American flag was floating there, and that the lease had been made under an appropriation by Congress with a provision for renewal. He argued that the government in possession was simply declaring it would defend that possession if anyone tried to wrest it away, and he attacked the long speeches made against the Grant administration over the affair.

records.headline: An article in the New National Era argues that talk of humiliation
records.summary_en: An article in the New National Era argues that talk of humiliation or degradation regarding the annexation of Santo Domingo is groundless, asking what state would be degraded by becoming the equal of Massachusetts and New York. To be an American citizen is described as one of the highest privileges, sought by hundreds of thousands from Europe who leave their homelands to better their condition, just as Santo Domingo would share in the blessings of a free and stable government. In answer to the objection that the country it calls Dominica would be ruled by the United States, the writer contends that it would enjoy an equal voice with other states, with its senators and representatives in Congress as much respected as those of any other state.
records.summary_es: Un artículo en el New National Era sostiene que hablar de humillación o degradación ante la anexión de Santo Domingo carece de fundamento, preguntando qué estado se degradaría al convertirse en igual de Massachusetts y Nueva York. Describe la ciudadanía estadounidense como uno de los privilegios más altos, buscado por cientos de miles de europeos que abandonan sus tierras natales para mejorar su condición, del mismo modo en que Santo Domingo compartiría las bendiciones de un gobierno libre y estable. En respuesta a la objeción de que el país que llama Dominica sería gobernado por los Estados Unidos, el autor sostiene que disfrutaría de una voz igual a la de los demás estados, y que sus senadores y representantes en el Congreso serían tan respetados como los de cualquier otro estado.

records.headline: An article in the New National Era reports that the climate of Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: An article in the New National Era reports that the climate of Santo Domingo is salubrious rather than unhealthy, with steady trade winds and high central mountain ranges draining the fertile clay loam soil. The writer states that white families can thrive there with modest acclimation, and observes that the population of the country it calls Dominica is small, comparing it in numbers to Newark, New Jersey, and noting that Santo Domingo and Hayti combined have fewer inhabitants than Philadelphia. Under a second heading, the writer asserts that the intellectual and moral interests of the United States will be advanced by annexation, declaring that human rights and free institutions are not restricted by latitude.
records.summary_es: Un artículo en el New National Era informa que el clima de Santo Domingo es saludable y no perjudicial, con vientos alisios constantes y altas cordilleras centrales que drenan el fértil suelo franco arcilloso. El autor afirma que las familias blancas pueden prosperar allí con una aclimatación moderada, y observa que la población del país que llama Dominica es reducida, comparándola en número con Newark, Nueva Jersey, y señalando que Santo Domingo y Haití juntos tienen menos habitantes que Filadelfia. Bajo un segundo encabezado, el autor afirma que los intereses intelectuales y morales de los Estados Unidos se verán impulsados por la anexión, declarando que los derechos humanos y las instituciones libres no están restringidos por la latitud.

records.headline: A dispatch under the heading "Boundary Between Hayti and St. Domingo" reports
records.summary_en: A dispatch under the heading "Boundary Between Hayti and St. Domingo" reports that the Haytien minister has been authorized by his government to declare that Hayti does not seek to conquer or control the Dominican Republic. Its sole stated object is to establish the boundary line between Hayti and Dominica, which it wishes to see guaranteed by the United States government. The dispatch adds that the minister has had the report of the St. Domingo commissioners translated into French to distribute it in Hayti and in Europe.
records.summary_es: Un despacho bajo el encabezado «Boundary Between Hayti and St. Domingo» informa que el ministro haitiano ha sido autorizado por su gobierno a declarar que Haití no pretende conquistar ni dominar la República Dominicana. Su único objetivo declarado es fijar la línea divisoria entre Haití y Dominica, la cual desearía ver garantizada por el gobierno de los Estados Unidos. El despacho añade que el ministro ha hecho traducir al francés el informe de los comisionados de Santo Domingo para distribuirlo en Haití y en Europa.

records.headline: The Gold Hill Daily News publishes the text of a congressional
records.summary_en: The Gold Hill Daily News publishes the text of a congressional joint resolution defining the duties of commissioners appointed to examine conditions in the Dominican Republic. The commission is instructed to report on Dominican boundaries, public debt, foreign treaties, land grants and concessions, and the terms on which the Dominican government desires annexation to the United States as a territory. Section 2 directs the commissioners to submit their report to the President for transmission to Congress as soon as convenient. Section 3 provides that the commissioners shall serve without compensation beyond expenses, with an explicit proviso that nothing in the resolution commits Congress to the policy of annexing the territory of the republic of Dominica.
records.summary_es: El Gold Hill Daily News publica el texto de una resolución conjunta del Congreso que define las funciones de los comisionados designados para examinar la situación en la República Dominicana. La comisión tiene instrucciones de informar sobre los límites dominicanos, la deuda pública, los tratados exteriores, las concesiones de tierras y los términos en que el gobierno dominicano desea la anexión a los Estados Unidos como territorio. La sección 2 ordena a los comisionados presentar su informe al presidente para su remisión al Congreso tan pronto como sea conveniente. La sección 3 dispone que los comisionados presten servicios sin más compensación que sus gastos, con la salvedad expresa de que nada en la resolución compromete al Congreso con la política de anexar el territorio de la república de Dominica.

records.headline: The Haytien minister has received authority from his government

Its only purpose is to fix a boundary line between Hayti and Dominica, with the desire that this boundary be guaranteed by the United States. The item further notes that the minister has had the report of the San Domingo commissioners translated into French for distribution across Hayti and Europe.

Su único propósito es fijar una línea divisoria entre Haití y Dominica, con el deseo de que dicha frontera sea garantizada por los Estados Unidos. La nota señala además que el ministro ha hecho traducir al francés el informe de los comisionados de Santo Domingo para distribuirlo en Haití y en Europa.

records.headline: A letter from Santo Domingo in the Worcester Daily Spy depicts
records.summary_en: A letter from Santo Domingo in the Worcester Daily Spy depicts local customs, social composition, and economic distress in the Dominican capital. The correspondent observes that bulls are commonly used as beasts of burden alongside mules and donkeys, ridden into town with fruit and vegetable panniers by Dominican country people. The population is described as largely mixed African, Spanish, and French, alongside an aging community of Black Americans who emigrated from northern cities forty years earlier. The writer emphasizes that severe poverty pervades the town and republic, noting that while the people are eager to work, the government provides no industrial security, subjects young men to a seven-year military draft, and pays soldiers only a roll of bread and five cents a day.
records.summary_es: Una carta desde Santo Domingo en el Worcester Daily Spy describe las costumbres locales, la composición social y las penurias económicas en la capital dominicana. El corresponsal observa que los toros se emplean comúnmente como bestias de carga junto a mulas y burros, montados hacia el pueblo con serones de frutas y verduras por campesinos dominicanos. La población se describe en su mayoría como una mezcla de razas africana, española y francesa, junto con una comunidad envejecida de negros estadounidenses que emigraron desde ciudades del norte hace cuarenta años. El autor subraya que una pobreza extrema impera en la ciudad y en la república, y señala que, aunque el pueblo desea trabajar, el gobierno no ofrece seguridad a la industria, somete a los jóvenes a un reclutamiento militar de siete años y paga a los soldados solo un pan y cinco centavos al día.
