records.headline: A Tribune reporter interviews Mr. Hazard regarding the plans of the newly
records.summary_en: A Tribune reporter interviews Mr. Hazard regarding the plans of the newly chartered Samaná Bay Company. Hazard disclaims annexation as the company's objective, stating that maintaining separate status while exercising its granted rights is far more profitable, even if populating the territory with Americans might ease future annexation. Asked whether the enterprise could establish a model republic in Santo Domingo, Hazard affirms there is opportunity for free trade, suffrage, and general improvements. The paper notes reports that the company has already subleased a maritime privilege in Samaná Bay for an amount equaling its entire annual payment obligation, leaving nearly all of its resources untouched.
records.summary_es: Un reportero del Tribune entrevista al señor Hazard sobre los planes de la recién constituida Compañía de la Bahía de Samaná. Hazard descarta que la anexión sea el objetivo de la compañía, señalando que mantener una condición separada en ejercicio de los derechos otorgados resulta mucho más provechoso, aun cuando poblar el territorio con estadounidenses pudiera facilitar una anexión futura. Preguntado sobre si la empresa podría establecer una república modelo en Santo Domingo, Hazard afirma que existe la oportunidad de instituir el libre comercio, el sufragio y mejoras generales. El periódico menciona informes de que la compañía ya ha subarrendado un derecho marítimo en la bahía de Samaná por una suma equivalente a toda su obligación de pago anual, dejando casi todos sus recursos intactos.

records.headline: In a letter extract on the ratification of the Samaná lease
records.summary_en: In a letter extract on the ratification of the Samaná lease, Dr. Samuel G. Howe details the sovereign powers secured by the Samaná Bay Company. The corporation holds eminent domain over the entire peninsula and bay of Samaná, possessing authority to enact laws, appoint police and judicial officers, collect customs duties, establish a bank, and construct roads, canals, and telegraph lines across the Dominican Republic in return for alternate leagues of public land. The company has bought out all prior government concessions, whose holders formally renounced their claims, and retains a virtual monopoly barring the Dominican government from chartering any rival enterprise without offering the same terms to the company.
records.summary_es: En un extracto de carta sobre la ratificación del arrendamiento de Samaná, el doctor Samuel G. Howe detalla los poderes soberanos obtenidos por la Compañía de la Bahía de Samaná. La corporación ejerce dominio eminente sobre toda la península y la bahía de Samaná, gozando de facultades para promulgar leyes, designar funcionarios policiales y judiciales, recaudar derechos aduaneros, fundar un banco y construir caminos, canales y líneas telegráficas a través de la República Dominicana a cambio de leguas alternas de tierras públicas. La compañía ha adquirido todas las concesiones gubernamentales previas, cuyos titulares renunciaron formalmente a sus derechos, y conserva un monopolio virtual que prohíbe al gobierno dominicano autorizar empresas rivales sin antes ofrecer las mismas condiciones a la compañía.

records.headline: A despatch announces the completion of a treaty between the Samana Bay Company and the Republic of St. Domingo
records.summary_en: A despatch announces the completion of a treaty between the Samana Bay Company and the Republic of St. Domingo under President Baez, ceding the peninsula of Samana with the waters of the bay, its islands and reefs. Under the treaty the company may acquire and sell property, carry on any kind of business, issue bonds, establish banks, collect port dues and taxes in its possessions, keep its own police and other forces, and sail vessels under its own flag, with the stated object of building up a free state and a great centre of trade at Samana Bay.

records.summary_en: According to *The New York Herald* on January 17, 1873, a business or stock-jobbing scheme involving St. Domingo gained thousands of dollars in free advertising through press coverage. The newspaper stated that while American enterprise abroad is acceptable provided the government is not dragged into defending land grants, the President must define the administration's position to prevent annexation or complications. Finally, the article expressed strong opposition to annexing St. Domingo, describing it as a distant tropical island with little trade and a sparse population, while asserting that the United States already has sufficient territory.
records.summary_es: Según *The New York Herald* del 17 de enero de 1873, un tinglado especulativo de bolsa centrado en Santo Domingo cosechó miles de dólares en publicidad gratuita mediante la cobertura periodística. El diario opinó que, si bien la iniciativa privada estadounidense en el exterior es lícita con tal de que no comprometa al gobierno en la defensa de mercedes de tierras, el presidente debe deslindar la postura oficial para precaver anexiones o conflictos. Finalmente, el artículo expresó una enérgica repulsa a incorporar a Santo Domingo, caracterizándola como una remota isla tropical de precario comercio y escaso vecindario, concluyendo que los Estados Unidos gozan ya de suficiente extensión territorial.

records.full_text:
These facts may create a suspicion that General Grant is not only "deeply interested" in this private enterprise of American citizens—as Mr. Hazard, the secretary of the company, says, though not in a personal sense, we presume—but that this scheme is favored by him with the ulterior view of bringing about annexation in an indirect manner—thus accomplishing his long-cherished object which the Senate mercilessly squelched. We do not think the President would act in such a surreptitious manner. We believe he honestly thinks that the possession of the territory of St. Domingo, or the Samana portion of it, by an American company, would be a benefit to the trade of the country. This, we presume, is the "deep interest" he takes in the project, and for no other reason. Still, the American people will be disposed to believe that the President has the ulterior object of annexation in view, and he should at once remove such an impression by disavowing any purpose of the nature.

The new St. Domingo Company, like the old one, if, indeed, it be not the old one revived and reorganized, shows a great deal of skill in the initiation of its project. It has obtained, to begin operations, a systematic and extensive advertisement in the press of this city and of the country gratuitously. records.headline: The Samaná Bay Company agreement is criticized in a Herald editorial
records.summary_en: The Samaná Bay Company agreement is criticized in a Herald editorial, which observes that company revenues will prove a windfall to President Báez following the loss of United States payments for a naval wharf at Samaná. The paper condemns Báez as a dictator and usurper, challenging his authority to alienate Dominican territory and warning American investors to scrutinize the legitimacy of any titles he confers. While conceding that genuine commercial development of Dominican trade would be welcome under valid title, the Herald emphatically protests against using the project as a pretext for annexation, urging Americans not to be misled by promotional misrepresentations.

records.full_text:
The company is entitled to emit bonds for railroad, canal, telegraph and highroad constructions, with the faculty of guaranteeing payment there-against, and further, shall have the right to hypothecate the bonds emitted for the purpose of raising funds to carry on the work, and shall further have the right to emit further stock for the completion of said work.

Neither:—Emigrants who shall purchase land of the company or the agents of said company, or merchants who shall be engaged in commercial pursuits between Samana and other points of the Dominican Republic shall be compelled to pay higher imposts than Dominican citizens. It is also further understood that no taxes shall be levied by the Dominican government upon works of public utility, or the banking establishments—and, in a word, the company shall be treated as the most favored of Dominican citizens.

The company shall have the privilege of authorizing the formation of other companies, and has the right of ceding land to them upon such terms and stipulations as may be considered most advantageous, and, by so doing, carry out the aims and objects for which the company was organized.

The aforesaid smaller companies shall have their names designated by the said Samana Bay Company, and shall be under the superintendence and inspection of the said company, which shall have the privilege of holding shares in the said smaller companies.

The privileges and concessions accorded to this company shall be without prejudice to privileges and concessions accorded to any other person or persons by the Dominican government, for, up to the present time, no such privileges or concessions have been granted similar to those now conceded to the Samana Bay Company, which is now empowered, for the space of thirty days, to accept or refuse said treaty.

ART. 10.—These concessions, rights, privileges and immunities shall take effect on the first day of January, in the year eighteen hundred and seventy-three, and will continue in force and will remain in force for ninety-nine years from the said date (with the exception of a certain time that is to be conceded to the company for the purpose of taking possession, on the condition that the said company, its successors or representatives, pay or cause to be paid, to the Dominican government the sum of $150,000, in American gold, in advance, to the Dominican government. The said sum to be charged in advance to the company on the 1st day of January of each year, and the payment thereagainst to be made in the capital city of St. Domingo on the same, or at any place that may be designated by the Dominican government.

The first of these annual advance payments shall be made on the 1st of January, in the year 1873, unless it has been made before. The company and its territories shall remain under the united protection of the Dominican Republic and the United States of America, and the company and its agents, when they deem it necessary, shall ask the protection and intervention of either of these nations or of both.

ART. 11.—For the purposes of ratifying this convention a vote will be taken on the subject by the Dominican nation and the Dominican Senate. The non-payment of the annual rent alluded to in article 10 or the breaking out of war or other circumstances of force majeure will cause the said convention to be considered null and void after thirty days' notice has been given by the Dominican government.

records.full_text:
The Herald says: "It is absurd to speak of a vast trade with St. Domingo. One little steamer making monthly trips does the principal trade with the United States. There is hardly any other. The Company speaks of a prospective trade amounting to hundreds of millions. This is ridiculous. San Domingo has scarcely any production in itself. However rich the soil may be, there is not the labor, nor do we think it can be carried there to make the soil productive. Then it is an error to say that the island has a commanding position for trade with the Antilles and South America. It lies on the outer verge of the whole group, and is not properly in the track of commerce."

The Company, however, say they will make Samana virtually a free port, and gradually absorb all the trade of the West Indies. Governor Fabens has posted the Company's flag at Samana, and the steamship Tybee, at Pier No. 4, North River, floats the same emblem from her fore. It is a combination of the Dominican and United States flags. From edge to edge across its centre, lengthwise and crosswise, is a broad white band, dividing the flag into four other parts. In the upper left-hand corner is the union jack, a blue field and white stars. The upper right-hand corner is red, the lower right blue, and the lower left-hand corner red. The negotiations with Baez for the purchase of Samana extended through two weeks. Audiences were given daily in the Executive Palace, the hours being from 8:30 a. m. to 4:30 p. m., with an intermission for dinner. The negotiations were conducted in Spanish, and during their progress the Commissioners had no relations of intimacy with the members of the Government, living on board the ship, and not seeing the Dominicans except in business hours. When the negotiations were completed, and the treaty ratified, the President gave a grand ball in honor of the Commissioners, who returned the compliment by a dinner on the Tybee.

Several times the negotiations were nearly broken off. On one occasion the Commissioners retired to their steamer, got up steam, blew their whistle, and were nearly off, and then they were recalled. Whether the Dominicans were frightened by the steam whistle is not known, but the negotiations were resumed, and finally the President and his Ministers ratified the contract. It was then referred to the Senate, which comprises nine members. The Senate discussed the Convention several days, during which the members of the Government were invited before that body to explain the various provisions of the treaty. The result of these deliberations was the ratification by the Senate. That branch of the Government agreed with the Executive, that a treaty, which was such an innovation on the laws of the country, and which granted such unusual and extraordinary powers to a private company, should not be finally and wholly carried into effect without its ratification by the people at the polls. This has doubtless been accomplished before the present date. Perhaps nine-tenths of the population, altogether about 240,000, are uneducated and ignorant. The voters of this class are expected to have no opinion but to vote as their superiors direct. The educated and wealthier classes favor the scheme and therefore the Company have no doubt that the Convention will be overwhelmingly ratified at the polls.

records.full_text:
SAMANA BAY.

Further Details of the Sale to the American Company—Creation of a Sovereign Power—Speculations and Surmises Regarding the Future Action of the New Nation.
Special Despatch to The Chicago Tribune.
NEW YORK, Jan. 18.—The full text of the Samana purchase convention confirms the fact that the Company has obtained absolute sovereignty over the peninsula, with its inhabitants and private interests. The sovereignty conceded to the Company is greater than that of the State of New York, or any other State in the Union, for it includes the right to levy and collect custom duties, and to do many other things which can only be done by a sovereign nation. Baez not only sells them these extraordinary privileges, but he sells them the flag of the Republic of St. Domingo to use as they may see proper. Besides all this, the Company can build railroads and telegraphs in any part of the island, obtaining grants as extraordinary as those accorded to the Union Pacific and other railroads when Congress was giving away the public domain. Every league of railroad constructed by the Company brings its square league of land, and every three leagues of telegraph, a square league grant. The Company promised Baez to use all their influence with Congress to bring Dominican products into the ports of the United States, free of duty, which would be a singular discrimination against other tropical countries.

A most extraordinary feature of the treaty is that it frees the men composing the Company from the operation of our Register and Navigation laws. Under the acts of Congress, American merchants cannot buy ships abroad. This Company, though composed mostly of Americans, can buy ships where it can buy them cheapest, for it has bought a flag under which to run them.

The Herald says on this head: "A few judicious alliances with American railway monopolies would make the Company as powerful in the United States as in St. Domingo, and in the end it might rule us as effectually as our tan-colored brethren in the West Indies."

[To the Associated Press.]
NEW YORK, Jan. 18.—A great deal of speculation is rife in this city as to the Samana Bay Company seeking aid from the United States Government in furthering its objects. It is thought that the Company will endeavor first to obtain the formal protection of our Government, and, if possible, to lease it a naval station in the bay, and, further, to agitate the idea of annexation. Already it is stated that powerful lobby interests are to be created with these ends in view, and that Congress will be asked soon to pass exceptional tariff laws applying to the trade from San Domingo.

records.headline: The News outlines how the Samana Bay Company of Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The News outlines how the Samana Bay Company of Santo Domingo was organized, formed by American capitalists after negotiations between the United States and the Dominican Republic broke off. Prominent corporators include S. L. M. Barlow, Alden B. Stockwell of the Pacific Mail Company, Dr. Samuel G. Howe, Henry Clews, Oliver Ames, and William G. Fargo. Capitalized at $20,000,000 in one-hundred-dollar shares, the company is governed by five to thirteen directors elected annually. The corporation is empowered to buy, sell, mortgage, and lease property of every description in Santo Domingo and elsewhere, as well as issue bonds.
records.summary_es: El News detalla la organización de la Samana Bay Company of Santo Domingo, constituida por capitalistas estadounidenses después de que se interrumpieran las negociaciones entre los Estados Unidos y la República Dominicana. Entre los socios destacados figuran S. L. M. Barlow, Alden B. Stockwell de la Pacific Mail Company, el Dr. Samuel G. Howe, Henry Clews, Oliver Ames y William G. Fargo. Capitalizada en $20,000,000 en acciones de cien dólares, la empresa estará gobernada por entre cinco y trece directores elegidos anualmente. La corporación está facultada para comprar, vender, hipotecar y arrendar propiedades de toda clase en Santo Domingo y otros lugares, además de emitir bonos.

records.headline: An editorial in the Tribune argues that the Samana Bay Company
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Tribune argues that the Samana Bay Company has obtained an unprecedentedly broad charter that renders it a sovereign government rather than a mere commercial corporation. Because the company assumes governing functions, the paper contends the United States Government must not extend special protection to it, leaving the enterprise to face the ordinary risks of war and revolution on its own. The editorial questions President Báez's legal authority to convey Dominican territory to private capitalists, suggesting the deal may provoke resistance from Haiti, objections from Spain, or revolution from dispossessed concession holders.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en el Tribune sostiene que la Samana Bay Company ha obtenido una concesión de una amplitud sin precedentes que la convierte en un gobierno soberano y no en una simple corporación comercial. Debido a que la empresa asume funciones de gobierno, el periódico afirma que el gobierno de los Estados Unidos no debe extenderle una protección especial, dejando que la compañía enfrente por su cuenta los riesgos habituales de guerra y revolución. El editorial cuestiona la autoridad legal del presidente Báez para transferir territorio dominicano a capitalistas privados, señalando que la transacción podría provocar la resistencia de Haití, objeciones de España o una revolución de titulares de concesiones despojados.

records.headline: An editorial in the Herald criticizes a clause in the Samana Bay Company's convention
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Herald criticizes a clause in the Samana Bay Company's convention requiring vessels flying the American or Dominican flag to be manned and commanded by citizens of either nation. The paper warns that this provision appears designed to evade United States registry and navigation laws by intertwining American shipping with Santo Domingo under a private corporation exercising governmental powers. It questions whether President Grant is aware of the arrangement and urges the American public to investigate the scheme thoroughly rather than be misled by the company's extravagant claims.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en el Herald critica una cláusula del convenio de la Samana Bay Company que exige que las embarcaciones que naveguen bajo bandera estadounidense o dominicana sean tripuladas y comandadas por ciudadanos de cualquiera de las dos naciones. El periódico advierte que esta disposición parece concebida para evadir las leyes de registro y navegación de los Estados Unidos al entrelazar la navegación estadounidense con Santo Domingo bajo una corporación privada que ejerce poderes gubernamentales. Cuestiona si el presidente Grant tiene conocimiento del acuerdo e insta al público estadounidense a examinar minuciosamente el proyecto en lugar de dejarse engañar por las extravagantes pretensiones de la compañía.

records.headline: The Tribune introduces an exposé. It regards the political scheming
records.summary_en: The Tribune introduces an exposé. It regards the political scheming behind the Dominican annexation project and the subsequent lease of Samaná Bay to American capitalists. Warning that the transaction may prove a costly burden on the United States Treasury to bail out English speculators, the paper publishes a communication titled "For Sale, a Republic." The correspondent opens with a biographical sketch of Buenaventura Báez in 1865 and 1866, describing him living near poverty in Bordeaux while planning to recoup power in Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: El Tribune presenta una denuncia sobre las intrigas políticas detrás del proyecto de anexión dominicana y el posterior arrendamiento de la bahía de Samaná a capitalistas estadounidenses. Tras advertir que la transacción podría resultar una costosa carga para el Tesoro de los Estados Unidos con el fin de rescatar a especuladores ingleses, el periódico publica una comunicación titulada «Se vende una república». El corresponsal inicia con un bosquejo biográfico de Buenaventura Báez en 1865 y 1866, describiéndolo viviendo cerca de la pobreza en Burdeos mientras planeaba recuperar el poder en Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: Continuing a letter in the Tribune, a correspondent alleges that financial speculator Hartmont, backed by the English firm of Lawsons, lobbied Washington for two years before helping engineer the Samaná Bay concession under various aliases. Turning to describe the Dominican Republic, the writer characterizes the country as an earthly paradise of unparalleled tropical scenery and natural wealth. He notes that the island produces exceptional mahogany, supplies abundant lignum vitae to England and the United States, and possesses soils capable of yielding unsurpassed sugar cane, oranges, lemons, and citrons.

Al pasar a describir la República Dominicana, el autor califica al país como un paraíso terrenal de paisajes tropicales y riqueza natural sin igual. Señala que la isla produce una caoba excepcional, suministra abundante guayacán a Inglaterra y a los Estados Unidos, y posee tierras capaces de producir caña de azúcar, naranjas, limones y cidras inigualables.

records.headline: The Tribune reports on the Samana Bay Company's plans to establish
records.summary_en: The Tribune reports on the Samana Bay Company's plans to establish a weekly steamship line between New York and Samaná, contracting for three vessels and chartering a steamer to carry tourists to the island. It then prints the formal report submitted to Chairman Alden B. Stockwell by the commissioners dispatched to negotiate the concession. Appointed on December 4, the commissioners sailed on the Tybee and arrived at Santo Domingo City on December 14. Finding President Báez forty miles away at Azua commanding the army observing the Haitian frontier, they presented their credentials to Secretary of State Gautier.
records.summary_es: El Tribune informa sobre los planes de la Samana Bay Company para establecer una línea semanal de vapores entre Nueva York y Samaná, mediante la contratación de tres embarcaciones y el fletamento de un vapor para llevar turistas a la isla. Luego publica el informe formal presentado al presidente de la junta, Alden B. Stockwell, por los comisionados enviados a negociar la concesión. Nombrados el 4 de diciembre, los comisionados zarparon en el Tybee y llegaron a la ciudad de Santo Domingo el 14 de diciembre. Al hallar al presidente Báez a cuarenta millas de distancia en Azua al mando del ejército que observaba la frontera haitiana, presentaron sus credenciales al secretario de Estado Gautier.

records.headline: An editorial in the Republican analyzes the sweeping privileges
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Republican analyzes the sweeping privileges granted to the Samana Bay Company, describing the leased territory as highly fertile for sugar cane, coffee, and cocoa, and rich in minerals such as iron. Beyond territorial jurisdiction, the company receives rights to establish a bank of issue whose paper is legal tender for internal taxes, a practical monopoly on future railways, canals, and telegraphs with extensive land grants, and immunity from burdensome taxation. The paper cautions that the venture assumes ultimate annexation by the United States, warning that the speculators face ruin if annexation fails to occur or if the Dominican population resists.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en el Republican analiza los amplios privilegios otorgados a la Samana Bay Company, y describe el territorio arrendado como sumamente fértil para la caña de azúcar, el café y el cacao, y rico en minerales como el hierro. Más allá de la jurisdicción territorial, la empresa recibe derechos para establecer un banco emisor cuyo papel moneda sea de curso legal para los impuestos internos, un monopolio práctico sobre futuros ferrocarriles, canales y telégrafos con extensas concesiones de tierras, y exención de impuestos gravosos. El periódico advierte que la empresa da por sentada la anexión final por parte de los Estados Unidos, señalando que los especuladores enfrentan la ruina si la anexión no llega a concretarse o si la población dominicana se resiste.

records.headline: The Appeal questions the financial and legal foundations of the Samana Bay Company's agreement
records.summary_en: The Appeal questions the financial and legal foundations of the Samana Bay Company's agreement with President Báez. The paper doubts that the enterprise can generate the required $150,000 annual payment in advance without speculative stock sales, noting that Báez shrewdly insisted on payment in American gold on pain of nullifying the contract. It further warns that treaty provisions authorizing company vessels to fly the American or Dominican flag, manned by citizens of either country, appear designed to circumvent United States registry and navigation laws while entangling the federal government in the company's private rule.
records.summary_es: El Appeal cuestiona los fundamentos financieros y legales del acuerdo de la Samana Bay Company con el presidente Báez. El diario duda de que la empresa pueda generar el pago anual requerido de $150,000 por adelantado sin recurrir a la venta especulativa de acciones, y señala que Báez insistió astutamente en recibir pagos en oro estadounidense bajo pena de anulación del contrato. Advierte además que las cláusulas del tratado que autorizan a los buques de la compañía a enarbolar la bandera estadounidense o la dominicana, tripulados por ciudadanos de cualquiera de los dos países, parecen diseñadas para eludir las leyes de registro y navegación de los Estados Unidos al tiempo que involucran al gobierno federal en el régimen privado de la empresa.

records.headline: Reprinting an editorial from the New York Herald, the Appeal scrutinizes
records.summary_en: Reprinting an editorial from the New York Herald, the Appeal scrutinizes article ten of the convention between the Dominican government and the Samana Bay Company. The clause specifies that the company and its territories shall remain under the joint protection of the Dominican Republic and the United States, with the company authorized to solicit intervention from either or both nations. The paper asks whether President Grant or Congress authorized this guarantee, or whether the speculators inserted it without sanction to market their stock and bonds while President Báez safeguarded his personal financial interests.
records.summary_es: Al reproducir un editorial del New York Herald, el Appeal examina el artículo diez del convenio entre el gobierno dominicano y la Samana Bay Company. La cláusula establece que la empresa y sus territorios permanecerán bajo la protección conjunta de la República Dominicana y los Estados Unidos, autorizando a la compañía a solicitar la intervención de cualquiera de las dos naciones o de ambas. El periódico cuestiona si el presidente Grant o el Congreso autorizaron esta garantía, o si los especuladores la introdujeron sin autorización para colocar sus acciones y bonos mientras el presidente Báez resguardaba sus intereses financieros personales.

records.headline: An editorial headed "The Samana Bay Purchase" traces President Báez's efforts
records.summary_en: An editorial headed "The Samana Bay Purchase" traces President Báez's efforts to monetize Dominican territory following his victory over Cabral. The paper asserts that after failing to secure a French loan, Báez's agent Hartmont engaged the English firm of Lawson & Son for £80,000, prompting the British financiers to seek reimbursement through United States annexation. When Senators Sumner and Schurz helped defeat that scheme, the English investors and Báez turned to New York bankers and speculators, who have now agreed to lease the territory and supply the sought-after funds.
records.summary_es: Un editorial titulado «The Samana Bay Purchase» describe las gestiones del presidente Báez para monetizar el territorio dominicano tras su victoria sobre Cabral. El periódico afirma que, tras fracasar en la obtención de un préstamo francés, el agente de Báez, Hartmont, comprometió a la firma inglesa Lawson & Son por unas £80,000, lo que impulsó a los financieros británicos a buscar su reembolso mediante la anexión a los Estados Unidos. Cuando los senadores Sumner y Schurz contribuyeron a derrotar dicho plan, los inversionistas ingleses y Báez recurrieron a banqueros y especuladores neoyorquinos, quienes ahora han acordado arrendar el territorio y suministrar los anhelados fondos.

records.headline: The Republican outlines the Samana Bay Company's commercial and administrative plans
records.summary_en: The Republican outlines the Samana Bay Company's commercial and administrative plans, reporting that Samaná Bay will serve as a duty-free hub exchanging tropical produce for American and European manufactures. Having purchased the steamer Tybee from the Spoffords, the company intends to construct iron steamships and establish connections with major shipping and express lines. The promoters also plan to establish a civil administration with institutions for education, charities, and corrections modeled on Massachusetts under the direction of Dr. Samuel G. Howe, who plans to reside on the island with Julia Ward Howe, while J. Warren Fabens serves as Governor of Samaná.
records.summary_es: El Republican expone los planes comerciales y administrativos de la Samana Bay Company, e informa que la bahía de Samaná servirá como centro libre de aranceles para el intercambio de productos tropicales por manufacturas estadounidenses y europeas. Tras haber adquirido el vapor Tybee a los Spofford, la compañía se propone construir buques de vapor de hierro y establecer conexiones con importantes líneas de navegación y empresas de transporte expreso. Los promotores proyectan además establecer una administración civil con instituciones de educación, beneficencia y corrección inspiradas en el modelo de Massachusetts bajo la dirección del Dr. Samuel G. Howe, quien planea residir en la isla junto a Julia Ward Howe, mientras J. Warren Fabens ejerce como gobernador de Samaná.

records.headline: Reprinting an exposé from the Chicago Tribune, the Bulletin publishes
records.summary_en: Reprinting an exposé from the Chicago Tribune, the Bulletin publishes a letter detailing the financial and political maneuvers surrounding the Dominican Republic under the headline stack "Dominica for Sale." An editorial preface warns that the recent acquisition of Samaná Bay by American capitalists may be a covert attempt to recoup English investments through the United States Treasury following the defeat of official annexation. Titled "For Sale, a Republic," the correspondence purports to disclose the origins of President Báez's political scheming to defeat Cabral after seeking buyers in France, England, and the United States.
records.summary_es: Al reproducir una denuncia del Chicago Tribune, el Bulletin publica una carta que detalla las maniobras financieras y políticas en torno a la República Dominicana bajo el encabezado «Dominica for Sale». Un prefacio editorial advierte que la reciente adquisición de la bahía de Samaná por capitalistas estadounidenses podría ser una tentativa encubierta para recuperar inversiones inglesas a través del Tesoro de los Estados Unidos tras el fracaso de la anexión oficial. Titulada «Se vende una república», la correspondencia pretende revelar los orígenes de las intrigas políticas del presidente Báez para derrotar a Cabral tras buscar compradores en Francia, Inglaterra y los Estados Unidos.

records.headline: In an installment of a letter reprinted from the Chicago Tribune
records.summary_en: In an installment of a letter reprinted from the Chicago Tribune, the Bulletin carries allegations that financial speculator Hartmont operated in Washington under various aliases, including Colonel Fabens, to orchestrate the Samaná Bay concession. The writer then provides a glowing geographical account of the Dominican Republic under the heading "The Island of San Domingo," describing it as an earthly paradise. He praises its magnificent scenery and forests, asserting that the country produces the finest mahogany in the world, large supplies of lignum vitae, and abundant citrus fruits and sugar cane.
records.summary_es: En una entrega de una carta reproducida del Chicago Tribune, el Bulletin presenta acusaciones de que el especulador financiero Hartmont operó en Washington bajo diversos alias, incluido el del coronel Fabens, para orquestar la concesión de la bahía de Samaná. El autor ofrece luego una entusiasta descripción geográfica de la República Dominicana bajo el título «The Island of San Domingo», calificándola de paraíso terrenal. Elogia sus magníficos paisajes y bosques, afirmando que el país produce la mejor caoba del mundo, abundantes suministros de guayacán, así como copiosos frutos cítricos y caña de azúcar.

records.headline: A letter recounts the San Domingo loan affair: a commission of five was sent to examine the securities offered for repayment
records.summary_en: A letter recounts the San Domingo loan affair: a commission of five was sent to examine the securities offered for repayment, which consisted of the country's revenues, a guano deposit said to exist on the island of Alta Vela, and gold mines. Henry Lawson returned to London persuaded the securities were worthless, yet a very large sum had already been sent to Baez, and the loan, after damaging newspaper articles, was withdrawn and voted a swindle; the account then follows the promoter Hartmont on to New York and the Samana Bay scheme.
records.summary_es: Una carta relata el asunto del préstamo de Santo Domingo: se envió una comisión de cinco personas a examinar las garantías ofrecidas para el pago, que consistían en las rentas del país, un depósito de guano que se decía existía en la isla de Alta Vela, y minas de oro. Henry Lawson regresó a Londres convencido de que las garantías no valían nada, pero ya se había enviado una suma muy grande a Báez, y el préstamo, tras artículos dañinos en los periódicos, fue retirado y considerado una estafa; el relato sigue luego al promotor Hartmont hasta Nueva York y el proyecto de la bahía de Samaná.

records.headline: The Bulletin questions a provision of the Samana Bay Company agreement
records.summary_en: The Bulletin questions a provision of the Samana Bay Company agreement allowing vessels to sail under the Dominican flag or any other the company has a right to use. The article argues that this clause refers to the United States flag, pointing to the requirement that all company vessels bearing either flag must be manned and commanded by American or Dominican citizens. Warning that this arrangement appears designed to evade United States registry and navigation laws by combining American shipping with an independent commercial government, the paper cautions against endorsing the venture without full scrutiny.
records.summary_es: El Bulletin cuestiona una disposición del acuerdo de la Samana Bay Company que permite a sus embarcaciones navegar bajo la bandera dominicana o cualquier otra que la compañía tenga derecho a usar. El artículo sostiene que esta cláusula alude a la bandera de los Estados Unidos, señalando el requisito de que todos los buques de la empresa que lleven cualquiera de las dos banderas deben ser tripulados y comandados por ciudadanos estadounidenses o dominicanos. Tras advertir que este arreglo parece concebido para evadir las leyes de registro y navegación de los Estados Unidos al combinar la marina mercante estadounidense con un gobierno comercial independiente, el periódico previene contra el respaldo a la empresa sin una investigación exhaustiva.

records.headline: An editorial headed "A Tremendous Ado About Samana" observes
records.summary_en: An editorial headed "A Tremendous Ado About Samana" observes that after President Grant failed to achieve annexation, a syndicate of New York and Boston speculators purchased the port and peninsula of Samaná from President Báez. Describing the concession as measuring twenty-five miles by five in the eastern portion of the Dominican Republic, the paper claims the area possesses immense mineral wealth and fertile soil, though it notes a reputation for unhealthiness. It reports that the company holds a monopoly over internal improvements, requiring its permission for any railway, telegraph, or road, and questions whether the arrangement is an indirect scheme to annex what Grant could not acquire officially.
records.summary_es: Un editorial titulado «A Tremendous Ado About Samana» observa que, luego de que el presidente Grant fracasara en lograr la anexión, un consorcio de especuladores de Nueva York y Boston compró el puerto y la península de Samaná al presidente Báez. Al describir la concesión como un territorio de veinticinco millas por cinco en la porción oriental de la República Dominicana, el periódico afirma que la zona posee una inmensa riqueza mineral y tierras fértiles, aunque señala su reputación de insalubridad. Informa que la compañía posee un monopolio sobre las mejoras internas, requiriéndose su autorización para cualquier ferrocarril, telégrafo o camino, y cuestiona si el arreglo es una maniobra indirecta para anexar lo que Grant no pudo obtener oficialmente.

records.summary_en: According to the Burlington weekly free press on January 31, 1873, U.S. Commissioners reported that a convention regarding a contract in the Dominican Republic was submitted to a public vote to prevent future administrative interference, with voting underway on the 9th inst. The Commissioners expressed confidence that the popular vote would be nearly or quite unanimous for ratification, making the convention part of the Republic's fundamental law. Additionally, they noted receiving good wishes from leading foreign merchants and European consular representatives, along with assurances that the free port and city of Samana could quickly attract a large population from various West Indian islands.
records.summary_es: Según el *Burlington Weekly Free Press* del 31 de enero de 1873, los comisionados de los Estados Unidos informaron que la convención relativa a un contrato en la República Dominicana se sometió a plebiscito popular para conjurar futuras injerencias de gobiernos venideros, habiéndose iniciado la votación el día 9 del corriente. Los delegados manifestaron su certidumbre de que el sufragio popular respaldaría casi unánimemente la ratificación, elevando la convención a rango de ley fundamental de la república. Añadieron haber recibido parabienes de los principales mercaderes foráneos y agentes consulares europeos, junto con el augurio de que la ciudad y puerto franco de Samaná atraerían prontamente una copiosa corriente inmigratoria proveniente de diversas islas antillanas.

records.headline: Dr. Samuel G. Howe writes
records.summary_en: Dr. Samuel G. Howe writes that he and Benjamin F. Wade, as United States Commissioners to Santo Domingo, favored political annexation, and that after annexation was rejected he worked for a commercial company to lease the peninsula and bay of Samana for ninety-nine years. He describes negotiating the terms with President Baez and his cabinet, consulting the Dominican Senate of Seven, and organizing the company, with the first year's rent of $150,000 to be paid in advance.
records.summary_es: El doctor Samuel G. Howe escribe que él y Benjamin F. Wade, como Comisionados de los Estados Unidos a Santo Domingo, favorecieron la anexión política, y que tras ser rechazada la anexión trabajó por una compañía comercial que arrendara la península y la bahía de Samaná por noventa y nueve años. Describe la negociación de los términos con el presidente Báez y su gabinete, la consulta al Senado dominicano de los Siete, y la organización de la compañía, con el primer año de renta de 150.000 dólares a pagar por adelantado.

records.headline: Dispatches in the Avis report on international reactions to the lease of Samaná Bay.
records.summary_en: Dispatches in the Avis report on international reactions to the lease of Samaná Bay. According to Washington intelligence, United States administration officials warmly favor the enterprise as an initial step toward final annexation, assuring the new company of moral support and physical protection for American lives and property on the island. A London cable reports that the Daily News anticipates no diplomatic complications from the lease of Samaná Bay, though the British paper expresses doubt regarding the wisdom of American territorial acquisition beyond continental borders.
records.summary_es: Despachos en el Avis informan sobre las reacciones internacionales al arrendamiento de la bahía de Samaná. Según noticias de Washington, funcionarios de la administración de los Estados Unidos respaldan calurosamente la empresa como un paso inicial hacia la anexión definitiva, asegurando a la nueva compañía apoyo moral y protección física para las vidas y propiedades de los estadounidenses en la isla. Un cable desde Londres informa que el Daily News no prevé complicaciones diplomáticas derivadas del arrendamiento de la bahía de Samaná, aunque el diario británico expresa dudas sobre la prudencia de la adquisición territorial estadounidense más allá de sus fronteras continentales.

records.headline: A correspondent's travel account in the Opinion describes the landscapes
records.summary_en: A correspondent's travel account in the Opinion describes the landscapes and historical remnants of the Dominican Republic. Coasting along the shores and the secluded bay of Samaná, the writer observes sparse human activity amid luxurious forests. In the ancient city of Santo Domingo, he notes the cathedral where the bones of Columbus rested for centuries, the walls of Ovando, and the ruins of Diego Columbus's residence, observing that years of revolution and adversity have impoverished the settlement. The report also praises the Vega Real, an expansive valley viewed from the Santo Cerro that contains the principal agricultural wealth of the island.
records.summary_es: El relato de viaje de un corresponsal en el Opinion describe los paisajes y vestigios históricos de la República Dominicana. Al navegar a lo largo de las costas y de la apartada bahía de Samaná, el autor observa escasa actividad humana entre exuberantes bosques. En la antigua ciudad de Santo Domingo, señala la catedral donde reposaron los restos de Colón durante siglos, las murallas de Ovando y las ruinas de la residencia de Diego Colón, advirtiendo que años de revolución y adversidad han empobrecido la población. El informe elogia asimismo la Vega Real, un amplio valle divisado desde el Santo Cerro que concentra la principal riqueza agrícola de la isla.

records.headline: A correspondent describes the Dominican part of the island as the center of a tobacco trade finding a market in Hamburg
records.summary_en: A correspondent describes the Dominican part of the island as the center of a tobacco trade finding a market in Hamburg, of rich cocoa plantations, and of gold and iron mining in the neighboring mountains, around towns including Cotui, La Vega and Santiago. The account then contrasts that region with the western division, Haiti, which it portrays in disparaging terms as bankrupt and decaying despite a favorable climate and soil.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal describe la parte dominicana de la isla como el centro de un comercio de tabaco que encuentra mercado en Hamburgo, de ricas plantaciones de cacao y de la minería de oro y hierro en las montañas vecinas, en torno a pueblos como Cotuí, La Vega y Santiago. El relato contrasta luego esa región con la división occidental, Haití, a la que retrata en términos denigrantes como arruinada y en decadencia pese a un clima y un suelo favorables.

records.headline: The News publishes a travel correspondence describing the geography
records.summary_en: The News publishes a travel correspondence describing the geography and historic sites of Santo Domingo. Sailing past the shores and the quiet waters of Samaná Bay, the correspondent notes luxuriant forests and little sign of human enterprise. He recounts visits to historic landmarks in the capital, including the cathedral housing Columbus's former tomb, Ovando's walls, and the ruins of Diego Columbus's house, lamenting that prolonged revolutions have impoverished the ancient city. The letter concludes with an admiration of the fertile Vega Real as seen from the summit of the Santo Cerro.
records.summary_es: El News publica una correspondencia de viaje que describe la geografía y los lugares históricos de Santo Domingo. Al navegar frente a las costas y las tranquilas aguas de la bahía de Samaná, el corresponsal advierte bosques exuberantes y escasos indicios de actividad humana. Relata visitas a monumentos históricos de la capital, entre ellos la catedral que albergó los restos de Colón, las murallas de Ovando y las ruinas de la casa de Diego Colón, lamentando que prolongadas revoluciones hayan empobrecido la antigua ciudad. La carta concluye con una admiración de la fértil Vega Real contemplada desde la cumbre del Santo Cerro.

records.headline: The Herald prints a revolutionary pronunciamiento issued from Jacmel
records.summary_en: The Herald prints a revolutionary pronunciamiento issued from Jacmel and circulating throughout Santo Domingo against the Samana Bay Company and President Báez, warning that American settlers at Samaná face mortal danger. The manifesto denounces the sale of the Samaná peninsula to an American joint-stock company as a renewed effort by speculators to execute the annexation that the United States Senate rejected in 1870. The insurgent leaders protest that the treaty dispossesses the Dominican people of their territory in violation of national law, asserting that no domestic legislature possesses the constitutional authority to alienate the country's sovereign lands.
records.summary_es: El Herald publica un pronunciamiento revolucionario emitido desde Jacmel y distribuido por todo Santo Domingo contra la Samana Bay Company y el presidente Báez, advirtiendo que los colonos estadounidenses en Samaná corren peligro de muerte. El manifiesto denuncia la venta de la península de Samaná a una sociedad por acciones estadounidense como un nuevo intento de los especuladores por consumar la anexión que el Senado de los Estados Unidos rechazó en 1870. Los líderes insurgentes protestan porque el tratado despoja al pueblo dominicano de su territorio en violación de las leyes nacionales, afirmando que ningún cuerpo legislativo nacional posee la facultad constitucional de enajenar las tierras soberanas del país.

records.headline: A proclamation issued at headquarters on January 10, 1873, and signed by Dominican leaders including Gregorio Luperon
records.summary_en: A proclamation issued at headquarters on January 10, 1873, and signed by Dominican leaders including Gregorio Luperon and Jose Maria Cabral, calls on Dominicans in this hour of sorrow to come as brethren and array themselves under the banner of liberty. It declares that the land must be rid now and forever of traitors and of the burning disgrace that has fallen upon it, and gives the rallying cry of liberty and independence, and down with Baez, their perpetual enemy.
records.summary_es: Una proclama emitida en el cuartel general el 10 de enero de 1873, y firmada por líderes dominicanos, entre ellos Gregorio Luperón y José María Cabral, llama a los dominicanos en esta hora de dolor a acudir como hermanos y formarse bajo la bandera de la libertad. Declara que la patria debe librarse ahora y para siempre de los traidores y de la ardiente vergüenza que ha caído sobre ella, y da como grito de unión libertad e independencia, y abajo Báez, su enemigo perpetuo.

records.headline: A special dispatch to the Tribune confirms that Dominican revolutionary leaders
records.summary_en: A special dispatch to the Tribune confirms that Dominican revolutionary leaders, headed by Gregorio Luperón and José María Cabral, have formed an alliance to overthrow President Báez following the sale of the Samaná peninsula. The paper publishes their pronunciamiento, which condemns the transaction with an American joint-stock company as an attempt to revive the rejected 1870 annexation treaty. Addressing the American public as "Sons of Washington," the manifesto invokes Senator Carl Schurz's warnings against acquiring tropical territories and insists that no Dominican Senate holds the legal authority to surrender national sovereignty over Samaná.
records.summary_es: Un despacho especial para el Tribune confirma que líderes revolucionarios dominicanos, encabezados por Gregorio Luperón y José María Cabral, han formado una alianza para derrocar al presidente Báez tras la venta de la península de Samaná. El diario publica su pronunciamiento, el cual condena la transacción con una compañía por acciones estadounidense como una maniobra para revivir el rechazado tratado de anexión de 1870. Al dirigirse al público estadounidense como «Hijos de Washington», el manifiesto invoca las advertencias del senador Carl Schurz contra la adquisición de posesiones tropicales e insiste en que ningún Senado dominicano posee la autoridad legal para ceder la soberanía nacional sobre Samaná.

records.headline: A dispatch from New York confirms that the revolutionary chiefs in San Domingo have allied against Baez, in a pronunciamiento
records.summary_en: A dispatch from New York confirms that the revolutionary chiefs in San Domingo have allied against Baez, in a pronunciamiento by Luperon, Cabral and twelve other leaders issued a few days after the sale of the Samana Peninsula. The proclamation protests the sale of Samana to an American company that will transfer its powers to the United States Government, denies that the Dominican Senate has power to grant such a commission to a foreign nation, and concludes with an appeal to all Dominicans to rally and wage a vigorous war against Baez.

records.headline: A Herald correspondent accompanies the Samana Bay Company's pioneers
records.summary_en: A Herald correspondent accompanies the Samana Bay Company's pioneers aboard their voyage to Santo Domingo, describing the expectations and diverse characters among the passengers. Led by Captain Samuels, the party includes a California miner named Oley seeking gold, a civil engineer named Halsey tasked with platting a future city and surveying a railroad line from Samaná Bay, and his assistant, Captain Plummer of West Point. Other settlers include Mr. Rennie of Canada, contemplating town lots, and Henry N. Marsh of New Jersey, who joined the expedition out of romantic enthusiasm for American colonization.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal del Herald acompaña a los pioneros de la Samana Bay Company en su travesía hacia Santo Domingo, y describe las expectativas y los diversos personajes entre los pasajeros. Encabezado por el capitán Samuels, el grupo incluye a un minero californiano llamado Oley en busca de oro, al ingeniero civil Halsey, encargado de trazar una futura ciudad y levantar el trazado de un ferrocarril desde la bahía de Samaná, y a su asistente, el capitán Plummer, egresado de West Point. Otros colonos incluyen al señor Rennie, de Canadá, quien contempla adquirir solares urbanos, y a Henry N. Marsh, de Nueva Jersey, quien se sumó a la expedición impulsado por el entusiasmo romántico hacia la colonización estadounidense.

records.headline: A Herald correspondent traveling in the Samana country reports that the Dominicans he meets are all for renting
records.summary_en: A Herald correspondent traveling in the Samana country reports that the Dominicans he meets are all for renting Samana Bay to an American company, expecting American capital and colonization to make their lives more prosperous; on the road he falls in with a party of Americans, one of them sketching with a banana stick a diagram of the country of La Vega and the course of the Yuna River.

records.headline: The Herald's correspondent describes an excursion into the countryside
records.summary_en: The Herald's correspondent describes an excursion into the countryside surrounding Samaná, portraying the extraordinary agricultural fertility of the leased territory. Visiting a grove with deep, black soil, the party sampled fresh coconuts and inspected cocoa trees, which mature in seven years, yield fruit for generations, and are valued at ten dollars each under local standards. The writer also tours a 150-acre sugar plantation that produces 400 barrels of sugar, 200 barrels of molasses, and substantial quantities of native aguardiente each year, concluding with an elaborate Dominican eleven o'clock breakfast.
records.summary_es: El corresponsal del Herald describe una excursión por los campos que rodean a Samaná, retratando la extraordinaria fertilidad agrícola del territorio arrendado. Al visitar una plantación con tierra negra y profunda, la comitiva probó cocos frescos e inspeccionó árboles de cacao, los cuales maduran en siete años, producen frutos durante generaciones y están valorados en diez dólares cada uno según los estándares locales. El autor recorre también un ingenio azucarero de 150 acres que produce anualmente 400 barriles de azúcar, 200 barriles de melaza y abundantes cantidades de aguardiente del país, concluyendo con un suculento desayuno dominicano servido a las once de la mañana.

records.headline: A New York Herald correspondent reports that trade in the Dominican Republic contends
records.summary_en: A New York Herald correspondent reports that trade in the Dominican Republic contends with a moneyless populace, worthless currency, a lack of roads, chronic dissension, and the specter of Haitian invasion. Turning to the mercantile outlook, the correspondent quotes Mr. Uhrlaub's view that many Puerto Plata merchants would open branch houses in Samana to benefit from its status as a free port. While some local wholesalers feared losing interior customers to Samana, others planned to secure premises there to retain trade, leaving general unease in Puerto Plata over the venture. A map key in the passage outlines areas under the sway of the Samana Bay Company totaling over two million acres, including Monte Cristi, Manzanillo Bay, the Royal Plain, and a mining district.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal del New York Herald informa que el comercio en la República Dominicana lidia con una población sin dinero, una moneda sin valor, la falta de caminos, discordias crónicas y el espectro de una invasión haitiana. Al abordar la perspectiva mercantil, el corresponsal cita la opinión del señor Uhrlaub de que muchos comerciantes de Puerto Plata abrirían sucursales en Samaná para beneficiarse de su condición de puerto libre. Si bien algunos mayoristas locales temían perder clientes del interior a favor de Samaná, otros planeaban adquirir locales allí para conservar su comercio, lo que dejaba una inquietud general en Puerto Plata sobre la empresa. Una clave de mapa en el pasaje describe zonas bajo el dominio de la Samana Bay Company que superan los dos millones de acres, entre ellas Monte Cristi, la bahía de Manzanillo, la Vega Real y un distrito minero.

records.headline: A correspondent's letter from Santa Barbara, Samana Bay, dated February 13, 1873, describes arriving aboard the Tybee
records.summary_en: A correspondent's letter from Santa Barbara, Samana Bay, dated February 13, 1873, describes arriving aboard the Tybee at sunrise and being welcomed by Colonel Joseph Warren Fabens, presented as governor of the peninsula, and by Mr. Price, the consul. The pioneer emigrants of the Samana Bay Company settlement are aboard inspecting the discharge of the vessel's freight and looking over the village of Santa Barbara, with its eighty-four houses, as the place where their future settlement and homes are to be made.
records.summary_es: La carta de un corresponsal desde Santa Bárbara, bahía de Samaná, fechada el 13 de febrero de 1873, describe la llegada a bordo del Tybee al amanecer y la bienvenida del coronel Joseph Warren Fabens, presentado como gobernador de la península, y del señor Price, el cónsul. Los emigrantes pioneros del asentamiento de la Compañía de la Bahía de Samaná están a bordo inspeccionando la descarga del cargamento del buque y observando el pueblo de Santa Bárbara, con sus ochenta y cuatro casas, como el lugar donde se harán su futuro asentamiento y sus hogares.
records.passage: plants and trees familiar to the readers of tropical botany. Presently there came on deck Colonel Joseph Warren Fabens, who owns a handsome slice of this territory. I looked for some display of emotion in his address of welcome, for was he not Governor of the Peninsula, and were we not the pioneer colony destined to make Samana the talk and the envy of the world! He was happy to see us, and so was Mr. Price, the Consul, whose residence on the high jutting promontory made every [pilgrim?] [illegible] expand with the anticipation of having some such elevated station for life. Fabens set about the work of inspecting the discharge of the vessel's freight, and the voice of Albert, the mate, might have been heard through the early morning echoing among the hills, keeping the dusky stevedores to their duty. One of the native canoes rowed by a darky, whose Philadelphia parents allowed him to get hopelessly involved in the Spanish dialect, took two of us to Santa Barbara, and through the various streets, lanes, alleys and nondescript squares of that singular village of eighty-four houses we wandered in the early forenoon. In the meantime, of course, there was great commotion among the emigrants on board. All eyes were riveted on the scene of the future settlement. records.headline: A Dominican minister, interviewed by the Herald's correspondent
records.summary_en: A Dominican minister, interviewed by the Herald's correspondent, complains that sections of the United States press unfairly portray the Santo Domingo government as guided solely by intrigue and dishonesty. Asked how the ratification vote on the Samana transfer was taken, the minister explains that polling the nation took roughly a month under the Dominican system. He states that more than 20,000 votes had been cast for the government's policy—expected to reach 22,000 once complete—surpassing the 4,000 votes cast for Spanish annexation and the 16,000 recorded for American annexation. He adds that local commanders kept registry books in each section, though poor communication and public apathy required keeping them open for several weeks.
records.summary_es: En una entrevista con el corresponsal del Herald, un ministro dominicano se queja de que sectores de la prensa de los Estados Unidos presentan injustamente al gobierno de Santo Domingo como guiado únicamente por la intriga y la deshonestidad. Al ser consultado sobre cómo se realizó la votación de ratificación de la cesión de Samaná, el ministro explica que sondear a la nación tomó aproximadamente un mes bajo el sistema dominicano. Afirma que se habían emitido más de 20.000 votos a favor de la política del gobierno —cifra que se esperaba alcanzara los 22.000 una vez completa—, superando los 4.000 votos emitidos para la anexión a España y los 16.000 registrados para la anexión a los Estados Unidos. Agrega que los comandantes locales mantenían libros de registro en cada sección, aunque la deficiente comunicación y la apatía pública exigían mantenerlos abiertos durante varias semanas.

records.headline: A dispatch from Samana dated February 21, 1873, reports that the steamer
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Samana dated February 21, 1873, reports that the steamer Tybee is departing for New York and that the visiting pilgrims have all left. The correspondent notes that one visitor paid $2,009 for a plantation near the city belonging to Burr, and that many strangers have arrived. The writer promises to inspect the locality that evening and provide a full account of its health and prospects at another time.

El corresponsal señala que un visitante pagó 2.009 dólares por una plantación cercana a la ciudad perteneciente a Burr y que han llegado muchos forasteros. El autor promete recorrer el lugar esa misma tarde y ofrecer en otra oportunidad un informe completo sobre sus condiciones sanitarias y perspectivas.

records.headline: An editorial presents a first look at the 'dreamland' in St. Domingo
records.summary_en: An editorial presents a first look at the 'dreamland' in St. Domingo that speculators of the Samana Bay Company have fenced in with treaties, leases and powers, describing Santa Barbara as a delightful spot, the bay as first-class anchorage, and the soil as fertile. It notes that the $150,000 paid to Baez smoothed away much of the first difficulty and that Baez's ministers reported 22,000 votes cast for the treaty, while questioning what would happen when the people saw how little of the company's money reached beyond Baez's coffers.
records.summary_es: Un editorial presenta una primera mirada al 'país de ensueño' en Santo Domingo que los especuladores de la Samana Bay Company han cercado con tratados, arrendamientos y poderes, describiendo Santa Bárbara como un lugar encantador, la bahía como un fondeadero de primera clase, y el suelo como fértil. Señala que los 150.000 dólares pagados a Báez allanaron gran parte de la primera dificultad y que los ministros de Báez informaron de 22.000 votos a favor del tratado, mientras se pregunta qué pasará cuando la gente vea lo poco del dinero de la compañía que llega más allá de las arcas de Báez.

records.headline: A New York Herald commissioner reports from Puerto Plata on February 10
records.summary_en: A New York Herald commissioner reports from Puerto Plata on February 10, 1873, describing his arrival aboard the steamer Tybee alongside a party of pilgrims seeking golden fortunes under the auspices of the Samana Bay Company. The correspondent reflects that Columbus landed nearby more than four centuries earlier, giving the island the name Hispaniola and styling it the Cradle of the New World. Citing Brown's history of Santo Domingo, the writer remarks that the island ultimately proved an unfortunate cradle for all concerned. The passage also includes a series of display headlines outlining upcoming sections on Samana sugar plantations, interviews on the ratification vote, and the company's mercantile aspects.
records.summary_es: Un comisionado del New York Herald informa desde Puerto Plata el 10 de febrero de 1873, describiendo su llegada a bordo del vapor Tybee junto a un grupo de peregrinos que buscaban amasar fortunas bajo el auspicio de la Samana Bay Company. El corresponsal reflexiona que Colón desembarcó en las cercanías hace más de cuatro siglos, bautizando la isla con el nombre de La Española y calificándola como la Cuna del Nuevo Mundo. Al citar la historia de Santo Domingo de Brown, el autor señala que la isla resultó ser, en definitiva, una cuna desafortunada para todos los involucrados. El pasaje incluye además una serie de titulares destacados que anuncian secciones sobre plantaciones de azúcar en Samaná, entrevistas sobre la votación de ratificación y los aspectos mercantiles de la compañía.

records.headline: Advices from San Domingo report the publication, and the dissemination through the island, of a pronunciamiento on behalf of a number of revolutionary leaders.
records.summary_en: Advices from San Domingo report the publication, and the dissemination through the island, of a pronunciamiento on behalf of a number of revolutionary leaders. The pronunciamiento aims at the overthrow of President Baez and the establishment of an independent government.
records.summary_es: Noticias de Santo Domingo informan de la publicación, y de la difusión por toda la isla, de un pronunciamiento en nombre de varios líderes revolucionarios. El pronunciamiento tiene por objeto el derrocamiento del presidente Báez y el establecimiento de un gobierno independiente.

records.headline: In an interview with a Herald commissioner, President Grant states
records.summary_en: In an interview with a Herald commissioner, President Grant states that he anticipates no difficulties arising from the Samana Bay Company, characterizing its leaders as practical businessmen who will avoid expensive entanglements. The President predicts that within ten or fifteen years the company will have developed the country's resources so substantially that the United States will annex it as a bargain for ten or fifteen million dollars, having missed obtaining it earlier for one and a half million. Emphasizing that he means the Dominican Republic, Grant adds that his administration desires peace and expects no trouble with Haiti. The Herald commissioner remarks that such an outcome would not surprise him, even though Alaska's purchase had dampened American enthusiasm for annexation.
records.summary_es: En una entrevista con un comisionado del Herald, el presidente Grant declara que no prevé dificultades derivadas de la Samana Bay Company, calificando a sus dirigentes de hombres de negocios prácticos que evitarán complicaciones costosas. El presidente predice que dentro de diez o quince años la compañía habrá desarrollado los recursos del país de forma tan notable que los Estados Unidos lo anexarán como una ganga por diez o quince millones de dólares, habiendo perdido la oportunidad de adquirirlo antes por un millón y medio. Al recalcar que se refiere a la República Dominicana, Grant añade que su gobierno desea la paz y no espera problemas con Haití. El comisionado del Herald comenta que dicho desenlace no le causaría sorpresa, aun cuando la compra de Alaska hubiese templado el entusiasmo estadounidense por la anexión.

records.headline: An editorial in the New York Herald comments on an interview
records.summary_en: An editorial in the New York Herald comments on an interview with President Grant, noting that in the matter of Santo Domingo the President did a major favor for the backers of the Samana Bay Company. The writer remarks that company secretary Rowland Hazard's eyes must have beamed with delight upon reading Grant's prediction that the nation would buy the bay from them in ten or fifteen years for ten or fifteen million dollars. The editorial observes that Hazard was the figure who orchestrated the commercial transaction, before turning to Grant's views on Cuba, Louisiana, and travel plans.

El editorial subraya que Hazard fue quien gestionó la operación comercial, antes de abordar las opiniones de Grant sobre Cuba, Luisiana y sus planes de viaje.

records.headline: A Washington report in The Weekly Visitor reviews President Grant's optimistic
records.summary_en: A Washington report in The Weekly Visitor reviews President Grant's optimistic perspectives on foreign and domestic affairs. Regarding Santo Domingo, the President expressed confidence that the recent purchase and proposed American settlement there will succeed, ultimately leading to the annexation of the Dominican Republic to the United States within ten or fifteen years. The report notes Grant's equally confident forecasts concerning Spanish republicanism, Cuban independence, Mormon compliance with federal law, and conditions in Louisiana, concluding that the Chief Magistrate holds an exceptionally roseate view of public affairs.
records.summary_es: Una crónica de Washington en The Weekly Visitor analiza las optimistas perspectivas del presidente Grant sobre los asuntos internos y exteriores. Respecto a Santo Domingo, el mandatario expresó su convicción de que la reciente adquisición y el proyectado asentamiento estadounidense en la zona tendrán éxito, conduciendo finalmente a la anexión de la República Dominicana a los Estados Unidos en un plazo de diez o quince años. El informe recoge los pronósticos igualmente confiados de Grant acerca del republicanismo español, la independencia de Cuba, el acatamiento de las leyes federales por parte de los mormones y la situación en Luisiana, concluyendo que el presidente mantiene una visión sumamente optimista del panorama nacional.

records.headline: The paper reports that a Dominican governor forcibly removed three men who had sought refuge under the British flag
records.summary_en: The paper reports that a Dominican governor forcibly removed three men who had sought refuge under the British flag at the home of the British consul, an act the community feared could draw a response from an expected British warship. It also recounts an earlier mountain revolt against President Báez, linked in the report to opposition to a territorial surrender to a company, which the governor quickly crushed.
records.summary_es: El periódico informa que un gobernador dominicano sacó por la fuerza a tres hombres que habían buscado refugio bajo la bandera británica en la casa del cónsul británico, un acto que, según se temía en la comunidad, podría provocar una respuesta de un buque de guerra británico esperado. También relata una revuelta anterior en las montañas contra el presidente Báez, vinculada en el informe a la oposición a una cesión territorial a una compañía, que el gobernador aplastó rápidamente.

records.headline: A Puerto Plata report prints a letter from the British vice-consul stating that General Juan Nuezl, former governor of the city
records.summary_en: A Puerto Plata report prints a letter from the British vice-consul stating that General Juan Nuezl, former governor of the city, and his sons Martin and Claudia had claimed the protection of the British flag at his home. When the authorities ruled that the consul's private house was not his consulate, the mayor surrounded the house, entered it by force after three summonses, and took the three Nuezis prisoner to the fort in irons; one son said his father opposed the Samana lease and had determined to oppose it by physical force.
records.summary_es: Un informe de Puerto Plata publica una carta del vicecónsul británico que declara que el general Juan Nuezl, antiguo gobernador de la ciudad, y sus hijos Martín y Claudia habían reclamado la protección de la bandera británica en su casa. Cuando las autoridades resolvieron que la casa particular del cónsul no era su consulado, el alcalde rodeó la casa, entró en ella por la fuerza tras tres requerimientos, y llevó a los tres Nuezl prisioneros al fuerte con grilletes; un hijo dijo que su padre se oponía al arrendamiento de Samaná y había decidido oponerse a él por la fuerza física.

records.headline: A Herald correspondent interviews an imprisoned former governor who says he took up arms because he wanted liberty of expression
records.summary_en: A Herald correspondent interviews an imprisoned former governor who says he took up arms because he wanted liberty of expression in the vote concerning the sale of Samana. He insists the people were dragooned into voting for the Baez measure and would have voted against it if the pressure had been taken off, that none of the money paid by the Americans would benefit the country but would go into the pockets of Baez and his associates, and that the government has done nothing for the people toward Monte Cristo who have had no rain in two years.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal del Herald entrevista a un exgobernador encarcelado que dice que tomó las armas porque quería libertad de expresión en la votación sobre la venta de Samaná. Insiste en que la gente fue obligada a votar por la medida de Báez y habría votado en contra si se le hubiera quitado la presión, que nada del dinero pagado por los estadounidenses beneficiaría al país sino que iría a los bolsillos de Báez y sus asociados, y que el gobierno no ha hecho nada por la gente de hacia Monte Cristi que lleva dos años sin lluvia.

records.headline: A New York Herald correspondent reports that the formal transfer of Samana Bay involved
records.summary_en: A New York Herald correspondent reports that the formal transfer of Samana Bay involved no ceremony, as President Báez cared only for the $150,000 in gold paid as annual rent. The dispatch satirizes Joseph Fabens, now serving as governor of Samana, and his son Joe, describing the youth as aspiring to become president of Santo Domingo on a diet of lemonade and ship biscuits. The correspondent remarks that Fabens holds unknown quantities of land in Samana, and reflects that Santa Barbara—which promoters proposed renaming Stockwell—could become an agreeable town if roads were built, swamps drained, chills and fever eliminated, and streets properly graded.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal del New York Herald informa que el traspaso formal de la bahía de Samaná se efectuó sin ceremonia alguna, ya que al presidente Báez sólo le interesaban los 150.000 dólares en oro entregados como renta anual. El despacho satiriza a Joseph Fabens, quien funge ahora como gobernador de Samaná, y a su hijo Joe, describiendo al joven con aspiraciones de ser algún día presidente de Santo Domingo a base de limonada y galletas de barco. El corresponsal observa que Fabens posee una cantidad indeterminada de solares en Samaná, y reflexiona que Santa Bárbara —a la que los promotores pretendían rebautizar como Stockwell— podría ser un pueblo agradable si se construyera una calzada costera, se drenaran los pantanos, se erradicaran las fiebres y se nivelaran adecuadamente las calles.

records.headline: An editorial reports that at Puerto Plata a civil and military force under the Dominican Minister of Finance forcibly
records.summary_en: An editorial reports that at Puerto Plata a civil and military force under the Dominican Minister of Finance forcibly entered the residence of the British Vice Consul, Mr. Hamburger, and seized three citizens, enemies of Baez and opponents of the Samana sale, who were thrown into a dungeon, and that Baez approved the arrests and ordered the prisoners brought to Santo Domingo City. It warns that a British man-of-war is expected to demand satisfaction, and that Baez must not imagine the United States will protect him, since the Americans who paid $150,000 down for a year's rent of Samana Bay represent only themselves and their purchase implies no American protectorate.
records.summary_es: Un editorial informa que en Puerto Plata una fuerza civil y militar bajo el ministro de Finanzas dominicano entró por la fuerza en la residencia del vicecónsul británico, el señor Hamburger, y apresó a tres ciudadanos, enemigos de Baez y opositores a la venta de Samana, que fueron arrojados a un calabozo, y que Baez aprobó los arrestos y ordenó llevar a los prisioneros a la ciudad de Santo Domingo. records.headline: Writing from Santiago de los Caballeros on March 4, the correspondent describes his eight-day journey across St. Domingo
records.summary_en: Writing from Santiago de los Caballeros on March 4, the correspondent describes his eight-day journey across St. Domingo from Samana, three days of it in a canoe slowly ascending the Yuna River from Santa Barbara to Almacen. On the way the party spent a night in hammocks at Bebedero and joined a marriage feast at a house near Santa Capuza, with music, dancing, tiny cups of coffee and revolver shots fired in honour of the event, before entering the small mouth of the Yuna at midday.
records.summary_es: Escribiendo desde Santiago de los Caballeros el 4 de marzo, el corresponsal describe su viaje de ocho días a través de Santo Domingo desde Samaná, tres de ellos en una canoa que remontaba lentamente el río Yuna desde Santa Bárbara hasta Almacén. En el camino el grupo pasó una noche en hamacas en Bebedero y se unió a una fiesta de boda en una casa cerca de Santa Capuza, con música, baile, tacitas de café y disparos de revólver en honor del acontecimiento, antes de entrar al mediodía por la boca pequeña del Yuna.
records.passage: retired to a palm grove, near the house, and fired off half a dozen rounds of ammunition in honor of the event, a proceeding which tickled the rejoicing household Immensely. It was midday When we entered the Boca [Chica?] or small mouth of the Yuna, the river on which the Samana Bay Company expect to put a steamer one of these days to drain the trade of the La Vega country. There is a bar at this mouth and a bar at the other, a short distance off the Boca Grande or large mouth, and the depth of water over each is about two feet and a half. The shores at the entrance, covered with vegetation, are exceedingly low, not more than a few inches above the water, disappearing altogether when the river is full. Here the festive alligator may be found and the mud he loves, for his pallet is spread over endless acres. A few hundred feet within the mouth of the river the depth is three feet, which is retained throughout all the tortuous windings of this stream to the village of Almasin, thirty-three miles' sailing distance, or seventeen as the bird flies.
