records.summary_en: The *Waterbury Evening Democrat* reported on the clandestine expedition of the steamer *Fanita*, which picked up exiled General Villanueva and pilot Chris Roberts at Great Inagua while concealing insurgent troops in its hold. Led by General Juan Isidro Jimenes, the expedition aimed to overthrow President Heureaux following extensive preparations. Although early observers expected success, the Dominican consul reported that the insurgent force had been defeated upon landing at Monte Cristi.

Encabezada por el general Juan Isidro Jimenes, la expedición tenía por objetivo derrocar al presidente Heureaux tras minuciosos preparativos. Aunque los primeros observadores auguraban el éxito, el cónsul dominicano informó que la fuerza insurgente había sido derrotada al desembarcar en Monte Cristi.

records.summary_en: The *Wichita Daily Eagle* reported conflicting accounts regarding an armed expedition led by General Juan Isidro Jimenes against Dominican President Heureaux. While the Dominican consul claimed the insurgents were defeated at Monte Cristi, other reports stated the rebels had landed munitions from the *Fanita* and were marching toward Puerto Plata and Santiago de los Caballeros. The paper described Jimenes as an influential merchant and former presidential heir who had long avoided Heureaux's violent crackdowns on political rivals.
records.summary_es: El *Wichita Daily Eagle* informó sobre versiones contradictorias relativas a una expedición armada encabezada por el general Juan Isidro Jimenes contra el presidente dominicano Heureaux. Mientras el cónsul dominicano aseguraba que los insurgentes habían sido derrotados en Monte Cristi, otros informes señalaban que los rebeldes habían desembarcado pertrechos desde el *Fanita* y marchaban hacia Puerto Plata y Santiago de los Caballeros. El diario describió a Jimenes como un influyente comerciante e hijo de un antiguo mandatario que durante largo tiempo había evadido las violentas represalias de Heureaux contra sus rivales políticos.

The most circumstantial reports have it that the insurgents are now in considerable force, and under Generals Jiminez and Villanueva they are marching on Puerto Plata, while another detachment is moving against Santiago de los Caballeros, on the Yaqui river, 100 miles east of this place. records.headline: An editorial on the Spanish-American republics: they are republics
records.summary_en: An editorial on the Spanish-American republics: they are republics only in name, in the throes of revolutions, liberty is nominal, and the presidents are more like military dictators than anything else, the inhabitants speaking French in the republic of Hayti and Spanish in the republic of Santo Domingo. An attempt to overturn President Heureaux's government in Santo Domingo has recently been foiled, and its leading instigators have been executed, and this is only one of a long series of similar revolts on the island; and the editorial, rating the native people of Cuba as considerably superior in intelligence and ability to the Haytians and Dominicans, doubts whether a stable government can be secured for the Cubans in a short space of time without the aid and protection of the United States.
records.summary_es: Un editorial sobre las repúblicas hispanoamericanas: son repúblicas solo en el nombre, en medio de revoluciones, la libertad es nominal y los presidentes son más parecidos a dictadores militares que a otra cosa, hablando los habitantes francés en la república de Haití y español en la república de Santo Domingo. Un intento de derrocar el gobierno del presidente Heureaux en Santo Domingo ha sido frustrado recientemente, y sus principales instigadores han sido ejecutados, y esto es solo una de una larga serie de revueltas similares en la isla; y el editorial, que estima a los nativos de Cuba como considerablemente superiores en inteligencia y habilidad a los haitianos y los dominicanos, duda que pueda asegurarse un gobierno estable para los cubanos en poco tiempo sin la ayuda y protección de los Estados Unidos.

records.headline: The Tribune prints the assassination rumor from Cape Haytien
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints the assassination rumor from Cape Haytien: it is rumored there that President Heureaux of San Domingo has been assassinated, and the Associated Press correspondent at Monte Cristi, San Domingo, gives further confirmation of the failure of the attempted revolution there. The son of Señor Jiminez, the wealthy merchant who took part in the revolution in San Domingo, at 11 o'clock this morning was still without news from the revolutionists as to the result of the attempt to overthrow President Heureaux, but he is disposed to believe the worst; he ascribes the supposed defeat of the revolutionists to the lack of opportunity to land from the Fanita at Monte Cristi, to the failure to seize Señor Galito, the Governor of the province, as had been planned, and to the death at the first fire of the two foremost military leaders.

records.headline: The Tribune prints the captain's account of the Monte Cristi landing:
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints the captain's account of the Monte Cristi landing: General Jiminez again went ashore, returning to the ship with ten men, who, he told the captain, were laborers engaged by him to unload the cargo as soon as the vessel reached Cuba, and he added that his advices were still to the effect that it was unsafe to land an expedition in Cuba just yet, and that he desired to touch at Monte Cristi, San Domingo, where important news was awaiting him. Monte Cristi was reached on Thursday, June 2; on casting anchor the captain was surprised to see General Jiminez come on deck in uniform and fully armed, followed by General Morrillo and the other two officers, similarly equipped; they ordered thirty-seven rifles and two cases of ammunition to be put aboard the long boat that was to row them ashore, and then commanded the ten alleged laborers to take their seats in the boat, 'Chris' Roberts remaining on board the Fanita. The captain understood that something was wrong, but he was reassured by Roberts and General Jiminez, and shortly after 6 o'clock in the morning the boat was rowed ashore by three sailors and the second mate of the Fanita; no sooner had they reached the wharf, where General Jiminez and his party landed, than a volley of musketry was heard and three of the men fell wounded, the first to fall being General Morrillo, pierced through the breast by a bullet; troops were seen advancing in large numbers, and the little band of fourteen was soon cut down to five, and the sailors in the Fanita's boat shoved off from the wharf amid a rain of bullets.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica el relato del capitán sobre el desembarco de la Fanita en Monte Cristi: el general Jiminez bajó de nuevo a tierra, regresando al buque con diez hombres, quienes, según dijo al capitán, eran jornaleros contratados por él para descargar el cargamento tan pronto como el buque llegara a Cuba, y añadió que sus avisos seguían siendo en el sentido de que todavía no era seguro desembarcar una expedición en Cuba, y que deseaba tocar Monte Cristi, Santo Domingo, donde le esperaba noticia importante. Se llegó a Monte Cristi el jueves 2 de junio; al echar el ancla el capitán se sorprendió de ver al general Jiminez salir a cubierta en uniforme y completamente armado, seguido por el general Morrillo y los otros dos oficiales, igualmente equipados; ordenaron poner a bordo de la lancha que los llevaría a tierra treinta y siete rifles y dos cajas de municiones, y luego mandaron a los diez supuestos jornaleros tomar sus asientos en la lancha, quedando 'Chris' Roberts a bordo de la Fanita. El capitán entendió que algo andaba mal, pero fue tranquilizado por Roberts y el general Jiminez, y poco después de las 6 de la mañana la lancha fue remada a tierra por tres marineros y el segundo oficial de la Fanita; apenas llegaron al muelle, donde desembarcaron el general Jiminez y su grupo, se escuchó una descarga de fusilería y tres de los hombres cayeron heridos, siendo el primero en caer el general Morrillo, atravesado el pecho por una bala; se vieron tropas avanzando en gran número, y la pequeña banda de catorce pronto quedó reducida a cinco, y los marineros de la lancha de la Fanita se alejaron del muelle en medio de una lluvia de balas.

records.headline: The Call prints word of the arrest of Señor Jiminez at Inagua
records.summary_en: The Call prints word of the arrest of Señor Jiminez at Inagua and an interview with President Heureaux: Señor Jiminez, the leader of the revolutionary expedition which recently landed in Santo Domingo from Hayti, on his arrival at Inagua from Monte Cristi, Santo Domingo, was arrested by the British authorities for a violation of the navigation laws in flying a Clyde line flag, though the Fanita, the vessel in which the expedition sailed, had been sold by the Clyde line company six months before; Chris Roberts, the pilot of the expedition, made a complaint on the above ground, and the American Consul also prosecuted Señor Jiminez, alleging that the expedition was illegal, inasmuch as the Fanita's papers were ostensibly for service in Cuban waters. From Puerto Plata, Dominican Republic, June 6, the correspondent reports an interview with President Heureaux, who proceeds to Monte Cristi to-night on board a warship; he declares the country quiet, and has confiscated all the property of Jiminez.
records.summary_es: El Call publica la noticia del arresto del señor Jiminez en Inagua y una entrevista con el presidente Heureaux: el señor Jiminez, el líder de la expedición revolucionaria que recientemente desembarcó en Santo Domingo procedente de Haití, a su llegada a Inagua desde Monte Cristi, Santo Domingo, fue arrestado por las autoridades británicas por una violación de las leyes de navegación al enarbolar una bandera de la línea Clyde, aunque la Fanita, el buque en que zarpó la expedición, había sido vendida por la compañía de la línea Clyde seis meses antes; Chris Roberts, el piloto de la expedición, presentó una denuncia por ese motivo, y el cónsul americano también procesó al señor Jiminez, alegando que la expedición era ilegal, ya que los papeles de la Fanita eran ostensiblemente para servicio en aguas cubanas. Desde Puerto Plata, República Dominicana, el 6 de junio, el corresponsal informa de una entrevista con el presidente Heureaux, quien parte hacia Monte Cristi esta noche a bordo de un buque de guerra; declara que el país está tranquilo, y ha confiscado toda la propiedad de Jiminez.

crop will, no doubt, be the lightest the
Lodi section has known in years— possibly

records.headline: The Press prints a dispatch on the aftermath of the Monte Cristi landing:
records.summary_en: The Press prints a dispatch on the aftermath of the Monte Cristi landing: three prisoners were taken in the recent abortive revolutionary attempt headed by Jiminez and Morales, and Commodore Jansen landed to receive the report of the Dominican consul on the illegal shipments of men from this point by the two leaders to participate in the landing at Monte Cristi. The warships left Monte Cristi at eleven o'clock this morning, and a rumor is current that after they left President Heureaux was made a prisoner in a new uprising and was shot, the report having it that Joaquin Taveras, Lieutenant Commander at Monte Cristi under Governor Galito, led the new movement; the story is not believed, although no explicit reply is forthcoming from Monte Cristi to cabled inquiries. It appears that General Jiminez was transferred from the Fanita, on which he escaped from Monte Cristi, to another steamer before landing at Great Inagua, and it is said that he has been released on bail of 200 pounds; the Fanita did not venture within the jurisdiction of the island authorities on her return voyage.

Los buques de guerra salieron de Monte Cristi a las once de esta mañana, y corre el rumor de que después de su salida el presidente Heureaux fue hecho prisionero en un nuevo levantamiento y fusilado, sosteniendo el reporte que Joaquín Taveras, teniente comandante en Monte Cristi bajo el gobernador Galito, encabezó el nuevo movimiento; la historia no es creída, aunque no llega de Monte Cristi respuesta explícita alguna a las indagaciones cablegráficas. Parece que el general Jiminez fue transferido de la Fanita, en la que escapó de Monte Cristi, a otro vapor antes de desembarcar en Gran Inagua, y se dice que ha sido liberado bajo fianza de 200 libras; la Fanita no se aventuró dentro de la jurisdicción de las autoridades de la isla en su viaje de regreso.

records.headline: The Enterprise prints the Fanita's story, a filibustering voyage
records.summary_en: The Enterprise prints the Fanita's story, a filibustering voyage: so far from being engaged in peaceful traffic, she had been for two weeks on a filibustering expedition, and from Tampa the Fanita was ordered to Mobile, ostensibly to take an expedition to Cuba under the charge of Jiminez and Morrillo, both Dominicans, but strongly sympathetic with the movement for Cuban independence. Monte Cristi, San Domingo, was reached on June 2; on casting anchor the captain was surprised to see Jiminez come on deck in uniform, fully armed, and the others similarly equipped; they ordered 37 rifles and two cases of ammunition to be put aboard the boat that was to row them ashore, and then commanded the ten alleged laborers on board to take their seats in the boat; the captain understood that something was wrong, but the boat was rowed ashore. No sooner had they reached the wharf, where Jiminez and his party landed, than a volley of musketry was heard and three of the party fell wounded, the first to fall being Morrillo, pierced through the breast by a bullet; troops were seen advancing in large numbers, and the little band of 14 was soon cut down to five; the sailors in the Fanita's boat were seized with terror and shoved off from the wharf amid a rain of bullets; Jiminez jumped into the boat just in time and, seizing an oar, joined the crew in pulling for dear life, and the last seen of the landing party was the figures of two men covered with blood struggling desperately against superior odds in the face of blazing muskets; Jiminez reached the Fanita in safety.

records.headline: The State Journal prints a Cape Haytien dispatch on President Heureaux's pursuit of Jiminez:
records.summary_en: The State Journal prints a Cape Haytien dispatch on President Heureaux's pursuit of Jiminez: some mystery was observed regarding the visit of the Dominican gunboat Restoracion to that port last evening, and it transpired that President Heureaux of San Domingo was aboard the vessel, and that from there he goes to Inagua, where Señor Jiminez was last known to be located, the Restoracion having left Cape Haytien before 5 o'clock this morning. Commodore Jansen, who came ashore shortly after the arrival of the Restoracion to receive the report of the Dominican consul on the alleged illegal shipment of men from that point by Señor Jiminez and his fellow leader to take part in the landing of the revolutionists at Monte Cristi, spent the greater part of the night with the consul. The Dominican gunboat Independencia did not enter the port in company with the Restoracion, as cabled last night; she proceeded to Port de Paix in order to investigate the report of Jiminez's presence at that place, just before the revolutionary attempt at Monte Cristi; and it is understood that if President Heureaux finds that Jiminez is still there he will make an effort to induce the authorities to deliver the insurgent to him on the charge of piracy.
records.summary_es: El State Journal publica un despacho de Cabo Haitiano sobre la persecución de Jiminez por el presidente Heureaux: se observó cierto misterio en torno a la visita del cañonero dominicano Restoracion a ese puerto anoche, y se supo que el presidente Heureaux de Santo Domingo iba a bordo del buque, y que desde allí va a Inagua, donde se supo por última vez que estaba el señor Jiminez, habiendo la Restoracion salido de Cabo Haitiano antes de las 5 de esta mañana. El comodoro Jansen, que bajó a tierra poco después de la llegada de la Restoracion para recibir el informe del cónsul dominicano sobre el alegado embarque ilegal de hombres desde ese punto por el señor Jiminez y su compañero líder para tomar parte en el desembarco de los revolucionarios en Monte Cristi, pasó la mayor parte de la noche con el cónsul. El cañonero dominicano Independencia no entró al puerto en compañía de la Restoracion, como se cablegrafió anoche; procedió a Port de Paix para investigar el reporte de la presencia de Jiminez en ese lugar, justo antes del intento revolucionario en Monte Cristi; y se entiende que si el presidente Heureaux encuentra que Jiminez todavía está allí hará un esfuerzo para inducir a las autoridades a entregarle al insurgente bajo el cargo de piratería.

records.headline: The Sun prints a letter on the Dominica and Santo Domingo names
records.summary_en: The Sun prints a letter on the Dominica and Santo Domingo names: a correspondent protests against the name Dominica given to the island he has known as Hayti, of which San Domingo is one of the political divisions; the island of Dominica, as he has known it, is one of the Windward group near Martinique, owned by Great Britain, and the people of that island are known as Dominicans, while San Domingo, which should properly be called Santo Domingo — the original Española of Columbus, for centuries after its discovery known by the Latinized form of Hispaniola — is quite a different country from Dominica, and the Santo Domingoans are an entirely different people from the Dominicans. Dominica is the ecclesiastical form of Domingo, the Spanish for Sunday, and was applied to the island which bears the name because Columbus discovered it on that day; the island was later settled by the French and ultimately passed into the hands of the English, and the writer thinks it important to call attention to these facts in these days when Americans are obtaining such rapid lessons in West India geography. He has also seen in the press many allusions to the meaning of the word morro, which some have confused with 'Moro,' the Spanish for 'Moor'; the Spaniards employed the word morro to signify any round-shaped projection, whether horizontal like a promontory or perpendicular like a circular butte or mountain, or for a round fortification like Castle Williams.

records.headline: The Republican prints the June 10 dispatch from Cape Haytien
records.summary_en: The Republican prints the June 10 dispatch from Cape Haytien: President Ulysses Heureaux, of the Dominican Republic, believes he has discovered proof that the steamer Fanita, formerly of the Clyde line, which was used by Señor Jiminez and Morales in their unsuccessful attempt to overthrow the Dominican government, left the United States with the countenance of the American government, under a mere pretense of taking munitions of war to Cuba. President Heureaux arrived there yesterday on the Dominican gunboat Restauracion, from Great Inagua; while there he personally made a charge of piracy against Señor Jiminez, who had previously been released on bail under a charge of having violated the navigation laws, and a Dominican agent was left at Matthew Town to look after the case until an advocate can be sent there from San Domingo to push the prosecution. General Heureaux talked with the greatest apparent freedom about the recent revolutionary attempt, ridiculing Jiminez and the preparations the latter had made; he told how the revolution was nipped in the bud, and how he had executed nearly all the prisoners, reserving only those who, he thought, might be useful in obtaining further information about the conspiracy; and he said distinctly that he could make no charge against the United States government, believing that the government had been misled, and that a feeble country could not enforce a demand against so strong a neighbor.

records.summary_en: The Tribune prints President Heureaux's words in interview: he spoke of the interpretation the State Department at Washington would give of the 'moral support' it had promised in the event of European Powers demanding the same privileges under the most-favored-nation clause, and of San Domingo's refusing compliance. 'I have always been,' he said, 'and am still desirous of favoring foreign investment in my country to the greatest extent possible. We are at a pass where we must continue to progress or we will recede as rapidly as Hayti is doing.' President Heureaux denied the reported wholesale shooting of the employes of Jimenez, asserting that the only two shot were those found with arms in their hands; Chuchu Mercado, a prisoner on the gunboat, was spared as an informer, and the younger Villanueva was spared because of the friendship of the Governor for his father.

records.headline: The Republican sums up the past week's reports of the San Domingo revolution:
records.summary_en: The Republican sums up the past week's reports of the San Domingo revolution: President Heureaux has been reported assassinated, and the report denied; however, the revolutionary attempt appears to have been unsuccessful, and its originators are now fugitives. The two principal leaders of the revolutionary attempt in the Dominican republic, J. I. Jiminez and General Agustin Morales, are well known in this country, particularly in New York city and Washington, says the New York Tribune; both of them have been conspicuous in their efforts in favor of the Cuban cause, which they rightly considered as intimately connected with that of the liberal party in their native country, San Domingo; while General Heureaux, president of that republic, ever evidenced strong pro-Spanish proclivities, for which he was rewarded with a decoration by the Madrid government.

records.headline: The Times prints a feature on Santiago de Cuba and its antiquity
records.summary_en: The Times prints a feature on Santiago de Cuba and its antiquity: as General Shafter's army approaches Santiago, citizens of the United States will take new interest in that ancient city, the oldest standing city in the new world, except Santo Domingo, which was established by Columbus four hundred years ago, Santiago itself having been founded only eighteen years after Santo Domingo. Santiago was the former capital and is the third city of commercial importance on the island of Cuba; it is the residential town of the archbishop and is the seat of several yearly religious festivals which are celebrated with pomp and ceremony; it is the terminus of two railroad lines, one of which is the outlet of Lomas de Cobre, the celebrated copper mines, situated several miles inland, and the second passes through the rich sugar country, affording transportation for that staple article of exportation; the exports from Santiago are said to reach the sum of $8,000,000 annually, tobacco, honey, rum, cocoa and mahogany being also exported in great quantities, and the city is inclosed on three sides by hills rising rapidly from the bay to mountains of great height and beauty.

Revolutionary agents were also reportedly active in southern Dominican provinces enlisting prominent figures. Additionally, Haitian officials, acting upon the Dominican government's request, ordered the son of rebel leader General Jimenes to leave Haiti.

records.headline: The Tribune prints part of its correspondent's account of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints part of its correspondent's account of President Heureaux at Cape Haytien: Heureaux entertained a good deal of suspicion of the Haytian authorities, which may not be entirely allayed, and the correspondent judges his ambition not unequal to an attempt to consolidate the whole island under his sway, if ever a fair excuse and a fairer opportunity offered, rating Hayti, though a little stronger in the armament of her gunboats and in the paper strength of her army, greatly inferior to Santo Domingo in the warlike qualities of her people, as also in their capacity for culture and industrial and commercial advancement. One of the notable traits of Heureaux's conversation while in the port of Cape Haytien the second time, last Thursday, the 9th, was his contempt, not the least bit concealed, for the Haytians; nevertheless, on this visit he ordered the regulation salute of twenty-one guns to be fired, and it was returned after the usual lazy fashion by the Haytians from the two or three small field-pieces of ancient type which constitute about the whole of the serviceable artillery there. Under the head 'Night Excursions in Disguise,' the account adds that Heureaux is a man of mystery and of mystification, as well as of promptitude and blood, and that after each of his departures from Cape Haytien it was reported he had been ashore in the evening in disguise, and thus, for purposes of his own, had made a tour of the city.

records.headline: A report on Dominican politics under President Heureaux describes Emmanuel Jimines as a young man of pleasing
records.summary_en: A report on Dominican politics under President Heureaux describes Emmanuel Jimines as a young man of pleasing manners who has much sympathy, but calls his Monte Cristi attempt one of the worst planned and feeblest ever known. It recounts how Heureaux employs a large number of spies, many of them women, yet is his own best spy, telling of him disguised as a laborer learning of a conspiracy, confronting conspirators in their own meeting, and pardoning a hired assassin who revealed who sent him, while thousands of dollars have secretly been offered for his assassination and the common people believe he leads a charmed life.
records.summary_es: Un reportaje sobre la política dominicana bajo el presidente Heureaux describe a Emmanuel Jimines como un joven de modales agradables que despierta mucha simpatía, pero califica su intento de Monte Cristi como uno de los peor planeados y más débiles que se hayan conocido. Relata cómo Heureaux emplea un gran número de espías, muchos de ellos mujeres, aunque él mismo es su mejor espía, y cuenta que disfrazado de obrero se enteró de una conspiración, que enfrentó a los conspiradores en su propia reunión y que perdonó a un asesino a sueldo que reveló quién lo había enviado, mientras se han ofrecido en secreto miles de dólares por su asesinato y el pueblo común cree que lleva una vida protegida por un encanto.

records.headline: The Star prints the Associated Press 'Pen Picture' of President Heureaux:
records.summary_en: The Star prints the Associated Press 'Pen Picture' of President Heureaux: its correspondent writes from Cape Haytien, Hayti, June 12, that the remarkable audiences President Heureaux granted on his gunboat, the Restauracion, in that harbor on Thursday last deserve a special record, and that the interview may be properly appreciated it is necessary to give it a descriptive setting. The correspondent went out to the Restauracion accompanied by the American consul, Dr. Livingston, and Mr. A. J. Redpar, who is in charge of the most successful foreign enterprise there and who met Heureaux some years ago in his own capital; they did not need to send their cards ahead, and were received on the quarter deck by Ulysses himself, the dreaded tyrant president, clad in a modest naval uniform, of which a short blue jacket with small gold buttons and a white cap with hardly any gold lace were the conspicuous features; he greeted them with a scrutinizing air, and with a gesture of bonhomie invited them to be seated. The president is a mulatto of medium color, with rather regular features, showing the blending of the African and Caucasian blood.
records.summary_es: El Star publica el «Pen Picture» de la Associated Press sobre el presidente Heureaux: su corresponsal escribe desde Cabo Haitiano, Haití, el 12 de junio, que las notables audiencias que el presidente Heureaux concedió en su cañonero, la Restauracion, en aquel puerto el jueves pasado merecen un registro especial, y que para que la entrevista pueda apreciarse debidamente es necesario darle un marco descriptivo. El corresponsal salió hacia la Restauracion acompañado por el cónsul americano, el Dr. Livingston, y el señor A. J. Redpar, quien está a cargo de la empresa extranjera más exitosa de allí y quien conoció a Heureaux hace algunos años en su propia capital; no necesitaron enviar sus tarjetas por adelantado, y fueron recibidos en el alcázar por Ulises mismo, el temido presidente tirano, vestido con un modesto uniforme naval, del cual una chaqueta azul corta con pequeños botones dorados y una gorra blanca casi sin galón dorado eran los rasgos conspicuos; los saludó con un aire escrutador, y con un gesto de bonhomía los invitó a sentarse. El presidente es un mulato de color medio, de facciones más bien regulares, que muestran la mezcla de la sangre africana y caucásica.

The president is about five feet eight inches in height, of athletic mold, though his right arm is still half disabled from the effects of two old wounds near the elbow; his movements are usually deliberate, as if all that he did in public was nicely calculated, yet he is capable of great animation, volubility and vivacity, spices his talk with satire and irony, and occasionally laughs broadly at his own joke or epigram, and it is impossible not to be impressed by the strong grasp of his mind and by the subtlety of his cunning. records.headline: The Star's pen picture of President Heureaux closes with the story of his brother-in-law:
records.summary_en: The Star's pen picture of President Heureaux closes with the story of his brother-in-law: it would matter very little to Heureaux, the correspondent writes, who of his own family interceded with him in favor of one of his enemies, and his conduct toward his own brother-in-law is still vividly remembered; he took the man to live with him in the presidential palace at Santo Domingo, clothed him, fed him and gave him official dignities, and twice the beneficiary conspired against the benefactor — the first time he was forgiven, but the second time Heureaux called him to him and said: 'I have tried to make a gentleman of you. Now I want you to put on your full-dress costume. In one hour you will be shot. There is no use for you to say anything. It must be. Only I particularly request that you behave like a gentleman' — and the brother-in-law was shot dead at the hour and minute. The prominent Haytiens who visited the president all hold offices related more or less to the administration of the port of Cape Haytien, and, with the exception of General Jules Pariden, whose wife is a cousin of Heureaux, they all presented veiled excuses or statements in exculpation of themselves in connection with the shipping of insurrectionists there when the Fanita departed for Monte Cristi, an implied acknowledgment of the comparative impotence of their own government and of the force and much-dreaded will power of the president of Santo Domingo.

The correspondent went out to the gunboat accompanied by the American Consul, Dr. Livingston, and Mr. A. J. Redpar, who is in charge of the most successful foreign enterprise there and who met Heureaux some years ago in his own capital; they did not need to send their cards ahead, and were received on the quarter deck by Ulises himself, the dreaded tyrant President, clad in a modest naval uniform, of which a short blue jacket with small gold buttons and a white cap with hardly any gold lace were the conspicuous features; he greeted them with a scrutinizing air and with a gesture of bonhomie invited them to be seated. The President is a mulatto of medium color, with rather regular features, showing the blending of the African type, a square Caesarian brow, strong, resolute lips, though with a chin slightly receding, a broad fleshy nose, and fine crinkly hair.

records.headline: The Herald's account gives Heureaux's views on Hayti and the United States:
records.summary_en: The Herald's account gives Heureaux's views on Hayti and the United States: the President spoke without reserve of the errors of the Haytien nation and denounced the unwisdom of their repellent attitude toward foreigners; he recognized the fact that the future progress of his own country lay in the encouragement of foreign enterprises within its borders, and, above all, he would be chary of provoking the ill will of the United States of America. Some day, he declared, all of the greater Antilles would either belong to him or be under the protectorate of the American republic, and there was but one sensible course for Santo Domingo or for Hayti — to cultivate the best political and commercial relations with the United States. On the subject of neutrality General Heureaux was somewhat ambiguous: he was indisposed, he said, to offend either Spain or the United States, the enmity of the former being as disastrous to his government as that of the latter, but he allowed it to be understood that, if it came to choice, he must decide to stand with the Americans. It was when the conversation turned to the late abortive uprising at Monte Cristo that the real opportunity to study the character of the dictator presented itself, and some of the Dominicans and prominent Haytiens who came aboard to pay homage to Heureaux had been hand in glove with the conspirators.
records.summary_es: El relato del Herald recoge las opiniones de Heureaux sobre Haití y los Estados Unidos: el presidente habló sin reserva de los errores de la nación haitiana y denunció la insensatez de su actitud repelente hacia los extranjeros; reconoció el hecho de que el progreso futuro de su propio país residía en el fomento de las empresas extranjeras dentro de sus fronteras, y, sobre todo, sería cauteloso en provocar la mala voluntad de los Estados Unidos de América. Algún día, declaró, todas las Antillas mayores o le pertenecerían a él o estarían bajo el protectorado de la república americana, y no había sino un camino sensato para Santo Domingo o para Haití: cultivar las mejores relaciones políticas y comerciales con los Estados Unidos. Sobre el tema de la neutralidad, el general Heureaux fue algo ambiguo: no estaba dispuesto, dijo, a ofender ni a España ni a los Estados Unidos, pudiendo la enemistad de la primera ser tan desastrosa para su gobierno como la de los segundos, pero dejó entender que, si llegaba a tener que escoger, debía decidirse a estar con los americanos. Fue cuando la conversación giró hacia el reciente alzamiento abortado en Monte Cristi que se presentó la verdadera oportunidad de estudiar el carácter del dictador, y algunos de los dominicanos y prominentes haitianos que subieron a bordo a rendir homenaje a Heureaux habían estado en íntima connivencia con los conspiradores.

records.headline: The Star prints the feature on the Columbus remains at Santo Domingo:
records.summary_en: The Star prints the feature on the Columbus remains at Santo Domingo: the news of the discovery sent those of San Domingo into spasms of delight and those of Spain into corresponding rage, and when the news reached Madrid the Royal Academy instituted a searching inquiry, which resulted in sustaining the Havana theory, but the learned men of San Domingo are still firm in their belief that they have the only and original bones — the true and authenticated remains of the immortal Columbus. The writer was sent to San Domingo for the express purpose of sifting the existing evidence and making a personal examination, and bore letters of recommendation from the then Secretary of State, Mr. Blaine, to the president of the Dominican republic, and every opportunity was afforded him for a rigid investigation: the minister of public affairs himself accompanied him to the cathedral, and by his command the revered relics were brought from their place of deposit, in an ancient cedar chest within a dark cell near the presbytery, and exposed to the light of day. Photographs were then taken of the vault, the original place of sepulture being pointed out, the two vaults opened and their relative position shown, and also of the casket at present holding the bones, and of the crystal and satinwood case in which this is contained; this last is bound about with ribbons, secured by the great seal of the republic, and to obtain even a glimpse of the remains it is first necessary to get the sanction of the ecclesiastical, the municipal and the national authorities.
records.summary_es: El Star publica el reportaje sobre los restos de Colón en Santo Domingo: la noticia del descubrimiento envió a los de Santo Domingo a espasmos de deleite y a los de España a una rabia correspondiente, y cuando la noticia llegó a Madrid la Real Academia instituyó una indagación escudriñadora, que resultó en sostener la teoría habanera, pero los sabios de Santo Domingo se mantienen firmes en su creencia de que tienen los únicos y originales huesos: los verdaderos y autenticados restos del inmortal Colón. El escritor fue enviado a Santo Domingo con el propósito expreso de escudriñar la evidencia existente y hacer un examen personal, y llevaba cartas de recomendación del entonces secretario de Estado, el señor Blaine, al presidente de la República Dominicana, y se le brindó toda oportunidad para una investigación rigurosa: el ministro de fomento, o de asuntos públicos, lo acompañó él mismo a la catedral, y por su orden las veneradas reliquias fueron traídas de su lugar de depósito, en un antiguo cofre de cedro dentro de una celda oscura cerca del presbiterio, y expuestas a la luz del día. Se tomaron entonces fotografías de la bóveda, señalándose el lugar original de sepultura, abiertas las dos bóvedas y mostrada su posición relativa, y también del ataúd que actualmente contiene los huesos, y de la caja de cristal y madera de satín en que este está contenido; esta última está ceñida con cintas, aseguradas por el gran sello de la república, y para obtener siquiera una mirada a los restos es primero necesario conseguir la sanción de las autoridades eclesiástica, municipal y nacional.

records.headline: The News prints the feature on the Columbus remains at Santo Domingo:
records.summary_en: The News prints the feature on the Columbus remains at Santo Domingo: the news of the discovery sent those of San Domingo into spasms of delight and those of Spain into corresponding rage, and when the news reached Madrid the Royal Academy instituted a searching inquiry, which resulted in sustaining the Havana theory, but the learned men of San Domingo are still firm in their belief that they have the only and original bones — the true and authenticated remains of the immortal Columbus. The writer was sent to San Domingo for the express purpose of sifting the existing evidence and making a personal examination, and bore letters of recommendation from the then Secretary of State, Mr. Blaine, to the president of the Dominican republic, and every opportunity was afforded him for a rigid investigation: the minister of public affairs himself accompanied him to the cathedral, and by his command the revered relics were brought from their place of deposit, in an ancient cedar chest within a dark cell near the presbytery, and exposed to the light of day. Photographs were then taken of the vault, the original place of sepulture being pointed out, the two vaults opened and their relative position shown, and also of the casket at present holding the bones, and of the crystal and satinwood case in which this is contained; this last is bound about with ribbons, secured by the great seal of the republic, and to obtain even a glimpse of the remains it is first necessary to get the sanction of the ecclesiastical, the municipal and the national authorities, the three keys to the cell in which they are guarded.
records.summary_es: El News publica el reportaje sobre los restos de Colón en Santo Domingo: la noticia del descubrimiento envió a los de Santo Domingo a espasmos de deleite y a los de España a una rabia correspondiente, y cuando la noticia llegó a Madrid la Real Academia instituyó una indagación escudriñadora, que resultó en sostener la teoría habanera, pero los sabios de Santo Domingo se mantienen firmes en su creencia de que tienen los únicos y originales huesos: los verdaderos y autenticados restos del inmortal Colón. El escritor fue enviado a Santo Domingo con el propósito expreso de escudriñar la evidencia existente y hacer un examen personal, y llevaba cartas de recomendación del entonces secretario de Estado, el señor Blaine, al presidente de la República Dominicana, y se le brindó toda oportunidad para una investigación rigurosa: el ministro de fomento, o de asuntos públicos, lo acompañó él mismo a la catedral, y por su orden las veneradas reliquias fueron traídas de su lugar de depósito, en un antiguo cofre de cedro dentro de una celda oscura cerca del presbiterio, y expuestas a la luz del día. Se tomaron entonces fotografías de la bóveda, señalándose el lugar original de sepultura, abiertas las dos bóvedas y mostrada su posición relativa, y también del ataúd que actualmente contiene los huesos, y de la caja de cristal y madera de satín en que este está contenido; esta última está ceñida con cintas, aseguradas por el gran sello de la república, y para obtener siquiera una mirada a los restos es primero necesario conseguir la sanción de las autoridades eclesiástica, municipal y nacional, las tres llaves de la celda en que están guardados.

records.headline: The Sun prints the Puerto Rican Correo's English editorial on San Domingo:
records.summary_en: The Sun prints the Puerto Rican Correo's English editorial on San Domingo: its editor takes strong ground for a free San Domingo, and 'The time is changed,' the editorial begins; not long ago the Spanish authorities did not allow them there the expression of their thoughts, and they were called to court to answer for their attacks on the murderer who commands in Santo Domingo, and a little after, in a moment of indignation in the Spanish government against the Antillean satrap, they could at least utter their complaints; now liberty commands in Puerto Rico, and the editorial makes one of its first English articles under the new state of affairs in that island a warm calling for help to withdraw the murderer who stains the Dominican Republic's humble but bright history. Cuba will be free and happy after her four centuries of shadows, Puerto Rico, if not independent, will no doubt be soon a prosperous people, and the Dominican Republic, the heroic and beautiful sister of Cuba and Puerto Rico, will only remain, the editorial cries, under the feet of a ferocious and savage tyrant.

records.headline: The Leader prints a feature on the Columbus remains and Ober's report:
records.summary_en: The Leader prints a feature on the Columbus remains and Ober's report: the honor of possessing these relics is claimed alike by Havana and San Domingo, and there seems to be no doubt that at each place there is the tomb of a Columbus, but which is the original and only genuine is a matter subject to argument. Some years ago Frederick A. Ober was sent to San Domingo for the express purpose of sifting the existing evidence and making a personal examination, and bore letters of recommendation from the then secretary of state, Mr. Blaine, to the president of the Dominican republic, and every opportunity was afforded him for a rigid investigation: the minister of public affairs himself accompanied him to the cathedral, and by his command the revered relics were brought from their place of deposit, in an ancient cedar chest within a dark cell near the presbytery, and exposed to the light of day. Photographs were then taken of the vault, the original place of sepulture being pointed out, the two vaults opened and their relative position shown, and also of the casket at present holding the bones, and of the crystal and satinwood case in which this is contained. In his report to this government, Mr. Ober said in substance that the conclusion reached by the Spanish academy is that the remains of Columbus are in the cathedral of Havana, in the shadow of the glorious banner of Castile, and that it is most fitting that over his sepulcher waves the same flag that sailed with him from Palos.

records.headline: The News, commenting on the finances of San Domingo, reports
records.summary_en: The News, commenting on the finances of San Domingo, reports the denial of the report that they are in so bad a way that bankruptcy is threatened: the authority for the denial is the president of the New York syndicate that collects and disburses the revenue of San Domingo — that is, the customs receipts, for, it is said, San Domingo has no other taxes of any nature, and survives and thrives on customs. Incidentally, interest is aroused in San Domingo's financial machinery by the revenues being collected at its ports and handled in New York; from all accounts, the policy of the San Domingo government of hiring expert New York financiers to run its money affairs works well, and might be imitated with advantage by other nations, though there is probably something in it too for the syndicate, especially as its agent doubtless has the first hand on the revenues.
records.summary_es: El News, comentando las finanzas de Santo Domingo, reporta la negación del reporte de que están en tan mal estado que la bancarrota amenaza: la autoridad para la negación es el presidente del sindicato de Nueva York que cobra y desembolsa las rentas de Santo Domingo — es decir, los ingresos de aduanas, pues, según se dice, Santo Domingo no tiene otros impuestos de ninguna naturaleza, y sobrevive y prospera con las aduanas. Incidentalmente, el interés se despierta en la maquinaria financiera de Santo Domingo por el hecho de que las rentas se cobran en sus puertos y se manejan en Nueva York; según todos los informes, la política del gobierno de Santo Domingo de contratar financieros expertos de Nueva York para manejar sus asuntos de dinero funciona bien, y podría ser imitada con ventaja por otras naciones, aunque probablemente hay también algo en ello para el sindicato, especialmente porque su agente tiene sin duda la primera mano en las rentas.

records.headline: The Journal prints a list of the capitals of the autonomous governments of the world
records.summary_en: The Journal prints a list of the capitals of the autonomous governments of the world, with their populations: Port au Prince, Hayti, is given at 33,000, and Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic, at 20,000. This list, the paper says, is believed to include every autonomous government in the world, but there are a number in doubt, like Nepal, in India, and Monaco, which are said to be independent principalities; there are no doubt still other obscure governments in the interior of Asia which are independent, but there are no statistics of any reliability concerning such; and a number of capitals, like Calcutta, Budapest, Havana and Manila, are not technically capitals of autonomous governments, but are the seats of the governments which administer affairs for those peoples.
records.summary_es: El Journal publica una lista de las capitales de los gobiernos autónomos del mundo, con sus poblaciones: Puerto Príncipe, Haití, figura con 33,000, y Santo Domingo, capital de la República Dominicana, con 20,000. records.headline: A section of the President's message reports that a claim of an American citizen against the Dominican Republic for a public bridge
records.summary_en: A section of the President's message reports that a claim of an American citizen against the Dominican Republic for a public bridge over the Ozama river, long in diplomatic controversy, has been settled by expert arbitration. The award, amounting to about $130,000, was in favor of the claimant, but it remains unpaid despite urgent demands for its settlement under the terms of the compact.

El laudo, que asciende a unos 130.000 dólares, fue a favor del reclamante, pero permanece sin pagar a pesar de las urgentes demandas de su liquidación según los términos del acuerdo.

records.headline: The News reports that President Ulysses Heureaux has been assassinated
records.summary_en: The News reports that President Ulysses Heureaux has been assassinated while attending a christening incognito, and gives a sketch of him: Gen. Ulysses Heureaux has been president of the republic of San Domingo for about ten years; he is a Haytian, about 58 years of age, and a fine type physically of the West Indian negro; while in office he has become immensely wealthy, and has several manufacturing monopolies, notably that of soap, the importation of which is practically impossible; several insurrections have taken place with the idea of overthrowing President Heureaux, but he has succeeded in putting them all down, shooting the leaders very often without trial; and in the early part of June last it was also reported that Gen. Heureaux had been assassinated during a revolution in San Domingo.
records.summary_es: El News reporta que el presidente Ulysses Heureaux ha sido asesinado mientras asistía de incógnito a un bautizo, y ofrece un esbozo de él: el general Ulysses Heureaux ha sido presidente de la república de Santo Domingo por unos diez años; es haitiano, de unos 58 años de edad, y un fino tipo físico del negro antillano; en el cargo se ha hecho inmensamente rico, y tiene varios monopolios de manufactura, notablemente el del jabón, cuya importación es prácticamente imposible; han tenido lugar varias insurrecciones con la idea de derrocar al presidente Heureaux, pero él ha logrado sofocarlas todas, fusilando a los líderes muy a menudo sin juicio; y a principios de junio pasado también se reportó que el general Heureaux había sido asesinado durante una revolución en Santo Domingo.

records.headline: The Tribune prints part of an editorial on the report of President Heureaux's assassination:
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints part of an editorial on the report of President Heureaux's assassination: it recalls the president of Uruguay, who was murdered at a public ceremony, and, as to the incognito, General Heureaux has been admitted by his most bitter enemies to be a daring man, going everywhere without an escort, even after he had caused the execution of some of his adversaries; still, he must have sown many seeds of vengeance, and if he is ever assassinated it will be as the result of a personal hatred and not of politics. The people of San Domingo seem to be resigned to the dictatorship of President Heureaux, as shown in the latest revolutionary landing last June at Monte Cristi, where the unfortunate General Morales did not meet a single man of all those who had promised to support him on landing; he was killed, with the twelve men who landed with him, but M. Isidro Jimenes, the merchant banker and aspirer to the Presidency in his country, succeeded in saving his own life by pulling out from the shore, where his friends were slaughtered; he is now in exile at Paris, but, naturally, he must follow the course of events in San Domingo, inasmuch as he has one of his mercantile houses at Cape Haytien, whence the false report was received. There were recently some financial difficulties in the Dominican Republic, but they were reported as having been satisfactorily settled at a conference held between General Heureaux and the president of an American company largely interested in the industrial and commercial development of San Domingo.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica parte de un editorial sobre el reporte del asesinato del presidente Heureaux: recuerda al presidente del Uruguay, que fue asesinado en una ceremonia pública, y, en cuanto al incógnito, el general Heureaux ha sido admitido por sus enemigos más encarnizados como un hombre audaz, que va a todas partes sin escolta, aun después de haber causado la ejecución de algunos de sus adversarios; aun así, debe haber sembrado muchas semillas de venganza, y si alguna vez es asesinado será como resultado de un odio personal y no de la política. El pueblo de Santo Domingo parece estar resignado a la dictadura del presidente Heureaux, como se mostró en el último desembarco revolucionario en junio pasado en Monte Cristi, donde el desafortunado general Morales no encontró ni un solo hombre de todos los que habían prometido apoyarlo al desembarcar; fue muerto, con los doce hombres que desembarcaron con él, pero el señor Isidro Jimenes, el comerciante banquero y aspirante a la Presidencia en su país, logró salvar su propia vida alejándose de la orilla, donde sus amigos fueron masacrados; ahora está exiliado en París, pero, naturalmente, debe seguir el curso de los eventos en Santo Domingo, ya que tiene una de sus casas mercantiles en Cabo Haitiano, de donde se recibió el reporte falso. Recientemente hubo algunas dificultades financieras en la República Dominicana, pero se reportó que habían sido satisfactoriamente arregladas en una conferencia celebrada entre el general Heureaux y el presidente de una compañía americana ampliamente interesada en el desarrollo industrial y comercial de Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The Star reports a bill in equity filed today by Ogden P. Pell, who seeks an accounting and to have a lien declared: the Secretary of State of the United States of America and others are named defendants. Mr. Pell sets forth that in 1887 the city of Santo Domingo, in the Dominican Republic, granted Mr. McKay a concession to build a bridge across the Ozama river, agreeing to pay him a certain amount and allow him a certain proportion of the tolls; Mr. Pell claims that he advanced money to Mr. McKay and the bridge company, he to have a lien for his advances in the sum to be paid for compensation for the building of the bridge; he carried out his part of the contract, he says, but has not received in return what is due him. It is further represented that the republic of Santo Domingo has entered into an agreement with the United States under which the sum of $75,000 is to be paid, through the Secretary of State, to discharge all claims of Mr. McKay or his assigns in connection with the bridge; Mr. Pell asks that his claim be adjudicated as a lien in the fund of $75,000, and that all other persons be enjoined from collecting from it until his claim is paid; and Judge Cox, in Equity Court No. 1, issued a rule to show cause, returnable January 18, why Mr. Pell's prayers should not be granted.
records.summary_es: El Star reporta una demanda en equidad presentada hoy por Ogden P. Pell, quien busca una rendición de cuentas y que se declare un gravamen: el secretario de Estado de los Estados Unidos de América y otros son nombrados demandados. El señor Pell expone que en 1887 la ciudad de Santo Domingo, en la República Dominicana, concedió al señor McKay una concesión para construir un puente sobre el río Ozama, acordando pagarle cierta cantidad y permitirle cierta proporción de los peajes; el señor Pell alega que adelantó dinero al señor McKay y a la compañía del puente, habiendo de tener un gravamen por sus adelantos en la suma a pagarse como compensación por la construcción del puente; él cumplió su parte del contrato, dice, pero no ha recibido a cambio lo que se le debe. Se representa además que la república de Santo Domingo ha entrado en un acuerdo con los Estados Unidos bajo el cual la suma de $75,000 ha de pagarse, a través del secretario de Estado, para saldar todas las reclamaciones del señor McKay o sus cesionarios en conexión con el puente; el señor Pell pide que su reclamación sea adjudicada como un gravamen en el fondo de $75,000, y que a todas las demás personas se les prohíba cobrar de él hasta que su reclamación sea pagada; y el juez Cox, en la Corte de Equidad No. 1, emitió una orden de mostrar causa, retornable el 18 de enero, de por qué no deben concederse las peticiones del señor Pell.

records.summary_en: The *Anaconda Standard* published an overview of the Dominican Republic, detailing its geography, population of 610,000, and history from colonial rule through its independence on February 27, 1844. The report described the nation's political structure, public education system, and major agricultural exports, including tobacco, sugar, coffee, and mahogany. It also observed that while rich mineral deposits of gold, copper, and iron existed, the country's mineral resources remained largely undeveloped.
records.summary_es: *The Anaconda Standard* publicó una reseña general de la República Dominicana, detallando su geografía, una población de 610.000 habitantes y su historia desde la época colonial hasta su independencia el 27 de febrero de 1844. El informe describía la estructura política del país, el sistema de educación pública y sus principales exportaciones agrícolas, entre ellas tabaco, azúcar, café y caoba. Observó asimismo que, si bien existían ricos yacimientos minerales de oro, cobre y hierro, los recursos mineros del país permanecían en gran medida inexplotados.
records.passage: expand in the West Indies than in the East Indies. The island of Santo Domingo is the largest of the West Indies next to Cuba. There are two republics on the island, the republic of Dominica being the larger and comprising about two-thirds of the island, while the republic of Hayti occupies the western end of the island. The island was first settled by the Spanish and was called Hispaniola. Then French buccaneers gained a foothold on it. In 1697 the western part was ceded by Spain to France. In 1800 Toussaint Louverture seized the Spanish part of the island and also stirred up an insurrection in the French part. Through treachery he was enticed to France and died in jail. On February 27, 1844, the Spanish or eastern part of the island threw off allegiance to Spain and formed the republic of Dominica. The republic contains 18,045 square miles and has a population of 610,000. The president is elected for four years, chosen by universal suffrage. He is assisted by a congress of twenty-two deputies elected for two years by popular vote with restricted suffrage. The Spanish language is principally spoken. Education is free and obligatory. The schools are good. The products are mainly tobacco, sugar, rice, coffee, maize, cocoa, bananas, pine apples, sweet potatoes and cotton. Gold, silver, copper, coal, iron and tin exist on the island, but no efforts have been made to develop the mineral resources. Logwood and mahogany are among the principal exports. records.headline: Under the head 'Only Nine Heroes in Sight,' the Tribune prints
records.summary_en: Under the head 'Only Nine Heroes in Sight,' the Tribune prints Juan I. Jimenes's explanation of why his last revolution failed: Jimenes, who has desired for years to overthrow President Heureaux of the Dominican Republic, has issued an 'appeal to the Dominican people,' which, for fluency in the use of adjectives and power of vituperation, is hard to beat, and the translation into English, which he is distributing in this country, makes interesting, if not lucid, reading. Of his last attempt at a revolution, which ended in a fizzle, he writes: 'The proof of my determination was made evident on my landing in the harbor of Monte Cristi for the purpose of taking that city, with the nine men who accompanied me; upon seeing that my plan had failed, by which the city was to be surrendered to me by those expected to storm the place, in spite of this disappointment, I took the city and made its Governor my prisoner; but for the fact that the chief of the fortress managed to escape and give the alarm amongst the few soldiers asleep in the fortress, the latter would have fallen more easily, and the revolution would have continued its successful course; the uprisings that were to take place in other sections of the country did not occur, because of the instructions I had given to the effect that such uprisings must be carried out only after the city was in my possession, or not at all should I fail to take it.'
records.summary_es: Bajo el título «Only Nine Heroes in Sight», el Tribune publica la explicación de Juan I. Jimenes de por qué fracasó su última revolución: Jimenes, que ha deseado por años derrocar al presidente Heureaux de la República Dominicana, ha emitido un «llamado al pueblo dominicano», que, por fluidez en el uso de adjetivos y poder de vituperio, es difícil de superar, y la traducción al inglés, que él está distribuyendo en este país, hace una lectura interesante, si no lúcida. De su último intento de revolución, que terminó en un fiasco, escribe: «La prueba de mi determinación se hizo evidente en mi desembarco en el puerto de Monte Cristi con el propósito de tomar esa ciudad, con los nueve hombres que me acompañaron; al ver que mi plan había fracasado, por el cual la ciudad había de serme entregada por los que se esperaba asaltaran la plaza, a pesar de esta decepción, tomé la ciudad e hice prisionero a su Gobernador; si no hubiera sido porque el jefe de la fortaleza logró escapar y dar la alarma entre los pocos soldados dormidos en la fortaleza, esta habría caído más fácilmente, y la revolución habría continuado su curso exitoso; los levantamientos que habían de tener lugar en otras secciones del país no ocurrieron, por causa de las instrucciones que yo había dado al efecto de que tales levantamientos debían llevarse a cabo solo después de que la ciudad estuviera en mi posesión, o no hacerse en absoluto si yo fracasaba en tomarla».

records.headline: The Democrat prints a story accusing General Maximo Gomez of plotting
records.summary_en: The Democrat prints a story accusing General Maximo Gomez of plotting to overthrow the government of Santo Domingo: 'Having abandoned the hope of becoming the head of the Cuban republic and unwilling to emulate the example of those patriots who, in similar conditions, have thrust aside personal interest and retired to private life, Gomez is conferring with discontented Dominicans, among whom is General Bautista, who is now in Havana, with a view of organizing an expedition composed of former American and Cuban soldiers to attack Santo Domingo, kill President Heureaux and proclaim Gomez dictator. We are informed that Gomez, though an old man, is of infinitely more value than all the Dominican generals put together.' It is scarcely necessary to say, the Democrat adds, that this story is generally discredited.

Se nos informa que Gomez, aunque un hombre viejo, vale infinitamente más que todos los generales dominicanos juntos». Es casi innecesario decir, añade el Democrat, que esta historia es generalmente desacreditada.

The Dominican President, General Ulysses Heureaux, is also a worshipper of all memories and relics relative to the history of his country; he caused recently the building of a handsome mausoleum at Santo Domingo, where were deposited last December the alleged remains of Columbus — the real ones, according to the Dominicans, who say that it is only the ashes of Diego, the son of Columbus, which have been transported by the Spaniards to the Seville cathedral; and the newspapers of Santo Domingo and public opinion there approve the intention of the government to decline the request of Venezuela and to keep the ashes of Ojeda in the lands of Cibao and San Juan, his last abode on earth.

records.headline: Under the head 'Bullet Pierced Heureaux's Heart,' the News prints
records.summary_en: Under the head 'Bullet Pierced Heureaux's Heart,' the News prints details of the murder of President Heureaux of Santo Domingo, received at Cape Haytien, July 27: the president was assassinated as he was about to leave on horseback for Santiago de los Caballeros; the assassin, who was surrounded by several accomplices, approached the president as he was talking with some friends and fired twice with a revolver — the first bullet struck the president in the left side and penetrated the heart, causing instant death, and the second bullet killed an old man who was standing near. The assassin and his accomplices then fled to avoid the shots fired at them by the president's friends, and it is not known whether any of them were wounded; the body of the president was taken to the palace of the governor of Moca.

records.headline: The Argus closes its assassination dispatch with the remains of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Argus closes its assassination dispatch with the remains of President Heureaux to be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services, and, under the head 'Comments at Washington on the Event,' prints a Washington item of July 27: pending official notice of the assassination of President Heureaux of the Dominican republic, which has not been received at this writing, no formal action will be taken by this government; officials here recall that attempts have been made heretofore on the life of Heureaux, and Secretary Hay paid a brief tribute to the work of the deceased president, saying he understood that he had given the country a good administration; should the developments of the next few days show a feeling of unrest and uncertainty regarding the future affairs of the republic, a United States man-of-war will be dispatched to that vicinity to look out for the protection of American interests. Under the head 'Consul General Is Amazed,' the Argus prints a New York item of July 27: Señor Don Alejandro Woss y Gil, consul general of the Dominican republic, when seen at his home there last night, could scarcely credit the news of the assassination of his president, Señor Ulysses Heureaux: 'President Heureaux did wonders to make our people happy and give us prosperity. He was serving his second term, and in a year would have finished his labors as president. He was formerly minister of the interior, and also served as secretary of war. Moca is a town three days' ride by horse from Santo Domingo.'
records.summary_es: El Argus cierra su despacho del asesinato con los restos del presidente Heureaux a ser llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres, y, bajo el título «Comments at Washington on the Event», publica una nota de Washington del 27 de julio: pendiente el aviso oficial del asesinato del presidente Heureaux de la República Dominicana, que no se ha recibido al momento de escribir, no se tomará ninguna acción formal por este gobierno; los funcionarios aquí recuerdan que se han hecho antes intentos contra la vida de Heureaux, y el secretario Hay rindió un breve tributo a la obra del presidente fallecido, diciendo que entendía que él había dado al país una buena administración; si los acontecimientos de los próximos días muestran un sentimiento de inquietud e incertidumbre respecto a los asuntos futuros de la república, un buque de guerra de los Estados Unidos será despachado a esa vecindad para velar por la protección de los intereses americanos. Bajo el título «Consul General Is Amazed», el Argus publica una nota de Nueva York del 27 de julio: el señor don Alejandro Woss y Gil, cónsul general de la República Dominicana, al ser visitado en su casa allí anoche, apenas podía creer la noticia del asesinato de su presidente, el señor Ulysses Heureaux: «El presidente Heureaux hizo maravillas para hacer feliz a nuestro pueblo y darnos prosperidad. Estaba sirviendo su segundo período, y en un año habría terminado sus labores como presidente. Fue antes ministro del interior, y también sirvió como secretario de guerra. Moca es un pueblo a tres días de camino a caballo desde Santo Domingo».

Heureaux first saw the light of day in Puerto Plata in 1845; a soldier's life attracted him, and in 1862 he became a private, later becoming commandant in the District of Puerto Plata; he served continuously in the war against Spain, was twice exiled for political reasons, retired for two years from political life, and in 1878 again assumed command to put down a Spanish uprising; he was wounded many times.

records.headline: The Scranton Tribune completes the Fort de France dispatch of July 27
records.summary_en: The Scranton Tribune completes the Fort de France dispatch of July 27 and prints the news at Washington: General Ulysses Heureaux, president of the Dominican republic, was assassinated at Moca, San Domingo, at half past four o'clock this afternoon; the name of the murderer is Ramon Casceros; he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic pursuit was at once begun and it is probable that he will soon be captured; Vice-President General Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the president's death, assumed the direction of affairs; at present calmness prevails in the republic; and the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to San Domingo for the funeral services. The Washington item, of July 26, says no information was received up to a late hour tonight from the consular representatives of the United States in Santo Domingo regarding the assassination of President Heureaux, and that, pending official advices of the assassination, no formal action will be taken by this government: Hon. William F. Powell, the minister to Hayti, is also chargé d'affaires to Santo Domingo, while this government is directly represented in the republic in the person of Campbell L. Maxwell, who is consul general, and John A. Read, who is vice consul; officials here recall that attempts have been made heretofore on the life of Mr. Heureaux; and Secretary Hay paid a brief tribute to the work of the deceased president, saying he understood that he had given the country a good administration.

records.headline: The News completes its assassination dispatch and prints a sketch of Heureaux's career:
records.summary_en: The News completes its assassination dispatch and prints a sketch of Heureaux's career: Vice President Gen. Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the president's death, assumed the direction of affairs; at present calmness prevails everywhere in the republic; and the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services. Gen. Ulysses Heureaux was born in 1838, when San Domingo was a Spanish colony, the republic not being established until 1845; he lived to fight for his country's independence, being one of the bravest leaders in the insurrection which ended the brief Spanish occupation during the civil war; he was first elected president in 1882, taking his seat in 1883, and was re-elected in 1884, 1888, 1892 and 1896, his first term being the unexpired term of his predecessor; he was a brave and determined man, and whenever there was a disturbance in his country he always proceeded to the scene in person, as a soldier, not as president of the country; during his lifetime he passed through many battles and escaped several attempts at assassination — no longer ago than May of last year he outwitted a band of revolutionists headed by Gen. Jiminez, and though another attempt was made to overturn the government by the hand of an assassin, he escaped unharmed; he was a man of medium height, a mulatto, and weighed about 170 pounds, and he spoke English fluently.
records.summary_es: El News completa su despacho del asesinato y publica un esbozo de la carrera de Heureaux: el vicepresidente general Wenceslao Figuereo, inmediatamente después del anuncio de la muerte del presidente, asumió la dirección de los asuntos; al presente prevalece la calma en todas partes en la república; y los restos del presidente Heureaux serán probablemente llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres. El general Ulysses Heureaux nació en 1838, cuando Santo Domingo era una colonia española, no habiéndose establecido la república hasta 1845; vivió para luchar por la independencia de su país, siendo uno de los líderes más bravos en la insurrección que terminó la breve ocupación española durante la guerra civil; fue elegido presidente por primera vez en 1882, tomando su asiento en 1883, y fue reelegido en 1884, 1888, 1892 y 1896, siendo su primer período el período no expirado de su predecesor; era un hombre bravo y determinado, y siempre que había un disturbio en su país procedía siempre a la escena en persona, como soldado, no como presidente del país; durante su vida pasó por muchas batallas y escapó de varios intentos de asesinato — no hace más que mayo del año pasado en que burló a una banda de revolucionarios encabezada por el general Jiminez, y aunque se hizo otro intento de derrocar el gobierno por la mano de un asesino, escapó ileso; era un hombre de estatura mediana, un mulato, y pesaba unas 170 libras, y hablaba inglés fluidamente.

Maxwell, who is consul general, and John A. Read, who is vice-consul; officials here recall that attempts have been made heretofore on the life of Mr. Heureaux; Secretary Hay paid a brief tribute to the work of the deceased president, saying he understood that he had given the country a good administration; and Secretary Long said he could not recall that there were any ships of the United States navy now in Santo Domingo waters, and that, should the developments of the next few days show a feeling of unrest and uncertainty regarding the future affairs of the republic, a United States man-of-war will be dispatched to that vicinity to look out for the protection of American interests. The New York item says Señor Don Alejandro Woss y Gil, consul general of the Dominican republic, said last night that he had not been notified of the assassination of President Ulysses Heureaux and thought the report incredible: 'The meagre details given argue that it is improbable. The village of Moca is three days by horse from San Domingo and there is no railroad. President Heureaux would not be in such a place, I am sure. On Monday he sent me a cipher message by cable. No, I feel the story is not true. If it be true, then is our country sorely afflicted. President Heureaux did wonders to make our people happy and give us prosperity'; he was serving his second term, the consul general added, and in a year would have finished his labors.

records.headline: Under the head 'Full Details of the Crime,' the Star prints
records.summary_en: Under the head 'Full Details of the Crime,' the Star prints a Cape Haytien dispatch of July 27 with details of the murder of President Heureaux of Santo Domingo, received there: a financial crisis having arisen in Santo Domingo, and an insurrection being feared owing to the number of malcontents, President Heureaux went to the north and west of the island to prepare for all eventualities; he was assassinated as he was about to leave Moca on horseback for Santiago de las Caballeros — booted and spurred, ready to mount his horse, he sat under the gallery of a house in the Rue Colon, talking with two friends, at 4:30 in the afternoon, when an old man approached to ask for alms, and just as the president gave the old man some money, Caceres, the assassin, rushed forward quickly and fired twice from his revolver: one bullet struck the heart of the president, killing him instantly, and the other killed the old man by his side. The crime was committed so rapidly that the friends of the president were not able to interfere in time to prevent it, but they fired a number of shots at Caceres, who ran away, accompanied by several persons; the assassin's party returned the fire of the president's friends, and Caceres escaped, and it is not known whether he was wounded or not.
records.summary_es: Bajo el título «Full Details of the Crime», el Star publica un despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 27 de julio con detalles del asesinato del presidente Heureaux de Santo Domingo, recibidos allí: habiendo surgido una crisis financiera en Santo Domingo, y temiéndose una insurrección debido al número de descontentos, el presidente Heureaux fue al norte y al oeste de la isla para prepararse para todas las eventualidades; fue asesinado cuando estaba a punto de partir de Moca a caballo para Santiago de los Caballeros — con botas y espuelas, listo para montar su caballo, estaba sentado bajo la galería de una casa en la Rue Colon, hablando con dos amigos, a las 4:30 de la tarde, cuando un anciano se acercó a pedir limosna, y justo cuando el presidente le dio al anciano algún dinero, Caceres, el asesino, se abalanzó rápidamente y disparó dos veces con su revólver: una bala alcanzó el corazón del presidente, matándolo instantáneamente, y la otra mató al anciano a su lado. El crimen se cometió tan rápidamente que los amigos del presidente no pudieron intervenir a tiempo para impedirlo, pero dispararon un número de tiros a Caceres, que huyó, acompañado por varias personas; el partido del asesino devolvió el fuego de los amigos del presidente, y Caceres escapó, y no se sabe si fue herido o no.

records.headline: The Star prints the text of President McKinley's message of condolence:
records.summary_en: The Star prints the text of President McKinley's message of condolence: 'In the name of the American people and my own, I offer to your excellency and the Dominican nation most sincere condolences by reason of the death of President Heureaux. (Signed) William McKinley.' With the message the Star prints the Washington item and the opening of a sketch of the dead president's career: Mr. William F. Powell, the minister to Hayti, is also chargé d'affaires to Santo Domingo, while this government is directly represented in the republic in the person of Campbell L. Maxwell, who is consul general, and John A. Read, who is vice consul; officials here recall that attempts have been made heretofore on the life of Mr. Heureaux; Secretary Hay paid a brief tribute to the work of the deceased president, saying he understood that he had given the country a good administration; and Secretary Long said that there were no ships of the United States navy now in Santo Domingo waters, and that, should the developments of the next few days show a feeling of unrest and uncertainty regarding the future affairs of the republic, a United States man-of-war will be dispatched to that vicinity to look out for the protection of American interests. Heureaux has been called the Napoleon of the south: he was born at Puerto Plata, a town on the north coast of Santo Domingo, in 1846; he became a private soldier in 1862, volunteering in the native service in the uprising against the Spaniards; when the Spaniards left the island, Heureaux had risen to the rank of colonel; and he was a leader in the various attempts to drive from power Buenaventura Baez, who in 1867 usurped absolute power.

(Firmado) William McKinley». Con el mensaje, el Star publica la nota de Washington y la apertura de un esbozo de la carrera del presidente muerto: el señor William F.
