records.headline: The Journal prints the McKinley cable of condolence and Erwin York's statement
records.summary_en: The Journal prints the McKinley cable of condolence and Erwin York's statement on protection for American debtors: by direction of President McKinley, who is now at Lake Champlain, the following message was sent in his name to Vice-President Wenaslao de Figuereo, who has assumed the reins of government in Santo Domingo: 'In the name of the American people, and in my own, I offer to your excellency and the Dominican nation most sincere condolences by reason of the death of President Heureaux.' Under the head 'American Debtors Will Insist on Protection,' Erwin York, secretary of the Santo Domingo Improvement Company, which controls the country's finances, said yesterday: 'Should the new administration attempt to repudiate our contracts we shall certainly, as American citizens, call upon the Washington administration for protection. I do not believe there will be any revolution.' The contract with the improvement company was signed by President Heureaux in 1863; it gives to the company the railroads and the right to collect the customs, and in return for these concessions the company has assumed the national debt of the country, which is principally held in the United States; and this fact alone, the Journal adds, has generally been considered sufficient for the interference of a power in the affairs of another country when conditions become disturbed.

Bajo el título «American Debtors Will Insist on Protection», Erwin York, secretario de la Santo Domingo Improvement Company, que controla las finanzas del país, dijo ayer: «Si la nueva administración intentara repudiar nuestros contratos ciertamente, como ciudadanos americanos, llamaremos a la administración de Washington para protección. No creo que habrá ninguna revolución». El contrato con la compañía de mejoras fue firmado por el presidente Heureaux en 1863; da a la compañía los ferrocarriles y el derecho de cobrar las aduanas, y en retorno por esas concesiones la compañía ha asumido la deuda nacional del país, que es principalmente poseída en los Estados Unidos; y este hecho solo, añade el Journal, ha sido generalmente considerado suficiente para la interferencia de una potencia en los asuntos de otro país cuando las condiciones se perturban.

records.headline: The Journal prints General Moscoso's account of Heureaux's rule
records.summary_en: The Journal prints General Moscoso's account of Heureaux's rule and a Puerto Plata dispatch on the assassin's revenge: speaking of General Heureaux, General Moscoso said the assassination ought not to be unexpected by those who have followed the political history of the island; the president of San Domingo was assassinated by the son of a prominent statesman who was himself assassinated in very much the same manner; the assassin had evidently cherished the memory of his father's death, and there was much of revenge in his act; General Heureaux has ruled San Domingo with an iron hand, has killed more than a thousand persons who were opposed to him politically, and put many others in jail; and he drove out more than four hundred prominent persons who were opposed to him from the country, twenty of them now in this country like himself, seventy-five in Cuba, a hundred in Venezuela, and seventy-five in Puerto Rico. Under the head 'President Heureaux Shot for Revenge,' the Puerto Plata dispatch says President Heureaux was killed by the son of a man whom the president had put to death in 1884: the son, Ramon Caceres, vowed revenge for the execution of his father, who was merely suspected of joining in a rebel plot, and has never lost an opportunity to foment insurrection. During the past few weeks there has been much discontent, owing to the financial crisis, and a revolution was feared.

records.headline: The Journal completes its assassination account: the pursuit
records.summary_en: The Journal completes its assassination account: the pursuit, the conveyance of the body, and the burial decision at Santiago. Pursuit was hurriedly sent after Caceres, but he had a good start and has so far escaped capture; President Heureaux's body was taken to the house of the governor of Moca, and this morning it was conveyed to Santiago de las Caballeros; the president's widow requested that the remains be brought to Puerto Plata by train, and then conveyed to Santo Domingo, the capital, by sea; as soon as the news of the assassination reached the capital, Vice-President Figuereo assumed the presidential functions and issued strict orders to suppress the rebellion that is rapidly fomenting, and disorder is feared in many sections; the new president declined to accede to the request of the widow and notified her that the body of her husband will be interred at Santiago under direction of the governor of that town, a course decided upon in order to avoid the excitement and manifestations that would result from the removal of the body to the capital. Meantime the situation in the country is critical: enemies of the government are trying to disturb the peace; it is reported that the assassin's party are gathering forces preparatory to an attack upon the government troops; and General Pepin, governor of Santiago, says the murder was the result of a political conspiracy, with Caceres, who had a personal desire for revenge, as the assassin, and has asked the government to send him more arms and ammunition.
records.summary_es: El Journal completa su relato del asesinato: la persecución, el traslado del cuerpo, y la decisión del entierro en Santiago. La persecución fue enviada apresuradamente tras Caceres, pero él tenía una buena ventaja y hasta ahora ha escapado de la captura; el cuerpo del presidente Heureaux fue llevado a la casa del gobernador de Moca, y esta mañana fue trasladado a Santiago de los Caballeros; la viuda del presidente solicitó que los restos fueran traídos a Puerto Plata por tren, y luego trasladados a Santo Domingo, la capital, por mar; tan pronto como la noticia del asesinato llegó a la capital, el vicepresidente Figuereo asumió las funciones presidenciales y emitió órdenes estrictas de suprimir la rebelión que se está fomentando rápidamente, y se teme desorden en muchas secciones; el nuevo presidente declinó acceder a la solicitud de la viuda y le notificó que el cuerpo de su esposo será enterrado en Santiago bajo la dirección del gobernador de esa ciudad, un curso decidido para evitar la excitación y las manifestaciones que resultarían del traslado del cuerpo a la capital. Mientras tanto la situación en el país es crítica: enemigos del gobierno están tratando de perturbar la paz; se reporta que el partido del asesino está reuniendo fuerzas en preparación de un ataque a las tropas del gobierno; y el general Pepin, gobernador de Santiago, dice que el asesinato fue el resultado de una conspiración política, con Caceres, que tenía un deseo personal de venganza, como el asesino, y ha pedido al gobierno que le envíe más armas y municiones.

records.headline: Details of Heureaux's assassination at Moca: Ramón Cáceres, whose father Heureaux had put to death in 1884, shot the president
records.summary_en: Details of Heureaux's assassination at Moca: Ramón Cáceres, whose father Heureaux had put to death in 1884, shot the president as he mounted for Santiago; Figuereo succeeds; President McKinley's condolence cable to the Dominican nation.
records.summary_es: Detalles del asesinato de Heureaux en Moca: Ramón Cáceres, cuyo padre fue ejecutado por orden de Heureaux en 1884, disparó contra el presidente cuando montaba para ir a Santiago; Figuereo lo sucede; el cable de condolencia del presidente McKinley a la nación dominicana.
records.passage: ed by several accomplices, approached the President as he was talking with some friends and fired twice with a revolver. The first bullet struck the President in the left side and penetrated the heart, causing instant death. The second bullet killed an old man who was standing near the President. ASSASSIN FLED. The assassin and his accomplices then fled to avoid the shots fired at them by the President's friends. It is not known whether any of the men were wounded. The body of the President was taken to the Palace of the Governor of Moca. President Heureaux's death has caused a panic. It is said that one Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection in June, 1898, is candidate for President. It is reported that General Maximo Gomez, former President of the Cuban insurrectionists, who is a native of Santo Domingo, also aspires to the Presidency. The father of Caceres, the assassin, was put to death by order of President Heureaux in 1884. FIRED AT THEM. The crime was committed so rapidly that the friends of the President were not able to interfere in time to prevent it, but they fired a number of shots at Caceres, who ran away accompanied by several persons. The assassin's party returned the fire of the President's party and Caceres escaped. It is not known whether he was wounded or not. The authorities immediately sent troops to pursue him. The Governor of Santiago confirms the general opinion that the assassination of the President was a political crime.

records.headline: The Dispatch prints an editorial squib on the president's name
records.summary_en: The Dispatch prints an editorial squib on the president's name: Heureux means 'happy' in French, it says, yet the lot of the recently assassinated Heureux was not a happy one, though he accumulated much wealth and wielded some power while he was president of the Dominican republic; the Dominicans twisted his 'Heureux' into 'Heureaux,' and to this distortion of what should mean 'happy' is due, the paper suggests, the unhappiness of his career and his end, an explanation the French at least would accept, in view of the suggested violence done to their beautiful language. The squib is headed 'What's in a Name?'.
records.summary_es: El Dispatch publica una nota editorial sobre el nombre del presidente: Heureux significa «feliz» en francés, dice, sin embargo la suerte del recientemente asesinado Heureux no fue una feliz, aunque acumuló mucha riqueza y ejerció algún poder mientras fue presidente de la República Dominicana; los dominicanos torcieron su «Heureux» en «Heureaux», y a esta distorsión de lo que debería significar «feliz» se debe, sugiere el periódico, la infelicidad de su carrera y su fin, una explicación que los franceses al menos aceptarían, en vista de la violencia sugerida hecha a su hermoso idioma. La nota se titula «What's in a Name?».

records.headline: The Spy prints an editorial comment on the report of Heureaux's death
records.summary_en: The Spy prints an editorial comment on the report of Heureaux's death and the caution it was received with: President Heureaux of the Dominican republic has been captured by rebels and put to death more than once, only to return to life after his hidden enemies had exposed themselves and brought about their ruin, and therefore the report of his death was to be received with caution and even incredulity; a man who has been through several revolutions, helped drive the Spaniards from the island, and carried the scars of many wounds, not to mention two unextracted bullets in his body, can have no great fear of death; and Heureaux has ruled despotically and not without cruelty, but on the whole, the paper says, the black republic has been the gainer thereby, for it was a case of dog eat dog whoever held the reins of government.
records.summary_es: El Spy publica un comentario editorial sobre el reporte de la muerte de Heureaux y la cautela con que fue recibido: el presidente Heureaux de la República Dominicana ha sido capturado por rebeldes y ejecutado más de una vez, solo para volver a la vida después de que sus enemigos ocultos se habían expuesto ellos mismos y acarreado su ruina, y por tanto el reporte de su muerte debía ser recibido con cautela y hasta incredulidad; un hombre que ha pasado por varias revoluciones, ayudó a expulsar a los españoles de la isla, y llevó las cicatrices de muchas heridas, sin mencionar dos balas no extraídas en su cuerpo, no puede tener gran temor a la muerte; y Heureaux ha gobernado despóticamente y no sin crueldad, pero en conjunto, dice el periódico, la república negra ha salido ganando con ello, pues era un caso de perro come perro quienquiera que tuviera las riendas del gobierno.

records.headline: The Tribune prints an editorial on the assassination and the standing of the republic
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints an editorial on the assassination and the standing of the republic among nations: there were not a few who, on hearing the news of General Heureaux's assassination, cynically remarked, 'What, another?' as though such tragedies were common in that land; the fact is, however, that it is unique: two of our own Presidents have been murdered, and one of France's; recent years have witnessed the murder of a Russian Czar and an Austrian Empress; there were attempts upon the life of the first German Emperor, and even the Queen of England has not escaped such outrage; but now, for the first time, Santo Domingo mourns a murdered Chief of State, and it is for other nations not to rail at her, but to sympathize. Nor is the little republic thus brought into prominence in other respects a fitting target for our scorn: it has had numerous revolutions, but we think it has fared no worse in that respect than many others, certainly not if we take into account the disabilities under which it has labored — a republic of mixed races, by the side of a negro State and isolated from all others and treated with scorn and selfishness by all its betters, is not a likely candidate for the title of Utopia; nevertheless, this one has of late years been making steady progress, peace has prevailed, and industrial and commercial prosperity has been maintained and increased.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica un editorial sobre el asesinato y la posición de la república entre las naciones: no fueron pocos los que, al oír la noticia del asesinato del general Heureaux, remarcaron cínicamente, «¿Qué, otro?», como si tales tragedias fueran comunes en esa tierra; el hecho es, sin embargo, que es único: dos de nuestros propios Presidentes han sido asesinados, y uno de Francia; años recientes han presenciado el asesinato de un Zar ruso y de una Emperatriz austríaca; hubo intentos contra la vida del primer Emperador alemán, y hasta la Reina de Inglaterra no ha escapado de tal ultraje; pero ahora, por primera vez, Santo Domingo llora a un Jefe de Estado asesinado, y corresponde a las otras naciones no burlarse de ella, sino simpatizar. Ni es la pequeña república así traída a la prominencia en otros respectos un blanco apropiado para nuestro desprecio: ha tenido numerosas revoluciones, pero pensamos que no ha salido peor en ese respecto que muchas otras, ciertamente no si tomamos en cuenta las desventajas bajo las cuales ha trabajado — una república de razas mezcladas, al lado de un Estado negro y aislada de todos los demás y tratada con desprecio y egoísmo por todos sus superiores, no es una candidata probable para el título de Utopía; sin embargo, esta ha estado en años recientes haciendo un progreso constante, la paz ha prevalecido, y la prosperidad industrial y comercial ha sido mantenida y aumentada.

records.headline: The News prints the Fort de France details of the assassination
records.summary_en: The News prints the Fort de France details of the assassination and the vice president's precautions: a financial crisis having arisen in Santo Domingo and an insurrection being feared owing to the number of malcontents, President Heureaux went to the north and west of the island to prepare for all eventualities; he was about to leave Moca for Santiago de las Caballeros when he was killed: booted and spurred, ready to mount his horse, he sat under the gallery of a house in the Rue Colon, talking with two friends in the afternoon, when an old man approached and asked for alms, and just as the president gave the man some money, Caceros, the assassin, rushed forward quickly and fired twice with his revolver; the first bullet struck the heart of the president, killing him instantly, and the other killed the old man by his side. The crime was committed so quickly that the friends of the president were not able to interfere in time to prevent it, but they fired a number of shots at Caceros, who ran away, accompanied by several persons; the assassin's party returned the fire of the president's friends, and Caceros escaped; it is not known whether he was wounded or not; and the authorities immediately sent troops to pursue him. The news of the president's death spread rapidly and caused much emotion among the inhabitants of the island; it is believed by many that the murder was the result of a political conspiracy; and Vice President Figuereo has taken precautions to prevent disorder.
records.summary_es: El News publica los detalles de Fort de France sobre el asesinato y las precauciones del vicepresidente: habiendo surgido una crisis financiera en Santo Domingo y temiéndose una insurrección por el número de descontentos, el presidente Heureaux fue al norte y al oeste de la isla a prepararse para todas las eventualidades; estaba a punto de partir de Moca para Santiago de los Caballeros cuando fue muerto: con botas y espuelas, listo para montar su caballo, estaba sentado bajo la galería de una casa en la Rue Colon, hablando con dos amigos en la tarde, cuando un anciano se acercó y pidió limosna, y justo cuando el presidente le dio al hombre algún dinero, Caceros, el asesino, se abalanzó rápidamente y disparó dos veces con su revólver; la primera bala hirió el corazón del presidente, matándolo instantáneamente, y la otra mató al anciano a su lado. El crimen fue cometido tan rápidamente que los amigos del presidente no pudieron interferir a tiempo para prevenirlo, pero dispararon un número de tiros a Caceros, que huyó, acompañado por varias personas; el partido del asesino devolvió el fuego de los amigos del presidente, y Caceros escapó; no se sabe si fue herido o no; y las autoridades enviaron inmediatamente tropas a perseguirlo. La noticia de la muerte del presidente se extendió rápidamente y causó mucha emoción entre los habitantes de la isla; muchos creen que el asesinato fue el resultado de una conspiración política; y el vicepresidente Figuereo ha tomado precauciones para prevenir desorden.

records.headline: The News completes its account with the Santiago burial decision
records.summary_en: The News completes its account with the Santiago burial decision, the panic item, the Puerto Plata report, and the opening of the condolence item: the removal of the remains to the city of Santo Domingo would have brought excitement and manifestations, and foreseeing the possibility of disturbances, Gen. Pepin, governor of Santiago, has taken important precautionary measures and has decided to demand that ammunition be forwarded to him from Santo Domingo; advices from Santiago received at a late hour report the situation there is becoming more serious. President Heureaux's death has caused a panic: one Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, is said to be a candidate for President; Gen. Maximo Gomez, formerly president of the Cuban insurrectionists, who is a native of Santo Domingo, aspires to the presidency; and the father of Caceros, the assassin, was put to death by order of President Heureaux in 1884. Under the head 'Situation Is Critical,' a Puerto Plata item of July 27 says the body of President Heureaux has been brought to Santiago, attended by a government escort and members of the late president's family; the situation is critical; enemies of the government are trying to disturb the peace; Gen. Wenceslao Figuereo, the vice president, succeeds to the presidency and will continue the plan of retiring paper money; and President Heureaux went to Moca attended by only six persons. Under the head 'McKinley's Condolence,' a Washington item of July 27 says the State Department received confirmation of the death of the president of Santo Domingo in a despatch from the United States consul at Puerto Plata, 'President Heureaux assassinated,' and the news was communicated to the president at Lake Champlain by the State Department, and a cable message was sent by his direction.
records.summary_es: El News completa su relato con la decisión del entierro en Santiago, la nota del pánico, el reporte de Puerto Plata, y el comienzo de la nota de condolencia: el traslado de los restos a la ciudad de Santo Domingo habría traído excitación y manifestaciones, y previendo la posibilidad de disturbios, el gen. Pepin, gobernador de Santiago, ha tomado importantes medidas precautorias y ha decidido demandar que municiones le sean enviadas desde Santo Domingo; avisos de Santiago recibidos a última hora reportan que la situación ahí se está volviendo más seria. La muerte del presidente Heureaux ha causado un pánico: se dice que un tal Juan Isidoro Jiminez, que tomó parte en el intento de insurrección de junio de 1898, es candidato a la Presidencia; el gen. Máximo Gómez, ex presidente de los insurrectos cubanos, que es nativo de Santo Domingo, aspira a la presidencia; y el padre de Caceros, el asesino, fue ejecutado por orden del presidente Heureaux en 1884. Bajo el título «Situation Is Critical», una nota de Puerto Plata del 27 de julio dice que el cuerpo del presidente Heureaux ha sido traído a Santiago, atendido por una escolta del gobierno y miembros de la familia del difunto presidente; la situación es crítica; enemigos del gobierno están tratando de perturbar la paz; el gen. Wenceslao Figuereo, el vicepresidente, sucede a la presidencia y continuará el plan de retirar el papel moneda; y el presidente Heureaux fue a Moca atendido por solo seis personas. Bajo el título «McKinley's Condolence», una nota de Washington del 27 de julio dice que el Departamento de Estado recibió confirmación de la muerte del presidente de Santo Domingo en un despacho del cónsul de los Estados Unidos en Puerto Plata, «Presidente Heureaux asesinado», y la noticia fue comunicada al presidente en Lake Champlain por el Departamento de Estado, y un mensaje por cable fue enviado por su dirección.

records.headline: The New Mexican completes an item on Caceres and prints a Cape Haytien dispatch
records.summary_en: The New Mexican completes an item on Caceres and prints a Cape Haytien dispatch on the funeral: Caceres started on his mission a few weeks ago, leaving Mrs. Caceres behind, and his friends are confident he took precautions to insure his escape. The Cape Haytien dispatch says the funeral of President Heureaux took place at 5 o'clock last evening in Santiago de las Caballeros; the population was panic-stricken, but there was no disorder; a report has been received here that the adversaries of the government attacked Moca last night; the news of the death of President Heureaux was hardly credited by the people generally until last evening, when undoubted confirmation was received; and there was great rejoicing among Dominican exiles, many of whom live around Cape Haytien — exiles driven out of their country by Heureaux, who are preparing to arm and enter Santo Domingo, where they expect their chief, Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, to join them; and the Dominican government is making preparations on a large scale to maintain itself. Under the head 'Timely Precaution,' the Washington item of July 28 says a naval vessel is to be sent immediately to Santo Domingo on the request of Secretary Hay: the Machias, now at San Juan, Porto Rico, only a day's run from Santo Domingo, will proceed to that island; this is a measure of precaution, rather than a necessity, at present, for Minister Powell has not suggested any such action.

records.headline: The Review completes its assassination dispatch and prints a Washington item of July 27
records.summary_en: The Review completes its assassination dispatch and prints a Washington item of July 27 on the official attitude: at present calmness prevails in the republic, and the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services. The Washington item says no information was received last night from the consular representatives of the United States in San Domingo regarding the assassination of President Heureaux, and that pending official advices of the assassination no formal action will be taken by this government: William F. Powell, the minister to Hayti, is also chargé d'affaires to San Domingo, while this government is directly represented in the republic in the person of Campbell Maxwell, who is consul general, and John A. Read, who is vice consul; officials here recall that attempts have heretofore been made on the life of President Heureaux, and Secretary Hay paid a brief tribute to the work of the deceased president, saying he understood that he had given the country a good administration; and Secretary Long said he could not recall that there were any ships of the United States now in San Domingo waters, but that should the developments of the next few days show a feeling of unrest and uncertainty a United States man-of-war will be dispatched to protect American interests.
records.summary_es: El Review completa su despacho del asesinato y publica una nota de Washington del 27 de julio sobre la actitud oficial: en el presente prevalece la calma en la república, y los restos del presidente Heureaux probablemente serán llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres. La nota de Washington dice que anoche no se recibió información de los representantes consulares de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo respecto al asesinato del presidente Heureaux, y que, pendientes los avisos oficiales del asesinato, este gobierno no tomará ninguna acción formal: William F. Powell, el ministro en Haití, es también chargé d'affaires en Santo Domingo, mientras este gobierno está directamente representado en la república en la persona de Campbell Maxwell, que es cónsul general, y John A. Read, que es vicecónsul; los funcionarios aquí recuerdan que antes se han hecho atentados contra la vida del presidente Heureaux, y el secretario Hay rindió un breve tributo a la labor del presidente fallecido, diciendo que entendía que él había dado al país una buena administración; y el secretario Long dijo que no podía recordar que hubiera ahora ninguno de los buques de los Estados Unidos en aguas de Santo Domingo, pero que si los acontecimientos de los próximos días mostraran un sentimiento de inquietud e incertidumbre, un buque de guerra de los Estados Unidos será despachado para proteger los intereses americanos.

records.headline: The Silver State prints an editorial sketch of Heureaux's career
records.summary_en: The Silver State prints an editorial sketch of Heureaux's career and character: the sketch, in the paper's editorial voice, traces the development of his character to his ancestry, and says that in a more civilized community he would have become a more or less successful highwayman, while in the West Indies he developed into a patriot, a revolutionary leader, and a President. He commenced his public and military career at the same time, as a common soldier; he soon distinguished himself, for none dispute his bravery, and eventually became a commander; he served with distinction in Santo Domingo's war with Spain, pushing himself to the fore until the dignity of the title of General was his; after the war he kept on pushing himself forward, and in 1882 he was elected President of the Republic; he had, at the time of his death, held that office for seventeen years, having passed through four elections, more dangerous than war, and numerous plots to assassinate, more dangerous than either. The Dominican Republic, the paper says, is scarcely a republic as Americans understand it, nor Heureaux a President made such by popular suffrage: he was, in fact, a little tyrant of a small field, as proud as the queen of all the English, who took upon himself the airs of the greatest of rulers, yet could, when occasion required, assume the ways of the polished man of the world, and none were more courteous and thoughtful than he; and his morals, it adds, were quite as bad as those of the Prince of Wales.
records.summary_es: El Silver State publica una semblanza editorial de la carrera y el carácter de Heureaux: la semblanza, en la voz editorial del periódico, atribuye el desarrollo de su carácter a su ascendencia, y dice que en una comunidad más civilizada él se habría convertido en un salteador de caminos más o menos exitoso, mientras en las Indias Occidentales se desarrolló en un patriota, un líder revolucionario, y un Presidente. Él comenzó su carrera pública y militar al mismo tiempo, como soldado raso; pronto se distinguió, pues nadie disputa su valentía, y eventualmente llegó a ser un comandante; sirvió con distinción en la guerra de Santo Domingo con España, abriéndose paso hasta que la dignidad del título de General fue suya; después de la guerra siguió abriéndose paso hacia adelante, y en 1882 fue elegido Presidente de la República; él había, al tiempo de su muerte, ocupado ese cargo por diecisiete años, habiendo pasado por cuatro elecciones, más peligrosas que la guerra, y numerosos complots para asesinarlo, más peligrosos que cualquiera de las dos. La República Dominicana, dice el periódico, es escasamente una república como los americanos la entienden, ni Heureaux un Presidente hecho tal por el sufragio popular: él era, de hecho, un pequeño tirano de un campo pequeño, tan orgulloso como la reina de todos los ingleses, que tomó sobre sí los aires del más grande de los gobernantes, pero podía, cuando la ocasión lo requería, asumir las maneras del hombre de mundo refinado, y ninguno era más cortés y considerado que él; y su moral, añade, era tan mala como la del Príncipe de Gales.

records.headline: The Dispatch prints the close of the Cape Haytien exiles item
records.summary_en: The Dispatch prints the close of the Cape Haytien exiles item and a Washington item of July 28 on the warships: the death of President Heureaux was hardly credited by the people generally until last evening, when undoubted confirmation was received, and then there was great rejoicing among the Dominican exiles, many of whom live in and around Cape Haitien; these exiles, who were driven out of their country by Heureaux, are now preparing to arm themselves and enter Santo Domingo, where they expect their chief, Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, to join them. Under the head 'To Protect American Interests,' the Washington item says Secretary Long to-day issued orders detaching the cruiser New Orleans from the North Atlantic squadron at Newport, and directing her to proceed at once to Santo Domingo city; orders were issued also to the Machias, now at St. Thomas, to proceed to the same point, via San Juan; these orders were made at the instance of the State Department, and as a precautionary measure, owing to the disturbed condition following the assassination of President Heureaux; neither the State nor the Navy Department has received any advices of an alarming character, but owing to the large American interests on the island it was deemed advisable to take every precaution; and it is understood that American capitalists have an arrangement with the Dominican authorities by which practically the entire machinery of the island administration is under their direction.

records.headline: The Call prints a Washington item on the crisis in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Call prints a Washington item on the crisis in Santo Domingo and the foreign interests at stake: the vessels are being sent solely as a precautionary measure; the press dispatches indicate political intrigues which may result in revolution; and, as American interests in the little republic are paramount to those of any other country, it is the part of prudence to have ample force at hand to see that full protection is given to those interests. As to the possibility of annexation as an immediate outcome of the assassination, Secretary Hay and Secretary Long think that it is going too fast to expect such a result and rather discourage this kind of talk; they do not deny, however, that the United States may be forced to serious responsibilities in connection with the future government of San Domingo. While no detailed information has been received regarding the plot which resulted in the assassination of President Heureaux, it is believed to be probable that it was planned and executed by partisans of Jiminez, the revolutionary leader; it is known that Heureaux had lived in fear of assassination for many months, and had frankly announced that he proposed to continue the Presidency as long as he lived. German interests in this republic are considerable, and President Heureaux was strongly backed by them; the future of the republic may depend largely upon the course taken by the foreign element in this crisis, and the course of the German Government in the present crisis will be watched with considerable interest by the American Government.
records.summary_es: El Call publica una nota de Washington sobre la crisis en Santo Domingo y los intereses extranjeros en juego: los buques están siendo enviados únicamente como medida precautoria; los despachos de prensa indican intrigas políticas que pueden resultar en revolución; y, como los intereses americanos en la pequeña república son primordiales frente a los de cualquier otro país, es propio de la prudencia tener amplia fuerza a mano para ver que se dé plena protección a esos intereses. En cuanto a la posibilidad de la anexión como resultado inmediato del asesinato, el secretario Hay y el secretario Long piensan que es ir demasiado rápido esperar tal resultado y más bien desalientan esta clase de conversación; ellos no niegan, sin embargo, que los Estados Unidos puedan verse forzados a serias responsabilidades en conexión con el gobierno futuro de Santo Domingo. Aunque no se ha recibido información detallada respecto al complot que resultó en el asesinato del presidente Heureaux, se cree probable que fue planeado y ejecutado por partidarios de Jiminez, el líder revolucionario; se sabe que Heureaux había vivido en temor de un asesinato por muchos meses, y había anunciado francamente que se proponía continuar la Presidencia mientras viviera. Los intereses alemanes en esta república son considerables, y el presidente Heureaux estaba fuertemente respaldado por ellos; el futuro de la república puede depender en gran medida del curso que tome el elemento extranjero en esta crisis, y el curso del Gobierno alemán en la crisis presente será vigilado con considerable interés por el Gobierno americano.

records.headline: The Register prints the New York interview with General Moscoso
records.summary_en: The Register prints the New York interview with General Moscoso under the head 'An Exile's Views': Gen. Abelardo A. Moscoso, an exiled leader of the Liberal party of Santo Domingo, now living in New York, said last night: 'The death of President Heureaux will, I think, surely be followed by a long state of disorder and revolution. I want to emphasize this prophecy — that the United States will eventually be compelled to interfere to establish peace in the island, just as this country did in Cuba. I favor the policy of peace. I shall be glad to return to my country and support such a policy if it is inaugurated by Gen. Figuereo, the vice president, who succeeds to the head of the government. But if something is not quickly done to establish order and peace, more revolutionary expeditions will follow, like that of Gen. Jimenez and Gen. Morales, who led a band from Cuba against Heureaux. There are now in this country Gen. Toribio Garcia and Edward Grullon, who share my views. We think that the United States ought to take an interest in our West Indian republic. records.headline: The Tribune continues its editorial on the assassination and the standing of the republic:
records.summary_en: The Tribune continues its editorial on the assassination and the standing of the republic: President Heureaux had been an eminently popular Chief Magistrate, commanding the support of all parties and credited by all with having secured for the country a stability of government and a general prosperity never known before; and the argument is strengthened by the fact that neither before the murder were there any symptoms of revolution nor have there been any since; Dominicans may not be versed in the highest culture of political revolutionists, but they probably know that a revolution is not to be effected by killing just one man and doing nothing more. There will doubtless be, as indeed there already is, a flocking to the scene of all manner of discontented and ambitious men eager to profit from whatever disturbance of affairs there may be; some professional revolutionists may try to stir up trouble; it is even rumored that General Gomez, having finished his work in Cuba, will make some effort to secure the Dominican Presidency — a rumor which it is difficult to credit. All such attacks upon the established order in Santo Domingo will be deplorable from every point of view, and will especially meet with the reprobation of Americans; in past years individual citizens of this country have more than once contributed to disorder and to revolt in the lands of tropical America, but they have never done so with the sympathy or countenance of the United States Government, and it is to be hoped none will be so unworthy as to join in such movements now.
records.summary_es: El Tribune continúa su editorial sobre el asesinato y la posición de la república: el presidente Heureaux había sido un Magistrado Jefe eminentemente popular, que comandaba el apoyo de todos los partidos y a quien todos acreditaban haber asegurado para el país una estabilidad de gobierno y una prosperidad general nunca conocidas antes; y el argumento se fortalece por el hecho de que ni antes del asesinato hubo síntomas de revolución ni los ha habido desde entonces; los dominicanos pueden no estar versados en la más alta cultura de los revolucionarios políticos, pero probablemente saben que una revolución no se efectúa matando a un solo hombre y no haciendo nada más. Habrá sin duda, como de hecho ya la hay, una afluencia a la escena de toda clase de hombres descontentos y ambiciosos deseosos de aprovechar cualquier perturbación de los asuntos que pueda haber; algunos revolucionarios profesionales pueden tratar de agitar problemas; se rumora incluso que el general Gómez, habiendo terminado su labor en Cuba, hará algún esfuerzo para asegurarse la Presidencia dominicana — un rumor que es difícil de creer. Todos tales ataques sobre el orden establecido en Santo Domingo serán deplorables desde todo punto de vista, y encontrarán especialmente la reprobación de los americanos; en años pasados ciudadanos individuales de este país han contribuido más de una vez al desorden y a la revuelta en las tierras de la América tropical, pero nunca lo han hecho con la simpatía o el consentimiento del Gobierno de los Estados Unidos, y es de esperar que ninguno sea tan indigno como para unirse ahora a tales movimientos.

records.headline: The Free Lance prints an editorial on Heureaux's policy and a sketch of his career:
records.summary_en: The Free Lance prints an editorial on Heureaux's policy and a sketch of his career: he hoped that San Domingo might flourish through the aid of foreign capital, and constructed railroads and telegraph lines to develop the resources of the country, but the atmosphere of insurrection and the fear of maladministration kept investors away, and the republic has remained in obscurity save for the recurrence of such tragedies as that now reported; the assassination of the president will be followed by upheavals, as long-suppressed aspirants for power step forward. Under the head 'Career of the Dead President': Heureaux has been called the Napoleon of the south; he was born at Puerto Plata, a town on the north coast of Santo Domingo, in 1846; he became a private soldier in 1862, volunteering in the native service in the uprising against the Spaniards; when the Spaniards left the island Heureaux had risen to the rank of colonel; he was a leader in the various attempts to drive from power Buenaventura Baez, who, in 1867, usurped absolute power in the island; Baez was successful, and Heureaux went into exile; in 1869 he again led the revolt against Baez: Baez's troops, regulars, 1,500 strong, were encamped about eighteen miles from the border line, and Colonel Heureaux had only seventy men, volunteers; after five hours' desperate fighting, the enemy having been surprised, Baez's troops fled — twenty-eight men were killed and eighty wounded, and on Heureaux's side eleven men were killed; and in 1874 the government of Baez ceased and General Gonzales came in.
records.summary_es: El Free Lance publica un editorial sobre la política de Heureaux y una semblanza de su carrera: él esperaba que Santo Domingo pudiera florecer mediante la ayuda del capital extranjero, y construyó ferrocarriles y líneas telegráficas para desarrollar los recursos del país, pero la atmósfera de insurrección y el temor de la mala administración mantuvieron alejados a los inversionistas, y la república ha permanecido en la oscuridad salvo por la recurrencia de tales tragedias como la ahora reportada; el asesinato del presidente será seguido de trastornos, a medida que aspirantes al poder por largo tiempo reprimidos den un paso adelante. Bajo el título «Career of the Dead President»: Heureaux ha sido llamado el Napoleón del sur; nació en Puerto Plata, una ciudad en la costa norte de Santo Domingo, en 1846; llegó a ser soldado raso en 1862, ofreciéndose como voluntario en el servicio nativo en el levantamiento contra los españoles; cuando los españoles salieron de la isla Heureaux había ascendido al rango de coronel; fue un líder en los varios intentos de expulsar del poder a Buenaventura Báez, que, en 1867, usurpó el poder absoluto en la isla; Báez tuvo éxito, y Heureaux se fue al exilio; en 1869 él de nuevo condujo la revuelta contra Báez: las tropas de Báez, regulares, 1,500 fuertes, estaban acampadas a unas dieciocho millas de la línea fronteriza, y el coronel Heureaux tenía solo setenta hombres, voluntarios; después de cinco horas de lucha desesperada, habiendo sido sorprendido el enemigo, las tropas de Báez huyeron — veintiocho hombres fueron muertos y ochenta heridos, y del lado de Heureaux once hombres fueron muertos; y en 1874 el gobierno de Báez cesó y el general Gonzales entró.

records.headline: The Times prints two items on the uprising in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Times prints two items on the uprising in Santo Domingo and the sailing of the warships: advices received from the Dominican frontier say that the insurgents have cut the telegraph wires in the neighborhood of Santiago de los Caballeros, and also near Moca, and that the insurgents in the western part of San Domingo await the arrival of Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, under whose leadership they expect to attack Santiago. Under the head 'Ships for San Domingo,' Captain Taylor, commanding the North Atlantic Squadron, telegraphed the Navy Department today that the cruiser New Orleans would be ready to sail from Newport for Santo Domingo city this afternoon; word came also from Commander Logan, of the gunboat Machias, that this vessel would get away from St. Thomas, Danish West Indies, on Sunday, and will go first to San Juan, Porto Rico — this will be good news, as the Navy Department believed that the Machias would not be ready for sea service for several days, Commander Logan having telegraphed on Thursday that she would be obliged to remain at St. Thomas for nine days while repairs were being made.

records.headline: The Argus completes its Havana item and prints the Moscoso interview
records.summary_en: The Argus completes its Havana item and prints the Moscoso interview under the head 'Annexation to Uncle Sam': with regard to the rumor that Gomez will be the next president of the republic of Santo Domingo, it is stated here that the most popular candidate is Senor Juan Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, and who is now in Havana; it is possible, however, so it is reported, that if a revolution takes place Senor Jiminez's opponents may offer Gomez the leadership; and El Diario de la Marina and La Lucha express the opinion that, considering the present expansion policy, the United States may intervene in San Domingo. The New York item of July 29 prints General Abelardo A. Moscoso, an exiled leader of the liberal party of Santo Domingo, now living in New York, who said Thursday night: 'The death of President Heureaux will, I think, surely be followed by disorder and revolution. I want to emphasize this prophecy that the United States will eventually be compelled to interfere to establish peace in the island, just as this country did in Cuba. If San Domingo must of necessity, I believe, ultimately become attached to this country.' General Moscoso has been an exile in New York for three years; he opposed the late president politically and had to flee to save his life.

Morales, who led a band from Cuba against Heureaux; advices from Santo Domingo to a Dominican here describe the existence of a well-planned and widespread plot by adherents of Jiminez to depose President Heureaux, which, it was thought, was sure to succeed; the assassination of President Heureaux is regarded here as an indication of the success of the plot; the city of Santo Domingo, it is reported, is in a state of great unrest and business is entirely suspended; the people fear an outbreak; last night a band of armed men attacked Moca, where President Heureaux was killed, and fired a number of shots; it is reported that the forces supporting the assassins have been augmented considerably; and the government has taken measures to put down the threatened insurrection.

records.headline: The Times completes the plot item and prints two dispatches
records.summary_en: The Times completes the plot item and prints two dispatches and the opening of the Plattsburg item: the government has taken measures to put down the threatened insurrection. A Cape Haytien dispatch of July 29 says the news of the death of President Heureaux was hardly credited there by the people generally until last evening, when undoubted confirmation was received; then there was great rejoicing among the Dominican exiles, many of whom live in and around Cape Haytien — exiles who were driven out of their country by Heureaux and are now preparing to arm themselves and enter Santo Domingo, where they expect their chief, Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, to join them. A Port au Prince item of July 28 says William F. Powell, United States minister to Hayti and diplomatic representative to the Republic of Santo Domingo, has sent a telegram to Vice-President Figuereo, who has assumed the presidency, expressing the keen regret of the United States government at the assassination of President Heureaux; and the latest news from Santo Domingo is that all is quiet throughout the territory of the republic. Under the head 'Figuereo's Thanks,' the Plattsburg item opens with the President's receipt of Figuereo's dispatch in reply to his message of condolence sent yesterday.

records.headline: The State Journal completes its Havana item on General Gomez
records.summary_en: The State Journal completes its Havana item on General Gomez and the succession in Santo Domingo: Gen. Gomez refused to discuss the presidency of the Dominican republic, claiming to know nothing regarding the matter; when questioned concerning the rumors circulating in the cafes as to his aspirations regarding a Dominican republic, Gomez's action proved his contempt for the stories, yet in the clubs and cafes he is seriously accused of conspiring to bring both the island of Hayti and Cuba under the dominion of the United States; in alluding to the cafe conspirators Gomez made use of a contemptuous term which is used among Cubans to signify cowards, and said he did not believe that many men belonging to the army would have anything to do with such people, who, he declared, do not represent Cuba, yet cause much misrepresentation; and he also classed a number of papers in the same category. General Gomez's wife and family left Santo Domingo on board the steamer Maria Herrera and are expected to arrive in Havana on Monday next; and with regard to the rumor that Gomez will be the next president of the republic of Santo Domingo, it is stated here that the most popular candidate is Senor Juan Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, and who is now in Havana; it is possible, however, so it is reported, that if a revolution takes place Senor Jiminez's opponents may offer Gomez the leadership; and El Diario de La Marina and La Lucha express the opinion that, considering the present expansion policy, the United States may intervene in San Domingo.
records.summary_es: El State Journal completa su nota de La Habana sobre el general Gómez y la sucesión en Santo Domingo: el gen. Gómez se negó a discutir la presidencia de la República Dominicana, alegando no saber nada respecto al asunto; al ser preguntado sobre los rumores circulados en los cafés en cuanto a sus aspiraciones respecto a una república dominicana, la acción de Gómez demostró su desprecio por las historias, pero en los clubes y cafés es seriamente acusado de conspirar para traer ambas, la isla de Hayti y Cuba, bajo el dominio de los Estados Unidos; al aludir a los conspiradores de café Gómez hizo uso de un término despectivo que es usado entre los cubanos para significar cobardes, y dijo que no creía que muchos hombres pertenecientes al ejército tuvieran algo que ver con tal gente, que, declaró, no representan a Cuba, pero causan mucha mala representación; y él también clasificó a un número de periódicos en la misma categoría. La esposa y la familia del general Gómez salieron de Santo Domingo a bordo del vapor Maria Herrera y se espera que lleguen a La Habana el próximo lunes; y con respecto al rumor de que Gómez será el próximo presidente de la república de Santo Domingo, se afirma aquí que el candidato más popular es el señor Juan Jiminez, que tomó parte en el intento de insurrección de junio de 1898, y que está ahora en La Habana; es posible, sin embargo, según se reporta, que si tiene lugar una revolución, los oponentes del señor Jiminez ofrezcan a Gómez el liderazgo; y El Diario de La Marina y La Lucha expresan la opinión de que, considerando la presente política de expansión, los Estados Unidos pueden intervenir en San Domingo.

records.headline: The Leader prints the Washington warships item and a Chicago item
records.summary_en: The Leader prints the Washington warships item and a Chicago item on General Gomez under the head 'Gomez May Go Home': Secretary Long has sent telegraphic orders to the cruiser New Orleans, at Newport, directing that she proceed at once to San Domingo, and at the same time an order was sent to the gunboat Machias, at St. Thomas, to leave for San Domingo; it is expected that the New Orleans will be able to leave during the day, and the Machias will be in San Domingo waters within a day or two; and this action was not due to the receipt of any official advices indicating possible trouble, but entirely to the desire to be beforehand in dealing with any possible disturbance. The Chicago item, a Tribune special from Washington of July 29, says that by the assassination of President Heureaux, of San Domingo, Cuba may lose one of its central figures, as it is well known General Maximo Gomez aspires to the presidency of the republic; this bar will not confront General Gomez in San Domingo, as he was born on that island and his family still reside there; some time ago, General Gomez issued a manifesto to the Cuban army, in which he bade his soldiers good bye and signified his intention to return to San Domingo, his native land; and as Gomez's love for adventure and fighting for what he calls liberty are well known, it is believed he will start for San Domingo at once, organize an army, and endeavor to fight his way to the presidency.

Y.: En nombre de la República Dominicana y en el mío propio me apresuro a presentar a Su Excelencia el testimonio de nuestra más ferviente gratitud por su condolencia por razón de la muerte del presidente Heureaux. W. Figuereo». El Presidente recibió unos pocos visitantes hoy, entre los cuales estuvieron el señor Cannon, presidente del Fourth National Bank de Nueva York, el coronel Rice y el teniente coronel Duval, del Vigésimo Sexto Regimiento, el Hon. S. M. Weed, y el nuevo colector de aduanas del distrito de Champlain; el Dr. A. H. Eaton, pastor de la Primera Iglesia Metodista Episcopal de Plattsburgh, y el Hon. Alfred Guibord también visitaron e invitaron al Presidente a asistir a la iglesia allí el domingo, y él prometió que lo haría si le fuera posible dejar a la señora McKinley; y se están haciendo arreglos para recibir al vicepresidente Hobart la próxima semana.

records.headline: The Tribune completes its Havana item on General Gomez and the succession
records.summary_en: The Tribune completes its Havana item on General Gomez and the succession, and opens a Columbus item on Consul-General Maxwell: Gomez's actions indicated his contempt for the stories, yet in the clubs and cafés he is seriously accused of conspiring to bring both Hayti and Cuba under the dominion of the United States; in alluding to the café conspirators, Gomez made use of a contemptuous term which is used among Cubans to signify cowards, and said he did not believe that many men belonging to the army would have anything to do with such people, who, he declared, do not represent Cuba, yet cause much misrepresentation. General Gomez's wife and family left Santo Domingo on board the steamer Maria Herrera, and are expected to arrive in Havana on Monday next; with regard to the rumor that Gomez will be the next president of the Republic of Santo Domingo, it is stated here that the most popular candidate is Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, and who is now in Havana; it is possible, however, so it is reported, that if a revolution takes place Senor Jiminez's opponents may offer Gomez the leadership; and 'El Diario de la Marina' and 'La Lucha' express the opinion that, considering the present expansion policy, the United States Government may intervene in Santo Domingo. Under the head 'Regret of a Personal Friend,' a Columbus, Ohio, item of July 28 opens: Campbell L. Maxwell, consul-general to the Republic of Santo Domingo, is in the city as the guest of E. J. Miller.
records.summary_es: El Tribune completa su nota de La Habana sobre el general Gómez y la sucesión, y abre una nota de Columbus sobre el cónsul general Maxwell: las acciones de Gómez indicaron su desprecio por las historias, pero en los clubes y cafés es seriamente acusado de conspirar para traer ambas, Hayti y Cuba, bajo el dominio de los Estados Unidos; al aludir a los conspiradores de café, Gómez hizo uso de un término despectivo que es usado entre los cubanos para significar cobardes, y dijo que no creía que muchos hombres pertenecientes al ejército tuvieran algo que ver con tal gente, que, declaró, no representan a Cuba, pero causan mucha mala representación. La esposa y la familia del general Gómez salieron de Santo Domingo a bordo del vapor Maria Herrera, y se espera que lleguen a La Habana el próximo lunes; con respecto al rumor de que Gómez será el próximo presidente de la República de Santo Domingo, se afirma aquí que el candidato más popular es Jiminez, que tomó parte en el intento de insurrección de junio de 1898, y que está ahora en La Habana; es posible, sin embargo, según se reporta, que si tiene lugar una revolución, los oponentes del señor Jiminez ofrezcan a Gómez el liderazgo; y «El Diario de la Marina» y «La Lucha» expresan la opinión de que, considerando la presente política de expansión, el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos puede intervenir en Santo Domingo. records.headline: The Journal and Courier prints a Plattsburgh item with President Figuereo's reply
records.summary_en: The Journal and Courier prints a Plattsburgh item with President Figuereo's reply to the President's message of condolence: 'San Domingo, via Hayti, July 27, 1899. To His Excellency, the President of the United States: In the name of the Dominican republic, and in my own, I hurry to present to your excellency the testimony of our most fervent gratitude for your condolence on account of the death of President Heureaux. W. Figuereo.' Among those who called on the President to-day were Colonel Rice and Lieutenant Colonel Duvall, of the Twenty-sixth Volunteer Regiment at Plattsburgh, Hon. Smith M. Weed and Henry W. Cannon, president of the Fourth National Bank of New York City; the President has been deluged with invitations from the surrounding places, but owing to Mrs. McKinley's health he has been compelled to decline all invitations, and will accept no invitations that will take him away from Mrs. McKinley even for a day; and on Sunday the President and Miss Duncan, accompanied by Dr. and Mrs. Rixey, will attend divine worship at the First Methodist Church of Plattsburgh, if Mrs. McKinley continues to improve.

records.headline: The Press completes a naval item and prints a Cape Haytien dispatch
records.summary_en: The Press completes a naval item and prints a Cape Haytien dispatch on the insurgents in Santo Domingo: the vessel is on the way to Porto Rico, to land Commander Snow, who is to take charge of the naval station there, and the commander of the New Orleans also announced his readiness to start for San Domingo to-day, so that before the middle of next week the American navy will be sufficiently represented in San Domingo to protect American interests of all kinds should there be a revolution. The Cape Haytien dispatch of July 29 says advices just received from the Dominican frontier say that the insurgents have cut the telegraph wires in the neighborhood of Santiago de los Caballeros, and near Moca, and that the insurgents in the western part of San Domingo await the arrival of Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, under whose leadership they intend to attack Santiago.
records.summary_es: El Press completa una nota naval y publica un despacho de Cabo Haitiano sobre los insurgentes en Santo Domingo: el buque está en camino a Puerto Rico, para desembarcar al comandante Snow, que ha de encargarse de la estación naval allí, y el comandante del New Orleans también anunció su disposición de partir para San Domingo hoy, de modo que antes de mediados de la próxima semana la marina americana estará suficientemente representada en San Domingo para proteger los intereses americanos de toda clase si hubiera una revolución. El despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 29 de julio dice que avisos recién recibidos de la frontera dominicana dicen que los insurgentes han cortado los cables telegráficos en el vecindario de Santiago de los Caballeros, y cerca de Moca, y que los insurgentes en la parte occidental de San Domingo esperan la llegada de don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, bajo cuyo liderazgo intentan atacar Santiago.

records.headline: The Times prints a Havana item on the choice of a successor
records.summary_en: The Times prints a Havana item on the choice of a successor to President Heureaux: there is a good deal of agitation in the Havana press regarding the selection of Gen. Maximo Gomez or Gen. Juan Antonio Jiminez as President of the Republic of Santo Domingo, to succeed General Heureaux, who was assassinated the other day. General Gomez has said that he would not go to Santo Domingo in any event, his only ambition and mission in life being to see an independent Cuban Republic; and General Jiminez, whose father was at one time President of the Dominican Republic, is now living in Havana, and his business here is not of a character to interfere with his candidacy.
records.summary_es: El Times publica una nota de La Habana sobre la elección de un sucesor del presidente Heureaux: hay una buena medida de agitación en la prensa habanera respecto a la selección del gen. Máximo Gómez o del gen. Juan Antonio Jiminez como Presidente de la República de Santo Domingo, para suceder al general Heureaux, que fue asesinado el otro día. El general Gómez ha dicho que no iría a Santo Domingo en ningún caso, siendo su única ambición y misión en la vida ver una República Cubana independiente; y el general Jiminez, cuyo padre fue en un tiempo Presidente de la República Dominicana, está viviendo ahora en La Habana, y su negocio aquí no es de un carácter que interfiera con su candidatura.

records.headline: The Call completes a Washington item on the foreign navies and the errand of the men-of-war:
records.summary_en: The Call completes a Washington item on the foreign navies and the errand of the men-of-war: there is no foreign man-of-war in these waters to protect its citizens in the event of a revolution, the absence of such vessels being taken as an indication that other countries are satisfied to depend upon the United States to look after foreign interests in case of an uprising; Germany, the correspondent is told, has not a single man-of-war on this station, her North Atlantic squadron having recently been withdrawn to participate in the autumn maneuvers at Kiel; it was stated that a vessel was to be sent to Guatemala to demand the payment of debts due to certain German subjects, but the Navy Department has not been informed of her departure. The only possible fear of any undue interference in affairs in San Domingo has been from Germany: it is known that she has some interests there, and it has been stated that some of the German residents are in sympathy with Jiminez, who is said to be heading a movement antagonistic to the legitimate successor of Heureaux; while, keeping a careful watch that there is no foreign interference, the immediate work of the two men-of-war to be sent to San Domingo will be to protect American citizens, and if necessary marines will be landed to protect the American consulate and American property; the moral effect of the presence of these ships will, the authorities hope, be sufficient to put a damper on any revolutionary movements; and Secretary Long said to-day that he expected the Machias would reach San Domingo city by Monday, her repairs having been expedited so that she will be able to sail from St. Thomas to-morrow evening.
records.summary_es: El Call completa una nota de Washington sobre las marinas extranjeras y la misión de los buques de guerra: no hay ningún buque de guerra extranjero en estas aguas para proteger a sus ciudadanos en el evento de una revolución, tomándose la ausencia de tales buques como una indicación de que otros países están satisfechos de depender de los Estados Unidos para cuidar los intereses extranjeros en caso de un levantamiento; Alemania, según se dice al corresponsal, no tiene un solo buque de guerra en esta estación, habiendo sido retirada recientemente su escuadra del Atlántico Norte para participar en las maniobras de otoño en Kiel; se afirmó que un buque iba a ser enviado a Guatemala a demandar el pago de deudas debidas a ciertos súbditos alemanes, pero el Departamento de Marina no ha sido informado de su partida. El único posible temor de cualquier interferencia indebida en los asuntos en San Domingo ha sido de Alemania: se sabe que ella tiene algunos intereses allí, y se ha afirmado que algunos de los residentes alemanes simpatizan con Jiminez, de quien se dice que encabeza un movimiento antagónico al sucesor legítimo de Heureaux; mientras, manteniendo una vigilancia cuidadosa de que no haya interferencia extranjera, la labor inmediata de los dos buques de guerra que serán enviados a San Domingo será proteger a los ciudadanos americanos, y si fuera necesario se desembarcarán infantes de marina para proteger el consulado americano y la propiedad americana; el efecto moral de la presencia de estos buques será, esperan las autoridades, suficiente para poner un freno a cualquier movimiento revolucionario; y el secretario Long dijo hoy que esperaba que el Machias llegaría a la ciudad de San Domingo para el lunes, habiéndose acelerado sus reparaciones para que pueda partir de St. Thomas mañana por la noche.

records.headline: The Call prints the Port de France dispatch of July 29 on Monte Cristi
records.summary_en: The Call prints the Port de France dispatch of July 29 on Monte Cristi and Moca: tranquility prevails at Monte Cristi, but all the people are anxiously awaiting the important events which it is expected will occur shortly; General Pichardo, the governor of the city, has taken all possible measures to repel any attack which may be made by the followers of Senor Juan Jiminez, one of the candidates for the presidency of the republic; it is said that General Pichardo has advised the Government to issue a decree proclaiming amnesty for all Dominican exiles, with a view to appeasing the people; at La Vega General Don Pedro Bobea has taken steps to suppress outbreaks should any occur; up to the present time perfect order has been maintained, but notwithstanding that fact all law-abiding citizens have been called upon to bear arms and hold themselves in immediate readiness for service; and at Moca, where the people criticize harshly the laxity of the governor, General Juan Gonzales, many versions are in circulation regarding the killing of the President — one has it that the assassin shot him with the muzzle of the weapon held close to Heureaux's body.
records.summary_es: El Call publica el despacho de Port de France del 29 de julio sobre Monte Cristi y Moca: prevalece la tranquilidad en Monte Cristi, pero todo el pueblo espera ansiosamente los importantes eventos que se espera ocurrirán en breve; el general Pichardo, gobernador de la ciudad, ha tomado todas las medidas posibles para repeler cualquier ataque que pueda ser hecho por los seguidores del señor Juan Jiminez, uno de los candidatos a la presidencia de la república; se dice que el general Pichardo ha aconsejado al Gobierno emitir un decreto proclamando amnistía para todos los exiliados dominicanos, con miras a apaciguar al pueblo; en La Vega el general don Pedro Bobea ha tomado pasos para suprimir estallidos si alguno ocurriera; hasta el presente momento se ha mantenido un orden perfecto, pero no obstante ese hecho todos los ciudadanos respetuosos de la ley han sido llamados a tomar las armas y mantenerse en disposición inmediata para el servicio; y en Moca, donde el pueblo critica duramente la laxitud del gobernador, el general Juan Gonzales, circulan muchas versiones respecto a la muerte del Presidente — una sostiene que el asesino le disparó con la boca del arma pegada al cuerpo de Heureaux.

records.headline: The Republican completes the uprising item and prints two Washington items of July 29
records.summary_en: The Republican completes the uprising item and prints two Washington items of July 29 on the sailing of the warships: the insurgents in the western part of Santo Domingo await the arrival of Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, under whose leadership they expect to attack Santiago. Under the head 'To Protect Americans,' the first item says a cablegram has been received at the Navy Department from the commander of the Machias, now at St. Thomas, W. I., stating that he would sail to-morrow for San Domingo, and that the commander of the New Orleans also announced his readiness to start for San Domingo to-day, so that before the middle of next week the American navy will be sufficiently represented in San Domingo to protect American interests should there be a revolution. Under the head 'Nothing Officially Heard,' the second item says the Navy Department had not heard up to the close of office hours this morning of the sailing of the New Orleans for Santo Domingo, and that there were no dispatches indicating cause for alarm over the situation in the island.

records.headline: The Tribune prints the views of Charles W. Wells on the situation
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints the views of Charles W. Wells on the situation in the republic: the Santo Domingo Improvement Company, of this city, whose offices are in the Empire Building, own the railroad system in the republic, and are trustees for the Government bonds, as security for which they have charge of the collection of the revenues of the country. Mr. Wells, president of the company, has often visited in Santo Domingo; he returned from there about a month ago, after having spent several weeks with President Heureaux and other State officials, and was to have met the President in August; he is thoroughly familiar with the political, social and industrial condition of the republic, and, having large interests at stake himself, his views on the situation should be of comfort to other foreigners who hold Dominican securities: 'I am not in the least worried about Santo Domingo. To be sure, the republic has lost an able man and a good President by the death of Senor Heureaux, but one man does not make or even hold together a nation. In the United States it seems to be the prevailing opinion that the inhabitants of Santo Domingo are a lot of ignorant, uneducated savages. On the other hand, they are, as a whole, well bred, intelligent and refined. They devote a great deal of attention to education. Fathers whose means will permit of it educate their children.'

records.headline: The Dispatch prints the Havana item on General Gomez and the succession
records.summary_en: The Dispatch prints the Havana item on General Gomez and the succession in Santo Domingo: 'I believe all papers lie,' said Gomez, 'and those of one country are in this respect no better than those of another; in the future I will give over my own signature, or through the Associated Press alone, anything I may have to say to the press.' General Gomez refused to discuss the presidency of the Dominican republic, claiming to know nothing regarding the matter; when questioned concerning the rumors circulating in the cafes as to his aspirations regarding the presidency of the Dominican republic, his action proved his contempt for the stories, yet in the clubs and cafe he is seriously accused of conspiracy to bring both the island of Haiti and Cuba under the dominion of the United States. With regard to the rumor that Gomez will be the next President of the republic of Santo Domingo, it is stated here that the most popular candidate is Senor Juan Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, and who is now in Habana; it is possible, however, so it is reported, that if a revolution takes place Senor Jiminez's opponents may offer Gomez the leadership.

records.headline: The Leader completes the Havana papers item, then prints the Moscoso interview
records.summary_en: The Leader completes the Havana papers item, then prints the Moscoso interview and the Cape Haytien wires item: considering the present expansion policy, the United States may intervene in San Domingo. Under the head 'More Trouble Feared,' a New York item of July 31 prints General Abelardo A. Moscoso, an exiled leader of the Liberal party of Santo Domingo, now living in New York: 'The death of President Heureaux will, I think, surely be followed by a long state of disorder and revolution. I want to emphasize this prophecy — that the United States will eventually be compelled to interfere to establish peace in the island, just as this country did in Cuba. I favor the policy of peace. I shall be glad to return to my country and support such a policy if it is inaugurated by General Figuereo, the vice president, who succeeds to the head of the government. But if something is not quickly done to establish order and peace, more revolutionary expeditions will follow that of General Jiminez and General Morales, who led a band from Cuba against Heureaux.' Under the head 'Telegraph Wires Cut,' the Cape Haytien dispatch says advices just received from the Dominican frontier say the insurgents have cut the telegraph wires in the neighborhood of Santiago de los Caballeros and also near Moca, and that the insurgents in the western part of Santo Domingo await the arrival of Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, under whose leadership they expect to attack Santiago.

Quiero enfatizar esta profecía — que los Estados Unidos serán eventualmente obligados a intervenir para establecer la paz en la isla, justo como este país hizo en Cuba. Yo favorezco la política de paz. Estaré contento de regresar a mi país y apoyar tal política si es inaugurada por el general Figuereo, el vicepresidente, que sucede a la jefatura del gobierno. records.headline: The State Journal prints an editorial on the assassination of the president of San Domingo
records.summary_en: The State Journal prints an editorial on the assassination of the president of San Domingo and the republic's future. In the paper's own voice it argues that when the islands become parts of the great republic, revolutions and assassinations will cease, calling such responsibilities a part of the burden that must be shouldered some time whether we wish it or not. The president of San Domingo who was assassinated last week, the paper says, was serving his fourth term in the presidency, having been first chosen to that office in 1886; the Dominican republic occupies the larger part of the eastern end of the island of Hayti; it has a population of about 425,000; was organized in 1844, and its constitution was readopted in 1865 when the Spanish left the island; its government is complicated — besides the president and vice president, the president's cabinet, and a legislative body of twenty-two members, each province and district, parish and town has its distinctive officers; and having a republican form of government already in operation, it could fall into place as a state of the American union much more readily perhaps than could Cuba or Porto Rico.
records.summary_es: El State Journal publica un editorial sobre el asesinato del presidente de San Domingo y el futuro de la república. En su propia voz argumenta que cuando las islas lleguen a ser partes de la gran república, las revoluciones y los asesinatos cesarán, llamando tales responsabilidades una parte de la carga que debe ser asumida algún día lo deseemos o no. El presidente de San Domingo que fue asesinado la semana pasada, dice el periódico, estaba sirviendo su cuarto término en la presidencia, habiendo sido elegido por primera vez a ese cargo en 1886; la República Dominicana ocupa la mayor parte del extremo oriental de la isla de Hayti; tiene una población de cerca de 425,000; fue organizada en 1844, y su constitución fue readoptada en 1865 cuando los españoles salieron de la isla; su gobierno es complicado — además del presidente y el vicepresidente, el gabinete del presidente, y un cuerpo legislativo de veintidós miembros, cada provincia y distrito, parroquia y pueblo tiene sus funcionarios distintivos; y teniendo ya en operación una forma republicana de gobierno, podría caer en su lugar como un estado de la unión americana mucho más fácilmente quizás que Cuba o Puerto Rico.

records.headline: The News prints the Fort de France assassination dispatch of July 27:
records.summary_en: The News prints the Fort de France assassination dispatch of July 27: Gen. Ulises Heureaux, president of the Dominican Republic, was assassinated last evening at Moca; the name of the murderer is Ramon Caceros, and he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic pursuit was at once begun, and it is probable that he will soon be captured; the vice-president, General Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the president's death assumed direction of affairs; at present calmness prevails everywhere in the republic; and the remains of Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for funeral services. Gen. Ulises Heureaux, the paper adds, had been president of the Dominican republic since Sept. 1, 1886.
records.summary_es: El News publica el despacho del asesinato de Fort de France del 27 de julio: el gen. Ulises Heureaux, presidente de la República Dominicana, fue asesinado anoche en Moca; el nombre del asesino es Ramón Caceros, y logró escapar, pero se inició de inmediato una persecución enérgica y es probable que pronto sea capturado; el vicepresidente, general Wenceslao Figuereo, inmediatamente después del anuncio de la muerte del presidente asumió la dirección de los asuntos; en el presente prevalece la calma en todas partes de la república; y los restos de Heureaux probablemente serán llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres. El gen. Ulises Heureaux, añade el periódico, había sido presidente de la República Dominicana desde el 1 de septiembre de 1886.
