Because Disgusted With Her Home.
Leavenworth, Kan., July 29. Artie
Hoover, the 14-year-old girl who ran
away from her home at Kansas City,
Mo., and who was located by the police
in this city, says she will not go back
to her home. She says her mother had
been married several times and that
the family made her do errands for
them, such as earry beer. She had
become tired and disgusted with this
life and had determined to seek a new
home.
What Congressman Bailey Thinks.
Houston, Tex., July 29. Congress
man J. W. Bailey to-day said: "I am
fully persuaded that the national ad
ministration has entered into a full
and complete agreement for an alliance
between Great Britain and the United
States. This alliance, in my opinion
is to be both offensive and defensive.
I think the reason it has not been pub
lished the world is that for political
reasoaas the president is afraid to do so.

records.headline: The Tribune prints a correction headed 'Grullon Not with the Firm'
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints a correction headed 'Grullon Not with the Firm' and a Washington item of August 2: Señor Adrianno Grullon, the representative in the United States of the revolutionary party in San Domingo and the former business partner of Señor J. Y. Jimenez, the leader of the insurrectionists, in making a statement on Tuesday night of the reasons why President Heureaux was assassinated, gave the impression that he was connected with the firm of Huttlinger Vivié, of No. 101 Pearl-st.; what he evidently intended to say was that he might be reached through this firm; the firm last night denied that Señor Grullon was identified in any way with their business, or that they represent Señor Jimenez and his followers in this country; they say, however: 'We, in common with the houses trading with San Domingo, are in full sympathy with the efforts to bring about reform in the deplorable administration of affairs in that republic.' The Washington item prints the report of Commander Logan of the Machias, which arrived at Santo Domingo City yesterday: the United States Consul says that the report of the death of the President of Santo Domingo is believed not to have any political significance; the motive of the assassin is supposed to be personal revenge; the Vice-President of Santo Domingo has succeeded without political disturbance and reappointed the former Cabinet; no disorder exists; and the commander requests permission to delay sailing five days to repair boiler. A further head reports Minister Powell's action approved by the State Department.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica una corrección titulada «Grullon Not with the Firm» y una nota de Washington del 2 de agosto: el señor Adrianno Grullon, representante en los Estados Unidos del partido revolucionario en Santo Domingo y antiguo socio comercial del señor J. Y. Jimenes, el líder de los insurrectos, al hacer una declaración el martes por la noche sobre las razones por las que el presidente Heureaux fue asesinado, dio la impresión de que estaba conectado con la firma de Huttlinger Vivié, del No. 101 de Pearl-st.; lo que evidentemente quiso decir fue que se le podía localizar a través de esta firma; la firma negó anoche que el señor Grullon estuviera identificado de modo alguno con su negocio, o que ellos representen al señor Jimenes y sus seguidores en este país; dicen, sin embargo: «Nosotros, en común con las casas que comercian con Santo Domingo, simpatizamos plenamente con los esfuerzos por lograr una reforma en la deplorable administración de los asuntos en esa república». La nota de Washington publica el informe del comandante Logan del Machias, que llegó ayer a la ciudad de Santo Domingo: el cónsul de los Estados Unidos dice que se cree que el reporte de la muerte del presidente de Santo Domingo no tiene ningún significado político; se supone que el móvil del asesino fue venganza personal; el vicepresidente de Santo Domingo ha sucedido sin perturbación política y ha vuelto a nombrar al gabinete anterior; no existe desorden; y el comandante solicita permiso para demorar la salida cinco días para reparar la caldera. Un título adicional reporta la acción del ministro Powell aprobada por el Departamento de Estado.

records.headline: The Register completes a cable item on the revolution in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Register completes a cable item on the revolution in Santo Domingo and prints the Puerto Plata dispatch of July 31 headed 'The Situation Is Critical': the private cablegram says demoralization is growing through the death of the president; in the event of the revolution succeeding still, it is probable that Jiminez and the other reputed leaders of the revolution will agree to retire, offering the presidency to Gen. Maximo Gomez, who would prove acceptable to all parties; a deputation, it is reported, is going to Cuba to confer with Gen. Gomez. The Puerto Plata dispatch says the situation is critical and an outbreak is momentarily expected; the friends of the government are under arms and ready for action to protect property and preserve the peace; a feeble attempt was made to seize the body of President Heureaux by the assassins Ramon Caceres, Manuel Caceres, Horacio Vasquez and Domingo Pichardo, who are in the country about Moca with their followers; the burial of President Heureaux was conducted with fitting honors; Gov. Pepin has assembled troops in Moca, and the governor of La Vega has 1,000 men; the minister of the treasury has arrived at Moca in hot haste; the government is taking steps for the protection of business and the finance of the country, and expects to carry out the contemplated cancellation of the state bank notes; in Puerto Plata there is an urgent demand that the government send a sufficient force to Moca to hunt down the assassins of the president.
records.summary_es: El Register completa una nota cablegráfica sobre la revolución en Santo Domingo y publica el despacho de Puerto Plata del 31 de julio titulado «The Situation Is Critical»: el cablegrama privado dice que la desmoralización crece por la muerte del presidente; en caso de que la revolución tenga éxito aun así, es probable que Jimenes y los demás líderes reputados de la revolución acuerden retirarse, ofreciendo la presidencia al gen. Máximo Gómez, quien probaría ser aceptable para todos los partidos; una diputación, se reporta, va a Cuba a conferenciar con el gen. Gómez. El despacho de Puerto Plata dice que la situación es crítica y se espera un estallido de un momento a otro; los amigos del gobierno están en armas y listos para la acción para proteger la propiedad y preservar la paz; un débil intento fue hecho de apoderarse del cuerpo del presidente Heureaux por los asesinos Ramón Cáceres, Manuel Cáceres, Horacio Vásquez y Domingo Pichardo, que están en el campo cerca de Moca con sus seguidores; el entierro del presidente Heureaux fue conducido con honores apropiados; el gobernador Pepín ha reunido tropas en Moca, y el gobernador de La Vega tiene 1,000 hombres; el ministro de hacienda ha llegado a Moca con gran prisa; el gobierno toma pasos para la protección de los negocios y las finanzas del país, y espera llevar a cabo la contemplada cancelación de los billetes del banco estatal; en Puerto Plata hay una demanda urgente de que el gobierno envíe una fuerza suficiente a Moca para cazar a los asesinos del presidente.

records.headline: The Register prints the Fort de France assassination dispatch
records.summary_en: The Register prints the Fort de France assassination dispatch headed 'President Assassinated': Gen. Ulysses Heureaux, president of the Dominican republic, was assassinated at Moca, Santo Domingo, at 4:30 o'clock yesterday afternoon; the name of the murderer is Ramon Caceros; he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic pursuit was at once begun, and it is probable that he will soon be captured; Vice-President Gen. records.headline: The Bulletin completes the Fort de France assassination dispatch
records.summary_en: The Bulletin completes the Fort de France assassination dispatch and prints a New York item of July 28: Vice President General Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the president's death, assumed direction of affairs; at present calmness prevails in the republic, and the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services. In the New York item, Señor Don Alejandro Woss y Gil, consul general of the Dominican republic, when seen at his home, could scarcely credit the news of the assassination of his president, Señor Ulysses Heureaux; he said: 'President Heureaux did wonders to make our people happy and give us prosperity. He was serving his second term, and in a year would have finished. He was formerly minister of the interior, and also served as secretary of war. Moca is a town three days' ride by horse from Santo Domingo.'
records.summary_es: El Bulletin completa el despacho de Fort-de-France sobre el asesinato y publica una nota de Nueva York del 28 de julio: el vicepresidente general Wenceslao Figuereo, inmediatamente después del anuncio de la muerte del presidente, asumió la dirección de los asuntos; en la actualidad prevalece la calma en la república, y los restos del presidente Heureaux probablemente serán llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres. En la nota de Nueva York, el señor don Alejandro Woss y Gil, cónsul general de la república dominicana, al ser visitado en su casa, apenas podía creer la noticia del asesinato de su presidente, el señor Ulises Heureaux; dijo: «El presidente Heureaux hizo maravillas para hacer feliz a nuestro pueblo y darnos prosperidad. Cumplía su segundo período, y en un año habría terminado. Fue anteriormente ministro del Interior, y también se desempeñó como secretario de Guerra. Moca es un pueblo a tres días a caballo desde Santo Domingo».

records.headline: The Republican prints the warship-orders item from Washington of July 31:
records.summary_en: The Republican prints the warship-orders item from Washington of July 31: Secretary of the Navy Long has issued orders detaching the cruiser New Orleans from the North Atlantic squadron at Newport and directing her to proceed at once to Santo Domingo city; orders were issued also to the Machias, now at St. Thomas, to proceed to the same point by way of San Juan; these orders were made at the instance of the State Department, and as a precautionary measure, owing to the disturbed conditions following the assassination of President Heureaux of Santo Domingo; the item is headed 'Warships for Santo Domingo.'
records.summary_es: El Republican publica la nota de Washington del 31 de julio sobre las órdenes a los buques de guerra: el secretario de la Marina, Long, ha emitido órdenes que separan al crucero New Orleans de la escuadra del Atlántico Norte en Newport y le ordenan dirigirse de inmediato a la ciudad de Santo Domingo; también se emitieron órdenes para el Machias, ahora en Santo Tomás, de dirigirse al mismo punto vía San Juan; estas órdenes fueron emitidas a solicitud del Departamento de Estado y como medida de precaución, debido a las condiciones perturbadas tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux de Santo Domingo; la nota lleva por título «Warships for Santo Domingo».

ary measure, owing to the disturbed

of President Heureaux of Santo Do

records.headline: The Republican prints a Cape Haytien dispatch of July 31 and a Washington item of July 29:
records.summary_en: The Republican prints a Cape Haytien dispatch of July 31 and a Washington item of July 29: advices just received from the Dominican frontier say the insurgents have cut the telegraph wires in the vicinity of Santiago de los Caballeros, and also near Moca; the insurgents in the western part of Santo Domingo await the arrival of Jiminez, under whose leadership they expect to attack Santiago. In the Washington item, Secretary Long has ordered the cruiser New Orleans, now at Newport, and the gunboat Machias, at St. Thomas, to proceed at once to San Domingo; this action is due entirely to a desire to be forehanded in case of possible disturbances. The dispatch is headed 'Insurrection at Santo Domingo Believed to Be at Hand,' and the item 'Gunboat to San Domingo.'
records.summary_es: El Republican publica un despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 31 de julio y una nota de Washington del 29 de julio: noticias recién recibidas desde la frontera dominicana dicen que los insurrectos han cortado los cables telegráficos en las inmediaciones de Santiago de los Caballeros, y también cerca de Moca; los insurrectos de la parte occidental de Santo Domingo aguardan la llegada de Jiménez, bajo cuyo mando esperan atacar Santiago. En la nota de Washington, el secretario Long ha ordenado al crucero New Orleans, ahora en Newport, y a la cañonera Machias, en Santo Tomás, dirigirse de inmediato a San Domingo; esta acción se debe enteramente al deseo de estar preparados ante posibles disturbios. El despacho lleva por título «Insurrection at Santo Domingo Believed to Be at Hand», y la nota, «Gunboat to San Domingo».

records.headline: The Press completes the assassination dispatch, prints a Washington item of July 27
records.summary_en: The Press completes the assassination dispatch, prints a Washington item of July 27 headed 'Not Officially Notified,' and opens a sketch headed 'Heureaux's Career': the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services. The Washington item says no information was received up to half past nine o'clock Wednesday night from the consular representatives of the United States in Santo Domingo regarding the assassination there Wednesday of President Heureaux; pending official advices of the assassination, no formal action will be taken by this government; Hon. William F. Powell, the minister to Hayti, is also chargé d'affaires to Santo Domingo, and this government is directly represented in the republic in the person of Campbell L. Maxwell, who is consul general, and John A. Read, who is vice consul; officials here recall that attempts have been made heretofore on the life of Mr. Heureaux. The sketch says Ulysses Heureaux, the late president of Santo Domingo, was born about 1838; little is known of his early life except that he was a power in the politics of the little West Indian republic when he was a young man; his first real prominence was attained during the war with the Spaniards in 1866, when he commanded the Santo Domingo army; after the cessation of hostilities he became very prominent in politics; he held several positions of trust and honor, and finally was elected president; he served one term; he was again placed in the presidential chair, and has been elected continuously ever since; Heureaux faced dozens of revolutions during his long period of office holding, but he always came out victorious.

records.headline: The Republican prints the Grullon statement issued at New York
records.summary_en: The Republican prints the Grullon statement issued at New York, headed 'The Assassination of Heureaux': Adrianno Grullon, of Huttlinger Vivié, New York, the representative in the United States of the San Domingo revolutionists, and formerly the business partner of Señor Jiminez, leader of the insurrection, Tuesday night made public at New York a statement, which in part is as follows: 'The assassination of President Heureaux was not an act of revenge for the murder of Caceres's father, but the signal for the commencement of the uprising against the existing government there. Caceres is the cousin of Gen. Horacio Vasquez, and was with him at the time of the shooting. Gen. Vasquez is a member of one of the best families of Moca. Neither Mr. Caceres nor Gen. Vasquez can be considered common assassins, as their motives were not personal, but patriotic. They attacked the president in broad daylight, in an open space, and not from ambush, although their little party was outnumbered two to one by the president and his body guard. For 14 years Heureaux has held power by a system of terrorizing: citizens were sent to prison without the slightest process of law, and more than 300 were clandestinely shot, without any trial whatever or without even being given a reason for their incarceration. There has been no legal election of any kind since 1889, and then Heureaux retained power through a fraudulent count.'
records.summary_es: El Republican publica la declaración de Grullón emitida en Nueva York, titulada «The Assassination of Heureaux»: Adriano Grullón, de Huttlinger Vivié, Nueva York, representante en los Estados Unidos de los revolucionarios de San Domingo y antiguo socio comercial del señor Jiménez, líder de la insurrección, hizo pública el martes por la noche en Nueva York una declaración, que en parte dice lo siguiente: «El asesinato del presidente Heureaux no fue un acto de venganza por el asesinato del padre de Cáceres, sino la señal para el comienzo del levantamiento contra el gobierno existente allí. Cáceres es primo del general Horacio Vásquez y estaba con él en el momento del tiroteo. El general Vásquez es miembro de una de las mejores familias de Moca. Ni el señor Cáceres ni el general Vásquez pueden ser considerados asesinos comunes, pues sus motivos no fueron personales, sino patrióticos. Atacaron al presidente a plena luz del día, en un espacio abierto y no desde una emboscada, aunque su pequeño grupo era superado dos a uno por el presidente y su guardia. Durante 14 años Heureaux ha mantenido el poder mediante un sistema de terror: ciudadanos fueron enviados a prisión sin el menor proceso legal, y más de 300 fueron fusilados clandestinamente, sin juicio alguno ni siquiera una razón para su encarcelamiento. No ha habido elección legal de ninguna clase desde 1889, y entonces Heureaux retuvo el poder mediante un conteo fraudulento».

records.headline: The Chronicle prints the funeral dispatch from Fort de France
records.summary_en: The Chronicle prints the funeral dispatch from Fort de France on the burial of President Heureaux, under the heads 'Murdered President Buried' and 'Revolution Threatened on Island of Santo Domingo': advices from Fort de France, Martinique, state that the funeral services over the remains of President Heureaux, which took place at Santiago de las Caballeros at 5 o'clock Thursday evening, were attended by a large number of people and were conducted with great solemnity; the body, which had lain in state throughout the day, was buried in the cathedral; the governor of the province superintended the public mourning; throughout the island cannon were fired hourly, and flags were placed at half mast on all public buildings; the government has issued a decree ordering a period of national mourning for nine days; the city of Santo Domingo is in a state of great unrest and business is entirely suspended, and the people fear an outbreak; Thursday night a band of armed men attacked Moca, where President Heureaux was killed, and fired a number of shots; it is reported that the forces supporting the assassin have been augmented considerably; the government has taken measures to put down the threatened insurrection; William F. Powell, United States minister to Hayti and American diplomatic representative to the republic of Santo Domingo, sent a telegram to Vice President Figuereo, who assumed the presidency, expressing the keen regret of the United States government at the assassination of President Heureaux; and the latest news from Santo Domingo is that all is quiet.
records.summary_es: El Chronicle publica el despacho fúnebre desde Fort-de-France sobre el entierro del presidente Heureaux, bajo los títulos «Murdered President Buried» y «Revolution Threatened on Island of Santo Domingo»: noticias procedentes de Fort-de-France, Martinica, afirman que los servicios fúnebres por los restos del presidente Heureaux, celebrados en Santiago de los Caballeros a las cinco de la tarde del jueves, contaron con la asistencia de gran número de personas y se realizaron con gran solemnidad; el cuerpo, que había estado expuesto todo el día, fue enterrado en la catedral; el gobernador de la provincia supervisó el duelo público; en toda la isla se dispararon cañones cada hora y las banderas se colocaron a media asta en todos los edificios públicos; el gobierno ha emitido un decreto que ordena un período de luto nacional de nueve días; la ciudad de Santo Domingo se encuentra en un estado de gran agitación y los negocios están totalmente suspendidos, y el pueblo teme un estallido; el jueves por la noche una banda de hombres armados atacó Moca, donde fue asesinado el presidente Heureaux, y disparó numerosos tiros; se informa que las fuerzas que apoyan al asesino han aumentado considerablemente; el gobierno ha tomado medidas para sofocar la insurrección amenazante; William F. Powell, ministro de los Estados Unidos en Haití y representante diplomático estadounidense ante la república de Santo Domingo, envió un telegrama al vicepresidente Figuereo, que asumió la presidencia, expresando la profunda pena del gobierno de los Estados Unidos por el asesinato del presidente Heureaux; y las últimas noticias de Santo Domingo son que todo está en calma.

records.headline: The Bee prints an editorial on Santo Domingo: the Dominican republic
records.summary_en: The Bee prints an editorial on Santo Domingo: the Dominican republic has very little in common with the United States; its population of about 600,000 people is composed of a mixed race of Spanish, Indian and African descent; its government is nominally republican, but its late president, who has just fallen by the hand of an assassin, was in reality a cruel tyrant, who scrupled at nothing to rid himself of political rivals; a country so governed, with frequent attempts at revolution, with financial affairs in a low condition, and with a population entirely alien to American institutions and ideas — what greater folly would there be than to annex Santo Domingo to the United States? We certainly do not want the Dominican republic upon our hands.

records.headline: A Puerto Plata dispatch dated August 1 calls the situation in Santo Domingo critical after President Heureaux's
records.summary_en: A Puerto Plata dispatch dated August 1 calls the situation in Santo Domingo critical after President Heureaux's assassination, with an outbreak expected at any moment and friends of the government under arms to protect property and preserve the peace. It says the assassins, Ramón Cáceres, Manuel Cáceres, Horacio Vásquez and Domingo Pichardo, were in the country about Moca with their followers, that the president was buried with military honors, and that troops were being assembled at Moca and La Vega.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Puerto Plata fechado el 1 de agosto califica de crítica la situación en Santo Domingo tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux, con un estallido esperado en cualquier momento y los amigos del gobierno en armas para proteger la propiedad y preservar la paz. Dice que los asesinos, Ramón Cáceres, Manuel Cáceres, Horacio Vásquez y Domingo Pichardo, estaban en el campo cerca de Moca con sus seguidores, que el presidente fue enterrado con honores militares, y que se estaban reuniendo tropas en Moca y La Vega.

A private cable dispatch received at Kingston, Jamaica, on August 1 says the revolution in San Domingo is progressing favorably, that Heureaux's body was held and buried at Santiago because the country between Santiago and Puerto Plata is occupied by insurgents who are concentrating to attack the feebly garrisoned Puerto Plata, and that if the revolution succeeds Jiminez and his fellow leader will likely retire and offer the presidency to General Maximo Gomez.

records.summary_en: The Journal completes the Kingston dispatch, prints the Gleaner's comment on American intervention, and prints a Cape Haytien dispatch of August 3: the insurgents not possessing the means of prosecuting a protracted conflict, the premature departure of President Heureaux threatened to frustrate this scheme, whereupon an enthusiast, who was watching the President's movements, committed the act; a subsequent attack on Moca being repulsed, the insurgents withdrew into the fastnesses between Moca and Porto Plata, hoping to secure sufficient accessions of men and arms to attack Porto Plata and prosecute the movement in spite of its initial failure. Commenting on a London cablegram relative to possible American intervention in Santo Domingo, the Gleaner, under the head 'Would Curb America's Ambition,' to-day says it anticipates the 'finding of an excuse to add the island of Hayti to the string of Antillian gems on the new colonial diadem,' and invokes the powers to 'curb America's ambition.' records.headline: The Tribune prints the close of a dispatch on the revolution
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints the close of a dispatch on the revolution in Santo Domingo and a Kingston item of August 3 headed 'Meant to Capture Heureaux': later advices from the Dominican Republic indicate that the revolution is growing in strength; at Santiago de la Cruz five hundred well armed men have risen under the command of General Ramon Pacheco, and General P. Reyes, who is very influential in certain districts, has joined the insurgents with several other generals, each commanding fairly important forces. The Kingston item says that, owing to the efforts of the Government of Santo Domingo to suppress news and information about the recent assassination of President Heureaux and the reported revolution in Santo Domingo, the facts in the case are difficult to obtain; but a dispatch received by a messenger who has passed through Hayti indicates that the assassination of President Heureaux was not on the programme, the purpose of the revolutionists being to capture Moca, with the President, thus decapitating the Dominican Government at the first blow, the insurgents not possessing the means of prosecuting a protracted conflict; the premature departure of President Heureaux threatened to frustrate this scheme, whereupon an enthusiast, who was watching the President's movements, committed the act; a subsequent attack on Moca being repulsed, the insurgents withdrew into the fastnesses between Moca and Porto Plata, hoping to secure sufficient accessions of men and arms to attack Porto Plata and prosecute the movement, in spite of its initial failure.

records.summary_en: The Expositor completes a Puerto Plata dispatch on the critical situation in Santo Domingo: the situation is critical and an outbreak is expected at any time; the friends of the government are under arms and ready for action to protect property and preserve peace; a feeble attempt was made to seize the body of President Heureaux by the assassins Ramon Caceres, Manuel Caceres, Horacio Vasquez and Domingo Pichardo, who are in the country about Moca with their followers; Gov. Pepin has assembled troops in Moca, and the governor of La Vega Real has 1,000 men; the government is taking steps for the protection of business and the finance of the country, and expects to carry out the contemplated cancellation of the state bank notes; in Puerto Plata there is an urgent demand that the government send a sufficient force to Moca to hunt down the assassins of the president.

records.headline: The Union prints a Cape Haytien dispatch of July 28 with the details of the murder:
records.summary_en: The Union prints a Cape Haytien dispatch of July 28 with the details of the murder: General Ulysses Heureaux, president of the Dominican republic, was killed by an assassin at Moca, Santo Domingo, at half past 4 o'clock yesterday afternoon; the name of the murderer is Ramon Caceros, and he succeeded in escaping. Details of the murder received here are to the effect that the president was assassinated as he was about to leave on horseback for Santiago de las Caballeros; the assassin, Ramon Caceros, surrounded by several accomplices, approached the president as he was talking with some friends and fired twice with a revolver; the first bullet struck the president in the left side and penetrated the heart, causing instant death; the second bullet killed an old man who was standing near the president; the assassin and his accomplices then fled to avoid the shots fired at them by the president's friends; it is not known whether any of them was wounded; the body of the president was taken to the palace of the governor of Moca; President Heureaux's death has caused a panic; it is said that Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of last year, is a candidate for the presidency; Jiminez landed from the Fanita, but was driven off with the loss of most of his band of ten men; the dispatch is headed 'Revenge on a President.'

records.summary_en: A report on President Heureaux's assassination at Moca says his death caused a panic, that Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of the previous year, is a candidate for the presidency, and that General Maximo Gomez is also reported to aspire to it. It notes that the father of Caceres, the assassin, was put to death by order of Heureaux in 1884, that Vice President Wenceslao Figuereo at once assumed the direction of affairs, and that President McKinley sent Figuereo a cable of condolences in the name of the American people.

He used to boast that he was a more absolute ruler than any czar or emperor in the world. His ability and shrewdness made a great impression on Europeans and Americans who met him. His daring was remarkable and his shrewdness was said to be equal to that of the most experienced European diplomats. The president was frequently reported assassinated. He had numerous enemies. As a political mystifier he had great talent and boldness. He himself caused reports to be circulated that he had been seized by revolutionists, imprisoned and subsequently shot. records.headline: The Call prints the closing words of a dispatch on the revolution
records.summary_en: The Call prints the closing words of a dispatch on the revolution in Santo Domingo — 'has joined the insurgents with several other generals, each commanding fairly important forces' — a Havana interview of August 3 with Juan Isidro Jiminez, and a Washington item of August 3: in conversation with a Herald correspondent to-day, Juan Isidro Jiminez, candidate for the dictatorship of San Domingo, said: 'For the last few years I have been working against President Heureaux. I have worked among foreign powers, I have landed filibustering expeditions, and at last my plans are successful. records.headline: The Transcript prints the statement of Señor Adriano Grullon
records.summary_en: The Transcript prints the statement of Señor Adriano Grullon, of the firm of Huttlinger Vivié, New York, headed 'Not an Act of Revenge': Señor Grullon, the representative in the United States of the Santo Domingo revolutionists and formerly the business partner of Señor Jiminez, the leader of the insurrection, has made public the following statement of the reasons for the recent assassination of President Heureaux: 'The assassination of President Heureaux was not an act of revenge for the murder of Caceres' father, but the signal for the commencement of the uprising against the existing government there. Caceres is a cousin of General Horacio Vasquez and was with him at the time of the shooting. General Vasquez is a member of one of the best families of Moca and was for some years a partner in the house of Cosmo Batile, a firm well known there, and former agents of the Clyde Steamship company. Neither Mr. Caceres nor General Vasquez can be considered common assassins, as their motives were patriotic. They attacked the president in broad daylight and in an open space and not from an ambush of any kind nor even in the dark, although their little party was outnumbered 2 to 1 by the president and his bodyguard. For 14 years Heureaux has held power by a system of tyrannism. Persons were sent to prison without the slightest pretense of law and more than 300 were clandestinely shot.'

records.headline: The Herald completes a Kingston dispatch on the plot against President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Herald completes a Kingston dispatch on the plot against President Heureaux and prints the Gleaner's comment on American intervention: the assassination of President Heureaux was not on the programme, the purpose of the revolutionists being to capture Moca with the president, thus decapitating the Dominican government at the first blow, the insurgents not possessing the means of prosecuting a protracted conflict; the premature departure of President Heureaux threatened to frustrate this scheme, whereupon an enthusiast who was watching the president's movements committed the act; a subsequent attack on Moca being repulsed, the insurgents withdrew into the fastnesses between Moca and Porto Plata, hoping to secure sufficient accessions of arms and ammunition to attack Porto Plata and prosecute the movement in spite of its initial failure. Commenting on a London cablegram relative to possible American intervention in Santo Domingo, the Gleaner to-day says it anticipates the finding of an excuse 'to tie the string of Antillian gems on the new colonial diadem,' and invokes the powers to 'curb America's ambition.'

records.headline: The Leader prints a sketch of the late president, Gen. Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Leader prints a sketch of the late president, Gen. Heureaux, with the story of his life: immediately upon the announcement of the president's death, Vice-President Gen. Wenceslao Figuereo assumed control of the government; several attempts have been made before to take the life of President Heureaux, but they were frustrated — on one occasion, while passing through the arched entrance to the palace between lines of guards, his quick eye caught one of the soldiers, who appeared to lower his rifle in his direction; quickly pulling a revolver he shot the man dead in his tracks, and passed on to his private office, where he gave orders to remove a dead man lying at the main entrance. Gen. Heureaux was born in Porto Plata in 1846 and served in the war against Spain from 1868 to 1874; later he was put at the head of the advanced Dominicans, who sought to improve their country by inducing foreign capital to locate on the island; as he advanced, all the wealthy inhabitants joined his forces, and when he arrived at the gates of the historic city of Santo Domingo he was chosen president of the republic and served his term of four years; at the expiration of every four years an electoral college assembles in the city to vote for a president for the following term, but owing to Gen. Heureaux's popularity and ability he has always been unanimously re-elected, and was serving his fifth term.
records.summary_es: El Leader publica una semblanza del difunto presidente, el general Heureaux, con la historia de su vida: inmediatamente después del anuncio de la muerte del presidente, el vicepresidente, el general Wenceslao Figuereo, asumió el control del gobierno; antes se habían hecho varios intentos de quitar la vida al presidente Heureaux, pero fueron frustrados: en una ocasión, al pasar por la entrada abovedada del palacio entre filas de guardias, su ojo rápido percibió a uno de los soldados, que pareció bajar su fusil en su dirección; sacando rápidamente un revólver, lo mató en el acto y siguió hasta su despacho privado, donde dio órdenes de retirar a un hombre muerto que yacía en la entrada principal. El general Heureaux nació en Puerto Plata en 1846 y sirvió en la guerra contra España de 1868 a 1874; después fue puesto al frente de los dominicanos avanzados, que buscaban mejorar su país atrayendo capital extranjero a la isla; a medida que avanzaba, todos los habitantes acaudalados se unieron a sus fuerzas, y cuando llegó a las puertas de la histórica ciudad de Santo Domingo fue elegido presidente de la república y sirvió su período de cuatro años; al expirar cada cuatro años, un colegio electoral se reúne en la ciudad para votar por un presidente para el período siguiente, pero debido a la popularidad y la capacidad del general Heureaux siempre ha sido reelegido por unanimidad, y servía su quinto período.

records.summary_en: The Gazette prints an editorial on Santo Domingo: the country, it says, is subject to insurrections, and a president there will not be scrupulous about the use of force, since his subjects must have a fear of him to deter them from plots, and if he would retain his power he must often use what in an established republic like ours would be called rigor. Present reports affirm that the assassin of President Heureaux was the son of an offender whom he had put to death over a dozen years ago; the young man's name was Caceros, and he came to our country shortly after his father's death, attended one of our higher literary institutions, but seems to have brooded over his father's death and fostered revenge; he shot his victim as he was preparing to mount his horse, and the whole land is convulsed. The population is about six hundred thousand; Vice President Figuereo assumes control of public affairs, but how long he may have peaceable supremacy is uncertain; and it is asserted that Gen. Gomez is designing to leave Cuba to see if he can obtain authority in San Domingo. The Dominican republic and Hayti, the editorial says, occupy different parts of the island formerly called by the latter name: Hayti has control of the western part, while San Domingo claims the eastern section; the republic contains not far from twenty thousand square miles of territory, of great fertility, its area about equal to the combined area of New Hampshire and Vermont; it used to produce a great deal of coffee, though of an inferior quality, and it furnishes mahogany.
records.summary_es: La Gazette publica un editorial sobre Santo Domingo: el país, dice, está sujeto a insurrecciones, y un presidente allí no será escrupuloso en el uso de la fuerza, ya que sus súbditos deben temerle para disuadirlos de conspiraciones, y si quiere conservar su poder a menudo debe usar lo que en una república establecida como la nuestra se llamaría rigor. Los informes actuales afirman que el asesino del presidente Heureaux era hijo de un delincuente a quien él había hecho ejecutar hacía más de una docena de años; el joven se llamaba Caceros y vino a nuestro país poco después de la muerte de su padre, asistió a una de nuestras instituciones literarias superiores, pero parece haber rumiado la muerte de su padre y fomentado la venganza; disparó contra su víctima cuando se preparaba a montar su caballo, y todo el país está convulsionado. La población es de unos seiscientos mil habitantes; el vicepresidente Figuereo asume el control de los asuntos públicos, pero es incierto cuánto tiempo podrá mantener la supremacía en paz; y se afirma que el general Gómez se propone salir de Cuba para ver si puede obtener autoridad en San Domingo. La república dominicana y Haití, dice el editorial, ocupan partes diferentes de la isla llamada antiguamente por este último nombre: Haití controla la parte occidental, mientras que San Domingo reclama la sección oriental; la república contiene cerca de veinte mil millas cuadradas de territorio, de gran fertilidad, con una superficie aproximadamente igual a la superficie combinada de New Hampshire y Vermont; antes producía mucho café, aunque de calidad inferior, y suministra caoba.

records.headline: The Capital completes the Washington item on the warship orders
records.summary_en: The Capital completes the Washington item on the warship orders for Santo Domingo and prints an item on the creditors of San Domingo: orders were issued also to the Machias, at St. Thomas, to proceed to Santo Domingo city by way of San Juan; these orders were made at the instance of the State Department, and as a precautionary measure owing to the disturbed conditions following the assassination of President Heureaux of San Domingo. The trouble between the Government of San Domingo and its creditors has reached an acute stage; the creditors, who are almost entirely Americans, have begun to clamor for an American protectorate, which would necessarily be the first step in the direction of annexation; political plots are already shaping themselves; the adherents of Gen. Jiminez seek to put him at the head of affairs, while the friends of Gen. Maximo Gomez are talking of making him the ruler of the republic; and it is said by officers who have recently been in San Domingo that interference by this Government would be welcomed by a large proportion of the inhabitants of the island.
records.summary_es: El Capital completa la nota de Washington sobre las órdenes a los buques de guerra para Santo Domingo y publica una nota sobre los acreedores de San Domingo: también se dieron órdenes al Machias, en Saint Thomas, de dirigirse a la ciudad de Santo Domingo pasando por San Juan; estas órdenes se dieron a instancias del Departamento de Estado, y como medida de precaución debido a las condiciones perturbadas tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux de San Domingo. El problema entre el gobierno de San Domingo y sus acreedores ha llegado a una etapa aguda; los acreedores, que son casi en su totalidad americanos, han comenzado a clamar por un protectorado americano, que necesariamente sería el primer paso en dirección a la anexión; ya se están formando complots políticos; los partidarios del general Jiminez buscan ponerlo al frente de los asuntos, mientras que los amigos del general Máximo Gómez hablan de hacerlo gobernante de la república; y oficiales que han estado recientemente en San Domingo dicen que una intervención de este gobierno sería bien recibida por una gran proporción de los habitantes de la isla.

records.headline: The Capital prints an item headed 'San Domingo Ruler Slain'
records.summary_en: The Capital prints an item headed 'San Domingo Ruler Slain' and the opening of a sketch of President Heureaux: Gen. Ulises Heureaux, president of the Dominican republic, was assassinated at Moca, Santo Domingo, Wednesday afternoon; several attempts formerly have been made to kill him; the murderer, Ramon Caceros, made his escape; and the death of Gen. Heureaux has cast a gloom over the entire Dominican government. Immediately upon the announcement of the president's death, Vice-President Gen. Wenceslao Figuereo assumed control of the government; several attempts have been made before to take the life of President Heureaux, but they were frustrated — on one occasion, while passing through the arched entrance to the palace between lines of guards, his quick eye caught one of the soldiers who appeared to lower his rifle in his direction.
records.summary_es: El Capital publica una nota titulada 'San Domingo Ruler Slain' y el inicio de una semblanza del presidente Heureaux: el general Ulises Heureaux, presidente de la república dominicana, fue asesinado en Moca, Santo Domingo, el miércoles por la tarde; antes se habían hecho varios intentos de matarlo; el asesino, Ramón Caceros, logró escapar; y la muerte del general Heureaux ha sumido en la tristeza a todo el gobierno dominicano. Inmediatamente después del anuncio de la muerte del presidente, el vicepresidente, el general Wenceslao Figuereo, asumió el control del gobierno; antes se habían hecho varios intentos de quitar la vida al presidente Heureaux, pero fueron frustrados: en una ocasión, al pasar por la entrada abovedada del palacio entre filas de guardias, su ojo rápido percibió a uno de los soldados que pareció bajar su fusil en su dirección.

records.headline: President Ulises Heureaux of the Dominican Republic was assassinated at Moca on Wednesday afternoon, after several earlier
records.summary_en: President Ulises Heureaux of the Dominican Republic was assassinated at Moca on Wednesday afternoon, after several earlier attempts on his life, and his murderer, Ramon Caceres, made his escape. Immediately on the announcement of his death, Vice President General Wenceslao Figuereo assumed control of the government, and the paper gives an account of Heureaux's career, from his birth at Puerto Plata and service in the war against Spain to his rise to the presidency.
records.summary_es: El presidente Ulises Heureaux de la República Dominicana fue asesinado en Moca el miércoles por la tarde, tras varios intentos anteriores contra su vida, y su asesino, Ramón Cáceres, logró escapar. Inmediatamente después del anuncio de su muerte, el vicepresidente general Wenceslao Figuereo asumió el control del gobierno, y el periódico ofrece un relato de la carrera de Heureaux, desde su nacimiento en Puerto Plata y su servicio en la guerra contra España hasta su ascenso a la presidencia.

Ramon Pacheco, and Gen. P. Reyes, who is very influential in those districts, has joined the insurgents with several other generals, each commanding fairly important forces. Reyes, muy influyente en esos distritos, se ha unido a los insurgentes junto con varios otros generales, cada uno al mando de fuerzas bastante importantes. MYSTERIOUSLY MURDERED.
CHICAGO, August 3.—George C.
Gallagher, a young plumber, was mys
teriously murdered at his home last
night, while his mother and cousin were
asleep in an adjoining room. The only
clues to the murders are a torn window
netting in Gallagher’s room and a re
volver found in the rear of the house.

records.headline: The Press prints the Fort de France assassination dispatch and a London item of August 1:
records.summary_en: The Press prints the Fort de France assassination dispatch and a London item of August 1: Ulysses Heureaux, president of the Dominican republic, was assassinated at Moca, Santo Domingo, at 4:30 p. m.; the name of the murderer is Ramon Caceros; he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic search was at once begun, and it is probable that he will soon be captured; Vice President Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the president's death, assumed direction of affairs. The London item says the Daily Chronicle's Rome correspondent reports that the newspapers say that in view of possible complications in Central America the Italian squadron has started from Buenos Ayres; there has been an interchange of views between the cabinets of the great powers with reference to the probability of an active war in Santo Domingo and the eventual intervention by the United States. The dispatch is headed 'Assassin's Deed,' and the item 'America Might Intervene.'
records.summary_es: El Press publica el despacho de Fort de France sobre el asesinato y una nota de Londres del 1 de agosto: Ulises Heureaux, presidente de la república dominicana, fue asesinado en Moca, Santo Domingo, a las 4:30 p. m.; el nombre del asesino es Ramón Caceros; logró escapar, pero de inmediato se inició una enérgica búsqueda, y es probable que pronto sea capturado; el vicepresidente Wenceslao Figuereo, inmediatamente después de la muerte del presidente, asumió la dirección de los asuntos. La nota de Londres dice que el corresponsal en Roma del Daily Chronicle informa que los periódicos dicen que, ante posibles complicaciones en Centroamérica, la escuadra italiana ha partido de Buenos Aires; ha habido un intercambio de opiniones entre los gabinetes de las grandes potencias con referencia a la probabilidad de una guerra activa en Santo Domingo y la eventual intervención de los Estados Unidos. El despacho lleva por título 'Assassin's Deed', y la nota 'America Might Intervene'.

records.headline: The Sentinel prints an editorial on the Monroe Doctrine and Santo Domingo:
records.summary_en: The Sentinel prints an editorial on the Monroe Doctrine and Santo Domingo: the doctrine, it is alleged, makes it necessary for us to warn Europe to keep its hands off, since we are the 'paramount power' in this part of the world, and if the revolutionists of the Dominican Republic do not behave themselves the United States alone has the right to restrain them; the doctrine sustained a very severe shock, it argues, when the United States became a 'world power' and established itself in the 'Far East,' but the imperialists maintain that it is our mission to take whatever is desirable in any part of the world, while not recognizing the right of Europe to adopt the same principle on this side of the world. With a reasonable pretext for intervention in Santo Domingo, it is not unlikely that the annexation scheme of President Grant's administration will be revived; we should not gain anything by annexation, the editorial says, and all depends upon the syndicate which has been financing the island: if these gentlemen can exploit Santo Domingo to advantage as an American possession, they may get their imperialist friends in and out of Congress to boom an annexation project.
records.summary_es: El Sentinel publica un editorial sobre la Doctrina Monroe y Santo Domingo: la doctrina, se alega, hace necesario que advirtamos a Europa que mantenga las manos fuera, ya que somos la 'potencia suprema' en esta parte del mundo, y si los revolucionarios de la República Dominicana no se comportan, solo los Estados Unidos tienen el derecho de contenerlos; la doctrina sufrió un golpe muy severo, argumenta, cuando los Estados Unidos se convirtieron en una 'potencia mundial' y se establecieron en el 'Lejano Oriente', pero los imperialistas sostienen que es nuestra misión tomar lo que sea deseable en cualquier parte del mundo, sin reconocer el derecho de Europa a adoptar el mismo principio en este lado del mundo. Con un pretexto razonable para intervenir en Santo Domingo, no es improbable que se reviva el plan de anexión de la administración del presidente Grant; no ganaríamos nada con la anexión, dice el editorial, y todo depende del sindicato que ha estado financiando la isla: si estos caballeros pueden explotar Santo Domingo con ventaja como posesión americana, quizá consigan que sus amigos imperialistas dentro y fuera del Congreso promuevan un proyecto de anexión.

records.headline: The Dispatch prints part of an interview with General Jiminez
records.summary_en: The Dispatch prints part of an interview with General Jiminez and an item headed 'Funeral of Heureaux': 'I did hear,' he continued, 'that Heureaux was sending men to Cuba to kill me, but I knew nothing whatever regarding the plot to kill him. I had no connection with Ramon Caceres, who did the shooting. I do not believe that the United States will interfere with my government in San Domingo, which will be a government peaceful and helpful to all, for the United States did not interfere with the government of Heureaux, who robbed and murdered for fourteen years.' General Jiminez admits that he has often been to the United States incognito, but says he has not had interviews with official persons; he considers that there is no need of promoting expeditions to land in San Domingo, as there are already a thousand men waiting for him, a force which he deems quite sufficient for his purpose; referring to the future relations of San Domingo with the United States, he expressed a desire to be on friendly terms with Washington, and said he believed he could count upon American sympathy; Gomez he referred to as 'esteemed by all classes of Dominicans, but not sought for as President'; and the people of San Domingo, he declares, are impetuous, and are urging him to come to them at once, but for a time he prefers delay, as 'each day is worth a battle won.' The funeral item, from San Domingo, August 4, says solemn funeral services in memory of the late President Heureaux were held in the Cathedral to-day, and the diplomatic and consular bodies were present.
records.summary_es: El Dispatch publica parte de una entrevista con el general Jiminez y una nota titulada 'Funeral of Heureaux': 'Sí oí', continuó, 'que Heureaux enviaba hombres a Cuba para matarme, pero no supe absolutamente nada del complot para matarlo a él. No tuve ninguna relación con Ramón Cáceres, que hizo los disparos. No creo que los Estados Unidos vayan a interferir con mi gobierno en San Domingo, que será un gobierno pacífico y útil para todos, porque los Estados Unidos no interfirieron con el gobierno de Heureaux, que robó y asesinó durante catorce años'. El general Jiminez admite que ha estado a menudo en los Estados Unidos de incógnito, pero dice que no ha tenido entrevistas con personas oficiales; considera que no hay necesidad de promover expediciones para desembarcar en San Domingo, ya que ya hay mil hombres esperándolo, una fuerza que juzga bastante suficiente para su propósito; al referirse a las relaciones futuras de San Domingo con los Estados Unidos, expresó su deseo de mantener relaciones amistosas con Washington y dijo que creía poder contar con la simpatía americana; de Gómez se refirió como 'estimado por todas las clases de dominicanos, pero no buscado como presidente'; y el pueblo de San Domingo, declara, es impetuoso y lo insta a ir junto a ellos de inmediato, pero por un tiempo prefiere la demora, ya que 'cada día vale una batalla ganada'. La nota fúnebre, desde San Domingo, el 4 de agosto, dice que hoy se celebraron en la Catedral solemnes servicios fúnebres en memoria del difunto presidente Heureaux, y que estuvieron presentes los cuerpos diplomático y consular.

records.headline: Fort-de-France dispatch: President Ulises Heureaux of the Dominican Republic was assassinated at Moca at 4:30
records.summary_en: Fort-de-France dispatch: President Ulises Heureaux of the Dominican Republic was assassinated at Moca at 4:30 yesterday afternoon by Ramón Cáceres, who escaped; Vice-President Wenceslao Figuereo has assumed direction of affairs and calm prevails.
records.summary_es: Despacho de Fort-de-France: el presidente Ulises Heureaux de la República Dominicana fue asesinado en Moca a las 4:30 de ayer por la tarde por Ramón Cáceres, que escapó; el vicepresidente Wenceslao Figuereo ha asumido la dirección de los asuntos y reina la calma.
records.passage: The remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services. Washington, July 27. Pending official advices of the assassination of President Heureaux of Santo Domingo no formal action will be taken by this government. Hon. William F. Powell, the minister to Haiti, is also charge d'affaires to Santo Domingo, while this government is directly represented in the republic in the person of [illegible] I. Maxwell, who is consul general and John A. Head, who is vice consul. Officials here recall that attempts have been made heretofore on the life of President Heureux. [illegible] paid a brief tribute to the work of the deceased president, saying he understood that he had given the country a good administration. If the next few days develop any signs of unrest in the islands the United States will send a warship there. The [illegible] Strike. Cleveland, O., July 27. A step in which there is hope of conciliating the street railway company and its striking employes was taken here last night by the committee of the council, which succeeded in settling the first strike a month ago. The committee made a request for a special meeting of the council to-night to discuss the ways and means of putting an end to the present distressing situation. The work of the committee, which is expected to result from the meeting of councilmen, will be primarily to discover if the agreement by which the first strike was ended has been violated, and if so, by whom. records.headline: The murder of Heureaux in detail: shot through the heart as he talked with friends before leaving Moca for Santiago
records.summary_en: The murder of Heureaux in detail: shot through the heart as he talked with friends before leaving Moca for Santiago, the assassin Cáceres escaping under fire; Jiménez, of the June 1898 attempt, is a candidate for the succession, and Máximo Gómez is said to aspire to it.
records.summary_es: El asesinato de Heureaux en detalle: atravesado el corazón de un disparo mientras conversaba con amigos antes de partir de Moca hacia Santiago, con el asesino Cáceres escapando bajo el fuego; Jiménez, del intento de junio de 1898, es candidato a la sucesión, y se dice que Máximo Gómez aspira a ella.
records.passage: physicians have registered since the last meeting, April [illegible]. The report also shows that there have been 237 cases of smallpox within the state since the first of the year. President Heureaux. [illegible] Wenceslao is the officer next in line to President Heureaux, and succeeds to the office of president. Details of the Murder. Cape Haytien, July [illegible]. Details of the murder of President Heureaux of Santo Domingo received here are to the effect that he was assassinated as he was about to leave on horseback for Santiago de Las Caballeros. The assassin, Ramon Caceres, surrounded by several accomplices, approached the president as he was talking with [some?] friends and fired twice with a revolver. The first bullet struck the president in the left side and penetrated the heart, causing instant death. The second bullet killed an old man who was standing near the president. The Assassin Fled. The assassin and his accomplices then fled to avoid the shots fired at them by the president's friends. It is not known whether any of them was wounded. The body of the president was taken to the palace of the government of Moca. It Caused a Panic. President Heureaux's death has caused a panic. It is said that one Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June [illegible], is a candidate for the presidency. It is reported that Gen. Maximo Gomez, formerly president of the Cuban insurrectionists, who is a native of Santo Domingo, also aspires to the presidency. [illegible]

records.headline: The Courant prints the assassination dispatch from Fort de France
records.summary_en: The Courant prints the assassination dispatch from Fort de France and a London item of August 1: Ulysses Heureaux, president of the Dominican republic, was assassinated at Moca, Santo Domingo, at 4:30 p. m.; the name of the murderer is Ramon Caceros; he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic search was at once begun, and it is probable that he will soon be captured; Vice President Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the president's death, assumed direction of affairs. The London item says the Daily Chronicle's Rome correspondent reports that the newspapers say that in view of possible complications in Central America the Italian squadron has started from Buenos Ayres; there has been an interchange of views between the cabinets of the great powers with reference to the probability of an active war in Santo Domingo and the eventual intervention by the United States. The dispatch is headed 'Assassin's Deed,' and the item 'America to Intervene.'
records.summary_es: El Courant publica el despacho del asesinato desde Fort de France y una nota de Londres del 1 de agosto: Ulises Heureaux, presidente de la república dominicana, fue asesinado en Moca, Santo Domingo, a las 4:30 p. m.; el nombre del asesino es Ramón Caceros; logró escapar, pero de inmediato se inició una enérgica búsqueda, y es probable que pronto sea capturado; el vicepresidente Wenceslao Figuereo, inmediatamente después de la muerte del presidente, asumió la dirección de los asuntos. La nota de Londres dice que el corresponsal en Roma del Daily Chronicle informa que los periódicos dicen que, ante posibles complicaciones en Centroamérica, la escuadra italiana ha partido de Buenos Aires; ha habido un intercambio de opiniones entre los gabinetes de las grandes potencias con referencia a la probabilidad de una guerra activa en Santo Domingo y la eventual intervención de los Estados Unidos. El despacho lleva por título 'Assassin's Deed', y la nota 'America to Intervene'.

records.headline: The Sentinel prints an item on Ramon Caceros, the assassin of President Heureaux:

records.newspaper: The Daily Morning Journal and Courier
records.headline: The Journal and Courier prints the closing part of the Jiminez interview:
records.summary_en: The Journal and Courier prints the closing part of the Jiminez interview: he replied that he had not made the statement attributed to him — that he would proceed to the United States to organize an expedition against the existing government of San Domingo; he said that it was quite unnecessary for him to proclaim himself hostile to the present government, as it could not possibly last beyond the 15th of this month. 'I did hear,' he continued, 'that Heureaux was sending men to Cuba to kill me, but I knew nothing whatever regarding the plot to kill him. I had no connection and have no connection with Ramon Caceres, who did the shooting. I do not believe that the United States will interfere with my government in San Domingo, which will be a government peaceful and helpful to all, for the United States did not see fit to interfere with the government of Heureaux.' General Jiminez admits that he has often been to the United States incognito, but says he has not had interviews with official persons; he considers that there is no need of promoting expeditions to land in San Domingo, as already there are a thousand men waiting for him, a force which he deems quite sufficient for his purposes; referring to the future relations of San Domingo with the United States, he expressed a desire to be on friendly terms with Washington and said he believed he could count upon American sympathy; Gomez, he referred to as 'esteemed by all classes of Dominicans, but not sought for as president'; and the people of San Domingo, he declared, are impetuous, and are urging him to come to them at once.
records.summary_es: El Journal and Courier publica la parte final de la entrevista con Jiminez: respondió que no había hecho la declaración que se le atribuía —que se dirigiría a los Estados Unidos para organizar una expedición contra el gobierno existente de San Domingo—; dijo que era bastante innecesario que se declarara hostil al gobierno actual, ya que este no podría durar en modo alguno más allá del 15 de este mes. 'Sí oí', continuó, 'que Heureaux enviaba hombres a Cuba para matarme, pero no supe absolutamente nada del complot para matarlo a él. No tuve ni tengo ninguna relación con Ramón Cáceres, que hizo los disparos. No creo que los Estados Unidos vayan a interferir con mi gobierno en San Domingo, que será un gobierno pacífico y útil para todos, porque los Estados Unidos no consideraron oportuno interferir con el gobierno de Heureaux'. El general Jiminez admite que ha estado a menudo en los Estados Unidos de incógnito, pero dice que no ha tenido entrevistas con personas oficiales; considera que no hay necesidad de promover expediciones para desembarcar en San Domingo, ya que ya hay mil hombres esperándolo, una fuerza que juzga bastante suficiente para sus propósitos; al referirse a las relaciones futuras de San Domingo con los Estados Unidos, expresó su deseo de mantener relaciones amistosas con Washington y dijo que creía poder contar con la simpatía americana; de Gómez se refirió como 'estimado por todas las clases de dominicanos, pero no buscado como presidente'; y el pueblo de San Domingo, declaró, es impetuoso y lo insta a ir junto a ellos de inmediato.

records.headline: The Citizen prints the closing part of a dispatch on the burial of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Citizen prints the closing part of a dispatch on the burial of President Heureaux and the situation at Santiago: the remains are to be buried at Santiago de las Caballeros, and orders for the carrying out of this plan have been given to the governor of Santiago; it is currently reported that this course was decided upon in order to avoid the excitement and manifestations which would be the result of the removal of the remains to the city of Santo Domingo; foreseeing the possibility of disturbances, and in order to be prepared for any emergency, General Pepin, governor of Santiago, has taken important precautionary measures and has decided to demand that arms and ammunition be forwarded to him from Santo Domingo; advices from Santiago report that the situation there is becoming more serious; the governor of Santiago confirms the general opinion that the assassination of President Heureaux was a political crime; it is reported that the assassin's party is gathering forces preparatory to an attack on the government troops; it has been learned that Caceros' companions when President Heureaux was killed were Juan Pichardo and Horacio Vasquez, the latter the brother of a deputy in parliament; a financial crisis having arisen in Santo Domingo, and an insurrection being feared owing to the number of malcontents, President Heureaux went to the north and west of the island to prepare for what might happen, and was about to leave Moca for Santiago de las Caballeros when he was killed. Under the head 'Bullet Straight to the Heart,' the dispatch closes: booted and spurred, ready to mount his horse, he sat under the gallery of a house in the Rue Colon, talking with two friends, at 4:30 in the afternoon.
records.summary_es: El Citizen publica la parte final de un despacho sobre el entierro del presidente Heureaux y la situación en Santiago: los restos serán enterrados en Santiago de los Caballeros, y se han dado órdenes para la ejecución de este plan al gobernador de Santiago; se informa corrientemente que este curso se decidió para evitar la excitación y las manifestaciones que resultarían del traslado de los restos a la ciudad de Santo Domingo; previendo la posibilidad de disturbios, y para estar preparado ante cualquier emergencia, el general Pepín, gobernador de Santiago, ha tomado importantes medidas de precaución y ha decidido exigir que se le envíen armas y municiones desde Santo Domingo; noticias de Santiago informan que la situación allí se está volviendo más grave; el gobernador de Santiago confirma la opinión general de que el asesinato del presidente Heureaux fue un crimen político; se informa que el partido del asesino está reuniendo fuerzas en preparación de un ataque contra las tropas del gobierno; se ha sabido que los compañeros de Caceros cuando fue asesinado el presidente Heureaux fueron Juan Pichardo y Horacio Vásquez, este último hermano de un diputado del parlamento; habiendo surgido una crisis financiera en Santo Domingo, y temiéndose una insurrección por el número de descontentos, el presidente Heureaux fue al norte y al oeste de la isla para prepararse ante lo que pudiera suceder, y estaba a punto de salir de Moca hacia Santiago de los Caballeros cuando fue asesinado. Bajo el título 'Bullet Straight to the Heart', el despacho cierra: con botas y espuelas, listo para montar su caballo, estaba sentado bajo la galería de una casa en la calle Colón, hablando con dos amigos, a las 4:30 de la tarde.

records.headline: The Leader prints a Cape Haytien dispatch on the Dominican revolt
records.summary_en: The Leader prints a Cape Haytien dispatch on the Dominican revolt and a Washington item: an armed insurrection has broken out at La Vega, a town 78 miles northwest of Santo Domingo, in favor of Jiminez, who aspires to the presidency in succession to the late President Heureaux; later advices from the Dominican republic indicate that the revolution is growing in strength; at Santiago de la Cruz well-armed men have risen under the command of General Ramon Pacheco, and General P. Reyes, who is very influential in this district, has joined the insurgents, with several other generals, each commanding fairly important forces. The Washington item says the cruiser New Orleans has arrived at Santo Domingo City, where she was sent to protect American interests in case of an outbreak.
records.summary_es: El Leader publica un despacho de Cabo Haitiano sobre la revuelta dominicana y una nota de Washington: ha estallado una insurrección armada en La Vega, pueblo situado a 78 millas al noroeste de Santo Domingo, a favor de Jiminez, que aspira a la presidencia en sucesión del difunto presidente Heureaux; noticias posteriores de la república dominicana indican que la revolución crece en fuerza; en Santiago de la Cruz se han levantado hombres bien armados bajo el mando del general Ramón Pacheco, y el general P. Reyes, muy influyente en este distrito, se ha unido a los insurgentes, junto con varios otros generales, cada uno al mando de fuerzas bastante importantes. La nota de Washington dice que el crucero New Orleans ha llegado a la ciudad de Santo Domingo, adonde fue enviado para proteger los intereses americanos en caso de un estallido.

records.headline: The Times prints the opening of its feature 'The Character of Santo Domingo's Assassinated Ruler.'
records.summary_en: The Times prints the opening of its feature 'The Character of Santo Domingo's Assassinated Ruler.' From a New York item of August 4: 'Ulisses Heureaux was a peculiar figure in modern history, in many respects,' said a merchant whom long years of travel and trade in the West Indies have enabled to be entertainingly reminiscent, 'not, perhaps, so very different from the average successful politician of the smaller Spanish-creole republics, but still a decided anomaly in this nineteenth century and within such a short distance of a civilization like ours. For years he held his post with a tact and finesse that would have done credit to a finished diplomat; threatening one man, paying hush money to another, alternately disgracing and rewarding friends and enemies alike; securing vast sums for his personal expenditure, and through it all managing somehow to keep the national credit from falling utterly, while he boasted openly, and with that peculiar bonhomie that he sometimes chose to affect, that "no five men in the island could kill him." Three of them did it, however, the other day, but, if the reports are to be believed, not in open fight.'

records.headline: The Times prints the continuation of its feature 'The Character of Santo Domingo's Assassinated Ruler':
records.summary_en: The Times prints the continuation of its feature 'The Character of Santo Domingo's Assassinated Ruler': the merchant says Heureaux was shrewd, crafty, and remorseless if thwarted, and that under his rule human life was held cheaper than he ever believed could be possible; to say that he had friends would hardly be possible, but he had many adherents, for disloyalty meant, sooner or later, death to the transgressor. A friend of his, an English merchant, told him last January that while in conversation with Heureaux the latter had alluded to his own quickness in suppressing crime, instancing a case where, some years before, a man adjudged guilty of burning a sugar cane plantation had been seized, quietly carried across the river from San Domingo City to a place called Pajarito, and there hung to a tree, to remain for three days, a warning to the people at large; the fact that no form of legal trial had been gone through mattered little — the President, as a man of decisive action, had sustained his reputation. The feature adds that Heureaux, born of a Haitian father and a mother who came from St. Thomas, took part in Santo Domingo's early struggles against Spain, and during the war of liberation in 1853-'63 rose to the post of colonel of staff; later he served in the uprisings under Cabral, and held one minor office after another until 1871, when President Merino made him his Minister of the Interior; when Merino's term of office ceased, Heureaux was made President for the then constitutional term of two years, at the close of which he retired to private life.
records.summary_es: El Times publica la continuación de su reportaje 'The Character of Santo Domingo's Assassinated Ruler': el comerciante dice que Heureaux era astuto, artero e implacable si se le contrariaba, y que bajo su gobierno la vida humana se tenía por más barata de lo que él jamás creyó posible; decir que tenía amigos difícilmente sería posible, pero tenía muchos partidarios, porque la deslealtad significaba, tarde o temprano, la muerte para el transgresor. Un amigo suyo, un comerciante inglés, le contó en enero pasado que, mientras conversaba con Heureaux, este aludió a su propia rapidez para suprimir el crimen, citando un caso en el que, algunos años antes, un hombre juzgado culpable de quemar una plantación de caña de azúcar había sido apresado, llevado en silencio al otro lado del río desde la ciudad de San Domingo a un lugar llamado Pajarito, y allí colgado de un árbol, para permanecer durante tres días, como advertencia para el pueblo en general; el hecho de que no se hubiera seguido ninguna forma de juicio legal importaba poco: el presidente, como hombre de acción decisiva, había sostenido su reputación. El reportaje añade que Heureaux, nacido de un padre haitiano y una madre que vino de Saint Thomas, tomó parte en las primeras luchas de Santo Domingo contra España, y durante la guerra de liberación de 1853-'63 ascendió al puesto de coronel de estado mayor; después sirvió en los levantamientos bajo Cabral, y ocupó un cargo menor tras otro hasta 1871, cuando el presidente Merino lo nombró su ministro de lo Interior; cuando cesó el período de Merino, Heureaux fue nombrado presidente por el entonces período constitucional de dos años, al cabo del cual se retiró a la vida privada.

records.headline: The Tribune prints a traveler's narrative of Santo Domingo:
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints a traveler's narrative of Santo Domingo: the city of Santo Domingo, the capital of the republic, was again reached after spending a month in visiting Samana Bay and the north coast, scaling the lofty Cibao range, descending into La Vega Real, where Christopher Columbus had explored, and journeying across the roadless, bridgeless island, swimming rivers or ferrying across them in dugouts, and sleeping nights in hammocks swung between giant mahogany trees in pristine forests. Before departing on this cruise along the coast and starting on an overland ride from the north to Santo Domingo City on the south, the Government furnished letters to the governors of the districts, which everywhere received the most respectful consideration. At the time a rival named Cabral was cruising in Samana Bay on an ancient ferryboat called the Telegrafo, mounting several smooth-bores; the Dominican navy could muster a fleet of four or five one- and two-masted schooners, each carrying an 8-inch Spanish gun of the seventeenth century. The same afternoon Señor Manuel Mona Gautier, Secretary of State, called at the hotel with an invitation to dine with the President, Buenaventura Baez, and the members of his official household, at his own residence, the Palace not being occupied at the time; United States Consul Somers Smith was also a guest.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica la narración de un viajero sobre Santo Domingo: se llegó de nuevo a la ciudad de Santo Domingo, la capital de la república, después de pasar un mes visitando la bahía de Samaná y la costa norte, escalando la elevada cordillera del Cibao, descendiendo a La Vega Real, donde Cristóbal Colón había explorado, y viajando a través de la isla sin caminos ni puentes, cruzando ríos a nado o en canoas, y durmiendo de noche en hamacas colgadas entre gigantescos árboles de caoba en bosques prístinos. Antes de partir en este crucero por la costa e iniciar una cabalgata por tierra desde el norte hasta la ciudad de Santo Domingo, en el sur, el gobierno facilitó cartas para los gobernadores de los distritos, que en todas partes recibieron la más respetuosa consideración. En esa época un rival llamado Cabral navegaba en la bahía de Samaná en un antiguo ferry llamado el Telégrafo, que montaba varios cañones de ánima lisa; la marina dominicana podía reunir una flota de cuatro o cinco goletas de uno y dos mástiles, cada una con un cañón español de 8 pulgadas del siglo diecisiete. Esa misma tarde, el señor Manuel Mona Gautier, secretario de Estado, se presentó en el hotel con una invitación a cenar con el presidente, Buenaventura Báez, y los miembros de su casa oficial, en su propia residencia, ya que el Palacio no estaba ocupado en ese momento; el cónsul de los Estados Unidos, Somers Smith, también fue invitado.

records.summary_en: This retrospective account tells how General Babcock returned with the San Domingo annexation treaty, which President Grant sent to the Senate at once, and how Charles Sumner, chairman of the Committee on Foreign Relations, bitterly opposed it, accusing Baez of being an adventurer held in power by the United States Navy. On June 30, 1870, the treaty failed to receive two-thirds and was rejected, Sumner was removed from his chairmanship, and Baez, when told the result, told the Dominican Congress the measure would nevertheless succeed in the end, while Grant declined to repeat the effort.
records.summary_es: Este recuento retrospectivo narra cómo el general Babcock regresó con el tratado de anexión de Santo Domingo, que el presidente Grant envió de inmediato al Senado, y cómo Charles Sumner, presidente del Comité de Relaciones Exteriores, se opuso amargamente a él, acusando a Báez de ser un aventurero mantenido en el poder por la Marina de los Estados Unidos.
