records.headline: Advices in Foster's Daily Democrat, from Kingston, Jamaica
records.summary_en: Advices in Foster's Daily Democrat, from Kingston, Jamaica, dated August 12, report that a mail dispatch from Santo Domingo confirms cable accounts of the spread and significance of the revolution throughout the Dominican Republic. Prominent civil and military men are taking the field on the understanding that Jiminez is the prime mover and will arrive shortly from Cuba with munitions of war, while Generals Ramon Pacheco and Pablo Reyes are advancing westward by forced marches with armed followers, including regular soldiers, to cut off Monte Christo from reinforcements and unite with insurgent forces from Hayti ahead of the Jiminez expedition. Attributing the movement's popularity to the name of Gomez, the dispatch states that if he declines the presidency or Jiminez finally opposes his election, prominent leaders are considering a plebiscite on renewing the 1871 vote for American annexation or an American protectorate rather than elect another dictator.

records.headline: In an item in the New-York Tribune, Jiminez, described as aspirant
records.summary_en: In an item in the New-York Tribune, Jiminez, described as aspirant to the presidency of the Dominican Republic, denies all knowledge of any expedition of his having been captured off Jamaica and asserts that there are no Dominicans there. Regarding Pedro Lluberas, former Minister of the Interior and Police under the late President Heureaux, Jiminez states that despite Lluberas's claims of friendship he doubts his loyalty and considers him to have a bad record as a member of the Heureaux clique. Jiminez believes Lluberas has gone to San Domingo to try to save the incumbent government, which Jiminez remains confident cannot survive the current month.
records.summary_es: En una nota publicada en el New-York Tribune, Jiminez, descrito como aspirante a la presidencia de la República Dominicana, niega todo conocimiento sobre la captura de expedición alguna suya frente a Jamaica y asegura que allí no hay dominicanos. Respecto a Pedro Lluberas, antiguo ministro de Interior y Policía bajo el difunto presidente Heureaux, Jiminez afirma que, pese a sus muestras de amistad, duda de su lealtad y sostiene que tiene malos antecedentes como integrante de la camarilla de Heureaux. Jiminez cree que Lluberas ha ido a San Domingo para intentar salvar al gobierno actual, el cual Jiminez sigue seguro de que no podrá sobrevivir al presente mes.

A stop of an hour or two will be made in Ogden, and at other towns on the line to give the people a chance to greet the returning heroes. Arriving in Salt Lake City, the boys will march through the principal streets to Liberty Park, where a program will be carried out. The Utah men will leave the Presidio for their homes on the afternoon of August 17, at 3 o'clock. Unless something unexpected happens this program will be carried out to the letter. records.headline: Under the heading "Passes Over San Domingo," The Semi-Weekly Messenger reports
records.summary_en: Under the heading "Passes Over San Domingo," The Semi-Weekly Messenger reports that the West Indian hurricane crossed Porto Plata and appears to have ravaged the north of the Dominican Republic. Because all communication between Porto Plata and the interior, not including San Domingo, is interrupted, no accurate account of the damage can yet be obtained, although it is believed to be substantial. The railroad from Porto Plata to San Domingo is out of operation, and the storm eventually passed over Cape Haytien with reduced violence and correspondingly light damage.
records.summary_es: Bajo el título "Passes Over San Domingo", The Semi-Weekly Messenger informa que el huracán antillano cruzó Porto Plata y parece haber devastado el norte de la República Dominicana. Debido a que toda comunicación entre Porto Plata y el interior, sin incluir a San Domingo, está interrumpida, aún no es posible obtener un recuento exacto de los daños, aunque se cree que son importantes. El ferrocarril de Porto Plata a San Domingo dejó de funcionar y la tormenta pasó finalmente sobre Cape Haytien con menor violencia y daños proporcionalmente leves.

records.headline: The Dominican uprising: two sections of The Houston Daily Post address
records.summary_en: The Dominican uprising: two sections of The Houston Daily Post address it, beginning with a report that the establishment of a Jiminez junta in New York to encourage revolution against the recognized government of Santo Domingo is viewed with little official concern at present, although a sharp watch will be kept over its headquarters to prevent breaches of neutrality. Recalling authorities' efforts against filibustering expeditions during the Cuban insurrection, the item indicates that no special action is expected against Jiminez's friends so long as they commit no unlawful overt acts against the Dominican president recognized by President McKinley. Separately, the paper's foreign news summary states that residents of Puerto Plata, San Domingo, are in wild panic as revolutionists gain ground beyond the government forces' ability to cope with them, and adds that filibustering expeditions are believed to have already left Santiago for San Domingo.
records.summary_es: La insurrección dominicana: dos secciones de The Houston Daily Post la abordan, comenzando con un informe según el cual el establecimiento de una junta de Jiminez en Nueva York para alentar la revolución contra el gobierno reconocido de Santo Domingo se ve por ahora con poca preocupación oficial, aunque se mantendrá una estrecha vigilancia sobre su sede para impedir violaciones de la neutralidad. Al recordar la actuación de las autoridades frente a las expediciones filibusteras durante la insurrección cubana, la nota indica que no se prevé prestar atención especial a los partidarios de Jiminez mientras no violen la ley mediante actos abiertos contra el presidente dominicano reconocido por el presidente McKinley. Por separado, el resumen de noticias extranjeras del diario señala que la población de Puerto Plata, San Domingo, presa de pánico desbordado, ve avanzar a los revolucionarios sin que las fuerzas gubernamentales puedan contenerlos, y añade que se cree que ya han partido expediciones filibusteras desde Santiago rumbo a San Domingo.

records.headline: Reporting on Dominican exiles in New York, the Barre Evening Telegram quotes
records.summary_en: Reporting on Dominican exiles in New York, the Barre Evening Telegram quotes General Moscoso as stating that the revolutionary junta already possesses all the arms and money it needs and that within a few days an expedition will sail secretly from a U.S. port other than New York to join insurgents fighting the existing government of the Dominican Republic. Moscoso expects to lead the expedition into the field alongside the three other junta members, while 21 additional Dominicans in New York have declared themselves ready to go to Santo Domingo and fight. According to Moscoso, every Dominican in New York actively backs the revolution except the Dominican consul there, who is listed as neutral, and local revolutionists in contact with the island expect an important development in Santo Domingo at any moment. Predicting that the government will be overthrown within 30 days unless division among the revolutionists thwarts them, Moscoso condemns the regime as an ignorant despotism resting solely on execution and exile and characterizes Heureaux's successor, Figuero, as nothing more than a good fighter.

records.headline: Tranquillity prevails throughout the Dominican Republic, a Santo Domingo dispatch
records.summary_en: Tranquillity prevails throughout the Dominican Republic, a Santo Domingo dispatch in the Omaha Daily Bee states, according to government officials. The assassins of President Heureaux, reported to number sixteen, remain at large, although steps have been taken to capture them. The dispatch adds that the recent storm inflicted severe damage in the districts around Samana and Puerto Plata, and that the U.S. cruiser New Orleans has departed Santo Domingo for Porto Rico.

records.headline: In an account of Dominican revolutionary preparations in New York
records.summary_en: In an account of Dominican revolutionary preparations in New York, The Evening Times reports that General Moscoso is joined in the junta by Father Charles Philip Morales, a Catholic priest who escaped from Santo Domingo the week President Heureaux was assassinated. Moscoso stated that the junta already holds all necessary arms and funds for a secret expedition expected to sail within a few days from a U.S. port other than New York, led by himself and the three other junta members, while twenty other Dominicans in New York have volunteered to go to Santo Domingo and fight. Every Dominican in New York actively favors the revolution except Consul Woz y Gil, who is listed as neutral, and local revolutionists in contact with the island anticipate a major event in Santo Domingo momentarily. Declaring success certain unless internal divisions intervene, Moscoso remarked that no monarch holds more absolute power than the Dominican president and that Heureaux wielded it tyrannically by exiling and killing his enemies.
records.summary_es: En una crónica sobre los preparativos revolucionarios dominicanos en Nueva York, The Evening Times informa que junto al general Moscoso integra la junta el padre Charles Philip Morales, sacerdote católico que escapó de Santo Domingo la semana en que fue asesinado el presidente Heureaux. Moscoso declaró que la junta ya dispone de todas las armas y fondos necesarios para una expedición secreta que zarpará en pocos días desde un puerto estadounidense distinto de Nueva York, encabezada por él mismo y los otros tres miembros de la junta, mientras que otros veinte dominicanos en Nueva York se han ofrecido para ir a Santo Domingo a combatir. Todos los dominicanos en Nueva York apoyan activamente la revolución salvo el cónsul Woz y Gil, tenido por neutral, y los revolucionarios locales en contacto con la isla aguardan de un momento a otro un acontecimiento importante en Santo Domingo. Tras asegurar el triunfo salvo que surjan divisiones internas, Moscoso afirmó que ningún rey ejerce un poder tan absoluto como el presidente de Santo Domingo y que Heureaux lo empleó como tirano al exiliar y matar a sus enemigos.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported that a Dominican revolutionary junta in New York was coordinating with General Juan Isidro Jimenes in Havana to organize expeditions against the Dominican government. Agents Adriano and Maximiliano Grullon worked to mobilize Dominican diaspora communities in New York, Philadelphia, and Boston to back the insurrection. Meanwhile, officials in Santo Domingo reported general tranquillity, though the sixteen conspirators who killed President Heureaux remained at large and the national economy remained paralyzed by currency difficulties.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó que una junta revolucionaria dominicana en Nueva York se coordinaba con el general Juan Isidro Jimenes en La Habana para organizar expediciones contra el gobierno dominicano. Los agentes Adriano y Maximiliano Grullón trabajaban para movilizar a las comunidades de la diáspora dominicana en Nueva York, Filadelfia y Boston en apoyo a la insurrección. Entretanto, las autoridades en Santo Domingo informaban de una tranquilidad general, aunque los dieciséis conspiradores que mataron al presidente Heureaux seguían prófugos y la economía nacional permanecía paralizada por dificultades monetarias.

There are also some natives of Santo Domingo in Boston and Philadelphia whose interest has been enlisted in the cause. records.headline: Advices from Cape Haitien dated August 15 in The Times report
records.summary_en: Advices from Cape Haitien dated August 15 in The Times report that a defeat of the Jiminez forces in Santo Domingo by government troops under General Escoboza is considered unlikely to end the insurrection. Losses on both sides were reportedly heavy, and government authorities claim the rebels' fight turned into a massacre, while two thousand government soldiers are expected at Monte Cristi and insurgents continue forwarding money, arms, and ammunition. The Dominican warship Independencia visited Cape Haitien that day and reported quiet everywhere, while Haitian authorities barred Generals Candelario de las Rosas and Avido from landing off the German steamer Venetia arriving from St. Thomas.
records.summary_es: Informes fechados en Cabo Haitiano el 15 de agosto en The Times señalan que una derrota sufrida por las fuerzas de Jiminez en Santo Domingo ante las tropas del gobierno al mando del general Escoboza difícilmente pondrá fin a la insurrección. Se informa de cuantiosas bajas en ambos bandos y, según las autoridades gubernamentales, el combate de los rebeldes se convirtió en una masacre, mientras se esperan dos mil soldados del gobierno en Monte Cristi y los insurgentes continúan enviando dinero, armas y municiones. El buque de guerra dominicano Independencia estuvo ese día en Cabo Haitiano y reportó calma en todas partes, en tanto que las autoridades haitianas impidieron el desembarco de los generales Candelario de las Rosas y Avido del vapor alemán Venetia, procedente de St. Thomas.

records.summary_en: Under a headline referring to the Dominican Republic as 'Dominica,' The Beatrice Daily Express prints August 16 dispatches from Havana and New York on revolutionary preparations. From Havana, it reports that the collector of customs at Baracoa seized 143 carbines and 18,000 rounds of ammunition evidently destined for San Domingo, where twenty-five Cubans and Dominicans who arrived at Baracoa on Friday aboard the Mortera are apparently planning to carry arms. A companion New York dispatch states that a San Domingo junta formed there is believed to communicate daily by cable with Jiminez in Havana, where he directs the revolutionary forces, while plans are underway to dispatch expeditions from the West Indies and possibly the United States against the existing Dominican government.

records.summary_en: Two Dominican items appear in The Wheeling Daily Intelligencer. The closing paragraphs of an earlier report note enormous numbers of wounded on both sides in a battle regarded as decisively ending the Jiminez uprising, while adding that the government's plan for gradually withdrawing paper money has restored confidence, short-term bills of exchange on Europe sell at 300 per cent silver, and Dominicans almost unanimously favor using American currency. records.headline: In an interview published by The Times, Father Morales and General Moscoso express
records.summary_en: In an interview published by The Times, Father Morales and General Moscoso express firm Dominican opposition to surrendering national autonomy or accepting U.S. annexation. Moscoso states that while Dominicans admire the United States and wish to adopt American ideas, they do not need American control to achieve stability; once the remnant of Heureaux's misgovernment is swept away, the 400 exiles representing Santo Domingo's education, intelligence, and civilization will return to establish settled rule and lasting peace rather than burden the United States with a 'white elephant.' Both Moscoso and Morales, however, enthusiastically endorse a U.S. protectorate—which Moscoso claims a majority of Dominicans favor—explaining that it would back a civilized established government, by force if necessary, against tyrants like Heureaux while defending Santo Domingo against foreign aggression.
records.summary_es: En una entrevista publicada por The Times, el padre Morales y el general Moscoso expresan la firme oposición dominicana a ceder su autonomía nacional o aceptar la anexión a los Estados Unidos. Moscoso afirma que, aunque los dominicanos admiran a la república estadounidense y desean adoptar sus ideas, no necesitan su dominio para lograr un gobierno estable; tan pronto sea barrido el resto del mal gobierno de Heureaux, los 400 exiliados que representan la educación, la inteligencia y la civilización de Santo Domingo regresarán para instaurar una administración ordenada y una paz duradera en vez de cargar a los Estados Unidos con un «elefante blanco». No obstante, tanto Moscoso como Morales respaldan con entusiasmo un protectorado estadounidense —apoyado, según Moscoso, por la mayoría del pueblo—, explicando que sostendría, incluso por la fuerza, a un gobierno civilizado frente a tiranos como Heureaux y defendería a Santo Domingo de agresiones extranjeras.

records.headline: Writing editorially, the Bridgeton Pioneer rejects as historically
records.summary_en: Writing editorially, the Bridgeton Pioneer rejects as historically unwarranted commentary treating assassination in what critics termed the 'Black Republic' as a routine occurrence. The paper points out that since the Dominican Republic came into existence, two U.S. presidents and one French president have been assassinated, other French chief executives have faced murderous assaults or threats, a Russian czar and an Austrian empress have been murdered, and attempts have been made on the lives of the first German emperor and Queen Victoria of England. Observing that Santo Domingo now mourns a murdered chief of state for the first time, the editorial concludes that other nations should offer sympathy rather than derision.
records.summary_es: En un comentario editorial, el Bridgeton Pioneer rechaza por carecer de fundamento histórico las opiniones que presentaban el magnicidio en la llamada «República Negra» como un suceso cotidiano. El periódico señala que, desde que existe la República Dominicana, han sido asesinados dos presidentes de los Estados Unidos y un presidente de Francia, otros jefes de Estado franceses han sufrido atentados o amenazas de muerte, fueron asesinados un zar ruso y una emperatriz austríaca, y se atentó contra el primer emperador de Alemania y la reina Victoria de Inglaterra. Al destacar que Santo Domingo llora ahora por primera vez a un jefe de Estado asesinado, el editorial concluye que a las demás naciones les corresponde solidarizarse con la pequeña república en vez de vituperarla.

records.headline: A Havana dispatch of August 16 in the New-York Tribune reports
records.summary_en: A Havana dispatch of August 16 in the New-York Tribune reports that General Juan Isidro Jiminez, aspirant to the presidency of San Domingo, will probably depart Havana for the island the following day via a south coast steamer from Batabano, traveling unarmed with two friends. Believing the moment has arrived to place himself at the head of the movement, Jiminez construes a dispatch from a former Dominican interior minister in Santiago urging revolutionists to deny the uprising's success as merely a device to deter Cuban and American adventurers eager to sail for San Domingo, and he likewise dismisses as probably false a telegram received that day reporting a rebel defeat, citing uniformly favorable reports from his own representatives. Jiminez adds that although he wished to leave long ago, he remained in Havana on his friends' advice until his presence was needed at the scene of action, and having cabled his intention, he expects to start the next day unless advised otherwise.
records.summary_es: Un despacho fechado en La Habana el 16 de agosto en el New-York Tribune informa que el general Juan Isidro Jiminez, aspirante a la presidencia de San Domingo, probablemente partirá de La Habana hacia la isla al día siguiente en un vapor de la costa sur desde Batabanó, viajando desarmado en compañía de dos amigos. Convencido de que ha llegado el momento de ponerse al frente del movimiento, Jiminez interpreta un despacho enviado desde Santiago por un exministro dominicano del Interior que instaba a negar la prosperidad de la revuelta tan solo como un medio para frenar a los aventureros cubanos y estadounidenses deseosos de embarcarse hacia San Domingo, y del mismo modo descarta por probablemente falso un telegrama recibido ese día sobre una derrota rebelde, alegando que los informes personales de sus representantes solo hablan de éxitos. Jiminez añade que, aunque deseaba partir desde hacía mucho tiempo, permaneció en La Habana por consejo de sus amigos hasta que su presencia fue necesaria en el teatro de los hechos y, tras cablegrafiar su intención, prevé salir al día siguiente salvo aviso en contrario.

records.headline: Reporting on efforts to overthrow the Dominican government
records.summary_en: Reporting on efforts to overthrow the Dominican government, The Topeka State Journal notes that General Jiminez remains in Havana directing revolutionary forces while arrangements proceed to send expeditions from points in the West Indies and possibly the United States. About 14 months earlier, Jiminez's close friend Adriano Grullon came to New York as representative of the revolutionary party, building ties with local Dominicans as well as natives of Santo Domingo in Boston and Philadelphia, and about a week ago his cousin Maximillian Grullon arrived in New York from Havana on a secret mission from Jiminez. Together with Rev. Father Charles Phillip Morales—brother of the late General Morales, whom President Heureaux had executed a year earlier, and an arrival from Santo Domingo around the first of the month—and longtime New York resident General A. A. Moscoso, Grullon has held several meetings to oversee U.S. work backing Jiminez.
records.summary_es: Al informar sobre los esfuerzos para derrocar al gobierno dominicano, The Topeka State Journal señala que el general Jiminez permanece en La Habana dirigiendo las fuerzas revolucionarias mientras avanzan los preparativos para enviar expediciones desde puntos de las Antillas y posiblemente desde los Estados Unidos. Unos 14 meses antes, Adriano Grullon, amigo íntimo de Jiminez, llegó a Nueva York como representante del partido revolucionario, estrechando vínculos con los dominicanos locales así como con nativos de Santo Domingo en Boston y Filadelfia, y hace alrededor de una semana su primo Maximillian Grullon arribó a Nueva York desde La Habana en misión secreta de Jiminez. Junto con el reverendo padre Charles Phillip Morales —hermano del difunto general Morales, ejecutado por orden del presidente Heureaux un año atrás, y llegado de Santo Domingo hacia el primero del mes en curso— y el general A. A. Moscoso, residente en Nueva York desde hace varios años, Grullon ha sostenido varias reuniones para dirigir en los Estados Unidos las labores en apoyo de Jiminez.

records.summary_en: According to the Waterbury Evening Democrat, Dominican presidential aspirant Isidro Jimenez will probably leave Havana for Santo Domingo that day aboard a south coast steamer from Batabano, accompanied by two friends and unarmed. Judging the time ripe to take personal command of his movement, he interprets a dispatch sent from Santiago by former Dominican interior minister Pedro Lluberas—urging revolutionists to deny the movement's prosperity—as merely a measure to hold back Cuban and American adventurers eager to sail for Santo Domingo. On the same basis, Jimenez dismisses as probably false a telegram received the previous day reporting the revolutionary forces' defeat, stating that his own representatives report only successes and that having remained in Havana only on his friends' counsel, his presence is now required at the scene of action.
records.summary_es: Según el Waterbury Evening Democrat, el aspirante a la presidencia dominicana Isidro Jimenez probablemente saldrá ese día de La Habana rumbo a Santo Domingo en un vapor de la costa sur desde Batabanó, acompañado por dos amigos y desarmado. Al considerar llegado el momento de ponerse al frente de su movimiento, interpreta un despacho enviado desde Santiago por el exministro dominicano del Interior Pedro Lluberas —en el que instaba a los revolucionarios a negar la prosperidad de la causa— tan solo como un recurso para contener a los aventureros cubanos y estadounidenses ansiosos por embarcarse hacia Santo Domingo. Con el mismo criterio, Jimenez descarta por probablemente falso un telegrama recibido el día anterior sobre la derrota de las fuerzas revolucionarias, afirmando que sus propios representantes solo comunican éxitos y que, tras haber permanecido en La Habana únicamente por consejo de sus amigos, su presencia es ya necesaria en el lugar de los hechos.

records.headline: An August 12 dispatch from Kingston, Jamaica, in the Gilpin Observer reports
records.summary_en: An August 12 dispatch from Kingston, Jamaica, in the Gilpin Observer reports that letters dated August 3 confirm cable accounts of the revolution's spread across the Dominican Republic, with prominent civil and military figures taking the field in the expectation that Jimenez is the prime mover and will soon arrive from Cuba with war munitions. Generals Ramon Pacheco and Pablo Reyes, leading armed followings that include regular soldiers, are advancing westward by forced marches to cut off Monte Cristi from reinforcements and link up with insurgents from Hayti so as to clear a path for Jimenez's expedition. Attributing the revolt's popularity to the use of the name of Gomez, the dispatch adds that if Gomez declines the presidency or Jimenez opposes his election, prominent leaders are already considering a plebiscite on renewing the 1871 vote for U.S. annexation or an American protectorate rather than electing another dictator.
records.summary_es: Un despacho fechado en Kingston, Jamaica, el 12 de agosto en el Gilpin Observer informa que cartas del 3 de agosto confirman los cables sobre la propagación de la revolución en toda la República Dominicana, donde destacadas figuras civiles y militares han salido a campaña bajo el entendido de que Jimenez es el principal promotor y llegará pronto desde Cuba con pertrechos de guerra. Los generales Ramon Pacheco y Pablo Reyes, al frente de contingentes armados que incluyen soldados regulares, avanzan hacia el oeste mediante marchas forzadas para aislar de refuerzos a Monte Cristi y enlazar con las fuerzas insurgentes procedentes de Haití a fin de abrir paso a la expedición de Jimenez. Tras atribuir la popularidad de la revuelta al uso del nombre de Gomez, el despacho añade que, si este rechaza la presidencia o Jimenez se opone a su elección, importantes dirigentes ya contemplan convocar un plebiscito para renovar la votación de 1871 a favor de la anexión a los Estados Unidos o de un protectorado estadounidense antes que elegir a otro dictador.

records.headline: Commenting editorially, The Columbian remarks that the recent
records.summary_en: Commenting editorially, The Columbian remarks that the recent assassination of President Heureaux of the Dominican Republic and the disputed succession are likely to confront the United States with new problems. Noting allegations that a powerful American syndicate practically controls the country's finances and affairs and that two warships have been ordered to San Domingo to protect American interests, the paper observes ironically that syndicates have been well cared for by the McKinley administration. If seizing the Philippines can be justified, the editorial concludes sarcastically, there is no reason not to take in San Domingo as well, since all territorial syndicates ought to look alike to Mr. McKinley and 'manifest destiny' should not discriminate between friends.
records.summary_es: En un comentario editorial, The Columbian señala que el reciente asesinato del presidente Heureaux de la República Dominicana y la disputada sucesión probablemente plantearán nuevos problemas a los Estados Unidos. Tras recoger versiones de que un poderoso sindicato estadounidense controla prácticamente las finanzas y los asuntos del país y de que se han enviado dos buques de guerra a San Domingo para proteger los intereses estadounidenses, el periódico observa con ironía que el gobierno actual ha cuidado muy bien de los sindicatos. Si puede justificarse la toma de las Filipinas, concluye sarcásticamente el editorial, no hay razón para no incorporar también a San Domingo, pues todos los sindicatos territoriales deberían parecerle iguales al señor McKinley y el «destino manifiesto» no debería discriminar entre amigos.

records.summary_en: In an editorial note, the Freeland Tribune suggests that the recent assassination of President Heureaux of the Dominican Republic and the contested succession are likely to raise new problems for the United States. Citing allegations that a powerful American syndicate holds virtual control over Dominican finances and affairs, alongside the dispatch of two warships to San Domingo to safeguard American interests, the paper remarks pointedly that syndicates have fared very well under the current administration. It adds sarcastically that if seizing the Philippines can be justified, there is no reason not to annex San Domingo too, since Mr. McKinley should treat all territorial syndicates alike and 'manifest destiny' should make no distinction among friends.
records.summary_es: En una nota editorial, el Freeland Tribune señala que el reciente asesinato del presidente Heureaux de la República Dominicana y la disputada sucesión probablemente traerán nuevos problemas a las puertas de los Estados Unidos. Al mencionar versiones de que un poderoso sindicato estadounidense ejerce en la práctica el control de las finanzas y los asuntos dominicanos, junto con el envío de dos buques de guerra a San Domingo para proteger los intereses estadounidenses, el periódico apunta con ironía que la actual administración ha atendido muy bien a los sindicatos. Añade con sarcasmo que, si puede justificarse la toma de las Filipinas, no hay motivo para no incorporar también a San Domingo, pues todos los sindicatos territoriales deberían parecerle iguales al señor McKinley y el «destino manifiesto» no debería hacer distinciones entre amigos.

records.headline: Two brief dispatches in The San Juan Islander report on fighting
records.summary_en: Two brief dispatches in The San Juan Islander report on fighting along the Haitian-Dominican frontier. According to the first item, revolutionary Dominican troops assembled at Munaminthe crossed the border and occupied Dajabon, prompting the garrison to withdraw to the commanding position of Fort Belair and the foreign residents and Haytian consul to leave the town, while the Haytian government is taking active steps to prevent Jiminez from landing on its territory. A second dispatch from Fort de France, Martinique, dated August 10 notes that although news from the Dominican Republic is difficult to obtain, exiled Dominicans gathered at Munaminthe, Hayti, are reported to have crossed the Santo Domingo frontier and captured Dajabon.
records.summary_es: Dos breves despachos en The San Juan Islander informan sobre las operaciones en la frontera dominico-haitiana. Según la primera nota, tropas revolucionarias dominicanas concentradas en Munaminthe cruzaron la línea fronteriza y ocuparon Dajabon, lo que llevó a la guarnición a replegarse hacia la posición estratégica de Fort Belair y a la población extranjera y al cónsul haitiano a abandonar la localidad, mientras el gobierno de Haití adopta medidas activas para impedir que Jiminez desembarque en su territorio. Un segundo despacho fechado en Fort-de-France, Martinica, el 10 de agosto señala que, aunque resulta muy difícil obtener noticias sobre lo que ocurre en la República Dominicana, se informa que dominicanos exiliados reunidos en Munaminthe, Haití, cruzaron la frontera de Santo Domingo y tomaron Dajabon.

records.headline: The Springfield Weekly Republican, accompanying a map drawn
records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican, accompanying a map drawn at about 60 miles to an inch, distinguishes the two republics sharing the island: French-speaking Hayti in the west, occupying slightly less than a third of the territory after French settlement from 1665, colony-wide prosperity until 1790, proclaimed independence in 1800, and the expulsion of the French in 1803; and Spanish-speaking San Domingo in the east. According to the paper's historical sketch, San Domingo threw off Spanish rule in 1821, was governed under the Haytian republic from 1803 to 1806 and again from 1822 to 1844, expelled a temporary Spanish occupation lasting from 1863 to 1865, and voted nearly unanimously in 1871 for U.S. annexation, which was declined. Alongside Haytian coastal towns, the article identifies the southern port city of San Domingo as the Dominican capital, together with Samana on the east coast and Santiago de Los Caballeros in the northern interior, before breaking off as it begins discussing the current presidential contest.
records.summary_es: El Springfield Weekly Republican, junto a un mapa trazado a una escala aproximada de 60 millas por pulgada, distingue las dos repúblicas que comparten la isla: Haití en el oeste, de habla francesa criolla, que ocupa algo menos de un tercio del territorio tras el asentamiento francés desde 1665, el auge colonial hasta 1790, la proclamación de independencia en 1800 y la expulsión de los franceses en 1803; y San Domingo en el este, de lengua española. Según el resumen histórico del periódico, San Domingo se libró del dominio español en 1821, estuvo bajo la república haitiana de 1803 a 1806 y nuevamente de 1822 a 1844, expulsó una ocupación española temporal entre 1863 y 1865, y votó casi por unanimidad en 1871 a favor de su anexión a los Estados Unidos, solicitud que no fue aceptada. Además de los puertos haitianos, el artículo señala a la ciudad sureña de San Domingo como capital dominicana, junto con Samaná en la costa oriental y Santiago de Los Caballeros en el interior norte, antes de cortarse cuando empieza a abordar la contienda presidencial del momento.

records.headline: Reporting on Jiminez's movements, the Omaha Daily Bee notes
records.summary_en: Reporting on Jiminez's movements, the Omaha Daily Bee notes that after receiving dispatches from friends in Santo Domingo, he departed unarmed accompanied by two friends to meet a private yacht placed at his disposal at or off Santiago, declining to name the vessel's owner. In an August 17 Havana dispatch, Jiminez is quoted as claiming that he will bring what the text calls 'all the islands of Santo Domingo' under a single strong administration to the benefit of all parties, asserting that plenty of honest, competent men are available for public office and that conditions in neighboring Hayti—which he describes as bordering on revolution—favor the plan. His son is remaining in Havana to wind up his affairs and expects to join his father shortly should the Santo Domingo venture succeed.
records.summary_es: Al informar sobre los movimientos de Jiminez, el Omaha Daily Bee señala que, tras recibir despachos de amigos en Santo Domingo, partió desarmado en compañía de dos amigos para abordar en Santiago o frente a sus costas un yate privado puesto a su disposición, cuyo propietario se negó a revelar. En un despacho de La Habana del 17 de agosto, se cita a Jiminez afirmando que reunirá bajo un solo gobierno fuerte lo que el texto denomina «todas las islas de Santo Domingo» en beneficio de todas las partes, asegurando que abundan hombres honestos y competentes para ocupar los cargos y que la situación en el vecino Haití —país que describe al borde de una revolución— favorece esa idea. Su hijo permanece en La Habana para liquidar sus asuntos y prevé reunirse pronto con su padre si este triunfa en Santo Domingo.

records.headline: In an editorial comment signed "DEM.," the Washington Standard warns
records.summary_en: In an editorial comment signed "DEM.," the Washington Standard warns that the recent assassination of President Heureaux of the Dominican Republic and the disputed succession there are likely to bring new problems to the United States. Noting allegations that a powerful American syndicate practically controls the country's finances and affairs, the item reports that two warships have been ordered to San Domingo to protect American interests. The writer remarks ironically that syndicates have been well cared for by the present Administration and argues that if the seizure of the Philippines can be justified, there is no reason not to take in San Domingo as well, since all territorial syndicates should look alike to Mr. McKinley and "manifest destiny" ought not to discriminate among friends.
records.summary_es: En un comentario editorial firmado «DEM.», el Washington Standard advierte que el reciente asesinato del presidente Heureaux de la República Dominicana y la disputada sucesión en ese país probablemente traerán nuevos problemas a los Estados Unidos. Tras señalar versiones de que un poderoso sindicato estadounidense controla en la práctica las finanzas y los asuntos del país, la nota informa que dos buques de guerra han recibido órdenes de dirigirse a San Domingo para proteger los intereses estadounidenses. El autor observa con ironía que los sindicatos han sido muy bien atendidos por la actual Administración y sostiene que, si puede justificarse la toma de las Filipinas, no hay razón para no incorporar también a San Domingo, pues todos los sindicatos territoriales deberían parecerle iguales al señor McKinley y el «destino manifiesto» no debería hacer distinciones entre amigos.

records.headline: Reporting from Havana, a dispatch in the New-York Tribune states
records.summary_en: Reporting from Havana, a dispatch in the New-York Tribune states that General Jiminez, after reportedly receiving dispatches from friends in San Domingo, departed unarmed with two companions to meet a private yacht placed at his disposal at or off Santiago, though he declined to name the vessel's owner. According to the dispatch, Jiminez declares that he will place the entire island of San Domingo under a single strong government staffed by honest and competent men, asserting that the situation in neighboring Hayti—described as a country bordering on revolution—favors the plan. His son is remaining in Havana to settle his affairs and plans to join him shortly if the San Domingo expedition succeeds. Although Chief of Police Detectives Colonel Bacallao told General Ludlow shortly before 9 o'clock that evening that Jiminez was still in Havana, an Associated Press correspondent saw him depart by train that morning, and after detectives watched his house until 6 o'clock the "Heraldo" issued an extra announcing that he had gone.

Según el despacho, Jiminez declara que pondrá toda la isla de San Domingo bajo un solo gobierno fuerte integrado por hombres honestos y competentes, afirmando que la situación en el vecino Hayti —descrito como un país al borde de una revolución— favorece dicho proyecto. Su hijo permanece en La Habana para liquidar sus asuntos y piensa reunirse pronto con él si la expedición a San Domingo tiene éxito. Aunque el coronel Bacallao, jefe de detectives de la policía, informó al general Ludlow poco antes de las 9 de esa noche que Jiminez seguía en La Habana, un corresponsal de The Associated Press lo vio partir en tren esa mañana, y después de que dos detectives vigilaran su casa hasta las 6 en punto el «Heraldo» publicó una edición extraordinaria anunciando su salida.

records.headline: The Houston Daily Post, concluding an item on Jiminez's expedition
records.summary_en: The Houston Daily Post, concluding an item on Jiminez's expedition plans, reports that a vessel placed at his disposal will meet him at or off Santiago, that he proposes to place all of Santo Domingo under one strong government—claiming that conditions in neighboring Hayti, a country bordering on revolution, favor the idea—and that his son will join him shortly if his Santo Domingo expedition succeeds. A separate New York dispatch dated August 17, citing a Herald report from Santo Domingo under the headline "Dominican Uprising," states that another invasion from Hayti was attempted on Tuesday, when government forces met and dispersed the insurgents near Monte Cristo after severe fighting and reportedly captured some of them. Because the revolutionary movement lacks organization and has waged only sporadic guerrilla warfare, the government is undismayed; interior reports describe everything as quiet, several leaders have been arrested, and despite lingering discontent the public generally hopes the civil troubles will soon be settled.
records.summary_es: The Houston Daily Post, al concluir una nota sobre los planes expedicionarios de Jiminez, informa que una embarcación puesta a su disposición se reunirá con él en Santiago o frente a esa costa, que se propone poner todo Santo Domingo bajo un solo gobierno fuerte —afirmando que la situación en el vecino Hayti, país al borde de una revolución, favorece la idea— y que su hijo se le unirá pronto si su expedición a Santo Domingo prospera. Un despacho aparte fechado en Nueva York el 17 de agosto, que cita un informe del Herald desde Santo Domingo bajo el titular «Dominican Uprising», señala que el martes se intentó otra invasión desde Hayti, cuando las fuerzas gubernamentales enfrentaron y dispersaron a los insurgentes cerca de Monte Cristo tras recios combates y, según se informa, capturaron a algunos de ellos. Dado que el movimiento revolucionario carece de organización y solo ha librado una guerra de guerrillas esporádica, el gobierno no se muestra alarmado; los informes del interior indican que todo está tranquilo, varios cabecillas han sido arrestados y, pese al descontento persistente, la población espera en general que pronto se resuelvan los disturbios civiles.

records.headline: Opening a feature article on Dominican politics, The Indianapolis Journal states
records.summary_en: Opening a feature article on Dominican politics, The Indianapolis Journal states that General Don Juan Isidro Jiminez claims to be the real leader of the Dominicans, asserts that his agents murdered President Heureaux, and declares that he is going to take possession of the government. Alluding to an earlier episode in which Jiminez allegedly deceived the United States government and nearly drew it unwittingly into his schemes, the paper asks whether the Navy Department has hurriedly dispatched the New Orleans and the Machias southward out of fear that Jiminez will gain the presidency of San Domingo, or whether the administration wishes to see him seated and secure the annexation of San Domingo. Adopting a satirical tone, the writer adds that the island had room for only one "big man" at a time—the late President Heureaux—alongside Jiminez, a wealthy merchant and frequent traveler owning vast island plantations as well as warehouses and commercial branches in New York, Hamburg, and other cities, joking that whenever Jiminez landed the island sagged toward the coast and tilted Heureaux's inland palace forty-five degrees.
records.summary_es: Al iniciar un artículo especial sobre la política dominicana, The Indianapolis Journal señala que el general Don Juan Isidro Jiminez afirma ser el verdadero líder de los dominicanos, asegura que sus agentes asesinaron al presidente Heureaux y declara que va a tomar posesión del gobierno. Aludiendo a un episodio anterior en el que Jiminez supuestamente engañó al gobierno de los Estados Unidos y casi lo involucró sin saberlo en sus planes, el periódico pregunta si el Departamento de Marina ha enviado a toda prisa al New Orleans y al Machias hacia el sur por temor a que Jiminez ocupe la presidencia de San Domingo, o si la administración desea verlo instalado para asegurar la anexión de San Domingo. En tono satírico, el autor añade que en la isla solo cabía un «gran hombre» a la vez —el difunto presidente Heureaux— frente a Jiminez, acaudalado comerciante y gran viajero dueño de inmensas plantaciones en la isla así como de almacenes y sucursales comerciales en Nueva York, Hamburgo y otras ciudades, bromeando que cada vez que Jiminez desembarcaba la isla se hundía hacia la costa e inclinaba cuarenta y cinco grados el palacio interior de Heureaux.

records.headline: Under the subheading "Warning to Jiminez," The Indianapolis Journal presents
records.summary_en: Under the subheading "Warning to Jiminez," The Indianapolis Journal presents a satirical champagne scene in which President Heureaux—after a servant opens a third bottle of champagne with a machete—tells General Don Juan Jiminez that the presidency views his growing popularity and his friendly standing at the custom house with apprehension. Declaring that the island is growing poorer while Jiminez grows richer, Heureaux announces plans to float a multi-million-dollar loan with Americans, rebond the customs of San Domingo as security, and place a foreigner in charge of the customs. Heureaux warns Jiminez to curb his popularity before it proves fatal, boasting that during sixteen years of rule no fewer than 400 gentlemen on the island have been eliminated because of their growing popularity, and adding that Heureaux and Jiminez can remain on the island together only if one of them stays quiet.

Tras declarar que la isla se empobrece mientras Jiminez se enriquece, Heureaux anuncia planes de colocar un empréstito de muchos millones de dólares con los estadounidenses, volver a comprometer las aduanas de San Domingo como garantía y sentar a un extranjero al frente de las aduanas. records.headline: Continuing its narrative of General Jiminez's earlier expedition
records.summary_en: Continuing its narrative of General Jiminez's earlier expedition, The Indianapolis Journal relates that Jiminez had sent word ahead counseling General Garcia at Monte Christi to have at least a thousand men ready to take arms, attack the forts, slaughter the garrisons, and march on San Domingo city and Heureaux's palace, though that message never reached Garcia. When the vessel arrived off Monte Christi at daybreak and neither Garcia nor the thousand men could be seen on shore, the ship anchored and lowered two boats carrying Jiminez and some eighteen armed fighting men. Upon landing, Jiminez shouted "Viva, San Domingo libre!" and fired the first shot into the air; finding the governor absent from his palace, the party dragged an astonished Garcia from bed by the heels at his home, returned to seize the governor at his palace, and moved toward the fortress at Jiminez's command.

Cuando la embarcación avistó Monte Christi al amanecer y ni Garcia ni los mil hombres aparecieron en la costa, el buque echó anclas y arriaron dos botes con Jiminez y unos dieciocho combatientes armados. records.headline: In a concluding section on Dominican-American friction, The Indianapolis Journal notes
records.summary_en: In a concluding section on Dominican-American friction, The Indianapolis Journal notes that the attempt to overthrow Heureaux occurred two months earlier and states that two weeks ago the Dominican president was stabbed to death in Moca. Recounting the aftermath of Heureaux's earlier failure to put Jiminez behind bars, the paper describes the Dominican president's outrage that a U.S. government vessel flying the Stars and Stripes, loaded with government arms, and officered by Americans had engaged in a filibustering expedition against an island at peace with the United States, while the War Department in Washington fumed that Jiminez had tricked Uncle Sam by diverting an expedition intended for Cuba. Assistant Secretary Meiklejohn telegraphed the leaders of the financial syndicate that had loaned President Heureaux a vast sum secured by the island's customs; after a secret Washington conference produced mutual explanations and closed the incident, the Fanita was later sent to Cuba with her cargo for Gomez.
records.summary_es: En un pasaje final sobre las fricciones domínico-estadounidenses, The Indianapolis Journal señala que el intento de derrocar a Heureaux ocurrió dos meses atrás y afirma que hace dos semanas el presidente dominicano fue muerto a puñaladas en Moca. Al relatar las secuelas del fracaso previo de Heureaux en encarcelar a Jiminez, el diario describe la indignación del mandatario dominicano ante el hecho de que un buque del gobierno estadounidense que enarbolaba la bandera de las barras y las estrellas, cargado con armas oficiales y al mando de oficiales estadounidenses, participara en una expedición filibustera contra una isla en paz con los Estados Unidos, mientras el Departamento de Guerra en Washington rabiaba porque Jiminez había engañado al Tío Sam desviando una expedición destinada a Cuba. El subsecretario Meiklejohn telegrafió a los jefes del sindicato financiero que había prestado al presidente Heureaux una cuantiosa suma garantizada con las aduanas; tras una conferencia secreta en Washington que dio lugar a explicaciones mutuas y cerró el incidente, el Fanita fue enviado posteriormente a Cuba con su cargamento para Gomez.

records.headline: Opening with reaction to Jiminez's arrest, The Beatrice Daily Express reports
records.summary_en: Opening with reaction to Jiminez's arrest, The Beatrice Daily Express reports general sentiment that authorities had no right to arrest him as an unarmed citizen apparently traveling to Santiago de Cuba, and that even if bound for San Domingo he would merely be returning to his native country. Under the headline "Searching for Jiminez," an August 19 dispatch from Kingston cites advices from Santo Domingo stating that the Dominican government is desperately apprehensive of the momentarily expected arrival of revolutionary leader Jiminez, which would sway undecided popular opinion, and has ordered armed vessels patrolling the coast to search every strange ship and capture him under any flag, armed or not. An accompanying August 19 dispatch from Santiago de Cuba adds that American representatives are rapidly recruiting expeditions on the north coast, that Havana ordered the men recently captured at Baracoa held pending investigation, and that although several expeditions have escaped without interference, General Leonard Wood is determined to enforce neutrality.
records.summary_es: Al iniciar con las reacciones al arresto de Jiminez, The Beatrice Daily Express recoge la opinión generalizada de que las autoridades no tenían derecho a detenerlo como ciudadano desarmado que viajaba aparentemente hacia Santiago de Cuba, y de que aun si se dirigiera a San Domingo solo estaría regresando a su país natal. Bajo el titular «Searching for Jiminez», un despacho de Kingston fechado el 19 de agosto cita informes de Santo Domingo según los cuales el gobierno dominicano teme desesperadamente la llegada inminente del líder revolucionario Jiminez, que inclinaría por completo a la opinión pública indecisa, y ha ordenado a buques armados que patrullan la costa registrar toda embarcación extraña y capturarlo bajo cualquier bandera, armado o no. Un despacho adjunto desde Santiago de Cuba, también del 19 de agosto, añade que representantes estadounidenses reclutan rápidamente expediciones en la costa norte, que La Habana ordenó retener bajo investigación a los hombres capturados recientemente en Baracoa y que, aunque varias expediciones han logrado salir sin interferencia, el general Leonard Wood está decidido a hacer cumplir la neutralidad.

records.headline: Writing editorially, The Magnolia Gazette contends that the recent
records.summary_en: Writing editorially, The Magnolia Gazette contends that the recent assassination of President Heureaux of the Dominican Republic and the disputed succession there are likely to bring new problems to the United States. The paper notes allegations that a powerful American syndicate practically controls the country's finances and affairs, and states that two warships have been ordered to San Domingo to protect American interests. Observing sarcastically that syndicates have been well looked after by the current administration, the editorial remarks that there is no reason not to take in San Domingo if the seizure of the Philippines can be justified, adding that all territorial syndicates should look alike to Mr. McKinley and "manifest destiny" ought not to discriminate between friends.
records.summary_es: En un comentario editorial, The Magnolia Gazette sostiene que el reciente asesinato del presidente Heureaux de la República Dominicana y la disputada sucesión en ese país probablemente traerán nuevos problemas a las puertas de los Estados Unidos. El periódico recoge versiones de que un poderoso sindicato estadounidense controla prácticamente las finanzas y los asuntos de esa nación, e informa que dos buques de guerra han recibido órdenes de dirigirse a San Domingo para proteger los intereses estadounidenses. Observando con sarcasmo que los sindicatos han sido muy bien atendidos por la actual administración, el editorial señala que no hay motivo para no incorporar a San Domingo si puede justificarse la toma de las Filipinas, y añade que todos los sindicatos territoriales deberían parecerle iguales al señor McKinley y que el «destino manifiesto» no debería discriminar entre amigos.

records.summary_en: The *Passaic City Record* reported that while official tranquillity prevailed in Santo Domingo following President Heureaux's assassination, trade remained depressed due to public reluctance to withdraw paper currency. In addition, a devastating hurricane caused severe flooding and property destruction across San Pedro de Macoris, Samana, and Puerto Plata. In Cuba, American customs officers at Baracoa intercepted an arms shipment of 143 rifles and 18,000 rounds of ammunition bound for Dominican rebels.
records.summary_es: El *Passaic City Record* informó que, si bien prevalecía una aparente tranquilidad en Santo Domingo tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux, el comercio continuaba deprimido debido a la renuencia del público a aceptar el papel moneda. Además, un devastador huracán provocó graves inundaciones y destrucción material en San Pedro de Macorís, Samaná y Puerto Plata. En Cuba, agentes de aduanas estadounidenses en Baracoa interceptaron un cargamento clandestino de armas de 143 fusiles y 18.000 proyectiles con destino a los rebeldes dominicanos.
records.passage: throughout the country. The assassins of President Heureaux are still at large, but measures have been taken for their capture. It is said the band numbers sixteen. Although the rate for drafts is falling, and there are some signs of returning confidence, business continues dull, and imports are limited. The financial situation is bad. The problem of taking up the paper currency has not yet been solved, as the people in general do not wish it taken up. This is the real cause of dullness in business. Once the matter has been arranged, affairs should take on a different aspect. The latest news from Macoris regarding the effects of the hurricane shows that the damage was more serious than was at first supposed. The river overflowed its banks and inundated the ground. Many families had abandoned their houses for the time and boats were used in the streets to carry people from one point to another. The storm did severe damage in the country about Samana and Puerto Plata. The United States cruiser New Orleans has left San Domingo Harbor for Porto Rico. The United States gunboat Machias is still here. Watch on Filibusters. records.headline: The New York Journal and Advertiser, citing State Department
records.summary_en: The New York Journal and Advertiser, citing State Department denials, reports that proposed additional U.S. precautions were not prompted by representations from the Santo Domingo government, but rest on the duty of preventing filibustering against a friendly nation—a stance already shown by military orders barring filibustering expeditions from leaving Cuba. Asking the Navy to assist is viewed as an indication that efforts in Cuba to aid the Dominican insurgents are more active than reports from Havana and Santiago suggest. An accompanying August 18 dispatch from Santiago de Cuba states that Dominican agents are rapidly recruiting expeditions, especially on the north coast; orders arrived from Havana that day to hold recently captured men pending investigation, trading schooners are closely watched, the tug Adonis was armed the previous day and sent to Guantanamo to patrol the coast, and despite several expeditions having escaped unhindered, Military Governor General Wood is determined to enforce neutrality.
records.summary_es: El New York Journal and Advertiser, citando desmentidos del Departamento de Estado, informa que las medidas adicionales de precaución propuestas por los Estados Unidos no responden a gestiones del gobierno de Santo Domingo, sino al deber de impedir el filibusterismo contra una nación amiga, postura ya demostrada mediante las órdenes militares destinadas a evitar la salida de expediciones filibusteras desde Cuba. El hecho de haberse solicitado el auxilio de la Marina se interpreta como indicio de que en Cuba hay mayor actividad en apoyo de los insurgentes dominicanos de lo que reflejan los informes de La Habana y Santiago. Un despacho adjunto de Santiago de Cuba fechado el 18 de agosto señala que agentes dominicanos reclutan rápidamente expediciones, sobre todo en la costa norte; ese día llegaron órdenes de La Habana de retener bajo investigación a hombres capturados recientemente, las goletas mercantes son vigiladas de cerca, el remolcador Adonis fue armado la víspera y enviado a Guantanamo para patrullar la costa y, aunque varias expediciones lograron partir sin tropiezos, el gobernador militar general Wood está decidido a hacer cumplir la neutralidad.

records.headline: A feature on Santo Domingo describes its minerals, including rock salt, petroleum found near Azua, abundant copper
records.summary_en: A feature on Santo Domingo describes its minerals, including rock salt, petroleum found near Azua, abundant copper and great masses of iron ore in the interior, and explains that the president is chosen by an electoral college for four years with a cabinet of six. It says sugar, tobacco, cacao and coffee are the leading exports, that the United States led all other countries in trade with the republic, that most sugar estates are owned by Americans with the crop estimated at 65,000 tons, and that steamers of the Samana Bay Fruit Company carry fifteen to eighteen thousand bunches of bananas on each trip to the United States.
records.summary_es: Un artículo sobre Santo Domingo describe sus minerales, incluida la sal de roca, el petróleo encontrado cerca de Azua, el cobre abundante y grandes masas de mineral de hierro en el interior, y explica que el presidente es elegido por un colegio electoral por cuatro años con un gabinete de seis miembros. Dice que el azúcar, el tabaco, el cacao y el café son las principales exportaciones, que los Estados Unidos encabezaban a todos los demás países en el comercio con la república, que la mayoría de las fincas azucareras son propiedad de americanos con la cosecha estimada en 65.000 toneladas, y que los vapores de la Samana Bay Fruit Company llevan de quince a dieciocho mil racimos de bananas en cada viaje a los Estados Unidos.

In the Neyba valley there are two hills composed entirely of rock salt, which chemical analysis has proved to be of sufficient purity for commercial purposes. Petroleum has been found in the vicinity of Azua, and copper is said by geologists and prospectors to be abundant. There are said also to be great masses of iron ore in the interior, but at such a great distance from any port that they cannot be made available until railroads shall have been built. Other minerals in the Island are silver, platinum, manganese, tin, antimony, marble, coal, and chalcedony. Mineral springs abound. The executive authority is vested in the President, who is chosen by an electoral college, and serves for four years. He is assisted by a Cabinet of six members. There is also a Vice President. The republic is divided into eleven districts for purposes of administration. Six of these districts are called provinces. The Island's Trade. The four leading articles of export are sugar, tobacco, cacao, and coffee. Last year the United States led all Europe in the amount of exports to the republic by $636,403.05, and all the world, exclusive of the United States, by more than one-half million dollars. As might be supposed, large quantities of drills and cotton goods are used, these coming from England and the United States, but the greater part from England, mainly because of cheapness. records.headline: This account describes the Republic of Santo Domingo, which covers 18,045 of the island's 28,240 square miles, its rivers
records.summary_en: This account describes the Republic of Santo Domingo, which covers 18,045 of the island's 28,240 square miles, its rivers, its gold washings, the rock-salt hills of the Neyba valley, petroleum near Azua and other minerals, and a government headed by a president chosen by an electoral college for four years. Its four leading exports are sugar, tobacco, cacao and coffee; the sugar crop this season is estimated at 65,000 tons and most sugar estates are owned by Americans, tobacco goes chiefly to Germany, and the Samana Bay Fruit Company's steamers carry fifteen to eighteen thousand bunches of bananas on each trip to the United States.
records.summary_es: Esta descripción presenta la República de Santo Domingo, que cubre 18.045 de las 28.240 millas cuadradas de la isla, sus ríos, sus lavaderos de oro, las colinas de sal de roca del valle de Neyba, el petróleo cerca de Azua y otros minerales, y un gobierno encabezado por un presidente elegido por un colegio electoral por cuatro años. Sus cuatro principales productos de exportación son el azúcar, el tabaco, el cacao y el café; la cosecha de azúcar de esta temporada se estima en 65.000 toneladas y la mayoría de las haciendas azucareras son propiedad de americanos, el tabaco va principalmente a Alemania, y los vapores de la Samana Bay Fruit Company llevan de quince a dieciocho mil racimos de plátanos en cada viaje a los Estados Unidos.
records.passage: by Americans. English, French, German and Italian capital is also invested in this industry. Tobacco is extensively grown and much of it is said to be of a quality nearly equal to the celebrated Havana product. Germany is the chief market for this crop. The banana industry is a growing one. The steamers of the Samana Bay Fruit Company make three or four trips a month to the United States, and on each trip between fifteen and eighteen thousand bunches of the fruit are carried. Mahogany, lignum vitae, logwood, honey, wax, hides, fruits, and sugar are exported almost exclusively to this country, while the coffee, cocoa and tobacco find their market in Germany and other European countries. THE BISHOP A BORROWER. Church Mortgages to Be Raised With English Money. New York, Aug. 19—Bishop Wigger, of the Catholic Diocese of Newark, has confirmed the report that he proposes to accept a loan of $1,500,000 from an English syndicate to be used in taking up mortgages on the churches in his diocese, upon which 5 per cent interest is exacted. Under the new arrangement only 3 1-2 per cent interest will be charged by the foreign syndicate. The Bishop of Madison yesterday said he would probably have the money next week. It is estimated that Catholic Church property in this diocese, which is worth about 10,000,000, is mortgaged for nearly $2,000,000. The syndicate considers the property gilt-edged security, and is willing to advance another million if the loan of $1,500,000 does not prove sufficient.

records.headline: The Marietta Daily Leader prints advices from Santo Domingo via
records.summary_en: The Marietta Daily Leader prints advices from Santo Domingo via Kingston, Jamaica, dated August 20, stating that the Dominican government is growing desperately apprehensive of the momentarily expected arrival of revolutionary leader Jiminez, which reportedly would completely turn partly undecided popular opinion. To intercept him, armed vessels are patrolling the coast under orders to search every strange ship and capture Jiminez under any flag, armed or not. An accompanying August 19 dispatch from Santiago de Cuba reports that Dominican agents are rapidly recruiting expeditions, particularly along the north coast; Havana sent orders on Friday to hold recently captured men pending an investigation, trading schooners are closely watched, the tug Adonis was armed on Thursday and sent to Guantanamo to patrol the coast, and although several expeditions have gotten away without interference, Military Governor General Leonard Wood is determined to enforce neutrality.

Con el fin de interceptarlo, embarcaciones armadas patrullan la costa con órdenes de registrar todo buque extraño y capturar a Jiminez bajo cualquier bandera, esté armado o no. records.headline: Dispatches in The San Francisco Call report that Santo Domingo government
records.summary_en: Dispatches in The San Francisco Call report that Santo Domingo government forces trying to suppress the revolution have been defeated and driven back at Monte Cristi, while the province of San Pedro Macoris has enthusiastically proclaimed a revolution in favor of presidential aspirant General Juan Isidro Jiminez. An August 19 dispatch from Port-au-Prince adds that a revolutionary band gathered between Cupey and Esterovasa in Santo Domingo dispersed without fighting and re-entered Haitian territory, while a thousand men under Minister Cordero guard Fort Belair and watch the frontier as warships patrol the coast to prevent Jiminez from landing. Under the headline "Neutrality Laws Are to Be Enforced," an August 19 Washington dispatch reports Secretary Root's statement that General Jiminez was arrested by the collector of customs at Cienfuegos—presumably on orders from General Brooke under recent instructions to prevent U.S. neutrality violations from Cuba and keep Jiminez under close surveillance—and notes that Washington has heard nothing of his release and will send Brooke no instructions unless requested.
records.summary_es: Despachos publicados en The San Francisco Call informan que las fuerzas del gobierno de Santo Domingo empeñadas en sofocar la revolución han sido derrotadas y rechazadas en Monte Cristi, mientras que la provincia de San Pedro Macoris ha proclamado con gran entusiasmo la revolución en favor del aspirante presidencial general Juan Isidro Jiminez. Un despacho de Puerto Príncipe fechado el 19 de agosto añade que un grupo revolucionario reunido entre Cupey y Esterovasa, en Santo Domingo, se dispersó sin combatir y reingresó en territorio haitiano, en tanto que mil hombres al mando del ministro Cordero resguardan el fuerte Belair y vigilan la frontera mientras buques de guerra patrullan la costa para impedir el desembarco de Jiminez. Bajo el titular «Neutrality Laws Are to Be Enforced», un despacho de Washington del 19 de agosto recoge las declaraciones del secretario Root de que el general Jiminez fue arrestado por el administrador de aduanas en Cienfuegos —presumiblemente por orden del general Brooke conforme a instrucciones recientes para impedir violaciones de las leyes de neutralidad estadounidenses desde Cuba y mantener estrecha vigilancia sobre Jiminez—, e indica que en Washington no consta su liberación ni se enviarán instrucciones a Brooke salvo que las solicite.

records.headline: Commenting editorially on Cuban and Dominican affairs, The Times of Washington dismisses
records.summary_en: Commenting editorially on Cuban and Dominican affairs, The Times of Washington dismisses the suggestion advanced by U.S. authorities in Cuba—seeking, in the paper's view, to escape blame for persecuting "so good an Administration man"—that Maximo Gomez is responsible for the affair involving Jiminez. Even if Gomez and Jiminez are reportedly no longer friendly, the editorial argues that Gomez must be counted out for financial reasons, observing pointedly that he is not worth fourteen million dollars, has no one-million-dollar cash Dominican campaign fund, and has no New York partner traveling to Lake Champlain to see the President. The paper predicts that Jiminez will likely sail again successfully and soon sit upon Heureaux's "throne," guarding the remains of Christopher Columbus in the cathedral at San Domingo City while also looking after the interests of the Smith M. Weed syndicate.
records.summary_es: En un comentario editorial sobre asuntos cubanos y dominicanos, The Times de Washington descarta la idea promovida por las autoridades estadounidenses en Cuba —en un intento, según el diario, de eludir culpas por perseguir a «tan buen hombre de la Administración»— de que Maximo Gomez sea responsable de todo el asunto relacionado con Jiminez. Aun si según se dice Gomez y Jiminez ya no mantienen amistad, el editorial sostiene que hay que descartar a Gomez por razones financieras, señalando con mordacidad que este no posee catorce millones de dólares, carece de un fondo de campaña dominicano de un millón en efectivo y no tiene un socio neoyorquino que viaje a Lake Champlain para ver al Presidente. El periódico pronostica que con toda probabilidad Jiminez volverá a zarpar con éxito y pronto ocupará el «trono» de Heureaux, custodiando los restos de Cristóbal Colón en la catedral de la ciudad de San Domingo sin olvidar tampoco velar por los intereses del sindicato de Smith M. Weed.

records.headline: In an ironic editorial note, The Times of Washington observes
records.summary_en: In an ironic editorial note, The Times of Washington observes that the Consul of Santo Domingo in New York insists everything is peaceful and orderly in his country. Although Figuereo's troops have been routed at Monte Cristi, another province has declared for Jiminez, and the revolution has outgrown the nominal government's ability to resist it, the paper remarks sarcastically that none of this shakes the consul's confidence that there is not even the suspicion of a revolution in Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: En una irónica nota editorial, The Times de Washington observa que el cónsul de Santo Domingo en Nueva York asegura que todo se mantiene pacífico y en orden en su país. Aunque las tropas de Figuereo han sido derrotadas en Monte Cristi, otra provincia se ha pronunciado en favor de Jiminez y la revolución ha desbordado la capacidad del gobierno nominal para hacerle frente, el diario comenta con sarcasmo que nada de ello altera en lo más mínimo la confianza del cónsul de que no existe ni siquiera la sospecha de una revolución en Santo Domingo.

records.headline: A dispatch from Santiago, Cuba, in the New York Journal and Advertiser states
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Santiago, Cuba, in the New York Journal and Advertiser states that General Juan Isidro Jiminez is expected to arrive at Santiago or Manzanillo within a day or two, and reports that an American passenger aboard the steamer when Jiminez was arrested at Cienfuegos overheard him offering Dominican army commissions to two Cuban army officers. Jiminez's agents are said to be very active among Cubans in Santiago, where two Cubans believed to be in his pay are under surveillance. An accompanying August 21 dispatch from Havana adds that former Cuban soldiers and Italians continue offering their services as would-be filibusters to Jiminez's son despite his repeated statements that he does not wish to organize an expedition, while rumors say an independent group of twenty to thirty men will leave that day to fight for Jiminez in Santo Domingo if his cause prospers.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Santiago, Cuba, publicado en el New York Journal and Advertiser señala que se espera la llegada del general Juan Isidro Jiminez a Santiago o a Manzanillo en uno o dos días, e informa que un pasajero estadounidense que viajaba en el vapor con Jiminez cuando fue arrestado en Cienfuegos escuchó una conversación en la que este ofreció grados en el ejército dominicano a dos oficiales del ejército cubano. Se afirma que los agentes de Jiminez despliegan gran actividad entre los cubanos en Santiago, donde dos cubanos que se cree están a su sueldo se hallan bajo vigilancia. Un despacho adjunto de La Habana fechado el 21 de agosto añade que exsoldados cubanos e italianos siguen ofreciendo sus servicios como aspirantes a filibusteros al hijo de Jiminez pese a la insistencia de este en que no desea organizar ninguna expedición, mientras se rumora que un grupo independiente de entre veinte y treinta hombres partirá ese día para combatir por Jiminez en Santo Domingo si su causa prospera.

records.headline: The Denison Review, following a comment that authorities had no right
records.summary_en: The Denison Review, following a comment that authorities had no right to arrest Jiminez as an unarmed citizen apparently going to Santiago de Cuba—and that even if bound for San Domingo he would only be returning to his native country—prints an August 19 Kingston dispatch under the headline "Searching for Jiminez." Citing advices from Santo Domingo, the dispatch reports that the government there is desperately apprehensive of the momentarily expected arrival of revolutionary leader Jiminez, which would completely turn partly undecided popular opinion, and has ordered armed vessels patrolling the coast to search every strange ship and capture him under any flag, armed or not. A partially garbled August 19 dispatch from Santiago de Cuba below it notes expeditions being recruited on the north coast, orders to hold recently captured men, several expeditions getting away without interference, and a determination to enforce neutrality.
records.summary_es: The Denison Review publica un despacho de Kingston del 19 de agosto bajo el titular «Searching for Jiminez», tras un comentario según el cual las autoridades no tenían derecho a arrestar a Jiminez como ciudadano desarmado que se dirigía aparentemente a Santiago de Cuba —y que aun si fuera a San Domingo solo regresaría a su país natal—. Citando informes de Santo Domingo, el despacho señala que el gobierno dominicano teme desesperadamente la llegada inminente del líder revolucionario Jiminez, la cual volcaría por completo a la opinión pública parcialmente indecisa, y ha ordenado a buques armados que patrullan la costa registrar toda embarcación extraña y capturarlo bajo cualquier bandera, armado o no. Más abajo, un despacho parcialmente mutilado desde Santiago de Cuba del 19 de agosto menciona el reclutamiento de expediciones en la costa norte, órdenes de retener a hombres capturados recientemente, la salida sin interferencia de varias expediciones y la determinación de hacer cumplir la neutralidad.

records.headline: An August 19 dispatch from Kingston, Jamaica, in the Mineral Point Tribune reports
records.summary_en: An August 19 dispatch from Kingston, Jamaica, in the Mineral Point Tribune reports advices from Santo Domingo, under the heading "To Intercept Jiminez," stating that the government is apprehensive of Jiminez's arrival, which would completely sway partly undecided popular opinion, and has armed vessels patrolling the coast with orders to search every strange ship and capture him under any flag, armed or not. A companion August 19 dispatch from Santiago de Cuba headed "To Enforce Neutrality" adds that Dominican agents are rapidly recruiting expeditions, particularly on the north coast, and that while several expeditions have escaped without interference, Military Governor General Wood has determined to do all in his power to enforce neutrality.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Kingston, Jamaica, fechado el 19 de agosto en el Mineral Point Tribune, bajo el título «To Intercept Jiminez», recoge informes de Santo Domingo según los cuales el gobierno teme la llegada de Jiminez, que inclinaría por completo a la opinión pública parcialmente indecisa, y mantiene embarcaciones armadas patrullando la costa con órdenes de registrar todo buque extraño y capturarlo bajo cualquier bandera, armado o no. Un despacho complementario del 19 de agosto desde Santiago de Cuba, titulado «To Enforce Neutrality», añade que agentes dominicanos reclutan rápidamente expediciones, en particular en la costa norte, y que aunque varias expediciones han logrado salir sin interferencia, el gobernador militar general Wood ha resuelto hacer todo cuanto esté a su alcance para hacer cumplir la neutralidad.

Vapores armados vigilan la costa para impedir el desembarco de cualquier expedición insurrecta, y el gobernador de Monte Cristo cuenta con 3,000 hombres sobre las armas para preservar la paz.

records.headline: In a column of brief world news items, the Northern Wisconsin Advertiser carries
records.summary_en: In a column of brief world news items, the Northern Wisconsin Advertiser carries two separate notices on the conflict in the Dominican Republic. One item states that the Santo Domingo revolutionists are reported to have suffered a crushing defeat, while a later item notes that revolutionary operations in San Domingo have caused a panic in Puerto Plata.

Una de ellas señala que, según informes, los revolucionarios de Santo Domingo han sufrido una aplastante derrota, mientras que otra apunta que las operaciones de los revolucionarios en San Domingo han desatado el pánico en Puerto Plata.

records.headline: Following a brief report via Puerto Plata, San Domingo, that Sanchez Blanco
records.summary_en: Following a brief report via Puerto Plata, San Domingo, that Sanchez Blanco and Moca have declared for the revolution and that Santiago—whose governor, General Pepin, left earlier to march against the insurgents—is expected to rise and march on La Vega, the New-York Tribune publishes a statement from Jiminez's representative in the United States, of No. 143 East Fifty-fifth Street (printed as 'Adriann Crullon'). Speaking to a Tribune reporter, the representative expresses surprise that the prudent revolutionary chief was arrested in Cienfuegos while peacefully traveling to Santiago de Cuba, contrasting the arrest with the freedom enjoyed by liberators in monarchical London. Although Jiminez was subsequently liberated, the representative states that the moral effect has somewhat disappointed the masses, describing Jiminez as a patriot who has abandoned family, business, and everything to free his country from despotism.
records.summary_es: Tras un breve informe vía Puerto Plata, San Domingo, según el cual Sanchez Blanco y Moca se han declarado a favor de la revolución y se espera que Santiago —cuyo gobernador, el general Pepin, partió hace algún tiempo para marchar contra los insurrectos— se levante y marche sobre La Vega, el New-York Tribune publica una declaración del representante de Jiminez en los Estados Unidos, domiciliado en el número 143 de la calle 55 Este (impreso como «Adriann Crullon»). En conversación con un reportero del Tribune, el representante expresa sorpresa por el arresto del prudente jefe revolucionario en Cienfuegos mientras viajaba pacíficamente hacia Santiago de Cuba, contrastando la detención con la libertad de que gozaban los libertadores en el Londres monárquico. Aunque Jiminez fue puesto en libertad posteriormente, el representante afirma que el efecto moral ha decepcionado en cierta medida a las masas, y describe a Jiminez como un patriota que ha abandonado familia, negocios y todo para librar a su país del despotismo.
