records.headline: Drawing on a letter from Puerto Plata to the New York Sun, The Appeal sketches
records.summary_en: Drawing on a letter from Puerto Plata to the New York Sun, The Appeal sketches the biography of the assassinated Dominican ruler Ulises Heureaux, familiarly called "Lilis," noting that many consider his killing to have freed the Dominican people from twenty years of tyranny. Born in Puerto Plata about forty-six years earlier as the illegitimate son of D'Assas Heureaux, a Haitian mulatto, and Josefa Lebert, a Black woman of St. Thomas, he began as a Dominican soldier, rose to general of division, and first distinguished himself under Gen. Luperon in the restoration wars against the Spaniards. After serving as executive delegate in the Cibao provinces and provisional government delegate in the southern provinces, he became minister of the interior and president of the council of ministers under Merino, assuming sole control of government combinations before winning election as president for 1882 to 1884 and again in 1887.
records.summary_es: Basándose en una carta enviada desde Puerto Plata al New York Sun, The Appeal traza la biografía del asesinado gobernante dominicano Ulises Heureaux, llamado familiarmente «Lilis», señalando que muchos consideran que su muerte liberó al pueblo dominicano de veinte años de tiranía. Nacido en Puerto Plata unos cuarenta y seis años atrás como hijo ilegítimo de D'Assas Heureaux, un mulato haitiano, y de Josefa Lebert, una mujer negra de St. Thomas, comenzó como soldado dominicano, ascendió a general de división y se distinguió por primera vez bajo las órdenes del general Luperon en las guerras de la Restauración contra los españoles. Tras desempeñarse como delegado del Poder Ejecutivo en las provincias del Cibao y delegado del gobierno provisional en las provincias del sur, fue nombrado ministro de lo Interior y presidente del consejo de ministros durante el gobierno de Merino, asumiendo el control exclusivo de las combinaciones políticas antes de ser elegido presidente de 1882 a 1884 y nuevamente en 1887.

records.headline: Describing the espionage network maintained by "Lilis" (Heureaux
records.summary_en: Describing the espionage network maintained by "Lilis" (Heureaux), The Appeal reports that he employed a whole army of spies—including many women, chiefly from the lower classes—both inside the Dominican Republic and abroad in Haiti, Cuba, Porto Rico, St. Thomas, Jamaica, Paris, New York, Turk's Island, and wherever else opponents might travel. Some agents held diplomatic posts abroad in which official representation was largely a sinecure and pay corresponded to the value of their intelligence on the movements of Heureaux's enemies. Although expensive to maintain, this network warned him in time of brewing conspiracies, and when in doubt he pitted one spy against another to verify reports, while none could fathom his politics—likely, the writer remarks, because he had none.
records.summary_es: Al describir la red de espionaje mantenida por «Lilis» (Heureaux), The Appeal informa que empleaba todo un ejército de espías —incluidas muchas mujeres, principalmente de las clases bajas— tanto dentro de la República Dominicana como en el exterior, en Haití, Cuba, Puerto Rico, St. Thomas, Jamaica, París, Nueva York, Turk's Island y cualquier otro punto adonde pudieran dirigirse sus enemigos. Algunos agentes ocupaban cargos diplomáticos en el extranjero cuyas funciones oficiales eran en gran medida una sinecura, recibiendo pago en proporción al valor de sus informes sobre los movimientos de los adversarios de Heureaux. Aunque costosa de sostener, esta red le advertía a tiempo de las conspiraciones en ciernes y, en caso de duda, enfrentaba a un espía con otro para corroborar datos, sin que ninguno lograra descifrar su política, probablemente —observa el autor— porque nunca tuvo ninguna.

records.headline: The Appeal, examining custom-house administration and currency
records.summary_en: The Appeal, examining custom-house administration and currency issues under "Lilis," reports that although Dominican revenues were managed for bondholders through a board in Santo Domingo, the custom houses yielded as much for Lilis and his followers as for the bondholders, and his joint arrangement with the American syndicate is widely blamed for the Dominican Republic's current bankruptcy. After the vice president reportedly answered Lilis's complaints about his finances by urging more paper money, $3,600,000 in paper was put into circulation on an authorized issue of $1,000,000, becoming worthless paper and provoking a panic that indirectly led Lilis to Moca and his death at the hands of Roman Caceres. The article adds that Lilis's long tenure owed more to heavy debt than fear, relying in every town on three agents—a merchant, a governor, and a commandant—who enriched themselves through custom-house jobbery and favoritism.
records.summary_es: The Appeal, al examinar la administración aduanera y las emisiones monetarias bajo «Lilis», informa que, aunque las rentas dominicanas se manejaban en favor de los tenedores de bonos mediante una junta en Santo Domingo, las aduanas producían tanto para Lilis y sus allegados como para los bonistas, y su acuerdo conjunto con el sindicato estadounidense es considerado generalmente la causa de la actual bancarrota de la República Dominicana. Después de que el vicepresidente supuestamente respondiera a las quejas financieras de Lilis aconsejando emitir más papel moneda, se pusieron en circulación $3,600,000 en billetes sobre una emisión autorizada de $1,000,000, convirtiéndose en papel sin valor y provocando un pánico que llevó indirectamente a Lilis a Moca, donde halló la muerte a manos de Roman Caceres. El artículo añade que la larga permanencia de Lilis en el poder se debió más a su fuerte endeudamiento que al temor, apoyándose en cada pueblo en tres agentes —un comerciante, un gobernador y un comandante— que se enriquecían mediante manejos y favoritismos en las aduanas.

records.headline: Recalling an earlier visit by a French warship to Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: Recalling an earlier visit by a French warship to Santo Domingo, The Appeal relates an anecdote in which President "Lilis" remarked to the visiting admiral on what he called the tenacity of the Black race in never letting go of anything once grasped. Less than two months after Lilis was shot, however, his political opponent at the head of the Liberal party holds power without a shot having been fired, and Jiminez's journey from his landing at Puerto Plata to Santo Domingo city has been a triumphal march while Lilis's boasted following vanished. Ramon Caceres is now celebrated by the public not as an assassin but as a patriot and political redeemer, and the country remains quiet amid expectations of reconstruction and prosperity under Jiminez's administration.
records.summary_es: Recordando la visita años atrás de un buque de guerra francés a Santo Domingo, The Appeal relata una anécdota en la que el presidente «Lilis» comentó al almirante visitante lo que calificó como la tenacidad de la raza negra para no soltar jamás aquello que llegaba a empuñar. Sin embargo, a menos de dos meses de haber sido baleado Lilis, su adversario político al frente del Partido Liberal ocupa el poder sin haber disparado un solo tiro, y el recorrido de Jiminez desde su desembarco en Puerto Plata hasta la ciudad de Santo Domingo ha sido una marcha triunfal mientras el numeroso séquito del que Lilis solía jactarse se desvanecía. Ramon Caceres es hoy aclamado por el pueblo no como un asesino sino como patriota y redentor político, y el país permanece tranquilo ante la expectativa de una etapa de reconstrucción y prosperidad bajo la administración de Jiminez.

records.headline: The Twice-a-Week Courier-Journal, reprinting an account that cites
records.summary_en: The Twice-a-Week Courier-Journal, reprinting an account that cites prior reports in the Herald, describes the fear and apprehension accompanying the comparatively bloodless revolution that followed the assassination of President Heureaux, whose eighteen-year rule had maintained a "bloody peace" in Santo Domingo while reducing the island's inhabitants nearly to slavery through crime, extravagance, and licentiousness. Held together around the aged Vice President Wenceslao Figuereo only by immediate emergency, Heureaux's cabinet was riven by personal ambitions, jealousies, and hatreds that raised fears of civil war and twenty years of buried vengeance. Although Figuereo—described as aged, mild, inoffensive, and not unpopular—might have remained in office until the next regular presidential election had he dismissed the Heureaux ministry, he hesitated weakly until the opportunity passed.
records.summary_es: The Twice-a-Week Courier-Journal, reproduciendo una crónica que cita informes previos en el Herald, describe el temor y la aprensión que acompañaron la revolución relativamente incruenta posterior al asesinato del presidente Heureaux, cuyo dominio de dieciocho años había mantenido una «paz sangrienta» en Santo Domingo mientras reducía a los habitantes de la isla casi a la esclavitud mediante crímenes, extravagancias y libertinaje. Unido en torno al anciano vicepresidente Wenceslao Figuereo únicamente por la emergencia inmediata, el gabinete de Heureaux estaba desgarrado por ambiciones personales, celos y odios que despertaban temores de guerra civil y veinte años de venganzas reprimidas. Aunque Figuereo —descrito como anciano, apacible, inofensivo y no impopular— habría podido continuar en el poder hasta la siguiente elección presidencial ordinaria si hubiese destituido al ministerio de Heureaux, vaciló débilmente hasta dejar pasar su oportunidad.

records.headline: A Santo Domingo letter says the revolution just ended was comparatively bloodless but filled with terror, after the assassination of President Heureaux removed
records.summary_en: A Santo Domingo letter says the revolution just ended was comparatively bloodless but filled with terror, after the assassination of President Heureaux removed the hand that had preserved a bloody peace for eighteen years. It describes Vice President Figuereo's government, held together by the Heureaux ministry, losing its chance by hesitating, and the revolt that began at San Francisco de Macoris in the interest of Jimines spreading as Macoris, Moca and La Vega went over, Santiago surrendered, the wires were cut, and the government suppressed the news and doubled the guards in the capital.
records.summary_es: Una carta de Santo Domingo dice que la revolución recién terminada fue comparativamente sin sangre pero llena de terror, después de que el asesinato del presidente Heureaux apartó la mano que había preservado una paz sangrienta durante dieciocho años. Describe cómo el gobierno del vicepresidente Figuereo, sostenido por el ministerio de Heureaux, perdió su oportunidad por vacilar, y cómo la revuelta que comenzó en San Francisco de Macoris a favor de Jimines se extendió cuando Macoris, Moca y La Vega se pasaron a ella, Santiago se rindió, se cortaron los cables y el gobierno suprimió las noticias y duplicó las guardias en la capital.

records.headline: The Twice-a-Week Courier-Journal, commenting on public sentiment
records.summary_en: The Twice-a-Week Courier-Journal, commenting on public sentiment in Santo Domingo after Heureaux's death, remarks that people in the United States have wondered to hear that a man named Ramon—whose surname is garbled in the print as "Caoares" and "Cocorss"—who killed Heureaux in cold blood and cast his body into the street where a mob mutilated it, has become a popular idol and was called to serve as Minister of War. That wonder lessens, the writer suggests, given the admiration fellow citizens accord someone who rid the country of its tyrant, adding that he carries his honors modestly and has just resigned from the Vasques cabinet citing his own unfitness for executive office. At the same time, residents of Santo Domingo, chiefly foreigners, contend that only an iron hand like Heureaux's can govern what they call a thoughtless and revolutionary people who yield only to force.
records.summary_es: The Twice-a-Week Courier-Journal, al comentar el sentimiento público en Santo Domingo tras la muerte de Heureaux, señala que en Estados Unidos ha causado asombro saber que un hombre llamado Ramon —cuyo apellido aparece distorsionado en el impreso como «Caoares» y «Cocorss»—, quien mató a Heureaux a sangre fría y arrojó su cuerpo a la calle donde una turba lo mutiló, se ha convertido en ídolo popular y fue llamado a ocupar la cartera de Ministro de Guerra. Ese asombro se atenúa, sugiere el autor, ante la admiración que sus conciudadanos profesan a quien libró al país de su tirano, añadiendo que lleva sus honores con modestia y acaba de renunciar al gabinete de Vasques alegando su propia falta de aptitud para un cargo ejecutivo. Al mismo tiempo, residentes de Santo Domingo, principalmente extranjeros, sostienen que solo una mano de hierro como la de Heureaux puede gobernar a lo que califican de pueblo irreflexivo y revolucionario que únicamente se doblega ante la fuerza.

records.headline: The Indianapolis Journal reports that Mr. Powell has been instructed
records.summary_en: The Indianapolis Journal reports that Mr. Powell has been instructed to proceed from Port-au-Prince to San Domingo to urge the Jiminez government to pay an overdue installment in the arbitration award to the McKay estate arising from the government's absorption of a bridge concession. During this visit, Powell is also looking after broader American interests in San Domingo, including the concession granted to the Weed syndicate to farm the republic's customs revenues for a term of years. Another issue to be presented to the Dominican government stems from the repudiation of debts totaling about $500,000 incurred by the late President Heureaux to Mr. J. Sala of New York, for which claimants seek to hold the government responsible at least for the portion not chargeable to Heureaux personally. Because certain German creditors have also sought to hold the government house occupied by Heureaux as security for debts, the paper notes that Powell may face a difficult task in separating conflicting claims.
records.summary_es: The Indianapolis Journal informa que el Sr. Powell ha recibido instrucciones de trasladarse desde Port-au-Prince a San Domingo para instar al gobierno de Jiminez a pagar un plazo vencido del laudo arbitral a favor de la sucesión McKay, derivado de la absorción gubernamental de una concesión de puente. Durante esta visita, Powell también atiende en general los intereses estadounidenses en San Domingo, incluidos los vinculados con la concesión otorgada al sindicato Weed para recaudar las rentas aduaneras de la república por un período de años. Otro asunto que se presentará al gobierno dominicano surge del repudio de deudas que suman alrededor de $500,000 contraídas por el fallecido presidente Heureaux con el Sr. J. Sala, de Nueva York, por las cuales se procura responsabilizar al gobierno al menos en la parte no imputable personalmente a Heureaux. Dado que ciertos acreedores alemanes también han intentado retener como garantía la casa de gobierno ocupada por Heureaux, el diario señala que Powell podría enfrentar una difícil tarea al deslindar las reclamaciones en conflicto.

records.headline: According to the New-York Tribune, Mr. Powell, the United States minister
records.summary_en: According to the New-York Tribune, Mr. Powell, the United States minister to Hayti and San Domingo, has received instructions to go from Port au Prince to San Domingo to press the Jiminez government for payment of an overdue installment in the McKay estate arbitration award resulting from the government's absorption of a bridge concession. Powell is likewise attending to general American interests in San Domingo during his visit, including the concessions held by the Weed syndicate for farming the republic's customs revenues over a term of years. In addition, the Dominican government will be presented with a claim growing out of the repudiation of debts totaling about $500,000 incurred by the late President Heureaux to J. Sala of New-York, with efforts to hold the government liable at least for the portion not chargeable against Heureaux personally. Certain German creditors have also sought to hold the government house occupied by Heureaux as security for some of his debts, leaving Powell a difficult task in separating these conflicting claims.
records.summary_es: Según el New-York Tribune, el Sr. Powell, ministro de los Estados Unidos en Hayti y San Domingo, ha recibido instrucciones de dirigirse desde Port au Prince a San Domingo para gestionar ante el gobierno de Jiminez el pago de un plazo vencido del laudo arbitral a favor de la sucesión McKay por la absorción gubernamental de una concesión de puente. Ciertos acreedores alemanes también han buscado retener la casa de gobierno ocupada por Heureaux como garantía de algunas de sus deudas, lo que plantea a Powell una ardua labor para separar estas reclamaciones en conflicto.

records.headline: Opening with a Spanish proverb translated as "He who lives by the sword
records.summary_en: Opening with a Spanish proverb translated as "He who lives by the sword shall die by the sword," the Brookings Weekly Register recounts how President Ulises Heureaux was shot through the heart in Moca, Santo Domingo, on July 26, 1899, by an assailant (printed as "ltamon Cacerea") avenging the assassination of his father at Heureaux's order, an act many say also freed the Dominican people from twenty years of tyranny. Born in Puerto Plata about forty-six years earlier as the illegitimate son of D'Assas Heureaux, a Haytian mulatto, and Josefa Lebert, a Black woman of St. Thomas, Heureaux entered the Dominican army in his youth, rose to general of division, first gained notice under Gen. Luperon, and distinguished himself in the wars of the restoration against the Spaniards. After serving as delegate of the executive power in the provinces of Cibao in 1879 and of the provisional government in the southern provinces in 1880, he was named minister of the interior and president of the council of ministers during Merino's administration. From that point until his death, the article notes before breaking off, he assumed sole responsibility for governing the republic.
records.summary_es: Comenzando con un proverbio en español equivalente a «El que a hierro mata, a hierro muere», el Brookings Weekly Register relata cómo el presidente Ulises Heureaux murió de un disparo en el corazón en Moca, Santo Domingo, el 26 de julio de 1899, a manos de un atacante (impreso como «ltamon Cacerea») que vengaba el asesinato de su padre ordenado por Heureaux, acto que según muchos liberó además al pueblo dominicano de veinte años de tiranía. Nacido en Puerto Plata unos cuarenta y seis años antes como hijo ilegítimo de D'Assas Heureaux, un mulato haitiano, y de Josefa Lebert, una mujer negra de St. Thomas, Heureaux sirvió desde muy joven como soldado dominicano, ascendió hasta general de división, se dio a conocer bajo el general Luperon y se distinguió en las guerras de la Restauración contra los españoles. Tras desempeñarse como delegado del poder ejecutivo en las provincias del Cibao en 1879 y del gobierno provisional en las provincias del sur en 1880, fue nombrado ministro del Interior y presidente del consejo de ministros durante la administración de Merino. Desde ese momento hasta el día de su muerte, señala el texto antes de cortarse, asumió él solo la responsabilidad del gobierno de la república.

records.headline: Writing editorially under the heading "No Dominican Cuba," The Jamesburg Record describes
records.summary_en: Writing editorially under the heading "No Dominican Cuba," The Jamesburg Record describes General Jimenez as a "mystery man" surrounded by contradictory reports put forward on equal authority: that he both planned President Heureaux's murder and had no knowledge of it, that he will both use the United States as a filibustering base and scrupulously obey neutrality laws, and that he is both fomenting insurrection in "Dominica" and doing nothing against the lawful government of President Figuero. Such conflicting claims, the paper remarks, leave a casual observer to conclude either that Jimenez has outdone Jekyll and Hyde or that someone is lying. On one point, however, the editorial insists there can be no doubt: there must be no repetition of the Cuban experience between the United States and the Dominican Republic, noting that past Cuban insurrections cost the Federal Treasury millions of dollars to enforce neutrality laws and suppress filibustering.
records.summary_es: En un editorial titulado «Ninguna Cuba dominicana», The Jamesburg Record describe al general Jimenez como un «hombre misterioso» rodeado de versiones contradictorias atribuidas a autoridades equivalentes: que planeó el asesinato del presidente Heureaux y a la vez no tuvo conocimiento alguno de él, que usará a los Estados Unidos como base filibustera y a la vez acatará escrupulosamente las leyes de neutralidad, y que fomenta la insurrección en «Dominica» mientras no hace ni dice nada contra el gobierno legítimo del presidente Figuero. Tales informes opuestos, comenta el periódico, llevan al observador a concluir que Jimenez ha superado a Jekyll y Hyde o que alguien miente descaradamente. En un punto, sin embargo, el editorial sostiene que no cabe duda alguna: no debe repetirse el caso cubano entre los Estados Unidos y la República Dominicana, recordando que las insurrecciones en Cuba costaron millones de dólares al Tesoro Federal para hacer cumplir la neutralidad y reprimir el filibusterismo.

records.headline: Continuing its editorial on the Dominican Republic, The Jamesburg Record declares
records.summary_en: Continuing its editorial on the Dominican Republic, The Jamesburg Record declares that the United States wants no more filibustering "Juntas" and provides asylum rather than a ground for conspiracies, so if Jimenez wishes to wage war against the Dominican Republic he must camp outside the United States and U.S.-controlled West Indian islands. Expressing hope that "Dominica" will not repeat the Cuban conflict through a war of desolation and extermination, the paper warns that neither Jimenez nor anyone else could make a worse mistake than precipitating a "reign of horror" in hopes of provoking American intervention. Although the United States has at times played the "knight-errant," the editorial concludes that Washington will observe neutrality, tolerate no filibusters, and hope against any breach of peace or outrage upon humanity in what it calls "the one remaining independent island in the Great Antilles."
records.summary_es: Continuando su editorial sobre la República Dominicana, The Jamesburg Record declara que los Estados Unidos no quieren más «Juntas» filibusteras y ofrecen asilo pero no espacio para conspiraciones, de modo que si Jimenez desea hacer la guerra contra la República Dominicana deberá establecer su campamento fuera de los Estados Unidos y de las islas antillanas bajo control estadounidense. Expresando la esperanza de que «Dominica» no repita el conflicto cubano mediante una guerra de desolación y exterminio, el diario advierte que ni Jimenez ni nadie podría cometer mayor error que precipitar un «reino del horror» con la esperanza de provocar una intervención estadounidense. Aunque los Estados Unidos han actuado en cierta medida como «caballero andante», el editorial concluye que observarán la neutralidad, no tolerarán a los filibusteros y esperan que no haya quebrantamiento de la paz ni ultraje a la humanidad en lo que denomina «la única isla independiente que queda en las Grandes Antillas».

records.headline: Discussing a pending French claim against Santo Domingo, The Age-Herald reports
records.summary_en: Discussing a pending French claim against Santo Domingo, The Age-Herald reports that an agreement President Heureaux was understood to have arranged to settle the dispute was disregarded by his successor, President Jiminez. The paper notes that the United States could eventually become involved through the "San Dominican syndicate," controlled by New York capitalists, which holds a Dominican government concession entitling it to collect all customs revenues in return for paying interest on the public debt and assisting the city government. Because the current Santo Domingo administration is believed too short of funds to pay the sum demanded by France, a delicate question could arise should French naval commanders attempt to seize the customs revenues, though the State Department has not yet been informed that Jiminez recognizes the New York syndicate's concession from the late President Heureaux as still in force.
records.summary_es: Al abordar una reclamación francesa pendiente contra Santo Domingo, The Age-Herald informa que un acuerdo que según se entendía había dispuesto el presidente Heureaux para resolver el asunto fue desconocido por su sucesor, el presidente Jiminez. El diario señala que los Estados Unidos podrían verse finalmente involucrados por medio del «San Dominican syndicate», controlado por capitalistas de Nueva York, el cual posee una concesión del gobierno dominicano que le da derecho a recaudar todas las rentas aduaneras a cambio de sufragar los intereses de la deuda pública y asistir al gobierno de la ciudad. Dado que se cree que la actual administración de Santo Domingo carece de fondos suficientes para pagar la suma exigida por Francia, podría surgir una cuestión delicada si los comandantes navales franceses intentaran incautar las rentas aduaneras, aunque el Departamento de Estado aún no ha sido informado de que Jiminez reconozca como vigente la concesión otorgada al sindicato neoyorquino por el fallecido presidente Heureaux.

records.headline: A dispatch in The Salt Lake Herald reports that subscriptions
records.summary_en: A dispatch in The Salt Lake Herald reports that subscriptions raised to pay a 280,000-franc claim pressed by the French consul largely cover the required sum, adding that although a French fleet is expected to visit Santo Domingo, the country remains quiet, strong patriotic feeling is expressed, and a United States gunboat has departed. Under a January 6 New York dateline headed "Claim Will Be Settled," General Alejandro "Whozy" Gil, who served for six years as consul general of the Dominican Republic in New York until the assassination of President Heureaux, responded to word that France had ordered its Atlantic squadron to sail for Santo Domingo. He stated the previous night that he had no doubt whatever that the claim would be settled to the French government's complete satisfaction regardless of the intended naval visit.
records.summary_es: Un despacho en The Salt Lake Herald informa que las suscripciones recaudadas para liquidar una reclamación de 280,000 francos exigida por el cónsul francés cubren en gran medida el monto necesario, añadiendo que, aunque se espera la visita de una flota francesa a Santo Domingo, el país permanece tranquilo, se expresa un notable sentimiento patriótico y una cañonera estadounidense ha partido del lugar. Bajo un fechado en Nueva York del 6 de enero titulado «La reclamación será resuelta», el general Alejandro «Whozy» Gil, quien fue cónsul general de la República Dominicana en esa ciudad durante seis años hasta el asesinato del presidente Heureaux, se refirió a la noticia de que Francia había ordenado a su escuadra del Atlántico zarpar hacia Santo Domingo. Declaró la noche anterior que no tenía duda alguna de que la reclamación se resolvería a entera satisfacción del gobierno francés, independientemente de la visita naval prevista.

MEETS FRENCH ADMIRAL.

Jimenez Confers With Richard—Settlement Expected To-Day.

SPECIAL BY CABLE.
Santo Domingo, Jan. 9.—(Copyright, 1900, by James Gordon Bennett.)—Admiral Richard of the French navy, with his staff, formally called upon President Jimenez this morning. No business was transacted. The French Consul was present. It is rumored on good authority that the French Consul has not been sustained by his Government, and that he has been asked for his resignation.

It is expected that official action will be taken to-morrow. Americans of this place have asked the United States not to allow France to dictate terms to the Dominican Government. An American cruiser is expected to arrive to-day. One is reported to have left Sanchez yesterday.

ORDERS TO THE MACHIAS.
REPUBLIC SPECIAL.
Washington, Jan. 9.—Instructions were to-day cabled to Commander L. C. Logan, commanding the Machias, directing him to promptly return to Santo Domingo.

In compliance with this instruction, it is presumed the Machias has left San Juan bound for the capital of Santo Domingo. Upon his arrival Commander Logan will consult with the American Minister relative to the protection of American interests. It was said at the State Department this evening that no appeal for the intervention of the United States had been received from Santo Domingo and it is hardly likely that this Government will interfere, in view of the fact that the Jimenez Government has collected by popular subscription the money necessary to pay the French claims. It is possible that Minister Powell may act as a mediator between the French fleet and President Jimenez, looking to compliance with the French demand for an apology, but now that the money has been collected [illegible] [illegible] believed that the worst is about over.

records.headline: According to a naval report in The Sun, an American naval commander
records.summary_en: According to a naval report in The Sun, an American naval commander notified the Navy Department from Santo Domingo City that he was departing in his vessel for San Juan to join the flagship New York, acting on orders sent to him by the Navy Department the previous day. The report states that keeping an American warship at Santo Domingo is no longer necessary because the trouble between France and the Dominican Republic, which had prompted France to send two warships to Santo Domingo City, has ended peaceably.
records.summary_es: Según un informe naval publicado en The Sun, un comandante naval estadounidense notificó al Departamento de Marina desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo que partía en su buque hacia San Juan para reunirse con el buque insignia New York, en cumplimiento de órdenes enviadas por el Departamento de Marina el día anterior. El reporte señala que ya no es necesario mantener un buque de guerra estadounidense en Santo Domingo debido a que el conflicto entre Francia y la República Dominicana, que había llevado a Francia a enviar dos buques de guerra a la ciudad de Santo Domingo, ha concluido pacíficamente.

records.headline: A January 16 dispatch from Santo Domingo in The Yale Expositor states
records.summary_en: A January 16 dispatch from Santo Domingo in The Yale Expositor states that Admiral Richard of the French navy, after investigating all the facts, found the Dominican government correct in its position on the "Bolsmare-Caccavelli" claim and accepted the terms the government had proposed to the French consul before his protest without demanding money. Having contracted a loan, the Dominican government prefers to pay the claim itself and will thank the public for the popular subscription, which will not be used, while the French consul is expected to be recalled soon. Meanwhile, the French warship Suchet has departed for Haiti to enforce payment of 200,000 francs paid to the late President Heureaux for lands never ceded under a secret boundary settlement.
records.summary_es: Un despacho fechado en Santo Domingo el 16 de enero en The Yale Expositor informa que el almirante Richard, de la marina francesa, tras investigar todos los hechos, halló correcta la postura del gobierno dominicano sobre la reclamación «Bolsmare-Caccavelli» y aceptó sin exigir dinero los términos que el gobierno había propuesto al cónsul francés antes de su protesta. Habiendo contratado un empréstito, el gobierno dominicano prefiere pagar por sí mismo el monto de la reclamación y agradecerá al pueblo de la república la suscripción popular, que no será utilizada, mientras se prevé el pronto retiro del cónsul francés. Entretanto, el buque de guerra francés Suchet partió hacia Haití para exigir el pago de 200,000 francos entregados al fallecido presidente Heureaux por tierras nunca cedidas conforme a un arreglo secreto sobre cuestiones fronterizas.

records.summary_en: The *Chariton Courier* reported that French Admiral Richard concurred with the Dominican government's position on the Boismare-Caccavelli claims dispute and accepted the terms previously proposed by Dominican authorities. The Dominican government secured a loan to satisfy the financial claim, releasing citizens from the funds collected by popular subscription. Meanwhile, the French warship *Suchet* departed for Haiti to collect 200,000 francs connected to a secret border agreement negotiated with the late President Heureaux.
records.summary_es: El *Chariton Courier* informó que el almirante francés Richard coincidió con la postura del gobierno dominicano respecto a la controversia por las reclamaciones Boismare-Caccavelli y aceptó los términos propuestos con anterioridad por las autoridades dominicanas. El gobierno dominicano obtuvo un préstamo para saldar la reclamación financiera, liberando a los ciudadanos de los fondos reunidos por suscripción popular. Entretanto, el buque de guerra francés *Suchet* zarpó hacia Haití para cobrar 200.000 francos vinculados a un acuerdo fronterizo secreto negociado con el difunto presidente Heureaux.

Santo Domingo, Jan. 16. — The French admiral finds on investigation of all facts that the Dominican government was correct in its attitude on the Boismare-Caccavelli claim. Admiral Richard of the French navy is not demanding money, but he has accepted the terms which the Dominican government proposed to the French consul before his protest. The Dominican government, having contracted a loan, prefers to pay the amount of the claim, and will thank the people of the republic for the popular subscription, which will not be used. It is probable that the French consul will be recalled soon. records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported on diplomatic friction in Santo Domingo arising from the French consul's abrupt demand on December 5 for immediate installment payments on the Boismare-Caccavelli claims. Dominican citizens held public meetings to protest the consul's haste, while carefully avoiding anti-French hostility. Foreign Minister Henríquez y Carvajal responded to consular complaints on January 4, defending the dignified conduct of the Dominican populace and reaffirming friendship with France.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó sobre las tensiones diplomáticas en Santo Domingo surgidas por la abrupta exigencia del cónsul francés el 5 de diciembre para el pago inmediato de cuotas por las reclamaciones Boismare-Caccavelli. Los ciudadanos dominicanos celebraron asambleas públicas para protestar contra la premura del cónsul, evitando con cautela cualquier hostilidad antifrancesa. El ministro de Relaciones Exteriores Henríquez y Carvajal respondió a las quejas consulares el 4 de enero, defendiendo la digna conducta de la población dominicana y reafirmando la amistad con Francia.

This was dated Dec. 5, and the consul added that he expected the payment to be made before the sailing of the French steamer, Dec. 15. Such precipitateness was bitterly resented by the people of the city of Santo Domingo. They held a mass meeting in the public square, and loudly protested, though being careful in their speeches to show that they did not hold France herself responsible for the inconsiderate and, as they declared, too hasty acts of the French minister of foreign affairs. records.headline: Yet this is the principal product the Government depends upon to
records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported further statements by Judge Durham concerning the collapse of the Dominican currency system under late President Heureaux. Durham disclosed that Heureaux systematically evaded agreements with the San Domingo Improvement Company by shifting printing plates between American firms to produce excessive quantities of unauthorized paper money. This unchecked currency inflation created widespread commercial distrust, leaving the Improvement Company with large unusable balances and bringing local commerce to an abrupt standstill upon the president's death.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó sobre declaraciones adicionales del juez Durham relativas al colapso del sistema monetario dominicano bajo el mandato del difunto presidente Heureaux. Durham reveló que Heureaux eludía sistemáticamente los convenios con la San Domingo Improvement Company transfiriendo matrices de impresión entre compañías estadounidenses para fabricar cantidades excesivas de papel moneda sin autorización. Esta inflación monetaria desmedida generó una desconfianza comercial generalizada, dejando a la Improvement Company con abultados saldos inutilizables y paralizando repentinamente el comercio local tras el deceso del mandatario.
records.passage: sugar product. Yet this is the principal product the Government depends upon to meet the demands of the San Domingo Improvement Company in its handling of the revenues. How is the Government going to better this situation? It is absolutely necessary that there be a reduction in this taxation that we may successfully market our product in the United States. At the same time the Government has an equally urgent necessity for Increased revenues. The late President had at one time twenty five clerks employed signing this paper money. The issue was authorized by the San Domingo Improvement Company to the extent of about a million, but when the President began the issue he had control of the plates and went on issuing. The improvement company tried to get control of the plates, but as fast as they traced them the President changed them to some other printing establishment in the United States and the company was unable to control the issue. The company itself had agreed, in order to give them circulation, to accept a certain per cent In customs duties, but so great was the issue that the company found itself in possession of $400,000 of the money that it was unable to dispose of. The abundance of this money created general distrust, and when the President was assassinated there was practically no currency in the island and business was at a standstill. records.headline: The Topeka State Journal, describing a financial agreement between
records.summary_en: The Topeka State Journal, describing a financial agreement between the Dominican government and an American improvement company, reports that the arrangement contemplates a three-year period to clear the country's external and floating debt. Originally suggested by the improvement company at President Heureaux's request, the plan provides for the company to take up bond coupons for three years as bonds are presented and issue scrip to holders, giving the administration a respite expected to allow it to meet all obligations or at least accumulate funds guaranteeing prompt payment of all debts. While retaining its agents in the Dominican custom houses, the company will grant the government a larger monthly budget allowance, resolving a longstanding sore point with authorities and the public and leading observers to judge that Santo Domingo has secured favorable terms.
records.summary_es: The Topeka State Journal, al describir un acuerdo financiero entre el gobierno dominicano y una compañía estadounidense de mejoras, informa que el arreglo contempla un período de tres años para liquidar la deuda externa y flotante del país. Propuesto originalmente por la compañía de mejoras a solicitud del presidente Heureaux, el plan dispone que la empresa recoja durante tres años los cupones de los bonos en circulación conforme se presenten y emita certificados a sus tenedores, otorgando a la administración un respiro que permitiría cubrir todas las obligaciones o al menos acumular fondos que garanticen el pronto pago de todas las deudas. Aunque mantendrá a sus agentes en las aduanas dominicanas, la compañía concederá al gobierno una asignación mensual más amplia para su presupuesto, subsanando un viejo motivo de malestar entre las autoridades y la población y llevando a considerar que Santo Domingo ha obtenido condiciones favorables.

records.summary_en: A June 1 dispatch from Santiago, Cuba, in the Waterbury Evening Democrat reports that General Maximo Gomez arrived the previous day from Santo Domingo and spent the day with political leaders of the "black party," who were jubilant at his return. In a bad humor, Gomez flatly refused to be interviewed and declined to speak on either Cuban or Dominican politics. Newspapers supporting the "black party" declared that his return meant the failure of an alleged American, Spanish, and English conspiracy to annex Cuba, and Gomez departed for Havana that evening.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that President McKinley received the credentials of the new Dominican Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary at the White House. In his address, the Dominican minister emphasized the historical friendship between both nations and advocated concluding a reciprocal commercial treaty. President McKinley welcomed the envoy and reciprocated the desire to establish closer, mutually beneficial trade relations between the two republics.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el presidente McKinley recibió en la Casa Blanca las cartas credenciales del nuevo enviado extraordinario y ministro plenipotenciario dominicano. En su alocución, el ministro dominicano destacó la histórica amistad entre ambas naciones y abogó por la concertación de un tratado de reciprocidad comercial. El presidente McKinley dio la bienvenida al enviado y correspondió al deseo de entablar relaciones comerciales más estrechas y mutuamente beneficiosas entre ambas repúblicas.
records.passage: government has honored me is a new proof of the sincere friendship which it cherishes toward the American people, and of the desire which animates it to draw still more closely upon solid commercial foundations the fraternal bonds which happily have thus far united them. The different productions of both countries, as well as their neighborhood, have made my government believe that it would be of mutual advantage for both countries to celebrate a commercial treaty which might increase the good and cordial relations which have united them. I am especially charged to present to your excellency, in the name of the president of the Dominican republic, his most sincere wishes, as well as my own. for your personal happiness and the expression of his enthusiastic admiration for the great republic of the north." President McKinley's Reply. The President replied as follows: "Mr. Minister-It gives me pleasure to receive at your hands the letters of credence by which the president of the Dominican republic accredits you as envoy extraordinary and minister plenipotentiary near this government. I am glad to recognize in this special mission a new proof of the friendship which unites the two republics. I cordially reciprocate the wishes of your government for closer and still more advantageous commercial relations. "I beg you will convey to his excellency, the president of the Dominican republic, my best wishes and those of the people of the United States for the prosperity and happiness of the Dominican people. -and I

records.headline: In a June 9 Washington dispatch, the New-York Tribune reports
records.summary_en: In a June 9 Washington dispatch, the New-York Tribune reports that Francisco Vasquez presented his credentials to President McKinley as minister of the Dominican Republic, ending a period of several years during which the country had no minister at Washington and becoming the second new minister received in a week. Vasquez was accompanied to the State Department by Perry Allen, who will serve as counsellor of the Dominican Legation, while Secretary Hay made the introductions. In the speeches exchanged at the ceremony, both President McKinley and Minister Vasquez expressed a mutual desire for a commercial treaty between the United States and San Domingo.
records.summary_es: En un despacho fechado el 9 de junio en Washington, el New-York Tribune informa que Francisco Vasquez presentó sus credenciales ante el presidente McKinley como ministro de la República Dominicana, poniendo fin a varios años sin ministro dominicano en Washington y convirtiéndose en el segundo nuevo ministro recibido en una semana. Vasquez acudió al Departamento de Estado acompañado por Perry Allen, quien actuará como consejero de la legación dominicana, mientras que el secretario Hay realizó las presentaciones. En los discursos pronunciados durante el acto, tanto el presidente McKinley como el ministro Vasquez expresaron el deseo mutuo de concertar un tratado comercial entre los Estados Unidos y San Domingo.

records.summary_en: The *Times* published the diplomatic exchange between President McKinley and the newly accredited Dominican Minister Plenipotentiary during the presentation of credentials. The Dominican representative conveyed warm regards from his government and proposed celebrating a commercial treaty to strengthen economic ties. President McKinley warmly reciprocated, expressing American commitment to cordial friendship and expanded bilateral trade.
records.summary_es: El *Times* publicó el intercambio diplomático entre el presidente McKinley y el recién acreditado ministro plenipotenciario dominicano durante la presentación de credenciales. El representante dominicano transmitió los cordiales saludos de su gobierno y propuso concertar un tratado comercial para fortalecer los vínculos económicos. El presidente McKinley correspondió con calidez, expresando el compromiso estadounidense con una amistad cordial y la ampliación del comercio bilateral.

records.headline: A plot to assassinate Ramon Caceres, the governor of Santiago
records.summary_en: A plot to assassinate Ramon Caceres, the governor of Santiago, has been uncovered by authorities, according to a July 26 dispatch from San Domingo in Washington's Evening Star, and twenty-five of the conspirators have been imprisoned. Several military officers are implicated in the conspiracy, and the accused are to be tried by court-martial. The dispatch adds that President Jiminez is touring the interior and that the country as a whole remains quiet.
records.summary_es: Las autoridades descubrieron un complot para asesinar a Ramon Caceres, gobernador de Santiago, y encarcelaron a veinticinco de los conspiradores, según un despacho fechado el 26 de julio en San Domingo y publicado por el Evening Star de Washington. Varios oficiales militares están implicados en la conjura y los acusados serán juzgados por un consejo de guerra. El despacho añade que el presidente Jiminez visita el interior y que el país en general permanece tranquilo.

records.headline: The Times of Washington reports that Salvador Ros of New York
records.summary_en: The Times of Washington reports that Salvador Ros of New York, a Cuban-born naturalized U.S. citizen, appeared the previous day before State Department Solicitor Penfield—in the presence of San Domingo's New York Consul General, Mr. Maxwell—seeking U.S. protection for rights he claims under a Dominican concession. Ros stated that he carried out harbor improvements at San Pedro under a grant from the late Dominican President Heureaux, to be repaid by collecting certain import and export taxes, but Heureaux was assassinated before signing the concession and the Dominican Congress refused to confirm it. Alleging that Dominican authorities now bar him from collecting those taxes, Ros wants U.S. intervention, though the State Department will not take up the matter until formal papers are filed.
records.summary_es: The Times de Washington informa que Salvador Ros, residente en Nueva York y ciudadano estadounidense naturalizado de origen cubano, compareció el día anterior ante el procurador Penfield del Departamento de Estado —en presencia del cónsul general de San Domingo en Nueva York, el señor Maxwell— para pedir protección estadounidense sobre derechos que reclama en virtud de una concesión dominicana. Ros declaró haber realizado mejoras portuarias en San Pedro bajo una concesión del fallecido presidente dominicano Heureaux, pagaderas mediante el cobro de determinados impuestos de importación y exportación, pero Heureaux fue asesinado antes de firmarla y el Congreso dominicano se negó a confirmarla. Alegando que las autoridades dominicanas le impiden recaudar dichos impuestos, Ros solicita el respaldo de los Estados Unidos, aunque el Departamento de Estado no examinará el caso hasta que se presenten los documentos formales.

records.headline: Continuing an account in the New-York Tribune, this passage
records.summary_en: Continuing an account in the New-York Tribune, this passage describes a one-day welcome for the President—marked by American, European, and Dominican flags, speeches, a dinner, and a ball—at a property of a corporation owned in New York, Boston, and Providence, followed at 5 a.m. by an excursion on decorated flatcars as guests of the Samana Bay Fruit Company. The company operates three engines, forty cars, a machine shop, a telephone exchange, and iron fruit-loading piers along a mountain railway overlooking Samana Bay, where company officers' hilltop homes stand and breakfast was served. The writer notes that earlier U.S. Government interest spurred American immigration, including an 1837 settlement of freed American slaves whose English-speaking descendants are reliable workers but too few for local demand, prompting the fruit company's not wholly satisfactory importation of three hundred English-speaking laborers from St. Kitts at wages of sixty cents a day in gold amid minimal living costs.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that Belgian bondholders, who held £6,000,000 in Dominican bonds, refused to accept an adjustment contract agreed to with the Dominican Improvement Company. Concurrently, an official notified his government that $350,000 collected from Santo Domingo was being deposited for bondholders following the deduction of Belgian state expenses. The Dominican government simultaneously gave assurances to the American Minister that the interests of American bondholders would be safeguarded.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que los tenedores de bonos belgas, en posesión de 6.000.000 de libras esterlinas en bonos dominicanos, se negaron a aceptar un contrato de ajuste acordado con la San Domingo Improvement Company. Al mismo tiempo, un funcionario notificó a su gobierno que se estaban depositando 350.000 dólares recaudados en Santo Domingo para los tenedores de bonos tras deducir los gastos estatales belgas. Simultáneamente, el gobierno dominicano garantizó al ministro estadounidense que se salvaguardarían los intereses de los tenedores de bonos estadounidenses.

records.headline: Opening mid-sentence on a report from Cape Haytien of a Dominican
records.summary_en: Opening mid-sentence on a report from Cape Haytien of a Dominican revolution, the New-York Tribune prints a cabled reply declaring that reports of rebellion are "absolutely false" and that the entire country is tranquil. The cable was received at No. 10 Pearl Street by a personal friend of President Jiminez with interests in San Domingo (printed "Osear Hucilinger"), who had cabled General Jiminez to ask whether the rumor of trouble was true. Recalling that after President Heureaux's assassination a year earlier General Vasquez held the government only until General Jiminez arrived from Cuba despite having ample opportunity to proclaim himself president, the article quotes a friend stating that Vasquez has no presidential ambitions and adds that Dominicans blame unfriendly relations with Hayti for recurring rumors sent to injure their country.
records.summary_es: Comenzando a mitad de frase sobre una noticia procedente de Cape Haytien acerca de una revolución en la República Dominicana, el New-York Tribune reproduce una respuesta por cable que declara que los informes de rebelión son «absolutamente falsos» y que todo el país está tranquilo. El mensaje fue recibido en el número 10 de Pearl Street por un amigo personal del presidente Jiminez con intereses en San Domingo (impreso «Osear Hucilinger»), quien había enviado un cable al general Jiminez preguntando si el rumor de disturbios era cierto. Recordando que tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux un año antes el general Vasquez asumió el gobierno únicamente hasta la llegada del general Jiminez desde Cuba pese a haber tenido amplia oportunidad de proclamarse presidente, el artículo cita a un amigo según el cual Vasquez carece de ambiciones presidenciales y añade que los dominicanos atribuyen estos rumores frecuentes procedentes de Haití al propósito de perjudicar al país, dado que ambas repúblicas no mantienen relaciones muy amistosas.

records.headline: Washington's The Times, beginning with a cabled message stating
records.summary_en: Washington's The Times, beginning with a cabled message stating that reports of rebellion are "absolutely false" and the entire country is tranquil, reports that the dispatch was received in reply to an inquiry by Oscar Huetfinger of 101 Pearl Street, a personal friend of President Jiminez with large interests in San Domingo. The rumors had alleged an uprising led by Vice President Vasquez and Gen. Ramon Caceres of the State of Santiago, but the article notes that Vasquez took temporary control after President Heureaux's assassination a year ago without seizing the presidency while awaiting Jiminez from Cuba, and quotes a friend stating today that Vasquez has no presidential ambition and is among Jiminez's best friends. Dominicans contend that periodic reports of strife coming from Haiti are circulated intentionally to harm the Dominican Republic because the two republics are not on very friendly terms.
records.summary_es: The Times de Washington, iniciándose con un mensaje por cable que afirma que los informes de rebelión son «absolutamente falsos» y que todo el país se halla tranquilo, informa que el despacho fue recibido en respuesta a una consulta de Oscar Huetfinger, del 101 de Pearl Street, amigo personal del presidente Jiminez y poseedor de importantes intereses en San Domingo. Los rumores atribuían un supuesto levantamiento al vicepresidente Vasquez y al general Ramon Caceres, del estado de Santiago, pero el artículo recuerda que Vasquez asumió el mando provisional tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux hace un año sin proclamarse presidente mientras aguardaba a Jiminez desde Cuba, y cita a un amigo que aseguró hoy que Vasquez no ambiciona la presidencia y es uno de los mejores amigos de Jiminez. Los dominicanos sostienen que los informes periódicos de conflictos procedentes de Haití se difunden con el fin de perjudicar a la República Dominicana debido a las relaciones poco amistosas entre ambas repúblicas.

records.headline: In a September 28 dispatch from New York, the Waterbury Evening Democrat reports
records.summary_en: In a September 28 dispatch from New York, the Waterbury Evening Democrat reports that President Jimenez of Santo Domingo has cabled a denial of a report received from Cape Haitien alleging a revolution in the Dominican Republic. Jimenez's dispatch states that the reports of rebellion are "absolutely false" and that the entire country is tranquil.
records.summary_es: En un despacho fechado el 28 de septiembre en Nueva York, el Waterbury Evening Democrat informa que el presidente Jimenez de Santo Domingo desmintió por cable una noticia recibida desde Cape Haitien sobre una supuesta revolución en la República Dominicana. El mensaje de Jimenez afirma que los informes de rebelión son «absolutamente falsos» y que todo el país está tranquilo.

records.headline: SAN DOMINGO, Republic of Santo Domin go, November 14, via Haitian
records.summary_en: Under the heading Affairs in Santo Domingo, a November 14 dispatch reports that the Dominican Congress will meet in special session on November 23 to discuss the reciprocity treaty with the United States. It adds that Leovigildo Cuello has been appointed minister of posts and telegraphs, that the sugar crop harvest will begin early in December, and that the country is quiet.
records.summary_es: Bajo el título de asuntos de Santo Domingo, un despacho del 14 de noviembre informa que el Congreso dominicano se reunirá en sesión extraordinaria el 23 de noviembre para discutir el tratado de reciprocidad con los Estados Unidos. Añade que Leovigildo Cuello ha sido nombrado ministro de Correos y Telégrafos, que la cosecha de azúcar comenzará a principios de diciembre y que el país está tranquilo.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* published a travel account describing the peaceful transition of power following the assassination of President Heureaux and the enthusiastic election of President Juan Isidro Jimenes. The author provided a geographic description of Santo Domingo, noting its fertile soil, moderate tropical climate, and central position among the Greater Antilles. The article observed that despite its rich natural advantages, a century of persistent internal conflict had discouraged foreign capital investment.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* publicó una crónica de viaje que describía la pacífica transición de poder tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux y la entusiasta elección del presidente Juan Isidro Jimenes. El autor ofreció una descripción geográfica de Santo Domingo, destacando su suelo fértil, su clima tropical moderado y su posición central entre las Grandes Antillas. El artículo observaba que, pese a sus ricas ventajas naturales, un siglo de persistentes conflictos internos había desincentivado la inversión de capitales extranjeros.

records.summary_en: The *Chickasha Daily Express* reported that Dominican President Juan Isidro Jimenes had sent an envoy to the United States to organize a financial syndicate to assume the national debt under an American protectorate, though the attempt proved unsuccessful. The paper highlighted Washington rumors that Santo Domingo might seek territorial status similar to Puerto Rico under Jimenes's leadership. The report also recalled President Grant's failed 1870s annexation campaign and the historical overtures made by Dominican President Buenaventura Báez.
records.summary_es: El *Chickasha Daily Express* informó que el presidente dominicano Juan Isidro Jimenes había enviado un emisario a los Estados Unidos para organizar un consorcio financiero que asumiera la deuda nacional bajo un protectorado estadounidense, si bien la gestión resultó infructuosa. El periódico destacó los rumores en Washington de que Santo Domingo podría solicitar un estatus territorial semejante al de Puerto Rico bajo el liderazgo de Jimenes. El informe recordó asimismo la fallida campaña de anexión del presidente Grant en la década de 1870 y los históricos ofrecimientos efectuados por el presidente dominicano Buenaventura Báez.

records.summary_en: The *Topeka State Journal* reported that the Dominican Congress voted financial compensation for the San Domingo Improvement Company of New York as the government resumed direct control over national customs collection. Under the new arrangement, customs duties were to be received by a mixed commission composed of Dutch, Belgian, American, French, and Dominican representatives. The resumption of national control was greeted with general public satisfaction, and the president received widespread congratulations.
records.summary_es: El *Topeka State Journal* informó que el Congreso dominicano votó una compensación financiera para la San Domingo Improvement Company de Nueva York mientras el gobierno reasumía el control directo de la recaudación aduanera nacional. Conforme al nuevo esquema, los aranceles aduaneros debían ser percibidos por una comisión mixta integrada por representantes holandeses, belgas, estadounidenses, franceses y dominicanos. La recuperación del control nacional fue acogida con general satisfacción pública y el mandatario recibió amplias felicitaciones.

records.summary_en: Washington reported on January 12 that the government would probably take cognizance of the troubles in San Domingo and act as necessary for the protection of American interests, but that the State Department had not yet heard from Consul-General Maxwell on the reports that the Dominican Government had resumed the direction of its own fiscal affairs, terminating the system by which an American syndicate collected the duties and paid the debts of the government. The plan had been adopted some years earlier, and some Belgian bond owners were understood to have objected to it. Representatives of the San Domingo Improvement Company held long conferences with Acting Secretary Hill and Solicitor Penfield concerning the reported repudiation of the companys grant, and a cable message of inquiry was sent to the American representative in San Domingo.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published an interview with Dominican leader Horacio Vásquez, who described the nation's abundant mineral resources, including deposits of copper, precious metals, and vast salt reserves. Vásquez maintained that political stability had been quickly restored after President Heureaux's assassination through the establishment of a provisional government. He sharply criticized the San Domingo Improvement Company, asserting that it had merely constructed a railroad with Dominican state funds, enriching itself, Heureaux, and local financier Cosme Batlle at the country's expense.

Vásquez sostuvo que la estabilidad política se restableció con rapidez tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux mediante la constitución de un gobierno provisional. Criticó duramente a la San Domingo Improvement Company, aseverando que únicamente había construido un ferrocarril con fondos del Estado dominicano, enriqueciéndose a sí misma, a Heureaux y al financista local Cosme Batlle a expensas del país.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that nationalist pressure compelled President Jimenes to confront the San Domingo Improvement Company and threaten its agent with expulsion after the company challenged Dominican customs authority. Meanwhile, Belgian Foreign Minister de Favereau instructed his consul in Santo Domingo to ensure that bondholder funds in the treasury safe remained strictly protected for European creditors. Additionally, the semi-official Dominican press responded defiantly to rumors that the American gunboat *Scorpion* was en route to coerce the government.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que presiones nacionalistas obligaron al presidente Jimenes a confrontar a la San Domingo Improvement Company y a amenazar a su agente con la expulsión después de que la empresa desafiara la autoridad aduanera dominicana. Mientras tanto, el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores belga, De Favereau, instruyó a su cónsul en Santo Domingo para que garantizara que los fondos de los tenedores de bonos en la caja fuerte de la tesorería permanecieran estrictamente resguardados para los acreedores europeos. records.headline: Dr. Henriquez y Carvajal, the Dominican Foreign Minister, met
records.summary_en: Dr. Henriquez y Carvajal, the Dominican Foreign Minister, met that day with Acting Secretary of State Dr. Hill, Washington's The Evening Times reports, concerning Santo Domingo's revocation of its contract with the New York improvement company (printed "Santo Deminpgan Improvement Company"), which had been entrusted with collecting national revenues, making public improvements, and funding the public debt. Henriquez was accompanied by Andre Julio R. Aybar, Santo Domingo's chargé d'affaires in Washington (printed "Feo Leonte Vasquez"), and Perry Allen of the Dominican Legation. Following the conference, the Dominican Republic acquiesced in Dr. Hill's advice that an equitable basis likely existed for settling the dispute and that negotiations should take place directly between the parties rather than through the U.S. Government.
records.summary_es: El doctor Henriquez y Carvajal, ministro de Relaciones Exteriores dominicano, se entrevistó ese día con el secretario de Estado interino, el doctor Hill, acerca de la revocación por Santo Domingo de su contrato con la compañía neoyorquina de mejoras (impresa «Santo Deminpgan Improvement Company»), encargada de recaudar las rentas públicas, ejecutar obras públicas y consolidar la deuda pública. Henriquez estuvo acompañado por Andre Julio R. Aybar, el encargado de negocios de Santo Domingo en Washington (impreso «Feo Leonte Vasquez») y Perry Allen, de la legación dominicana. Como resultado de la reunión, la República Dominicana aceptó el consejo del doctor Hill de que probablemente existía una base equitativa de arreglo y de que las negociaciones debían llevarse a cabo directamente entre las partes en conflicto y no por intermedio del gobierno de los Estados Unidos.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Belgian envoy Willem Willems presented the State Department with legal credentials representing 3,619 European bondholders holding over twelve million dollars in Dominican bonds. Willems informed American officials that the European bondholders supported the Dominican government in its dispute with the San Domingo Improvement Company. He argued that the contract granting the American syndicate control over customs revenues was legally invalid because it was never ratified by the bondholders as required.

Willems comunicó a los funcionarios estadounidenses que los tenedores de bonos europeos respaldaban al gobierno dominicano en su disputa con la San Domingo Improvement Company. Sostuvo que el contrato que otorgaba al consorcio estadounidense el control sobre los ingresos aduaneros carecía de validez legal por no haber sido nunca ratificado por los tenedores de bonos conforme se exigía.

records.summary_en: Continuing an account of a legal complaint in the New-York Tribune, this passage states that sixty-five thousand dollars in stock was returned and $12,500 was later paid in cash before San Domingo company directors Weed, Brown, and Wells were voted out of office. Newly elected officers found $137,000 in San Domingo Government scrip certificates carrying $14,980 in unpaid interest arrears, and were informed by the Dominican government that the San Domingo Finance Company had already received funds to pay interest charges and faced cancellation of its contract over unpaid scrip interest. The bill further alleges that Weed, Brown, and Wells organized the San Dominican Railroad Company, broke an original construction contract with New York's Drake Stratton Construction Company for the Puerto Plata–Santiago railroad, caused the railroad company to confess a judgment dated two years back and secured by improvement and finance company assets, and intentionally formed corporations to deceive the public.

records.summary_en: The *San Antonio Daily Light* reported rising tensions along the Haitian-Dominican border following the failure of a joint boundary commission established under the Sam-Heureaux convention. Haitian authorities accused Dominican forces of illegally occupying frontier positions that Haitian troops had evacuated in good faith to facilitate negotiations. Violent skirmishes erupted at Philobert along the Massacre River, where Haitian border posts established to suppress smuggling came under repeated Dominican attack.

records.headline: Opening mid-sentence with information attributed to persons
records.summary_en: Opening mid-sentence with information attributed to persons recently returned from the island, the Deseret Evening News presents a historical sketch stating that what is known as the Dominican Republic, or Santo Domingo, was once "a province of the republic of Hayti." According to the paper, internal troubles and anarchy resulting from the revolution that overthrew President Boyer after twenty-five years in office—dated in the OCR text as 1841—led the eastern portion of the island to secede and proclaim its independence, which the Haytien government later recognized in a year obscured by conflicting OCR readings. Before breaking off mid-sentence, the article notes that the delicate question of frontier delimitation arose because the Dominican Republic's territory has never been defined.
records.summary_es: Comenzando a mitad de frase con informes atribuidos a personas recién regresadas de la isla, el Deseret Evening News ofrece una reseña histórica según la cual lo que se conoce como República Dominicana, o Santo Domingo, fue alguna vez «una provincia de la república de Haití». De acuerdo con el periódico, los disturbios internos y la anarquía derivados de la revolución que derrocó al presidente Boyer tras veinticinco años en el cargo —fechada en el texto impreso con OCR como 1841— propiciaron la separación de la parte oriental de la isla y la proclamación de su independencia, reconocida posteriormente por el gobierno haitiano en un año afectado por lecturas conflictivas de OCR. Antes de cortarse a mitad de oración, el artículo señala que la delicada cuestión de la delimitación fronteriza surgió porque el territorio de la República Dominicana nunca ha sido definido.

records.summary_en: The *Morning Astorian* reported on the breakdown of the joint boundary commission that convened at Anses-à-Pitres to define the Haitian-Dominican border based on 1874 territorial positions. Negotiations collapsed after Dominican delegates insisted on conditional compliance and Dominican troops moved into vacated frontier points, prompting Haitian accusations of bad faith. Tensions escalated sharply following armed confrontations at Philobert near the Massacre River, where Haitian border outposts repelled attacks from Dominican territory.

Las negociaciones fracasaron luego de que los delegados dominicanos insistieran en un cumplimiento condicional y las tropas dominicanas avanzaran hacia puntos fronterizos desocupados, lo que motivó acusaciones haitianas de mala fe. Las tensiones se intensificaron bruscamente tras choques armados en Philobert, cerca del río Masacre, donde los puestos fronterizos haitianos repelieron ataques procedentes de territorio dominicano.

records.summary_en: In a May 24 dispatch from New York citing that day's Herald, The Topeka State Journal outlines the terms of a reported settlement involving the Dominican government and the San Domingo Improvement and Finance companies. Under the reported agreement, the Dominican government is to buy the companies' interests at a price to be agreed upon, while the improvement company renounces all rights and privileges and, together with its affiliated companies, must submit a detailed accounting by a June date garbled in print. The Dominican government will also acquire the National Bank of San Domingo and the railroad connecting Santiago, Moca, and Macoris, and—before the text cuts off at an adjacent advertisement—will take over "800,000 of the Dominican 4."
records.summary_es: En un despacho fechado el 24 de mayo en Nueva York que cita al Herald de ese día, The Topeka State Journal expone los términos de un supuesto acuerdo entre el gobierno dominicano y las compañías de mejoras y finanzas de San Domingo. Según el convenio reportado, el gobierno dominicano comprará los intereses de dichas empresas a un precio por convenir, mientras que la compañía de mejoras renuncia a todos sus derechos y privilegios y, junto con sus compañías afiliadas, deberá presentar una rendición detallada de cuentas antes de una fecha de junio ilegible en el impreso. El gobierno dominicano adquirirá además el Banco Nacional de San Domingo y el ferrocarril que une Santiago, Moca y Macoris, y —antes de que el texto se interrumpa ante un anuncio comercial vecino— asumirá «800,000 of the Dominican 4».

records.headline: Opening mid-article after a reference to 1874, the Western Kansas World explains
records.summary_en: Opening mid-article after a reference to 1874, the Western Kansas World explains that frontier delimitation became an issue because the Dominican Republic's territory has never been defined, and reports that Haytiens regard a recent northern border incident at Phitobert—where Haytien posts  combating cross-border smuggling and brigandage have fended off repeated attacks—as premeditated Dominican provocation endangering relations between the two republics. By mutual consent, the River Massacre separating the Dominican province of Dajabon (or Laxavon) from Haytien territory had long been provisionally accepted as the natural boundary, with the right bank acknowledged as belonging to Santo Domingo and the left bank to Hayti. Before breaking off mid-sentence, the writer recounts that a year or two ago residents on the Dominican right bank conceived the idea of expanding Dominican territory by diverting the river's course.
records.summary_es: Comenzando a mitad de artículo tras una mención de 1874, el Western Kansas World explica que la delimitación fronteriza surgió porque el territorio de la República Dominicana nunca ha sido definido, e informa que los haitianos consideran un reciente incidente en Phitobert, en la frontera norte —donde puestos haitianos establecidos contra el contrabando y el bandolerismo transfronterizos han debido defenderse de repetidos ataques—, como una provocación premeditada dominicana que pone en grave peligro las relaciones entre ambas repúblicas. De mutuo acuerdo, el río Massacre, que separa la provincia dominicana de Dajabon (o Laxavon) del territorio haitiano, había sido aceptado provisionalmente durante mucho tiempo como límite natural, reconociéndose la margen derecha a Santo Domingo y la izquierda a Haití. Antes de interrumpirse a mitad de frase, el autor relata que hace uno o dos años habitantes de la margen derecha concibieron la idea de ampliar el territorio dominicano desviando el cauce del río.

records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune, describing General Gomez's departure in good health aboard the steamer Seguranca amid cheering Cubans on the pier, notes that Gomez bade farewell by embracing Dr. William F. Holcombe, Tomas Estrada Palma, and José Ellis Cambiaso, a grandson of Dominican admiral J. B. Cambiaso and former Chancellor of the Dominican Republic. Cambiaso remarked that many Cubans favored a government modeled on the Swiss Confederation, adding that he believed a confederation of Cuba, San Domingo, and Hayti with a U.S.-style constitution under U.S. government protection would be the best form of government for the peoples of those islands.

records.headline: In an item addressing Dominican-Haitian border delimitation
records.summary_en: In an item addressing Dominican-Haitian border delimitation, the Freeland Tribune reports that an incident at Phitobert on the northern frontier has gravely endangered relations between the two republics, with Haitians viewing it as premeditated Dominican provocation. Haitian border posts established to curb cross-border smuggling and brigandage have repeatedly defended against attacks along the frontier. By mutual consent, the Massacre River dividing the Dominican province of Dajabon (or Baxavon) from Haitian territory had long served as the provisional boundary, with the right bank acknowledged as Santo Domingo and the left bank as Haiti. The paper adds that residents on the Dominican side recently attempted to expand their territory by scheming to alter the river's course.
records.summary_es: En una nota sobre la delimitación fronteriza domínico-haitiana, el Freeland Tribune informa que un incidente ocurrido en Phitobert, en la frontera norte, ha puesto en grave peligro las relaciones entre ambas repúblicas, pues los haitianos lo consideran una provocación dominicana premeditada. Los puestos haitianos establecidos para reprimir el contrabando y el bandolerismo transfronterizo han debido defenderse de reiterados ataques a lo largo de la frontera. Por mutuo acuerdo, el río Masacre, que divide la provincia dominicana de Dajabón (o Baxavón) del territorio haitiano, había servido durante mucho tiempo como límite provisional, reconociéndose la margen derecha a Santo Domingo y la margen izquierda a Haití. El periódico añade que habitantes del lado dominicano intentaron recientemente ampliar su territorio planeando alterar el curso del río.

records.headline: The patriots won, the Spaniards were forced to capitulate, and Gomez
records.summary_en: The *Phillipsburg Herald* reviewed the military career of General Máximo Gómez, noting his early service with Spanish forces during the Dominican annexation before becoming a leader in Cuba's ten years' war for independence. In 1887, Gómez returned to Santo Domingo to cultivate tobacco in Guayubín near Monte Cristi, where his widespread popularity quickly aroused political suspicion. Fearing that Gómez harbored presidential ambitions and planned an insurrection, President Heureaux secretly arranged for his arrest and execution.
records.summary_es: El *Phillipsburg Herald* repasó la carrera militar del general Máximo Gómez, destacando su servicio inicial en las fuerzas españolas durante la anexión dominicana antes de convertirse en un caudillo de la guerra de los Diez Años por la independencia de Cuba. En 1887, Gómez regresó a Santo Domingo para cultivar tabaco en Guayubín, cerca de Monte Cristi, donde su inmensa popularidad despertó pronto suspicacias políticas. Por temor a que Gómez albergara ambiciones presidenciales y tramara una insurrección, el presidente Heureaux dispuso secretamente su arresto y ejecución.
