records.headline: An unnamed observer in the Phillipsburg Herald, recounting an episode of unwritten
records.summary_en: An unnamed observer in the Phillipsburg Herald, recounting an episode of unwritten history concerning General Gomez ("Don Maximo"), asserts that the Cuban leader never realized how near he came to imprisonment and death in Santo Domingo, from which he was saved only through the intervention of the United States consulate. After being confined to the city and granted a passport, Gomez departed for Haiti and Jamaica before leading Cuban revolutionary forces alongside Maceo. The commentator further states that Gomez was at heart an annexationist who had favored the annexation of Santo Domingo to the United States under the Biaz administration, praising him as the ideal first president for a Cuban republic.
records.summary_es: Un observador no identificado en el Phillipsburg Herald, al relatar un episodio de historia no escrita sobre el general Gómez ("Don Máximo"), afirma que el líder cubano nunca supo cuán cerca estuvo de la prisión y la muerte en Santo Domingo, de las cuales se salvó únicamente gracias a la intervención del consulado de los Estados Unidos. Tras haber tenido la ciudad por cárcel y recibir su pasaporte, Gómez partió hacia Haití y Jamaica antes de encabezar a las fuerzas revolucionarias cubanas junto a Maceo. El comentarista señala además que Gómez era en el fondo un anexionista que había favorecido la anexión de Santo Domingo a los Estados Unidos bajo la administración de Biaz, elogiándolo como el primer presidente ideal para una república cubana.

records.summary_en: A biographical account in the Richmond Dispatch relates that as a young soldier from "Ciebo," Gomez allied with the annexationists and fought alongside the Spaniards during the Dominican War of the Restoration before departing for Havana as a Mariscal de Campo and later fighting in Cuba's Ten Years' War. records.headline: A Santo Domingo dispatch of April 1 in The Wilmington Daily Republican reports
records.summary_en: A Santo Domingo dispatch of April 1 in The Wilmington Daily Republican reports that revolutionists attacked and captured the southern coastal town of Barahona after a severe engagement that left forty killed or wounded. A government gunboat subsequently bombarded the town and landed troops who recaptured Barahona, forcing the insurgents to withdraw to a nearby stronghold. In response to the outbreak, the Dominican minister of war proceeded to the area to restore order, while the Dominican congress decreed martial law throughout the republic and suspended constitutional guarantees.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del 1 de abril desde Santo Domingo en The Wilmington Daily Republican informa que los revolucionarios atacaron y tomaron la ciudad costera sureña de Barahona tras un fuerte enfrentamiento que dejó cuarenta muertos o heridos. Posteriormente, un cañonero gubernamental bombardeó la población y desembarcó tropas que la recuperaron, obligando a los insurgentes a replegarse hacia una fortaleza en los alrededores. Ante la sublevación, el ministro de Guerra dominicano se trasladó a la zona para restablecer el orden, mientras que el congreso dominicano decretó la ley marcial en toda la república y suspendió las garantías constitucionales.

records.headline: The town of Barahona, on the south coast, was at tacked
records.summary_en: The *Arizona Republican* reported that Dominican insurgents captured the southern coastal town of Barahona after heavy fighting that resulted in forty casualties. A government gunboat subsequently bombarded the port and landed forces that successfully recaptured the town, driving the rebels into nearby strongholds. In response to the uprising, the Dominican Congress suspended constitutional guarantees and declared nationwide martial law.
records.summary_es: El *Arizona Republican* informó que insurgentes dominicanos tomaron la localidad costera meridional de Barahona tras intensos combates que causaron cuarenta bajas. Con posterioridad, un cañonero gubernamental bombardeó el puerto y desembarcó tropas que recuperaron con éxito la ciudad, obligando a los rebeldes a replegarse hacia reductos cercanos. En respuesta a la sublevación, el Congreso dominicano suspendió las garantías constitucionales y declaró la ley marcial en todo el territorio nacional.
records.passage: Insurgent Gains Government Puts Island Under Martial Law. San Domingo, Republic of Santo Domingo, March 31. The town of Barahona, on the south coast, was attacked and captured by revolutionists after a severe fight in which forty were killed or wounded. Later a government gunboat bombarded Barahona and landed troops, who retook the town. The revolutionists retired to a stronghold in the neighborhood. The Dominican minister of war proceeded to Barahona with other troops and will take severe measures to re-establish order. Revolutionary activity is for the present confined to Barahona. The Dominican congress has declared that martial law shall be established throughout the whole republic and that constitutional guarantees be suspended. FROM DULUTH TO THE GULF Funds Raised for a Road to Cut "All Trans-Continental Lines. Duluth, Minn.. March 31. The News- Tribune publishes a statement to the effect that the banques Francaise and Colonial of Paris and Belgium have agreed to take $12,000,000 of the bonds for the building of the Manitoba Gulf railroad on a basis of 95 per cent. The road will run from Duluth to Omaha and Kansas City, cutting every one of the great trans-continental lines. It is the intentions of the promoters to either make connections with the Gould interests or continue the road as an independent line to the gulf. Work will commence immediately.

records.headline: The gunboat Machias was ordered to proceed to San Domingo City
records.summary_en: The gunboat Machias was ordered to proceed to San Domingo City and Samana Bay to protect American interests during the Dominican outbreak, according to The Washington Times; the Machias, under Commander Henry McCrea, was stationed at San Juan, Puerto Rico. Following the unrest, it was revealed that the Dominican consul general in New York had visited the State Department the prior week, warning that an uprising would likely occur unless liberal tariff concessions were granted to Santo Domingo. The consul argued that proposed U.S. reciprocity with Cuba would severely disadvantage Dominican sugar and provoke rebellion, though the State Department offered no encouragement due to legislative resistance and the Senate's rejection of earlier West Indian reciprocity treaties.
records.summary_es: El cañonero Machias, estacionado en San Juan de Puerto Rico bajo el mando del comandante Henry McCrea, recibió órdenes de trasladarse a la ciudad de Santo Domingo y a la bahía de Samaná para proteger los intereses estadounidenses durante los disturbios dominicanos, según The Washington Times. A raíz de la insurrección, se supo que el cónsul general dominicano en Nueva York había visitado el Departamento de Estado la semana anterior, advirtiendo que probablemente estallaría un levantamiento a menos que se concedieran concesiones arancelarias liberales a Santo Domingo. El cónsul sostuvo que la reciprocidad propuesta entre Estados Unidos y Cuba perjudicaría gravemente al azúcar dominicano y desataría una rebelión, aunque el Departamento de Estado no ofreció aliento alguno ante la resistencia legislativa y la negativa del Senado a ratificar los tratados previos de reciprocidad con las islas de las Indias Occidentales.

Powell stated that the Dominican insurrection was spreading slowly and had reached Azura province, where rumors reported fighting on April 7, prompting the government to dispatch troops and put about 2,400 men into the field with further reinforcements planned. Since sending that written dispatch, Powell telegraphed the State Department to report that the rebellion has been crushed.

records.headline: Telegraphic communication between Haiti and Santo Domingo has been completely
records.summary_en: Telegraphic communication between Haiti and Santo Domingo has been completely severed following another revolution, reports an April 29 Port-au-Prince dispatch in the Evening Times-Republican. Dispatches received in the Haitian capital from the northern Dominican port of Porto Plata state that Santiago is the center of the revolt, which is led by Vice President Horatio Vasquez (rendered in the text as "Vanquez"). Observers in Port-au-Prince nevertheless believe that Dominican government forces will likely suppress the uprising.

Los informes recibidos en la capital haitiana desde el puerto dominicano norteño de Puerto Plata señalan a Santiago como el centro de la revuelta, la cual está encabezada por el vicepresidente Horacio Vásquez (mencionado en el texto como "Vanquez"). No obstante, en Puerto Príncipe se cree que las fuerzas del gobierno dominicano probablemente sofocarán la insurrección.

All of the Cibao ("ilm.i") region, with the sole exception of Puerto Plata on the north coast, is in the hands of the revolutionists, while another uprising has erupted in the south. The Dominican government's position appears critical as overland telegraph communication has been cut, leaving news difficult to obtain.

Toda la región del Cibao ("ilm.i"), con la única excepción de Puerto Plata en la costa norte, se halla en poder de los revolucionarios, mientras que otro levantamiento ha estallado en el sur. La posición del gobierno dominicano parece crítica debido a que los rebeldes han cortado la comunicación telegráfica terrestre, dificultando la obtención de noticias.

records.summary_en: Page 1 of The Topeka State Journal carries an April 30 Cape Haytien dispatch reporting that General Navarro, sent to reinforce government troops at Guayabin ("Guayanbun"), defected to the Dominican revolutionists and marched against Monte Cristi, prompting Governor Garcia to evacuate his troops and munitions to Puerto Plata. An outbreak also occurred at Sanchez on Samana Bay, while fighting took place yesterday at Sosua ("Pocua" / "Socua"). During the engagement at Sosua, the local agent of the American United Fruit Company was forced to flee his home and seek shelter with his family on coastal rocks, leading the local governor to dispatch reinforcements.

También se produjo un estallido en Sánchez, en la bahía de Samaná, mientras que ayer se libraron combates en Sosúa ("Pocua" / "Socua"). records.headline: Insurgents led by Vice President Vasquez have advanced to near
records.summary_en: Insurgents led by Vice President Vasquez have advanced to near Cotuy ("Cotyiy") and Santo Domingo, holding nearly all of the Cibao region while a separate uprising erupts in the south, according to dispatches in the Santa Fe New Mexican. In the north, General Navarro defected with his relief force at Guayabin ("Cuaban") and marched on Monte Cristi, forcing Governor Garcia to abandon the city, while outbreaks occurred at Sanchez and a battle was fought at Sosua. Under the subhead "A Clyde Line Steamer Held," an April 30 Cape Haytien dispatch adds that the governor of Puerto Plata detained the Clyde Line steamer Cherokee bound for Samana over her commander's protest.
records.summary_es: Los insurgentes liderados por el vicepresidente Vásquez han avanzado cerca de Cotuy ("Cotyiy") y Santo Domingo, controlando casi toda la región del Cibao mientras estalla un levantamiento aparte en el sur, según despachos en el Santa Fe New Mexican. En el norte, el general Navarro desertó con sus fuerzas de auxilio en Guayabín ("Cuaban") y marchó sobre Monte Cristi, obligando al gobernador García a abandonar la plaza, al tiempo que se producían brotes en Sánchez y se libraba una batalla en Sosúa. Bajo el subtítulo "A Clyde Line Steamer Held", un despacho del 30 de abril desde Cape Haytien añade que el gobernador de Puerto Plata retuvo al vapor Cherokee de la Línea Clyde con destino a Samaná, a pesar de la protesta de su comandante.

records.headline: In The St. Louis Republic, advices indicate that the Dominican government
records.summary_en: In The St. Louis Republic, advices indicate that the Dominican government faces a critical situation after revolutionists severed land telegraph lines. General Navarro, dispatched to reinforce government forces at Guayuban, joined the Dominican insurgents and marched on Monte Cristi, compelling the local governor to abandon the post and withdraw with his munitions toward Puerto Plata. records.summary_en: A Port-au-Prince dispatch in the Oakes Republican reports that another revolution has erupted in Santo Domingo, completely severing telegraphic communication with Haiti. Advices from the north-coast seaport of Porto Plata identify Santiago as the focal point of the uprising, which is led by Vice President Horatio Vasquez. Observers in the Haitian capital nevertheless believe the rebellion will likely be suppressed by the Dominican government.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Puerto Príncipe en el Oakes Republican informa que ha estallado otra revolución en Santo Domingo, interrumpiendo por completo la comunicación telegráfica con Haití. Informes recibidos desde el puerto de Puerto Plata, en la costa norte, señalan a Santiago como el centro de los disturbios revolucionarios, dirigidos por el vicepresidente Horatio Vasquez. Observadores en la capital haitiana consideran sin embargo que la rebelión probablemente será sofocada por el gobierno dominicano.

records.headline: The Daily Morning Journal and Courier prints multiple dispatches
records.summary_en: The Daily Morning Journal and Courier prints multiple dispatches detailing the rapid spread of the Dominican revolution against President Jimenez. A report from Cape Haytien notes that the insurrection's leader, Vice President Horacio Vasquez, has reached Guerra near the capital, with the government's collapse imminent, while Porto Plata remains quiet under Governor General Deschamps, who has resolved to defend the port with concentrated troops and a Dominican war vessel. Further dispatches from San Domingo and Port-au-Prince indicate that lines of communication to the interior are cut and that Vasquez's forces control nearly the entire republic.
records.summary_es: The Daily Morning Journal and Courier publica múltiples despachos que detallan la rápida propagación de la revolución dominicana contra el presidente Jiménez. Un informe procedente de Cabo Haitiano señala que el líder de la insurrección, el vicepresidente Horacio Vásquez, ha llegado a Guerra, cerca de la capital, con la inminente caída del gobierno, mientras que Puerto Plata permanece en calma bajo el mando del gobernador general Deschamps, quien ha resuelto defender el puerto con tropas concentradas y un buque de guerra dominicano. Otros despachos de Santo Domingo y Puerto Príncipe indican que las líneas de comunicación con el interior están cortadas y que las fuerzas de Vásquez controlan casi toda la república.

records.headline: Dispatches from Port-au-Prince and San Domingo covering the uprising
records.summary_en: Dispatches from Port-au-Prince and San Domingo covering the uprising led by Vice President Horacio Vasquez are printed in The Portland Daily Press. According to the wire reports, Vasquez's insurgent forces hold nearly all of the republic except Puerto Plata and the capital, and were advancing on San Domingo in strong numbers. While telegraphic communication with the interior has been severed, the Dominican government is taking active measures to defend the capital, which remained quiet awaiting events.
records.summary_es: The Portland Daily Press publica despachos de Puerto Príncipe y Santo Domingo que cubren el levantamiento encabezado por el vicepresidente Horacio Vásquez. Según los informes cablegráficos, las fuerzas insurgentes de Vásquez controlan casi toda la república salvo Puerto Plata y la capital, y avanzaban en gran número hacia Santo Domingo. Aunque la comunicación telegráfica con el interior ha sido cortada, el gobierno dominicano toma medidas activas para defender la capital, que permanecía en calma a la espera de los acontecimientos.

records.headline: Dispatches compiled in the Wheeling Register trace the rapid
records.summary_en: Dispatches compiled in the Wheeling Register trace the rapid escalation of the Dominican insurrection headed by Vice President Horacio Vasquez. While Governor General Deschamps prepares to defend Porto Plata with concentrated government troops and a Dominican war vessel, rebel forces have seized control of the rest of the republic outside the capital. Wire reports from San Domingo note that communications to the interior have been severed, with Vasquez advancing with a large force and expected to arrive before the capital today.
records.summary_es: Los despachos recopilados en el Wheeling Register relatan la rápida escalada de la insurrección dominicana encabezada por el vicepresidente Horacio Vásquez. Mientras el gobernador general Deschamps se prepara para defender Puerto Plata con tropas gubernamentales concentradas y un buque de guerra dominicano, las fuerzas rebeldes han tomado el control del resto de la república fuera de la capital. Los informes cablegráficos de Santo Domingo señalan que las comunicaciones con el interior han sido cortadas, con Vásquez avanzando con una gran fuerza y previsto a llegar ante la capital hoy.

records.headline: The Evening Times, reporting from Washington, summarizes dispatches
records.summary_en: The Evening Times, reporting from Washington, summarizes dispatches from William F. Powell, United States minister to the Dominican Republic, who reported that the current revolution is led by the Dominican vice president. A second dispatch confirmed the settlement of the Sala & Co. claim for approximately $260,000, which originated from funds loaned to President Hippolyte for weapons and ammunition and which a previous administration had sought to repudiate. In response to these developments, the State Department requested that the Navy dispatch a warship to San Domingo, with the gunboat Machias expected to be assigned to protect American interests.
records.summary_es: The Evening Times, informando desde Washington, resume los despachos de William F. Powell, ministro de los Estados Unidos ante la República Dominicana, quien informó que la actual revolución está encabezada por el vicepresidente dominicano. Un segundo despacho confirmó el arreglo de la reclamación de Sala & Co. por aproximadamente 260.000 dólares, la cual se originó a partir de fondos prestados al presidente Hippolyte para armamento y municiones y que una administración anterior había intentado repudiar. En respuesta a estos sucesos, el Departamento de Estado solicitó que la Armada envíe un buque de guerra a Santo Domingo, esperándose que el cañonero Machias sea asignado para proteger los intereses estadounidenses.

records.headline: The New-York Tribune provides an overview of Dominican affairs
records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune provides an overview of Dominican affairs, reporting that insurgent forces under Vice-President Horacio Vasquez have overrun most of the country and are advancing on the capital as the government prepares its defense. A parallel dispatch reveals that United States Minister William F. Powell has secured a full settlement from the Dominican government for the longstanding Sala claim. The claim originated from war munitions and money supplied to the late President Heureaux by a Frenchman named Sala, whose American widow in New York subsequently pursued the debt with the assistance of the State Department.
records.summary_es: El New-York Tribune ofrece un panorama de los asuntos dominicanos al informar que las fuerzas insurgentes bajo el vicepresidente Horacio Vásquez han dominado la mayor parte del país y avanzan hacia la capital mientras el gobierno prepara su defensa. Un despacho paralelo revela que el ministro de los Estados Unidos, William F. Powell, ha logrado un arreglo definitivo con el gobierno dominicano para la antigua reclamación Sala. Dicha reclamación se originó a partir de municiones bélicas y dinero suministrados al difunto presidente Heureaux por un francés llamado Sala, cuya viuda estadounidense en Nueva York reclamó posteriormente la deuda con la asistencia del Departamento de Estado.

records.headline: Dispatches in the Evening Star, under the heading 'Santo Domingo Reported Taken,' describe
records.summary_en: Dispatches in the Evening Star, under the heading 'Santo Domingo Reported Taken,' describe conflicting developments in the Dominican rebellion. An initial report from Port-au-Prince states that rebel forces under the general commanding the reinforcements at Santiago were defeated by government troops, momentarily strengthening the executive's standing. However, a later dispatch from Jacmel announces that the capital, Santo Domingo, surrendered on Saturday to insurgent forces, forcing President Jiminez to seek asylum in the French consulate, while earlier reports confirmed that Vice President Horatio Vasquez was marching on the capital amidst severed telegraphic lines.
records.summary_es: Despachos en el Evening Star, bajo el encabezado «Se informa de la toma de Santo Domingo», describen acontecimientos contradictorios en la rebelión dominicana. Un informe inicial desde Puerto Príncipe señala que las fuerzas rebeldes bajo el general al mando de los refuerzos en Santiago fueron derrotadas por tropas del gobierno, fortaleciendo momentáneamente la posición del ejecutivo. Sin embargo, un despacho posterior desde Jacmel anuncia que la capital, Santo Domingo, se rindió el sábado ante las fuerzas insurgentes, obligando al presidente Jimenes a buscar asilo en el consulado francés, mientras informes previos confirmaban que el vicepresidente Horacio Vásquez marchaba hacia la capital en medio de líneas telegráficas cortadas.

records.summary_en: According to a Washington dispatch in The San Francisco Call, United States officials expressed satisfaction that American Minister Powell's request for naval protection in the Dominican Republic had been approved following the reported fall of Santo Domingo. Powell was informed that the cruiser Cincinnati had been ordered to the country to protect American interests. The dispatch further notes that Powell had caused the arrest of Charles H. Loinaz, the Norwegian vice consul at Porto Plata, on charges of conspiring to overthrow the Jiminez administration, though the local consular corps subsequently secured his release.
records.summary_es: Según un despacho de Washington en The San Francisco Call, las autoridades de los Estados Unidos expresaron satisfacción de que se hubiera aprobado la solicitud de protección naval del ministro estadounidense Powell en la República Dominicana tras la reportada caída de Santo Domingo. Se le informó a Powell que el crucero Cincinnati había sido enviado al país para proteger los intereses estadounidenses. El despacho añade además que Powell había ordenado el arresto de Charles H. Loinaz, vicecónsul noruego en Puerto Plata, acusado de conspirar para derrocar al gobierno de Jimenes, aunque el cuerpo consular local logró posteriormente su liberación.

records.summary_en: The *Minneapolis Journal* reported that Dominican Vice President Horacio Vásquez broke with President Juan Isidro Jimenes over detrimental financial contracts and successfully captured the capital. President Jimenes sought asylum in the French consulate following the city's capitulation, while Governor Deschamps at Puerto Plata refused to yield without direct executive orders. In response to the crisis, the United States Navy dispatched the cruiser *Cincinnati* under rush orders to protect American interests.
records.summary_es: El *Minneapolis Journal* informó que el vicepresidente dominicano Horacio Vásquez rompió con el presidente Juan Isidro Jimenes por causa de contratos financieros perjudiciales y tomó con éxito la capital. El presidente Jimenes buscó asilo en el consulado francés tras la capitulación de la ciudad, mientras el gobernador Deschamps en Puerto Plata se negaba a rendirse sin órdenes ejecutivas directas. En respuesta a la crisis, la Armada de los Estados Unidos despachó con órdenes perentorias al crucero *Cincinnati* para proteger los intereses estadounidenses.

records.headline: Dispatches in The Daily Morning Journal and Courier announce
records.summary_en: Dispatches in The Daily Morning Journal and Courier announce that the capital of the Dominican Republic has surrendered to insurgent forces. President Jiminez is reported to have sought protection at the French consulate in Santo Domingo, with communications remaining heavily disrupted. A referenced dispatch from Puerto Plata dated April 26 notes that Vice President Horatio Vasquez, the leader of the uprising, had been marching directly against the capital to depose Jiminez.
records.summary_es: Despachos en The Daily Morning Journal and Courier anuncian que la capital de la República Dominicana se ha rendido ante las fuerzas insurgentes. Se informa que el presidente Jimenes ha buscado protección en el consulado francés de Santo Domingo, mientras las comunicaciones permanecen gravemente interrumpidas. Un despacho citado de Puerto Plata con fecha del 26 de abril señala que el vicepresidente Horacio Vásquez, líder del levantamiento, había estado marchando directamente hacia la capital para deponer a Jimenes.

President Jiminez was also confirmed to have sought refuge in the French consulate at the capital. Meanwhile, negotiations between the revolutionists and General Deschamps, the governor of Puerto Plata, for the surrender of that port have fallen through, as Deschamps refuses to surrender without an order from the Dominican government.

records.headline: Vice President Horacio Vasquez has overthrown the government of President Juan I. Jiminez
records.summary_en: Vice President Horacio Vasquez has overthrown the government of President Juan I. Jiminez, an article in The Beatrice Daily Express reports, after field operations of less than two weeks. Friends of Vasquez claim he tried to support Jiminez until the president signed contracts financially harmful to the republic. In Puerto Plata, Governor Deschamps arrested Norwegian vice consul Charles H. Loinaz for allegedly conspiring against Jiminez, though foreign consuls secured his release. Deschamps commands a small troop detachment and a warship in port, but the town is expected to fall soon, while the 40-year-old Dominican-born Vasquez is expected to assume power immediately.

Deschamps comanda un pequeño destacamento de tropas y un buque de guerra en el puerto, pero se espera que la ciudad caiga pronto, mientras que Vasquez, dominicano de 40 años de edad, asumirá el poder de inmediato.

records.headline: President Juan Jiminez has been overthrown by Vice President Horacio Vasquez
records.summary_en: President Juan Jiminez has been overthrown by Vice President Horacio Vasquez in field operations lasting under two weeks, The Indianapolis Journal reports. Until recently, relations between the two leaders appeared cordial, but Vasquez's associates state he turned against Jiminez over government contracts that damaged national finances. In Puerto Plata, Governor Deschamps arrested Charles H. Loinaz, the Norwegian vice consul, on conspiracy charges before foreign consuls intervened to secure his release. Deschamps maintains a small garrison and a small warship in port, but the town is expected to fall quickly, clearing the way for the Dominican-born Vasquez to assume power.

Hasta hace poco, las relaciones entre ambos líderes parecían cordiales, pero los allegados a Vasquez afirman que se volvió contra Jiminez debido a contratos gubernamentales perjudiciales para las finanzas públicas. En Puerto Plata, el gobernador Deschamps arrestó a Charles H. Loinaz, vicecónsul noruego, bajo cargos de conspiración antes de que los cónsules extranjeros intervinieran para asegurar su liberación. Deschamps mantiene una pequeña guarnición y un pequeño buque de guerra en el puerto, pero se espera que la ciudad caiga rápidamente, allanando el camino para que Vasquez, nacido en el país, asuma el poder.

Vasquez, a Dominican described as progressive and honorable, began his campaign about two weeks ago following disputes over presidential contracts, and Puerto Plata's resisting garrison is expected to surrender soon.

Vasquez, un dominicano calificado de progresista y honorable, comenzó su campaña hace unas dos semanas tras discrepancias sobre contratos presidenciales, y se espera que la guarnición de Puerto Plata, que aún resiste, se rinda pronto.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that foreign diplomats led by United States Minister Powell intervened during General Horacio Vásquez's advance on Santo Domingo to ensure civilian safety under the rules of war. Although Vásquez initially agreed to a temporary truce, insurgent troops occupied positions along the Ozama River to control the harbor. Finding the insurgents in effective control of the city, the diplomatic corps facilitated negotiations between Vásquez and the Jimenes administration for a formal capitulation.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que diplomáticos extranjeros encabezados por el ministro estadounidense Powell intervinieron durante el avance del general Horacio Vásquez sobre Santo Domingo para garantizar la seguridad de los civiles conforme a las leyes de la guerra. Aunque Vásquez aceptó inicialmente una tregua provisional, las tropas insurgentes ocuparon posiciones a lo largo del río Ozama para dominar el puerto. Al constatar que los sublevados tenían el control efectivo de la ciudad, el cuerpo diplomático facilitó las negociaciones entre Vásquez y el gobierno de Jimenes para una capitulación formal.

The messenger returned with the reply that the revolutionary general had appointed the following morning for the interview, adding that, in the meanwhile, he would suspend all hostilities If the government would agree to adopt the same course. During that evening, however. Gen. records.summary_en: A Monte Cristo dispatch in The Portland Daily Press reports that the provisional government established by Horatio Vasquez will remain in power until elections can be held. Vasquez, the former vice president, led a successful uprising against President Jiminez, and his forces occupied Santo Domingo City last week following its capitulation. Peace is described as fully restored in the southern part of the republic, and an order suspending hostilities has been signed to facilitate discussion of surrender terms.

Vasquez, el exvicepresidente, lideró una exitosa sublevación contra el presidente Jiminez, y sus fuerzas ocuparon la ciudad de Santo Domingo la semana pasada tras su capitulación. Se describe que la paz ha quedado totalmente restablecida en la parte sur de la república, y se ha firmado una orden de suspensión de hostilidades para facilitar la discusión de los términos de rendición.

Vasquez, el exvicepresidente dominicano, depuso al presidente Jiminez, y sus fuerzas tomaron posesión de la ciudad de Santo Domingo tras la capitulación de la capital la semana pasada. El despacho señala que la paz ha sido restablecida en la región sur de la república y que se ha firmado un armisticio para debatir los términos de la rendición entre las fuerzas revolucionarias y gubernamentales.

Advices from Puerto Plata on the north coast add that the crew of the Dominican war vessel stationed there has sided with the insurgents and delivered a surrender order to the governor.

records.headline: The Adams County news analyzes the rapid overthrow of Dominican President Juan I. Jiminez
records.summary_en: The Adams County news analyzes the rapid overthrow of Dominican President Juan I. Jiminez by Vice President Vasquez after field operations of less than two weeks, explaining that Vasquez turned against Jiminez over contracts alleged to have harmed the republic financially. Although Puerto Plata's governor, Deschamps, holds a warship and a small garrison and may offer determined resistance, the town is expected to fall quickly, and Vasquez, having spent nearly all of his forty years in the country, is prepared to assume the reins of government. A Monte Cristi dispatch of May 7 adds that flag-of-truce messengers confirmed the capital's capitulation and Jiminez's flight to the French consulate, while surrender negotiations with Deschamps collapsed over his refusal to yield without government orders.
records.summary_es: El Adams County news analiza el rápido derrocamiento del presidente dominicano Juan I. Jiminez por parte del vicepresidente Vásquez tras operaciones militares de menos de dos semanas, explicando que Vásquez se enemistó con Jiminez debido a contratos que supuestamente perjudicaron las finanzas de la república. Aunque el gobernador de Puerto Plata, Deschamps, dispone de un buque de guerra y una pequeña guarnición y podría ofrecer una enérgica resistencia, se espera que la plaza caiga pronto, y Vásquez, quien ha vivido casi todos sus cuarenta años en el país, se encuentra preparado para asumir las riendas del poder. Un despacho de Montecristi del 7 de mayo añade que emisarios bajo bandera de tregua confirmaron la capitulación de la capital y el refugio de Jiminez en el consulado francés, mientras que las negociaciones de rendición con Deschamps fracasaron porque este se negó a entregarse sin órdenes gubernamentales.

records.headline: A Port-au-Prince dispatch of May 3 in the New Ulm review states
records.summary_en: A Port-au-Prince dispatch of May 3 in the New Ulm review states that the entire republic of Santo Domingo, with the exceptions of Puerto Plata on the north coast and the capital, San Domingo, on the south coast, is in the hands of Dominican revolutionists commanded by Vice-President Vasquez. Vasquez was reported to be advancing with considerable forces and was expected to arrive before San Domingo on Friday.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del 3 de mayo desde Puerto Príncipe en el New Ulm review señala que toda la república de Santo Domingo, con las excepciones de Puerto Plata en la costa norte y la capital, Santo Domingo, en la costa sur, se encuentra en manos de los revolucionarios dominicanos comandados por el vicepresidente Vásquez. Se informaba que Vásquez avanzaba con fuerzas considerables y se esperaba que llegara ante las puertas de Santo Domingo el viernes.

records.headline: The Wheeling register reports the surrender of Puerto Plata
records.summary_en: The Wheeling register reports the surrender of Puerto Plata to Dominican revolutionists and the departure of its former governor, General Deschamps, aboard a French steamer for Hayti, while President Jiminez took refuge in the French consulate when San Domingo city capitulated. A Santo Domingo dispatch of May 2 recounts that victorious troops under General Vasquez entered the capital quietly with no public enthusiasm after two days of heavy combat that inflicted many casualties on both sides. Meanwhile, Washington advices of May 7 confirm that Jiminez signed a relinquishment of his claims to the presidency, whereupon Horatio Vasquez granted amnesty to adherents of the late government and assumed executive office.

Un despacho de Santo Domingo fechado el 2 de mayo relata que las tropas victoriosas bajo el general Vásquez entraron pacíficamente a la capital sin entusiasmo popular tras dos días de intensos combates que causaron numerosas bajas en ambos bandos. Mientras tanto, informes del 7 de mayo desde Washington confirman que Jiminez firmó la renuncia a sus reclamos a la presidencia, tras lo cual Horatio Vasquez concedió una amnistía a los partidarios del gobierno anterior y asumió la jefatura del Estado.

records.summary_en: A San Domingo dispatch in the Ottumwa semi-weekly courier, dated May 8, states that United States Minister Powell has suspended all relations with the revolutionary government owing to local unrest. Powell is preparing to leave for Hayti, where he is also accredited, on account of grave difficulties and an ongoing revolution in that republic. The dispatch further notes that the Dominican congress has been dissolved and a provisional government organized under General Horacio Vasquez.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Santo Domingo en el Ottumwa semi-weekly courier, fechado el 8 de mayo, señala que el ministro de Estados Unidos Powell ha suspendido todas las relaciones con el gobierno revolucionario debido a los disturbios locales. Powell se prepara para partir hacia Haití, país donde también está acreditado, a causa de graves dificultades y una revolución en curso en esa república. El despacho señala además que el congreso dominicano ha sido disuelto y que se ha organizado un gobierno provisional bajo la dirección del general Horacio Vasquez.

records.headline: The Houston daily post reports that the provisional government
records.summary_en: The Houston daily post reports that the provisional government under Vice President Vasquez will hold power in Santo Domingo until new elections are conducted, with peace fully reestablished in the south. At Puerto Plata, the crew of the Dominican war vessel sided with the insurgents and delivered a surrender order to General Deschamps, leading to a temporary suspension of hostilities to arrange terms of capitulation. Following the prior surrender of Santo Domingo City, where President Jiminez sought refuge in the French consulate, Puerto Plata capitulated to the revolutionists, who occupied the town and fort while Deschamps departed aboard a French steamer for Hayti.
records.summary_es: The Houston daily post informa que el gobierno provisional bajo el vicepresidente Vásquez mantendrá el poder en Santo Domingo hasta que se efectúen nuevas elecciones, habiéndose restablecido plenamente la paz en el sur. En Puerto Plata, la tripulación del buque de guerra dominicano se puso del lado de los insurgentes y entregó una orden de rendición al general Deschamps, lo que propició una suspensión temporal de las hostilidades para fijar las bases de capitulación. Tras la rendición previa de la ciudad de Santo Domingo, donde el presidente Jiminez buscó refugio en el consulado francés, Puerto Plata capituló ante los revolucionarios, quienes ocuparon la localidad y el fuerte mientras Deschamps partía hacia Haití en un vapor francés.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Times-Republican* reported that United States Minister Powell convened the diplomatic corps in Santo Domingo to safeguard foreign nationals and establish terms of engagement as insurgent forces approached. Despite an agreed temporary pause in hostilities, General Vásquez advanced his troops to command the Ozama River and secure the city. Concurrently, President Jimenes notified foreign ministers that he would agree to capitulate provided that full safety guarantees were granted to government officials and defenders.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Times-Republican* informó que el ministro de los Estados Unidos Powell convocó al cuerpo diplomático en Santo Domingo para salvaguardar a los ciudadanos extranjeros y acordar normas de beligerancia ante la aproximación de las fuerzas insurgentes. A pesar de una suspensión temporal de las hostilidades pactada, el general Vásquez avanzó sus tropas para dominar el río Ozama y asegurar la plaza. Al unísono, el presidente Jimenes comunicó a los ministros extranjeros que aceptaría capitular siempre que se otorgaran plenas garantías de seguridad a los funcionarios y defensores del gobierno.

The nature of the reply of the government was not made public. When the revolutionists were sighted, Minister Powell called a meeting of the diplomatic and consular bodies at the United States legation, with the result that a delegation, composed of the United States minister, the French minister and the Spanish, German, Italian and British consuls, was appointed to wait upon General Vasquez and inform him that no attack could be made on the capital, under the rules of war, until due notice had been given to the diplomatic and consular corps here. Vasquez appointed the following morning for an interview, adding that in the meanwhile he would suspend all hostilities. During that evening, however, Vasquez Informed the government that he was shipping munitions of war on a gunboat to San Domingo, and that he had sent troops to the River Ozama. The provisional government established there is to retain power until new elections can be held. A later dispatch reports that Puerto Plata likewise capitulated to the revolutionists, who took possession of the town and fort, while the former governor, General Deschamps, boarded a French steamer bound for Hayti, leaving Puerto Plata quiet.

El gobierno provisional allí constituido retendrá el poder hasta que puedan realizarse nuevas elecciones. Un despacho posterior señala que Puerto Plata capituló de igual modo ante los revolucionarios, quienes se apoderaron del poblado y del fuerte, mientras que el exgobernador, el general Deschamps, abordó un vapor francés rumbo a Haití, quedando Puerto Plata en completa calma.

records.summary_en: A Monte Cristi dispatch of May 7 in The Princeton union reports that the provisional government established by Horatio Vasquez will remain in power until elections take place. Vasquez, the former vice president of the Dominican Republic, led a successful revolution against President Jiminez, his forces occupying Santo Domingo city the previous week after the capital capitulated. Peace has been fully reestablished in the southern part of the republic, and an order suspending hostilities between revolutionary and government forces has been signed to enable discussions over terms of surrender.

La paz se ha restablecido plenamente en la región sur de la república, y se ha firmado una orden de suspensión de hostilidades entre las fuerzas revolucionarias y gubernamentales para permitir deliberaciones sobre las condiciones de rendición.

records.headline: San Domingo, capital of Santo Domingo, surrendered the previous Friday
records.summary_en: San Domingo, capital of Santo Domingo, surrendered the previous Friday to revolutionary forces commanded by Vice-President Vasquez, The Delaware gazette and state journal reports, with a provisional government retaining power until elections are held. Peace has been restored throughout the southern portion of the republic, while dispatches from Puerto Plata announce that the crew of the Dominican war vessel sided with the insurgents and presented Governor General Deschamps with a surrender order. A temporary suspension of hostilities was signed at Puerto Plata to arrange terms of capitulation, and President Jiminez took refuge in the French consulate when the capital surrendered.

La paz se ha restablecido en la parte sur de la república, mientras que despachos desde Puerto Plata anuncian que la tripulación del buque de guerra dominicano se pasó a los insurgentes y entregó una orden de rendición al gobernador general Deschamps. Se firmó una suspensión temporal de las hostilidades en Puerto Plata para fijar las condiciones de capitulación, y el presidente Jiminez se refugió en el consulado francés al rendirse la capital.

records.headline: President of the Dominican Republic Has Retired.
records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported that the Dominican capital surrendered to General Horacio Vásquez on May 2 following two days of severe combat outside the city. President Jimenes took refuge in the French consulate, while other officials sought asylum in the American and French legations as rebel troops occupied the capital without public demonstrations. The report added that Puerto Plata, the final stronghold loyal to Jimenes, had also capitulated, leaving Vásquez in full control of the country.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó que la capital dominicana se rindió al general Horacio Vásquez el 2 de mayo tras dos días de encarnizados combates en las afueras de la urbe. El presidente Jimenes se refugió en el consulado francés, mientras otros funcionarios solicitaron asilo en las legaciones estadounidense y francesa cuando las tropas rebeldes ocuparon la capital sin manifestaciones públicas. El informe agregó que Puerto Plata, el último bastión leal a Jimenes, también había capitulado, dejando a Vásquez con el control absoluto del país.

records.full_text:
PRESIDENT OF THE DOMINICAN REPUBLIC HAS RETIRED.

Horacio Vasquez, Leader of the Successful Revolutionary Movement, Now at Head of the Government.

SURRENDER OF PUERTO PLATA

LAST CITY THAT WAS HELD BY THE EX-PRESIDENT'S TROOPS.

New Government Probably Will Be Promptly Recognized by the United States—The Looting of a Town.

WASHINGTON, May 7.—Cable advices received here state that President Jimenez, of the Dominican Republic, has signed a relinquishment of his claims to the presidency and on his part Horacio Vasquez, the late Vice President, has granted amnesty to the adherents of the late government and assumed the presidential office.

Senor Don Foo Leonte Vasquez, the charge of the Dominican Republic, has received cable advices from home announcing the success of the revolution. It is probable that he will now become a resident minister here. Naturally the charge is desirous that the United States shall recognize at once the new government. This is a matter, however, that is by custom left to the United States minister resident, but it is not doubted that Mr. Powell will, as he has heretofore done, soon put himself in communication with the de facto government.

Puerta Plaza, the last place held by the Jimenez adherents, has capitulated.

Advices from San Domingo, under date of May 2, say the Dominican capital capitulated to-day to the revolutionary forces commanded by Gen. Horatio Vasquez, the Vice President of the republic. President Jimenez sought refuge in the French consulate and many government officers obtained shelter in the French and United States legations. The revolutionary troops entered the capital quietly. There was no enthusiasm shown by the population here at the entry of the victorious army. The approach of the revolutionists to the capital was announced after two days of heavy fighting between the government troops and the forces of General Vasquez, during which many were killed or wounded on both sides. When it became known here that General Vasquez threatened to attack Santo Domingo, the United States minister, J. S. Powell, as dean of the diplomatic corps, requested the Dominican government to inform him regarding the arrangements made to protect the lives and property of foreigners here, adding that in case no precautions were taken he would consider it his duty to take measures to provide for their safety as the situation demanded. The reply was satisfactory.

SACKING OF BARAHONA.

Sailors Describe the Capture of the Town by Revolutionists.

NEW YORK, May 7.—Members of the British brigantine Alice, Captain Inness, which has just arrived from the West Indies, report that while the brigantine lay about eighty-five yards from the shore at Barahona, on the southwest coast of San Domingo, a force of revolutionists entered the town and began discharging rifles. Inhabitants of the port ran shrieking from their homes along the beach. “The revolutionists first sacked the principal saloon in the town,” said one of the crew. “They broke all the windows, drank all the liquor in bottles and then smashed the bar. They rolled barrels of rum out into the street, and what they could not drink they turned into the gutters. Next they attacked the jail and took out all the prisoners they wanted. The freed convicts joined the insurrectionists. In the attack eleven guards and one prisoner were killed. Two civilians were killed in the woods, which thickly skirt the town at the base of the mountain. The women and children who fled along the beach sought the protection of Captain Inness, who brought off as many as the gig would hold. A sloop brought off the rest of the refugees. The refugees, 100 in number, remained about three days. Meantime about 100 government soldiers appeared and were driven to retreat by the revolutionists, who then disappeared.”

records.summary_en: The *Age-Herald* detailed the formal capitulation terms accepted by President Jimenes, which guaranteed the security of state officials, the protection of private property, and the immediate liberation of political prisoners. Insurgent troops took possession of government buildings in Santo Domingo under terms monitored by the foreign diplomatic corps, while the cruiser *Cincinnati* was en route to the island. Meanwhile, Puerto Plata surrendered to the revolutionists, and its deposed governor, General Deschamps, boarded a French steamer for Haiti.
records.summary_es: El *Age-Herald* detalló las condiciones de capitulación formal aceptadas por el presidente Jimenes, las cuales garantizaban la seguridad de los funcionarios del Estado, la protección de la propiedad privada y la liberación inmediata de los presos políticos. Tropas insurgentes tomaron posesión de los edificios gubernamentales en Santo Domingo bajo condiciones supervisadas por el cuerpo diplomático extranjero, mientras el crucero *Cincinnati* navegaba rumbo a la isla. Mientras tanto, Puerto Plata se rindió ante los revolucionarios y su depuesto gobernador, el general Deschamps, abordó un vapor francés con destino a Haití.
records.passage: Vasquez from President Jiminez consenting to the drawing up of a treaty of capitulation, which was to provide a full guarantee for the safety of the officials, employers and defenders of the government as well as for the security of per sonal property. The President and Ministers, it was further agreed, were not to leave the country before the submission of all the authorities of the different districts of San Domingo had been received and all political prisoners were to be liberated. Diplomats Meet. When the revolutionists were sighted. Minister Powell called a meeting of the diplomats and consular bodies at the United States legation for the purpose of deciding upon the best means for protecting life and property and to prevent injury to non-combatants in case of an assault being made on San Domingo, with the result that a delegation was appointed. The revolutionary army entered San Domingo at 11 a. m. the same day, Friday, and took possession of the government buildings. The form of the new government of San Domingo has not been decided. As this dispatch is sent no foreign war ships have arrived here. The United States cruiser Cincinnati left Norfolk for San Domingo May 4 and should arrive here tomorrow (Thursday.) Monte Christi, Santo Domingo, May 7.— Later in the day it became known here that Puerto Plata had capitulated to the revolutionists, who today took possession of the town and the fort. General Deschamps, the former Governor, embarked aboard a French steamer bound for Hayti. All is quiet at Puerto Plata.

records.headline: All intercourse with the revolutionary government has been suspended
records.summary_en: All intercourse with the revolutionary government has been suspended by United States Minister Powell, a dispatch from San Domingo in the Evening times-Republican reports, owing to local conditions. Powell is preparing to depart for Hayti, where he is also accredited, due to grave difficulties and a reported revolution in that country. The dispatch further notes that the Dominican congress has been dissolved and that a provisional government headed by General Horacio Vasquez has been formed.
records.summary_es: Toda relación con el gobierno revolucionario ha sido suspendida por el ministro de los Estados Unidos Powell, informa un despacho desde San Domingo en el Evening times-Republican, debido a las condiciones locales. Powell se prepara para partir hacia Hayti, donde también está acreditado, debido a graves dificultades y a una supuesta revolución en ese país. El despacho señala además que el congreso dominicano ha sido disuelto y que se ha formado un gobierno provisional encabezado por el general Horacio Vasquez.

records.headline: A Santo Domingo dispatch of May 2 in The Bourbon news reports
records.summary_en: A Santo Domingo dispatch of May 2 in The Bourbon news reports that the Dominican capital has capitulated to revolutionary forces commanded by Gen. Horacio Vasquez, vice president of the republic. President Jiminez took refuge in the French consulate, while many government officers sought safety in the French and United States legations. The victorious troops entered the city quietly, with no enthusiasm displayed by the local population. The advance of the revolutionists on the capital followed two days of heavy fighting against government troops.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Santo Domingo del 2 de mayo en The Bourbon news informa que la capital dominicana capituló ante las fuerzas revolucionarias comandadas por el general Horacio Vasquez, vicepresidente de la república. El presidente Jiminez se refugió en el consulado francés, mientras que muchos funcionarios del gobierno buscaron seguridad en las legaciones francesa y estadounidense. Las tropas victoriosas entraron a la ciudad con tranquilidad, sin que la población local mostrara entusiasmo. El avance de los revolucionarios sobre la capital se produjo tras dos días de intensos combates contra las tropas del gobierno.

records.summary_en: A New York dispatch in the Oakes Republican, citing a Herald dispatch from Puerto Plata, reports that insurgents have seized the entire republic except Puerto Plata, having taken the capital on Sunday. Governor Deschamps declared he will not surrender Puerto Plata without official notification from the government. The dispatch reports that Vice President Horacio Vasquez has overthrown President Juan I. Vasquez is expected to take charge of the government immediately.

records.summary_en: Messengers under a flag of truce confirmed the capitulation of the Dominican capital on Friday at Puerto Plata, The Berne witness reports, and President Jiminez's flight to the French consulate. records.headline: A dispatch from Santo Domingo in the Richmond dispatch reports
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Santo Domingo in the Richmond dispatch reports that United States Minister William F. Powell has suspended relations with the revolutionary government and is preparing to leave for Haiti, where a revolution is reportedly underway. Powell's departure halts negotiations to settle the claims of the Dominican Improvement Company of New York against Santo Domingo, which had been receiving favorable consideration from the overthrown government. The report lists the dissolution of Congress and the formation of a provisional cabinet under General Horacio Vasquez as Supreme Chief of the Revolution, with Juan Francisco Sanchez, Emiliano Tejera, Miguel A. Pichardo, and Casimiro Cordero among the ministers. Existing local laws and decrees are to remain in force under a revolutionary decree.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Santo Domingo en el Richmond dispatch informa que el ministro de los Estados Unidos William F. Powell ha suspendido las relaciones con el gobierno revolucionario y se prepara para partir hacia Haití, donde según informes se desarrolla una revolución. La partida de Powell detiene las negociaciones para solucionar las reclamaciones de la Dominican Improvement Company de Nueva York contra Santo Domingo, que recibían consideración favorable del gobierno derrocado. El informe detalla la disolución del Congreso y la conformación de un gabinete provisional bajo el general Horacio Vasquez como jefe supremo de la revolución, con Juan Francisco Sanchez, Emiliano Tejera, Miguel A. Pichardo y Casimiro Cordero entre los ministros. Por decreto revolucionario, las leyes y decretos locales existentes permanecerán en vigor.

records.headline: Revolutionary forces led by Vice President Horacio Vasquez are advancing
records.summary_en: Revolutionary forces led by Vice President Horacio Vasquez are advancing on Santo Domingo, The Emmons County record reports, which the government is taking active measures to defend despite severed telegraph lines with the interior. Vasquez reached Guerra near the capital, with the fall of President Jiminez's government anticipated the following day, leaving only the capital and Puerto Plata outside insurgent hands. At Puerto Plata, large numbers of government troops supported by Dominican warships have concentrated under Governor Gen. Deschamps, who has resolved to defend the port.
records.summary_es: El Emmons County record informa que fuerzas revolucionarias lideradas por el vicepresidente Horacio Vasquez avanzan hacia Santo Domingo, ciudad que el gobierno toma medidas activas para defender a pesar del corte de las líneas telegráficas con el interior. Vasquez llegó a Guerra, cerca de la capital, previéndose la caída del gobierno del presidente Jiminez al día siguiente, lo que deja únicamente a la capital y a Puerto Plata fuera del control insurgente. En Puerto Plata, numerosos efectivos gubernamentales respaldados por buques de guerra dominicanos se han concentrado bajo el mando del gobernador general Deschamps, quien ha resuelto defender el puerto.

records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican reports news reached Monte Christi from Santo Domingo: the provisional government established by Horatio Vasquez will remain in power until elections are held. Vasquez, formerly vice-president of the Dominican Republic, led a successful revolution against President Jiminez, with forces under his command taking possession of Santo Domingo city last week after the capital capitulated. Peace has been fully re-established in the southern part of the republic, and an order suspending hostilities has been signed while surrender terms are discussed.

La paz se ha restablecido plenamente en la parte sur de la república y se ha firmado una orden de suspensión de hostilidades mientras se discuten los términos de la rendición.

records.headline: A May 9 dispatch from Santo Domingo in The Indianapolis Journal reports
records.summary_en: A May 9 dispatch from Santo Domingo in The Indianapolis Journal reports that former President Jiminez and his ministers have emerged from the foreign legations where they had sought asylum, with tranquility returning to the city. The capital's hospitals are filled with casualties from the final clashes between Dominican revolutionists and former government forces, and a Red Cross hospital has been organized to provide care, while the U.S. cruiser Cincinnati arrived in port that day. In addition, an introductory dispatch notes that General Deschamps, former governor of Puerto Plata—the last place to surrender to the revolutionists—boarded a French steamer and took refuge at Cape Haitien, Haiti.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del 9 de mayo desde Santo Domingo en The Indianapolis Journal informa que el expresidente Jiminez y sus ministros salieron de las legaciones extranjeras donde se habían asilado, restableciéndose la tranquilidad en la ciudad. Los hospitales de la capital se encuentran repletos de heridos de los últimos combates entre los revolucionarios dominicanos y las fuerzas del antiguo gobierno, y se ha organizado un hospital de la Cruz Roja para brindar atención, mientras que el crucero estadounidense Cincinnati arribó a puerto ese mismo día. Asimismo, un despacho preliminar señala que el general Deschamps, exgobernador de Puerto Plata —el último lugar en rendirse ante los revolucionarios—, abordó un vapor francés y se refugió en Cabo Haitiano, Haití.

records.summary_en: The *Billings Gazette* described the tense diplomatic negotiations that preceded the surrender of Santo Domingo to General Horacio Vásquez. United States Minister Powell and representatives from France, Spain, Germany, Italy, and Great Britain met with Vásquez to enforce the rules of war and protect non-combatants. Although Vásquez initially pledged a temporary ceasefire, his forces swiftly encircled the capital, prompting the diplomatic delegation to mediate formal surrender terms.
records.summary_es: La *Billings Gazette* describió las tensas negociaciones diplomáticas que precedieron a la rendición de Santo Domingo ante el general Horacio Vásquez. El ministro de los Estados Unidos Powell y representantes de Francia, España, Alemania, Italia y Gran Bretaña se reunieron con Vásquez para hacer cumplir las leyes de la guerra y proteger a los no combatientes. Aunque Vásquez prometió en un principio un alto el fuego temporal, sus fuerzas cercaron rápidamente la capital, lo que llevó a la delegación diplomática a mediar en los términos formales de la rendición.

De Jouax; the Spanish consul, Dr. Perera Blesa; the German consul, Herr Von Krosigk; the Italian consul, Signor Cammbiaso, and the British consul, Mr. Gosling, was appointed to wait on General Vasquez and inform him that no attack could be made on the capital under the rules of war until due notice had been given to the diplomatic and consular representatives here. records.headline: Messengers arriving under a flag of truce at Puerto Plata confirmed
records.summary_en: Messengers arriving under a flag of truce at Puerto Plata confirmed the capitulation of the Dominican capital on Friday, The Star reports, with President Jiminez taking refuge in the French consulate at San Domingo. Negotiations between the revolutionists and the governor of Puerto Plata for the surrender of that northern port have reportedly collapsed, as the governor refuses to yield without an explicit directive from the Dominican government. As a result, the insurgents hold control of the entire republic with the sole exception of Puerto Plata.
records.summary_es: Emisarios llegados bajo bandera de tregua a Puerto Plata confirmaron la capitulación de la capital dominicana el viernes, informa The Star, tras lo cual el presidente Jiminez se refugió en el consulado francés de Santo Domingo. Se informa que las negociaciones entre los revolucionarios y el gobernador de Puerto Plata para la rendición de dicho puerto septentrional han fracasado, ya que el gobernador se niega a ceder sin una orden explícita del gobierno dominicano. Como resultado, los insurgentes controlan la totalidad de la república con la única excepción de Puerto Plata.

records.headline: In an overview of island political history, the Evening Star presents
records.summary_en: In an overview of island political history, the Evening Star presents a chronology of revolutionary movements and changes of leadership in Santo Domingo and Haiti since 1843. Following the withdrawal of Spain in 1865 (printed '18G5') and the promulgation of new constitutions, the newspaper tracks successive political convulsions in Santo Domingo, including the banishments, returns, and overthrow of President Baez alongside administrations headed by Cabral and subsequent leaders. The dispatch records concurrent insurrections, executions, and presidential successions in Haiti, underscoring decades of recurrent turmoil across both nations.
records.summary_es: En una reseña histórica sobre la política insular, el Evening Star presenta una cronología de los movimientos revolucionarios y relevos de poder en Santo Domingo y Haití a partir de 1843. Tras la retirada de España en 1865 (impreso '18G5') y la promulgación de nuevas constituciones, el periódico registra las continuas convulsiones políticas en Santo Domingo, entre ellas los destierros, retornos y derrocamiento del presidente Baez junto a las administraciones de Cabral y mandatarios posteriores. El recuento consigna insurrecciones, ejecuciones y sucesiones presidenciales paralelas en Haití, subrayando décadas de agitación recurrente en ambas naciones.

records.headline: Writing editorially, The Houston Daily Post cautions against United States intervention
records.summary_en: Writing editorially, The Houston Daily Post cautions against United States intervention in Santo Domingo and Haiti, arguing that simultaneous domestic revolutions and the deposition of Dominican President Jiminez offer an easy excuse for expansionist ambitions. The editorial underscores that the financial affairs of the Dominican Republic have been largely entrusted to an American firm, the San Domingo Improvement Company, which could readily petition for military protection. The paper satirically decries establishing high-salaried governors and commissioners over newly conquered populations to expand an "American zoo," though it observes that the American minister has departed the island.
records.summary_es: En un artículo editorial, The Houston Daily Post advierte contra una intervención de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo y Haití, argumentando que las revoluciones internas simultáneas y el derrocamiento del presidente dominicano Jiminez brindan una excusa propicia para las ambiciones expansionistas. El editorial destaca que los asuntos financieros de la República Dominicana han estado encomendados en gran medida a una firma estadounidense, la San Domingo Improvement Company, la cual podría solicitar fácilmente protección militar. El periódico censura con ironía la designación de gobernadores y comisionados con altos sueldos sobre poblaciones recién sometidas para ampliar un «zoológico estadounidense», si bien observa que el ministro estadounidense ha salido de la isla.

records.summary_en: A dispatch from Santo Domingo dated May 10 in The Hood River Glacier reports that ex-President Jiminez of the Dominican Republic and his ministers have vacated the foreign legation where they had sought refuge. Calm has returned to the capital, though local hospitals remain crowded with men wounded during the final engagement between Dominican revolutionists and government forces. A Red Cross hospital has been established to attend to the injured, and the United States cruiser Cincinnati has arrived at the port.

La calma ha retornado a la capital, aunque los hospitales locales continúan abarrotados de heridos del último enfrentamiento entre los revolucionarios dominicanos y las fuerzas del gobierno. Se ha establecido un hospital de la Cruz Roja para atender a los heridos y el crucero estadounidense Cincinnati ha llegado al puerto.

records.headline: Under the headline "Hayti in More Trouble," the Dakota Farmers' Leader reports
records.summary_en: Under the headline "Hayti in More Trouble," the Dakota Farmers' Leader reports under a San Domingo dateline that United States Minister Powell has suspended all diplomatic intercourse with the revolutionary government in the Dominican Republic, to which he is accredited. Powell's departure is prompted by grave disturbances in Haiti, where a revolution is said to be underway. The notice also reports that the Dominican Congress has been dissolved and a provisional government headed by General Horacio Vasquez has been established.
records.summary_es: Bajo el titular «Haití en mayores problemas», el Dakota Farmers' Leader informa bajo una línea de fecha de Santo Domingo que el ministro de los Estados Unidos, Powell, ha suspendido toda relación diplomática con el gobierno revolucionario en la República Dominicana, ante el cual se encuentra acreditado. La partida de Powell obedece a las graves alteraciones en Haití, donde se afirma que se desarrolla una revolución. La nota añade asimismo que el Congreso dominicano ha sido disuelto y que se ha establecido un gobierno provisional encabezado por el general Horacio Vasquez.

records.headline: Former Dominican president Jiminez and the country's new executive
records.summary_en: Former Dominican president Jiminez and the country's new executive, General Horacio Vasquez, have their revolutionary careers sketched by The Citizen, opening mid-narrative. The paper recalls Jiminez sailing from Mobile for Santo Domingo under the American flag, landing at Monte Christi with eleven men where his supporters failed to assemble, leaving him the sole member of his party to escape death or capture. Jiminez subsequently organized an uprising against President Heureaux from Havana in 1899, was briefly detained at Cienfuegos, and was joyfully welcomed by the populace after Heureaux was assassinated, subsequently winning unanimous election to the presidency alongside Vasquez as vice president. Vasquez, a native Dominican about forty years of age who headed the army and organized the provisional government after Heureaux's death, had maintained friendly relations with Jiminez until disputes over contracts precipitated a breach.
records.summary_es: El expresidente dominicano Jiminez y el nuevo mandatario del país, el general Horacio Vasquez, ven reseñadas sus carreras revolucionarias por The Citizen, comenzando a mitad de relato. El periódico recuerda que Jiminez zarpó desde Mobile hacia Santo Domingo bajo bandera estadounidense y desembarcó en Monte Christi con once hombres, donde sus partidarios no lograron reunirse, dejándolo como el único de su grupo que escapó de la muerte o la captura. Posteriormente, Jiminez organizó un levantamiento contra el presidente Heureaux desde La Habana en 1899, fue detenido brevemente en Cienfuegos y fue recibido con júbilo por el pueblo tras el asesinato de Heureaux, resultando luego elegido presidente por unanimidad junto con Vasquez como vicepresidente. Vasquez, un dominicano nativo de unos cuarenta años de edad que comandaba el ejército y organizó el gobierno provisional tras la muerte de Heureaux, había mantenido relaciones amistosas con Jiminez hasta que disputas en torno a contratos provocaron una ruptura.

records.headline: The Boletín Mercantil de Puerto Rico, reporting local maritime
records.summary_en: The Boletín Mercantil de Puerto Rico, reporting local maritime arrivals, notes the morning arrival in San Juan of the steamship Julia, flying the flag of the Cuban Republic, from Cuba and Santo Domingo. Among the vessel's passengers were Don Juan Henriquez, consul general of the Dominican Republic, Francisco Cigada, baritone of an Italian opera company that had recently performed locally, and thirty-four other passengers. Cigada transferred to the steamer Montevideo bound for Spain en route to his home in Italy.
records.summary_es: El Boletín Mercantil de Puerto Rico, al reportar las llegadas marítimas locales, señala la llegada esa mañana a San Juan del vapor Julia, con bandera de la República de Cuba, procedente de Cuba y Santo Domingo. Entre los pasajeros de la embarcación figuraban don Juan Henríquez, cónsul general de la República Dominicana, Francisco Cigada, barítono de una compañía de ópera italiana que había actuado recientemente en el país, y otros treinta y cuatro pasajeros. Cigada tomó pasaje en el vapor Montevideo con destino a España en viaje de regreso a su hogar en Italia.

records.headline: A San Juan dispatch dated June 28 in The Saint Paul Globe relays
records.summary_en: A San Juan dispatch dated June 28 in The Saint Paul Globe relays contents of a letter received by a Santo Domingo native residing in Puerto Rico, warning that the Dominican Republic is in a decidedly critical condition and that its new government faces momentary overthrow. According to this correspondent, President Vasquez is reported to be mentally affected and unaware of what he is doing half the time. The letter further states that the country's finances are in a deplorable state, government employees receive only half pay, the public has lost all confidence in the administration, many people are leaving the country, and the current regime cannot last beyond October.

Según este corresponsal, se informa que el presidente Vasquez padece problemas mentales y que la mitad del tiempo no sabe lo que hace. La carta añade que las finanzas del país se hallan en estado deplorable, que los empleados del gobierno reciben solo la mitad de su sueldo, que la población ha perdido toda confianza en la administración, que numerosas personas están abandonando el país y que el régimen actual no podrá durar más allá de octubre.

records.summary_es: Un informe de San Juan cita una carta recibida por un natural de Santo Domingo residente allí, según la cual la situación en la República Dominicana es decididamente crítica y el nuevo gobierno corre peligro de ser derrocado en cualquier momento. La carta presenta al presidente Vásquez como mentalmente afectado, las finanzas de la república en una condición deplorable con los empleados del gobierno recibiendo solo la mitad del sueldo, al pueblo sin ninguna confianza y a muchos marchándose del país, y declara que el régimen actual no puede durar más allá de octubre.
records.passage: VASQUEZ ADMINISTRATION EXPECTED TO TUMBLE SOON. San Juan, P. R.. June 28--A native of San Domingo, living here, is in receipt of a letter, the writer of which says the situation in the Dominican Republic is decidedly critical. The new government, according to this correspondent, is in momentary danger of being overthrown. President Vasquez, it is reported, is mentally affected and half the time does not know what he is doing. The writer of the letter adds that the finances of the republic are in a deplorable condition, that the government employees receive only half pay, that the people have lost all confidence in the administration and that numbers of them are leaving the country. The present regime, he declares, cannot last longer than October. records.summary_en: Under the subhead Situation in Santo Domingo, The Indianapolis Journal prints a dispatch from San Juan, dated June 3, relaying a letter received by a native of Santo Domingo living in Puerto Rico. The writer reports that the situation in the Dominican Republic is decidedly critical and that the new government is in momentary danger of being overthrown. President Vasquez is reported to be mentally affected and half the time unaware of what he is doing. The letter adds that the republic's finances are in a deplorable condition and government employees receive only half pay before the excerpt breaks off.
records.summary_es: Bajo el subtítulo Situación en Santo Domingo, The Indianapolis Journal publica un despacho desde San Juan, fechado el 3 de junio, que transmite una carta recibida por un nativo de Santo Domingo residente en Puerto Rico. El autor señala que la situación en la República Dominicana es decididamente crítica y que el nuevo gobierno corre peligro momentáneo de ser derrocado. Se informa que el presidente Vasquez padece trastornos mentales y que la mitad del tiempo no sabe lo que hace. La carta añade que las finanzas de la república se encuentran en condición deplorable y que los empleados del gobierno reciben únicamente la mitad de su sueldo antes de que el extracto se interrumpa.

records.headline: Reporting on military and strategic debates, The Washington Times discusses
records.summary_en: Reporting on military and strategic debates, The Washington Times discusses arguments concerning American acquisition of Haiti, which the paper defines geographically as including Santo Domingo. Under the subhead Value as Naval Base, the article observes that although the possession of Porto Rico, potential coaling stations in Cuba, and negotiations for the Danish West Indies had lessened military interest, strategists expect the next American war to be fought primarily in the Caribbean. The paper reports that the strategic roadstead of Samana Bay in Dominican territory is considered by many to provide sufficient grounds for serious consideration of annexation, noting that even the conservative Cleveland administration previously sought to acquire Samana Bay for naval purposes.
records.summary_es: Al informar sobre debates militares y estratégicos, The Washington Times analiza los argumentos en torno a la adquisición estadounidense de Haití, isla que el periódico define geográficamente como comprensiva de Santo Domingo. Bajo el subtítulo Valor como base naval, el artículo señala que, si bien la posesión de Puerto Rico, las posibles estaciones de carboneras en Cuba y las negociaciones por las Antillas danesas habían reducido el interés militar, los estrategas prevén que la próxima guerra de Estados Unidos se librará principalmente en el Caribe. El diario informa que la rada estratégica de la bahía de Samaná en territorio dominicano es considerada por muchos como justificación suficiente para sopesar seriamente la anexión, recordando que incluso la administración conservadora de Cleveland intentó previamente adquirir la bahía de Samaná con fines navales.

records.headline: General Deschamps, former governor of Porto Plata, has taken
records.summary_en: General Deschamps, former governor of Porto Plata, has taken up arms against the provisional government of Santo Domingo, The Worcester Spy reports, sparking uprisings at Monte Christi, Dajabon, Savanett, and Guayabin. The paper recalls that during Vice President Vasquez's successful revolution against President Jiminez in May, Deschamps held Porto Plata stubbornly against the insurgents from May 1 until May 7 before embarking on a French steamer bound for Haiti as Jiminez relinquished his claims to the presidency. A separate Santo Domingo dispatch dated October 13 adds that another former governor named Navarro has revolted and seized Monte Christo on the northern coast near the Haitian border, prompting the government to adopt prompt measures to restore order.
records.summary_es: El general Deschamps, exgobernador de Puerto Plata, se ha levantado en armas contra el gobierno provisional de Santo Domingo, informa The Worcester Spy, provocando alzamientos en Monte Christi, Dajabón, Savanett y Guayabín. El periódico recuerda que durante la exitosa revolución del vicepresidente Vasquez contra el presidente Jiminez en mayo pasado, Deschamps resistió tenazmente en Puerto Plata frente a los insurgentes desde el 1 hasta el 7 de mayo antes de embarcarse en un vapor francés hacia Haití cuando Jiminez renunció a sus reclamos a la presidencia. Un despacho separado de Santo Domingo fechado el 13 de octubre añade que otro exgobernador de nombre Navarro se ha sublevado y ha tomado posesión de Monte Christo en la costa norte cerca de la frontera haitiana, lo que llevó al gobierno a tomar prontas medidas para restablecer el orden.

In response, Commander Mason of the cruiser *Cincinnati* departed Cape Haitien to investigate the disturbances and protect American interests at the Dominican port. records.headline: Under the headline Revolution in San Domingo, The Evening Times reports
records.summary_en: Under the headline Revolution in San Domingo, The Evening Times reports that Commander Mason of the cruiser Cincinnati advised the Navy Department yesterday of a revolution in the Dominican Republic. Commander Mason stated that he would proceed immediately to Monte Cristo, San Domingo, where the disturbances had broken out. In addition, Mason reported that the Haitian capital, Gonaives, was held by General Firmin, leader of the Haitian revolution.
records.summary_es: Bajo el titular Revolución en Santo Domingo, The Evening Times informa que el comandante Mason del crucero Cincinnati notificó ayer al Departamento de la Armada sobre una revolución en la República Dominicana. El comandante Mason declaró que se trasladaría de inmediato a Monte Cristo, Santo Domingo, donde se reportaban los disturbios. Asimismo, Mason informó que la capital haitiana, Gonaïves, se encontraba en poder del general Firmin, líder de la revolución haitiana.
