records.headline: In an excerpt from a naval dispatch dated at Cape Haytien, The Savannah Morning News reports
records.summary_en: In an excerpt from a naval dispatch dated at Cape Haytien, The Savannah Morning News reports that Commander Mason of the USS Cincinnati communicated advice from the United States consul at Monte Cristi regarding a revolution and disturbances in the Dominican Republic. Mason stated he would proceed the following day to investigate the situation and send reports directly from Monte Cristi. A later dispatch confirmed that the Cincinnati had already sailed from Cape Haytien for Monte Cristi, which the paper describes as a small town located about thirty miles to the east.
records.summary_es: En un fragmento de un despacho naval fechado en Cabo Haitiano, The Savannah Morning News informa que el comandante Mason del USS Cincinnati transmitió noticias del cónsul de Estados Unidos en Monte Cristi sobre una revolución y disturbios en la República Dominicana. Mason declaró que procedería al día siguiente a investigar la situación y a enviar informes directamente desde Monte Cristi. Un despacho posterior confirmó que el Cincinnati ya había zarpado desde Cabo Haitiano hacia Monte Cristi, que el periódico describe como un pequeño poblado situado a unas treinta millas al este.

records.headline: A dispatch addressed to the Secretary of the Navy and published
records.summary_en: A dispatch addressed to the Secretary of the Navy and published in the Wheeling Register details a report from Commander Mason of the cruiser Cincinnati, dated yesterday at Cape Haytien. Mason transmits notification from the United States consul at Monte Cristi that a revolution and disturbances have occurred in the Dominican Republic, adding that he will investigate the following day and report from that port. A subsequent report stated that the Cincinnati had already sailed from Cape Haytien for Monte Cristi, described as a small town situated approximately thirty miles to the east.

Un informe posterior señalaba que el Cincinnati ya había zarpado de Cabo Haitiano hacia Monte Cristi, descrita como una pequeña localidad situada a unas treinta millas al este.

records.headline: The Evening Star, opening mid-sentence, reports that the Dominican government
records.summary_en: The Evening Star, opening mid-sentence, reports that the Dominican government has consented to arbitrate directly with the New York firm of J. Sala & Co. over a claim of approximately $215,000 (printed 1215,000) for unpaid supplies furnished to the late President Heureaux of San Domingo. State Department officials expressed gratification that the Dominican authorities agreed to direct settlement without undue pressure from the United States, noting that the surviving head of the firm is a woman. Frederick Van Dyne, assistant solicitor of the State Department, was selected by the firm as its arbitrator because of his familiarity with the case, while Bolivian Minister Guachalla was designated by San Domingo, with the two expected to choose a third arbitrator to complete the board.
records.summary_es: El Evening Star, comenzando a mitad de frase, informa que el gobierno dominicano ha aceptado arbitrar directamente con la firma neoyorquina J. Sala & Co. una reclamación de aproximadamente 215.000 dólares (impresa en el texto como 1215,000) por suministros impagos provistos al difunto presidente Heureaux de Santo Domingo. Funcionarios del Departamento de Estado expresaron satisfacción por el hecho de que las autoridades dominicanas accedieran a una solución directa sin presiones indebidas de Estados Unidos, destacando que la titular sobreviviente de la empresa es una mujer. Frederick Van Dyne, procurador adjunto del Departamento de Estado, fue seleccionado por la firma como su árbitro debido a su familiaridad con el caso, mientras que el ministro boliviano Guachalla fue designado por Santo Domingo, previéndose que ambos elijan a un tercer árbitro para completar el tribunal.

records.headline: Under the headline The Sala Claim, The Montgomery Advertiser publishes
records.summary_en: Under the headline The Sala Claim, The Montgomery Advertiser publishes a San Domingo dispatch dated January 19 stating that the Dominican government has paid United States Minister Powell the balance of $60,000 (rendered in the text as (60.000) due on the Sala claim, virtually disposing of the controversy. The article explains that Sala was a Frenchman who loaned money and supplied munitions of war to the late President Heureaux of Santo Domingo, and that while the Dominican government recognized the claim after Heureaux's death, it subsequently showed a disposition to ignore it. Following Sala's death, the claim passed to his widow, an American resident of New York, leading the State Department about a year ago to prosecute her claim through Minister Powell.

records.headline: A San Domingo dispatch dated January 31 in The Birmingham Age -Herald
records.summary_en: A San Domingo dispatch dated January 31 in The Birmingham Age-Herald reports that the Dominican government has declined a request made by United States Minister Powell on behalf of the American government concerning claims of the Clyde steamship line. Dominican officials stated that if the company feels aggrieved by the government's action, it should seek redress before a tribunal of the Dominican Republic rather than appealing to Washington. In a strongly worded reply, Minister Powell notified the Dominican authorities that the United States will insist upon redress for its citizens and demands that the pending cases be settled directly by the government rather than through the courts.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Santo Domingo fechado el 31 de enero en The Birmingham Age-Herald informa que el gobierno dominicano ha rechazado una solicitud formulada por el ministro de Estados Unidos Powell en nombre del gobierno estadounidense respecto a las reclamaciones de la línea de vapores Clyde. Las autoridades dominicanas señalaron que, si la compañía se siente agraviada por la acción gubernamental, debe solicitar reparación ante un tribunal de la República Dominicana en lugar de apelar a Washington. En una enérgica respuesta, el ministro Powell notificó a las autoridades dominicanas que Estados Unidos insistirá en la reparación para sus ciudadanos y exige que los casos pendientes sean resueltos directamente por el gobierno y no mediante los tribunales.

records.headline: Observing that the United States is collecting a "little bill
records.summary_en: Observing that the United States is collecting a "little bill" owed to American citizens by what it terms "Dominica, the black republic in the West Indies," The Plymouth Tribune publishes a cable from Santo Domingo on diplomatic negotiations. The Dominican minister for foreign affairs made public a message from Secretary of State Hay stating that a Dominican envoy sent to Washington would be received and heard, but reaffirming that Minister Powell remains entrusted with negotiating and concluding the claims of American citizens. After Dominican Secretary General Sanchez informed Powell that pending cases would not be considered until the commissioner returned from Washington, Powell replied that the claims admitted no further delay and notified the secretary general that a settlement must be effected within a few days. The dispatch adds that Powell's determined stand in pressing the Clyde line and Ross cases surprised the Dominican government, which was expected to yield.
records.summary_es: Al señalar que Estados Unidos está cobrando una «pequeña factura» que se le adeuda a ciudadanos estadounidenses por lo que denomina «Dominica, la república negra de las Indias Occidentales», The Plymouth Tribune publica un cable desde Santo Domingo sobre las negociaciones diplomáticas. El ministro de Relaciones Exteriores dominicano hizo público un mensaje del secretario de Estado Hay manifestando que el enviado dominicano enviado a Washington sería recibido y escuchado, pero reafirmando que el ministro Powell seguía encargado de negociar y concluir las reclamaciones de los ciudadanos estadounidenses. Después de que el secretario general dominicano Sánchez informó a Powell que los casos pendientes no se considerarían hasta el regreso del comisionado desde Washington, Powell respondió que las reclamaciones no admitían más demoras y notificó al secretario general que debía alcanzarse un arreglo en pocos días. El despacho añade que la firme postura adoptada por Powell para resolver los casos de la Línea Clyde y de Ross sorprendió al gobierno dominicano, estimándose que este último tendría que ceder.

records.summary_en: Opening mid-sentence on military uprisings, the New-York Tribune reports that revolutionary generals Ramon Tavarez, Ynginio Albelo, and Desiderio Arias are operating successfully in the northeastern part of San Domingo. In the northwest, General Zeno, who holds chief command of the revolutionists' operations, has captured Guayubin and is advancing toward Porto Plata at the head of a large body of insurgents. Meanwhile, Generals Perico Lasala and Eliseo Gratero lead approximately eight hundred revolutionists against Santiago de los Caballeros and La Vega, while General Raphael Rodriguez advances toward the capital, having reached the vicinity of Las Damas. In what the dispatch terms the eastern part of Dominica, General Candelario de la Rosa is likewise operating with a numerous force of insurgents.

En lo que el despacho denomina la parte oriental de Dominica, el general Candelario de la Rosa opera asimismo con una numerosa fuerza insurgente.

Sala & Co. against the Dominican government. The board consists of Frederick Van Dyke, assistant solicitor for the State Department, and the Bolivian minister, Señor Guachalla (printed Guschzlla). records.headline: Opening mid-sentence, the New-York Tribune reports that the Dominican minister
records.summary_en: Opening mid-sentence, the New-York Tribune reports that the Dominican minister in Washington has received a dispatch from his brother, President Horacio Vasquez, announcing that the revolutionary movement against him has been effectually crushed. Minister Vasquez disclosed that New York served as the conspirators' headquarters, where arms and ammunition were purchased, stored in an uptown Spanish-American hotel, and loaded onto vessels bound for West Indian ports before being smuggled into uninhabited points along the Dominican coast. In addition, Minister Vasquez obtained a letter signed by former Dominican president General Juan I. Jimenes, who is currently residing in New York, which reportedly establishes his complicity in the conspiracy to overthrow President Vasquez.

El ministro Vasquez reveló que Nueva York sirvió como cuartel general de los conspiradores, donde se adquirieron armas y municiones, se almacenaron en un hotel hispanoamericano de la parte alta de la ciudad y se cargaron en embarcaciones con destino a puertos antillanos antes de ser introducidas clandestinamente por puntos deshabitados de la costa dominicana. Asimismo, el ministro Vasquez obtuvo una carta firmada por el expresidente dominicano general Juan I. Jimenes, quien reside actualmente en Nueva York, la cual demuestra presuntamente su complicidad en la conspiración para derrocar al presidente Vasquez.

To extend the uprising, a revolutionary commission departed aboard the warship Independence for Azua and Barahona to demand their surrender, while the warship Colon sailed from the capital for San Pedro de Macoris to compel that municipality to yield.

records.summary_en: Advices from Santo Domingo in The News & Observer report that General Alejandro Wos y Gil and his followers have gained mastery of the capital, prompting Minister of War General Miguel Pichardo and Minister of Foreign Affairs General Juan Francisco Sanchez to surrender after seeking shelter in the United States consulate. The revolutionists control two of three Dominican warships, the Independencia and the Colon, while President Horacio Vasquez sailed from Porto Plata to Sanchez on the cruiser Presidente, the only warship remaining to the government. Vasquez is believed to be preparing an assault on the capital in alliance with General Luis Maria Hernandez, governor of San Pedro de Macoris, while local skirmishes have already inflicted notable equipment losses on government troops.
records.summary_es: Noticias procedentes de Santo Domingo en The News & Observer indican que el general Alejandro Wos y Gil y sus seguidores se han adueñado de la capital, lo que motivó la rendición del ministro de Guerra, general Miguel Pichardo, y del ministro de Relaciones Exteriores, general Juan Francisco Sanchez, tras refugiarse en el consulado de los Estados Unidos. Los revolucionarios controlan dos de los tres buques de guerra dominicanos, el Independencia y el Colón, mientras que el presidente Horacio Vasquez zarpó de Puerto Plata hacia Sánchez en el crucero Presidente, el único navío de guerra en poder del gobierno. Se cree que Vasquez prepara un ataque contra la capital en alianza con el general Luis Maria Hernandez, gobernador de San Pedro de Macorís, en tanto que escaramuzas locales ya han causado notables pérdidas de pertrechos a las tropas del gobierno.

records.headline: Revolutionary commissioners returned after their mission failed
records.summary_en: Revolutionary commissioners returned after their mission failed, having been sent from Santo Domingo to Bahia Honda, Azua, and San Pedro de Macoris, dispatches published in The San Francisco Call state, leaving the capital quiet with business suspended while awaiting news from the north. From New York, the Dominican consul received word from Governor Caceres at Santiago reporting that General Horacio Vasquez captured the cruiser Independencia at Macoris, imprisoning all revolutionary chiefs aboard and confining the rebellion to besieged Santo Domingo City, while Washington reports the cruiser Atlanta departed Cap-Haitien for the Dominican capital.

records.headline: Former Dominican President General Penceslao Figuerero sailed
records.summary_en: Former Dominican President General Penceslao Figuerero sailed Monday night aboard the revolutionary warship Independencia, The New-York Tribune reports, for Azua de Compostella in an attempt to avert further bloodshed, with an engagement between warships feared upon her return. Cable and telegraph lines to the city remain severed, while General Pichardo arrived after being summoned from exile in Curacao and revolutionary land forces marched toward San Pedro de Macoris. The inhabitants of San Cristobal have joined the revolt, other regions remain loyal to General Vasquez's government, and the Clyde Line steamer New-York is reportedly detained at San Pedro de Macoris.
records.summary_es: El expresidente dominicano general Penceslao Figuerero zarpó el lunes por la noche a bordo del buque revolucionario Independencia, informa el New-York Tribune, hacia Azua de Compostela para intentar evitar más derramamiento de sangre, temiéndose un combate entre navíos a su regreso. Las líneas de cable y telégrafo hacia la ciudad permanecen cortadas, mientras que el general Pichardo llegó tras ser llamado del exilio en Curazao y fuerzas terrestres revolucionarias marcharon hacia San Pedro de Macorís. Los habitantes de San Cristóbal se han sumado a la revuelta, otras zonas continúan fieles al gobierno del general Vasquez, y se informa que el vapor New-York de la Clyde Line permanece retenido en San Pedro de Macorís.

records.headline: A three-hour battle between government troops and revolutionists
records.summary_en: A three-hour battle between government troops and revolutionists took place along the River Ozama near Santo Domingo, The New-York Tribune reports, leaving one hundred casualties, while President Vasquez demanded the city's surrender and insurgents pledged to resist to the end. A March 31 dispatch adds that the United States cruiser Atlanta anchored off Santo Domingo, establishing a signal station on shore prepared to land marines if necessary. Another engagement at San Antonio de Guerra resulted in 146 killed or wounded, further river fighting ensued, and the Clyde Line steamer New-York remains prevented from arriving from San Pedro de Macoris amid widespread suspension of business and communications.
records.summary_es: Se libró un combate de tres horas entre tropas gubernamentales y revolucionarios a lo largo del río Ozama cerca de Santo Domingo, informa el New-York Tribune, con un saldo de cien bajas, mientras el presidente Vasquez exigió la rendición de la ciudad y los insurgentes prometieron resistir hasta el final. Un despacho del 31 de marzo agrega que el crucero estadounidense Atlanta fondeó frente a Santo Domingo, estableciendo una estación de señales en tierra lista para desembarcar infantes de marina si fuera necesario. Otro enfrentamiento en San Antonio de Guerra dejó 146 muertos o heridos, estallaron nuevos choques en el río, y el vapor New-York de la Clyde Line sigue sin poder llegar procedente de San Pedro de Macorís en medio de una paralización generalizada del comercio y las comunicaciones.

Dice que una cañonera gubernamental disparó tres tiros la noche anterior sin causar daños, que la ciudad estaba fortificada y decidida a resistir, y que se desembarcaron marines para proteger el consulado.

records.summary_en: The *Essex County Herald* emphasized the strategic importance of Samana Bay as the naval key to the Caribbean, recalling President Grant's earlier annexation efforts. It reported that an unexpected revolution had seized the capital of Santo Domingo during the president's absence, complicating recent American diplomatic agreements compensating a U.S. steamship company. With the Dominican president on the run and the foreign minister sheltering in the American consulate, the paper suggested U.S. marine landings or intervention might follow.
records.summary_es: El *Essex County Herald* subrayó la importancia estratégica de la bahía de Samaná como la llave naval del Caribe, recordando los anteriores intentos de anexión del presidente Grant. Informó que una revolución imprevista se había apoderado de la capital de Santo Domingo durante la ausencia del presidente, complicando recientes acuerdos diplomáticos estadounidenses que indemnizaban a una compañía naviera de los Estados Unidos. Con el presidente dominicano en fuga y el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores refugiado en el consulado estadounidense, el periódico sugirió que podrían producirse desembarcos de la infantería de marina de EE. UU. o una intervención militar.

records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch in The Montgomery Advertiser, under the heading "Resting Place," reports that the forthcoming volume of foreign relations contains a note from United States Minister Powell in the Dominican Republic series. Minister Powell recounted that during a visit to Santo Domingo by Cuban General Maximo Gomez, Dominican authorities honored the general by exposing the casket containing the alleged bones of Christopher Columbus and permitting him to handle them. According to the minister, the casket measured six feet by ten inches and twelve inches deep, marking only the fiftieth time it had been shown, and contained a bullet imbedded in the explorer's leg; Powell added that he too was permitted to hold some of the relics.

El ministro Powell relató que durante una visita a Santo Domingo del general cubano Máximo Gómez, las autoridades dominicanas homenajearon al general mostrándole la urna que contiene los supuestos restos de Cristóbal Colón y permitiéndole sostenerlos. Según el ministro, la urna medía seis pies por diez pulgadas y doce pulgadas de profundidad, constituyendo apenas la quincuagésima vez que se exhibía, y contenía una bala alojada en la pierna del explorador; Powell agregó que a él también se le permitió sostener algunas de las reliquias.

records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch in The Indianapolis Journal, under the headline "Shown on Rare Occasions," reports that the forthcoming foreign relations volume includes a dispatch from Minister Powell in the Dominican Republic series. Powell related that during Cuban General Maximo Gomez's visit to Santo Domingo, authorities allowed him to view and handle the casket holding the bones of Christopher Columbus. The minister noted that the relics are kept in a casket eighteen by ten inches and twelve inches deep, that this was only the fifth time they had been publicly shown, that the box contained an unextricated bullet from the explorer's leg, and that he was also allowed to hold some of the relics.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Washington en The Indianapolis Journal, bajo el titular "Mostrado en raras ocasiones", informa que el próximo volumen de relaciones exteriores incluye una comunicación del ministro Powell dentro de la serie sobre la República Dominicana. Powell relató que durante la visita del general cubano Máximo Gómez a Santo Domingo, las autoridades le permitieron ver y sostener la urna que guarda los restos de Cristóbal Colón. El ministro señaló que las reliquias reposan en una urna de dieciocho por diez pulgadas y doce pulgadas de profundidad, que esta era apenas la quinta vez que se exhibían en público, que la caja contenía una bala nunca extraída de la pierna del explorador, y que a él también se le permitió sostener algunas de las reliquias.

Dominican officials permitted Gomez to view and handle the casket holding what are claimed to be the mortal remains of Christopher Columbus. The relics are kept in a casket measuring eighteen by ten inches and twelve inches deep, displayed for only the fifth time, and contain a bullet that was never extracted from the discoverer's leg, with Powell adding that he too was allowed to hold some of the relics.

Las reliquias reposan en una urna que mide dieciocho por diez pulgadas y doce pulgadas de profundidad, expuesta apenas por quinta vez, y contienen una bala que nunca fue extraída de la pierna del descubridor, añadiendo Powell que a él también se le permitió sostener algunas de las reliquias.

records.summary_en: The Birmingham Age-Herald reports a note, included in the Dominican Republic series of the forthcoming Foreign Relations volume, detailing the reception accorded to General Maximo Gomez during his visit to Santo Domingo. U.S. Minister Powell informed the State Department that Dominican authorities, as a mark of high esteem, permitted the Cuban soldier to view and handle the casket containing the bones of Christopher Columbus. The relics are kept in a casket measuring eighteen by ten inches and twelve inches deep, exposed to public view on this occasion for only the fifth time. The minister added that the casket contains a bullet said to have been embedded in the discoverer's leg and never extracted, which authorities cite as proof of the remains' authenticity.
records.summary_es: The Birmingham Age-Herald informa de una nota, incluida en la serie sobre la República Dominicana del próximo volumen de Relaciones Exteriores, que detalla la acogida brindada al general Máximo Gómez durante su visita a Santo Domingo. El ministro estadounidense Powell comunicó al Departamento de Estado que las autoridades dominicanas, en testimonio de gran aprecio, permitieron al soldado cubano observar y sostener el cofre que contiene los restos óseos de Cristóbal Colón. Las reliquias se conservan en un cofre de dieciocho por diez pulgadas y doce pulgadas de profundidad, expuesto al público en esta ocasión por apenas quinta vez. El ministro añadió que la urna contiene una bala que presuntamente quedó incrustada en la pierna del descubridor sin haber sido extraída jamás, dato que las autoridades esgrimen como prueba de la autenticidad de los restos.

records.summary_en: The Savannah Morning News publishes an account of the forthcoming Foreign Relations volume highlighting a diplomatic communication from Mr. Powell, United States minister to the Dominican Republic. Writing to the State Department, Powell recounted that Dominican hosts paid tribute to General Maximo Gomez during the Cuban soldiers' visit to Santo Domingo by permitting him to view and handle the casket containing the bones of Christopher Columbus. The casket, measuring 18 by 10 inches and 12 inches deep, was opened for public inspection for only the fifth time. Powell noted that it contains an unextracted bullet reputedly lodged in the discoverer's leg, which Dominicans offer as evidence of the remains' identity, and added that he himself was allowed to hold some of the relics.
records.summary_es: The Savannah Morning News publica una reseña sobre el próximo volumen de Relaciones Exteriores que destaca una comunicación diplomática del señor Powell, ministro de los Estados Unidos ante la República Dominicana. En su nota dirigida al Departamento de Estado, Powell relató que las autoridades dominicanas rindieron homenaje al general Máximo Gómez durante la visita de los soldados cubanos a Santo Domingo, permitiéndole ver y sostener el cofre que guarda los restos óseos de Cristóbal Colón. El cofre, de 18 por 10 pulgadas y 12 pulgadas de profundidad, fue abierto para inspección pública por apenas quinta vez. Powell señaló que en su interior yace una bala nunca extraída, presuntamente alojada en la pierna del descubridor, lo que los dominicanos presentan como prueba de la identidad de las reliquias, y añadió que a él mismo se le permitió sostener parte de ellas.

The casket, measuring eighteen by ten inches and twelve inches deep, was exposed to public view for the fifth time, and contains an unextracted bullet said to have been embedded in the discoverer's leg. The dispatch concludes by noting that the minister was likewise permitted to hold some of the relics in his own hands.

records.headline: Describing diplomatic records scheduled for publication in the Foreign Relations
records.summary_en: Describing diplomatic records scheduled for publication in the Foreign Relations volume, an April 11 Washington telegram to the New-York Tribune focuses on the Dominican Republic series. U.S. Minister Powell communicated to the State Department that Dominican hosts honored General Maximo Gomez on his visit to San Domingo by showing him the casket of Christopher Columbus and allowing him to handle the bones. Powell described the casket as measuring 18 by 10 inches and 12 inches deep, noting that this marked only the fifth occasion it had been placed on public view. He also reported that an unextracted bullet remains inside the box, said to have been embedded in the discoverer's leg, and stated that he was personally permitted to hold some of the bones.
records.summary_es: Al describir documentos diplomáticos previstos para su publicación en el volumen de Relaciones Exteriores, un telegrama de Washington del 11 de abril enviado al New-York Tribune se enfoca en la serie correspondiente a la República Dominicana. El ministro estadounidense Powell comunicó al Departamento de Estado que las autoridades dominicanas agasajaron al general Máximo Gómez durante su visita a Santo Domingo mostrándole el cofre de Cristóbal Colón y permitiéndole tocar sus restos óseos. Powell describió la urna con unas medidas de 18 por 10 pulgadas y 12 pulgadas de profundidad, señalando que esta constituía apenas la quinta ocasión en que se exponía al público. Asimismo informó que en la caja permanece una bala nunca extraída, supuestamente incrustada en la pierna del descubridor, y declaró que a él personalmente se le permitió sostener parte de los huesos.

records.headline: A front-page report in The Indianapolis Journal recounts revolutionary movements
records.summary_en: A front-page report in The Indianapolis Journal recounts revolutionary movements against government authorities along the northern Dominican coast. Harbor officials who boarded the rebel gunboat Independencia believing she belonged to the government were seized and carried off as prisoners, except for a single man sent ashore to report the incident. The warship proceeded toward Manzanillo carrying rebel leaders, a large crew, and arms, while Governor Don Epiflano Rodriguez of Monte Cristi prepared to resist an attack and local foreigners demanded a warship for protection as the German steamer Valencia offered an avenue of escape. A subsequent St. Thomas dispatch of April 19 adds that rebels are besieging Monte Cristi by land and sea with the Independencia anchored in the harbor, as the revolution gains adherents across the country.
records.summary_es: Una crónica de primera plana en The Indianapolis Journal relata los movimientos revolucionarios contra las autoridades gubernamentales a lo largo de la costa norte dominicana. Los funcionarios del puerto que abordaron el cañonero rebelde Independencia creyendo que pertenecía al gobierno fueron capturados y llevados prisioneros, a excepción de un único hombre enviado a tierra para relatar el suceso. El buque continuó hacia Manzanillo llevando a los jefes rebeldes, una nutrida tripulación y pertrechos, mientras el gobernador de Monte Cristi, don Epiflano Rodríguez, se preparaba para resistir un ataque y los extranjeros de la localidad exigían un buque de guerra para su protección, al tiempo que el vapor alemán Valencia ofrecía una vía de escape. Un posterior despacho fechado el 19 de abril en Saint Thomas añade que los rebeldes están asediando Monte Cristi por tierra y mar con la Independencia fondeada en el puerto, en momentos en que la revolución suma partidarios por todo el país.

records.headline: A Santo Domingo dispatch of April 13 in The Indianapolis Journal reports
records.summary_en: A Santo Domingo dispatch of April 13 in The Indianapolis Journal reports that government troops shelled the capital and launched an assault that ended in severe defeat. Following artillery fire that damaged several houses the previous day, government forces attacked the city in strength at multiple points this morning for one hour before being forced to withdraw with over one hundred men killed or wounded. Government fatalities included General Coredoro, Minister of the Interior, General Alverez, Governor of Puerto Plata, and General Quesada, while President Vasquez narrowly escaped being shot. The revolutionists captured horses, ammunition, and prisoners with only light casualties, while the rebel gunboat Independencia returned and General Navvarro reportedly landed ammunition near Monte Cristi, which rebels are surrounding.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del 13 de abril desde Santo Domingo publicado en The Indianapolis Journal informa que las fuerzas gubernamentales bombardearon la capital y emprendieron un asalto que concluyó en una grave derrota. Tras el fuego de artillería que dañó varias casas el día anterior, las tropas del gobierno atacaron la ciudad con fuerza en múltiples puntos esta mañana durante una hora antes de verse forzadas a replegarse con más de cien bajas entre muertos y heridos. Entre las bajas fatales del gobierno figuraron el general Coredoro, ministro de lo Interior, el general Alverez, gobernador de Puerto Plata, y el general Quesada, mientras que el presidente Vásquez escapó por poco de ser alcanzado por los disparos. Los revolucionarios capturaron caballos, municiones y prisioneros con pérdidas mínimas, al tiempo que regresó el cañonero rebelde Independencia y se informó que el general Navvarro desembarcó pertrechos cerca de Monte Cristi, plaza que los rebeldes mantienen cercada.

records.summary_en: Government forces renewed artillery fire on the capital and suffered a disastrous repulse, according to an April 21 dispatch from Santo Domingo in The Beatrice Daily Express. After damaging several houses with shelling, government soldiers attacked the city in force at various points for one hour before being beaten back with more than 100 men killed or wounded. Minister of the Interior General Cordera, Puerto Plata Governor General Alvarez, and General Queseda were among the government dead, while President Vasquez narrowly escaped being shot. The revolutionists took prisoners, horses, and ammunition with only slight losses, while the rebel gunboat Independence returned and General Navarro landed ammunition near Monte Cristo, which remains surrounded by insurgents.

records.headline: A note regarding the Dominican Republic in the forthcoming Foreign Relations volume
records.summary_en: A note regarding the Dominican Republic in the forthcoming Foreign Relations volume is highlighted in The Weekly Register, citing a report from U.S. Minister Powell. Powell recounted that Dominican officials extended special honors to General Maximo Gomez during the visit of Cuban soldiers to Santo Domingo, allowing him to inspect and handle the casket holding the bones of Christopher Columbus. The relics are kept in a casket measuring 18x10 inches and 12 inches deep, exposed on this occasion for only the fifth time. The dispatch notes that the casket contains an unextracted bullet embedded in the discoverer's leg, which Dominican authorities claim proves these relics are his authentic mortal remains and not those taken from Havana some years ago, while Powell added that he personally held some of the bones.

records.headline: The Portland Daily Press publishes a series of dispatches from San Domingo chronicling
records.summary_en: The Portland Daily Press publishes a series of dispatches from San Domingo chronicling the rapid collapse of the Dominican government in late April. Following fighting that transformed the capital, the whereabouts of President Vasquez and his followers remained unknown, though they were believed to have fled toward San Pedro de Macoris. An April 21 dispatch notes that government garrisons at Azua de Compostela, Bani, and San Cristobal joined the revolution, the rebel gunboat Independence sailed to enforce the surrender of San Pedro de Macoris, and 300 families were left homeless in the capital after the burning of San Carlos. By April 22, garrisons at Barahona, San Pedro de Macoris, and Seibo had also joined the northern insurgents, completing the overthrow of Vasquez and leading to the formation of a provisional government headed by A. Wos-Gil.
records.summary_es: The Portland Daily Press publica una serie de despachos desde Santo Domingo que documenta el rápido colapso del gobierno dominicano a finales de abril. Tras los combates que transformaron la situación en la capital, se desconocía el paradero del presidente Vásquez y sus partidarios, aunque se presumía que habían huido hacia San Pedro de Macorís. Un despacho del 21 de abril señala que las guarniciones gubernamentales de Azua de Compostela, Baní y San Cristóbal se sumaron a la revolución, el cañonero rebelde Independence zarpó para forzar la capitulación de San Pedro de Macorís, y unas 300 familias quedaron sin hogar en la capital tras el incendio del suburbio de San Carlos. Para el 22 de abril, las fuerzas de Barahona, San Pedro de Macorís y El Seibo también se habían unido a los insurrectos del norte, consumando el derrocamiento de Vásquez y propiciando la formación de un gobierno provisional presidido por A. Wos-Gil.

records.headline: A Cape Haytien cable of April 23 in The Savannah Morning News relays
records.summary_en: A Cape Haytien cable of April 23 in The Savannah Morning News relays reports brought by the German cruiser Vineta regarding the battle for Santo Domingo on April 18. President Vasquez led a vigorous morning assault that breached the city after an hour of fierce fighting, but government troops were quickly driven back with heavy casualties, confirming the deaths of Interior Minister Casimero Cordero and Puerto Plata Governor General Alvarez. The retreat degenerated into panic, leaving Vasquez with barely fifty loyal men as he fled and abandoned all supplies. When the Vineta departed on April 20, quiet had returned to the capital amid acute food shortages, while foreign consuls at besieged Monte Cristi requested naval vessels as drinking water rose to forty cents per five gallons.
records.summary_es: Un cable fechado el 23 de abril en Cabo Haitiano y publicado en The Savannah Morning News transmite los informes aportados por el crucero alemán Vineta sobre la batalla librada en Santo Domingo el 18 de abril. El presidente Vásquez encabezó un vigoroso asalto matutino que logró penetrar en la ciudad tras una hora de combate encarnizado, pero las tropas del gobierno fueron expulsadas con rapidez sufriendo graves pérdidas, confirmándose la muerte del ministro de lo Interior Casimero Cordero y del gobernador de Puerto Plata general Alvarez. La retirada se convirtió en pánico y dejó a Vásquez con apenas cincuenta hombres leales al huir abandonando todos sus pertrechos. Al partir el Vineta el 20 de abril, la tranquilidad había retornado a la capital en medio de una severa escasez de víveres, mientras los cónsules extranjeros en la asediada Monte Cristi solicitaban buques de guerra debido a que el agua potable alcanzaba los cuarenta centavos por cada cinco galones.

records.headline: Telegraphic dispatches published in the Wheeling Register report
records.summary_en: Telegraphic dispatches published in the Wheeling Register report on the collapse of the Dominican government and the flight of General Vasquez. An April 27 wire from Havana states that Vasquez, the former president of Santo Domingo, landed that day at Guantanamo, Cuba, aboard a Dominican gunboat. A companion Washington dispatch reveals that Minister Powell informed the State Department that revolutionists had forced the president to transfer his capital to Santiago, while a subsequent cable from Consul Simpson at Puerto Plata confirmed that the Vasquez government had resigned and was in flight.
records.summary_es: Despachos telegráficos publicados en el Wheeling Register dan cuenta del colapso del gobierno dominicano y de la huida del general Vásquez. Un cable del 27 de abril desde La Habana señala que Vásquez, expresidente de Santo Domingo, desembarcó ese mismo día en Guantánamo, Cuba, a bordo de un cañonero dominicano. Un despacho simultáneo de Washington revela que el ministro Powell comunicó al Departamento de Estado que los revolucionarios habían obligado al mandatario a trasladar su capital a Santiago, mientras que un telegrama posterior del cónsul Simpson desde Puerto Plata confirmó que el gobierno de Vásquez había renunciado y se encontraba en fuga.

records.headline: Interviewed in New York following dispatches from Puerto Plata
records.summary_en: Interviewed in New York following dispatches from Puerto Plata, the Dominican consul general and chargé d'affaires welcomed his brother President Vasquez's decision to surrender power, according to the New-York Tribune. Identifying loyal governors General Ramon Caceres of Santiago and General Luis Maria Hernandez of San Pedro de Macoris, the consul general declared that his brother preferred national peace over an office plagued by ceaseless uprisings. Vasquez stated he will relinquish the consulate once instructed and move with his five children to Cuba to join his brother in an agricultural enterprise. The report reviews how Vasquez had overthrown General Juan Isidro Jiminez a year earlier, and notes that General Alejandro Wos y Gil, leader of the current revolt who now assumes the presidency, had previously served as president from 1835 to 1887 as printed in the dispatch and represented the Heureaux administration in New York.
records.summary_es: Entrevistado en Nueva York a raíz de despachos procedentes de Puerto Plata, el cónsul general y encargado de negocios dominicano acogió con satisfacción la decisión de su hermano, el presidente Vásquez, de deponer el mando, según consigna el New-York Tribune. Al identificar a los leales gobernadores general Ramón Cáceres, de Santiago, y general Luis María Hernández, de San Pedro de Macorís, el cónsul general declaró que su hermano prefería la paz nacional antes que retener un cargo agobiado por incesantes insurrecciones. Vásquez anunció que abandonará el consulado tan pronto como reciba instrucciones y se trasladará a Cuba junto a sus cinco hijos para emprender un proyecto agrícola con su hermano. La crónica recuerda cómo Vásquez había derrocado al general Juan Isidro Jimenes un año antes, y subraya que el general Alejandro Wos y Gil, cabecilla de la actual sublevación que asume la presidencia, ya había gobernado el país entre 1835 y 1887 según el texto impreso y representado al gobierno de Heureaux en Nueva York.

records.headline: A correspondence published in the New-York Tribune condemns
records.summary_en: A correspondence published in the New-York Tribune condemns the harsh treatment inflicted by Vasquez officials on the daughter of the late Dominican hero General Luperon. The paper observes that while the late despot Heureaux—killed four years earlier in Moca by Ramon Caceres—considered Luperon his enemy, he never molested his daughter, whereas Vasquez's subordinates placed an armed cordon around her Puerto Plata villa where she lived with her grandmother and two young children. For five days no one was permitted to enter or leave, and a domestic servant was jailed simply for attempting to fetch water from a street pump. The account emphasizes that the accusation of funding the revolution was entirely baseless, stirring widespread indignation in Puerto Plata since the lady never took part in politics.
records.summary_es: Una correspondencia publicada en el New-York Tribune condena el trato vejatorio infligido por los funcionarios de Vásquez contra la hija del prócer dominicano general Luperón. El periódico destaca que si bien el difunto déspota Heureaux —muerto cuatro años antes en Moca a manos de Ramón Cáceres— consideraba a Luperón su enemigo, jamás hostigó a su hija, mientras que los subalternos de Vásquez tendieron un cerco armado alrededor de su villa en Puerto Plata, donde residía pacíficamente con su abuela y dos hijos pequeños. Durante cinco días no se permitió la entrada ni salida de persona alguna, y un sirviente doméstico fue encarcelado por el simple hecho de intentar buscar agua en una bomba pública de la calle. La crónica enfatiza que la acusación de suministrar fondos a la revolución era totalmente infundada, lo que provocó una viva indignación en Puerto Plata, dado que la dama jamás intervino en política.

records.headline: Reviewing the tumultuous Dominican upheaval, The Hawaiian Gazette sketches
records.summary_en: Reviewing the tumultuous Dominican upheaval, The Hawaiian Gazette sketches the military and political career of forty-three-year-old General Vasquez. The article recounts that Vasquez, exiled to New York under Heureaux, allegedly returned in time to assist in the dictator's assassination, became vice president under Jiminez, and subsequently led the revolt that overthrew Jiminez following the capitulation of San Domingo. Although popular with foreign residents, Vasquez faced domestic opposition from Heureaux's allies, including General Peppin and General Wos Gil, who launched a new uprising supported by arms from Jiminez's New York junta. Following Peppin's death in battle, Wos Gil assumed power in the capital and was elected president, though the return of Jiminez to the island now forces Gil either to yield office to the ex-president or face renewed conflict.
records.summary_es: Al reseñar la turbulenta convulsión dominicana, The Hawaiian Gazette bosqueja la trayectoria militar y política del general Vásquez, de cuarenta y tres años de edad. El artículo relata que Vásquez, quien fue desterrado a Nueva York durante el régimen de Heureaux, supuestamente regresó a tiempo para cooperar en el ajusticiamiento del dictador, ejerció como vicepresidente bajo la presidencia de Jimenes y luego encabezó la revuelta que derrocó a este tras la capitulación de Santo Domingo. Si bien contaba con el aprecio de los residentes extranjeros, Vásquez enfrentó la hostilidad interna de los allegados a Heureaux, entre ellos el general Peppin y el general Wos Gil, quienes iniciaron una nueva insurrección pertrechada con armas facilitadas por la junta neoyorquina de Jimenes. Tras la muerte de Peppin en combate, Wos Gil tomó el poder en la capital y fue proclamado presidente, aunque el regreso de Jimenes a la isla obligará a Gil a ceder el cargo ante el expresidente o precipitarse a una nueva guerra.

records.headline: A biographical overview of Dominican politics in The Hawaiian Star outlines
records.summary_en: A biographical overview of Dominican politics in The Hawaiian Star outlines the events surrounding General Vasquez and his recent overthrow. Vasquez, aged forty-three, gained military experience in periodic civil conflicts and was exiled to New York by Heureaux before allegedly returning just in time to assist in Heureaux's assassination. After serving as vice president under Jiminez, Vasquez spearheaded the movement that toppled Jiminez and took the presidency upon securing the capitulation of San Domingo. His domestic unpopularity soon prompted Heureaux's associates, including General Peppin and General Wos Gil, to launch an insurrection backed with weapons from Jiminez's junta in New York; following Peppin's battlefield death, Wos Gil gained the presidency in the capital, where he now confronts the choice of yielding power to the returning Jiminez or waging another revolution.
records.summary_es: Una reseña biográfica sobre la política dominicana publicada en The Hawaiian Star expone los acontecimientos en torno al general Vásquez y su reciente derrocamiento. Vásquez, de cuarenta y tres años, adquirió rango militar en constantes guerras civiles y fue desterrado a Nueva York por Heureaux antes de regresar supuestamente justo a tiempo para cooperar en el ajusticiamiento del dictador. Tras actuar como vicepresidente de Jimenes, Vásquez encabezó el levantamiento que despojó a este del poder y asumió la presidencia al lograr la capitulación de Santo Domingo. Su impopularidad interna motivó que partidarios de Heureaux, encabezados por el general Peppin y el general Wos Gil, desataran una insurrección abastecida de pertrechos por la junta de Jimenes en Nueva York; caído Peppin en combate, Wos Gil se alzó con la presidencia en la capital, donde ahora encara el dilema de transferir el mando al retornado Jimenes o librar otra contienda armada.

records.headline: An editorial in The Sun reconsiders arguments that annexing
records.summary_en: An editorial in The Sun reconsiders arguments that annexing the Dominican Republic would make its colored inhabitants United States citizens entitled to statehood, observing that conditions have completely changed. The article asserts that the Dominican people would be entirely satisfied with the status currently held by the inhabitants of Porto Rico, where American authority would ensure similar prosperity. Furthermore, the paper maintains that under United States control they would achieve a level of material well-being exceeding what the inhabitants of Porto Rico or even Cuba could hope to reach in agriculture.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en The Sun reexamina los antiguos argumentos de que la anexión de la República Dominicana convertiría a sus habitantes de color en ciudadanos de los Estados Unidos con derecho a la condición de estado, observando que las condiciones han cambiado por completo. El artículo afirma que el pueblo dominicano estaría plenamente satisfecho con el estatus que actualmente tienen los habitantes de Puerto Rico, donde la autoridad estadounidense les garantizaría una prosperidad similar. Además, el periódico sostiene que bajo el control de los Estados Unidos alcanzarían un nivel de bienestar material superior al que los habitantes de Puerto Rico o incluso de Cuba podrían aspirar a lograr en la agricultura.

records.headline: This article argues that Samana Bay, on the eastern coast of Santo Domingo, is one of the great maritime positions of the Antilles
records.summary_en: This article argues that Samana Bay, on the eastern coast of Santo Domingo, is one of the great maritime positions of the Antilles, a harbour from which operations could be conducted by any kind of war vessel and in which a blockaded fleet might lie in safety. It praises the island's fertility, rivalling Cuba's, and its possible products of tobacco, coffee, indigo, sugar, cocoa, fruits and vegetables, noting that millions of acres lie wild for lack of cultivators and transport, and recalls the era of comparative peace under President Heureaux, who was assassinated on July 26, 1899.
records.summary_es: Este artículo sostiene que la bahía de Samaná, en la costa oriental de Santo Domingo, es una de las grandes posiciones marítimas de las Antillas, un puerto desde el cual podrían realizarse operaciones con cualquier clase de buque de guerra y en el que una flota bloqueada podría permanecer a salvo. Elogia la fertilidad de la isla, que rivaliza con la de Cuba, y sus posibles productos de tabaco, café, añil, azúcar, cacao, frutas y vegetales, señalando que millones de acres permanecen incultos por falta de cultivadores y de transporte, y recuerda la era de paz comparativa bajo el presidente Heureaux, asesinado el 26 de julio de 1899.

records.headline: Writing editorially, The Savannah Morning News comments on recent
records.summary_en: Writing editorially, The Savannah Morning News comments on recent announcements regarding the striking of oil in Santo Domingo following German capitalist initiatives, observing that these new supplies challenge the belief that American and Russian trusts monopolize the world's petroleum. The editorial remarks that the presence of oil may stimulate a desire in the United States for the annexation of the island. The paper adds that Mr. Rockefeller could more easily capture the Dominican oil fields under the American flag, assisted by his allies in the Republican Party.
records.summary_es: En una nota editorial, The Savannah Morning News comenta los recientes anuncios sobre el descubrimiento de petróleo en Santo Domingo tras las iniciativas de capitalistas alemanes, observando que estas nuevas fuentes desafían la creencia de que los monopolios estadounidenses y rusos acaparan el petróleo del mundo. El editorial señala que la presencia de petróleo podría avivar en los Estados Unidos el deseo de anexar la isla. El periódico añade que el señor Rockefeller podría apoderarse más fácilmente de los yacimientos petrolíferos dominicanos bajo la bandera estadounidense, con la ayuda de sus aliados del Partido Republicano.

records.headline: The New-York Tribune reports that the Dominican consulate in New York
records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune reports that the Dominican consulate in New York, closed for three months pending an appointment by the new administration, is set to reopen under Señor Manuel Galvan as consul general and chargé d'affaires appointed by President A. Wos y Gil. When General Wos y Gil overthrew President Horacio Vasquez, the former consul general, who was Vasquez's brother, resigned and left consular affairs under Spanish Consul Seiral by instruction of the victorious rebel chief. Speaking at the Hotel Muro, Señor Galvan stated that the Dominican people are well pleased with President Wos y Gil and look forward to an extended period of peace and prosperity.
records.summary_es: El New-York Tribune informa que el consulado dominicano en Nueva York, cerrado durante tres meses a la espera de una designación por parte de la nueva administración, reabrirá sus puertas bajo la dirección del señor Manuel Galván como cónsul general y encargado de negocios nombrado por el presidente A. Wos y Gil. Cuando el general Wos y Gil derrocó al presidente Horacio Vasquez, el anterior cónsul general, hermano de Vasquez, renunció y dejó los asuntos consulares en manos del cónsul español Seiral por instrucciones del victorioso jefe rebelde. En declaraciones desde el Hotel Muro, el señor Galván manifestó que el pueblo dominicano está muy complacido con el presidente Wos y Gil y anticipa un prolongado período de paz y prosperidad.

records.headline: Reporting on diplomatic representations, The Birmingham Age-Herald states
records.summary_en: Reporting on diplomatic representations, The Birmingham Age-Herald states that the United States government will not accept the neutralization of Dominican waters or opening of free ports, given that San Domingo is a neighboring state. Washington declares it will not allow European coaling stations, territorial cessions, or exclusive foreign naval access in Dominican waters in peace or war. Furthermore, no Dominican territory may be classed as neutral if it conflicts with the Clyde Line concession exempting its vessels from foreign port dues. The paper notes that the protest has excited considerable comment, highlighting Minister Powell's determination to see American rights respected by the government of Dominica.
records.summary_es: Al informar sobre representaciones diplomáticas, The Birmingham Age-Herald señala que el gobierno de los Estados Unidos no aceptará la neutralización de las aguas dominicanas ni la apertura de puertos francos, dado que Santo Domingo es un estado vecino. Washington declara que no permitirá estaciones carboneras europeas, cesiones territoriales ni el acceso naval exclusivo de extranjeros en aguas dominicanas en tiempos de paz o de guerra. Asimismo, ningún territorio dominicano podrá considerarse neutral si entra en conflicto con la concesión de la línea Clyde, la cual exime a sus buques de derechos portuarios extranjeros. El periódico añade que la protesta ha despertado considerables comentarios, destacando la determinación del ministro Powell de lograr que los derechos estadounidenses sean respetados por el gobierno de Dominica.

records.headline: The United States government will not view in a friendly spirit
records.summary_en: The United States government will not view in a friendly spirit the neutralization of Dominican waters or the creation of free ports, The Courier-Journal reports, observing that San Domingo is a neighboring state. The dispatch emphasizes that Washington forbids the establishment of European coaling ports, territorial cessions, and exclusive foreign naval use of Dominican waters in peace or war. In addition, no territory may be classed as neutral to the detriment of the Clyde Line's port due exemptions. The paper notes that the American protest has aroused considerable discussion, underscoring Minister Powell's resolve to have American rights respected by the Government of Dominica.
records.summary_es: El gobierno de los Estados Unidos no verá con ánimo amistoso la neutralización de las aguas dominicanas ni la creación de puertos francos, informa The Courier-Journal, observando que Santo Domingo es un estado vecino. El despacho recalca que Washington prohíbe el establecimiento de puertos carboneros europeos, las cesiones territoriales y el uso naval exclusivo de aguas dominicanas por parte de extranjeros en tiempos de paz o de guerra. Además, ningún territorio podrá declararse neutral en perjuicio de las exenciones de derechos portuarios de la línea Clyde. El periódico señala que la protesta estadounidense ha suscitado amplios comentarios, subrayando la resolución del ministro Powell de hacer respetar los derechos de los estadounidenses ante el gobierno de Dominica.

records.headline: The Omaha Daily Bee reports that United States Minister Powell delivered
records.summary_en: The Omaha Daily Bee reports that United States Minister Powell delivered a vigorous reply rejecting the Dominican government's bill to neutralize Dominican waters and create free ports, calling the foreign minister's response highly objectionable. Meanwhile, the Dominican foreign office informed Powell that it will pay the long-disputed claim of J. Sala & Co. within a few days under the American minister's adjustment proposal. Originating from approximately 1215,000 in loans and munitions supplied by Sala to late President Heureaux of the Dominican Republic, the claim passed to Sala's American widow and was awarded $523,000 with interest by an international tribunal. After Salvador declared the award void—a finding Secretary Hay refused to recognize—a compromise settlement was reached at 67H percent of the awarded amount.
records.summary_es: El Omaha Daily Bee informa que el ministro de los Estados Unidos Powell presentó una enérgica respuesta rechazando el proyecto del gobierno dominicano para neutralizar las aguas dominicanas y crear puertos francos, calificando la respuesta del ministro de relaciones exteriores de sumamente objetable. Mientras tanto, la cancillería dominicana comunicó a Powell que liquidará la prolongada reclamación de J. Sala & Co. en pocos días conforme a la propuesta de ajuste del ministro estadounidense. Originada en aproximadamente 1215,000 en préstamos y pertrechos suministrados por Sala al difunto presidente Heureaux de la República Dominicana, la reclamación pasó a su viuda estadounidense y un tribunal internacional le concedió $523,000 con intereses. Luego de que Salvador anulara el laudo —medida que el secretario Hay rehusó reconocer—, se alcanzó un acuerdo transaccional al 67H por ciento de la suma concedida.

records.headline: The Salt Lake Herald reports that United States Minister Powell delivered
records.summary_en: The Salt Lake Herald reports that United States Minister Powell delivered an autograph letter from President Roosevelt at the national palace congratulating General Wos y Gil upon his election as constitutional president of the Dominican Republic. Powell conveyed the cordial wishes of the American president and people for the republic's prosperity, emphasizing that Santo Domingo must fulfill its obligations and agreements to preserve this friendship. The minister affirmed that Washington does not seek to impair the nation's autonomy and stands ready to protect its territorial rights if needed, though it will not intervene to shield Santo Domingo against lawful creditors. President Gil responded that Santo Domingo desires to act in complete accord.
records.summary_es: The Salt Lake Herald informa que el ministro de los Estados Unidos Powell entregó en el palacio nacional una carta autógrafa del presidente Roosevelt felicitando al general Wos y Gil por su elección como presidente constitucional de la República Dominicana. Powell transmitió los cordiales deseos del presidente y del pueblo estadounidense por la prosperidad de la república, recalcando que Santo Domingo debe cumplir con sus obligaciones y acuerdos para conservar dicha amistad. El ministro afirmó que Washington no procura menoscabar la autonomía de la nación y está dispuesto a proteger sus derechos territoriales en caso de necesidad, aunque no intervendrá para escudar a Santo Domingo frente a sus acreedores legítimos. El presidente Gil respondió que Santo Domingo desea actuar en completo acuerdo.

President Gil replied that Santo Domingo intends to act in complete harmony with its powerful neighbor and resolve differences amicably, expressing gratitude for the kind words from President Roosevelt and welcoming his desire for the prosperity of Dominica and its people.

No obstante, los Estados Unidos no intervendrán para proteger a Santo Domingo de sus acreedores legítimos. El presidente Gil respondió que Santo Domingo se propone actuar en completa armonía con su poderoso vecino y solventar las diferencias de forma amistosa, manifestando su agradecimiento por las amables palabras del presidente Roosevelt y celebrando su deseo en favor de la prosperidad de Dominica y de su pueblo.

records.headline: A dispatch from Cape Haitien in The Kendrick Gazette reports
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Cape Haitien in The Kendrick Gazette reports that the town of Santiago in the Dominican Republic was surrounded by insurgent troops commanded by General Epifanio Rodriguez. Following several hours of severe fighting that left multiple men wounded, the revolutionists triumphed and captured Santiago. The insurrection in northern Santo Domingo, which has already established a provisional government at Puerto Plata under General Morales, was reportedly provoked by widespread customhouse frauds and the prevarications of the ministers of war and the foreign office.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Cabo Haitiano en The Kendrick Gazette informa que la ciudad de Santiago, en la República Dominicana, fue rodeada por tropas insurgentes al mando del general Epifanio Rodríguez. Tras varias horas de intensos combates que dejaron a varios hombres heridos, los revolucionarios triunfaron y se apoderaron de Santiago. La insurrección en el norte de Santo Domingo, que ya ha establecido un gobierno provisional en Puerto Plata presidido por el general Morales, fue presuntamente provocada por generalizados fraudes aduaneros y las prevaricaciones de los ministros de guerra y de relaciones exteriores.

records.headline: A Cape Haytien dispatch in the Rock Island Argus reports that a revolution
records.summary_en: A Cape Haytien dispatch in the Rock Island Argus reports that a revolution broke out on Saturday across northern Santo Domingo, establishing a provisional government at Puerto Plata under General Morales amid allegations of customhouse frauds and ministerial prevarications in war and finance. Supporters of President Wos y Gil in Puerto Plata were attacked Saturday evening, while forces from Monte Cristi, La Ligne, and Moca united to attack and surround Santiago, severing telegraphic communication. The revolutionary movement is expanding, Vice President Deschamps has fled to safety, and common opinion considers Wos y Gil's government doomed.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Cabo Haitiano en el Rock Island Argus informa que el sábado estalló una revolución en el norte de Santo Domingo, estableciendo un gobierno provisional en Puerto Plata bajo el general Morales en medio de denuncias de fraudes aduaneros y prevaricaciones ministeriales en guerra y hacienda. Los partidarios del presidente Wos y Gil en Puerto Plata fueron atacados el sábado por la noche, mientras que fuerzas de Montecristi, La Ligne y Moca se unieron para atacar y sitiar Santiago, cortando la comunicación telegráfica. El movimiento revolucionario se extiende, el vicepresidente Deschamps ha huido para ponerse a salvo y la opinión general da por perdido al gobierno de Wos y Gil.

records.headline: Insurgent forces under General Epifanio Rodriguez surrounded
records.summary_en: Insurgent forces under General Epifanio Rodriguez surrounded Santiago in the Dominican Republic and captured the town, The Daily Kennebec Journal reports, after several hours of severe combat that left several men wounded. The revolution which has broken out in the northern part of the republic of Santo Domingo and which has already resulted in the establishment of a provisional government at Puerto Plata under the presidency of General Morales, was caused, according to advices received here, by the numerous custom house frauds and the prevarications of the ministers of war and of finance. Telegraphic communication between Santiago and La Vega has been severed. The Cape Haytien dispatch says the revolutionary movement is extending; Vice President Deschamps has abandoned the government and has arrived here in a small sailing boat from Monte Cristi; and the general opinion is that the government of President Woss y Gil is lost.

records.summary_en: The Eagle prints the closing part of a Paris dispatch and a Cape Haytien dispatch of October 25: the revolutionary movement in the republic of Santo Domingo is in favor of former President Jiminez; the revolution is spreading and, according to the dispatches received here, all the inhabitants of the region of Monte Cibao have joined the uprising against the government; and the election of General Morales as president of the provisional government is said to be a step taken pending the arrival of General Jiminez, who will be elected president of the republic if the revolution is successful. The Cape Haytien dispatch says the town of Santiago in the Dominican republic was surrounded this morning by insurgent troops under the command of General Epifanio Rodriguez; after severe fighting, which lasted for several hours, and during which a number of men were wounded, the revolutionists triumphed and Santiago fell into their hands. The signal for the outbreak of the revolt was given at 2 o'clock on Saturday afternoon by three cannon shots; that same evening all the partisans of President Woss y Gil at Puerto Plata were arrested; the inhabitants of Monte Cristi, La Ligne and Moca united and attacked Santiago; and telegraphic communication between Santiago and La Vega has been severed.

records.headline: The Times prints the Santiago dispatch from its account of the causes of the revolution:
records.summary_en: The Times prints the Santiago dispatch from its account of the causes of the revolution: the revolution which has broken out in the northern part of the republic of Santo Domingo and which has already resulted in the establishment of a provisional government under the presidency of General Morales at Puerto Plata was, according to advices received here, caused by the numerous custom house frauds and the prevarications of the ministers of war and of finance. The signal for the outbreak of the revolt was given at 2 o'clock on Saturday afternoon by three cannon shots. That same evening all the partisans of President Woss y Gil at Puerto Plata were arrested. The inhabitants of Monte Cristi, La Ligne and Moca united and attacked Santiago. That town is now surrounded by revolutionists, who have severed telegraphic communication between Santiago and La Vega. The revolutionary movement is extending. Vice President Deschamps has sought safety in flight and is said to be hidden in Monte Cristi, where he is seeking an opportunity to embark on board some vessel bound for a foreign port. The general opinion is that the government of President Woss y Gil is lost. General Woss y Gil headed the revolution which broke out in Santo Domingo in March of the present year and resulted in the overthrow of Horacio Vasquez; Gil was elected president in June, and in July the Dominican congress ratified his election. The present revolution is said to be in favor of former President Jiminez, who was ousted in May, 1902, by the revolutionary forces commanded by Vasquez, at that time the vice president.

Esa población está ahora rodeada por los revolucionarios, quienes han cortado la comunicación telegráfica entre Santiago y La Vega. El movimiento revolucionario se extiende. El vicepresidente Deschamps ha buscado la seguridad en la fuga y se dice que está escondido en Monte Cristi, donde busca una oportunidad de embarcarse en algún buque con destino a un puerto extranjero. La opinión general es que el gobierno del presidente Woss y Gil está perdido. El general Woss y Gil encabezó la revolución que estalló en Santo Domingo en marzo del presente año y que resultó en el derrocamiento de Horacio Vásquez; Gil fue elegido presidente en junio, y en julio el congreso dominicano ratificó su elección. Se dice que la presente revolución es a favor del expresidente Jiménez, quien fue expulsado en mayo de 1902 por las fuerzas revolucionarias comandadas por Vásquez, en ese entonces el vicepresidente.

records.summary_en: The Times prints a dispatch from Cape Haitien, dated October 27: the town of Santiago, in the Dominican republic, was surrounded yesterday morning by insurgent troops under the command of General Epifanio Rodriguez; after severe fighting, which lasted for several hours and during which a number of men were wounded, the revolutionists triumphed and Santiago fell into their hands. Vice President Deschamps has arrived here in a small sailboat from Monte Cristi; he has abandoned the government. The revolution which has broken out in the northern part of the republic of Santo Domingo, and which already has resulted in the establishment of a provisional government under the presidency of General Carlos Morales at Puerto Plata, was, according to advices received here, caused by the numerous custom house frauds and the prevarications of the ministers of war and of finance. The dispatch appears under the head 'Insurgent Troops, Under General Rodriguez, Take Town After Severe Fighting.'

records.headline: The Journal prints a Cape Haytien dispatch dated October 27:
records.summary_en: The Journal prints a Cape Haytien dispatch dated October 27: the Dominican government cruiser Independencia appeared off Puerto Plata, the port on the north coast of Santo Domingo, which is in the hands of the Dominican revolutionists, to-day, and prevented the Cuban mail steamer Maria Herrera from entering that port; the Independencia then left Puerto Plata, going towards the American mail steamer Cherokee, coming from Monte Cristi, in order to prevent her from touching at Puerto Plata. The town of La Vega has been captured by insurgents under General Roca. In an interview to-day General Deschamps, the vice president of the Dominican republic, who has abandoned the government and fled to this port, said: 'The people were deceived when General Jiminez was appointed fiscal agent of the Dominican republic in the United States by President Woss y Gil, and his resignation agitated the public feeling. My departure provoked the insurrection in Cibao, where I had controlled the malcontents. It was sufficient that I turned my back for the gunpowder to ignite.' General Deschamps does not appear to have decided upon a course of action; his possible political pretensions are not known. It is said here that General Jiminez may arrive any moment at Monte Cristi, where he will be received by the people with enthusiasm.

records.headline: The Republic prints the closing words of a dispatch on the revolution
records.summary_en: The Republic prints the closing words of a dispatch on the revolution and a Washington item of October 27 headed 'Explanation Due': the leaders of the revolution are stated not to be in need of supplies, and it is the general opinion that the government of Woss-y-Gil is lost. The Washington item says a full explanation of the stopping of the American mail steamer Cherokee at Porto Plata by a Dominican warship will to-morrow be demanded of the Dominican Republic by the State Department; an American cruiser or gunboat will meantime be ordered to Porto Plata and prevent further arbitrary interference with commerce, either by so-called blockades or otherwise. Up to the time a Republic dispatch stating the Cherokee had been turned back at Porto Plata was shown to a State Department official to-night the department had received no advices regarding this occurrence; the only advices received to-day came from Minister Powell at Santo Domingo City and stated that Porto Plata was in a state of revolution. From this it is inferred the Dominican government has instituted a blockade with the idea of cutting off the revolutionists' source of supplies. According to international law, however, a blockade, to be recognized by other powers, must be preceded by a formal notification of its institution. The tendency of the Central American and West Indian governments, particularly Haiti and Santo Domingo, has been so arbitrary in this regard that no blockade not preceded by formal notification long enough to exempt ships sailing before notice is given will be tolerated by the United States government.
records.summary_es: El Republic publica las palabras finales de un despacho sobre la revolución y una nota de Washington del 27 de octubre titulada «Explanation Due»: se afirma que los líderes de la revolución no necesitan suministros, y es la opinión general que el gobierno de Woss-y-Gil está perdido. De ello se infiere que el gobierno dominicano ha instituido un bloqueo con la idea de cortar la fuente de suministros de los revolucionarios. Según el derecho internacional, sin embargo, un bloqueo, para ser reconocido por otras potencias, debe ir precedido de una notificación formal de su institución. La tendencia de los gobiernos centroamericanos y de las Indias Occidentales, particularmente Haití y Santo Domingo, ha sido tan arbitraria a este respecto que el gobierno de los Estados Unidos no tolerará ningún bloqueo que no haya sido precedido por una notificación formal con antelación suficiente para eximir a los buques que zarparon antes de que se diera el aviso.

records.headline: The Star prints a navy-yard item: the cruiser Baltimore, under orders
records.summary_en: The Star prints a navy-yard item: the cruiser Baltimore, under orders from Washington to proceed forthwith to Puerto Plata, San Domingo, to protect American interests at that blockaded port, cannot get away to-day and will necessarily be detained until to-morrow, being at the yard undergoing repairs; she is to convoy Lieut. Chandler's torpedo destroyer flotilla from Hampton Roads to the Philippine Islands. Orders have been sent to the Norfolk navy yard for the dispatch of the cruiser Baltimore without delay to Puerto Plata, San Domingo, to look after American interests in that vicinity; the Dominican government has established a blockade of Puerto Plata to prevent assistance reaching the revolutionists; it has been expected here that the Baltimore would be ready to-night and that she would reach Puerto Plata Wednesday next. The Baltimore has recently been fitted out to convoy the torpedo flotilla from Hampton Roads to the Philippines, but there has been some delay in the torpedo boat destroyers, and the fleet will hardly be ready to sail on its first cruise before the middle of November; on the present mission it is probable that she will await the torpedo boat flotilla in West Indian waters, starting with them from Hampton Roads. The cruiser is commanded by Captain Briggs of Boston, whose wife has just died as the result of a surgical operation in a Baltimore hospital.

Se han enviado órdenes al astillero naval de Norfolk para el envío del crucero Baltimore sin demora a Puerto Plata, Santo Domingo, para atender los intereses estadounidenses en esa vecindad; el gobierno dominicano ha establecido un bloqueo de Puerto Plata para impedir que llegue ayuda a los revolucionarios; se esperaba aquí que el Baltimore estuviera listo esta noche y que llegaría a Puerto Plata el próximo miércoles. El Baltimore ha sido equipado recientemente para escoltar la flotilla torpedera desde Hampton Roads hasta Filipinas, pero ha habido cierta demora en los destructores torpederos, y la flota difícilmente estará lista para zarpar en su primer crucero antes de mediados de noviembre; en la presente misión es probable que espere a la flotilla torpedera en aguas de las Indias Occidentales, partiendo con ellos desde Hampton Roads. records.headline: The Call prints the closing part of Powell's report on the revolution
records.summary_en: The Call prints the closing part of Powell's report on the revolution and a Washington item: the report says the adherents of the late President Jiminez are seeking to overthrow President Woss y Gil, and makes no mention of the reported blockade of that port by the government warship Independencia and the incidental turning away of a Cuban and an American steamship; the State Department has called the attention of the Navy Department to the reports of Powell, and the Navy Department will supply the necessary force to protect American interests. records.headline: The Star prints an item headed 'Minister Powell's Report' and a Norfolk dispatch of October 30:
records.summary_en: The Star prints an item headed 'Minister Powell's Report' and a Norfolk dispatch of October 30: reports say the whole of the northern part of the island has joined in the revolutionary movement. A cablegram received at the State Department to-day from United States Minister Powell at San Domingo reports that conditions in the republic are in a state of great disturbance; the State Department is making vigorous efforts to communicate with Mr. Powell by cable, but with unsatisfactory results, owing to the fact that the insurgents appear to be in possession of the land telegraph lines connecting the capital, San Domingo, with the cable station on the east coast; incidentally this has also interrupted communication with Venezuela. To guard against any further cable lapses the State Department is sending, through the Navy Department, written instructions to Minister Powell for his guidance during the revolution, and these will go forward on the Baltimore, which sails to-day from Hampton Roads directly for San Domingo. The Norfolk dispatch says the cruiser Baltimore sailed at high tide this afternoon for Puerto Plata, San Domingo, where she goes to protect American interests at that port.

records.summary_en: The Bystander prints the Santiago dispatch: Cape Haytien, Hayti, October 27 — the town of Santiago in the Dominican republic was surrounded yesterday morning by insurgent troops under the command of General Epifanio Rodriguez; after severe fighting which lasted for several hours, and during which a number of men were wounded, the revolutionists triumphed and Santiago fell into their hands. The revolution which has broken out in the northern part of the republic of Santo Domingo, and which has already resulted in the establishment of a provisional government at Puerto Plata, under the presidency of General Morales, was caused, according to advices received here, by the numerous customs house frauds and the prevarications of the ministers of war. The revolutionary outbreak is extending, and the general opinion is that the government of President Woss y Gil is lost. Vice-President Deschamps has arrived here in a small sail boat from Monte Cristi; he has abandoned the government. The dispatch appears under the head 'Dominican Revolt'.

records.headline: The Journal prints the closing lines of the martial-law dispatch
records.summary_en: The Journal prints the closing lines of the martial-law dispatch from San Domingo and three Cape Haytien items of October 29: a warship with troops has been sent to Puerto Plata. General Navarro, the revolutionary governor of Monte Cristi, San Domingo, at the head of a strong force of troops, has joined General Morales, commander-in-chief of the forces of the Dominican revolution, with the reported intention of moving the combined forces on the capital, San Domingo. Señor Caceres, former governor of Santiago de los Caballeros, Santo Domingo, under the presidency of General Vasquez, who was exiled to Cuba by the present government of Santo Domingo, has gone to join General Jiminez, the leader of the revolution, at some unknown point, and together they will make another attempt to land in Santo Domingo. It is reported that the French cruiser Jurien de la Graviere, now at Port au Prince, Hayti, has been ordered to San Domingo. Under the head 'Government Cruiser Attacks Puerto Plata,' the third item, sent via Paris, says the Dominican government cruiser Independence attacked to-day Puerto Plata, the port on the north coast of the island which is in the hands of the insurgents.
