records.summary_en: The News and Observer prints the closing part of the Cape Haytien dispatch of October 29 and the San Domingo martial-law dispatch of October 29: a strong force of troops has joined General Morales, commander-in-chief of the forces of the Dominican revolution, with the reported intention of moving the combined forces on the capital, San Domingo. The blockade of the port of Puerto Plata, on the north coast of Santo Domingo, which is held by the revolutionists, has caused provisions there to become very dear. A force of Dominican revolutionists has occupied Cotuy. It is presumed that the Dominican government forces will be concentrated at the capital, where heavy fighting is expected to take place. The San Domingo dispatch says that, owing to the rebellion in the northern part of the republic, the government has decreed the suspension of the constitutional guarantees and is enforcing martial law; this city and its vicinity is quiet; active measures are being taken to suppress the revolution; and a warship with troops has been sent to Puerto Plata.
records.summary_es: El News and Observer publica la parte final del despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 29 de octubre y el despacho de Santo Domingo sobre la ley marcial del 29 de octubre: una fuerte fuerza de tropas se ha unido al general Morales, comandante en jefe de las fuerzas de la revolución dominicana, con la intención reportada de mover las fuerzas combinadas sobre la capital, Santo Domingo. El bloqueo del puerto de Puerto Plata, en la costa norte de Santo Domingo, que está en manos de los revolucionarios, ha hecho que las provisiones allí se vuelvan muy caras. Una fuerza de revolucionarios dominicanos ha ocupado Cotuy. Se presume que las fuerzas del gobierno dominicano se concentrarán en la capital, donde se espera una lucha fuerte. El despacho de Santo Domingo dice que, debido a la rebelión en la parte norte de la república, el gobierno ha decretado la suspensión de las garantías constitucionales y está aplicando la ley marcial; esta ciudad y su vecindad están tranquilas; se están tomando medidas activas para suprimir la revolución; y un buque de guerra con tropas ha sido enviado a Puerto Plata.

records.headline: The Call prints a Santo Domingo dispatch of October 29 and a Puerto Plata dispatch of October 30:
records.summary_en: The Call prints a Santo Domingo dispatch of October 29 and a Puerto Plata dispatch of October 30: the political situation in this city is unchanged; quiet prevails, but serious troubles may arise here at any time and the presence of an American warship is desirable. The Clyde line steamer Cherokee from New York arrived to-day; she had been prevented by the Dominican government cruiser Independencia from calling at Puerto Plata, Samana, and Macoris; she reports that the whole of the northern part of the island is joined in the revolutionary movement. The Puerto Plata dispatch says 'On to the capital' is the cry of the revolutionists; preparations are being hurriedly made for an attack on Santo Domingo; more than 2,000 revolutionists are now at Cotuy under command of Generals Epifanio Rodriguez and Jose Bordas, organizing for battle against the principal city of the republic; the first resistance is expected at Sillon de la Viuda and a desperate battle is anticipated; General Morales is jubilant and confident of the success of the revolution; his friends have cabled money and he announces that his triumph will be accomplished within a few days; and secret advices to the revolutionists state that a steamer has been chartered in Porto Rico to run the blockade; this vessel, with arms and ammunition, is expected here to-morrow.

records.headline: It accuses President Wos y Gil of arbi trariness, jealousy, suspicion
records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that the entire northern region of the Dominican Republic had joined an armed insurrection against President Alejandro Wos y Gil. The insurgents published a manifesto at Puerto Plata detailing grievances against the administration, including the imprisonment of dissidents, widespread financial waste, and default on national debt obligations. The document also fiercely denounced new fiscal burdens on cocoa, port fee concessions granted to the Hamburg-American Line, and an unconstitutional proposal to neutralize Dominican harbors during wartime.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que toda la región norte de la República Dominicana se había sumado a una insurrección armada contra el presidente Alejandro Wos y Gil. Los insurgentes publicaron un manifiesto en Puerto Plata detallando sus agravios contra el gobierno, entre ellos el encarcelamiento de disidentes, el despilfarro financiero generalizado y el impago de las obligaciones de la deuda pública. El documento también repudiaba enérgicamente las nuevas cargas fiscales sobre el cacao, las exenciones de derechos portuarios otorgadas a la Hamburg-American Line y una propuesta inconstitucional para neutralizar los puertos dominicanos durante conflictos bélicos.

records.headline: The Standard prints the Santiago dispatch: Cape Haytien, Hayti
records.summary_en: The Standard prints the Santiago dispatch: Cape Haytien, Hayti, October 27 — the town of Santiago, in the Dominican republic, was surrounded this morning by insurgent troops under the command of General Epifanio Rodriguez; after severe fighting, which lasted for several hours and during which a number of men were wounded, the revolutionists triumphed and Santiago fell into their hands. The revolution which has broken out in the northern part of the republic of Santo Domingo and which has already resulted in the establishment of a provisional government at Puerto Plata under the presidency of General Morales, was caused, according to advices received here, by numerous custom house frauds and the prevarications of the ministers of war and of finance. The dispatch appears under the head 'Custom House Frauds and Acts of Ministers Cause Uprising — Santiago Captured by Rebels'.
records.summary_es: El Standard publica el despacho de Santiago: Cabo Haitiano, Haití, 27 de octubre — la población de Santiago, en la república dominicana, fue rodeada esta mañana por tropas insurgentes bajo el mando del general Epifanio Rodríguez; tras una lucha severa, que duró varias horas y durante la cual varios hombres resultaron heridos, los revolucionarios triunfaron y Santiago cayó en sus manos. La revolución que ha estallado en la parte norte de la república de Santo Domingo y que ya ha resultado en el establecimiento de un gobierno provisional en Puerto Plata bajo la presidencia del general Morales, fue causada, según informes recibidos aquí, por numerosos fraudes de aduanas y las prevaricaciones de los ministros de Guerra y de Hacienda. El despacho aparece bajo el titular «Custom House Frauds and Acts of Ministers Cause Uprising — Santiago Captured by Rebels».

records.headline: The Tribune prints the closing part of a New York item on the revolution:
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints the closing part of a New York item on the revolution: Señor Galvan said 500,000 cartridges are held at the order of the government and will be shipped by special steamer, probably to reach San Domingo to-morrow; the government has now a supply on hand of 1,000,000 cartridges, but the additional supply is sent, Señor Galvan said, 'so they don't run short.' The rebels are reported to be poorly armed and munitioned. It is asserted by exporters in this city, doing business with San Domingo, that the insurrection will be suppressed before it makes much headway. General Carlos Morales, who heads the movement, has been governor of Puerto Plata under the present government, having fought against President Vasquez to place General Woss y Gil in power; in fact, General Morales has rebelled against every government under which he has at various times served; he was formerly a priest, but renounced the church for politics, and it has long been his ambition to be president. General Juan Isidro Jiminez, ex-president of San Domingo, who left this city a short time ago and is now at Mayaguez, Porto Rico, is also anxious to get back to power; President Woss y Gil appointed him fiscal agent to the United States and Europe, with a salary of $12,000 a year, to keep him quiet, it is said; he resigned this office, however, that he might take part in the new revolutionary movement; and it is not considered likely that he will be selected as chief executive, even in the event of rebel success, which is regarded as improbable.

records.headline: The Tribune prints a Washington dispatch of October 31: Minister Powell
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints a Washington dispatch of October 31: Minister Powell has again sent a dispatch to the State Department from San Domingo that the disturbance in the republic growing out of the revolution which centres at Puerto Plata is increasing; he suggests the advisability of having a United States warship there. The cruiser Baltimore, which sailed yesterday from Hampton Roads for San Domingo, cannot arrive there until the middle of next week, so the Navy Department is arranging to hurry the Dixie, now at Guantanamo, across to San Domingo by way of Kingston, Jamaica. The dispatch appears under the heads 'Powell Asks Warship' and 'Dominican Rebellion Spreads — Hurry Orders to the Dixie'.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica un despacho de Washington del 31 de octubre: el ministro Powell ha enviado de nuevo un despacho al Departamento de Estado desde Santo Domingo diciendo que la agitación en la república, surgida de la revolución que se centra en Puerto Plata, está aumentando; sugiere la conveniencia de tener un buque de guerra estadounidense allí. El crucero Baltimore, que zarpó ayer de Hampton Roads hacia Santo Domingo, no puede llegar allí hasta mediados de la próxima semana, por lo que el Departamento de la Marina está arreglando apresurar el Dixie, ahora en Guantánamo, a través hasta Santo Domingo vía Kingston, Jamaica. El despacho aparece bajo los titulares «Powell Asks Warship» y «Dominican Rebellion Spreads — Hurry Orders to the Dixie».

records.headline: The Times prints an item: advices from Puerto Plata, Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Times prints an item: advices from Puerto Plata, Santo Domingo, indicate that the rebel forces are concentrating for an attack on the capital of that republic. President Woss y Gil has called his two gunboats to Santo Domingo, having been unable to maintain a blockade at Puerto Plata; the vessels are supposed to be needed to defend the capital. Insurgents are in control of telegraph lines operated in connection with the cable service. More than 2,000 armed men are at Cotuy ready for a dash into Santo Domingo; this force is expecting re-enforcements from the south, and the surrender of the capital is reported to be inevitable. The item appears under the head 'Dominican Rebels to Attack the Capital'.
records.summary_es: El Times publica una nota: los informes desde Puerto Plata, Santo Domingo, indican que las fuerzas rebeldes se están concentrando para un ataque contra la capital de esa república. Más de 2,000 hombres armados están en Cotuy listos para una incursión hacia Santo Domingo; esta fuerza espera refuerzos del sur, y se informa que la rendición de la capital es inevitable. La nota aparece bajo el titular «Dominican Rebels to Attack the Capital».

records.headline: The Constitution prints the closing part of a Washington item
records.summary_en: The Constitution prints the closing part of a Washington item on the blockade and a Cape Haytien dispatch of October 29 headed 'Rebels to Move on Capital': the Washington item says that if merchant vessels are simply served with a warning and are not seized by a blockading force, and if there is actually such force as to institute an effective blockade, there will be no ground for interference on our part; but if a vessel is seized without warning, or there is no sufficient government force to make more than a paper blockade, then the United States government will not recognize it. The dispatch says General Navarro, the revolutionary governor of Monte Cristi, Santo Domingo, at the head of a strong force of troops, has joined General Morales, commander-in-chief of the forces of the Dominican revolution, with the reported intention of moving the combined forces on the capital, San Domingo; the blockade of the port of Puerto Plata, on the north coast of Santo Domingo, which is held by the revolutionists, has caused provisions there to become very dear; a force of Dominican revolutionists has occupied Cotuy; and among the passengers on board the Cuban mail steamer Maria Herrera, which was prevented from entering Puerto Plata on Tuesday by the Dominican government cruiser Independencia, was Señor Caceres, former governor of Santiago de los Caballeros, Santo Domingo, under the presidency of General Vasquez, who was exiled to Cuba by the present government of Santo Domingo; Señor Caceres has now gone to join General Jiminez.

records.headline: Quiet prevails, but serious troubles may arise here at any time
records.summary_en: The *Willmar Tribune* reported that the steamer *Cherokee* arrived in Santo Domingo after being turned away from northern ports by a government cruiser, bringing word that northern regions had joined the revolution. The paper published an insurgent manifesto from Puerto Plata condemning President Wos y Gil for tyranny, crowded prisons, and extreme financial decay. The document highlighted unpaid public debts, heavy petroleum taxes, an odious $120,000 loan, and irregular four-year port concessions granted to the Hamburg-American Line.
records.summary_es: El *Willmar Tribune* informó que el vapor *Cherokee* arribó a Santo Domingo tras haber sido rechazado en puertos septentrionales por un crucero del gobierno, trayendo noticias de que las regiones del norte se habían sumado a la revolución. El diario publicó un manifiesto insurgente de Puerto Plata que condenaba al presidente Wos y Gil por tiranía, prisiones abarrotadas y una ruina financiera extrema. El documento destacaba las deudas públicas impagas, los elevados tributos al petróleo, un oneroso empréstito de 120.000 dólares y concesiones portuarias irregulares por cuatro años concedidas a la Hamburg-American Line.
records.passage: [illegible]mingo, Thursday, Oct. 29.—The political situation in this city is unchanged. Quiet prevails, but serious troubles may arise here at any time and the presence of a foreign warship is desirable. The Clyde steamer Cherokee, from New York, arrived here Friday. She had been prevented by the Dominican government cruiser Independencia from calling at Puerto Plata, Samana and Macoris. She reports that the whole of the northern part of the island has joined in the revolutionary movement. Manifesto of Revolutionists. St. Thomas, D. W. records.headline: The Tribune prints a Cape Haytien dispatch dated November 5:
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints a Cape Haytien dispatch dated November 5: a Dominican cruiser, charged with the duty of blockading Puerto Plata, in the belief that a French vessel was on her way to Cape Haytien having on board several revolutionary chiefs, among them Jimenez, has started for the latter port to intercept the French ship. The provisional government has decided that the new capital shall be at Santiago de los Caballeros. The dispatch appears under the heads 'To Intercept Jimenez' and 'Dominican Cruiser Sails for Cape Haytien — The Rebels' Capital'.

El gobierno provisional ha decidido que la nueva capital estará en Santiago de los Caballeros. El despacho aparece bajo los titulares «To Intercept Jimenez» y «Dominican Cruiser Sails for Cape Haytien — The Rebels' Capital».

records.headline: The Savannah Morning News prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch
records.summary_en: The Savannah Morning News prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch on the Cherokee, a Washington item, and two further dispatches: Minister Powell wrote a sharp note to the government demanding a permit for the Cherokee to depart; the government refused to allow a pilot to board the vessel, and Minister Powell then instructed Captain Archibald to take his ship out and proceed for Azua, keeping his cargo aboard and landing it at the ports of destination; the energetic action of Minister Powell has caused a great sensation, especially as his proceeding lacks the support of an American warship. The Washington item, of November 6, says a cablegram has been received at the State Department from Minister Powell, dated at San Domingo City to-day, stating that the insurgents are marching on that city and asking that a warship be sent at once; the cruiser Baltimore, which sailed from Hampton Roads several days ago, is now due at San Domingo, and the State Department believes that her presence there will be sufficient. A St. Thomas dispatch says the German warships there are coaling, and it is reported they have been hurriedly ordered to San Domingo owing to the seriousness of the situation there. A Cape Haytien dispatch of November 6 says the Clyde line steamer Cherokee, which was prevented by the authorities from entering the ports of Puerto Plata and Samana, forced the blockade at the former port and entered there yesterday.
records.summary_es: El Savannah Morning News publica la parte final de un despacho de San Domingo sobre el Cherokee, una nota de Washington y dos despachos más: el ministro Powell escribió una nota enérgica al gobierno exigiendo un permiso para que el Cherokee partiera; el gobierno se negó a permitir que un piloto subiera a bordo del buque, y el ministro Powell instruyó entonces al capitán Archibald a sacar su barco y dirigirse a Azua, conservando su cargamento a bordo y desembarcándolo en los puertos de destino; la enérgica acción del ministro Powell ha causado gran sensación, especialmente porque su proceder carece del apoyo de un buque de guerra estadounidense. La nota de Washington, del 6 de noviembre, dice que se ha recibido un cablegrama en el Departamento de Estado del ministro Powell, fechado hoy en la ciudad de Santo Domingo, en el que declara que los insurgentes marchan sobre esa ciudad y pide que se envíe un buque de guerra de inmediato; el crucero Baltimore, que zarpó de Hampton Roads hace varios días, debe llegar ya a San Domingo, y el Departamento de Estado cree que su presencia allí será suficiente. Un despacho de Santo Tomás dice que los buques de guerra alemanes allí fondeados están cargando carbón y se informa que se les ha ordenado apresuradamente dirigirse a San Domingo por la gravedad de la situación allí. Un despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 6 de noviembre dice que el vapor Cherokee, de la línea Clyde, al que las autoridades impidieron entrar en los puertos de Puerto Plata y Samaná, forzó el bloqueo en el primero de ellos y entró allí ayer.

records.headline: The Call prints a Washington special dispatch of November 6
records.summary_en: The Call prints a Washington special dispatch of November 6 and a Puerto Plata dispatch of the same date: Minister Powell has informed the State Department that the revolutionists' army is marching on the capital of the Dominican republic and that there is immediate necessity for the presence there of an American warship; the cruiser Newport has already been ordered from Savannah, Ga., to Puerto Plata, but her course will probably be diverted to Santo Domingo City; the cruiser Baltimore was due to-day at Puerto Plata, where orders await her directing her to go direct to Colon, Panama, to join the ships already assembled there as a result of the isthmian revolution. records.summary_en: The Messenger prints a Washington special dispatch and a Santo Domingo dispatch: a cablegram received at the State Department from Minister Powell at San Domingo reports that conditions in the republic are in a state of great disturbance; the State Department is making vigorous efforts to communicate with Mr. Powell by cable, but with unsatisfactory results, owing to the fact that the insurgents appear to be in possession of the land telegraph lines connecting the capital, San Domingo, with the cable station on the east coast; incidentally, this has interrupted communication with Venezuela; to guard against any further cable lapses the State Department is sending, through the Navy Department, written instructions to Minister Powell for his guidance during the revolution, and these went forward on the Baltimore, which sailed to-day. The Santo Domingo dispatch says the political situation in this city is unchanged; quiet prevails, but serious trouble may arise here at any time and the presence of a foreign warship is desirable; the Clyde Line steamer Cherokee, from New York, has arrived here, having been prevented by the Dominican government cruiser Independencia from calling at Puerto Plata, Samana and Macoris; she reports that the whole of the northern part of the island has joined in the revolutionary movement.
records.summary_es: El Messenger publica un despacho especial de Washington y un despacho de Santo Domingo: un cablegrama recibido en el Departamento de Estado del ministro Powell en San Domingo informa que las condiciones en la república están en un estado de gran agitación; el Departamento de Estado hace esfuerzos vigorosos para comunicarse con el señor Powell por cable, pero con resultados insatisfactorios, debido a que los insurgentes parecen estar en posesión de las líneas telegráficas terrestres que conectan la capital, Santo Domingo, con la estación de cable en la costa este; incidentalmente, esto ha interrumpido también la comunicación con Venezuela; para precaverse contra nuevas interrupciones del cable, el Departamento de Estado envía, por medio del Departamento de Marina, instrucciones escritas al ministro Powell para su orientación durante la revolución, y estas salieron en el Baltimore, que zarpó hoy. El despacho de Santo Domingo dice que la situación política en esta ciudad no ha cambiado; prevalece la tranquilidad, pero pueden surgir aquí problemas serios en cualquier momento y es deseable la presencia de un buque de guerra extranjero; el vapor Cherokee, de la línea Clyde, procedente de Nueva York, ha llegado aquí, habiéndole impedido el crucero gubernamental dominicano Independencia hacer escala en Puerto Plata, Samaná y Macorís; informa que toda la parte norte de la isla se ha unido al movimiento revolucionario.

records.headline: The Journal prints the closing part of the Cherokee dispatch
records.summary_en: The Journal prints the closing part of the Cherokee dispatch from San Domingo and a Cape Haitian dispatch of November 6 under the head 'Forced the Blockade': the president reiterated his demand that the Cherokee's cargo be landed at San Domingo, but Minister Powell refused to permit it and declared he would hold the government responsible should any violent action be adopted toward the Cherokee; when the Cherokee was ready to leave for Azua clearance papers were refused, and it was again demanded that she land her cargo at this port; Minister Powell wrote a sharp note to the government demanding a permit for the Cherokee to depart; the government refused to allow a pilot to board the vessel, and Minister Powell then instructed Captain Archibald to take his ship out and to proceed for Azua, keeping his cargo aboard and landing it at the ports of destination; the energetic action of Minister Powell has caused great excitement, especially as his proceeding lacked the support of an American warship; the Cherokee left the harbor without a pilot; the city is quiet, but preparations looking to its defense are in active progress. The Cape Haitian dispatch says the revolutionary leaders, Jiminez and Ramon Caceres, with thirty followers, are on board the French mail steamer St. Simon, which arrived to-day; the Haitian authorities prevented their debarkation and the vessel proceeded for Port-au-Prince.

records.headline: The Light prints a Santo Domingo dispatch of November 7: the Dominican government
records.summary_en: The Light prints a Santo Domingo dispatch of November 7: the Dominican government has issued a decree announcing that the northern ports of the republic are closed to maritime commerce; the political situation is unchanged; the arrival of foreign warships is anxiously expected. The Clyde line steamer Cherokee, which returned here from Macoris, where she went to see Minister Powell, after having been prevented from entering Puerto Plata on the north coast by a Dominican warship, has been ordered to Samana to await there the arrival of foreign warships; the situation is dangerous. The government intends to prevent the vessels from entering the northern ports, but Minister Powell has declared the blockade non-effective. The German consul has protested against the action of the Dominican government closing the ports.
records.summary_es: El Light publica un despacho de Santo Domingo del 7 de noviembre: el gobierno dominicano ha emitido un decreto que anuncia que los puertos del norte de la república están cerrados al comercio marítimo; la situación política no ha cambiado; la llegada de buques de guerra extranjeros se espera con ansiedad. El vapor Cherokee, de la línea Clyde, que regresó aquí desde Macorís, a donde fue a ver al ministro Powell, después de que un buque de guerra dominicano le impidió entrar en Puerto Plata, en la costa norte, ha recibido órdenes de dirigirse a Samaná para esperar allí la llegada de buques de guerra extranjeros; la situación es peligrosa. El gobierno tiene la intención de impedir que los buques entren en los puertos del norte, pero el ministro Powell ha declarado el bloqueo no efectivo. El cónsul alemán ha protestado contra la acción del gobierno dominicano de cerrar los puertos.

records.headline: The Star prints a Navy Department item: it is reported at the department
records.summary_en: The Star prints a Navy Department item: it is reported at the department that the Baltimore arrived at Sanchez, a port on the northern coast of Santo Domingo, on the 3d instant; Sanchez and Puerto Plata are not more than 400 miles apart, and it is not understood at the department why it took the Baltimore four days to cover that distance. Although the Baltimore may eventually be sent to Colon to reinforce the Nashville, Dixie and Atlanta, it is said at the Navy Department that no orders to that effect have been issued; in view of the fact that the situation on the isthmus is now well under control, it is believed that the Baltimore is likely to remain at Santo Domingo, where there seems to be great need for the presence of an American warship. The original report that the Baltimore was to be immediately dispatched to Colon was coupled with the statement that she would be relieved in Dominican waters by the gunboat Newport, which at that time was at Jacksonville; if such was the intention of the department, the plan has certainly been abandoned, for word was received at the department this morning that the Newport, instead of going south, left Jacksonville yesterday for Savannah, Ga., to be repaired and to take part in a local celebration.
records.summary_es: El Star publica una nota del Departamento de Marina: se informa en el departamento que el Baltimore llegó a Sánchez, un puerto en la costa norte de Santo Domingo, el día 3 del presente mes; Sánchez y Puerto Plata no están a más de 400 millas de distancia, y no se comprende en el departamento por qué el Baltimore tardó cuatro días en cubrir esa distancia. Aunque el Baltimore puede ser enviado eventualmente a Colón para reforzar al Nashville, al Dixie y al Atlanta, se dice en el Departamento de Marina que no se han emitido órdenes en ese sentido; en vista de que la situación en el Istmo está ahora bien controlada, sin perspectivas inmediatas de nuevos estallidos, se cree que el Baltimore probablemente permanecerá en Santo Domingo, donde parece haber gran necesidad de la presencia de un buque de guerra estadounidense. El informe original de que el Baltimore sería despachado de inmediato a Colón venía acompañado de la declaración de que sería relevado en aguas dominicanas por la cañonera Newport, que en ese momento estaba en Jacksonville; si tal fue la intención del departamento, el plan ciertamente ha sido abandonado, pues esta mañana se recibió en el departamento la noticia de que el Newport, en lugar de dirigirse al sur, salió ayer de Jacksonville hacia Savannah, Georgia, para ser reparado y participar en una celebración local.

records.headline: The News prints a Santo Domingo dispatch and a St. Thomas dispatch
records.summary_en: The News prints a Santo Domingo dispatch and a St. Thomas dispatch: the Dominican government has issued a decree announcing that the northern ports of the republic are closed to maritime commerce; the arrival of foreign warships is anxiously expected. The Clyde line steamer Cherokee, which returned here from Macoris, where she went to carry a report to Minister Powell, after having been prevented from entering Puerto Plata on the north coast by a Dominican warship, has been ordered to Samana to await there the arrival of foreign warships; the situation is dangerous. The government intends to prevent vessels from entering the northern ports, but Minister Powell has declared the blockade non-effective. The German consul has protested against the action of the Dominican government in closing the ports. The St. Thomas dispatch, to the Associated Press last night, said the German warships there were coaling and it is reported that they had been hurriedly ordered to Santo Domingo, owing to the seriousness of the situation in that republic.
records.summary_es: El News publica un despacho de Santo Domingo y un despacho de Santo Tomás: el gobierno dominicano ha emitido un decreto que anuncia que los puertos del norte de la república están cerrados al comercio marítimo; la llegada de buques de guerra extranjeros se espera con ansiedad. El vapor Cherokee, de la línea Clyde, que regresó aquí desde Macorís, a donde fue a llevar un informe al ministro Powell, después de que un buque de guerra dominicano le impidió entrar en Puerto Plata, en la costa norte, ha recibido órdenes de dirigirse a Samaná para esperar allí la llegada de buques de guerra extranjeros; la situación es peligrosa. El gobierno tiene la intención de impedir que los buques entren en los puertos del norte, pero el ministro Powell ha declarado el bloqueo no efectivo. El cónsul alemán ha protestado contra la acción del gobierno dominicano al cerrar los puertos. El despacho de Santo Tomás, enviado anoche a la Associated Press, decía que los buques de guerra alemanes allí fondeados estaban cargando carbón y se informa que se les había ordenado apresuradamente dirigirse a Santo Domingo, por la gravedad de la situación en esa república.

records.headline: The Journal prints a Washington item, a Santo Domingo dispatch of November 7
records.summary_en: The Journal prints a Washington item, a Santo Domingo dispatch of November 7 and a Navy Department order: the commander of the cruiser Baltimore cabled the Navy Department to-day from Puerto Plata, on the north coast of San Domingo, announcing his arrival and stating that the Cherokee was discharging her cargo; this indicates that the blockade has been raised. The dispatch says the Dominican government issued a decree last Wednesday announcing that the northern ports of the republic are closed to maritime commerce; the arrival of foreign warships is anxiously expected; the situation is dangerous; the government intended to prevent vessels from entering the northern ports, but Minister Powell has declared the blockade noneffective; the German consul has protested against the action of the Dominican government in closing the ports. The Navy Department has issued orders to the gunboat Newport, at Savannah, to coal and proceed at full speed to San Domingo; the action follows advices of the serious condition of affairs there.
records.summary_es: El Journal publica una nota de Washington, un despacho de Santo Domingo del 7 de noviembre y una orden del Departamento de Marina: el comandante del crucero Baltimore cablegrafió hoy al Departamento de Marina desde Puerto Plata, en la costa norte de San Domingo, anunciando su llegada y declarando que el Cherokee estaba descargando su cargamento; esto indica que el bloqueo ha sido levantado. El despacho dice que el gobierno dominicano emitió el miércoles pasado un decreto que anuncia que los puertos del norte de la república están cerrados al comercio marítimo; la llegada de buques de guerra extranjeros se espera con ansiedad; la situación es peligrosa; el gobierno tenía la intención de impedir que los buques entraran en los puertos del norte, pero el ministro Powell ha declarado el bloqueo no efectivo; el cónsul alemán ha protestado contra la acción del gobierno dominicano al cerrar los puertos. El Departamento de Marina ha emitido órdenes para la cañonera Newport, en Savannah, de cargar carbón y dirigirse a toda velocidad a San Domingo; la acción sigue a informes sobre la seria condición de los asuntos allí.

records.headline: Commander Metz of the United States gunboat Newport received peremptory orders at Savannah to coal at once and sail
records.summary_en: Commander Metz of the United States gunboat Newport received peremptory orders at Savannah to coal at once and sail for Puerto Plata, in the Dominican Republic. The coaling was rushed, the vessel steamed down the river and proceeded immediately to sea, and Commander Metz refused to discuss his orders beyond saying that they were urgent.
records.summary_es: El comandante Metz, de la cañonera estadounidense Newport, recibió órdenes perentorias en Savannah de cargar carbón de inmediato y zarpar hacia Puerto Plata, en la República Dominicana. El carboneo se hizo a toda prisa, la embarcación descendió por el río y se hizo a la mar inmediatamente, y el comandante Metz se negó a comentar sus órdenes más allá de decir que eran urgentes.

records.headline: The Bulletin prints a San Domingo dispatch and a Savannah dispatch
records.summary_en: The Bulletin prints a San Domingo dispatch and a Savannah dispatch: a Dominican gunboat, which returned here last night from Macoris, reports having bombarded that town; the damage done is not known; Macoris is still in the hands of the revolutionists. The forces of the revolutionists are approaching San Domingo; there was firing, which only lasted a short time, this morning outside the city; there are no foreign warships in port. The Savannah dispatch says Commander Metz, of the United States gunboat Newport, received preparatory orders to coal at once and sail for Puerto Plata, San Domingo; the coaling was rushed and at 9 o'clock Monday evening the vessel steamed down the river, proceeding immediately to sea; Commander Metz refused to discuss his orders, but said they were urgent.
records.summary_es: El Bulletin publica un despacho de San Domingo y un despacho de Savannah: una cañonera dominicana, que regresó aquí anoche desde Macorís, informa haber bombardeado esa población; el daño causado no se conoce; Macorís está todavía en manos de los revolucionarios. Las fuerzas de los revolucionarios se acercan a San Domingo; hubo disparos, que duraron solo un corto tiempo, esta mañana fuera de la ciudad; no hay buques de guerra extranjeros en el puerto. El despacho de Savannah dice que el comandante Metz, de la cañonera estadounidense Newport, recibió órdenes preparatorias de cargar carbón de inmediato y zarpar hacia Puerto Plata, San Domingo; el embarque de carbón se apresuró y a las 9 de la noche del lunes el buque bajó por el río, dirigiéndose de inmediato al mar; el comandante Metz se negó a discutir sus órdenes, pero dijo que eran urgentes.

records.summary_en: The Washington Times prints the closing part of a Washington dispatch and two items on the German warships and Macoris: Germany has ordered two warships from St. Thomas to Santo Domingo; the German steamer Athen was refused admission to the port of San Domingo, and a report of this affair to the German government caused an order to be issued at once for the movement of the German cruisers Panther and Gazelle into Dominican waters. Under the head 'Macoris Partly Destroyed,' the paper says Minister Powell, at Santo Domingo, has advised the State Department that a gunboat in charge of revolutionists stormed Macoris, an important port on the north coast of the island, and destroyed part of the town; the dispatch was under date of November 6; it is also stated in the dispatch that American interests in Macoris are large; Macoris is an important fruit-shipping center, and is only twenty miles from Puerto Plata, which has been the stronghold of the revolutionists since the outbreak of the insurrection. Under the head 'Warships Dispatched,' the paper says that in a previous dispatch Minister Powell asked that a warship be sent to protect American interests; the cruiser Baltimore has arrived at Santo Domingo since Mr. Powell sent the request for aid, and the Newport, which is now at Savannah, is coaling preparatory to sailing to the revolutionary republic.

Bajo el titular «Macoris Partly Destroyed», el periódico dice que el ministro Powell, en Santo Domingo, ha informado al Departamento de Estado que una cañonera en poder de revolucionarios tomó por asalto Macorís, un puerto importante en la costa norte de la isla, y destruyó parte de la población; el despacho tenía fecha del 6 de noviembre; también se declara en el despacho que los intereses estadounidenses en Macorís son grandes; Macorís es un importante centro de embarque de frutas y está a solo veinte millas de Puerto Plata, que ha sido el baluarte de los revolucionarios desde el estallido de la insurrección. Bajo el titular «Warships Dispatched», el periódico dice que en un despacho anterior el ministro Powell pidió que se enviara un buque de guerra para proteger los intereses estadounidenses; el crucero Baltimore ha llegado a Santo Domingo desde que el señor Powell envió la solicitud de ayuda, y el Newport, que está ahora en Savannah, está cargando carbón preparándose para zarpar hacia la república revolucionaria.

records.headline: The Tribune prints a dispatch on the German movement, a Savannah dispatch
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints a dispatch on the German movement, a Savannah dispatch under the head 'Newport Rushed to Puerto Plata,' and a Port-au-Prince dispatch: the cruisers Panther and Gazelle have been dispatched to San Domingo; the Athen returned to San Domingo yesterday morning, and it is reported that she will ignore the blockade, under the protection of the German warships. The Savannah dispatch, of November 9, says Commander Metz, of the gunboat Newport, received orders to-day to coal at once and sail for Puerto Plata; the coaling was rushed, and at 7:30 o'clock the Newport fired a gun to summon such members of her crew as had received shore leave; the vessel then steamed down the river, proceeding immediately to sea; Commander Metz refused to discuss his orders, but said that they were urgent. The Port-au-Prince dispatch, of November 9, says General Jimenez and thirty insurgents have arrived at Cape Haytien; the government of Hayti protests against their disembarking, as it is believed that the revolution cannot last longer than a few days; it is generally thought that the revolution will end in favor of Jimenez, who will probably try to disembark at some point near San Domingo.

records.headline: The Leader prints a Washington item of November 11: the State Department
records.summary_en: The Leader prints a Washington item of November 11: the State Department has received another belated dispatch from Minister Powell, at San Domingo City, dated the 6th inst., in which the minister says: 'Macoris has just been bombarded by a Dominican naval vessel and partially destroyed. The ship then returned to San Domingo City. The American interests in Macoris are very considerable.' Macoris is a fruit shipping port doing a large business with the United States, and the bombardment is supposed to have been without the required twenty-four hours' notice; if it appears that American interests have suffered by arbitrary action at the hands of the Dominican government, the State Department will demand full redress, and the cruiser Baltimore, now at Puerto Plata, undoubtedly will prevent further happenings of this kind; two German warships, which started from St. Thomas Monday morning, also are available by this time to aid in the maintenance of order. The item appears under the head 'Partially Destroyed'.

records.headline: The Forest Republican prints the Cherokee narrative from San Domingo:
records.summary_en: The Forest Republican prints the Cherokee narrative from San Domingo: a Dominican warship stopped the Clyde line steamer Cherokee as she was nearing Puerto Plata and informed the captain that he could not enter that port; the Cherokee then proceeded for Samana and was also prevented from entering that port, the minister of war ordering the captain of the Cherokee to proceed direct to the capital. On the arrival of the vessel at San Domingo the government demanded that the cargo intended for Puerto Plata and Samana be landed at that port; the agent of the company and the captain of the Cherokee refused to comply with this demand and appealed to Minister Powell for protection. When the Cherokee was ready to leave for Azua clearance papers were refused, and it was again demanded that she land her cargo at that port; Minister Powell wrote a sharp note to the government demanding a permit for the Cherokee to depart; the government refused to allow a pilot to board the vessel, and Minister Powell then instructed Captain Archibald to take his ship out and proceed for Azua, keeping his cargo aboard and landing it at the ports of destination. The energetic action of Minister Powell has caused a great sensation, especially as his proceeding lacked the support of an American warship; the Cherokee left the harbor without a pilot.
records.summary_es: El Forest Republican publica el relato del Cherokee desde San Domingo: un buque de guerra dominicano detuvo al vapor Cherokee, de la línea Clyde, cuando se acercaba a Puerto Plata e informó al capitán que no podía entrar en ese puerto; el Cherokee se dirigió entonces a Samaná y también se le impidió entrar en ese puerto, ordenando el ministro de Guerra al capitán del Cherokee dirigirse directamente a la capital. records.headline: The Journal prints two belated cables from Minister Powell and a Washington item:
records.summary_en: The Journal prints two belated cables from Minister Powell and a Washington item: the State Department received a cablegram from Minister Powell, dated San Domingo, November 6, 11 p. m.: 'Insurgents have reached the city. Attacked to-night on three sides. City being shelled. No damage.' Another belated dispatch under the same date said: 'Macoris has just been bombarded by a San Domingan naval vessel and partially destroyed. The ship then returned to San Domingo city. The American interests in Macoris are very considerable.' Macoris is a fruit-shipping port, doing a large business with the United States, and the bombardment is supposed to have been without the required twenty-four hours' notice; if it appears that American interests have suffered by arbitrary action at the hands of the Dominican government, the State Department will demand full redress, and the cruiser Baltimore, now at Puerto Plata, undoubtedly will prevent further happenings of this kind; two German warships which started from St. Thomas yesterday morning are also available by this time to aid in the maintenance of order. Late to-night Assistant Secretary Loomis, of the State Department, called at the executive offices of the White House and spent some time in the telegraph room; he refused to admit that he was cabling fresh instructions to Minister Powell, although he said that late in the afternoon he had notified the minister that the cruiser Baltimore was now on her way to that city and would probably reach there some time during the night; the dispatch reporting the capitulation of the city of San Domingo to the revolutionists was shown to Mr. Loomis.

Atacada esta noche por tres lados. La ciudad está siendo bombardeada. Ningún daño». El buque regresó entonces a la ciudad de San Domingo. Los intereses estadounidenses en Macorís son muy considerables». Macorís es un puerto de embarque de frutas, que hace un gran negocio con los Estados Unidos, y se supone que el bombardeo fue sin el aviso requerido de veinticuatro horas; si resulta que los intereses estadounidenses han sufrido por la acción arbitraria del gobierno dominicano, el Departamento de Estado exigirá plena reparación, y el crucero Baltimore, ahora en Puerto Plata, sin duda impedirá nuevos hechos de esta clase; dos buques de guerra alemanes que salieron de Santo Tomás ayer por la mañana también están disponibles a estas horas para ayudar en el mantenimiento del orden. Tarde esta noche el subsecretario Loomis, del Departamento de Estado, se presentó en las oficinas ejecutivas de la Casa Blanca y pasó algún tiempo en la sala de telégrafos; se negó a admitir que estaba cablegrafiando nuevas instrucciones al ministro Powell, aunque dijo que a última hora de la tarde había notificado al ministro que el crucero Baltimore ya venía en camino hacia esa ciudad y probablemente llegaría allí en algún momento durante la noche; el despacho que informaba de la capitulación de la ciudad de Santo Domingo ante los revolucionarios fue mostrado al señor Loomis.

records.headline: The Advertiser prints a sketch of Jiminez's career: Jiminez landed
records.summary_en: The Advertiser prints a sketch of Jiminez's career: Jiminez landed in Santo Domingo and was received joyfully by the people; after the death of Heureaux a provisional government was formed by General Horatio Vasquez; an election was ordered and Jiminez became president. Vasquez turned against Jiminez and led a successful revolution; Jiminez fled to New York. Early this year the Vasquez government was routed by the former friends of Jiminez, with General Woss y Gil at their head; Jiminez went to Santo Domingo, but Woss y Gil was made president. Now Jiminez is reported to have won the reins of power from those who headed a revolution while posing as his friends and ostensibly in his interests. The sketch adds that in 1898 he got possession of the American steamship Fanita, armed and equipped it for an expedition against the Spaniards in Cuba, and sailed from Mobile.
records.summary_es: El Advertiser publica una semblanza de la carrera del general Jiménez: Jiménez desembarcó en Santo Domingo y fue recibido jubilosamente por el pueblo; después de la muerte de Heureaux se formó un gobierno provisional por el general Horatio Vásquez; se ordenó una elección y Jiménez se convirtió en presidente. Vásquez se volvió contra Jiménez y encabezó una revolución exitosa; Jiménez huyó a Nueva York. Temprano este año el gobierno de Vásquez fue derrotado por los antiguos amigos de Jiménez, con el general Woss y Gil a la cabeza; Jiménez fue a Santo Domingo, pero Woss y Gil fue hecho presidente. Ahora se informa que Jiménez ha ganado las riendas del poder de manos de quienes encabezaron una revolución mientras fingían ser sus amigos y ostensiblemente actuaban en su interés. La semblanza añade que en 1898 se apoderó del vapor estadounidense Fanita, lo armó y lo equipó para una expedición contra los españoles en Cuba, y zarpó de Mobile.

records.headline: The Call prints a San Domingo dispatch of November 11: the insurgents
records.summary_en: The Call prints a San Domingo dispatch of November 11: the insurgents, having officially notified the foreign consuls yesterday that they contemplated a heavy bombardment on the capital, made an all night attack with shells and small arms; the attack was repulsed; the city government refused the rebels' demand to surrender. The special dispatch says General Paul Cabrera, at the head of 590 revolutionists, with six pieces of artillery and a treasure chest containing $4,000, arrived yesterday before the city; the guard for the German consulate, which was landed from the cruisers of Germany now in port, keeps in instant communication with the latter by means of a signal station which has been erected over the consulate; last night's artillery duel resulted in no damage, as the insurgents' shells failed to explode; both sides express confidence; the general idea is that the capital cannot be taken by assault, although the government forces have been bottled up since the last sortie. The German cruiser Gazelle, accompanied by the merchantman Athen, has returned from St. Thomas to force the blockade at Sanchez, Macoris, Puerto Plata and Samana. The foreign consuls held a two-hour conference yesterday and decided to ignore the insurgents.

El despacho especial dice que el general Paul Cabrera, al frente de 590 revolucionarios, con seis piezas de artillería y un cofre del tesoro que contiene $4,000, llegó ayer frente a la ciudad; la guardia del consulado alemán, que fue desembarcada de los cruceros de Alemania ahora en puerto, se mantiene en comunicación instantánea con estos últimos por medio de una estación de señales que ha sido erigida sobre el consulado; el duelo de artillería de anoche no resultó en daño alguno, pues las granadas de los insurgentes no explotaron; ambas partes expresan confianza; la idea general es que la capital no puede ser tomada por asalto, aunque las fuerzas del gobierno han estado embotelladas desde la última salida. El crucero alemán Gazelle, acompañado del mercante Athen, ha regresado de Santo Tomás para forzar el bloqueo en Sánchez, Macorís, Puerto Plata y Samaná. Los cónsules extranjeros celebraron ayer una conferencia de dos horas y decidieron ignorar a los insurgentes.

records.headline: Hundred revolutionists, with six pieces of ar tillery and a treasure
records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that 800 insurgents with artillery laid siege to the capital of Santo Domingo, prompting German warships *Panther* and *Gazelle* to land armed guards and escort the merchant steamer *Athen*. Dominican exiles in New York received reports that insurgent forces had proclaimed General Juan Isidro Jimenes president of the republic. Jimenes had previously resigned as Dominican fiscal agent to organize the armed movement to reclaim the presidency from which he had been ousted.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que 800 insurgentes con artillería sitiaron la capital de Santo Domingo, lo que motivó a los buques de guerra alemanes *Panther* y *Gazelle* a desembarcar destacamentos armados y escoltar al vapor mercante *Athen*. Exiliados dominicanos en Nueva York recibieron informes de que las fuerzas insurgentes habían proclamado presidente de la república al general Juan Isidro Jimenes. Jimenes había renunciado previamente a su cargo de agente fiscal dominicano con el propósito de organizar el movimiento armado para recuperar la presidencia de la cual había sido desalojado.

records.headline: The Times-Recorder prints a San Domingo dispatch on the bombardment of the capital:
records.summary_en: The Times-Recorder prints a San Domingo dispatch on the bombardment of the capital: the German cruiser Gazelle arrived Monday and landed marines; the German cruiser Panther arrived the preceding day; no other foreign war vessels are here. Previous to the beginning of the bombardment of San Domingo the revolutionists notified the diplomatic corps and the consular officers that they had previously served notice on the Dominican government that the forces of the revolution intended to adopt all means, including a bombardment, in their efforts to capture the city; the representatives of the powers met to-day and decided that they could only hold communication with the legally established government of the country. Paul Cabrera, at the head of 800 revolutionists, with six pieces of artillery and a treasure chest containing $4,000, arrived yesterday before the city. The situation here is becoming very critical, and the presence of more warships at San Domingo is urgently required. The guard for the German consulate, which was landed from the cruisers of Germany now in port, is in constant communication with the latter by means of a signal station which has been erected over the consulate. The German steamer Athen, which was prevented some days ago from landing her cargo at San Pedro de Macoris, under the protection of the German cruiser succeeded in landing her freight at that port, and has proceeded to the northern ports of Santo Domingo, for which she has cargo and passengers; the Athen has a German escort with her in order to facilitate the discharging of her freight.
records.summary_es: El Times-Recorder publica un despacho de San Domingo sobre el bombardeo de la capital: el crucero alemán Gazelle llegó el lunes y desembarcó infantes de marina; el crucero alemán Panther llegó el día anterior; no hay otros buques de guerra extranjeros aquí. Antes del comienzo del bombardeo de San Domingo, los revolucionarios notificaron al cuerpo diplomático y a los oficiales consulares que previamente habían notificado al gobierno dominicano que las fuerzas de la revolución tenían la intención de adoptar todos los medios, incluido un bombardeo, en sus esfuerzos por capturar la ciudad; los representantes de las potencias se reunieron hoy y decidieron que solo podían mantener comunicación con el gobierno legalmente establecido del país. Paul Cabrera, al frente de 800 revolucionarios, con seis piezas de artillería y un cofre del tesoro que contiene $4,000, llegó ayer frente a la ciudad. La situación aquí se está volviendo muy crítica, y la presencia de más buques de guerra en San Domingo se requiere con urgencia. La guardia del consulado alemán, que fue desembarcada de los cruceros de Alemania ahora en puerto, está en comunicación constante con estos últimos por medio de una estación de señales que ha sido erigida sobre el consulado. El vapor alemán Athen, al que se le impidió hace algunos días desembarcar su cargamento en San Pedro de Macorís, bajo la protección del crucero alemán logró desembarcar su flete en ese puerto, y ha proseguido hacia los puertos del norte de Santo Domingo, para los que tiene cargamento y pasajeros; el Athen tiene una escolta alemana con él para facilitar la descarga de su flete.

records.headline: The Savannah Morning News prints a San Domingo dispatch, a Washington item
records.summary_en: The Savannah Morning News prints a San Domingo dispatch, a Washington item under the head 'Baltimore to Stop It,' and an item under the head 'Won't Recognize Them': the revolutionists notified the diplomatic corps and the consular officers that they had previously served notice on the Dominican government that the forces of the revolution intended to adopt all means, including a bombardment, in their efforts to capture the city; the representatives of the powers met to-day and decided that they could only hold communication with the legally established government of the country; Gen. Paul Cabrera, at the head of 8,000 revolutionists, with six pieces of artillery and a treasure chest containing $4,000, arrived yesterday before the city. The Washington item, of November 11, says Capt. Briggs, commanding the cruiser Baltimore, telegraphed the Navy Department to-day from Puerto Plata that the Baltimore left there this morning for Macoris and San Domingo City; it is said at the State Department that the instructions to the American naval officers are of a character to prevent any further bombardment by either government or insurgent forces of any San Dominican port where American interests are involved without the notice required by international law. The third item, from San Domingo, November 11, says the revolutionists have addressed a letter to Minister Powell, informing him that engagements entered into with the United States by the government presided over by President Woss y Gil will not be recognized by them; the letter requests that Minister Powell recognize the revolutionists, but the minister has refused to hold communication with them; the political situation here is unchanged.

records.headline: The Star prints an account of the Cherokee's voyage: after some parley
records.summary_en: The Star prints an account of the Cherokee's voyage: after some parley the Cherokee was allowed to go into Puerto Plata, land her cargo and mails and reload cargo; off Macoris, on November 3, the Cherokee was stopped by the same vessel and again permitted to proceed; at Samana, November 5, the war vessel ordered the Cherokee away; the Cherokee waited until after dark, when the man-of-war sailed out of port without lights, and then went in and landed her cargo and mails; she succeeded in making schedule time at all her usual ports except Monte Cristi. Macoris was evacuated by the government forces November 3, the day of sailing, and all the ports except San Domingo City were in the hands of the insurgents when she finally sailed; at Puerto Plata, November 6, a French and a Cuban steamer were ordered away by the Dominican warship. The Dominican government officials refused the Cherokee clearance papers to leave San Domingo, and also refused to allow a pilot to take her out of the harbor; Minister Powell protested to the Dominican government and instructed the captain of the Cherokee to take his ship out without clearance papers or pilot. The Cherokee brought nineteen cabin passengers from San Domingo, but no refugees.
records.summary_es: El Star publica un relato del viaje del Cherokee: tras alguna negociación se permitió al Cherokee entrar en Puerto Plata, desembarcar su cargamento y correo y recargar cargamento; frente a Macorís, el 3 de noviembre, el Cherokee fue detenido por el mismo buque y de nuevo se le permitió proseguir; en Samaná, el 5 de noviembre, el buque de guerra ordenó al Cherokee alejarse; el Cherokee esperó hasta que oscureció, cuando el buque de guerra salió del puerto sin luces, y entonces entró y desembarcó su cargamento y correo; logró mantener el horario en todos sus puertos habituales excepto Monte Cristi. Macorís fue evacuado por las fuerzas del gobierno el 3 de noviembre, el día de la partida, y todos los puertos excepto la ciudad de Santo Domingo estaban en manos de los insurgentes cuando finalmente zarpó; en Puerto Plata, el 6 de noviembre, un vapor francés y uno cubano fueron alejados por orden del buque de guerra dominicano. Los oficiales del gobierno dominicano negaron al Cherokee los papeles de despacho para salir de San Domingo y también se negaron a permitir que un piloto lo sacara del puerto; el ministro Powell protestó ante el gobierno dominicano e instruyó al capitán del Cherokee a sacar su barco sin papeles de despacho ni piloto. El Cherokee trajo diecinueve pasajeros de cabina desde San Domingo, pero ningún refugiado.

records.headline: The Tribune prints an account of the Cherokee's outward voyage
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints an account of the Cherokee's outward voyage: on her outward voyage the Cherokee was stopped off Puerto Plata by a Dominican man-of-war, which fired several shots across her bow; after some trouble the Cherokee was allowed to proceed to Puerto Plata; there the customs officials ordered Captain Archibald to discharge all his cargo and mail, forbidding him to enter any other Dominican ports; this Captain Archibald refused to do. The next day he sailed for Macoris, expecting to find the Baltimore there; the cruiser was not at this port, but Minister Powell went aboard and conferred for half an hour with the captain of the Cherokee. From that port the Cherokee steamed for Samana; at the entrance to the harbor the Cherokee was again stopped by the Dominican gunboat El Presidente and Captain Archibald told that he could not proceed because of the blockade; the Cherokee waited until after dark, and when the gunboat sailed away she went into the harbor and discharged her cargo and mails. At Monte Christi, her next port, she was met again by the omnipresent El Presidente, which threatened to blow her out of the water if she evaded the blockade again; the Cherokee had to lay off Monte Christi all night. One of the passengers on the Cherokee, in discussing the revolution which was responsible for the vessel's troubles and the political situation in general, said that not only was there an absolute absence of animosity to Americans in the country, but that on the contrary there existed a strong sentiment in favor of the establishment of a protectorate over the republic.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica un relato del viaje de ida del Cherokee: en su viaje de ida el Cherokee fue detenido frente a Puerto Plata por un buque de guerra dominicano, que disparó varios tiros sobre su proa; después de alguna dificultad se permitió al Cherokee proseguir a Puerto Plata; allí los oficiales de aduana ordenaron al capitán Archibald descargar todo su cargamento y correo, prohibiéndole entrar en cualquier otro puerto dominicano; esto el capitán Archibald se negó a hacer. Al día siguiente zarpó hacia Macorís, esperando encontrar allí al Baltimore; el crucero no estaba en este puerto, pero el ministro Powell subió a bordo y conferenció durante media hora con el capitán del Cherokee. Desde ese puerto el Cherokee se dirigió a Samaná; a la entrada del puerto el Cherokee fue detenido de nuevo por la cañonera dominicana El Presidente y se dijo al capitán Archibald que no podía proseguir a causa del bloqueo; el Cherokee esperó hasta que oscureció, y cuando la cañonera se alejó entró en el puerto y descargó su cargamento y correo. En Monte Cristi, su puerto siguiente, fue recibido de nuevo por el omnipresente El Presidente, que amenazó con volarlo fuera del agua si evadía el bloqueo otra vez; el Cherokee tuvo que permanecer frente a Monte Cristi toda la noche. Uno de los pasajeros del Cherokee, al discutir la revolución que fue responsable de los problemas del buque y la situación política en general, dijo que no solo había una ausencia absoluta de animosidad hacia los estadounidenses en el país, sino que, por el contrario, existía un fuerte sentimiento a favor del establecimiento de un protectorado sobre la república.

records.headline: The Inter Mountain prints a Port-au-Prince dispatch: General Jiminez
records.summary_en: The Inter Mountain prints a Port-au-Prince dispatch: General Jiminez, head of the Dominican revolution, has left Port Au Prince, Hayti, on board the St. Simon, with the intention, according to report, of forcing the blockade of Puerto Plata on the northern coast of Santo Domingo; the Haytien authorities formally opposed the landing in Hayti of General Jiminez, in spite of his strong insistence upon being permitted to do so; it is said that if the St. Simon is interfered with she will ask for the assistance of the German cruiser Gazelle or other foreign ships which may be in Dominican waters; the French cruiser Jurien de la Graviere, which was in these waters recently, is understood to have returned to Martinique. Telegraphic communication with the interior of Santo Domingo was re-established yesterday morning, but now it is again interrupted, and it is reported that severe fighting must have occurred before San Domingo.
records.summary_es: El Inter Mountain publica un despacho de Puerto Príncipe: el general Jiménez, jefe de la revolución dominicana, ha salido de Puerto Príncipe, Haití, a bordo del St. Simon, con la intención, según se informa, de forzar el bloqueo de Puerto Plata en la costa norte de Santo Domingo; las autoridades haitianas se opusieron formalmente al desembarco en Haití del general Jiménez, a pesar de su fuerte insistencia en que se le permitiera hacerlo; se dice que si el St. Simon es interferido pedirá la ayuda del crucero alemán Gazelle o de otros buques extranjeros que puedan estar en aguas dominicanas; el crucero francés Jurien de la Graviere, que estuvo recientemente en estas aguas, se entiende que ha regresado a Martinica. La comunicación telegráfica con el interior de Santo Domingo fue restablecida ayer por la mañana, pero ahora está de nuevo interrumpida, y se informa que debe haber ocurrido una lucha severa frente a San Domingo.

records.headline: The Age-Herald prints a Cherokee voyage account: after the Dominican warship
records.summary_en: The Age-Herald prints a Cherokee voyage account: after the Dominican warship fired several shots across her bow and stopped her, and after some parley, the Cherokee was allowed to go into Puerto Plata, land her cargo and mails and reload cargo; off Macoris, on November 3, the Cherokee was stopped by the same vessel and again permitted to proceed; at Samana, on November 5, the war vessel ordered the Cherokee away, and the Cherokee waited until after dark, when the man-of-war sailed out of port without lights, and then went in and landed her cargo and mails; she succeeded in making schedule time at all her usual ports except Monte Cristi. Macoris was evacuated by the government forces on November 3, the day of sailing, and all the ports except San Domingo City were in the hands of the insurgents when she finally sailed; at Puerto Plata, on November 6, a French and a Cuban steamer were ordered away by the Dominican warship. The Dominican officials refused the Cherokee clearance papers to leave San Domingo, and also refused to allow a pilot to take her out of the harbor; Minister Powell protested to the Dominican government and instructed the captain of the Cherokee to take his ship out without clearance papers or pilot. The Cherokee brought nineteen cabin passengers from San Domingo, but no refugees.
records.summary_es: El Age-Herald publica un relato del viaje del Cherokee: después de que el buque de guerra dominicano disparó varios tiros sobre su proa y lo detuvo, y después de alguna negociación, se permitió al Cherokee entrar en Puerto Plata, desembarcar su cargamento y correo y recargar cargamento; frente a Macorís, el 3 de noviembre, el Cherokee fue detenido por el mismo buque y de nuevo se le permitió proseguir; en Samaná, el 5 de noviembre, el buque de guerra ordenó al Cherokee alejarse, y el Cherokee esperó hasta que oscureció, cuando el buque de guerra salió del puerto sin luces, y entonces entró y desembarcó su cargamento y correo; logró mantener el horario en todos sus puertos habituales excepto Monte Cristi. Macorís fue evacuado por las fuerzas del gobierno el 3 de noviembre, el día de la partida, y todos los puertos excepto la ciudad de Santo Domingo estaban en manos de los insurgentes cuando finalmente zarpó; en Puerto Plata, el 6 de noviembre, un vapor francés y uno cubano fueron alejados por orden del buque de guerra dominicano. Los oficiales dominicanos negaron al Cherokee los papeles de despacho para salir de San Domingo y también se negaron a permitir que un piloto lo sacara del puerto; el ministro Powell protestó ante el gobierno dominicano e instruyó al capitán del Cherokee a sacar su barco sin papeles de despacho ni piloto. El Cherokee trajo diecinueve pasajeros de cabina desde San Domingo, pero ningún refugiado.

records.summary_en: The Herald-Review prints a Cape Haitien dispatch of November 11 under the head 'San Domingo Has Capitulated to the Revolution': a dispatch received there states that San Domingo has capitulated to the revolutionists and that Gen. Jiminez has been proclaimed president of the republic. On Monday, November 2, the Clyde line steamer Cherokee was fired upon by the Dominican cruiser Presidente while the steamer was running the blockade of Samana and returned to the capital; the United States cruiser Baltimore reported to Minister Powell at the capital, and three hours later she left to convoy the Cherokee. On Wednesday the government forces abandoned Macoris, and the following day the Dominican cruiser Independencia bombarded the town.

records.headline: The Star prints part of a discussion of the island: the island
records.summary_en: The Star prints part of a discussion of the island: the island has an area of 28,000 square miles, and upon it are the two republics of Hayti and Santo Domingo; Santo Domingo itself is not thickly populated, and the paper says the business of the republic is conducted by the whites, who number about 20 per cent of the population, and as a rule hold the offices. The paper argues that both republics have retrograded steadily, that both are financially wrecked, and that the Monroe doctrine gives the United States control of the island so far as any European power is concerned. Under the head 'Strategic Value of Samana Bay,' the paper describes Samana Bay, thirty-one miles long, at the eastern extremity of the island, just across from Porto Rico, as one of the most beautiful and valuable bays in the West Indies, and says the United States has sought possession of this bay as a strategic point in the Caribbean Sea for almost one hundred years, Gen. Jackson having first recommended the purchase in a message to Congress.
records.summary_es: El Star publica parte de una discusión sobre la isla: la isla tiene una superficie de 28,000 millas cuadradas, y sobre ella están las dos repúblicas de Haití y Santo Domingo; Santo Domingo en sí no está densamente poblado, y el periódico dice que los negocios de la república son conducidos por los blancos, que suman alrededor del 20 por ciento de la población, y por regla general ocupan los cargos. El periódico sostiene que ambas repúblicas han retrocedido constantemente, que ambas están financieramente arruinadas, y que la doctrina Monroe da a los Estados Unidos el control de la isla en lo que concierne a cualquier potencia europea. Bajo el titular «Strategic Value of Samana Bay», el periódico describe la bahía de Samaná, de treinta y una millas de largo, en el extremo oriental de la isla, justo frente a Puerto Rico, como una de las bahías más hermosas y valiosas de las Indias Occidentales, y dice que los Estados Unidos han buscado la posesión de esta bahía como punto estratégico en el mar Caribe durante casi cien años, habiendo recomendado el general Jackson por primera vez la compra en un mensaje al Congreso.

records.headline: The Star prints a New York item: the agents here of the Clyde line
records.summary_en: The Star prints a New York item: the agents here of the Clyde line steamer Cherokee, which had trouble with the Dominican government authorities on her last trip to that island, declared to-day that the Cherokee will sail next Wednesday on her regular schedule and will pursue her regular itinerary, stopping at Samana Bay, Monte Christi, Sanchez, Puerto Plata and Macoris. Manuel de J. Galvan, consul general from San Domingo to New York, said to-day that the Cherokee will surely be sunk if she attempts to enter the five harbors named; he says that the entire San Domingan navy, the gunboats El Presidente and Independencia, are on guard to maintain the blockade of those ports, now in the hands of the rebels, under Jiminez. 'If the Cherokee attempts to enter any of those ports the gunboats will not parley with her this time,' said Mr. Galvan. 'They will surely sink her.' The item appears under the head 'Hostile Threats Made Against Steamer Cherokee'.

records.headline: The Star prints part of an account of the exiles' expedition
records.summary_en: The Star prints part of an account of the exiles' expedition from Cuba: the exiles decided to co-operate with a general uprising along the frontier of Haiti, taking in the towns of Monte Cristy, Dajabon and Guayubin, and extending to the towns of Santiago de los Caballeros and La Vega, having received notification from the governor of Puerto Plata, Gen. and ex-Priest Don Carlos Morales, of the result of their plans. Then they prepared to take the Cuban steamer Maria Herrera with a view of landing in Puerto Plata, which was held by Gen. Carlos Morales, and so join the revolutionary movement. Unfortunately the Dominican consul in Cuba became aware of their movements and applied to the Cuban authorities to have them prevented from embarking, but he was informed by them that as there was no evidence that these men were taking arms and war stores, and as they were leaving the country as peaceable citizens, they could not be interfered with. The Dominican consul then telegraphed to the president of the Dominican republic at the city of Santo Domingo informing him of their having embarked for some port of the republic, presumably Puerto Plata. Under the head 'Took Passage for San Juan,' the account continues: the Dominican exiles, being perfectly aware of the uncertainty of such uprisings, took passage for San Juan, Porto Rico, intending to disembark in Puerto Plata if all were well, but if not to continue to Porto Rico and join ex-President Jiminez. Upon arriving off the port of Puerto Plata a Dominican warship was sighted, but no attention was paid to her, and they continued their course.
records.summary_es: El Star publica parte de un relato de la expedición de los exiliados desde Cuba: los exiliados decidieron cooperar con un levantamiento general a lo largo de la frontera de Haití, que abarcaba las poblaciones de Monte Cristi, Dajabón y Guayubín, y se extendía a las poblaciones de Santiago de los Caballeros y La Vega, habiendo recibido notificación del gobernador de Puerto Plata, el general y ex sacerdote don Carlos Morales, del resultado de sus planes. Entonces se prepararon para tomar el vapor cubano María Herrera con miras a desembarcar en Puerto Plata, que estaba en poder del general Carlos Morales, y unirse así al movimiento revolucionario. Desafortunadamente el cónsul dominicano en Cuba se enteró de sus movimientos y solicitó a las autoridades cubanas que les impidieran embarcar, pero fue informado por ellas de que, como no había evidencia de que estos hombres llevaran armas y pertrechos de guerra, y como salían del país como ciudadanos pacíficos, no se podía interferir con ellos. El cónsul dominicano telegrafió entonces al presidente de la república dominicana en la ciudad de Santo Domingo informándole que habían embarcado hacia algún puerto de la república, presumiblemente Puerto Plata. Bajo el titular «Took Passage for San Juan», el relato continúa: los exiliados dominicanos, perfectamente conscientes de la incertidumbre de tales levantamientos, tomaron pasaje para San Juan, Puerto Rico, con la intención de desembarcar en Puerto Plata si todo iba bien, pero si no, continuar a Puerto Rico y unirse al ex presidente Jiménez. Al llegar frente al puerto de Puerto Plata se avistó un buque de guerra dominicano, pero no se le prestó atención, y continuaron su rumbo.

records.headline: The Star prints a further part of its account of the Dominican exiles
records.summary_en: The Star prints a further part of its account of the Dominican exiles and of President Woss y Gil: the account speaks of a warrior priest, brother of a renowned soldier who perished in the attack upon that town, as a man of great energy and high aspiration, determined to equal his brother in fame. All the exiles are confident of the fall of the government, as they say that Puerto Plata and Santiago de los Caballeros together form the keystone of the republic, and these towns are asserted to be in the hands of the rebels. President Alejandro Woss y Gil is a man of considerable worth as a statesman and soldier; he is a well-educated man and has lived abroad for a considerable time, representing the Dominican republic at Washington for quite a number of years during the presidency of General Heureaux. Under the head 'Second Presidential Term,' the account continues: this is his second presidential term, having occupied that position for the first time when he was about twenty-six or twenty-seven years of age, being the first Dominican to occupy that high post at such an early age; he was the intimate friend of President Heureaux, and is said to be a man of his school, that is to say, a man who does not hesitate to give his troublesome adversaries six feet of good Dominican soil whenever he can get hold of them, and a tenacious fighter, who is not to be daunted by either the large number or superior strategic position of the enemy.

records.summary_en: The Plain Dealer prints a Port-au-Prince dispatch: the French steamer St. Simon, with General Jiminez aboard, has left Port-au-Prince, Hayti, with the intention, according to report, of forcing the blockade of Puerto Plata, on the northern coast of Santo Domingo; the Haytien authorities formally opposed the landing in Hayti of Gen. Jiminez, in spite of his strong insistence upon being permitted to do so; it is said that if the St. Simon is interfered with she will ask for the assistance of the German cruiser Gazelle, or any other foreign warship which may be in Dominican waters; the French cruiser Jurien de la Graviere, which was in these waters recently, is understood to have returned to the island of Martinique. Telegraphic communication with the interior of Santo Domingo was re-established Friday morning, but now is again interrupted, and it is reported that severe fighting must have occurred before San Domingo.

records.headline: I am sure that the United States government is in sympathy
records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that Dominican Consul General Galván threatened that government gunboats would sink any vessel, including the Clyde Line steamer *Cherokee*, attempting to enter rebel-controlled ports. New York customs authorities refused to deny clearances to American merchantmen, stating that the United States had not recognized the blockade as effective. The report also noted that President Wos y Gil had agreed to arbitrate the San Domingo Improvement Company's four-million-dollar claim regarding railroad construction.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que el cónsul general dominicano Galván amenazó con que los cañoneros del gobierno hundirían cualquier embarcación, incluido el vapor *Cherokee* de la Clyde Line, que intentara ingresar a puertos bajo control rebelde. Las autoridades aduaneras de Nueva York se negaron a denegar el despacho a los mercantes estadounidenses, alegando que los Estados Unidos no habían reconocido el bloqueo como efectivo. El informe señaló asimismo que el presidente Wos y Gil había aceptado someter a arbitraje la reclamación de cuatro millones de dólares de la San Domingo Improvement Company relativa a la construcción del ferrocarril.
