records.headline: The Advertiser prints a New York item: the agents of the Clyde line
records.summary_en: The Advertiser prints a New York item: the agents of the Clyde line steamer Cherokee, which had trouble with the Dominican government authorities on her last trip to that island, declared to-day that the Cherokee will sail to-day on her regular schedule and will pursue her regular itinerary, stopping at Samana Bay, Monte Cristi, Sanchez, Puerto Plata and Macoris. Galvan, consul general from San Domingo to New York, said to-day that the Cherokee will surely be sunk if she attempts to enter the five harbors named; he says the entire San Dominican navy, the gunboats El Presidente and Independencia, are on guard to maintain the blockade of those ports, now in the hands of the rebels under Jiminez. Consul Galvan continued: 'Acting on orders from my government, I have notified the collector of the port that the ports of Samana Bay, Sanchez, Puerto Plata, Monte Cristi and Macoris are closed and that the Clyde steamers cannot be cleared for them. I do not know what action he will take. I understand the Clyde line is taking cargoes for these ports as usual. Several port shippers have called here to ask me about the situation. They say that the Clyde line agents tell them that the Cherokee is going to these ports under escort of United States vessels. I think they will find they are mistaken if they think anything of that sort.'

New York, November 16.—More trouble seems to be in store for the steamer Cherokee which arrived here last week from Dominican ports after several thrilling experiences. The agents of the Clyde line steamers In this city declared today that the Cherokee will sail next Wednesday on her regular schedule and will pursue her regular itinerary, stopping at Samana Bay, Monte Christi, Sanchez, Puerto Plata and Macoris. Manuel De J. Galvan, consul general from San Domingo to New York, said today that the Cherokee will certainly be sunk if she attempts to enter the five harbors named. He says that the entire San Domingoan navy the gunboats El Presidente and Independence are on guard to maintain the blockade of those ports, now in the hands of the rebels under Jiminez. “If the Cherokee attempts to enter any of those ports the gunboats will not parley with her this time,” said Mr. Galvan. R., November 16.—Official advices received at the San Domingo consulate here say General Jiminez Is in supreme command of the revolutionists and that General Deschamps, the vice president of the republic, is to join Jiminez with the best of the supporters of President Wos y Gil.

records.summary_en: The Advertiser prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch and a Washington item of November 17: General Woss y Gil refuses to capitulate and it is believed the fighting will be severe; the situation is desperate and fighting in the streets is liable to occur at any moment; the United States cruiser Baltimore has been compelled to leave to re-coal, and United States Minister Powell is endeavoring to protect American interests with the limited means at his disposal; a German naval vessel is ready to land troops at a moment's notice; the insurgents endeavored to have Minister Powell recognize them, but the minister refused to do so; the revolutionists fired on the Clyde Line steamer New York as she was entering the port of Samana, but the vessel was uninjured; the Dominican government has appointed Minister of Foreign Relations Galvan and Judge George Gray of Delaware as commissioners to arbitrate the Santo Domingo Improvement matter, as the result of Minister Powell's effort to compel the carrying out of the terms of the protocol, and Commissioner Galvan will leave for the United States tomorrow, though it is possible the insurgents may endeavor to capture him. The Washington item says the revolutionists of San Domingo applied to the State Department today for recognition by the United States, the application being presented by J. M. Giordan, who represented himself as the provisional agent of the revolutionary government of which General Jiminez is the head, and that the State Department declined the recognition.

N. Strahan, collector of the port of New York, who received telegraphic advices from the Treasury Department advising him that the State Department did not consider the blockade effective and had entered a vigorous protest against it, and who has notified masters of vessels sailing to San Domingo ports that clearance papers will be issued for any port in San Domingo, thus officially refuting the effectiveness of the blockade. At the offices of the Clyde line it was said that the Cherokee would clear tomorrow for her usual trip, calling at the ports which the local Dominican consul says are closed.

records.summary_en: The Review prints a Port-au-Prince dispatch: the French steamer St. Simon, with General Jiminez, head of the Dominican revolution, on board, has left Port-au-Prince, Hayti, with the intention, according to report, of forcing the blockade of Puerto Plata, on the northern coast of Santo Domingo; the Haytien authorities formally opposed the landing in Hayti of General Jiminez, in spite of his strong insistence upon being permitted to do so; it is said that if the St. Simon is interfered with she will ask for the assistance of the German cruiser Gazelle, or any other foreign warship which may be in Dominican waters; the French cruiser Jurien de la Graviere, which was in these waters recently, is understood to have returned to the island of Martinique; telegraphic communication with the interior of Santo Domingo was re-established Friday morning, but now is again interrupted, and it is reported that severe fighting must have occurred before San Domingo.

The Clyde line of steamers running from New York to Dominican ports are unpopular with a portion of the people of the country; the Clyde line had a claim against the Dominican government for $350,000 for refund of wharfage and other port dues, and, unable to get satisfaction from the government, finally secured a presentation of their claim through the United States government; Minister Powell demanded the settlement of the claim, but the matter was still in the air at the time the present revolution broke out; the port of Samana, in which the New York was fired upon, is being greedily watched by European powers that wish to secure it for a coaling station.

records.headline: The Advertiser prints part of a New York item on the Cherokee's sailing:
records.summary_en: The Advertiser prints part of a New York item on the Cherokee's sailing: C. I. Maxwell, consul general to San Domingo, sailed in the Cherokee; he said he would not be surprised to find the revolution ended when he reached there, and that in a way he has orders to advise the captain of the ship what to do in certain contingencies, though he cannot say what his advice will be until they reach the spot and he sees what confronts them. He thinks the Baltimore will be at Monte Cristi, their first port of call, before they get there, and in that event the officers will decide what they are to do; if the Dominican officials establish a blockade and can maintain it, of the five ports named, or any one of them, they cannot enter, but to make the blockade effectual it must be perpetual, the gunboats which meet them at Monte Cristi and prevent their entering that harbor being unable to follow them to another port and keep them out there. The Dominican government has two gunboats, capable of maintaining a blockade of two ports at the same time, but he does not think they could effectively blockade more than that; he has heard a rumor that the government has armed two sailing vessels as supplementary warships for this blockade service, but does not know that it is true. Consul Galvan said he understood several cases of arms were offered for shipment on the Cherokee to Puerto Plata, but the Clyde people would not take them unless he certified his consent; the shippers did not come to him for approval, and he does not know who they were.

records.headline: There was a heavy artillery duel between government troops and the insurgents at Santo Domingo City on the night of November
records.summary_en: There was a heavy artillery duel between government troops and the insurgents at Santo Domingo City on the night of November 17, and the United States cruiser Baltimore landed a force of marines for the protection of American interests. Minister Powell's despatches to the State Department call the situation desperate: the city is constantly under fire, shells are falling in it, it is surrounded on three sides, an assault is momentarily expected, and it is believed the Dominican government cannot much longer hold out against the revolutionists.

Los despachos del ministro Powell al Departamento de Estado califican la situación de desesperada: la ciudad está constantemente bajo fuego, caen proyectiles en ella, está rodeada por tres lados, se espera un asalto de un momento a otro y se cree que el gobierno dominicano no podrá resistir mucho más contra los revolucionarios.

records.summary_en: The Times prints a Santo Domingo item: Mr. Giordani did not say with whom the negotiations of President Woss y Gil have been begun, and the State Department has no knowledge of any such negotiations. Santo Domingo is still holding out against the attacks of the Dominican insurgents, but dispatches from the capital indicate that it cannot withstand the bombarding of the attacking forces much longer; all cities of importance, with the exception of Santo Domingo, are said to be under the control of the insurgents; the United States cruiser Baltimore is now at San Juan coaling, and in its absence from Santo Domingo the Newport went from Puerto Plata to look after American interests. The Clyde liner Cherokee, which forced the blockade at Dominican ports two weeks ago, left New York yesterday for another visit to Santo Domingo; Consul General Galvan, the Dominican representative in New York, refused to issue clearance papers for the vessel to enter any ports excepting Santo Domingo and Azua, but in spite of the refusal the Cherokee will attempt to enter Macoris, Puerto Plata, and other ports at which Santo Domingo is attempting to establish a blockade; the State Department does not recognize this blockade as effective; C. L. Maxwell, the United States consul general at Santo Domingo, is on the Cherokee and will advise the captain concerning his entrance into harbors where the blockade is supposed to be maintained.

records.headline: The Journal prints a Santo Domingo item: Commander Briggs's reports
records.summary_en: The Journal prints a Santo Domingo item: Commander Briggs's reports indicate that the bombardments of San Domingo by the insurrectionists have been hot; having stated that his coal supply was running low, Commander Briggs was authorized to take the Baltimore to San Juan for coal and then return to San Domingo city, and, in order that the interests of the United States in that city should not be left unprotected in the absence of the cruiser Baltimore, orders were telegraphed to Commander Diehl, commanding the gunboat Newport, at Puerto Plata, on the north coast of San Domingo, to proceed at once to San Domingo city, on the southern coast; it is stated it will not take the Baltimore more than a day or two to make the run to San Juan and back. A Cape Haytien dispatch of November 18 adds that information has been received at Monte Cristi from Santo Domingo that United States Minister Powell, accompanied by Minister of Foreign Relations Galvan, has gone aboard the United States cruiser Baltimore, the object of their visit to the warship being unknown, and that the arrival of the United States gunboat Newport is anxiously awaited, she being believed to be still at Puerto Plata. A New York item adds that Consul General Galvan, of San Domingo, refused to sign clearance papers for the Clyde Line steamer Cherokee to the five Dominican ports in the hands of insurgents, for which the Cherokee sailed today, but granted clearance papers for the ports of San Domingo and Azua.
records.summary_es: El Journal publica una nota de Santo Domingo: los informes del comandante Briggs indican que los bombardeos de San Domingo por los insurreccionistas han sido intensos; habiendo declarado que su suministro de carbón se estaba agotando, el comandante Briggs fue autorizado a llevar el Baltimore a San Juan por carbón y luego regresar a la ciudad de San Domingo, y, para que los intereses de los Estados Unidos en esa ciudad no quedaran desprotegidos en ausencia del crucero Baltimore, se telegrafiaron órdenes al comandante Diehl, al mando de la cañonera Newport, en Puerto Plata, en la costa norte de San Domingo, para que procediera de inmediato a la ciudad de San Domingo, en la costa sur; se afirma que el Baltimore no tardará más de un día o dos en hacer el viaje a San Juan y de regreso. Un despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 18 de noviembre añade que se ha recibido información en Monte Cristi desde Santo Domingo de que el ministro estadounidense Powell, acompañado por el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores Galván, ha subido a bordo del crucero estadounidense Baltimore, siendo desconocido el objeto de su visita al buque de guerra, y que la llegada de la cañonera estadounidense Newport es esperada con ansiedad, creyéndose que aún está en Puerto Plata. Una nota de Nueva York añade que el cónsul general Galván, de San Domingo, se negó a firmar papeles de despacho para el vapor Cherokee, de la línea Clyde, hacia los cinco puertos dominicanos en manos de los insurgentes, por los que el Cherokee zarpó hoy, pero concedió papeles de despacho para los puertos de San Domingo y Azua.

General Jiminez Will Attempt to
Force Blockade.
Cape Haytien, Hayti, Nov. 16.—The
French steamer St. Simon, with Gen
eral Jiminez, head of the Dominican
revolution, on board, has left Port
au Prince. Hayti, with the intention,
according to report, of forcing the
blockade of Puerto Plata, on the
northern coast of Santo Domingo.
The Haytian authorities formally
opposed the landing in Hayti of Gen
eral Jiminez in spite of his strong
insistence on being permitted to do so.
It is said that if the St. Simon is
interfered with she will ask for the
assistance of the German cruiser
Gazelle or any other foreign warship
which may be in Dominican waters.
SNOW DELAYS TRAFFIC.
Heavy Losses to Stock Anticipated in
Montana.
I-iewistown, Mont.. Nov. 16.—Over
twelve inches of snow have fallen on
the level in Fergus county, and under
the heavy winds of the past three days
has played havoc with mountain
passes, filling canyons with snow. The
Great Falls stage is stuck in the snow
somewhere between Lewistown and
Phills Rock. Lewistown has had no
trains since Friday and two engines
are now cab deep in drifts within a
few miles of Lewistown. It is feared
that heavy losses to stock will result
if a warm spell is not speedily forth
coming. The temperature is five be
low zero and still dropping.

records.summary_en: The Capital prints a feature under the head 'San Domingo's Queer Soldiers': some of the queerest soldiers in the world are to be found in San Domingo, or the Dominican Republic, as it is officially called; an Englishman who ran a steamship business in San Domingo City says there were four or five generals among the hundred coal carriers he employed, who coaled the steamers by carrying big baskets on their heads at 25 cents a day, and now and then would take a day off to review their armies, conduct manoeuvres or fight revolutionists; one of these generals, who had no uniform, stole a pair of gold-laced 'pants' from a shop, was caught with the goods and punished by being paraded around town on a donkey, face toward the tail, with the 'pants' tied around his neck; the soldiers are not volunteers, for when the government wants troops it simply sends into the country districts and seizes the laborers in the fields and the travelers on the roads, and though at first naturally discontented, they like the new job when they find that soldiers have no work to do; they are furnished with a suit of clothes every year, but it does not last them long, for they are inveterate gamblers and after they have lost all their money they gamble away their uniform, keeping nothing save their rifles, an old pair of trousers and a ragged shirt.

records.headline: The Republican prints a San Juan item and two Washington items
records.summary_en: The Republican prints a San Juan item and two Washington items: the St. Simon arrived at San Juan, Porto Rico, Wednesday from Hayti and San Domingo and reports that all of the Dominican republic, except the capital, San Domingo, was in the hands of the revolutionists, that General Jiminez, leader of the Dominican revolutionists, left Hayti the 16th and is due to arrive today before San Domingo and assume direction of the siege of that city, and that General Caceres was assisting in the military operations of the revolutionists. Associated Press dispatches from San Domingo Tuesday said that, yielding to the continued vigorous action of Minister Powell, the Dominican government had appointed Minister Galvan and Judge George Gray of Delaware to arbitrate the difficulties between that government and the San Domingo Improvement Company, an American concern, that Minister Galvan was to leave immediately for the United States, and that on his departure the insurgents might make an effort to capture him; the Improvement Company was operating under several concessions obtained from the Dominican government, when an attempt was made to withdraw the privileges granted under these concessions. Under the head 'Recognition Refused Revolutionists by United States,' the paper reports that the revolutionists of San Domingo Tuesday applied to the state department for recognition by the United States, the application being presented by J. H. Giordan, who represented himself as the provisional agent of the revolutionary government, of which General Jiminez is the head.

records.summary_en: The Times prints a Santo Domingo item: government forces at Santo Domingo are still holding out against the insurgents, but the little island republic is in a hopeless state of revolution; the minister of foreign affairs has started for this country, and it is believed an appeal for help will be made to the United States; French marines have landed at Santo Domingo to protect the French legation, and Minister Powell informed the State Department of the arrival of a French ship at Santo Domingo and the landing of marines; Dominican troops forced an entrance into the French legation and seized two refugees who had sought protection there; it is rumored Santo Domingo will offer the United States the use of Samana Bay as a coaling station in return for assistance in settling the trouble in the island; the United States cruiser Baltimore is at Santo Domingo, and the gunboat will arrive there today; Minister Powell has reported to the State Department that the failure of a general to obtain a cabinet position caused the revolution, which threatens to end the present government.
records.summary_es: El Times publica una nota de Santo Domingo: las fuerzas del gobierno en Santo Domingo aún resisten a los insurgentes, pero la pequeña república isleña se encuentra en un estado desesperado de revolución; el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores ha partido hacia este país, y se cree que se hará un llamamiento de ayuda a los Estados Unidos; marines franceses han desembarcado en Santo Domingo para proteger la legación francesa, y el ministro Powell informó al Departamento de Estado de la llegada de un buque francés a Santo Domingo y del desembarco de marines; tropas dominicanas forzaron la entrada a la legación francesa y se apoderaron de dos refugiados que habían buscado protección allí; se rumora que Santo Domingo ofrecerá a los Estados Unidos el uso de la bahía de Samaná como estación carbonera a cambio de ayuda para resolver los disturbios en la isla; el crucero estadounidense Baltimore está en Santo Domingo, y la cañonera llegará allí hoy; el ministro Powell ha informado al Departamento de Estado que el fracaso de un general en obtener un puesto en el gabinete causó la revolución, que amenaza con terminar con el gobierno actual.

records.headline: The News prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch
records.summary_en: The News prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch, with two items of November 18: it is believed the fighting will be severe; the situation is desperate and fighting in the streets is likely to occur at any moment; United States Minister Powell is endeavoring to protect American interests with the limited means at his disposal; the cruiser Baltimore has been compelled to leave to re-coal; a German naval vessel is ready to land troops at a moment's notice; the insurgents endeavored to have Minister Powell recognize them but he refused to do so; the revolutionists fired on the Clyde line steamer New York as she entered the port of Samana, but the vessel was uninjured. Under the head 'Blockade No Good,' a New York item says the United States government has refused to recognize the blockade of the San Dominican ports, made two days ago, and has protested against it, as confirmed by Nevada N. Stranahan, collector of the port of New York, who had notified the masters of vessels to San Dominican ports that clearance papers will be issued for any ports in San Domingo, thus officially refuting the effectiveness of the blockade. Under the head 'Recognition Here Comes Slowly,' a Washington item says the revolutionists of San Domingo yesterday, through J. M. Griordan, who represented himself as the agent of the revolutionary government, applied to the state department for recognition by the United States, and the state department declined recognition, informing Griordan that it had been the unbroken policy of the state department to recognize only the de facto government.
records.summary_es: El News publica la parte final de un despacho de San Domingo, con dos notas del 18 de noviembre: se cree que la lucha será severa; la situación es desesperada y la lucha en las calles puede ocurrir en cualquier momento; el ministro estadounidense Powell se esfuerza por proteger los intereses estadounidenses con los limitados medios a su disposición; el crucero Baltimore se ha visto obligado a partir a recargar carbón; un buque de guerra alemán está listo para desembarcar tropas en cualquier momento; los insurgentes trataron de que el ministro Powell los reconociera pero él se negó a hacerlo; los revolucionarios dispararon contra el vapor New York, de la línea Clyde, cuando entraba al puerto de Samaná, pero el buque no sufrió daños. records.headline: The Republic prints an editorial on the Santo Domingo situation
records.summary_en: The Republic prints an editorial on the Santo Domingo situation: to crown all, the paper says, there came recognition of Panama, which has strained relations with Colombia, and now Santo Domingo looms up on the horizon as a new field for intervention; Senor Galvan of the present government of Santo Domingo is said to be hastening to Washington to offer the United States Samana Bay as a naval station in exchange for the Washington government's support of President Woss y Gil, whose administration is tottering from the onslaught of General Jiminez; Samana Bay is not desired by the Navy Department, but those in Washington who are watching the situation closely say: 'After Santo Domingo, what next?'
records.summary_es: El Republic publica un editorial sobre la situación de Santo Domingo: para coronarlo todo, dice el periódico, llegó el reconocimiento de Panamá, que ha tensado las relaciones con Colombia, y ahora Santo Domingo se presenta en el horizonte como un nuevo campo de intervención; se dice que el señor Galván, del actual gobierno de Santo Domingo, se apresura a ir a Washington para ofrecer a los Estados Unidos la bahía de Samaná como estación naval a cambio del apoyo del gobierno de Washington al presidente Woss y Gil, cuya administración se tambalea ante la embestida del general Jiménez; la bahía de Samaná no es deseada por el Departamento de Marina, pero quienes en Washington observan de cerca la situación dicen: «Después de Santo Domingo, ¿qué sigue?».

records.headline: The News prints part of an editorial on Samana Bay: in spite of the fact
records.summary_en: The News prints part of an editorial on Samana Bay: in spite of the fact that this country is in possession of San Juan, of Culebra and of Guantanamo, it would be in a stronger and more impregnable position than ever if it acquired Samana Bay also, which besides being easily defended affords a harbor in which the whole American navy could ride in safety, without encountering the dangers of being bottled up as was Cervera's fleet at Santiago; should this country conclude to make the purchase, the fact will in no way affect the sovereignty of the Dominican republic, while we will be relieved of the incessant trouble and annoyance that would inevitably otherwise result; a man of great experience and keen observation has declared Samana Bay to be 'one of those maritime positions that are encountered in only two or three places in the world; it is not only the military key but the commercial key to this part of the world'; the advantages of Samana, the paper says, are as fully realized at Washington as anywhere else.

records.headline: The Eagle prints an editorial on General Juan Isidro Jiminez
records.summary_en: The Eagle prints an editorial on General Juan Isidro Jiminez, whom Cape Haytien dispatches announce as the new president of San Domingo: he is not a novice in the business of revolutions, so flourishing in the tropics; his title of general was conferred upon him after his participation in many such uprisings; the see-saw of militant politics has replaced him at the top, reducing General Woss y Gil to the level of a mere presidential possibility at a later day, when Jiminez's back is turned and the greater number of rifles are in the hands of his adherents; General Jiminez has been president of the Dominican republic before, and his recent action in marching upon the capital at the head of an army is guarantee of his firm purpose to retain the office.
records.summary_es: El Eagle publica un editorial sobre el general Juan Isidro Jiménez, a quien los despachos de Cabo Haitiano anuncian como el nuevo presidente de San Domingo: no es un novato en el negocio de las revoluciones, tan floreciente en los trópicos; su título de general le fue conferido después de su participación en muchas de esas revueltas; el vaivén de la política militante lo ha vuelto a colocar en la cima, reduciendo al general Woss y Gil al nivel de una mera posibilidad presidencial para más adelante, cuando Jiménez dé la espalda y el mayor número de fusiles esté en manos de sus partidarios; el general Jiménez ha sido presidente de la república dominicana antes, y su reciente acción de marchar sobre la capital al frente de un ejército es garantía de su firme propósito de retener el cargo.

records.headline: The Tribune prints part of an item on the New York's arrival
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints part of an item on the New York's arrival: she came in fully a day ahead of her best schedule time, because she had so little cargo to pick up from the ports outside of San Domingo which are in the hands of the insurgents, and brought only one passenger and about one-third her usual cargo; Captain Morimon and the other officers of the New York say they do not think that the Cherokee will have any trouble in making the five ports which the Dominican government has declared 'closed,' as they say no attempt at blockading them was in evidence when they left; they made all these ports, discharging cargo and mails and landing passengers unmolested, and the only passenger brought to this city was from Puerto Plata, one of the five 'closed' ports; on the trip down the New York was fired on by the insurgents as she tried to enter Samana Bay at 4 o'clock on the morning of November 11; 'It was just growing light,' said Captain Morimon, 'and we were heading in toward the entrance of the bay, when a shell from one of the forts passed close under our stern; I sounded three whistles, and no more shots were fired; later an apology was made, and the explanation offered that we were mistaken for a government gunboat'; the captain said his ship was much larger than the gunboats, and that it was bright moonlight when the shot was fired; the purser's coat was cut by a shell as he was going to the custom house.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica parte de una nota sobre la llegada del New York: el vapor llegó con un día completo de adelanto sobre su mejor horario, porque tenía muy poca carga que recoger de los puertos fuera de San Domingo que están en manos de los insurgentes, y trajo solo un pasajero y alrededor de un tercio de su carga habitual; el capitán Morimon y los demás oficiales del New York dicen que no creen que el Cherokee tenga ningún problema para hacer los cinco puertos que el gobierno dominicano ha declarado «cerrados», pues dicen que ningún intento de bloquearlos era evidente cuando partieron; hicieron todos esos puertos, descargando carga y correo y desembarcando pasajeros sin ser molestados, y el único pasajero traído a esta ciudad procedía de Puerto Plata, uno de los cinco puertos «cerrados»; en el viaje de ida el New York fue atacado a tiros por los insurgentes cuando trataba de entrar a la bahía de Samaná a las 4 de la mañana del 11 de noviembre; «Apenas comenzaba a clarear», dijo el capitán Morimon, «y nos dirigíamos hacia la entrada de la bahía, cuando un proyectil de uno de los fuertes pasó cerca, bajo nuestra popa; toqué tres silbatos, y no se hicieron más disparos; más tarde se presentó una disculpa, y la explicación ofrecida fue que nos habían confundido con una cañonera del gobierno»; el capitán dijo que su buque era mucho más grande que las cañoneras, y que había una brillante luna cuando se hizo el disparo; el abrigo del sobrecargo fue cortado por un proyectil cuando se dirigía a la aduana.

records.headline: The Star prints part of the profile of General Deschamps, an official of the Dominican republic
records.summary_en: The Star prints part of the profile of General Deschamps, an official of the Dominican republic in the government of President Alejandro Woss y Gil up to a few days ago, when he resigned his position to join his former chief, ex-President Juan Isidro Jiminez: General Deschamps is one of the most popular men in the Dominican republic; his popularity is not, however, due to military prowess, but to the fact that he has always been the people's friend, is a great lover of progress, has always had the tact to espouse the right cause, and above all because he has been the victim of the most terrible persecution; due to his bold opposition to President Heureaux's sanguinary and corrupted policy he was forced to leave Santo Domingo and live abroad, where he had to suffer many hardships; although living in exile he did not slacken in his attacks upon President Heureaux's policy, and about seven years ago, while residing in Ponce, Porto Rico, an assassin paid by President Heureaux to assassinate him drove a dagger into his back, very nearly killing him; the assassin escaped and Deschamps slowly recovered, but he has never succeeded in making the wound heal thoroughly, and it is a constant source of annoyance to him; at another time his wife, who had accompanied him in exile, embarked in a small schooner at the British island of Grand Turk for Puerto Plata, but on her arrival at that port she was not permitted to disembark, and though she was accompanied by her children and the eldest boy took ill on board, still she was not permitted to disembark.
records.summary_es: El Star publica parte del perfil del general Deschamps, un funcionario de la república dominicana en el gobierno del presidente Alejandro Woss y Gil hasta hace pocos días, cuando renunció a su cargo para unirse a su antiguo jefe, el expresidente Juan Isidro Jiménez: el general Deschamps es uno de los hombres más populares de la república dominicana; su popularidad no se debe, sin embargo, a sus proezas militares, sino al hecho de que siempre ha sido amigo del pueblo, es un gran amante del progreso, siempre ha tenido el tacto de abrazar la causa correcta y, sobre todo, porque ha sido víctima de la más terrible persecución; debido a su audaz oposición a la política sanguinaria y corrupta del presidente Heureaux se vio obligado a salir de Santo Domingo y vivir en el extranjero, donde tuvo que sufrir muchas penurias; aunque vivía en el exilio no aflojó en sus ataques contra la política del presidente Heureaux, y hace unos siete años, mientras residía en Ponce, Puerto Rico, un asesino pagado por el presidente Heureaux para asesinarlo le clavó un puñal en la espalda, casi matándolo; el asesino escapó y Deschamps se recuperó lentamente, pero nunca ha logrado que la herida sane por completo, y es para él una fuente constante de molestia; en otra ocasión su esposa, que lo había acompañado en el exilio, se embarcó en una pequeña goleta en la isla británica de Gran Turca rumbo a Puerto Plata, pero a su llegada a ese puerto no se le permitió desembarcar, y aunque la acompañaban sus hijos y el niño mayor enfermó a bordo, aun así no se le permitió desembarcar.

records.summary_en: The Star prints a sketch of General Ramon Caceres, the slayer of President Heureaux on June 26, 1899 and ex-governor of Santiago de los Caballeros: he is one of the chief leaders of the present revolution, ranks next to Jiminez, and will most likely be appointed to the vice presidency should the revolution triumph; General Caceres is a man of great energy and courage and has set his heart upon the highest position in the republic, but he is unfortunately a man of the sword and not of the pen, and although he might make an excellent president for the quelling of revolutions, he would certainly not know how to set about extracting the republic from its present financial difficulties, which are many and pressing; if the present revolution triumphs it will have many claims upon its hands: there is a Cuban claim for preventing the Cuban steamer Maria Herrera to enter the port of Puerto Plata to land her passengers, mail and cargo without there being any notification whatever of the existence of a regular blockade; there is just such another claim to be made by the Clyde Line of steamers, there is a German claim, and there is said to be a Spanish claim for the death of the chancellor of the Spanish consulate who was killed by a bullet while writing in his office during the last revolution, eight months ago, and others; meanwhile the resources of the country have been completely paralyzed, and sugar, which is the chief product, is lacking a market, the American market being the only one it ever had.
records.summary_es: El Star publica un bosquejo del general Ramón Cáceres, el asesino del presidente Heureaux el 26 de junio de 1899 y exgobernador de Santiago de los Caballeros: es uno de los principales líderes de la revolución actual, ocupa el segundo lugar después de Jiménez y muy probablemente será nombrado vicepresidente si la revolución triunfa; el general Cáceres es un hombre de gran energía y valor y ha puesto su corazón en la más alta posición de la república, pero es desafortunadamente un hombre de espada y no de pluma, y aunque podría ser un excelente presidente para sofocar revoluciones, ciertamente no sabría cómo sacar a la república de sus actuales dificultades financieras, que son muchas y apremiantes; si la revolución actual triunfa tendrá muchas reclamaciones entre manos: hay una reclamación cubana por impedir que el vapor cubano María Herrera entrara al puerto de Puerto Plata para desembarcar a sus pasajeros, el correo y la carga sin que hubiera notificación alguna de la existencia de un bloqueo regular; hay otra reclamación igual que hará la línea de vapores Clyde, hay una reclamación alemana, y se dice que hay una reclamación española por la muerte del canciller del consulado español, quien fue muerto por una bala mientras escribía en su oficina durante la última revolución, hace ocho meses, y otras; mientras tanto los recursos del país han quedado completamente paralizados, y el azúcar, que es el producto principal, carece de mercado, siendo el mercado estadounidense el único que jamás tuvo.

records.headline: The Sun's correspondent reports that the revolution begun at Puerto Plata by General Carlos Morales, whom President Wos y
records.summary_en: The Sun's correspondent reports that the revolution begun at Puerto Plata by General Carlos Morales, whom President Wos y Gil had himself made governor there, grew into a national movement that deposed Wos y Gil after only seven months as president, with former President Jiminez, now with the insurgents, considered most likely to succeed him. The same report tells how the Clyde Line steamer New York was fired on by insurgents as she entered Samana Bay at four in the morning on November 1, a shell whistling over Captain Marmion's head from a fort on the bluff above the narrow channel.
records.summary_es: El corresponsal de The Sun informa que la revolución iniciada en Puerto Plata por el general Carlos Morales, a quien el propio presidente Wos y Gil había nombrado gobernador allí, creció hasta convertirse en un movimiento nacional que depuso a Wos y Gil tras solo siete meses como presidente, y que el expresidente Jiménez, ahora con los insurgentes, era considerado el sucesor más probable. El mismo informe cuenta cómo el vapor New York, de la Clyde Line, fue atacado a tiros por los insurgentes cuando entraba en la bahía de Samaná a las cuatro de la mañana del 1 de noviembre, y una granada pasó silbando sobre la cabeza del capitán Marmion desde un fuerte en el risco sobre el estrecho canal.

records.summary_en: The Sun prints a New York item: the Clyde Line steamer New York was exposed at the capital, Santo Domingo, to the firing between the government and insurgent forces; entering the bay of Samana at 4 o'clock in the morning, she was fired on close to the ship from the insurgent fort; Captain Marmion of the New York said: 'We were entering the west channel about 4 o'clock in the morning, and I was standing on the bridge when I heard a report and a shell whistled over my head; the channel is very narrow and the shore rises into a high bluff; I never knew that bluff to be fortified before, in all my experience with Dominican revolutions, but learned later that the insurgents had two guns up there; it was impossible for them to hit us because they were so far above.'

records.headline: The Call prints a New York item of November 21 and three dispatches
records.summary_en: The Call prints a New York item of November 21 and three dispatches: the Clyde line steamship New York arrived here today from Dominican ports, at one of which, Samana, the steamship was fired upon by insurgents; the New York touched at all the other ports of the island without being molested, although at the capital, San Domingo, she was exposed to the firing between the government and insurgent forces; the New York was entering the bay of Samana at 4 o'clock in the morning on November 11 when a shot was fired close to the ship from the insurgent fort, and Captain Marmion of the New York is quoted. Dispatches received at Cape Haytien from Puerto Plata say that the city of San Domingo was surrendered to the revolutionists this morning and that President Woss y Gil and his ministers took refuge on board a German warship, and that great enthusiasm prevails there. In a cablegram received at Washington from Minister Powell, dated San Domingo, November 23, he announced that the president of San Domingo had agreed to surrender the city to the revolutionists, that the articles of capitulation are being drawn up, and that the surrender will occur today. A San Domingo item of Monday, November 23, says President Woss y Gil requested the ministers of the United States, Belgium, Hayti and Spain to intervene in behalf of the government, and that the insurgents refused to accept the terms offered and demanded the immediate capitulation of the city.
records.summary_es: El Call publica una nota de Nueva York del 21 de noviembre y tres despachos: el vapor New York, de la línea Clyde, llegó aquí hoy procedente de puertos dominicanos, en uno de los cuales, Samaná, el vapor fue atacado a tiros por los insurgentes; el New York tocó en todos los demás puertos de la isla sin ser molestado, aunque en la capital, San Domingo, estuvo expuesto al fuego entre las fuerzas del gobierno y los insurgentes; el New York entraba a la bahía de Samaná a las 4 de la mañana del 11 de noviembre cuando se hizo un disparo cerca del buque desde el fuerte insurgente, y se cita al capitán Marmion, del New York. Despachos recibidos en Cabo Haitiano procedentes de Puerto Plata dicen que la ciudad de San Domingo fue entregada a los revolucionarios esta mañana y que el presidente Woss y Gil y sus ministros se refugiaron a bordo de un buque de guerra alemán, y que reina un gran entusiasmo allí. En un cablegrama recibido en Washington del ministro Powell, fechado en San Domingo el 23 de noviembre, anunció que el presidente de San Domingo había aceptado entregar la ciudad a los revolucionarios, que se están redactando los artículos de capitulación y que la entrega ocurrirá hoy. Una nota de San Domingo del lunes 23 de noviembre dice que el presidente Woss y Gil pidió a los ministros de los Estados Unidos, Bélgica, Haití y España que intervinieran a favor del gobierno, y que los insurgentes se negaron a aceptar los términos ofrecidos y exigieron la capitulación inmediata de la ciudad.

records.headline: The Age-Herald prints a New York item of November 24 and a San Domingo item of November 24:
records.summary_en: The Age-Herald prints a New York item of November 24 and a San Domingo item of November 24: the Clyde line steamer New York arrived today from San Domingo; Captain Marmion says the New York was at San Domingo city during the bombardment, that the firing continued throughout the three days the ship was there, and that a threatened attack from the opposite side of the river hurried the steamer away; 'It was Fourth of July fireworks every night,' said the captain, 'and I don't believe the rebels could capture the city in ten years, if the money holds out'; the purser's boat was struck by a shell while going ashore to the custom house; on the night of November 14, while passing into the harbor of Samana, the New York was fired on by a battery of two guns in charge of the insurgents; Captain Marmion was told later that the ship was mistaken for a government cruiser, and the captain says his ship is much larger than the Dominican war vessels, and it was bright moonlight at the time, and the shots passed high over the vessel. The San Domingo item says President Woss y Gil requested the ministers of the United States, Belgium, Hayti and Spain to intervene in behalf of the government, and that the insurgents refused to accept the terms offered and demanded the immediate capitulation of the city. The New York item appears under the head 'Story of Bombardment'.
records.summary_es: El Age-Herald publica una nota de Nueva York del 24 de noviembre y una nota de San Domingo del 24 de noviembre: el vapor New York, de la línea Clyde, llegó hoy procedente de San Domingo; el capitán Marmion dice que el New York estuvo en la ciudad de San Domingo durante el bombardeo, que el fuego continuó durante los tres días que el buque estuvo allí, y que un ataque amenazado desde el lado opuesto del río apresuró la partida del vapor; «Era como los fuegos artificiales del Cuatro de Julio todas las noches», dijo el capitán, «y no creo que los rebeldes pudieran capturar la ciudad en diez años, si el dinero alcanza»; la lancha del sobrecargo fue alcanzada por un proyectil cuando se dirigía a tierra a la aduana; en la noche del 14 de noviembre, al pasar hacia el puerto de Samaná, el New York fue atacado a tiros por una batería de dos cañones a cargo de los insurgentes; al capitán Marmion se le dijo después que el buque había sido confundido con un crucero del gobierno, y el capitán dice que su buque es mucho más grande que los buques de guerra dominicanos, y que había una brillante luna en ese momento, y que los disparos pasaron alto sobre el buque. La nota de San Domingo dice que el presidente Woss y Gil pidió a los ministros de los Estados Unidos, Bélgica, Haití y España que intervinieran a favor del gobierno, y que los insurgentes se negaron a aceptar los términos ofrecidos y exigieron la capitulación inmediata de la ciudad. La nota de Nueva York aparece bajo el titular «Story of Bombardment».

records.headline: The Democrat prints a San Domingo dispatch and a Washington item of November 23:
records.summary_en: The Democrat prints a San Domingo dispatch and a Washington item of November 23: President Woss y Gil requested the ministers of the United States, Belgium, Haiti and Spain to intervene in behalf of the government; the insurgents refused to accept the terms offered and demanded the immediate capitulation of the city; United States Minister Powell informed the revolutionary chiefs that periodical revolutions ought to cease, because they interrupted commercial relations with other countries and augmented the debt of Santo Domingo, which was without means to pay foreign creditors; the minister said further that these periodical revolutions endanger the peace of his government and of the governments of other nations and that the present revolution, if continued, would imperil the sovereignty of Santo Domingo; it is said that the tide of revolution will once again cast Don Isidro Jiminez into the presidential chair of the Dominican republic, and he will thus find himself for the third time ruler of that turbulent little country. The Washington item says revolutionary success in Santo Domingo may unpleasantly involve the United States, and there is a possibility that this government will have to adopt a strong policy to obtain respect for American property interests in the Dominican republic, which may mean intervention by the Washington government for the purpose of bringing order and stable government out of revolutionary chaos and constant danger to foreign interests.
records.summary_es: El Democrat publica un despacho de San Domingo y una nota de Washington del 23 de noviembre: el presidente Woss y Gil pidió a los ministros de los Estados Unidos, Bélgica, Haití y España que intervinieran a favor del gobierno; los insurgentes se negaron a aceptar los términos ofrecidos y exigieron la capitulación inmediata de la ciudad; el ministro estadounidense Powell informó a los jefes revolucionarios que las revoluciones periódicas deben cesar, porque interrumpían las relaciones comerciales con otros países y aumentaban la deuda de Santo Domingo, que no tenía medios para pagar a los acreedores extranjeros; el ministro dijo además que estas revoluciones periódicas ponen en peligro la paz de su gobierno y de los gobiernos de otras naciones y que la revolución actual, si continúa, pondría en peligro la soberanía de Santo Domingo; se dice que la marea de la revolución lanzará una vez más a don Isidro Jiménez a la silla presidencial de la república dominicana, y así se encontrará por tercera vez como gobernante de ese turbulento y pequeño país. La nota de Washington dice que el éxito revolucionario en Santo Domingo puede involucrar desagradablemente a los Estados Unidos, y existe la posibilidad de que este gobierno tenga que adoptar una política enérgica para obtener respeto para los intereses de propiedad estadounidenses en la república dominicana, lo que puede significar la intervención del gobierno de Washington con el propósito de traer orden y un gobierno estable del caos revolucionario y el constante peligro para los intereses extranjeros.

records.headline: The Inquirer prints a Puerto Plata dispatch of November 25:
records.summary_en: The Inquirer prints a Puerto Plata dispatch of November 25: the city of Santo Domingo, capital of this republic, has capitulated to the revolutionary forces; salutes of twenty-one guns each were fired throughout the country, and there was great rejoicing over the triumph of the revolution; the defeated President Woss y Gil, accompanied by his cabinet, sought refuge on a German warship; this time the tide of revolution will once again cast Don Isidro Jiminez into the presidential chair of the Dominican republic, and he will find himself for the third time ruler of the turbulent little country; General Jiminez belongs to a family distinguished in the West Indies as fighters, revolutionists and politicians. The dispatch appears under the head 'Wos y Gil Deposed'.
records.summary_es: El Inquirer publica un despacho de Puerto Plata del 25 de noviembre: la ciudad de Santo Domingo, capital de esta república, ha capitulado ante las fuerzas revolucionarias; se dispararon salvas de veintiún cañonazos en todo el país, y hubo gran regocijo por el triunfo de la revolución; el derrotado presidente Woss y Gil, acompañado por su gabinete, buscó refugio en un buque de guerra alemán; esta vez la marea de la revolución lanzará una vez más a don Isidro Jiménez a la silla presidencial de la república dominicana, y se encontrará por tercera vez como gobernante del turbulento y pequeño país; el general Jiménez pertenece a una familia distinguida en las Indias Occidentales como luchadores, revolucionarios y políticos. El despacho aparece bajo el titular «Wos y Gil Deposed».

Chicago Murder Mystery Cleared Up.
Chicago, Nov. 25.—The mystery sur
rounding the holdup of the cashier's of
fice of the Chicago City railway last
August, during which .two of the em
ployees of the office were shot and
killed without warning, has been
cleared up by the confession of Gus
tave Marks, who has been arrested for
the murder of Detective John Quinn,
whom Marks shot down while trying to
escape arrest. Harvey Van Dine and
Peter Neidemier are named by Marks
as his accomplices in the car barn mur
ders. In all $2,250 was secured, and
Marks says the money was evenly di
vided between the three men.

records.summary_en: The Union prints a Cape Haytien dispatch of November 25 and a Washington item of November 25: dispatches received at Cape Haytien from Puerto Plata say that the city of San Domingo was surrendered to the revolutionists Tuesday morning and that President Woss y Gil and his ministers took refuge on board a German warship, and the dispatches further say that great enthusiasm prevailed throughout the country; in a cablegram received at Washington from Minister Powell, dated Santo Domingo, November 23, he announces that the president of San Domingo has agreed to surrender the city to the revolutionists, and that the articles of capitulation are being drawn up.

records.headline: The Democrat prints the closing part of an item on the fall of the government:
records.summary_en: The Democrat prints the closing part of an item on the fall of the government: the capture by the insurgents under General Jiminez of Santo Domingo, the capital of the Dominican republic, resulting in the fall of President Woss y Gil, is of the greatest importance to the United States; a few weeks ago the insurgents informed this government, and also notified Charge d'Affaires Powell, that they would not recognize agreements thereafter made by the de jure authority of the republic; subsequently Mr. Powell made an arrangement with President Woss y Gil's administration to submit to arbitration the long pending claim of the Santo Domingo Improvement company, and at the time of Woss y Gil's overthrow Mr. Powell was pressing for a settlement of other American claims; and this government will not permit the new authority in Santo Domingo to repudiate arrangements made with the Woss y Gil government, but will insist that these arrangements be carried out.

records.headline: The Press prints part of a feature on Santo Domingo's presidents
records.summary_en: The Press prints part of a feature on Santo Domingo's presidents: General Horatio Vasquez was at the head of the provisional government in Santo Domingo, and after the assassination of Ulysses Heureaux held the reins of government until General Jiminez should be able to break loose from the American entanglements in Cuba and reach Santo Domingo; when Jiminez was detained, Vasquez concluded that it was a good time for him to be president, and intimated that the American government would hold Jiminez indefinitely and that the people had better go ahead and make him president, an overture that was not favorably received, so that Vasquez did not become president at that time; Jiminez was received with acclaim, the country being without a president and in much need of one, and the revolution was peaceful and successful apparently; Vasquez, for his able services, was made vice president of the republic, which required his presence at the capital most of the time and apparently prevented any tendency he might have to get up a revolution on his own account, but the theory did not work well in practice; and Jiminez was duly elected for a four years' term, but at the end of two years Vasquez succeeded in organizing a successful revolution, and Jiminez was compelled to flee to New York.

records.headline: The Press prints part of a feature on Samana bay in the West Indies:
records.summary_en: The Press prints part of a feature on Samana bay in the West Indies: the bay, one of the fine and valuable bays in the West Indies, thirty-one miles long, lies at the eastern extremity of the island, just across from Porto Rico; for almost one hundred years the United States has sought possession of this bay as a strategic point in the Caribbean sea; General Jackson first recommended the purchase in a message to Congress, President Buchanan made two or three recommendations, and Presidents Lincoln and Johnson followed with like suggestions; able engineers were sent to report on the waters and various conditions, and the project finally culminated in President Grant's open effort to secure the bay for the United States, which was defeated by Sumner in the famous and bitter fight along about 1871; the report of the commission sent to Santo Domingo at that time is an elaborate and interesting document, and while no President has openly taken any stand since Grant's day the statesmen have all recognized the value of the possession, and it is an open secret in Washington that negotiations have been opened several times through the State Department for the purchase of the bay; the failure of the project was something General Grant never forgot, it was the most bitter defeat he ever received, and every message, including his last, referred to the mistake which had been made in not acquiring the bay of Samana; and under the head 'Efforts of the Powers' the feature adds that rumor reaches this country occasionally of the attempted purchase of ports in Hayti and Santo Domingo by European powers.

records.summary_en: In an interview, deposed President Alejandro Wos y Gil says the future of the Dominican Republic hinges on recognition of the protocol signed by the Vásquez government with Minister Powell, which demands arbitration of differences between Santo Domingo and the United States. He says President Roosevelt agreed he could accept no other arbitrator than his appointee, Señor Galván, now in Washington, and when asked if he was urging a United States protectorate, he put a finger to his lips and waved his hand, indicating the rumor about Galván's mission was true.
records.summary_es: En una entrevista, el depuesto presidente Alejandro Wos y Gil dice que el futuro de la República Dominicana depende del reconocimiento del protocolo firmado por el gobierno de Vásquez con el ministro Powell, que exige el arbitraje de las diferencias entre Santo Domingo y los Estados Unidos. Afirma que el presidente Roosevelt acordó que no podría aceptar otro árbitro que su designado, el señor Galván, ahora en Washington, y al ser preguntado si procuraba un protectorado estadounidense, se llevó un dedo a los labios y agitó la mano, dando a entender que el rumor sobre la misión de Galván era cierto.

"The future state of the Dominican republic hinges upon the recognition of the protocol signed by the Vasquez government with Minister Powell. This protocol demands the arbitration of certain differences between Santo Domingo and the United States. In accordance with President Roosevelt's agreement with me, personally signed by the President and received In Santo Domingo, Mr. Roosevelt cannot accept any other arbitrator than mine. records.headline: The Press prints a San Juan item of November 29: Woss y Gil arrived
records.summary_en: The Press prints a San Juan item of November 29: Woss y Gil arrived there last night on the German cruiser Falke, which started at daylight this morning on her return to San Domingo; in an interview with a representative of the Associated Press the general said that no significance attaches to the fact of his traveling on the cruiser Falke, that United States Minister Powell had offered him passage on the gunboat Newport to New Orleans or Kingston, Jamaica, but he preferred to come to San Juan, and the German officials kindly offered him transportation; regarding the overthrow of his government, he said it was due to the impatience of the people, and that with his respect for the constitution this impatience caused the revolution; if the new government starts constitutionally his people will agree with it, and if not they will try evolution rather than revolution; he had the chair through peace and does not want it through war, which is demoralizing to the country; and the future state of the Dominican republic hinges upon the recognition of the protocol signed by the Vasquez government with Minister Powell; the item appears under the head 'Wos y Gil at San Juan'.
records.summary_es: The Press publica una nota de San Juan del 29 de noviembre: Woss y Gil llegó allí anoche a bordo del crucero alemán Falke, que partió al amanecer de esta mañana de regreso a San Domingo; en una entrevista con un representante de la Associated Press el general dijo que no se atribuye importancia alguna al hecho de que viajara en el crucero Falke, que el ministro de los Estados Unidos, Powell, le había ofrecido pasaje en la cañonera Newport a Nueva Orleans o a Kingston, Jamaica, pero que él prefirió venir a San Juan, y que los funcionarios alemanes amablemente le ofrecieron el transporte; en cuanto al derrocamiento de su gobierno, dijo que se debió a la impaciencia del pueblo, y que con su respeto a la constitución esa impaciencia causó la revolución; si el nuevo gobierno comienza constitucionalmente, su pueblo estará de acuerdo con él, y si no, intentarán la evolución en vez de la revolución; ocupó la silla por la paz y no la quiere por la guerra, que es desmoralizadora para el país; y el estado futuro de la República Dominicana depende del reconocimiento del protocolo firmado por el gobierno de Vásquez con el ministro Powell; la nota aparece bajo el título «Wos y Gil at San Juan».

records.headline: The Star prints part of a Washington item on the arbitration of the claims of the San Domingo Improvement Company
records.summary_en: The Star prints part of a Washington item on the arbitration of the claims of the San Domingo Improvement Company against the Dominican republic, which was arranged for by ex-President Woss y Gil as one of the last of his official acts: Senor Galvan, secretary of finance under the Woss y Gil administration, was named as the Dominican representative in the arbitration, and the United States and San Domingo united in the selection of Judge George Gray as the umpire; it is stated that the State Department will support Minister Powell in his refusal to yield to the desire of the Dominican provisional government that the personnel of the arbitrators be changed so as to eliminate Senor Galvan; the State Department has been informed that already a new revolutionary movement has begun in San Domingo, even before the provisional government that ousted Woss y Gil has been able to solidify into a permanent government, and these repeated uprisings, in the face of Minister Powell's warning, have concentrated the attention of the Washington authorities upon the island, where much American capital is invested, and there may be a renewal in a more forcible manner of Minister Powell's declaration that the interests of the United States are not to be troubled in that fashion; and the arbitration commission held its first meeting today in the hearing room of the Interstate Commerce Commission, those present being Judge Gray, former Secretary Carlisle, Senor Galvan and John Bassett Moore, formerly assistant secretary of state.

records.headline: The Journal prints a Washington item on the United States and San Domingo:
records.summary_en: The Journal prints a Washington item on the United States and San Domingo: the State Department entertains absolutely no thought of establishing a protectorate over San Domingo or of annexing it; American interference in the island's affairs will be limited to the protection of American interests there, and while the frequent revolutions in the little republic are very much deplored by the administration, the Washington government will not meddle with the political conditions of San Domingo, but will simply see to it that existing engagements as to arbitration and concessions to Americans are conserved, and that American trade is not improperly obstructed; it is learned from trustworthy sources that Woss y Gil, the deposed president, is now on his way to the United States and is expected to land at New Orleans to-day or to-morrow, and that he will come to Washington and will see Senor Galvan, who expects to be in Washington again within the next ten days; and under the head 'Three Revolutions' the item adds that advices reached Washington that there are now three revolutions in San Domingo, the revolution led by Morales, a revolution at Monte Cristi led by the followers of Jiminez, and a third and stronger revolution in the south of the island, and that Morales has secured control by an appeal to the Dominicans that the United States intends to annex the island, and has received many courtesies from European representatives in the island, who are also opposed to a step by the United States in the direction of asserting the supremacy of its interests in the island.
records.summary_es: El Journal publica una nota de Washington sobre los Estados Unidos y San Domingo: el Departamento de Estado no abriga en absoluto la idea de establecer un protectorado sobre San Domingo ni de anexarlo; la injerencia norteamericana en los asuntos de la isla se limitará a la protección de los intereses norteamericanos allí, y aunque las frecuentes revoluciones de la pequeña república son muy deploradas por la administración, el gobierno de Washington no se inmiscuirá en las condiciones políticas de San Domingo, sino que simplemente velará por que se conserven los compromisos existentes en cuanto a arbitraje y concesiones a norteamericanos, y por que el comercio norteamericano no sea indebidamente obstruido; se sabe por fuentes fidedignas que Woss y Gil, el presidente depuesto, viene ahora hacia los Estados Unidos y se espera que desembarque en Nueva Orleans hoy o mañana, y que vendrá a Washington y verá al señor Galván, que espera estar de nuevo en Washington dentro de los próximos diez días; y bajo el título «Three Revolutions» la nota añade que llegaron a Washington avisos de que ahora hay tres revoluciones en San Domingo, la revolución acaudillada por Morales, una revolución en Monte Cristi acaudillada por los partidarios de Jiménez, y una tercera y más fuerte revolución en el sur de la isla, y que Morales ha logrado el control mediante un llamamiento a los dominicanos de que los Estados Unidos intentan anexar la isla, y ha recibido muchas cortesías de los representantes europeos en la isla, que también se oponen a un paso de los Estados Unidos en el sentido de afirmar la supremacía de sus intereses en la isla.

records.summary_en: The Star prints a Washington item on the protectorate question: it is stated that the State Department entertains absolutely no thought of establishing a protectorate over San Domingo or of annexing it; American interference in the island's affairs will be limited to the protection of American interests there, and while the frequent revolutions in the little republic are very much deplored by the administration, the Washington government will not meddle with the political conditions of San Domingo, but will simply see to it that existing engagements as to arbitrations and concessions to Americans are observed, and that American trade is not improperly obstructed; under the head 'Wos y Gil on His Way Here' the item adds that Woss y Gil, the deposed president, is now on his way to the United States and is expected to land at New Orleans today or tomorrow, and that he will come to Washington and consult with Senor Galvan, who expects to be in Washington again within the next ten days; advices reached Washington that there are now three revolutions in San Domingo, the revolution led by Morales, a revolution at Monte Cristi led by the followers of Jiminez, and a third and stronger revolution in the south of the island; it appears that Morales has obtained control by declaring to the Dominicans that the United States intends to annex the island, and it is also said that Morales has received many courtesies from European representatives in the island.
records.summary_es: The Star publica una nota de Washington sobre la cuestión del protectorado: se afirma que el Departamento de Estado no abriga en absoluto la idea de establecer un protectorado sobre San Domingo ni de anexarlo; la injerencia norteamericana en los asuntos de la isla se limitará a la protección de los intereses norteamericanos allí, y aunque las frecuentes revoluciones de la pequeña república son muy deploradas por la administración, el gobierno de Washington no se inmiscuirá en las condiciones políticas de San Domingo, sino que simplemente velará por que se observen los compromisos existentes en cuanto a arbitrajes y concesiones a norteamericanos, y por que el comercio norteamericano no sea indebidamente obstruido; bajo el título «Wos y Gil on His Way Here» la nota añade que Woss y Gil, el presidente depuesto, viene ahora hacia los Estados Unidos y se espera que desembarque en Nueva Orleans hoy o mañana, y que vendrá a Washington y consultará con el señor Galván, que espera estar de nuevo en Washington dentro de los próximos diez días; llegaron a Washington avisos de que ahora hay tres revoluciones en San Domingo, la revolución acaudillada por Morales, una revolución en Monte Cristi acaudillada por los partidarios de Jiménez, y una tercera y más fuerte revolución en el sur de la isla; parece que Morales ha obtenido el control declarando a los dominicanos que los Estados Unidos intentan anexar la isla, y se dice también que Morales ha recibido muchas cortesías de los representantes europeos en la isla.

records.headline: The News prints the closing part of the Washington item on the San Domingo Improvement Company arbitration:
records.summary_en: The News prints the closing part of the Washington item on the San Domingo Improvement Company arbitration: Senor Galvan, secretary of finance under the Woss y Gil administration, was named as the Dominican representative in the arbitration, and the United States and San Domingo united in the selection of Judge George Gray as the umpire; the State Department will support Minister Powell in his refusal to yield to the desire of the Dominican provisional government that the personnel of the arbitrators be changed so as to eliminate Senor Galvan; the State Department has been informed that already a new revolutionary movement has begun in San Domingo, even before the provisional government that ousted Woss y Gil has been able to solidify itself into a permanent government, and these repeated uprisings, in the face of Minister Powell's warnings, have concentrated the attention of the Washington authorities upon the island, where much American capital is invested, and there may be a renewal in a more forcible manner of Minister Powell's declaration that the peace of the United States is not to be troubled in this fashion; and the arbitration commission held a brief session to-day.

SAN JOSE, Dec. 4.— By the will of
Mrs. Louisa M. Ehrhorn, a pioneer
woman of this State, the King's Daugh
ters' Home for Incurables at San Fran
cisco and the Episcopal Board of Dio
cesan Missions will each receive $500.
Mrs. Ehrhorn died at Mountain View
on November 22, leaving an estate
valued at $62,000. She was the widow
of Adolphus EhFhorn, a pioneer mer
chant of San Francisco. Mrs. Ehrhorn
came to California In 1852 from Peru
and resided in San Francisco till 1873,
when she removed to Mountain View.
A petition for probating the will was
filed to-day by E. M. and G. H. Ehr
horn, sons, who are named as execu
tors. The estate consists of forty-eight
acres of bearing orchard and a home
and forty acres of unimproved land at
Mountain View valued at $30,000 and
532,000 worth of personal property.

records.summary_en: The Pioneer prints the closing part of a Santo Domingo item and a Washington item of December 4: the first says that Minister Powell declined to grant a demand concerning the board appointed by the government of President Woss y Gil to arbitrate the claims of the Santo Domingo Improvement company, and supplemented his declination by the statement that the United States government could only recognize the provisional government of Santo Domingo when it agreed to strictly observe all the acts and engagements entered into by former governments with the United States; the Washington item says it is learned that John G. Carlisle has been named as a representative of the United States in the arbitration of the claims of the San Domingo Improvement company against the Dominican republic, which was arranged for by former President Woss y Gil as one of the last of his official acts, that Senor Galvan, secretary of finance under the Woss y Gil administration, was named as the Dominican representative in the arbitration, and that the United States and San Domingo united in the selection of Judge George Gray as the umpire; the State Department will support Minister Powell in his refusal to yield to the desire of the Dominican provisional government that the personnel of the arbitrators be changed so as to eliminate Senor Galvan; and the State Department has been informed that already a new revolutionary movement has begun in San Domingo, even before the provisional government that ousted Woss y Gil has been able to solidify itself into a permanent government.

records.headline: The Northwestern prints the closing part of the Washington item
records.summary_en: The Northwestern prints the closing part of the Washington item on San Domingo and a San Domingo item on recognition: the president is now on his way to the United States and is expected to land at New Orleans today or tomorrow, and he will come to Washington; advices reached Washington that there are now three revolutions in San Domingo, the revolution led by Morales, a revolution at Monte Cristo led by the followers of Jiminez, and a third and stronger revolution in the south of the island, and that Morales has secured control by an appeal to the Dominicans that the United States intends to annex the island, and has received many courtesies from European representatives in the island, who are also opposed to a step by the United States in the direction of asserting the supremacy of its interests in the island; the San Domingo item says the provisional government has made an official request for recognition to the diplomatic and consular bodies, and gives United States Minister Powell's conditions on which the United States will recognize the new government: the government must agree to abide by and respect the agreements made by the preceding administrations, must recognize the manner of settlement arrived at in the case of the Santo Domingo Improvement company of New York and the Ros and Sala cases, must recognize and carry into full effect the concession to the steamship company, and must grant the privilege to the United States to establish at dangerous points on the coast lighthouses to aid maritime commerce.
records.summary_es: El Northwestern publica la parte final de la nota de Washington sobre San Domingo y una nota de San Domingo sobre el reconocimiento: el presidente viene ahora hacia los Estados Unidos y se espera que desembarque en Nueva Orleans hoy o mañana, y vendrá a Washington; llegaron a Washington avisos de que ahora hay tres revoluciones en San Domingo, la revolución acaudillada por Morales, una revolución en Monte Cristo acaudillada por los partidarios de Jiménez, y una tercera y más fuerte revolución en el sur de la isla, y que Morales ha logrado el control mediante un llamamiento a los dominicanos de que los Estados Unidos intentan anexar la isla, y ha recibido muchas cortesías de los representantes europeos en la isla, que también se oponen a un paso de los Estados Unidos en el sentido de afirmar la supremacía de sus intereses en la isla; la nota de San Domingo dice que el gobierno provisional ha hecho una solicitud oficial de reconocimiento a los cuerpos diplomáticos y consulares, y da las condiciones del ministro de los Estados Unidos, Powell, bajo las cuales los Estados Unidos reconocerán al nuevo gobierno: el gobierno debe convenir en acatar y respetar los acuerdos hechos por las administraciones precedentes, debe reconocer la manera de arreglo alcanzada en el caso de la Santo Domingo Improvement Company de Nueva York y en los casos de Ros y Sala, debe reconocer y llevar a pleno efecto la concesión a la compañía de vapores, y debe conceder a los Estados Unidos el privilegio de establecer faros en los puntos peligrosos de la costa para auxiliar al comercio marítimo.

records.headline: Plot against Powell: a letter from an official of the present Dominican government discloses a Woss y Gil party
records.summary_en: Plot against Powell: a letter from an official of the present Dominican government discloses a Woss y Gil party scheme to assassinate Minister Powell in a staged street fight - and President Jiménez by plain assassination, two attempts on him having already failed; the Powell plot was abandoned, but he is carefully guarded.
records.summary_es: Complot contra Powell: una carta de un funcionario del actual gobierno dominicano revela un plan del partido de Woss y Gil para asesinar al ministro Powell en una pelea callejera fingida - y al presidente Jiménez por asesinato directo, con dos atentados ya fallidos contra él; el complot contra Powell fue abandonado, pero se le custodia con cuidado.
records.passage: PLOT AGAINST POWELL. Wos y Gil Party Plans to Assassinate U. S. Minister. New York, Dec. 15. An alleged plot to assassinate William F. Powell, United States minister to Hayti and charge d'affaires at Port-au-Prince, Santo Domingo, has been disclosed in a communication from an official of the present Dominican government to a fellow countryman in this city, who formerly was an official under Wos y Gil, the recently deposed president of the republic. The letter states that the plot had been so arranged that ex-President Jiminez, under whose leadership Wos y Gil was overthrown, was to have been killed at about the same time. The plot to assassinate Minister Powell, it was asserted, was conceived because of his opposition to plans of certain officials. The plan as reported was to let two or three men get into a fight on a street along which Mr. Powell was passing. It was arranged that in the melee other plotters should engage, and it would be an easy matter to kill the American "by accident." With regard to Jiminez, the writer asserts that he was to be the victim of plain assassination and that already two unsuccessful attacks have been made upon his person. records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that the besieged Dominican provisional government was unable to raise a $20,000 loan for city defense, leaving the capital vulnerable to insurgent assault and street fighting. With the gunboat *Newport* remaining as the only foreign warship in port, concerns grew over the safety of foreign residents. Meanwhile, insurgent leader Juan Isidro Jimenes scored a decisive victory at Moca against 500 government troops under General Ramón Cáceres, who was wounded, clearing the path for an advance on Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported that the State Department withheld diplomatic recognition from Dominican factions despite claims by General Jimenes's followers that they controlled nearly the entire country outside the capital. United States officials observed that three rival governing authorities were contending for power simultaneously, leaving policy implementation to Minister Powell's judgment. Funcionarios de los Estados Unidos observaron que tres autoridades de gobierno rivales se disputaban el poder de forma simultánea, dejando la ejecución de la política al criterio del ministro Powell. Chicago, Jan. 21. — As the result of a storm train service on the South Side elevated road was paralyzed for nearly two hours during the day, endangering life and discommoding hundreds of passengers. Rain soaking the wood superstructure of the road caused the moisture to communicate to a defective third rail support near a network of switches. The electric current deserted the car motors and flowed through the ironwork of the structure to the ground. The entire structure for a considerable distance was electrified and menaced the safety of horses and men below, until the current was shut off at the powerhouse. Trains on the road were crowded. Passengers on the stalled trains, after waiting for some time for signs of life in the motors, took surface lines and reached their work downtown after long delay.
