records.headline: And it sticks its tongue in its cheek and looks at
records.summary_en: The *Washington daily news* published an editorial criticizing American assertions of non-imperialism, pointing to U.S. control across the Caribbean and Pacific, including customs administration in the Dominican Republic and marine occupation in Haiti. The piece derided official claims of purely benevolent motives while exercising regional dominance. It argued that Washington's treatment of its dependencies, particularly the curtailment of self-rule in the Philippines under General Leonard Wood, contradicted its anti-imperialist rhetoric.
records.summary_es: El *Washington daily news* publicó un editorial en el que criticaba las afirmaciones estadounidenses de no ejercer imperialismo, señalando el control de Estados Unidos en el Caribe y el Pacífico, incluida la administración de aduanas en la República Dominicana y la ocupación de la infantería de marina en Haití. El artículo ridiculizó los argumentos oficiales de motivaciones puramente benévolas mientras se ejercía el dominio regional. Sostuvo que el trato que Washington daba a sus dependencias, en particular el menoscabo de la autonomía en Filipinas bajo el general Leonard Wood, contradecía su retórica antiimperialista.
records.passage: "You say you are not imperialistic," it jeers. And it sticks its tongue in its cheek and looks at the Philippines and Porto Rico and Hawaii and Guam and the Virgin Islands; at our virtual protectorate over Cuba and the Republic of Panama; at our control of the customs of the Dominican Republic and Haiti, and our occupation of the latter country by marines; at our hegemony, as they call it, over Central and much of South America. And reviewing it all, it asks insinuatingly: "What are you up to in all those places?" "Just protecting the interests of the unfortunate peoples," we say. "Oh!" says the world, winking prodigiously! WELL, a showdown is approaching. The Philippines may well be the test case. And the case of the Philippines is this: Congress officially promised the Filipinos their freedom as soon as they proved they could govern themselves. Gov. Gen. Harrison from 1916 to 1921 gave them a chance, and they did a pretty good job. And President Wilson in 1920 told Congress the time had about come for America to make good her promise. Then bang! records.summary_en: The *Evening star* reported official statements declaring that the United States did not seek permanent dominion over Santo Domingo, but was actively preparing to evacuate its forces following free elections scheduled for mid-September. The statement explained that American policy in Haiti similarly aimed only to establish stability and competent self-governance following decades of revolution. U.S. authorities emphasized that they harbored no territorial ambitions on the island and would welcome the day American troops could safely withdraw.

El pronunciamiento explicaba que la política estadounidense en Haití aspiraba igualmente a restablecer la estabilidad y un gobierno autónomo competente tras décadas de revoluciones. Las autoridades de Washington hicieron hincapié en que carecían de ambiciones territoriales en la isla y celebrarían el momento en que los efectivos estadounidenses pudieran retirarse de forma segura.

records.summary_en: The *Ventnor news* published a first-hand travel narrative praising the stabilization of Santo Domingo under the U.S. Marine Corps, highlighting administrative order and revenue collection. The author described motoring two hundred miles from Monte Cristi through Santiago to Santo Domingo City over modern mountain highways recently constructed by American military engineers. The account commended the marines for modernizing infrastructure, civilizing the region, and establishing public safety.
records.summary_es: El *Ventnor news* publicó una crónica de viaje testimonial que elogiaba la estabilización de Santo Domingo bajo el Cuerpo de Marines de Estados Unidos, destacando el orden administrativo y la recaudación fiscal. El autor describió su trayecto en automóvil de doscientas millas desde Monte Cristi pasando por Santiago hasta la ciudad de Santo Domingo a través de modernas carreteras de montaña recién construidas por ingenieros militares estadounidenses. El relato alabó a los marines por modernizar la infraestructura, pacificar la región y establecer la seguridad pública.

records.summary_en: The *Evening star* assessed the outlook for stability in Santo Domingo following the evacuation of American troops, noting general agreement that the nation deserved its opportunity for independent self-government. The article reviewed the background of intervention, recalling that the 1916 marine occupation followed decades of civil strife and the 1905 crisis when foreign creditors threatened naval force over unpaid debts. It described how the United States helped arrange a $20,000,000 refunding loan backed by an American receiver-general collecting customs to make monthly debt payments.
records.summary_es: El *Evening star* evaluó las perspectivas de estabilidad en Santo Domingo tras la evacuación de las tropas estadounidenses, destacando el consenso general de que la nación merecía su oportunidad de autogobierno independiente. El artículo recapituló los antecedentes de la intervención, recordando que la ocupación de los marines en 1916 siguió a decenios de contiendas civiles y a la crisis de 1905, cuando acreedores extranjeros amenazaron con recurrir a la fuerza naval por deudas impagas. Describió cómo Estados Unidos facilitó la gestión de un empréstito de refinanciamiento de 20 000 000 de dólares respaldado por un receptor general estadounidense encargado de recaudar las rentas aduaneras para efectuar pagos mensuales de la deuda.

There are some familiar with the West Indies who feel a good deal of doubt on this question. But all agree that Santo Domingo should have its trial at domestic tranquillity — its chance to make good as an independent, responsible nation. When United States marines were landed on the island in 1916 it was to restore order out of a political and economic chaos that had lasted for many long years. As early as 1905 repeated revolutions had left the affairs of the Dominican government in such a hopeless state that the United States was compelled to come to its assistance in order to preserve the Monroe doctrine. A large group of foreign creditors, each ready to present his bill with a gunboat, clouded the horizon. Another large group of native creditors, each planning to enforce his claims against the government by insurrection, agitated the country's interior. Clearly something had to be done to reestablish Dominican credit, and the United States did it. Through its offices the republic was enabled to secure a loan of $20,000,000 with which to refund its foreign debts. records.summary_en: The paper recounted a struggle of more than eight years by the people of Santo Domingo to regain the sovereignty they contended was taken from them when the United States placed the country under a large military force and set up a military government. After repeated Dominican efforts for a withdrawal, former American minister Horace G. Knowles started a campaign in 1920 to secure sovereignty for the Dominicans, and a United States Senate committee then inquired into the occupation in Santo Domingo, which was followed by an agreement for withdrawal of the forces. Sovereignty was restored and an election was held on March 15, with General Vasquez elected President, while about 1,800 marines remained in Santo Domingo and transports had begun evacuating the troops.

La soberanía fue restablecida y se celebraron elecciones el 15 de marzo, en las que resultó electo presidente el general Vásquez, mientras unos 1.800 infantes de marina permanecían aún en Santo Domingo y los transportes habían comenzado a evacuar a las tropas.

records.full_text:
The Day in Washington

The house passed a bill to promote production and conservation of helium.

A bill for a new American embassy and consulate general in Tokio passed the house.

The senate rejected a proposal to withhold funds to maintain marines in Haiti.

A senate elections sub-committee recommended the seating of Senator Mayfield, democrat, Texas.

The senate called on Secretary Hughes for information on the Paris reparations agreement.

Heber H. Votaw, brother-in-law of the late President Harding resigned as superintendent of prisons.

The naval bill, containing a request that President Coolidge call an arms conference, passed the senate.

Members of the senate foreign relations committee and others were invited to a night dinner at the White House.

The senate ratified treaties with the Dominican republic on evacuation of American troops and refunding of the Dominican debt.

Senator Shipstead, farmer-labor, Minnesota, charged the increased prices for stocks and bonds were the result of a “stock gambling boom.”

Senator McKellar, democrat, Tennessee, presented a resolution asking President Coolidge to investigate whether England violated the arms treaty in building the battleships Rodney and Nelson.

Justice department took steps to subpoena Senator Wheeler, democrat, Montana, to appear before a grand jury here in connection with the home state indictment against him.

records.summary_en: The *Omaha morning bee* reported details of the treaty ratified by the U.S. Senate refunding the Dominican national debt of $25,000,000. The pact authorized the U.S. president to appoint a general receiver to collect all Dominican customs duties, applying proceeds to receivership expenses, interest, and sinking fund amortization before remitting any surplus to the Dominican government. Under an additional article, the Dominican Republic was prohibited from increasing its public debt without American consent until all refunding bonds were fully paid.
records.summary_es: El *Omaha morning bee* reportó detalles del tratado ratificado por el Senado de Estados Unidos para el refinanciamiento de la deuda nacional dominicana por 25 000 000 de dólares. El pacto autorizaba al presidente estadounidense a nombrar un receptor general para recaudar todos los derechos aduaneros dominicanos, aplicando lo recaudado a los gastos de la receptoría, intereses y amortización del fondo de amortización antes de transferir cualquier remanente al gobierno dominicano. Conforme a un artículo adicional, se prohibía a la República Dominicana aumentar su deuda pública sin consentimiento estadounidense hasta que la totalidad de los bonos de refinanciamiento quedara saldada.
records.passage: the refunding of the Dominican debt totaling $25,900,000. Under the terms of the refunding treaty, the president of the United States will appoint a general receiver of Dominican customs to collect all customs duties in the republic until the payment or retirement of all bonds issued for the refunding of its present obligations. The general receiver will apply the sum so collected first to the payment of expenses of the receivership; second, to payment of interest on all bonds outstanding; third to payment of the annual funds provided for amortization of these bonds, including interest upon all bonds held in the sinking fund and fourth, to purchase and cancellation or retirement and cancellation of any of the new issue of bonds as may be directed by the Dominican government. The remainder would be paid to the Dominican government. Under an additional article of the pact, the public debt of the Dominican republic could not be increased without consent of the United States until all bonds of the present debt have been paid. The report asserted that the occupation protected rural workers from forced military impressment and bandits, allowing them to farm and sell produce freely. It stated that peasants were better fed, clothed, and receiving medical treatment at free clinics, despite widespread illiteracy.

El reportaje afirmaba que la ocupación protegía a los trabajadores rurales del reclutamiento militar forzoso y de los bandoleros, permitiéndoles cultivar y vender sus productos libremente. Indicaba que los campesinos estaban mejor alimentados, mejor vestidos y recibían atención médica en dispensarios gratuitos, a pesar del analfabetismo generalizado.

Concurrently, the American military presence had been reduced to an 800-man marine force.

The department of public works is each year training a growing number of Haitian engineers, architects, artisans, office executives, hydrographic aids, steam gauge readers, telephone and telegraph operators and inspectors. The sanitary service is turning out Haitian physicians, surgeons, nurses, dentists, pharmacists and sanitary inspectors. Practically all the force of the financial adviser and general receiver of customs is purely Haitian. The recently formed office of the chief agricultural engineer is enrolling and training a Haitian personnel. In the ranks of the Haitian gendarmerie there are now approximately 60 Haitians of the best type who are either commissioned, acting or aspirant officers, or practically one-half of its commissioned strength. All these departments are organized into departments with district and subdistrict divisions, so that throughout Haiti the native Haitian is working shoulder to shoulder with Americans in the rehabilitation of the country. It produces for export coffee, sugar, cotton, logwood, and [cacao?]. It is the most fertile island in the West Indies. From the year 1910 to the year 1915, Haiti had seven revolutions, and seven presidents occupied uneasy thrones in that country. The last of the seven, Gen. Sam, was inaugurated March 4, 1915. He lasted until July 26, of that year. That day he took refuge in the French legation, and on that date, 200 political prisoners were massacred in the jail. The funeral services were being held, and the temper of the crowd was so dangerous, that they dragged President Sam out and killed him. Two hours after President Sam had passed, a United States cruiser entered the harbor of Port au Prince and landed marines and restored order. In 1916, a treaty between the United States and Haiti was ratified. By the terms of that treaty, the United States undertook a political and fiscal protectorate for a period of twenty years. Since then Haiti has known a measure of peace and prosperity. At this time there seem to be no danger of revolutions. Last October, there were 800 marines in Haiti with an armed constabulary of 2688 men, and a reserve of 20,000 men. The United States as usual did a good job. records.summary_en: The *New Britain Herald* reported on extensive infrastructure modernization in Haiti under President Borno, including more than 1,000 miles of paved roads, new schools, hospitals, and lighthouses. A concrete highway connecting Port-au-Prince with Santo Domingo had reached the border on the Haitian side, promising to reduce travel time between the capitals from days to hours once the Dominican section was completed. The report also highlighted telephone network expansion, tariff revisions to promote trade with the United States, and the continuing presence of 800 American marines.
records.summary_es: El *New Britain Herald* informó sobre la vasta modernización de infraestructura en Haití bajo el presidente Borno, con más de 1 000 millas de carreteras pavimentadas, nuevas escuelas, hospitales y faros. Una carretera de hormigón que comunicaba Puerto Príncipe con Santo Domingo había alcanzado la frontera del lado haitiano, prometiendo reducir el tiempo de viaje entre ambas capitales de días a horas una vez concluido el tramo dominicano. El despacho destacó asimismo la ampliación de la red telefónica, modificaciones arancelarias para estimular el comercio con Estados Unidos y la continua presencia de 800 infantes de marina estadounidenses.
records.passage: In the last ten years, more than 1,000 miles of paved roads have been laid, replacing highways that had deteriorated until they were little more than trails. A concrete highway connecting Port-au-Prince, the Haitian Capital, and Santo Domingo, capital city of the Dominican Republic, has been completed by the Haitians up to the border. When the Dominican portion is completed, the trip between the two capitals may be done in hours, where formerly it took days. This progress has been particularly notable during the administration of the present chief executive, President Borno, said a report in the booklet made by the Haitian minister of public works. His administration also has seen the construction of fourteen schools, thirteen hospitals and eleven lighthouses; installation of an automatic telephone system, and material progress in irrigation and canals. Since 1921, there has been an increase of 350 per cent in the number of telephones in use and the telegraph system has been augmented and improved. In order to foster trade between the United States and Haiti, the present Haitian Import Customs Tariff is being revised. Some eight hundred American Marines still remain in Haiti, completing their work of reorganizing the native constabulary. records.full_text:
REPORT STATES BOSS OF HAITI FINDS ALL O. K.

By Louis R. Lautier

During the past year the American treaty officials have been directing their efforts toward increasing the productive wealth of Haiti to the ultimate end of strengthening and improving the general economic condition, Brig. Gen. John H. Russell, American High Commissioner to Haiti, declared in his fifth annual report to the Secretary of State, which was made public by the State Department Monday.

In addition, he reported, the Haitian Government and the treaty officials have continued the general governing program for the stablization of Haitian finances, the maintenance of law and order, the construction of public works, and the improvement of the public health service.

A bumper coffee crop in a period of exceptionally high and abnormal prices and the re-election

BOSS OF HAITI REPORTS EVERYTHING IS O. K.

(Continued from page 1)

of President Borno contributed to the stability and the prosperity of Haiti in 1926, General Russell stated.

Business Confidence
“Confidence among business men, which, on account of the usual sensational rumors which precede a presidential election in Haiti, had been trembling in the balance, was restored immediately upon the promulgation of the results of the election,” General Russell reports. “This fact contributed largely in making the past year the greatest in the history of the Republic from a financial and business point of view.”

As a result of the visit of President Borno to the United States in last June he returned to Haiti imbued with a stronger desire to further the progress and development of his country and to make it a republic in being as well as in name, General Russell states.

The Haitian judiciary system is in need of complete renovation. “The courts are, if such could be possible, less effective than ever and their inefficiency and incompetency more notorious,” General Russell reports. “Trials by jury are farcial.”

There has been no reduction in the United States forces in Haiti. They consist of a skeleton brigade of United States marines and a mine sweeper of 950 tons displacement. Martial law has only been exercised upon the rarest occasions, says General Russell.

The customs receipts for the past year were unprecedented. The total receipts amounted to $9,072,929.62. Of this amount the sum of $8,118,996.35 was from custom revenues.

The Public Debt
The actual debt reducing amortization was $1,384,836.90. The required reduction was only $717,218.36. The total public debt amounts to $18,849,000.

As a result of the favorable year just closed the Haitian people have been benefited materially, says General Russell. They are better fed, better clothed, and better housed than ever before.

The commerce of Haiti during the past year has been most satisfactory, it is reported. There has been a healthy growth of shipping entering the harbors of the Republic and a gradual increase in traffic across the Dominican border.

Educational Ideas
The Haitian Government believes that its educational system should be designed to furnish agricultural education to the rural and industrial education to the urban population, the American high commissioner states. He says that “the Haitian Government considers it not only essential but vital that the Haitian people be taught to use their hands.”

General Russell also states in his report:
“The efforts that have been made and are being made to foster the further increase of production in Haiti will soon show results and with the passing of an appropriate revenue law and the renovation of the Haitian judiciary, the advance toward the stabilization of government will be most marked.

“As in past years President Borno has co-operated in every way for the carrying out of the provisions of the treaty of 1915, and has made the marked improvement of last year possible.

“The treaty officials have consistently, tactfully and energetically carried out their duties and the efficient management of the respective departments under their control has largely contributed to the remarkable progress which is being made in the bringing of happiness and prosperity to the Haitian people.”

Statements Contradictory
Statements in the report of General Russell are contradictory to those made upon the floor of the Senate by Senator William H. King, Democrat, of Utah, who was recently barred by President Borno from visiting Haiti because of derogatory remarks made by the Senator concerning the Haitian president in demanding that the American forces be withdrawn from the island republic.

In a speech in the Senate on February 1 last, Senator King declared:
“First, let it be remembered that by every standard of morality and justice there was no treaty. Our forces were in possession of the country. We had destroyed the legislative branch of the government and taken possession of all governmental agencies of the country. We set up a shadow government. It was not a Haitian government. A few Haitians were put into positions, but they were named by Naval officers of the United States and they did the will of those who named them. One of them we called a President, and he was required to sign a treaty prepared by the United States.”

Senator King described the re-election of President Borno as a farce. This “shadow president,” he said, was chosen by members of an assembly which he had appointed. “The Haitian people,” he declared, “are in a condition of political servitude.”

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that U.S. Senator William H. King, upon returning from the Caribbean, denounced Haitian President Borno as a puppet of the State Department and High Commissioner General John H. Russell. King produced official correspondence showing that Borno's order barring him from Haiti was enforced through American military officers, arguing that U.S. claims of Haitian sovereignty were a subterfuge. The senator vowed to renew his fight in Congress to withdraw American marines, asserting that 89 percent of Haitians opposed the occupation.

King, a su regreso del Caribe, denunció al presidente haitiano Borno como un títere del Departamento de Estado y del alto comisionado, general John H. Russell. King presentó correspondencia oficial que demostraba que la orden de Borno de impedirle la entrada a Haití fue ejecutada por oficiales militares estadounidenses, argumentando que las afirmaciones de Washington sobre la soberanía haitiana eran un subterfugio. El senador prometió renovar su lucha en el Congreso para retirar a los infantes de marina, asegurando que el 89 por ciento de los haitianos se oponía a la ocupación.

S. [illegible], American officer in charge of the gendarmerie in Haiti, and copies of correspondence showing that the order to exclude him had been referred to Gen. "The attitude of the State Department," the Senator said, "regarding the exclusion incident indicates that it was an effort to keep alive the fiction of Haitien independence. It has served to focus the attention of Americans upon the domination by this Government of Haitien affairs. Subterfuge, He Says. "As for the State Department's instructions to Gen. Russell to use his good offices with President Borno to persuade him to allow me to enter Haiti, that was a mere subterfuge." Senator King said he would renew his fight to have American Marines withdrawn from Haiti; if the Haitiens were permitted to express themselves, he added, 89 per cent would demand the withdrawal of United States forces. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reviewed American newspaper editorials defending the U.S. military occupation of Haiti against domestic critics. Excerpts from the *Charlotte Observer*, *Savannah Press*, and *Wall Street Journal* credited American administrators under Commissioner Russell with establishing stability, building schools and roads, and ending a cycle of violent revolutions. These commentaries maintained that the Haitian population benefited from American oversight and desired its continuation.

Northampton, Nov. 20 — The policy of the government at Washington in practicing intervention on the countries of Nicaragua, Haiti, and Santo Domingo was severely criticised by Horace G. Knowles, former American minister to the Dominican republic and now consul for that country, speaking under the auspices of the Hampshire County Progressive club at Carnegie hall tonight. Mr. Knowles said that the policies and acts presented were not those of the American people, nor even of the American Congress, but of the American government, which notwithstanding the fact that only Congress can declare war, had committed acts of war in these republics by the landing of armed forces. records.passage: United States is sovereign in this hemisphere. In the closing passages of the address the President vaguely refers to an "international system" peculiar to this hemisphere, which imposes on each nation certain "obligations," "defined by laws which we recognize as binding on all of us." What "laws" there are of the character referred to no one may know, inasmuch as the Monroe doctrine, even with its corollaries stretched to their most extreme imperialistic implication, remains a policy of the United States like Great Britain's old claim to dominate the high seas. Ignoring the realistic bases of the policy of the United States since the Spanish war, the President found himself able to say with perfect gravity, "We are thoroughly committed to the principle that they (the Colombias, Costa Ricas, Haytis, Nicaraguas, Panamas, Dominican Republics and Cubas) are better fitted to govern themselves than anyone else is to govern them. It is better for the people to make their own mistakes than to have someone else make their mistakes for them." Why, then, do we not clear out of the Philippine islands? Even in Cuba, why do we insist on special rights of intervention? Why are our gallant marines put to such work as bombing Nicaraguan villages? There is reason to suspect that two Coolidges were struggling for expression in the Havana address. records.passage: By the Associated Press. SANTO DOMINGO, Dominican Republic, February 6. — Col. Charles A. Lindbergh, now nearing the end of his good will flight to the Pan American conference at Havana, took off for Port-au-Prince, Haiti, at 11 a.m., local time. The route to Port-au-Prince, 160 miles by airplane from here, led entirely across land, unless Lindbergh in his flight should venture across the inland waters of Lake Enriquillo and Lake Saumatre. The path of the lone eagle was over a country teeming with bird life, wild duck, flamingo, herons and other shore birds. The route passed over mountains and deep forests where voodooism was brought from Africa and practiced for many years. It led over a land where negro slaves by their own efforts freed themselves and set up a republic, of which Port-au-Prince is the capital. Haiti is the second country to be visited by Col. Lindbergh in his good will tour where American Marines are present. In Nicaragua he found them engaged in an active campaign against the rebel Gen. Sandino. In Haiti they are engaged in maintaining order until the new republic is considered capable of exercising in full its rights of sovereignty. Col. Lindbergh was kept busy until late last night. He was the guest of honor at a brilliant ball held at the presidential palace, which was decorated with flowers and lights. All the diplomatic body, members of the Government and prominent society figures attended. CITY WILL HONOR COSTES AND LEBRIX French Flyers, Due Here Tomorrow

records.summary_en: The birthday of Toussaint L'Ouverture was commemorated at a memorial meeting in New York under the auspices of the American Negro Labor Congress, with Richard B. Moore acting as chairman. Moore said that a little more than a hundred years after Haiti's triumphant struggle against Napoleon for complete independence, the island found itself under American imperialism, a foreign control he called far more menacing and crushing than the political control of one state over another. The meeting heard that L'Ouverture was born enslaved in the French colony of Haiti, then known as Santo Domingo, overthrew slavery throughout the island and carried on the struggle against Napoleon's reaction, making way for the birth of the republic of Haiti.
records.summary_es: El cumpleaños de Toussaint L'Ouverture fue conmemorado en una reunión memorial en Nueva York, bajo los auspicios del Congreso Americano de Trabajadores Negros, con Richard B. Moore como presidente del acto. Moore declaró que poco más de cien años después de la lucha triunfante de Haití contra Napoleón por su independencia completa, la isla se encontraba bajo el imperialismo estadounidense, un control extranjero que calificó de mucho más amenazante y aplastante que el control político de un Estado sobre otro. En la reunión se recordó que L'Ouverture nació esclavo en la colonia francesa de Haití, entonces conocida como Santo Domingo, abolió la esclavitud en toda la isla y continuó la lucha contra la reacción de Napoleón, abriendo el camino al nacimiento de la república de Haití.

Mr. Moore said a little more than a hundred years after Haiti's triumphant struggle against Napoleon for her complete independence, this island of the West Indies finds itself under the steel heels of American imperialism; a foreign control far more menacing and crushing and deadening than ever attended the political control of one state over another. Toussaint L'Ouverture was born a slave in the French colony of Haiti, then known as Santo Domingo. When the revolution came in France at the close of the eighteenth century the revolutionary ideas of Danton and Robespierre found ready recruits among the toiling slaves and discontented mulattoes of the oppressed island. L'Ouverture was the foremost of the Santo Dominican leaders. He not only overthrew slavery throughout the island but carried on a successful struggle against Napoleon's Thermidorian policy of reaction and made way for the birth of the republic of Haiti, according to the records contained in Chaplain T. records.full_text:
DOMINICAN REBELLION STARTS AS HOOVER COMMISSION DEPARTS

Haiti Commission Sails From Key West; Marines Available to Put Down Any Disorder

Departure of President Hoover's Haitian commission today from Key West coincided with reports of a rebellion in the Dominican Republic which shares the island of Santo Domingo with Haiti.

The U. S. has assumed responsibilities under the existing Dominican-American treaty which might be made the basis for intervention in the Dominican Republic if disorder persists.

President Hoover said today his reports of revolutionary conditions contained no information that there is any danger to the life or liberty of Americans at the present time.

Marines Ready
Marines are available in Haiti and a force could be dispatched to the other part of the island.

Treaty relations between the U. S. and the Dominican Republic are financial. Article I authorizes the President of the U. S. to appoint a General Receiver of Dominican Customs, and Article II says:

“The government of the U. S. will give to the General Receiver and his assistants such protection as it may find to be requisite for the performance of their duties.”

Natives Killed
The President ordered additional marines to Haiti after disorders last December, but subsequently recalled them. Several natives were killed by the marines. The Haitian Commission, headed by Cameron Forbes, former Governor General of the Philippines, is sailing on the U. S. S. Rochester.

Marines were sent to the Dominican republic in 1916 to quiet a serious uprising. They formed a military government which continued in office until 1924 when Rear Admiral Samuel S. Robinson, military governor turned the government over to the newly elected president, Horacio Vasquez, who still is in office.

Extent Unknown
Reports received by the State Department from Minister Charles B. Curtis indicated rebellion against the Vasquez governments and said Senora Vasquez had sought safety in the American Legation. First reports to the department did not define the origin or extent of the disorder.

Dominican affairs have been tranquil for 10 years. The present treaty relationship with the U. S. began in 1907. Between 1865 and 1904 domestic disorder contributed to the creation of a national debt of $32,000,000, much of which was represented by bonds held in European countries.

Roosevelt Acted
In 1905 there were rumors that several European governments contemplated vigorous action in behalf of the bondholders. President Roosevelt negotiated a treaty which was rejected by the Senate because one clause was interpreted as establishing a protectorate.

Roosevelt then negotiated an executive agreement which was put in force, and subsequently put in treaty form.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Times* reported that a major rebellion had broken out against Dominican President Horacio Vásquez, prompting his wife to take shelter at the American Legation. Insurgents captured the fort and police station at Santiago de los Caballeros and took control of Dajabón near the Haitian border after disarming local authorities. The uprising was reported to be fueled largely by severe economic distress resulting from the sugar industry depression.

Los insurgentes tomaron la fortaleza y la estación de policía de Santiago de los Caballeros y asumieron el control de Dajabón, cerca de la frontera haitiana, tras desarmar a las autoridades locales. Trascendió que el alzamiento estuvo alimentado en gran medida por la grave penuria económica provocada por la depresión en la industria azucarera.

records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* reported that Dominican rebels seized Santiago de los Caballeros, Puerto Plata, and La Vega, leading to the resignation of Vice President Alfonseca. The paper charged that President Horacio Vásquez was being kept in power by U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis and Customs Receiver General William E. Pulliam to protect American financial investments. Curtis reportedly urged Vásquez to reconsider resigning, while the publication denounced the regime as a tool of Wall Street and the National City Bank of New York.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* informó que rebeldes dominicanos tomaron Santiago de los Caballeros, Puerto Plata y La Vega, lo que condujo a la renuncia del vicepresidente Alfonseca. Pulliam para salvaguardar las inversiones financieras norteamericanas. Según los informes, Curtis instó a Vásquez a reconsiderar su renuncia, mientras el rotativo tildaba al régimen de ser un instrumento de Wall Street y del National City Bank of New York.

records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* reported that Dominican President Vásquez offered to repeal electoral amendments extending his term from four to six years as rebel forces over 1,000 strong advanced from the interior. The article stated that public rebellion was fueled by fears that Vásquez would maintain power with U.S. support, alongside severe poverty caused by falling sugar and tobacco prices. It also reported that Vásquez remained in frequent consultation with the American minister regarding marine backing.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* informó que el presidente dominicano Vásquez ofreció derogar las enmiendas electorales que prolongaban su mandato de cuatro a seis años mientras fuerzas rebeldes de más de 1 000 hombres avanzaban desde el interior. El artículo indicó que el descontento popular estuvo avivado por el temor de que Vásquez se perpetuara en el poder con apoyo de Estados Unidos, unido a la extrema miseria provocada por la caída de los precios del azúcar y del tabaco. Reportó además que Vásquez celebraba continuas consultas con el ministro estadounidense en relación con un posible respaldo de la infantería de marina.

The original election laws provided for a four-year term for the president, and Vasquez passed a law giving himself an added two years to his term. records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* reported that following the marine withdrawal, Dominican President Vásquez assumed dictatorial powers that facilitated American corporate control of over 300,000 acres of sugar plantations. The article cited Charles G. Dawes's 1928 mission to structure the Dominican budget for repayments to the National City Bank under the customs treaty. It further claimed that High Commissioner Russell in Haiti feared the Dominican rebellion would inspire Haitian peasants to revolt against President Borno's administration.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* denunció que, tras la retirada de los marines, el presidente dominicano Vásquez asumió facultades dictatoriales que facilitaron el control corporativo estadounidense sobre más de 300 000 acres de plantaciones azucareras. El artículo citó la misión de Charles G. Dawes en 1928 para estructurar el presupuesto dominicano de cara a los reembolsos al National City Bank bajo el tratado aduanero. Asimismo, afirmó que el alto comisionado Russell en Haití temía que la rebelión dominicana incitara a los campesinos haitianos a alzarse contra el gobierno del presidente Borno.

records.summary_en: The *South Bend News-Times* reported that rebel chief Rafael Estrella Ureña entered Santo Domingo to negotiate with President Vásquez and U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis following the capture of northern and eastern cities by 4,000 insurgent troops. Rebel gunfire around the central plaza and cathedral caused alarm among hotel guests, while government operations ceased. Acting as mediator, Curtis sought a constitutional compromise by appointing a new secretary of the interior who could legally succeed Vásquez.

Curtis tras la toma de ciudades del norte y el este por parte de 4 000 combatientes insurgentes. Los disparos de los rebeldes en torno a la plaza central y la catedral causaron alarma entre los huéspedes de los hoteles, mientras se paralizaban las labores del gobierno. Actuando como mediador, Curtis procuró un acuerdo constitucional mediante la designación de un nuevo secretario de Interior que pudiera suceder legítimamente a Vásquez.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that insurgent troops occupied Santo Domingo while Army Commander General Trujillo held Fort Ozama before joining peace talks at the American Legation. Rebel leaders Rafael Estrella Ureña and Desiderio Arias demanded constitutional elections on May 15 without Vásquez as a candidate. U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis stated that Washington would not recognize a de facto regime, prompting discussions to designate Trujillo or Ángel Morales as provisional president upon Vásquez's resignation.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que tropas insurgentes ocuparon Santo Domingo mientras el comandante del ejército, general Trujillo, retenía la Fortaleza Ozama antes de sumarse a las conversaciones de paz en la legación estadounidense. Los líderes rebeldes Rafael Estrella Ureña y Desiderio Arias exigieron la celebración de elecciones constitucionales el 15 de mayo sin la candidatura de Vásquez. El ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis manifestó que Washington no reconocería un régimen de facto, lo que motivó deliberaciones para designar a Trujillo o a Ángel Morales como presidente provisional tras la renuncia de Vásquez.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that Rafael Estrella Ureña assumed the provisional presidency of the Dominican Republic after negotiating with Fort Ozama commander General Rafael Trujillo. Outgoing President Horacio Vásquez requested legislative permission to travel abroad due to ill health, while Trujillo declined consideration for the presidency. U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis, who had insisted on constitutional continuity, expressed satisfaction with the arrangement as rebel forces secured political control.

El presidente saliente Horacio Vásquez solicitó autorización legislativa para viajar al extranjero por motivos de salud, mientras que Trujillo declinó postularse a la presidencia. El ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis, quien había insistido en mantener la continuidad constitucional, expresó su conformidad con el acuerdo mientras las fuerzas rebeldes consolidaban el control político.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo on September 6 reports that relief agencies reaching the stricken
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo on September 6 reports that relief agencies reaching the stricken city found the horror of Wednesday's hurricane worse rather than better: an estimated 1,500 to 2,000 persons dead, more than 5,000 injured, 30,000 homeless, and of 10,000 buildings only 400 left standing, with property damage to pass $20,000,000. There is no water fit to drink, the dead are being collected and burned in heaps and in concrete cisterns used as funeral pyres, relief planes have brought some supplies and doctors from Port-au-Prince, Havana, the United States and Porto Rico, and the president has stopped food profiteering by ordering all food sold at cost under pain of court martial, while Santiago, La Vega and Puerto Plata are reported undamaged.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Associated Press desde Santo Domingo del 6 de septiembre informa que las agencias de socorro que llegaron a la ciudad devastada encontraron el horror del huracán del miércoles peor en vez de mejor: se estima que murieron entre 1,500 y 2,000 personas, más de 5,000 resultaron heridas, 30,000 quedaron sin hogar y de 10,000 edificios solo 400 quedaron en pie, con daños materiales que pasarán de $20,000,000. No hay agua apta para beber, los muertos están siendo recogidos y quemados en montones y en cisternas de concreto usadas como piras funerarias, aviones de socorro han traído algunos suministros y médicos desde Puerto Príncipe, La Habana, los Estados Unidos y Puerto Rico, y el presidente ha detenido la especulación con los alimentos ordenando que toda la comida se venda al costo bajo pena de consejo de guerra, mientras se informa que Santiago, La Vega y Puerto Plata no sufrieron daños.

The Ozama river is a raging torrent pouring out over a bar at its entrance, which effectively blocks what was the old harbor. One authority said he did not believe even a Navy launch could cross the bar. The suggestion has been made — and it appears plausible — that the relief ships may disembark their cargoes and men at San Geronimo, four kilometers south of the capital, where there is a good beach. records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported on catastrophic devastation in Santo Domingo caused by a hurricane that demolished poorer residential districts across a 160-square-mile area. President Rafael Trujillo assumed personal command of military forces to maintain order, clear debris, and organize relief before the arrival of outside assistance. Initial relief ships from Puerto Rico and commercial cable vessels landed medical units and provided emergency tents for 2,000 homeless survivors.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* informó sobre la devastación catastrófica en Santo Domingo causada por un huracán que demolió los distritos residenciales más humildes en un área de 160 millas cuadradas. El presidente Rafael Trujillo asumió el mando personal de las fuerzas militares para mantener el orden, despejar escombros y organizar el socorro antes de la llegada de ayuda exterior. Primeros barcos de auxilio procedentes de Puerto Rico y buques de tendido de cable comercial desembarcaron brigadas médicas y proveyeron tiendas de campaña de emergencia para 2 000 damnificados sin hogar.

Tonight it was possible for the first time to drive through any of the streets of the ruined city to gain anything like an intelligent idea of the storm's wreckage. The poorer sections of the city suffered the most damage. Whole areas inhabited by thousands were completely wiped out, without a single house remaining to give shelter. President Rafael Trujillo took heroic measures in his own hands and with troops under his personal command began clearing the streets and roads. He also gave personal attention to maintaining order. Cable Ship Brings Tents When the first relief ships arrived today they found that the efforts of President Trujillo had resulted in shaping conditions so that more headway may be made than had been hoped for. But it will be next week before there are any street lights and it will still be several days before the town water can be turned on. The All-America Cable company's cable ship today brought tents for 2000 persons. Cable Engineer Judo, of the cable ship All-America, who was an eye-witness of the hurricane which hit San Juan, Porto Rico, in September, 1928, declared this afternoon that the destruction wrought by Wednesday's storm was much greater and that the storm's intensity exceeded the San Juan hurricane. A relief boat from Porto Rico also arrived today and the Porto Rican medical unit was landed. Additional supplies will be here tomorrow for the use of the doctors and nurses besides

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that emergency relief centers in Santo Domingo were distributing daily food rations to approximately 10,000 hurricane survivors under Red Cross Director Ernest J. Swift. A 1,000-bed tent hospital was established under U.S. Navy Commander L. W. Johnson to perform surgeries and treat injured residents. Dominican soldiers and armed bluejackets from the USS *Grebe* stood guard over supply trucks and wharves to prevent desperate crowds from looting incoming provisions.

Soldados dominicanos y marineros armados del USS *Grebe* custodiaban camiones de abastecimiento y muelles para evitar que multitudes desesperadas saquearan los víveres que arribaban.

At one time today the crowd at a Red Cross food station became so large and so unmanageable for the civilians that Dominican soldiers were compelled to drive the crowd back before order could be restored. Food Supply Augmented Tonight for the first time in a week there were few among the city's homeless who were hungry. Imported food made possible the feeding of the thousands who had not only lost their homes and their loved ones, but also their sources of income. The food supply was greatly augmented by trucks bringing provisions from other parts of the Dominican republic. Surgical attention for the injured was greatly facilitated today with the opening of the Roosevelt emergency tent hospital, which has 1000 beds. Comdr. L. W. Johnson of the United States army was placed in charge of all the medical work in the city. Many Vessels In Port So many vessels arrived today that Capt. John Davis, chief of the port at Port-au-Prince, was delegated to the task of discharging their cargoes in an organized manner. At the same time, bluejackets from the United States ship Grebe were sent ashore to form an armed guard over food wagons passing from the wharves to the general warehouses from which relief is distributed. records.summary_en: The *Ronan Pioneer* reviewed Latin American political changes in 1930, noting that revolutionary upheavals began in February when Dominican President Horacio Vásquez sought reelection. Vásquez was forced from office after brief skirmishes and succeeded temporarily by General Estrella Ureña. In subsequent elections held on May 16, General Rafael Trujillo was elected president, officially taking office three months later.
records.summary_es: El *Ronan Pioneer* repasó las transformaciones políticas latinoamericanas en 1930, destacando que las conmociones revolucionarias se iniciaron en febrero cuando el presidente dominicano Horacio Vásquez pretendió reelegirse. Vásquez fue forzado a renunciar tras breves escaramuzas y sucedido transitoriamente por el general Estrella Ureña. En los comicios posteriores del 16 de mayo, el general Rafael Trujillo resultó electo presidente, asumiendo oficialmente el cargo tres meses más tarde.
records.passage: virtual dictators were ousted. Four new governments were established. As a preliminary to these events there was a revolution in the Dominican republic in February, the immediate cause being the announced intention of President Horacio Vasquez to stand for re-election. After a few skirmishes Vasquez was forced out of office, [illegible] succeeded temporarily by General Urena. Elections were held on May 16 and Gen. Rafael Trujillo was chosen president and inaugurated three months later. Bolivia was next on the list. There Dr. Hernando Siles tried, like Vasquez, to perpetuate his rule and was driven from office in May by the insurgents. He was permitted to take refuge in Chile, and his much hated right hand man, Gen. Hans Kundt of Prussia, fled back to his German home. A military junta took over the government, its chief being Gen. Carlos Blanco Galindo. Peru followed suit in August. The officers of the army led a movement against President Augusto B. Leguia, who had held the office for more than ten years and considered himself almost irremovable. He was forced to resign, turning over his powers to a military junta, and later Lieut. Col. Luis M. Sanchez Cerro was made provisional president. Leguia had been recognized as an efficient business president and Peru made great material strides during his regime, but the revolutionists accused him of "denial of civil liberties" and also of nepotism and the sale of concessions. He was imprisoned to await trial.

records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* condemned U.S. support for General Trujillo's regime in the Dominican Republic, noting heavy American capital investments and the use of U.S. currency on the island. Citing declarations from the Caribbean Red Aid, the publication alleged that Dominican authorities arbitrarily arrested workers as vagrants to condemn them to forced labor in brutal prisons. The editorial demanded that U.S. officials apply the same forced-labor import bans to Dominican sugar, cocoa, and tobacco that were imposed against Soviet imports.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* condenó el respaldo estadounidense al régimen del general Trujillo en la República Dominicana, resaltando las cuantiosas inversiones de capital norteamericano y el uso de la moneda de Estados Unidos en la isla. Citando declaraciones del Socorro Rojo del Caribe, el diario denunció que las autoridades dominicanas arrestaban arbitrariamente a trabajadores bajo cargos de vagancia para destinarlos a trabajos forzados en prisiones brutales. El editorial exigió a los funcionarios de Washington aplicar al azúcar, cacao y tabaco dominicanos las mismas restricciones de importación por trabajo forzado impuestas a los productos soviéticos.
records.passage: under General Trujillo set up a year ago, with which Washington is in perfect relations. To show how much an appendix is Santo Domingo to the U. S. A., we may merely state the fact that it has no national money of its own, and uses United States money. American investments a year ago totalled $29,548,000. Yet what do we hear about forced labor — not in the Soviet Union — but right here at America's doorstep and under its control? The workers' defense organization known as the Caribbean Red Aid, in a recent statement on conditions in Santo Domingo, protests at the terror against the Dominican working class, and says: "The troops stop and question workers in the streets of all the cities of the country and after brief questions and replies declare the passers-by 'vagrants' and take them off under arrest. Each one of those arrested awaits the most terrible prison regime and FORCED LABOR." Perhaps Secretary Mellon of the U. S. Treasury will now put an embargo on all sugar, cocoa and tobacco coming into American ports from Santo Domingo? Perhaps he will decree that "the burden of proof" rests on the various Yankee imperialist corporations and the National City Bank which finances them, to prove that Dominican sugar, cocoa and tobacco are not produced "in whole or in part by forced labor?" This is the bar put against Soviet lumber this last Monday. Ah, how vigilant the Washington officials are! Stimson contemplated an early withdrawal of U.S. Marines from Haiti, dependent on the efficiency of the local national guard. records.passage: Haiti in Line of Storms By United Press WASHINGTON, Sept. 11. — The hurricane which swept Porto Rico Thursday night with undetermined damage was reported by the weather bureau today to be approaching Haiti and the Dominican republic with undiminished violence. Dispatches received here said one person was killed and several were injured in San Juan Thursday night. Extent of damage in the interior of Porto Rico was unknown. Meantime, unofficial reports to the Tropical Radio Company said the city of Belize, British Honduras, had been destroyed by a hurricane Thursday night. The reports said 150 persons had been killed. The Belize hurricane was a disturbance far removed from that which hit Porto Rico. The weather bureau believes the former hurricane has about spent its force. It was centered today in the extreme southern part of the Gulf of Mexico. Warnings were sent by the bureau to Belize Thursday night that the city was in danger, but communications were interrupted. The bureau has charted the progress of the Belize disturbance for several days and added to the current hurricanes that one which reached San Juan shortly before midnight. The San Juan disturbance was about half-way between Porto Rico and Haiti today. Estimates of the violence of the hurricane varied from 70 to 100 miles an hour. Wind velocity of the storm which struck Belize was fifty miles an hour when last reported to the weather bureau. United States Consul Taggart was injured slightly. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Dominican Republic suspended principal amortization payments on its foreign debt while maintaining interest payments, diverting customs revenues to internal operational expenses. Officials viewed the move as a breach of the 1924 treaty governing the American customs receivership, which required U.S. consent for debt modifications. The article noted that American private investments totaled nearly $70,000,000 alongside over $17,000,000 in Dominican government bonds.

Funcionarios consideraron la medida como una violación del tratado de 1924 que regía la receptoría general de aduanas estadounidense, el cual exigía el consentimiento de Estados Unidos para cualquier modificación de la deuda. El artículo señaló que las inversiones privadas norteamericanas sumaban cerca de 70 000 000 de dólares, además de más de 17 000 000 de dólares en bonos del Estado dominicano.

TEGUCIGALPA, Honduras, June 15. — Augusto Sandino, Nicaraguan insurgent leader, contributed an article under his own signature to a newspaper here today in which he asserted that in the month of April his men had fought nine battles against the Nicaraguan national guard. Seven United States Marines serving with the guard were killed, he said, and in all the dead numbered 131. Thirty of the guards were wounded and the insurgents captured 29 rifles, seven machine guns and 19,000 cartridges, Sandino wrote. He asserted the only candidate for the Nicaraguan presidency acceptable to him is Gen. Horacio Portocarrero. "Nicaragua will be freed only by the bullets and blood of our people," he wrote, "we will oppose by force of arms whatever election farce may be attempted with the aid of foreign supervision."

THIS IS NEWS

At least one solvent country has been discovered in these days of unbalanced budgets and record breaking deficits. At Santo Domingo the Treasury of the Dominican Republic has announced that the government of President Trujillo has rigidly maintained its budget during the first six months of 1932, and that payment on foreign and other debts has been promptly met. The administration of this Carribean country is looked upon as a model by our State Department.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported favorably on conditions in the Dominican Republic on the eve of its sixty-ninth national anniversary, noting that President Trujillo's government had strengthened internal order and foreign credit. In contrast to political instability and financial defaults across much of Latin America since 1930, the commentary noted that the Dominican Republic maintained a balanced budget and steady governance. This administrative stability was credited with bolstering public support at home and prestige abroad.

En contraste con la inestabilidad política y las cesaciones de pagos en gran parte de América Latina desde 1930, el comentario destacó que la República Dominicana mantenía un presupuesto equilibrado y una gobernabilidad firme. Se atribuyó a esta estabilidad administrativa el haber afianzado el respaldo popular en el país y el prestigio en el extranjero.

Its successful management of the country's finances in such difficult times as these, and the recognition of that success by foreign nations, are constantly adding to its prestige, with the result that all sectors of public opinion in the island republic are rallying around the government. This contributes to strengthen the stability of the situation and this stability, in turn, is the best ally of the authorities in coping with the economic needs of the country. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* shared a private letter from an American resident in the Dominican Republic describing a luncheon given by sugar estates for President Rafael Trujillo on May 3. Following the meal, Trujillo lowered the presidential flag and personally hoisted the United States flag before 450 guests. The observer characterized the ceremony as a notable Pan-American gesture demonstrating Trujillo's continued goodwill toward the United States.

Al término de la comida, Trujillo arrió la bandera presidencial e izó personalmente la enseña de Estados Unidos ante 450 comensales. El observador calificó la ceremonia como un notable gesto panamericano que demostraba la constante buena voluntad de Trujillo hacia Estados Unidos.

The article recounted how Caperton took control of Port-au-Prince, suppressed opposition, and urged troop deployments to secure a financial treaty desired by the State Department and the National City Bank. records.headline: Pan-American Delegates Ready for Conference Opening Today
records.summary_en: One hundred delegates from the American nations gathered in Montevideo for the opening of the Pan-American Conference on economic and peace questions, with the Gran Chaco war between Bolivia and Paraguay and the monetary and debt situations among the subjects expected to be taken up. Cuba's delegation said its program rested on the complete independence of all American countries and freedom from intervention, while Haiti's delegate, Pierre Paul, charged that the United States had for eighteen years supported unjustifiable intervention in Haiti and said he would introduce a resolution establishing the principle of non-intervention. Secretary of State Cordell Hull visited the heads of delegations, including that of the Dominican Republic, and discussed the question of American financial control in Haiti with the Haitian delegation.

La delegación de Cuba declaró que su programa se basaba en la independencia integral de todos los países americanos y en la libertad frente a la intervención, mientras que el delegado de Haití, Pierre Paul, denunció que los Estados Unidos habían sostenido durante dieciocho años una intervención injustificable en Haití y anunció que presentaría una resolución que estableciera el principio de no intervención. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published a profile of Dominican President Rafael Trujillo, noting his rise from private to captain in the Marine-trained constabulary and his disciplined administrative methods. The article detailed his measures eliminating government automobiles for legislators and dropping 500 redundant employees from the state payroll. Despite the depression cutting government revenues by more than half, the piece credited Trujillo and his financial adviser with balancing the national budget and maintaining civic order.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó una semblanza del presidente dominicano Rafael Trujillo, destacando su ascenso de soldado raso a capitán en la guardia entrenada por los marines y sus métodos de disciplina administrativa. El artículo detalló sus medidas para suprimir los automóviles oficiales para legisladores y dar de baja a 500 empleados innecesarios de la nómina estatal. A pesar de que la depresión redujo los ingresos fiscales a más de la mitad, la nota atribuyó a Trujillo y a su consejero financiero el haber equilibrado el presupuesto nacional y preservado el orden cívico.
records.passage: sidelights respecting Gen. Rafael Leonides Trujillo, the President of the republic. Trujillo began life as a private in the constabulary forces in the island, long operated by the United States Marines; rose to be captain of it, and is now running the country in the thoroughly efficient, if somewhat hard-boiled, fashion of a marine. Trujillo's first act when he took office was to take away from all the members of the Dominican House and Senate their free government automobiles; his next act to drop 500 supernumeraries off the official pay roll. The depression in Santo Domingo cut the state's revenue in half—from $15,000,000 to $7,000,000, and Trujillo found an empty treasury. But now, thanks to Trujillo and to the advice of his financial adviser, the republic has a balanced budget and is sweet, sanitary and safe. records.full_text:
WASHINGTON OBSERVATIONS

The happily concluded negotiations for the adjustment of the foreign dollar bonds of the tiny Dominican Republic as announced last week is a new laurel crown for the Honorable Joseph E. Davies, whose prominent place in the Washington picture dates back to the days of the Wilson administration, when “Joe” Davies was first chairman of the Federal Trade Commission. Now in the private practice of law, though boomed for a place in the Roosevelt cabinet, Mr. Davies numbers the Dominican Republic among his clients and piloted the island’s government through the tortuous channel of debt negotiations with the Foreign Bondholders’ Protective Council. Friends of Mr. Davies are in receipt of copies of his brief in these proceedings, a magnus opus of 200 pages, in which the facts and the law and the argument are skillfully intertwined.

records.summary_en: Former Cuban ruler Gerardo Machado is practically recovered from the attack of indigestion that sent him to a hospital in Santo Domingo two weeks ago and is preparing to sail for Italy. Machado fled Cuba on August 12, 1933, and lived in Canada and the United States while Cuban governments sought his return for trial. His friends denied a version that his illness in Santo Domingo was poisoning, and in the Dominican Republic he was granted refuge by President Rafael Trujillo, long a friend of Machado.

Sus amigos negaron una versión de que su enfermedad en Santo Domingo fue un envenenamiento, y en la República Dominicana recibió refugio del presidente Rafael Trujillo, amigo de Machado desde hacía tiempo.

Morales stated that Trujillo, who rose from constabulary sergeant during the U.S. Marine occupation to seize power via a 1930 coup, had eliminated all other political parties and won unanimous reelection. records.headline: President Trujillo, the statement says: "With a will that brought comment
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published a statement praising President Trujillo for directing the rebuilding of Santo Domingo following its destruction, modernizing the city without incurring new debt or defaulting on bonded interest payments. The report highlighted extensive nationwide public works, including new roads, schools, hospitals, Latin America's largest suspension bridge, and a nearly completed $3,000,000 artificial port at Trujillo City. It added that despite public efforts to rename the capital in his honor, Trujillo had initially opposed the proposal.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó una declaración en la que elogiaba al presidente Trujillo por dirigir la reconstrucción de Santo Domingo tras su destrucción, modernizando la urbe sin contraer nueva deuda ni suspender el pago de intereses sobre los bonos. El informe destacó amplias obras públicas en todo el territorio nacional, como nuevas carreteras, escuelas, hospitales, el puente colgante más grande de América Latina y un puerto artificial de 3.000.000 de dólares a punto de concluirse en Ciudad Trujillo. Añadió que, pese a las gestiones públicas para rebautizar la capital en su honor, Trujillo se había opuesto inicialmente a dicha propuesta.
records.passage: President Trujillo, the statement says: "With a will that brought comment from the entire world, the 39-year-old Chief Executive personally directed the task of saving the impoverished population from starvation and epidemics. and then of constructing a new city to replace the old one. Rapidly new streets, buildings, homes and parks appeared, until Santo Domingo became a new metropolis in gleaming white, far surpassing the city it had replaced. "Without defaulting or postponing Interest payments on bonded indebtedness. and without incurring new indebtedness. President Trujillo conducted a vast program of public works throughout the nation, financed entirely from current revenue. New highways were laid into every corner of the country; great bridges were swung across rivers, among them the largest suspension bridge in Latin America; new schools, hospitals, libraries. were erected everywhere. Agricultural development mounted to new all-time highs and industry leaped from a handful of manufacturing establishments to more than 1,200. After his re-election in 1934. President Trujillo began an even more impressive public works program, the climax of which is the creation of an artificial port at Trujillo City, now nearly completed. At a cost of $3,000,000 this new port permits for the first time actual entry to the docks of the harbor. With an opening salute of 21 guns from the batteries of Ozama Fortress, the Dominican Republic today Inaugurated the most extensive and elaborate celebration of Washington's birthday ever held outside the United States. Dominican President Rafael Trujillo and Colombian President Alfonso López argued that an American league would serve regional purposes more effectively than the League of Nations in Geneva. records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported that the Dominican government declared closed the recent frontier incident in which more than 1,000 Haitians were reported killed. Dominican officials asserted that the affair was a private dispute between individuals along the border rather than an international matter, and denied dispatching troops to the frontier. The official statement reiterated the Dominican Republic's peaceful intentions.

records.summary_en: United States Minister Norweb was hastily dispatched from Havana, where he was attending an international radio conference, to Ciudad Trujillo, arriving by airplane yesterday, and was expected to confer immediately with President General Trujillo, although the State Department said no report had yet been received from him. Considerable apprehension was felt over the new threat to the peace of the hemisphere; Dominican troops were reported massing on the border, but this was denied by Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza in Washington. Reports reaching Washington said the Haitians were massacred because they had crossed the ill-defined border to farm lands, and because they angered Dominicans by working for cheaper wages and causing them to lose their jobs.

Massacre Stories Assailed as Lies

By LOUIS JAY HEATH
United Press Staff Correspondent

Haitian and Dominican politicians and revolutionists were charged with malicious distortion of a “small incident” which took place early in October near the Dominican-Haitian border, in a formal communique issued by Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza here today.

Haitian officials have charged that the so-called “small incident” referred to by Pastoriza consisted of “brutal killings of from 3000 to 5000 Haitian nationals by Dominican soldiers and police.” At the request of the Haitian government the United States, Mexico and Cuba have tendered their good offices to mediate the incident. To date the Dominican government has not accepted the tender and has sent special envoys to all three capitols to present the Dominican case.

The Pastoriza communique, addressed to editors, stated that the Dominican government already considered the “incident closed.”

USED BY ENEMIES
“The small incident . . . between Dominican citizens and Haitian citizens who were maintaining illegal residence in certain zones of the Dominican Republic, or who were violently entering the Dominican Republic,” the communique said, “is being used by political enemies of President Trujillo (of the Dominican Republic) and by Haitian elements interested in covering up the political unrest existing for some time in the Republic of Haiti. . . .”

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published an analysis attributing cross-border tensions between Haiti and the Dominican Republic to acute hunger and agricultural underproduction resulting from Haiti's dense population. The writer argued that food shortages drove impoverished Haitians across the frontier to steal livestock and farm animals. In turn, isolated Dominican homesteaders strongly resented these cattle thefts and feared for their lives and families.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó un análisis que atribuía las tensiones fronterizas entre Haití y la República Dominicana al hambre aguda y al déficit de producción agrícola causados por la alta densidad demográfica haitiana. El autor sostenía que la escasez de alimentos empujaba a haitianos desposeídos a cruzar la frontera para robar ganado y animales de labranza. Por su parte, los campesinos dominicanos de zonas aisladas resentían profundamente esos robos pecuarios y temían por la integridad de sus familias y vidas.
records.passage: cattle and farm animals. Haiti's teeming population literally cannot subsist on what is produced by their country's backward agriculture. Considerably greater production would be possible in Haiti, despite the fact that the soil has been treated villainously ever since the French were expelled, if it were not for a racial trait which is characteristic of the island. Well does the Haitian peasant know this weakness of his fellow-countrymen. Of what use for him—or, more accurately, for his wife—to work hard and produce an abundance if some one else is to reap the benefit? In Haiti, the prudent peasant never allows fruit to ripen on his trees—if he does, his neighbors, on the first dark night that comes along, will pick it for him. Thus the situation in Haiti is a combination of dense population with underproduction of food. When such a situation comes into being in any country it means trouble—trouble within the country and trouble for the neighbors without. Hunger Basic Cause. In a word, it is hunger, and not just a propensity for vicious thievery, that drives the poverty-stricken Haitians to commit depredations. The Haitian government contended that unprovoked attacks by Dominicans on Haitian citizens residing in Dominican territory were the cause of the tension, and Foreign Minister Georges Leger said at least 5,000 Haitians had been slain in wholesale massacres. records.headline: President Vincent asserted that the border question which once existed had
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Haitian President Sténio Vincent estimated 8,000 Haitians were assassinated in the Dominican Republic, maintaining that the border dispute had already been settled by treaty two years prior. Vincent asserted that the Dominican government should have used standard diplomatic channels to repatriate undesirable foreigners, rather than resorting to violence without warning. While Vincent requested mediation from the United States, Cuba, and Mexico, President Trujillo expressed surprise at the appeal, pointing to existing bilateral accords.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el presidente haitiano Sténio Vincent estimó en 8.000 los haitianos asesinados en la República Dominicana, sosteniendo que la disputa de límites ya había quedado resuelta mediante tratado hacía dos años. Vincent aseveró que el gobierno dominicano debió recurrir a los canales diplomáticos habituales para repatriar a los extranjeros indeseables en lugar de acudir a la violencia sin previo aviso. Mientras Vincent solicitaba la mediación de Estados Unidos, Cuba y México, el presidente Trujillo expresó sorpresa ante dicha apelación señalando la vigencia de los acuerdos bilaterales.
records.passage: President Vincent asserted that the border question which once existed had been settled, largely at the initiative of the Haitian government two years ago when a treaty was signed by the two nations. He said there had been no border question since then. Usual Channels Open. "If the Dominican government wanted to expel foreigners they believed for one reason or another undesirable. they could have used the usual channels, the same as Cuba did when it repatriated thousands of Haitians from Cuba recently," President Vincent said. "I vow that this government has never received the slightest indications that Haitians, many of whom resided in the Dominican Republic for many -years, suddenly had become undesirable, until I heard of the assassinations." President Vincent's estimate of 8.000 slain was higher even than reports circulating on the streets of this sultry little mountain capital, where the populace is clamoring for strong measures in dealing with the Dominican Republic. The United States State Department on November 13 announced it had received a request from President Vincent for the United States to offer its good offices, together with Cuba and Mexico, toward seeking a solution of the Haitian-Dominican controversy. When President Rafael Leonidas Trujillo of the Dominican Republic learned of President Vincent's action, he expressed surprise that the United States, Cuba and Mexico had been asked to mediate. He mentioned a diplomatic accord which exists between the two governments.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Dominican Minister Andrés Pastoriza announced President Trujillo would not seek reelection, instead endorsing Dr. Jacinto B. Peynado for president and Dr. Manuel de Jesús Troncoso de la Concha for vice president, though Trujillo remained ready to serve if needed. The announcement came amid ongoing diplomatic friction with Haiti, which alleged that over 12,000 Haitians were massacred on Dominican soil. Dominican officials denied the accusations, attributing the reports to political enemies and citing economic strain caused by illegal Haitian migration.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el ministro dominicano Andrés Pastoriza anunció que el presidente Trujillo no buscaría la reelección, respaldando en su lugar al Dr. Jacinto B. Peynado para la presidencia y al Dr. Manuel de Jesús Troncoso de la Concha para la vicepresidencia, si bien Trujillo permanecía dispuesto a servir de ser necesario. El anuncio se produjo en medio de continuas fricciones diplomáticas con Haití, que alegaba la masacre de más de 12.000 haitianos en suelo dominicano. Las autoridades dominicanas rechazaron las acusaciones, atribuyendo los informes a enemigos políticos y señalando la carga económica provocada por la inmigración clandestina haitiana.

The Minister's statement made no mention of the controversy between his country and Haiti, which grew out of clashes early in October. The Haitian government, through its Legation here, has charged more than 12,000 Haitians were "massacred" on Dominican soil. Dominican authorities have denied these assertions, charging in reply that many Haitians illegally entered the Dominican Republic, aggravating economic conditions there. records.summary_en: The *Times-News* reported that economic hardship and falling sugar prices exacerbated animosity toward thousands of Haitian laborers living in the Dominican Republic, culminating in nocturnal massacres where hundreds of Haitians were butchered with machetes along the Massacre River. Rather than retaliating militarily, Haitian President Sténio Vincent submitted the conflict to the Permanent Committee of Inter-American Conciliation under the 1923 Gondra Treaty. The resulting settlement required the Dominican government to pay a $750,000 indemnity, continue investigating the killings with full publicity, and cooperate to prevent future occurrences.
records.summary_es: El *Times-News* informó que las dificultades económicas y la caída del precio del azúcar avivaron la hostilidad hacia miles de braceros haitianos radicados en la República Dominicana, culminando en matanzas nocturnas donde cientos de haitianos fueron degollados a machetazos a lo largo del río Masacre. En lugar de tomar represalias militares, el presidente haitiano Sténio Vincent sometió la disputa a la Comisión Permanente de Conciliación Interamericana al amparo del Tratado Gondra de 1923. El acuerdo resultante obligó al gobierno dominicano a pagar una indemnización de 750.000 dólares, proseguir las investigaciones judiciales con amplia difusión pública y cooperar para prevenir hechos semejantes en el futuro.
