records.headline: An Adventurers' Club story tells of Charley, who worked six months for a sugar concern at La Romana and, while on vacation
records.summary_en: An Adventurers' Club story tells of Charley, who worked six months for a sugar concern at La Romana and, while on vacation in Santo Domingo City, received orders transferring him to a new project at Barahona, but found every steamer tied up by a steamship strike and no road to take him there. He took a small sailing vessel for what should have been an overnight trip, but a storm blew the boat ten miles off course and disabled its steering gear, leaving him becalmed for days with forty Haitian passengers, no food and hot drinking water, as the only white man aboard, paying the captain ten dollars for protection and sleeping lashed to the rail. On the third night he woke to see two men creeping toward him with machetes in their mouths and shot both dead as the ship erupted in uproar.
records.summary_es: Un relato del Club de Aventureros cuenta la historia de Charley, que trabajó seis meses para una empresa azucarera en La Romana y, estando de vacaciones en la ciudad de Santo Domingo, recibió órdenes de traslado a un nuevo proyecto en Barahona, pero encontró todos los vapores detenidos por una huelga naviera y ningún camino que lo llevara allí. Se embarcó en un pequeño velero para lo que debía ser un viaje de una noche, pero una tormenta desvió el barco diez millas de su rumbo y averió su timón, dejándolo en calma durante días con cuarenta pasajeros haitianos, sin comida y con el agua potable caliente, siendo el único hombre blanco a bordo, pagando al capitán diez dólares por protección y durmiendo atado a la barandilla. En la tercera noche despertó y vio a dos hombres acercándose a él arrastrándose con machetes en la boca, y les disparó a ambos hasta matarlos mientras el barco estallaba en alboroto.
records.passage: was hot and humid. Hunger gnawed at his innards, but he had to make the best of it. The natives were getting more and more restless. They eyed Charley's clothes with covetous looks that became more and more insolent and apparent. And still there was no sign of the wind that would blow them into Barahona. That night, worn out by two days and nights of wakefulness, Charley fell asleep. Sometime in the dark hours he woke up suddenly, by sheer instinct. In the dim light of a tropic moon he saw two dark figures creeping along the deck toward him — two natives — great, husky blacks with machetes in their mouths! "They didn't know my eyes were open," he says, "if they had known it I wouldn't be alive today. But their ignorance gave me an opportunity to draw my guns." Charley got those guns out just as the natives were taking their machetes from their mouths. He whipped up one gun and fired twice. In an instant, two men were dead on the deck and the whole ship was in an uproar. Dark figures came swarming toward him. The captain was a big, powerful fellow. Charley says he was built on the style of Harry Wills in his prime. He picked Charley up with one hand, threw him into his cabin head first, and then, with the aid of a revolver and his powerful physique, held that furious mob at bay. records.summary_en: The *Washington Times* reported that thirty-two German-Jewish refugees arriving in New York aboard the Red Star liner *Westernland* planned to establish new homes in the Dominican Republic. The article noted that the country's capital, originally named Santo Domingo, had been renamed Ciudad Trujillo by Rafael Trujillo, whose past record with immigrants was criticized. The arrival occurred as over 1,500 Jewish refugees faced potential return to Germany after Paraguay and Uruguay barred their entry.
records.summary_es: El *Washington Times* informó que treinta y dos refugiados judeoalemanes arribados a Nueva York a bordo del transatlántico *Westernland*, de la naviera Red Star, planeaban radicarse en la República Dominicana. El artículo anotó que la capital del país, originalmente llamada Santo Domingo, había sido rebautizada Ciudad Trujillo por Rafael Trujillo, cuyos antecedentes hacia la inmigración eran objeto de críticas. Su llegada se produjo mientras más de 1.500 refugiados judíos se enfrentaban a una posible repatriación a Alemania tras prohibírseles la entrada en Paraguay y Uruguay.

More than 1,500 German-Jewish refugees now on the high seas en route from Europe to Paraguay may be forced to return to their starting points without debarking from the ships on which they are passengers, it was learned today as both Paraguay and Uraguay indicated unwillingness to accept them as immigrants. The Paraguayan government intimated today that it will not admit any Jews regardless of their nationality, financial and social positions, unless they have passport visas dated prior to December 18. Passport visas granted at later dates to the refugees now on their way to South America were said to be fraudulent. Since the Uraguayan government has also established similar barriers, it appeared probable that the refugees would be forced to return to Europe without leaving their ships. records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* commented on reports that General Rafael Trujillo and his entourage were traveling to Germany, raising speculation about German interest in Samaná Bay as a potential submarine base. Although the Dominican Legation denied that Trujillo would meet Adolf Hitler, it did not deny he was traveling to Germany. The report also listed members of Señora de Trujillo's party, which included military aides, a private physician, and secretary J. M. Bonetti Burgos.

Pese a que la Legación dominicana desmintió que Trujillo fuera a entrevistarse con Adolf Hitler, no negó que viajara a territorio alemán. La crónica enumeró asimismo a los miembros de la comitiva de la señora de Trujillo, en la que figuraban edecanes militares, un médico de cabecera y el secretario J. M. Bonetti Burgos.

Trujillo had negotiated with Germany for the lease of that strategic body of water as a submarine base. The report emanated from Puerto Rico, where there are a number of exiled enemies of the Generalissimo. It does seem that in view of the fact the General desires only the friendliest relations with this country, he would be smarter than to enter into any such negotiations. Especially when he had so recently entertained a number of prominent Americans in his own house. The lease of the bay to the Nazis would not only be an unfriendly act to the United States, but a hostile one. And, also in view of this same friendliness, it is certain that at any emergency the General would permit the United States Navy the use of Samana Bay or any other Dominican port, as a submarine base or any other military faculty. records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* outlined the itinerary for General Rafael Trujillo's visit to Washington, D.C., following an invitation from Marine Corps Commandant Major General Thomas Holcomb. The schedule included wreath-laying ceremonies at Mount Vernon and Arlington National Cemetery, official meetings with Secretary of State Cordell Hull and President Roosevelt, and a Senate luncheon. Trujillo was also scheduled to inspect military sites including the Navy Yard, Marine Barracks, and Fort Meade.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* profiled General Rafael Trujillo, noting that despite being denounced as a tyrant and accused of the massacre of thousands of Haitians two years earlier, he was recognized for administrative energy and public works. Having taken power in 1930 under the slogan "God and Trujillo," he oversaw road construction, school expansion, and the rebuilding and renaming of the capital before handing the presidency to Dr. Jacinto Bienvenido Peynado. The article noted that Trujillo continued to direct Dominican governance while being celebrated by sympathetic biographers as an inspired leader.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* perfiló al general Rafael Trujillo, señalando que, a pesar de haber sido denunciado como un tirano y acusado de la matanza de miles de haitianos dos años antes, se le reconocía por su empuje administrativo y sus planes de obras públicas. Habiendo tomado el poder en 1930 bajo el lema «Dios y Trujillo», dirigió la construcción de caminos, la expansión de escuelas y la reedificación y cambio de nombre de la capital antes de traspasar la presidencia formalmente al Dr. Jacinto Bienvenido Peynado. El artículo consignaba que Trujillo seguía conduciendo las riendas del gobierno dominicano mientras biógrafos afines lo ensalzaban como un líder providencial.
records.passage: come and who plan to come. Even if he is denounced as a tyrant and accused of the massacre of thousands of Haitians two years ago, during a border struggle along the boundary between the Dominican Republic and Haiti, there is no doubt that he is a forceful leader with a certain genius in public finance. He has an extraordinary concept of himself as a child of destiny When he was still a boy, he resolved to be the president of the Dominican Republic, where storm and strife in politics and insecurity of tenure for presidents was the classical political situation. He won the post in 1930, when he was 39, after a campaign whose slogan was "God and Trujillo." He relinquished it last August to a devoted follower. Dr. Jacinto Bienvenido [Peynado?], who still follows his wishes devotedly. Gen. Trujillo's biographer suggests that in his governing he is guided by an "electric force" from Heaven. He has built roads and pursued other public works, increased the number of public schools, reconstructed the ancient capital of the republic, Santo Domingo, after the 1930 hurricane (and renamed it in his own honor) and enhanced the lot of those persons in his country who are willing to accept his leadership. He is energetic, industrious and a born leader. An inspired biography of him published as a panegyric is revealing for all its encomiums. Progress Through Discipline. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that General Rafael Trujillo hosted a lavish reception at the New York World's Fair aboard his yacht *Ramfis*, formerly owned by American millionaire Julius Fleischmann, before the vessel steamed toward Washington. The article noted Trujillo's fondness for military attire and listed dozens of high foreign orders and medals bestowed upon him across Europe and the Americas. Observers commented that Trujillo possessed more decorations than nearly any other anticipated foreign visitor.

records.summary_en: The *Gazette* contrasted the lavish military honors previously accorded to Latin American dictators like Trujillo with the restrained, informal reception given to visiting Haitian President Sténio Vincent in Washington. Despite Vincent being the sitting president of a nation of 2.6 million, he received no 21-gun salute, fanfare, or military parade, meeting only Undersecretary of State Sumner Welles and a small delegation at the station. Critics questioned the appropriateness of celebrating authoritarian figures while giving a chilly welcome to the head of a neighboring constitutional republic.

records.full_text:
Dominicans to Admit
100,000 Refugees

By the Associated Press.

CIUDAD TRUJILLO, Jan. 31.—A contract signed here between the Dominican government and the Dominican Republic Settlement Association provides for the immediate admisison of some 500 European political refugee families and aims at the establishment of 100,000 refugees over a period of years.

Most of the first group are German Jewish refugees, but the contract does not specify nationalities.

The settlement association will pay for establishing them and is to be reimbursed by income from their lands once they have regained their financial feet.

Welles also returned to Santo Domingo alongside Charles G. Dawes to examine Dominican national finances. These Caribbean experiences helped Welles formulate the non-interventionist diplomatic approach later known as the "Good Neighbor" policy.

Welles también volvió a Santo Domingo junto a Charles G. Dawes para examinar las finanzas públicas de la nación caribeña. Aquellas vivencias en las Antillas contribuyeron a que Welles articulara la doctrina diplomática no intervencionista conocida después como la política del «Buen Vecino».

records.headline: Dominican Republic Boss Bans Discussion of War
records.summary_en: NEA correspondent Thomas J. B. Wenner reports from Ciudad Trujillo that members of the Dominican Republic's only legal political party have been ordered not to discuss the European war, a decree of Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina, the country's virtual dictator. Party director Paino Pichardo explained that Trujillo, an ardent advocate of Pan-Americanism and a friend of the United States, does not wish his work to be made more difficult by sentiments at variance with the country's declared policy, and insisted the agreement applies to party members, not to the population at large. The article profiles Trujillo, 49, president since 1930, whose name the capital bears, and describes the armed forces he has modernized: a standing army of about 4,000 men, a navy of one military transport and several coast guard vessels, and an air force of about 25 planes.

El director del partido, Paino Pichardo, explicó que Trujillo, ardiente defensor del panamericanismo y amigo de los Estados Unidos, no desea que su labor se vea dificultada por sentimientos contrarios a la política declarada del país, e insistió en que el acuerdo se aplica a los miembros del partido, no a toda la población. El artículo perfila a Trujillo, de 49 años, presidente desde 1930, cuyo nombre lleva la capital, y describe las fuerzas armadas que ha modernizado: un ejército permanente de unos 4.000 hombres, una marina de un transporte militar y varias naves guardacostas, y una fuerza aérea de unos 25 aviones.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the State Department agreed to terminate the U.S. customs receivership in the Dominican Republic, restoring duty collections of roughly $4,000,000 annually to Dominican authorities. In exchange, the Dominican Republic granted the United States a first lien on its total revenues, estimated at $12,000,000, to guarantee the servicing of $15,400,000 in external debt. The treaty was negotiated in Ciudad Trujillo by U.S. Ambassador Hugh Wilson and Dominican Foreign Minister Arturo Despradel, ending the 1924 convention.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el Departamento de Estado acordó extinguir la receptoría aduanera estadounidense en la República Dominicana, devolviendo a las autoridades dominicanas la recaudación de tributos, estimada en unos 4.000.000 de dólares anuales. Como contraparte, la República Dominicana concedió a Estados Unidos un gravamen preferente sobre la totalidad de sus rentas fiscales, calculadas en 12.000.000 de dólares, para afianzar el servicio de 15.400.000 dólares de deuda externa. El tratado fue pactado en Ciudad Trujillo por el embajador estadounidense Hugh Wilson y el canciller dominicano Arturo Despradel, poniendo término a la convención de 1924.
records.passage: Terminated by U. S. By the Associated Press. The State Department announced yesterday that the United States had agreed to terminate its receivership of the Dominican Republic customs revenues and restore to that nation the privilege of handling collection of the approximately $4,000,000 annual intake from duties. In turn, the Dominican government agreed to give the United States first lien on total revenues of the Dominican government, a figure roughly estimated at $12,000.000. The department announced that the agreement was reached in Ciudad Trujillo by a United States commission headed by Ambassador Hugh Wilson and a Dominican commission headed by Arturo Despradel, Minister of Foreign Affairs. The agreement, embodied in a convention, terminates the convention of 1934 by which the United States assumed general receivership of customs in order to guarantee the servicing of the Dominican Republic's external debt of 1922 and 1928, computed at $15,400,000. records.summary_en: The *Daily Alaska Empire* reported that several New York creditors, including Louis Sherry, Cartier, Annin Flag Company, and an art gallery, sought payment from General Rafael Trujillo for services and goods provided during the previous year's World's Fair reception. Although creditors hired a lawyer and dispatched a U.S. Marshal to his hotel, Trujillo was shielded from legal action because he held diplomatic immunity as an Ambassador Extraordinary. As a result, creditors were unable to collect the debts or seize his yacht *Ramfis*, docked at the Washington Navy Yard.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Alaska Empire* informó que diversos acreedores neoyorquinos, entre ellos Louis Sherry, Cartier, la Annin Flag Company y una galería de arte, procuraban el cobro de deudas al general Rafael Trujillo por concepto de bienes y atenciones brindados durante la recepción de la Feria Mundial del año anterior. Si bien los acreedores contrataron a un letrado y comisionaron a un alguacil federal (U.S. Marshal) a su hotel, Trujillo quedó a salvo de acciones judiciales en virtud de su inmunidad diplomática como embajador extraordinario. Por consiguiente, los demandantes no pudieron cobrar los créditos ni embargar su yate *Ramfis*, atracado en el Astillero Naval de Washington.

Wilson had previously served as Ambassador to Germany and held various diplomatic posts before focusing on wartime issues in Europe and Latin America.

Mr. Wilson recently negotiated a new customs treaty with the Dominican Republic which is understood now to be ready for submission to the Senate for ratification. His work at the State Department also has been concerned with special problems arising from the war in Europe. Mr. Wilson, who is 55 years old. entered the foreign service in 1911 and has held posts in Lisbon, Guatemala. Buenos Aires, Vienna. Berne and Tokio, as well as Berlin. He also served as chief of the Division of Current Information and as an Assistant Secretary at the State Department. As a protest against Nazi anti-Semitic and other policies, Mr. Wilson was called home from Berlin "for report and consultation" in November, 1938. records.full_text:
Delegates Arriving
For Inter-American
Economic Parley

Welles to Be Keynoter
At Conference Here
Opening Tuesday

By HAROLD B. ROGERS.

As distinguished delegations of finance ministers, heads of central banks, and technical experts from the other American republics continued to arrive over the week-end, plans were being put into final shape for the first Inter-American Conference on Systems of Economic and Financial Control, to open Tuesday at the Pan American Union.

Under the agenda for the conference, which was authorized by the January meeting of Foreign Affairs Ministers at Rio de Janeiro, two different committees will be set up among the delegates. One will consider “international transactions” the other “domestic transactions,” as protection against Axis influence.

The first and last sessions of the conference will be public meetings, but the intervening technical sessions, under present plans probably will be behind closed doors, unless other public sessions “are agreed upon and so ordered by the delegates.” The conference may last about 10 days.

Republics Each Have One Vote.

Each of the 21 republics will have but one vote, regardless of the size of their various delegations.

“Proposals, reports, and projects,” it is provided in the agenda, “shall be considered approved when they have obtained the affirmative vote of an absolute majority of the countries represented at the respective meeting.”

The conference is only one of the several new inter-American developments which have grown out of the second World War to help the American republics present a more united front to the aggressor nations of Germany, Japan and Italy.

Authorized specifically by the Rio Conference of Foreign Ministers, this new gathering is operating under sponsorship of the Inter-American Financial and Economic Advisory Committee. This committee was set up in 1939 and has been regularly functioning since the outbreak of the second World War. At its headquarters in the Pan American Union, this committee, headed by Undersecretary of State Welles, has been holding regularly scheduled meetings and has prepared a comprehensive background of data, which according to experts, should provide much material of value for the forthcoming meeting.

Welles to Be “Keynoter.”

Mr. Welles, who will deliver the opening “keynote” address to the conference, and Dr. Leo S. Rowe, director general of the Pan American Union, who will welcome the delegates, will be followed by a spokesman for the Latin American group. This spokesman will be selected at a preliminary meeting of the delegates tomorrow. There was no official indication today as to who this spokesman may be.

Problems to be considered by the conference, involving the severance of commercial and financial ties between the Western Hemisphere and the Axis powers, are considered by officials to be virtually parallel to the vital issues of breaking diplomatic relations with the Axis, which absorbed major public attention at the Rio conference.

By the terms of two financial and economic resolutions at Rio, it was explained last night by one official, economic intercourse between the American republics and the Axis powers is to be cut; and transactions by nationals of Axis states, likely to benefit members of the tripartite pact (Germany, Italy and Japan) are to be placed under rigid control and supervision.

Other inter-American measures have been adopted to meet economic problems arising out of the war. The Inter-American Development Commission has set up national commissions in each of the Latin-American countries and is especially interested in the development of new industries in each country for which there may be markets in the other republics.

Commission’s Duties.

The Inter-American Maritime Technical Commission, created only a few months ago, is designed primarily to supervise the operation of the immobilized vessels taken over in ports of the American republics. The Office of Co-ordinator of Inter-American Affairs and the Board of Economic Warfare have wide authority and operate extensively in Latin-American affairs.

Over all the American representatives in these agencies, the State Department has exercised a guiding hand, though allowing to some far-reaching autonomy, within the limits of the general international policies laid down by the administration. The Inter-American Defense Board recommends defense measures.

The new program of international solidarity in the economic sphere aimed at by the Rio conference, according to Dr. Rowe, “was nothing short of pooling the resources of the American continent for the winning of the war, and at the same time adopting measures to protect the economic and financial structure of all the republics. The motive that guided the (Rio) delegates,” he added, “was not the selfish interest of any individual state, but the safety and welfare of the entire Western World.”

Many foreign delegations already have arrived and established headquarters. Some are in hotels, others are understood to be established in connection with their embarries or legations. Some of the delegates are ambassadors or ministers.

Brazilian Group Arrives.

Among the first to arrive recently was the group from Brazil. This delegation is headed by Francisco Alves dos Santos, jr., director of exchange, Bank of Brazil. With his technical adviser, Achilles Moreaux of the Bank of Brazil, and other experts he is at the Shoreham Hotel.

Delegates from the other republics, according to the official list, are as follows: Argentina, Eduardo Gagneaux, assistant general manager, Central Bank of Argentina; Bolivia, Humberto Cuenca, general manager, Central Bank of Bolivia; Chile, Pedro Enrique Alfonso, former Minister of Finance; Colombia, Alberto Bayon, chief, Office of Exchange and Import Control; Costa Rica, Paul Gurdian, former Minister of Foreign Affairs and former Minister of Finance; Cuba, Ramiro Guerra Sanchez, representative of Cuba on the Inter-American Financial and Economic Advisory Committee; Dominican Republic, Harry E. Henneman, speci[illegible] representative of the Ministry of Finance and Commerce; Ecuador, Eduardo Icaza, president, Central Bank; El Salvador, Carlos Adalberto Alfaro, charge d’affairs of El Salvador here; Guatemala, Luis Beltranena, dean, School of Economic Scieinces, University of Guatemala; Haiti, Abel La Croix, Minister of Finance; Honduras, Julian R. Caceres, Minister of Honduras here; Mexico, Eduardo Villaseñor, director, Bank of Mexico; Nicaragua, Leon De Bayle, Minister of Nicaragua here; Panama, Ricardo Marciacq, comptroller general of the Republic; Paraguay, Harmodio Gonzalez, manager, Bank of the Republic; Peru, Manuel Gallagher; Uruguay, Roberto E. MacEachen, Minister of Uruguay to Cuba; Venezuela, Diogenes Escalante, Ambasador of Venezuela here.

Ten of the Central American and Caribbean countries have declared war on the Axis, and all other Latin American republics have broken diplomatic relations with the Axis except Argentina and Chile.

The United States delegate will be Edward H. Foley, general counsel of the Treasury Department. He will be assisted by advisers from both the Treasury and State Departments and by L. Werner Knoke, vice president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Representative Hamilton Fish denied being questioned by the Internal Revenue Bureau regarding a $25,000 credit he received from Dominican dictator Rafael L. Trujillo in 1939. Fish stated that he acted solely as an agent in oil speculations, explaining that $12,500 was lost and the remaining $12,500 was returned to Trujillo. Fish added that tax officials had advised him the agency transaction did not need to be declared on his income tax return.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el legislador Hamilton Fish desmintió haber sido interrogado por la Oficina de Rentas Internas en torno a una partida de 25.000 dólares transferida por el dictador dominicano Rafael L. Trujillo en 1939. Fish alegó que se limitó a desempeñarse como comisionista intermediario en especulaciones petrolíferas, precisando que se esfumaron 12.500 dólares y se reembolsó a Trujillo el restante de 12.500. Fish arguyó asimismo que las autoridades impositivas le dictaminaron que dicha intermediación no requería ser asentada en su balance tributario anual.
records.passage: renomination in President Roosevelt's home district, today flatly declared that he had never been questioned by any representative of the Internal Revenue Bureau regarding a $25,000 credit he received from Gen. Rafael L. Trujillo, dictator of the Dominican Republic, in 1939. Mr. Fish discussed over the long distance telephone, from his office at 111 Broadway, New York, the copyrighted account of his dealings with Gen. Trujillo published in the Washington Post today. "There are four points," said Mr. Fish, "in connection with this matter. "First, no representative of the Internal Revenue Bureau has approached me to discuss this credit of $25,000. "Second, I was acting merely as an agent in the matter, in connection with some oil speculations. "Third, there was a total loss of $12,500, and the other $12,500 I returned to Gen. Trujillo. Consulted Bureau on Tax Returns. "Fourth, I wrote a letter to the Internal Revenue Bureau, after consulting two men in that bureau who informed me there was no reason for taking up the matter with the bureau, setting forth the details of the transaction. This was written after my campaign for renomination got under way, comparatively recently. "As a matter of fact, I consulted representatives of the bureau about this credit before I filed my income tax for 1939 and was told that as I was merely an agent, I did not have to Include a statement of the credit in my return." Secretary of the Treasury Morgenthau declined comment on the Fish matter at a press conference

records.headline: Trujillo, “perpetra tor of most outrageous atrocity,” re turned goodwill visit
records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* published a chronology of Representative Hamilton Fish's connections to General Rafael Trujillo, including a 1939 goodwill tour of the Dominican Republic. At a New York banquet that year, Fish praised Trujillo as a builder greater than Spanish conquistadores, even as protesters outside condemned the Dominican generalissimo. The paper noted that $25,000 was deposited to Fish's account as part of a $300,000 credit established for Trujillo through the Dominican Legation before Fish sailed for Europe.
records.summary_es: *The Washington Daily News* insertó una cronología sobre las vinculaciones del legislador Hamilton Fish con el general Rafael Trujillo, recordando su periplo de acercamiento a la República Dominicana realizado en 1939. Durante un banquete en Nueva York aquel año, Fish encumbró a Trujillo ponderándolo como un constructor superior a los conquistadores españoles, al paso que en la vía pública manifestantes fustigaban al generalísimo quisqueyano. El rotativo hizo notar que se giraron 25.000 dólares a la cuenta corriente de Fish mediante una partida de 300.000 dólares habilitada para Trujillo por conducto de la Legación dominicana antes de su viaje a Europa.

This rare picture of a submarine crash-diving for its life was taken as a big Bolingbroke bomber skippered by Warrant Officer C. S. Buchanan of London, Ontario, roared down to the attack. The U-boat, surprised on the surface, is suddenly plunging beneath the water, only its "jumping wires"—designed to ward off mines and nets—appearing above the surface as waves close over it. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported on statements by Dominican Minister Dr. Jesús María Troncoso, who expressed confidence that anti-submarine measures would soon reopen sea lanes for Dominican sugar shipments to Britain while expanding food exports to Puerto Rico. Troncoso asserted that Dominican economic warfare was its main Allied war contribution, defended strong Dominican leaders by comparing them to President Andrew Jackson, and denied that the country was run by a dictatorship. He also praised the agricultural settlement for European refugees established following the 1938 Évian Conference.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* reseñó declaraciones del ministro dominicano Dr. Jesús María Troncoso, quien exteriorizó su convicción de que las operaciones antisubmarinas restablecerían pronto las rutas marítimas para despachar azúcar dominicano hacia Gran Bretaña, incrementando a la par el aprovisionamiento de comestibles para Puerto Rico. Troncoso afirmó que la cooperación económica de su país constituía el aporte bélico medular a la causa aliada, justificó la firmeza de los caudillos patrios equiparándolos con el presidente Andrew Jackson y negó taxativamente que rigiera una dictadura en su patria. Ponderó de igual modo la colonia agrícola de refugiados europeos radicada en el país a consecuencia de la Conferencia de Évian de 1938.
records.passage: States and the Dominican Republic. He is optimistic in regard to the sugar problem, although shipping of the Republic's sugar has been interfered with seriously. He is sure that by the end of next year the Nazi U-boats will have been sufficiently checked to allow for the shipment of the mounting sugar supply to its British markets. Many other exports are sent to the United States. Senor Troncoso's government is developing the exportation of food to nearby Puerto Rico, which is facing an acute food shortage. Though the Republic has an army and navy, the economic warfare they wage is their most effective contribution toward an Allied victory. Unlike her friendly sister republic, Haiti, which is basically French, the tongue and customs of the Dominican Republic are from Spain. The government is modeled after that of the United States and the people enjoy freedom of press and speech. Dr. Troncoso explains that the leaders of the republic often have been strong men who bore out the strength of their convictions with action, but who, nevertheless, were far from being dictators. He compares these leaders to the American President Andrew Jackson, whose opinions in his time brought down cries of dictator. Dr. Troncoso praises the success of the refugee settlement in his country, an idea originated by the republic at the Evian Conference in France in 1939. The agricultural settlement was tested on a scientific basis, with a group of refugees from Europe selected for youth and health and character.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Captain Maurice Marshall Berck, an Army surgeon attached to Walter Reed Hospital, died from severe burns sustained in an apartment fire at the Brighton Hotel. Berck, a prominent New York chest surgeon who married Flor de Oro Trujillo in March 1942, had just returned to Washington from visiting his wife in New York. Firefighters found him unconscious on the floor of the ablaze room, and the cause of the fire remained undetermined.

Berck, prestigioso facultativo torácico neoyorquino que contrajo nupcias con Flor de Oro Trujillo en marzo de 1942, acababa de regresar a Washington tras visitar a su cónyuge en Nueva York. Los bomberos lo hallaron sin sentido tendido en el piso de la habitación envuelta en llamas, sin determinarse el origen del siniestro.

Although the war has brought its usual quota of shipping and trade problems. Particularly welcome have been orders from the U. S. War Department for Haitian coffee. Haitian sisal, too. is proving a valuable fiber to take the place of some of this lost raw material of the Orient, while rubber planting there also is expected to help meet war needs. records.headline: Roosevelt nominated Boaz Long of New Mexico, a native of Warsaw
records.summary_en: The *Daily Monitor Leader* reported that President Roosevelt nominated incumbent ministers across the Caribbean and Central America to become ambassadors, including Avra M. Warren in the Dominican Republic and John Campbell White in Haiti. Under the White House plan, the elevated envoys would continue receiving their ministerial salaries of $10,000 instead of the usual $17,500 ambassadorial pay. Other diplomats nominated for ambassadorial rank included Boaz Long, Robert M. Scotten, and James B. Stewart.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Monitor Leader* informó que el presidente Roosevelt propuso ascender al rango de embajadores a los ministros titulares de varias legaciones en Centroamérica y las Antillas, entre ellos Avra M. Warren en la República Dominicana y John Campbell White en Haití. Según lo dispuesto por la Casa Blanca, los dignatarios promovidos mantendrían sus emolumentos de ministro de 10.000 dólares anuales, en lugar de los 17.500 dólares asignados habitualmente a una embajada. Otros representantes nominados comprendieron a Boaz Long, Robert M. Scotten y James B. Stewart.
records.passage: Mr. Roosevelt nominated Boaz Long of New Mexico, a native of Warsaw, Ind., now ambassador to Ecuador, to be ambassador to Guatemala. Robert M. Scotten, of Detroit. Mich now minister to Costa Rica, was selected to succeed Long as ambassador to Ecuador. Fay A. [Desportes?] of Winnsboro, S. C., now minister to Guatemala, was nominated ambassador to Costa Rica. The other elevations were made by nominating the incumbent ministers to be ambassadors. Those involved were James B. Stewart of New Mexico, a native of Philadelphia, in Nicaragua, Walter Thurston of Arizona, a native of Colorado in El Salvador, John D. Erwin of Chattanooga, Tenn., in Honduras, Avra M. records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported on the diplomatic elevation of missions between the United States and seven Caribbean and Central American nations, including the Dominican Republic and Haiti, from legations to full embassies. Under reciprocal agreements, the respective ministers were elevated to ambassadors, leaving Canada as the only Western Hemisphere mission remaining at ministerial rank. Latin American diplomats gathered in Washington to celebrate the confirmations and exchange congratulations.
records.summary_es: *The Washington Daily News* reseñó el acto solemne de jerarquización institucional por el cual las misiones mutuas entre Estados Unidos y siete repúblicas centroamericanas y antillanas —entre ellas la República Dominicana y Haití— fueron elevadas de legaciones a embajadas de primera clase. Conforme a convenios de reciprocidad, los respectivos ministros pasaron a ser embajadores extraordinarios, quedando Canadá como la única sede diplomática continental que conservaba rango de legación. Los dignatarios hispanoamericanos se congregaron en Washington para festejar las acreditaciones e intercambiar salutaciones de estilo.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Flor de Oro Trujillo, daughter of Dominican President Rafael Trujillo, arrived en route to Washington to assume duties as first secretary of the Dominican Embassy. Miss Trujillo, whose husband Captain Maurice Berck died in an accident four months prior, expressed her desire to study international law, pursue diplomacy, and observe American women's customs to introduce them to her home country. She noted that she was fluent in Portuguese, German, French, and English in addition to Spanish.

La señorita Trujillo, cuyo cónyuge, el capitán Maurice Berck, pereciera en un infortunio cuatro meses antes, exteriorizó su inclinación hacia el estudio del derecho internacional, el ejercicio diplomático y el conocimiento de las costumbres cívicas de la mujer estadounidense para aplicarlas en su tierra natal. Añadió que dominaba a la perfección el portugués, alemán, francés e inglés, además de su castellano natal.

Miss Trujillo, daughter of the President of the Dominican Republic, arrived yesterday en route to Washington, where she will assume her post as first secretary to the Dominican Embassy. "This is a big chance my father has given me." the attractive brunette declared, "and I am going to study hard so that I will not disappoint him." The young diplomat has spent the last two years, until the past month, in the United States, as the wife of Capt. Maurice Berck. Capt. Berck. she said, was killed in an accident In Washington four months ago. Miss Trujillo, who was educated abroad, said she plans to pursue a diplomatic career and will study international law. She already speaks four languages in addition to Spanish—Portuguese, German, French and English. She was to leave today by plane for New York, where she will spend a week before assuming her post. records.full_text:
Don Anselmo Copello
Funeral Arranged
For Tomorrow

Members of the diplomatic corps and high Government officials will attend funeral services for Don Anselmo Copello, Ambassador from the Dominican Republic, at 11 a.m tomorrow at the Sacred Heart Church, Sixteenth street and Park road N.W. After temporary burial in Arlington Cemetery, the body will be taken to the Dominican Republic.

The Ambassador, who was 65, died yesterday in Doctors Hospital of a heart attack which followed pneumonia. He had been ill two days.

His work was praised in the following statement made yesterday by Secretary of State Stettinius:

“I have been greatly grieved to learn of the death of the distinguished Ambassador of the Dominican Republic. His excellency Anselmo Copella. In my association with him in dealing with the problems of mutual interest, I have come to know his outstanding qualities as a diplomat and as a friend.

“He has represented his country with distinction and has always evinced a most helpful spirit of cooperation in dealing with matters of common concern. The Dominican people will rightly mourn the passing of a gifted statesman and his many friends in this country will sincerely share their sorrow.”

Senor Copello returned to Washington Monday from the Dominican Republic, where he had been on official business for three months. He was accompanied by his only son, Jeronimo.

Before his appointment as Ambassador to this country in November, 1943, Senor Copello had never served as a government official except for several honorary posts. His credentials were received by President Roosevelt on December 20, 1943. He succeeded Dr. J. M. Troncoso, now Secretary of the Treasury of the Dominican Republic.

President of the principal tobacco company of the Dominican Republic, Senor Copello’s home was in Santiago.

Besides his widow, Senora de Copello, and his son, he is survived by four daughters, Adelina, Argentina, Ileana and Margarita. The family lives at the Embassy, 4530 Sixteenth street N.W.

Dr. J. R. Rodriguez, Minister Counselor, will direct the affairs of the Embassy until further arrangements are made by his government.

records.headline: Americas Plan Slap at Franco
records.summary_en: Consultations are under way among the foreign offices of the American nations over a simultaneous diplomatic break with the government of Generalissimo Francisco Franco in Spain, after the Uruguayan Senate forwarded a recommendation for a break and both houses of the Peruvian Congress approved one. In Central America and the Caribbean, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, the Dominican Republic and Haiti have already broken relations with Franco, and Mexico never recognized his dictatorship. A State Department spokesman in Washington denied a report that the United States and other American nations had agreed on a collective break, but other sources predicted that further diplomatic breaks with Spain could be expected.

En Centroamérica y el Caribe, Guatemala, Honduras, Panamá, la República Dominicana y Haití ya han roto relaciones con Franco, y México nunca reconoció su dictadura. Named to the post by his friend, revolutionary president Rómulo Betancourt, he will oversee the government's relations with American oil companies and other foreign investors, and has assured them he will respect their rights. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on an interview with President Rafael Trujillo in which he announced plans to encourage a two- or three-party system with free elections during the 450th anniversary of Santo Domingo. Trujillo denied operating as a dictator, asserting that his critics had private motives, and pledged to grant amnesty to all political refugees to allow their safe return. He stated that the nation had achieved stability ahead of the presidential election scheduled for May 16, 1947.

records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican reported on the extensive modernization of the Dominican Republic under President Rafael Trujillo over a sixteen-year span achieved without foreign loans. Improvements included a twenty percent decrease in illiteracy, hundreds of newly built schools, seventy new bridges, and irrigation projects reclaiming 85,000 acres. The article noted that the rebuilt capital, renamed Ciudad Trujillo by citizens, was growing into a major Caribbean tourist destination.

Los adelantos abarcaban una reducción del veinte por ciento en el analfabetismo, centenares de escuelas recién levantadas, setenta puentes nuevos e infraestructuras de regadío que recuperaron 85.000 acres de tierra. El informe agregaba que la reconstruida capital, rebautizada Ciudad Trujillo por la población, se afianzaba como un emporio turístico caribeño de primer orden.

Illiteracy dropped 20 per cent due to the building of hundreds of new schools and the allotment of 13 per cent of the national budget to furthering education. Beautifully paved roads and 70 new bridges put formerly isolated regions into easy communication with one another and with the capital. Vast irrigation projects brought 85,000 acres of land under cultivation. Factories employ twice as many people and produce three times as many exportable items as previously. New hospitals. clothing manufacture, water works, schools and public buildings transformed an ancient city of ruins into a modern metropolis. records.summary_en: Eyewitness reports from Matanzas, on the north coast, said a tidal wave from Sunday's earthquake swept as much as a mile inland, catching even a party fleeing by automobile, and left only eight of the town's 300 houses standing. Residents had taken refuge in trees and high places, and reports from Matanzas and Nagua said frightened inhabitants in the forests were suffering from hunger, with authorities considering dropping food from airplanes, as wrecked communications made the damage across more than 11 towns hard to assess.

Los vecinos se habían refugiado en árboles y lugares altos, y los informes de Matanzas y Nagua decían que habitantes asustados en los bosques padecían hambre, mientras las autoridades consideraban lanzar alimentos desde aviones y las comunicaciones destruidas dificultaban evaluar los daños en más de 11 pueblos.

In Haiti, President Dumarsais Estime dissolved the Communist Party by decree after Washington withheld a $20,000,000 loan needed for debt retirement and agricultural development. Similar anti-communist actions were noted in Brazil under President Dutra and Venezuela under President Betancourt.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que Brasil, Venezuela y Haití emprendían severas purgas anticomunistas con miras a captar auxilios y beneficios crediticios de los Estados Unidos. En Haití, el gobernante Dumarsais Estimé ilegalizó el Partido Comunista mediante decreto luego de que Washington suspendiera una partida financiera de 20.000.000 de dólares vital para redimir deuda y financiar planes agrarios. Represalias ideológicas similares fueron adoptadas en el Brasil presidido por Dutra y en la Venezuela del presidente Betancourt.

Now the party has been dissolved by presidential decree, and the Haitian government says it is not Communist. Behind this move is refusal of the United States to lend Haiti $20,100,000 to pay off its old debt to Uncle Sam and embark on an industrialization and agricultural expansion program. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican Ambassador Julio Ortega Frier alleged an army of 3,000 revolutionaries recruited from Cuba, Guatemala, Venezuela, and Puerto Rico was preparing in Cuba to invade and overthrow President Rafael Trujillo. Officials from Cuba, Guatemala, and Venezuela denied the allegations, while reports of an expedition leaving eastern Cuba remained unconfirmed. The U.S. State Department acknowledged hearing rumors of the invasion force but refrained from commenting due to insufficient evidence.

Autoridades de Cuba, Guatemala y Venezuela rechazaron las imputaciones, mientras no se confirmaban las versiones del zarpe de una flotilla armada desde el oriente cubano. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican Ambassador Julio Ortega Frier claimed an invasion expedition comprising two landing craft and a corvette had sailed from Cuba, accompanied by at least seven aircraft. A search started, and airports along both Florida coasts were checked without success, as were other Gulf areas. Meanwhile no Washington agency could be found that would admit ordering the alert.

Then, yesterday afternoon, the State Department acknowledged it had heard the rumor and said it had relayed it to the Customs Bureau and other agencies for investigation.

The statement disclosed that the State Department has had in effect for months a general alert, based on “general rumors of revolutionary plotting,” to make sure that “United States territory would not be used for conspiracy.”

Rumor Involves 7 Planes.

The statement, issued by Press Officer Reginald Mitchell, said the State Department has been receiving “rumors” and “fragmentary reports” of impending trouble in the Caribbean area but has declined to comment because of their unsubstantial nature. The statement continued:

“One such rumor was to the effect that there were seven combat planes at an airfield in Florida ready to depart for a Caribbean destination. The department Friday immediately communicated this rumor to the Customs Bureau and other United States Government agencies concerned and requested that an investigation be made and that these alleged planes be prevented from leaving the United States.

“The department has been informed that the Customs Bureau promptly notified its Florida headquarters office at Tampa which in turn alerted its subordinate customs offices at Miami, Jacksonville, West Palm Beach and elsewhere in Florida. The department has received no further information in this particular matter.

“The department heard general rumors of revolutionary plotting in the Caribbean area as long ago as January of this year and in an effort to make sure that United States territory would not be used for conspiracy alerted the appropriate law enforcement agencies, which since that date have kept a scrupulous watch.”

Easy Flight for Fighters.

At least some of the rumors were based on reports in Haitian and Dominican newspapers.

The P38 Lightning and the P51 Mustang, Army fighter planes extensively used in the war, would easily be able to fly from Florida to the Dominican Republic. The shortest airline distance is a little over 650 miles. There are the Bahama Islands and the tip of Cuba in between.

A War Department official said some Lightnings and Mustangs have been sold as surplus and may be in the hands of civilians.

“There are plenty of young fellows in this country who know how to fly these ships,” he said.

The Dominican Ambassador, Julio Ortega Frier, told a reporter some days ago that he knew the revolutionaries had at least seven planes. He said yesterday he didn’t know where these planes were bought.

Reported Sailing.

The Ambassador said last Saturday that an army of 3,000 “Communist revolutionaries” from Cuba, Guatemala, Venezuela and Puerto Rico was poised in Cuba for an invasion. The governments concerned denied it.

Thursday night he said two landing craft and one corvette had sailed from Cuba with invasion forces, but he had no further word on this.

The Ambassador said a call to Ciudad Trujillo produced this information:

“The government has air patrols around the coast. Everything is calm in Ciudad Trujillo and not a single aircraft has been heard in the sky. Nevertheless, the government is taking all precautions.”

Haitians returning from the Dominican Republic were quoted in Port-au-Prince newspapers as saying they left because of apprehension over heavy troop movements throughout the republic, which shares the island of Haiti.

records.summary_en: A historical account traces the United States customs receivership to the Dominican resolution of March 31, 1905, known as the Modus Vivendi, which conceded to the United States the same rights over customs income as an earlier pact. It states that the Dominican-American Covenant signed February 8, 1907, gave the United States President the right to name a General Receiver of Customs to collect all Dominican customs taxes until government bonds issued to settle debts were paid and retired.
records.summary_es: Un recuento histórico atribuye la receptoría aduanera estadounidense a la resolución dominicana del 31 de marzo de 1905, conocida como Modus Vivendi, que concedió a Estados Unidos los mismos derechos sobre los ingresos aduaneros que un pacto anterior. Señala que el Convenio domínico-estadounidense firmado el 8 de febrero de 1907 dio al presidente de Estados Unidos el derecho de nombrar un Receptor General de Aduanas para recaudar todos los impuestos aduaneros dominicanos hasta que se pagaran y retiraran los bonos gubernamentales emitidos para saldar deudas.

The Pact of February 7 of the same year re-affirmed these decisions; but since this was not satisfactory to the Congress of the United States because it did not approve the method employed by President Theodore Roosevelt in concluding this Pact, the Dominican Government itself, by the Resolution of March 31, 1905, conceded unilaterally to the United States the same rights that the Covenant has ceded it upon our customs income. THE COVENANT OF 1907 On February 8, 1907, the Dominican American Covenant was signed. It succeeded in obtaining the constitutional sanction of the Congress of the Republic and of the Senate of the United States. This Treaty gave to the President of the United States the right to name a General Receiver of Customs to collect all customs taxes of the Dominican Republic until payment and retirement of Dominican Government bonds which were to be issued for the purpose of settling its debts. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that federal customs authorities in Baltimore detained the *Patria*, a converted infantry landing craft suspected of involvement in anti-Trujillo activities. An investigation revealed the vessel was manned largely by affluent Dominican exiles and had been acquired by Cuban Cruz Alonso, though a search found no weapons or ammunition. The State Department stated the action enforced strict policy prohibiting the use of United States territory to launch civil strife in foreign nations.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que la policía aduanera federal destacada en Baltimore aprehendió al *Patria*, un buque de desembarco de infantería modificado sospechoso de involucramiento en actividades conspirativas contra Trujillo. Las pesquisas comprobaron que la dotación estaba formada mayoritariamente por acaudalados desterrados dominicanos y que la nave había sido adquirida por el cubano Cruz Alonso, si bien el registro ocular no arrojó hallazgo de municiones ni fusiles. El Departamento de Estado aclaró que la retención obedecía a la estricta política neutral de proscribir la utilización del suelo estadounidense para fraguar expediciones bélicas contra Estados soberanos.
records.passage: The newspaper said its investigation of State Department detention of a converted infantry landing craft in Baltimore Harbor disclosed the ship's "crew” was composed largely of Dominican exiles who “hated” Rafael L. Trujillo, for 17 years President of the republic. Customs officials ordered the 153 foot landing craft detained yesterday. A State Department spokesman said in Washington the action was in line with its instructions to the Federal Bureau of Investigation and other Government agencies to prevent the use of territory in this country as a possible base of operations to promote civil strife elsewhere. The Evening Sun said its investigation disclosed that nearly 40 men were aboard the LCI at one time, although a normal crew is 12 or 14, and that most of them “looked like college boys” and were either exiles or sons of exiles who had lost large land holdings under the Trujillo regime. Most of the "crew" had left “by last night.” the paper reported, and conversations aboard indicated many of them were from fairly wealthy families" and “were not Communists." Customs authorities announced yesterday that a search of the vessel for arms and ammunition had been fruitless. Workers at the ship repair yard where she was tied up were preparing today to seal her doors. The Evening Sun said the ship, called the Patria. originally was sold to a Cuban named Cruz Alonso by a New York ship broker and moved here for repairs from an anchorage on the James River in Virginia. Franco criticizing former Secretary of State Cordell Hull for congratulating President Rafael Trujillo on paying off the Dominican foreign debt. Franco condemned Hull's praise as inappropriate, accusing Trujillo of seizing power through treason in 1930 and maintaining control through terror and murder. Franco appealed to democratic nations to support the Dominican people in reclaiming their freedom rather than endorsing the dictatorship.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Cuban political leaders sharply condemned President Ramon Grau San Martin following the Cuban army's suppression of a 1,500-man expedition organized to invade the Dominican Republic. Senators Eduardo Chibas and Aurelio Alvarez accused Grau of using the anti-Trujillo movement to destabilize Cuban politics and consolidate personal dictatorial power. Military authorities detained over 1,100 expedition members and seized four ships along with extensive stockpiles of arms and explosives.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que destacados dirigentes políticos de Cuba enjuiciaron con dureza al presidente Ramón Grau San Martín tras la desarticulación por el ejército cubano de una expedición de 1.500 combatientes aprestada para invadir la República Dominicana. Los senadores Eduardo Chibás y Aurelio Álvarez acusaron a Grau de instrumentalizar la conspiración antitrujillista para subvertir el orden interno de Cuba y afianzar prerrogativas dictatoriales propias. Las fuerzas castrenses arrestaron a más de 1.100 conjurados e incautaron cuatro embarcaciones mercantes y nutridos arsenales de pertrechos, proyectiles y dinamita.
records.passage: Prensa Libre that the Cuban President "betrayed the cause of Dominican liberty after having offered hospitality and refuge to the political exiles of this sister republic." Move for Dictatorship Charged. "Grau, upon the pretext of liberating the Dominican Republic from the dictator (President Rafael) Trujillo, was conspiring to suspend the forthcoming elections and convert himself into the dictator of Cuba," Senator Chibas' statement said. The Senator previously had been considered one of the President's staunchest defenders. Senator Aurelio Alvarez, leader of the opposition, accused President Grau of having "armed gangs which sought to invade the Dominican Republic, in order to create an atmosphere of violence in Cuba and thus perpetuate himself in power." Some of the expedition's leaders were reported to be among this latter group.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Cuban magistrate Evelio Tabio ordered the release of nearly 1,200 participants in the aborted anti-Trujillo invasion expedition, holding only its purported leaders in custody. A captured diary published by the newspaper *Hoy* detailed training at Holguin and miserable conditions on Cayo Confites, where troops endured internal infighting, accidental drownings, and failed logistics aboard vessels including the *Aurora*, *Berta*, and *Angelita*. The collapse of the operation culminated in mass surrenders at Guinchos Cay and Antilla.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el magistrado judicial cubano Evelio Tabío dispuso la libertad de casi 1.200 integrantes de la frustrada expedición armada antitrujillista, reteniendo en presidio únicamente a los sindicados como cabecillas principales. Un diario de bitácora ocupado y divulgado por el diario *Hoy* detalló los adiestramientos castrenses en Holguín y las precarias penalidades sufridas en Cayo Confites, donde los reclutas padecieron motines internos, ahogamientos accidentales y severos descalabros de abasto a bordo de los barcos *Aurora*, *Berta* y *Angelita*. El fracaso del complot culminó con rendiciones multitudinarias en Cayo Guinchos y la bahía de Antilla.

In the meantime, Magistrate Evelio Tabio of the supreme tribunal of the Criminal Court announced that only the purported leaders of the expeditionary force would be kept in custody after today. Nearly 1,200 others now being held will be released. About 725 members of the expedition who surrendered Tuesday at the port of Antilla arrived here last night by train to join 360 others who were picked up earlier from Guinchos Cay, a sandspit off the Cuban coast. Mr. Tabio did not disclose the names of those he considered to be the leaders, nor their number. Hoy withheld the name of the trooper who wrote the diary. The diary's account: The volunteer enlisted July 20 for the campaign against President Rafael Trujillo, was trained at Holquin and then transferred with other revolutionaries from a coastal point to Confites Key. The diary said the men were moved aboard the ships Aurora and Berta and a Dominican schooner registered as the Angelita, which the expeditionary force captured near Confites Keys. Two volunteers drowned while being disembarked. One was a Cuban, the other a Venezuelan. One man was killed and some others were wounded in fighting among themselves. The troops became discontented over delays in action against the Dominican Republic. On August 16, which was D-day, a ship expected to arrive with war material and food did not make port. records.summary_en: Twenty-six alleged chiefs of a 1,007-man expeditionary force to depose President Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic were freed in Havana under bonds of $5,000 each. Special Magistrate Evelio Tabio charged them with jeopardizing the peace of the state and taking enlistments without authorization of the Cuban government. The group, mostly Dominicans and Cubans, included eight generals; the rest of the force, including three men from the United States, had been freed after surrendering on Guinchos Cay and at Antilla.
records.summary_es: Veintiséis presuntos jefes de una fuerza expedicionaria de 1,007 hombres para deponer al presidente Rafael Trujillo de la República Dominicana fueron liberados en La Habana bajo fianzas de $5,000 cada uno. El magistrado especial Evelio Tabio los acusó de poner en peligro la paz del Estado y de realizar alistamientos sin autorización del gobierno cubano. El grupo, en su mayoría dominicanos y cubanos, incluía ocho generales; el resto de la fuerza, incluidos tres hombres de Estados Unidos, había sido liberado tras rendirse en Cayo Guinchos y en Antilla.
records.passage: As additional sacrifices to buttress his aid-for-Europe campaign, launched formally with See BROADCAST On Page Two REBEL CHIEFTAINS FREED ON BONDS Special Magistrate Grants Bail Of $5,000 Each To 26 Men HAVANA, Oct. 5 —(UP)—Twenty-six alleged chiefs of a 1,007 man expeditionary force to depose President Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic were freed today under bonds of $5,000 each. Special Magistrate Evelio Tabio of the Supreme Tribunal accepted the bonds from a security company, which refused to say for whom it was acting Judge Tabio had ordered the 26 men charged with “having jeopardized the peace of the state” and having taken enlistments “without legal authorization of the Cuban government.” The group, mostly Dominicans and Cubans, included eight generals. The rest of the force was freed last week. Three men from the United States were among those released yesterday. They were Hollis Smith, 26, of Palisades Park, N.J. and Rupert E. Waddel, 27, and Thomas Sawyer, 26, both of New York city. The force surrendered to Cuban authorities early last week on Guinchos Cay off the North Cuban coast and at the port of Antilla.

records.headline: 9.— Manolo Castro, director of the Cuban Sports Commission, charged yesterday
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Manolo Castro, head of the Cuban Sports Commission, pleaded not guilty in federal court in Jacksonville to charges of illegally exporting weapons and explosives intended for an uprising against Dominican President Rafael Trujillo. Castro alleged that Trujillo's personal hostility was behind his indictment. Co-defendants Chester L. Miller and Percy H. Cyr also pleaded not guilty, while Hollis B. Smith entered a guilty plea to purchasing the munitions.

Castro alegó que su encausamiento respondía al encono personal que Trujillo le profesaba. Los coacusados Chester L. Miller y Percy H. Cyr sostuvieron igualmente su no culpabilidad, mientras que Hollis B. Smith admitió formalmente los cargos de adquisición ilícita de armas.

Cuban Blames Trujillo For Arms Plot Charges By the Associated Press JACKSONVILLE, Fla., Dec. 9.— Manolo Castro, director of the Cuban Sports Commission, charged yesterday that enmity of Rafael Trujillo was responsible for his implication in an alleged plot to export arms to Cuba for use in an unsuccessful revolt against the Dominican Republic President last summer. Castro, who came to Jacksonville for arraignment on an indictment charging illegal exportation of arms and high explosives from the United States, pleaded not guilty before Federal Judge Louie W. Strum. The case was set for trial January 5. Not guilty pleas also were entered by Chester L. Miller and Percy H. Cyr, both airplane pilots of Hasbrouck Heights, N. J. Hollis B. Smith, Palisades Park, N. J.. who is alleged to have purchased the arms, pleaded guilty. Smith was permitted to remain under bond pending disposition of the charges against the other defendants. He was a native of McDonald Mills, Va.

records.summary_en: The Daily Alaska Empire reported that a Venezuelan White Paper accused Dominican President Rafael Trujillo of stockpiling vast Brazilian arms shipments, transported via his presidential yacht, for potential aggression against Venezuela. Venezuelan authorities highlighted imports of 10,000 rifles and 800 machine guns as exceeding legitimate Dominican defense requirements. While asserting a right to sever diplomatic ties, the Venezuelan government affirmed it would not initiate hostilities unless compelled to defend its sovereignty.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Alaska Empire* informó que un Libro Blanco emitido por el gobierno de Venezuela denunció al gobernante dominicano Rafael Trujillo por acopiar voluminosos envíos de material de guerra procedentes del Brasil, trasladados a bordo de su yate oficial de recreo, con propósitos de agresión territorial contra suelo venezolano. La cancillería venezolana remarcó que las compras de 10.000 fusiles y 800 ametralladoras desbordaban con creces las urgencias ordinarias de defensa de la nación caribeña. Pese a arrogarse la prerrogativa de quebrar los tratos bilaterales, el régimen de Caracas aseguró que no desencadenaría hostilidades salvo que se viera forzado a salvaguardar su territorio nacional.

records.summary_en: A White Paper circulated by the Venezuelan Embassy charged that the Dominican Republic was plotting to send an armed invasion against Venezuela, accusing dictator Trujillo of harboring Venezuelan enemies and purchasing arms for them in Brazil. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Organization of American States referred the dispute between Haiti and the Dominican Republic over Col. Astrel Roland's subversive broadcasts to a peace commission, which advised direct bilateral negotiations. Haitian diplomats stated the broadcasts caused widespread unrest that necessitated declaring a state of siege to maintain public order. While Dominican authorities defended the broadcasts under free speech on a private station, Haitian officials contended the station was controlled by President Trujillo's brother.

El cuerpo diplomático haitiano adujo que las emisiones agitaron graves conmociones que forzaron a la promulgación del estado de sitio para restablecer la paz pública. records.summary_en: The Key West Citizen published an editorial describing President Rafael Trujillo's dictatorial grip on the Dominican Republic, asserting that citizens lived in fear of enforced disappearances and state repression. The article portrayed Trujillo traveling in armored convoys out of fear for his safety and enriching himself openly with national public revenues. It observed that these oppressive conditions inspired foreign volunteers, including Americans, to join a recent anti-Trujillo invasion attempt that ended as a poorly planned fiasco.

The Dominican Information Center stated that President Rafael Trujillo initiated domestic arms production after the U.S. State Department denied purchases of American war surplus arms following the 1947 Cayo Confites invasion attempt. Plans called for expanding the factory to produce ammunition, heavy artillery, and aircraft engines.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on regional political polarization pitting Cuba, Guatemala, and Costa Rica against the authoritarian regimes of Rafael Trujillo in the Dominican Republic and Anastasio Somoza in Nicaragua. While the United States maintained a policy of non-intervention, diplomats debated proposals by Panama's Ricardo J. Alfaro urging the Organization of American States to deny recognition to regimes seizing power through coups. Observers emphasized that enduring democratic stability in the Caribbean would require addressing deep-seated socioeconomic grievances.

records.full_text:
Dominican Republic
Asks New Airing of
Dispute With Cuba

By the Associated Press

A long-standing feud between Cuba and the Dominican Republic was spotlighted yesterday when the Dominican government formally asked for another airing of troubles between the two countries.

The development occurred in an exchange of notes between the Dominican government and the five-nation Inter-American Peace Committee.

The latter group was set up by the 21 hemisphere foreign ministers in 1940 to seek peaceful settlement of Inter-American disputes. The United States, Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Cuba are members.

After three weeks of discussion the committee Thursday night sent a note to the Dominican government expressing concern over special war powers granted to President Rafael Trujillo. The Dominican Republic replied that they resulted from a “profound state of emergency” in the Caribbean.

War Powers Granted.

Trujillo got from the Dominican Congress this month power to declare war on any country which he considers is harboring plotters working against him.

The move was directed to Cuba where Mr. Trupillo charged a new attempt to mount an invasion of the Dominican Republic is going on. This was strongly denied by Cuba.

The committee’s note asked Mr. Trujillo not to use force unless under armed attack in accordance with terms of the Rio mutual defense treaty.

In reply, Dominican Secretary of State Virgilio Diaz Ordonez said “no other country or government would fail to act in the same way as we are doing now.” But he added that the republic would respond to any conciliatory gesture to end the “abnormality with which we are confronted.”

His note added the government is ready to receive recommendations from the committee.

The feud between the two Caribbean nations is an old story to the committee. In 1948, the group got the two nations to agree to settle their differences through diplomatic channels. The Dominican charge then was based on an unsuccessful attempt in 1947 by various groups of exiles to create an invasion force in Cuba to overthrow Mr. Trujillo.

The following year the Dominicans went before the committee with the assertion the same group was being outfitted anew in Cuba.

A few months ago the committee issued a 14-point statement designed to calm Caribbean tension after an airborne invasion of the Dominican Republic failed.

In the meantime, it settled a flareup between the neighboring Dominican Republic and Haiti when the latter charged Mr. Trujillo was personally involved in a plot to ove-thorw the Port-au-Prince government.

Sanchez Arango argued that the ship was seized near Cape San Antonio, far from Dominican territory, and threatened to take the case to the United Nations and the World Court if Cuban crewmen were not freed. records.full_text:
SERVICE BY KEFAUVER

For a long time, I have been wondering about that Kefauver television show. Did it really accomplish something constructive? Obviously, it made Rudolph Halley a figure in New York politics and encouraged Estes Kefauver himself to run for President on the Democratic side.

Was that all?

Apparently, it is not so. I have received a circular from the Dominican Republic Information Center which is devoted to advertising the aforesaid Republic where Christopher Columbus is buried. According to the circular, the Dominican Republic is progressive and takes advantage of every opportunity. Therefore, as Kefauver drove gambling out of the United States, the Dominican Republic made gambling the cultural tie between the United States and the other Republic. The circular says:

“Gambling-in-the-sky via slot machines will feature a four-hour plane flight by the ‘Sportsmen’s Special,’ between Miami and Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic—the ‘Monte Carlo of the Caribbean’ where four legal gambling casinos flourish, if final flight negotiations are completed this week. Three of the casinos have opened since the Kefauver Crime Investigation closed many illegal gambling places in the U.S.

“Service by the 50-passenger chartered plane ‘Lady Luck’ is scheduled to commence on or about March 7 from Miami. The plane, though owned by the (CDA) Compania Dominicana de Aviacion, a Pan-American subsidiary, would be chartered to a sponsoring promotion group to begin the week-end round-trips between Miami and the West Indies country. The Dominican Government itself is not sponsoring the project but approves of it.”

In addition to approving of the slot-machines and other devices, the Dominican Government sends me this circular through the mails. If any American sent a similar circular through the mails, he would probably go to jail. But then Americans no longer count in the United States except to pay taxes and to have their sons conscripted for United Nations police actions.

I forgot to save the envelope in which this circular came and therefore I cannot tell you whether it used a paid-for stamp or came as diplomatic mail, free of charge. I get a lot of that kind of mail, all free, the object of which is always to educate me to love some foreign country. But if anyone wants to send some mail about loving America, a paid-for stamp is essential. It is a fine point, this business of who pays to have mail delivered advocating love.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that seven demonstrators from New York picketed outside a Washington office building during a diplomatic reception held by General Rafael Trujillo at the nearby Mayflower Hotel. Police enforced regulations barring demonstrations within 500 feet of the hotel, and the peaceful picketers displayed placards accusing Trujillo of political murders during his presidency. Trujillo was serving as Dominican minister of finance and chief United Nations delegate, while his brother Hector B. Trujillo held the presidency.

Domini can Republic. Oct. 27.—Michael Patrick O'Brien landed in his new homeland yesterday after shuttling about the world for nearly two years. O'Brien told reporters after flying here from Rio de Janeiro that he has no immediate plans. He expressed gratitude to the Dominican government, which invited him to this country. O'Brien. 58, told reporters he was born in Tacoma. Wash., and that he considers himself a United States citizen. The United States Department of Immigration has denied, however, that he is a citizen. The wanderer said the mixup occurred after he served nearly seven years in prison in Oregon on a holdup charge. He said he had not committed the hold up. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Dominican government stripped Porfirio Rubirosa of his diplomatic post as embassy counselor in Paris and revoked his diplomatic status citing scandalous personal conduct. Rubirosa's dismissal followed his naming as co-respondent in high-profile divorce litigation in London and the United States. His history of celebrity marriages included unions with Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's daughter Flor de Oro, French actress Danielle Darrieux, and American heiress Doris Duke.

La destitución de Rubirosa se produjo luego de ser señalado como codemandado en sonados litigios de divorcio en Londres y Estados Unidos. Su historial de matrimonios con celebridades incluía enlaces con la hija del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, Flor de Oro, la actriz francesa Danielle Darrieux y la heredera estadounidense Doris Duke.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported international reactions to Guatemalan accusations alleging a foreign conspiracy against President Jacobo Arbenz's government. The Dominican Foreign Ministry dismissed the charges as communist fabrications, denying any involvement with Guatemala or the Arbenz regime. Other accused figures, including Nicaraguan Colonel Anastasio Somoza Debayle and General Miguel Ydigoras Fuentes, ridiculed the conspiracy claims, while Panama dismissed an attache named in the Guatemalan communique.

El Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores dominicano desestimó las acusaciones considerándolas invenciones comunistas y negó cualquier vínculo con Guatemala o con el régimen de Árbenz. Otras figuras señaladas, como el coronel nicaragüense Anastasio Somoza Debayle y el general Miguel Ydígoras Fuentes, ridiculizaron las denuncias de conspiración, mientras que Panamá destituyó a un agregado mencionado en el comunicado guatemalteco.

Attending a diplomatic reception hosted by Argentine Ambassador General Martini for Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, the writer noted Black military officers and their wives socializing freely with senior officials and the Archbishop of Santo Domingo. records.summary_en: The Tribune recounted a travelogue by visiting members of the Pan American Medical Association touring historic and medical sites across Ciudad Trujillo, including the Alcazar de Colon and the Cathedral of Santa Maria la Menor. The physicians met with Dominican medical colleagues at a modern hospital facility before being received at the presidential palace by President Hector Trujillo. In accepting a diploma of honor for national public health achievements, Trujillo declared that state social welfare and health initiatives were essential to safeguarding civilization against communism.
records.summary_es: *The Tribune* relató una crónica de viaje de miembros visitantes de la Asociación Médica Panamericana que recorrieron sitios históricos y médicos en Ciudad Trujillo, incluidos el Alcázar de Colón y la Catedral de Santa María la Menor. Los médicos se reunieron con colegas dominicanos en unas modernas instalaciones hospitalarias antes de ser recibidos en el palacio presidencial por el presidente Héctor Trujillo. Al aceptar un diploma de honor por los logros nacionales en salud pública, Trujillo declaró que las iniciativas estatales de bienestar social y salud eran esenciales para proteger la civilización contra el comunismo.

From the ruins of the first hospital, we drove to the very latest modern hos pital where a meeting was held with physicians of the cruise and the physicians of the Dominican Republic. The place was in a long patio between two parts of the hospital. After the meet ing, we went on to the Pres ident’s palace. On the way, along the banks of the Ozama River, we passed the Tower of Homage, the oldest stone fortress in the Americas; it is now a pri son. Farther on, we saw Alcazar de Colon, a castle built in 1512 by Don Diego in honor of his father, Christopher Columbus. Next, we visited the Basil ica of Santa Maria la Menor, the oldest cathedral in the world where the remains of Columbus are supposed to be buried. Some of the jew els of Queen Isabella are on display there. By this time we reached the palace. In a Spanish address, President Trujillo welcomed the members of the Pan American Medical Association, we received copies of his speech in Spanish and English.
